Under Ottoman rule the Bulgarian church passed to the Greek patriarchate, yet the Slavic language survived, and the monk Paisius of Hilandar kindled a national revival with his Slavonic-Bulgarian History of 1762.
zh:
保加利亚人是南斯拉夫民族，由6至7世纪定居巴尔干的斯拉夫人、更早的罗马化和希腊化色雷斯人，以及说突厥语的草原部落联盟保加尔人融合而成；681年，保加尔可汗阿斯帕鲁赫在多瑙河以南建立第一保加利亚帝国。保加尔人后来逐渐改用斯拉夫语，864年鲍里斯一世皈依基督教，开启了保加利亚的黄金时代：普雷斯拉夫和奥赫里德学派发展出西里尔字母，沙皇西美昂一世更让国家足以与拜占庭抗衡。

1018年拜占庭征服终结了第一帝国，但1185年阿森和彼得兄弟起义重建国家；在伊凡·阿森二世治下，保加利亚版图再度抵达亚得里亚海与黑海。1337年，沙皇伊凡·亚历山大以特尔诺沃为都；奥斯曼人于1393年攻陷该城，1396年帝国灭亡。

奥斯曼统治时期，保加利亚教会转归希腊牧首管辖，但斯拉夫语仍然存续；1762年，希兰达修道院的修士帕伊西写成《斯拉夫—保加利亚史》，点燃了民族复兴运动。

en:
The Bullom are a West Atlantic people of the low-lying Sierra Leone coast, their name meaning low-lying land. They speak Bullom languages of the Mel branch, whose northern form is Bullom So and whose southern dialects include Sherbro, and Portuguese navigators already noted them in 1507.

In 1545 Mande invaders called the Mane defeated them in a great battle near Cape Mount, overrunning the country in the 1540s and 1550s and planting their own chiefdoms among them. During the seventeenth century Temne expansion to the coast split the Bullom: northerners kept their name while gradually assimilating to the Temne and Susu, and southerners came to be counted as Sherbro.

At Kaffu Bullom the missionary Nyländer printed a Bullom grammar in 1814, and in 1827 John Macaulay Wilson, son of a local chief, was elected king there.
zh:
布隆人是塞拉利昂低地海岸的大西洋语支族群，族名意为“低洼之地”。他们讲梅尔语支的布隆诸语，北部为布隆索语，南部方言包括歇尔布罗语；葡萄牙航海家早在1507年就记载了他们。

1545年，称马内人的曼德入侵者在芒特角附近大败布隆人，在16世纪40至50年代席卷其地，在他们中间建立自己的酋长邦。17世纪，泰姆内人向海岸扩张，把布隆人一分为二：北部一支保留族名，但逐渐融入泰姆内人和苏苏人，南部一支则被视为歇尔布罗人。

在卡富布隆，传教士尼伦德于1814年印行了布隆语语法书；1827年，当地酋长之子约翰·麦考利·威尔逊被推举为国王。

en:
The Bulu are the southernmost of the Beti-Pahuin Bantu peoples of the Cameroonian forest, their clans spread across the wooded hills between the Sanaga River and the Gabon border, including the Bulu proper around Sangmélima, Ebolowa and Kribi.

They speak Bulu, a Beti language intelligible with Ewondo and Fang, and trace their ancestry to Bantu groups who from the 700s drifted south from the central Cameroon grasslands into the equatorial forest, a movement still under way in the early 1800s as related Fang clans pushed on toward Río Muni and Gabon.

Bulu society had no kings: patrilineal lineages formed independent villages under clan heads who also led the ancestral rites. Farmers cleared the forest for manioc and maize, hunters supplied bushmeat, and carvers were noted for their masks and work in wood and ivory.
zh:
布鲁人是喀麦隆森林中贝蒂-帕胡因班图诸族里最靠南的一支，氏族分布在萨纳加河与加蓬边界之间的林木丘陵间，其中布鲁本部以桑梅利马、埃博洛瓦和克里比为中心。

他们操贝蒂语组的布鲁语，与埃翁多语和芳语互通；其祖先属于班图群体，从8世纪起由喀麦隆中部草原南下进入赤道森林，到19世纪初这一迁徙仍在继续，亲缘相近的芳人氏族继续向木尼河地区和加蓬推进。

布鲁社会没有王权：父系世系组成各自独立的村落，由氏族首领兼管祖先祭祀。农人砍伐森林种植木薯和玉米，猎人提供野味，工匠以面具以及木器和象牙雕刻闻名。

en:
The Bunak are a Papuan people of the mountainous interior of central Timor, their villages straddling the later border between West Timor and East Timor. Unlike their Atoni and Tetun neighbours, who speak Malayo-Polynesian languages, theirs belongs to the Trans-New Guinea family and shares a non-Austronesian vocabulary with other Timor Papuan tongues.

Papuan place names in their heartland suggest descent from Melanesian settlers who reached Timor around 3000 BC and were already there when Austronesian migrants arrived after 2500 BC. Without writing, they preserved history and custom in orally recited verse and, like the southern Tetun, organized society along matrilineal lines.

Portuguese influence reached Timor in the sixteenth century, and mid-eighteenth-century Dutch expansion split Bunak lands into Dutch and Portuguese spheres, though local traditional rulers long held real power.
zh:
布纳克人是帝汶岛中部山区的巴布亚语族群，村落横跨后来西帝汶与东帝汶的分界线。与说马来—波利尼西亚语言的邻族阿托尼人和德顿人不同，布纳克语属跨新几内亚语系，并与帝汶其他巴布亚语言共享一批非南岛语词汇。

其腹地的巴布亚语地名暗示，布纳克人可能是约公元前3000年抵达帝汶的美拉尼西亚定居者的后裔，在公元前2500年以后南岛语移民到来之前便已在此生息。布纳克人没有文字，历史与规范靠口传韵文记诵，并与南部德顿人一样按母系组织社会。

葡萄牙势力在16世纪进入帝汶，18世纪中叶荷兰的扩张把布纳克土地分成荷、葡两个势力范围，但实际权力长期仍掌握在本地传统首领手中。

en:
The Bundeli are the Indo-Aryan people of Bundelkhand, the dry hill country between the Yamuna River and the Vindhya Range, whose main settlements in 1337 included Khajuraho. Their language, Bundeli or Bundelkhandi, descends from Sauraseni Apabhramsha and belongs to the Western Hindi group, closely related to Braj Bhasha.

The region, once called Jejakabhukti, was the heartland of the Chandela dynasty, builders of the Khajuraho temples, until the twelfth century; it then passed to the Khangars and from the fourteenth century to the Bundela Rajputs, who gave Bundelkhand its present name. Bundeli bardic verse goes back to the Alha-Khand epic about twelfth-century heroes, while formal written literature developed under Mughal-era patronage, including works at the court of Chhatrasal of Panna.

The Bundela states submitted to the Mughals, although Chhatrasal of Panna rebelled against Aurangzeb and ruled from 1675 to 1731, and in the early nineteenth century they entered British paramountcy as tributary princely states.
zh:
本德尔人是印度中部本德尔肯德地区的印度-雅利安人，这片干旱丘陵地位于亚穆纳河与温迪亚山脉之间，1337年时的主要聚落包括克久拉霍。他们的语言本德尔语又称本德尔肯德语，由索拉塞尼阿帕布拉姆沙语演变而来，属西印地语支，与布拉杰语关系密切。

该地区旧称杰贾布克蒂，12世纪前是修建克久拉霍神庙的昌德拉王朝的核心地带，此后先后归汉加尔人统治，14世纪起又被本德尔拉杰普特人取代，本德尔肯德之名即来自这一氏族。本德尔人的吟游诗歌可追溯到讲述12世纪英雄故事的史诗《阿尔哈汗德》，书面文学则在莫卧儿时期的扶持下发展，帕纳的查特拉萨尔宫廷便产生了大量作品。

本德尔诸邦曾臣服于莫卧儿，不过帕纳的查特拉萨尔起兵反抗奥朗则布，于1675至1731年在位；19世纪初，这些邦又成为英国宗主权下的纳贡土邦。

en:
The Bundjalung are an Aboriginal Australian people of the far north coast of New South Wales and the south-eastern corner of Queensland. They are not one tribe but a nation of more than fifteen related groups whose dialects belong to the Yugambeh-Bundjalung language family.

Their own traditions trace them to the Three Brothers who came from the sea and landed at Goanna Headland, a place occupied for at least twelve thousand years. Their coast and rivers offered some of the richest hunting and fishing grounds on the continent.

In 1770 James Cook mapped the shore in Endeavour, naming Cape Byron and Mount Warning, which the Bundjalung call Wollumbin, and in 1828 Captain Henry Rous sailed into the Richmond River, the first European to explore it.
zh:
邦贾隆人是澳大利亚原住民，居住在新南威尔士州极北海岸与昆士兰州东南角。他们并非单一部落，而是由十五个以上亲缘群体组成的联盟，各方言属于尤甘贝-邦贾隆语系。

据他们自己的传说，先祖是渡海而来、在戈阿纳海岬登陆的三兄弟，那片地方至少已有一万两千年的人类居住史。他们的海岸与河流是澳大利亚大陆最丰饶的渔猎场所之一。

1770年，詹姆斯·库克驾“奋进号”测绘这段海岸，命名了拜伦角以及邦贾隆人称为沃伦宾的沃宁山；1828年，亨利·劳斯船长驶入里士满河，成为第一个勘探该河的欧洲人。

en:
The Bungku, who call themselves To Bungku, live on the southeastern peninsula of Central Sulawesi around Bungku town and the Menui Islands. Their coastal polity, the Kingdom of Bungku or Tambuku, was described as a lively trading settlement by the Spanish explorer Urdaneta in 1525.

In 1580 the Sultan of Ternate made Bungku his vassal, though Gowa held the overlordship from 1636 to 1667, after which it reverted to Ternate. Bungku chose its own king in 1672 and rejected Ternatean overlordship in 1689, keeping only a tributary tie.

The port grew rich on slaves, iron and spices, its shipping dominated by Bugis merchants from Bone and Makassar, and Lake Matano's iron ore was disputed with neighbouring Luwu. In the 1830s colonial observers called Bungku the leading port of Sulawesi's eastern coast, its rulers drawing farm tribute from inland mountain peoples.
zh:
朋古人自称“多邦古”，聚居在中苏拉威西东南半岛的朋古镇及梅努伊群岛一带。他们的沿海政权朋古王国又称坦布库，1525年西班牙探险家乌尔达内塔就曾把这里记述为繁忙的贸易聚落。

1580年，特尔纳特苏丹将朋古收为附庸；1636至1667年宗主权转归戈瓦，之后又回到特尔纳特手中。朋古于1672年自立国王，1689年拒绝特尔纳特的宗主权，仅保留朝贡关系。

这座港口靠奴隶、铁器和香料致富，航运由来自波尼和望加锡的布吉商人主导，马塔诺湖的铁矿还与邻国鲁乌长期相争。19世纪30年代，殖民观察者已把朋古视为苏拉威西东海岸的首要港口，其统治者还从山地内陆各族群收取农产贡赋。

en:
The Bourguignon are the people of Burgundy, the country of Dijon and the wooded Morvan hills, whose traditional speech is an Oïl Romance language descended from Vulgar Latin with surviving Gaulish words. The region takes its name from the Burgundians, a Germanic people who settled there in the fifth century and left a notable mark on local vocabulary.

A Duchy of Burgundy emerged early in the tenth century under Richard the Justiciar and was ruled from 1032 by a cadet line of the Capetians; after that line died out in 1361, the Valois duke Philip the Bold built a great Burgundian state stretching into Flanders and the Low Countries.

The venture ended when Charles the Bold fell at Nancy in 1477 and King Louis XI annexed the duchy to the French crown, leaving the Netherlands to the Habsburgs. Bourguignon remained the vernacular of town and countryside, though Parisian French increasingly dominated official life.
zh:
勃艮第人生活在以第戎和林木茂密的莫尔旺丘陵为中心的勃艮第地区，传统方言勃艮第语属奥依罗曼语，由通俗拉丁语演变而来，保留了少量高卢语词。地区得名于5世纪迁入的日耳曼勃艮第人，他们给当地方言留下了明显的词汇印记。

10世纪初，勃艮第公国在恶人理查治下兴起，1032年起由卡佩家族的支系统治；1361年该支绝嗣后，瓦卢瓦系的大胆者菲利普以公国为基础，建起一个延伸到佛兰德斯和低地国家的庞大勃艮第国家。

1477年大胆查理战死于南锡，法王路易十一将公国并入王室领地，低地省份则归入哈布斯堡家族。勃艮第语此后仍是城乡俗语，但巴黎法语在官方生活中的地位日益压过它。

en: The Burji are a Highland East Cushitic-speaking people whose homeland lies south of Lake Chamo in southern Ethiopia, beside the Konso country. Their language carries loanwords from Oromo, Amharic and even Swahili, marking long involvement in the caravan trade between the Ethiopian highlands and the Indian Ocean coast.
zh: 布尔吉人是操高地东库希特语的族群，故乡在埃塞俄比亚南部查莫湖以南、与孔索人地区相邻。他们的语言里有来自奥罗莫语、阿姆哈拉语乃至斯瓦希里语的借词，说明他们长期参与埃塞俄比亚高原与印度洋沿岸之间的商队贸易。

en:
The Burmese, or Bamar, are the Tibeto-Burman people of the Irrawaddy valley, whose ancestors moved south from the Yunnan-Tibet borderlands between the seventh and ninth centuries into the Pyu city-states. They built Pagan, which Anawrahta made the first Irrawaddy empire in the 1050s; his conquest of Mon Thaton in 1057 brought Theravada Buddhism and the Mon script, ancestor of the Burmese alphabet.

Mongol invasions ended Pagan in 1287, and in 1337 the Bamar heartland was divided between rival kingdoms, soon merged into Ava, founded in 1364. The long Ava period wore itself out in wars with the Mon and Shan, until the Toungoo dynasty of 1510 reunited the country; Bayinnaung, reigning from 1551, built Southeast Asia's largest empire yet.

After the empire's collapse around 1599 the Restored Toungoo kings rebuilt a smaller realm from Ava, until a Mon rebellion overthrew them in 1752. Alaungpaya then founded the Konbaung dynasty, crushed the Mon in 1757 and sacked Ayutthaya in 1767; the First Anglo-Burmese War of 1824 to 1826 stripped away Arakan and Assam.
zh:
缅人是伊洛瓦底江流域的藏缅语民族，其先民在7至9世纪间从云南与西藏交界地带南迁，定居在骠人城邦之间。他们建立了蒲甘，阿奴律陀在11世纪50年代将其扩展为伊洛瓦底江流域的第一个帝国；1057年他征服孟人城邦直通，带来了上座部佛教和孟人文字，缅文即由此演变而来。

1287年蒙古入侵终结了蒲甘，1337年缅人腹地分裂为对立的王国，不久被1364年建立的阿瓦王国合并。阿瓦在与孟人和掸人的战争中耗尽国力，1510年建立的东吁王朝重新统一全国，1551年即位的勃印曩更组建起东南亚有史以来最大的帝国。

帝国约1599年崩溃后，东吁后期诸王在阿瓦重建较小的国家，直到1752年孟人起义将其推翻。随后雍籍牙建立贡榜王朝，1757年击灭孟人政权，1767年攻陷阿瑜陀耶；1824至1826年的第一次英缅战争使缅甸丧失阿拉干和阿萨姆。

en:
The Buru, who call themselves Gebfuka, meaning people of the land, are the principal people of Buru, the third largest Maluku island, speaking a Central Malayo-Polynesian language. The island first appears in the 1365 Majapahit eulogy Nagarakretagama as Hutan Kadali.

Makassar traders built forts and forced the islanders to grow cloves until the Dutch drove them out in 1648 and burned the trees. In 1658 the Dutch East India Company fortified Kayeli Bay and moved some two thousand villagers, including much of the tribal nobility, into thirteen settlements to work clove plantations; these clans became the Kayeli, the island's loyal elite.

After the Company fell the Dutch crown reorganized Buru into fourteen regencies in 1824. The Buru kept the cult of the supreme deity Opo Hebe Snulat even as Islam spread in the north and Protestantism in the south, farming rice, sago and spices and hunting the Buru babirusa.
zh:
布鲁人自称格布夫卡，意为“大地之民”，是马鲁古第三大岛布鲁岛的主体原住民，操中部马来—波利尼西亚语言。该岛最早见于1365年满者伯夷颂诗《爪哇史颂》，时称胡坦·卡达利。

望加锡人在岛上修筑工事，强迫岛民种植丁香，直到1648年荷兰人将他们赶走并烧毁丁香树。1658年荷兰东印度公司在卡耶利湾设堡，把约两千名村民（包括大批部落贵族）迁进13个定居点，为丁香园服役；这些氏族后来成为卡耶利人，是岛上效忠公司的精英阶层。

公司解散后，荷兰王室于1824年把布鲁划分为14个土邦。在北方伊斯兰教与南方新教传播的同时，布鲁人仍保留着对至高神奥波·赫贝·斯努拉特的崇拜，他们种植水稻、西谷和香料，猎捕布鲁鹿豚。

en:
The Burusho, or Hunzakut, are the people of the Hunza and Nagar valleys in the high Karakoram, around fortresses such as Baltit. Their Burushaski tongue is a language isolate, unrelated to the Indo-Aryan languages around it, and they are thought to descend from an older population driven into the mountains by incoming Indo-Aryans.

Around 1200 their valleys formed the independent principality of Hunza, whose rulers were first called Thum and later Mir and claimed descent from the soldiers of Alexander the Great; neighbouring Nagar grew into a sister Burusho kingdom. The Burusho took to Islam, most following its Ismaili branch.

From about 1761 the Mir of Hunza recognized the suzerainty of the Qing emperor, sending an annual tribute of gold dust in exchange for silk, tea and porcelain, while his raiders also ranged across the Karakoram into the Kunlun.
zh:
布鲁绍人又称罕扎库特，居住在喀喇昆仑高地的罕萨和纳格尔河谷，以巴尔蒂特等堡垒为中心。他们讲的布鲁夏斯基语是语言孤立语，与周围所有印度-雅利安语言都没有亲缘关系；一般认为他们是更古老居民的后裔，在迁入的印度-雅利安人挤压下退入深山。

约1200年，他们的河谷形成独立的罕萨小邦，统治者最初称“苏姆”，后来称“米尔”，并自称是亚历山大大帝麾下士兵的后裔；相邻的纳格尔河谷发展为姊妹的布鲁绍王国。布鲁绍人后来皈依伊斯兰教，多数归入伊斯玛仪派。

约从1761年起，罕萨米尔承认清朝皇帝的宗主权，每年进贡金砂，换回丝绸、茶叶和瓷器，而其部众的劫掠活动也越过喀喇昆仑延伸到昆仑山区。

en: The Buruwai, also called Sabakor, are a Papuan people of Buruway District in Kaimana Regency, on Kamrau Bay at the western end of the Bomberai Peninsula. Their language forms the Kamrau Bay, or Sabakor, branch of the Asmat-Kamoro family, a cluster of closely related Trans-New Guinea languages of the southern New Guinea coast.
zh: 布鲁瓦伊人（又称萨巴科尔人）是巴布亚族群，住在邦贝拉伊半岛西端卡姆劳湾畔凯马纳县的布鲁瓦伊区。他们的语言属跨新几内亚语系阿斯马特-卡莫罗语族的卡姆劳湾（萨巴科尔）语支，该语族是新几内亚南岸一批亲缘很近的语言。

en:
The Buryats are the northernmost Mongol people, formed around Lake Baikal from Mongolic, Turkic, Tungusic and Samoyedic tribes. The name Buriyad first occurs in the Secret History of the Mongols, recording how Jochi, son of Genghis Khan, subdued them on the Angara in 1207.

In the late 1300s they joined the Oirats against the Eastern Mongols, and by the seventeenth century they paid tribute to the Khalkha khans while levying sable tribute from Evenk and Samoyed neighbours.

Russian Cossacks reached Transbaikalia in 1609 and Lake Baikal in 1643, putting down repeated revolts; the treaties of Nerchinsk in 1689 and Kyakhta in 1727 transferred both shores from Mongolia to Russia. Under Russian rule western Buryats took to agriculture and Orthodoxy, while eastern Buryats kept nomadic life and turned to Tibetan Buddhism, its first local monastery built after recognition in 1741.
zh:
布里亚特是分布最靠北的蒙古语族群，在贝加尔湖周围由蒙古、突厥、通古斯和萨莫耶德等部落融合而成。“布里亚特”一名最早见于《蒙古秘史》，书中记载1207年成吉思汗之子术赤北上，征服安加拉河一带的布里亚特人。

14世纪末，他们加入瓦剌一方对抗东蒙古；到17世纪，他们向喀尔喀诸汗纳贡，同时又向邻近的鄂温克、萨莫耶德人征收紫貂贡。

俄国哥萨克1609年进入外贝加尔、1643年抵达贝加尔湖，平定了多次反抗；1689年的《尼布楚条约》和1727年的《恰克图条约》正式把贝加尔湖两岸从蒙古划入俄国。入俄之后，湖西的布里亚特人逐渐改事农耕并皈依东正教，湖东布里亚特人则保持游牧生活，转而信奉藏传佛教；1741年藏传佛教获得俄国官方承认，当地第一座喇嘛寺随之建起。

en:
Butonese is the collective name for the related seafaring peoples of Buton and neighbouring Southeast Sulawesi islands, whose small vessels sailed throughout the Malay archipelago. Around the 1300s chiefdoms united at Wolio, the future Baubau, under their first ruler Wa Kaa Kaa, whose husband was said to descend from Majapahit; the islands had earlier been listed as Majapahit tributaries in the Negarakertagama and Palapa oath.

The kingdom converted to Islam in the mid-sixteenth century under King La Kilaponto, later Sultan Murhum, guided by a Johor scholar and Ternate's influence. It became an unusual constitutional monarchy with a written constitution, the Murtabat Tujuh, formalized under Sultan La Elangi (1597-1631).

Walled Baubau became one of the region's best-fortified centres, its palace fortress the largest of its kind, while farmers grew rice, cotton and coconuts. Most Butonese are Muslim, though Bajau nomads are sometimes mistakenly counted among them.
zh:
布敦人是东南苏拉威西布敦岛及邻近岛屿各相近航海族群的统称，驾驶小船往来马来群岛各地。约14世纪，各首领在沃利奥（即后来的巴务巴务）联合，拥戴首位统治者瓦·卡·卡阿，其丈夫据称有满者伯夷血统；《爪哇史颂》和帕拉帕誓约此前已将这些岛屿列为满者伯夷的属邦。

16世纪中叶，在柔佛学者和特尔纳特影响下，国王拉·基拉蓬多改宗伊斯兰教，后称苏丹穆尔胡姆。布敦成为少见的君主立宪政权，成文宪法《穆尔塔巴特·图朱》由苏丹拉·埃兰吉（1597—1631年）定型。

设防的王城巴务巴务成为当地最坚固的中心之一，王宫要塞规模冠绝同类；农民种植水稻、棉花和椰子。布敦人大多信奉伊斯兰教，不过巴瑶人有时会被误归入其中。

en:
The Butuanon are a Visayan group of the Agusan River delta in northeastern Mindanao, heirs to one of the Philippines' earliest recorded polities. Their Rajahnate of Butuan, Puduan in Chinese annals, was a gold-mining port whose balangay boats sailed as far as China and Majapahit; a tributary mission reached the Song court in 1001, and a later envoy presented a gold-tablet memorial.

Chinese annals record Brunei conquering Butuan in 1304, before it regained freedom. In 1521 the Butuan rajah Siagu attended the first Catholic mass in the Philippines at Limasawa with Ferdinand Magellan's men.

Legazpi granted Butuan as an encomienda in 1571, and a Jesuit mission opened its first church in 1597, as old Hindu, Buddhist and animist beliefs gave way to Catholicism. Their Butuanon language is a Southern Visayan tongue close to Surigaonon.
zh:
武端人是棉兰老东北部阿古桑河三角洲的米沙鄢族群，是菲律宾最早有文字记载的政权之一的继承者。他们的武端拉贾国在中国史籍中称蒲端国，是采金贸易港口，巴朗盖船远航至中国、满者伯夷等地；1001年朝贡使团抵达宋朝宫廷，后来的使者还进呈金片国书。

中国史籍记载，文莱于1304年征服武端，此后武端恢复独立。1521年，武端拉者西亚维在利马萨瓦出席菲律宾第一场天主教弥撒，与麦哲伦的部下同行。

1571年莱加斯皮把武端封为监护征赋地，1597年耶稣会传教站建成当地第一座教堂，印度教、佛教和万物有灵旧信仰逐渐让位于天主教。武端语是南米沙鄢语的一支，与苏里高语相近。

en: The Bwende, or Babwende, are a Bantu people of the Bakongo cluster living on both sides of the border between the two Congos, chiefly north of the Congo River between the Luala and Kenke rivers. They speak Bwende, a language close to Kikongo, and their lands once formed part of the Kingdom of Kongo.
zh: 布文德人是巴刚果族群中的一支班图人，散居在两个刚果边境两侧，主要住在刚果河以北、卢阿拉河与肯凯河之间。他们讲与刚果语相近的布文德语，故土曾是刚果王国的一部分。

en:
The Cabécar, who call themselves Kabekwa, are a Chibchan people of the rain-soaked Talamanca mountains of eastern Costa Rica. They have lived there some three thousand years and, with the related Bribri, form the Talamanca branch of the Chibchan family; their elders derive the name Cabécar from kabé, quetzal, and ká, place.

Before the conquest they headed the strongest Atlantic-facing chiefdom, and Talamanca was the one chiefdom the Spanish never fully overcame, becoming a refuge for peoples fleeing their rule. Revolts followed: Cabécar leaders Guaycorá and Sumamará burned the Spanish town of Santiago de Talamanca in 1610, and in 1709 Comesala joined Pablo Presbere in the largest Indian rising of Costa Rica's colonial history.

In round conical-roofed houses, farming rotated clearings of maize, beans and cassava, the Cabécar kept their language and mountain autonomy intact through the rest of the colonial era.
zh:
卡贝卡尔人自称卡贝夸人，是哥斯达黎加东部潮湿塔拉曼卡山区的奇布查语族群。他们在此已生活约三千年，与关系相近的布里布里人同属奇布查语系的塔拉曼卡分支；据长老解释，卡贝卡尔一名由意为格查尔鸟的卡贝和意为地方的卡两字合成。

征服时代以前，他们统领大西洋沿岸最强大的酋长国；塔拉曼卡也是西班牙人唯一未能完全征服的酋长国，成为各族逃避殖民统治的避难所。此后起义不断：卡贝卡尔首领瓜伊科拉和苏马拉于1610年焚毁西班牙人的圣地亚哥德塔拉曼卡城；1709年，科梅萨拉与巴勃罗·普雷斯贝雷共同领导了哥斯达黎加殖民史上规模最大的印第安人起义。

他们住圆锥形屋顶的圆形房屋，在轮歇火烧地上种植玉米、菜豆和木薯，在殖民时代后期保住了自己的语言和山地自治。

en:
The Cabinda culture covers the Kongo-speaking peoples of the forested Atlantic coast between the Chiloango River and the Congo mouth, above all the Woyo of Ngoyo and the people of Kakongo, both Bakongo.

In the thirteenth century the small Mayombe state of Vungu led a confederation including Ngoyo and Kakongo, regarded as one seed of the Kingdom of Kongo. The Woyo built hereditary Ngoyo, its ruler titled the Mangoyo, while Kakongo appears in a Kongo royal title in 1535 and traded independently with merchants from the 1620s in ivory, copper and slaves.

By 1700 Cabinda was the busiest slave port north of Luanda; in 1783 Ngoyo and Kakongo destroyed a Portuguese fort together, but the trade hollowed out the monarchies, and Ngoyo collapsed in the 1830s when its nobles could no longer choose a king.
zh:
卡宾达文化涵盖希卢安果河至刚果河口之间林木海岸上说刚果语的族群，主要是恩戈约的沃约人和卡孔戈人，均属巴刚果人。

13世纪，马永贝小邦丰古领导含恩戈约、卡孔戈的联盟，被视为刚果王国的源头之一。沃约人建立世袭的恩戈约王国，君主称曼戈约；卡孔戈1535年已见诸刚果国王头衔，17世纪20年代起独立通商，出口象牙、铜和奴隶。

到1700年，卡宾达已成为罗安达以北最繁忙的奴隶贸易港。1783年两国联手摧毁一座葡萄牙要塞，但贸易掏空了君主国：19世纪30年代贵族选不出国王，恩戈约瓦解。

en:
The Caddo are a confederacy of farming peoples of the Southeastern Woodlands, spread across northeastern Texas, western Louisiana, southwestern Arkansas and southeastern Oklahoma. Westernmost heirs of Mississippian culture, they built temple mounds from about 800, grandest at Spiro Mounds on the Arkansas River, and by 1200 maize fields supported dense farming villages.

The Great Drought of 1276 to 1299 and Siouan migrations thinned their northern lands. De Soto's expedition fought the Tula in 1541; Franciscan missions won few converts where villagers kept their sacred fires.

In the early eighteenth century French posts spawned Natchitoches and Nacogdoches, as smallpox and measles thinned the Caddo population. Spain, France and the United States after the 1803 Louisiana Purchase courted them, but they stayed neutral until the Removal Act of 1830; in 1835 the Kadohadacho confederacy moved by treaty into Texas, then part of Mexico, whose name comes from the Hasinai word for friend.
zh:
卡多人是东南林地的农耕诸部联盟，散布在今得克萨斯东北、路易斯安那西部、阿肯色西南和俄克拉荷马东南。作为密西西比文化最西边的继承者，他们约800年起修筑神庙土丘，以阿肯色河畔的斯派罗土丘最为宏大；到1200年，玉米田已供养起人口稠密的农耕村落。

1276至1299年的大旱和苏语群体迁徙使北方领地人烟稀疏。1541年德索托探险队与图拉人发生冲突；在村民守护圣火的地方，方济各会传教站收获寥寥。

18世纪初法国商栈促成纳基托什和纳科多奇斯两城兴起，天花和麻疹又使人口锐减。西班牙、法国及1803年购得路易斯安那后的美国先后拉拢，卡多人保持中立直到1830年《印第安人迁移法》；1835年，卡多哈达乔联盟签约迁往当时属墨西哥的得克萨斯，而得克萨斯之名来自哈西奈人意为朋友的词语。

en:
The Cahokia were the people of the greatest city of the Mississippian culture, which rose on the Mississippi floodplain opposite present-day Saint Louis around 1050. Around 1100 it held fifteen to twenty thousand people and some hundred and twenty mounds across six square miles, its trade linking the Great Lakes to the Gulf of Mexico.

At its centre stood Monks Mound, a four-terraced, thirty-metre platform, the largest pre-Columbian earthwork north of Mexico, crowned by a temple or ruler's residence; nearby timber circles called woodhenges marked the solstices, while Mound 72's rich burials show falcon imagery and sacrificed retainers.

The city's original name and the precise identity of its people are unrecorded, though linguistic evidence points to a Dhegiha Siouan-speaking population. Drought, floods, deforestation and upheaval emptied it by about 1350, leaving plazas and mounds to later archaeologists.
zh:
卡霍基亚人是密西西比文化最大城市的居民，这座城市约1050年兴起于今圣路易斯隔密西西比河相望的泛滥平原上。1100年前后鼎盛期，全城约有一万五千至两万人口，六平方英里内分布着约一百二十座土墩，贸易连接五大湖与墨西哥湾。

城市中心是分四层台地、高三十米的僧侣丘，为墨西哥以北最大的前哥伦布时期土方工程，丘顶建有神庙或首领宅邸；附近称木阵的木桩群标示冬至夏至，72号墩墓葬则可见隼鸟形象与殉葬侍从。

城市原名与居民的确切族属均无文字留存，语言证据指向操德吉哈苏语的人群。干旱、河患、森林耗尽和动荡使城市在1350年前后沦为空城，只留下广场和土墩，供后世考古学家重新发现。

en:
Calima is the archaeological name for a succession of pre-Columbian societies in the river valleys of the Valle del Cauca in western Colombia, where settled farming began with the Ilama culture around 1500 BCE.

The Ilama were followed by the Yotoco, who expanded toward the Cauca River and modern Cali, developed polychrome pottery and hammered goldwork, and lasted until about 1200 CE.

The Sonso culture then flourished from roughly 800 to 1600, with more centralized chiefdoms and cast gold-and-copper work, and Sonso communities still lived there when Spanish expeditions arrived. The label Calima itself comes from the area where their tombs, terraces and ceramics were excavated, not from any people known by that name.
zh:
卡利马是考古学对哥伦比亚西部考卡山谷河谷中一系列前后相继的史前文化的统称。约公元前1500年，伊拉马文化在这里最早进入定居农耕生活。

其后的约托科文化把疆域扩展到考卡河与今卡利一带，发展出多彩陶器和锤揲金器，延续到约1200年。

接着兴盛的是松索文化，年代约为800至1600年，其酋邦权力更加集中，金器采用金铜合铸工艺，因此西班牙探险队进入山谷时，这里仍生活着松索时期的社群。“卡利马”这个名称来自出土墓葬、梯田和陶器的地区名，而不是某个以此自称的民族。

en:
The Calusa were a fishing people of Florida's southwest coast, heirs of the Caloosahatchee culture, who built a hierarchical society on fisheries, not agriculture. Their capital Calos, probably on Mound Key, ruled a realm from Charlotte Harbor to Marco Island, with neighboring peoples under its influence.

War canoes met Juan Ponce de León in 1513, and in 1521 the Calusa drove off his expedition; he died of his wound. In 1566 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés founded a mission among them and married chief Carlos's sister. The Spanish later killed Carlos, abandoning the post by 1569.

Isolated and without firearms, the Calusa faced Creek and Yamasee raiders sweeping the peninsula after 1702. Epidemics and slave raids broke their power: 270 survivors were evacuated to Cuba in 1711, and when Florida passed to Britain in 1763 the last Calusa were removed there.
zh:
卡卢萨人是佛罗里达西南海岸的渔猎族群，承袭卡卢萨哈奇文化，凭渔业而非农业建成等级分明的社会。都城卡洛斯可能在芒德岛，辖境从夏洛特港到马科岛，邻近一些族群受其影响。

1513年他们驾战舟迎击庞塞·德莱昂，1521年击退其远征，庞塞·德莱昂伤重而死。1566年梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯在其地建传教站，娶首领卡洛斯的姐妹为妻；后来西班牙人杀死卡洛斯，1569年前弃守。

卡卢萨人长期隔绝、没有火器，1702年后克里克人和亚马西人席卷半岛。瘟疫和奴隶劫掠摧毁其势力：1711年270名幸存者撤往古巴，1763年佛罗里达割让英国时，最后的卡卢萨人也被迁往古巴。

en:
The Canta were the highland people of the Chillon valley, north-east of Lima, whose principal stronghold was the hilltop settlement of Cantamarca. Their language was Cauqui, a divergent relative of Jaqaru within the Aymaran family, and the name canta itself meant either a hillside or the cord used to snare vicunas.

For generations they lived scattered in village communities in the cold quechua and puna zones above the valley, until the Inca emperor Pachacutec brought the region under Cuzco's rule during his northern campaigns.

When the Spanish reached the valley in 1535 they found a prosperous land, and on 8 December 1544 the native communities, including Cantamarca, were forcibly resettled in the new Spanish-style town of Canta to be instructed in the Catholic faith.
zh:
坎塔人是利马东北方奇永河谷的高原居民，主要据点是山顶聚落坎塔马卡。他们使用考基语——艾马拉语系中哈卡鲁语的一支歧异方言；“坎塔”这个词在他们的语言里意为山坡，也指捕捉骆马用的套索。

他们世代以村社形式散居在河谷上方寒冷的克丘亚与普纳地带，直到印加君主帕查库特克在北方征战中将这一地区纳入库斯科的统治。

1535年西班牙人抵达河谷时，这里已是一片富庶之地；1544年12月8日，包括坎塔马卡在内的原住民村社被强行迁入按西班牙样式新建的坎塔镇，以便接受天主教教化。

en:
The Cappadocian Greeks are the Greek-speaking population of Cappadocia, the plateau of central-eastern Anatolia around Nevşehir. Greek settlers followed Alexander the Great, and under the Hellenistic kings of Cappadocia and later Roman rule Greek became the region's common language, producing the philosopher Apollonius of Tyana.

Cappadocia remained a heartland of Byzantine Christianity, dotted with rock-cut churches and underground towns that served as refuges. After Manzikert in 1071 the Seljuk Turks overran the plateau and made Konya the capital of their Sultanate of Rum, bringing the Greeks under Turkish rule and gradual bilingualism.

In 1337 Cappadocia was divided among Turkish principalities, while Orthodox villages around Niğde kept a dialect heavily mixed with Turkish. Ottoman conquest of the Karamanid lands in the later fifteenth century incorporated the Greek communities into the empire, yet Cappadocian Greek remained in use, and Turkish was even written in Greek letters for religious texts.
zh:
卡帕多西亚人是安纳托利亚中东部高原卡帕多西亚的说希腊语居民，居于内夫谢希尔一带。希腊移民随亚历山大东来，在希腊化王国与罗马统治下，希腊语成为当地通用语，诞生了提亚纳的哲人阿波罗尼奥斯。

卡帕多西亚长期是拜占庭基督教重镇，遍布岩洞教堂与地下城，战乱时地下城充当避难所。1071年曼齐刻尔特战败后，塞尔柱突厥人攻占高原，定科尼亚为鲁姆苏丹国都城，希腊人受其统治并渐成双语。

1337年卡帕多西亚分属各突厥王公，尼代一带的东正教村落仍保留突厥语成分很重的方言。15世纪后期奥斯曼征服卡拉曼领地，希腊人社群被纳入帝国，但卡帕多西亚希腊语仍沿用，甚至以希腊字母拼写突厥语书写宗教文本。

en:
The Caquetío were an Arawak-speaking people of the arid coast of northwestern Venezuela, around Coro, and of Aruba, Curaçao and Bonaire across the water. Mainland hunter-gatherers, they kept close ties with island kinsmen, perhaps six hundred of them on Aruba when the Spaniards arrived in 1499.

In 1513 the crown declared the islands useless, and in 1515 some two thousand Caquetío were shipped to Hispaniola's mines. Some were returned in 1526 to cut brazilwood, and their language died out by the mid-sixteenth century.

When the Dutch seized Aruba in 1636 they expelled the natives, then reemployed them as hunters and herders. By the later 1600s they spoke Spanish and were Catholic, and in 1723 about two hundred crossed to the mainland to found El Carrizal near Coro. They were gradually absorbed into the colonial populations of Venezuela and the Dutch islands.
zh:
卡克蒂奥人是阿拉瓦克语族群，住在委内瑞拉西北干旱海岸的科罗一带及隔海的阿鲁巴、库拉索、博奈尔三岛。大陆族人以狩猎采集为生，与岛上来往密切；1499年西班牙人抵达时，阿鲁巴岛上约有六百人。

1513年西班牙王室宣布这些岛屿无用，1515年约两千卡克蒂奥人被围捕运往伊斯帕尼奥拉矿山；1526年小部分人被送回采伐巴西红木，其语言到16世纪中叶消亡。

1636年荷兰人夺取阿鲁巴，先驱逐原住民，再雇他们狩猎放牧。17世纪后期岛民已改说西班牙语、信奉天主教，1723年约两百人渡海回大陆，在科罗附近建埃尔卡里萨尔镇。卡克蒂奥人逐渐融入委内瑞拉和荷兰诸岛的殖民人口。

en:
The Caranqui, also called Cara, were the people of the northern Ecuadorian sierra, holding the valleys of Imbabura around Caranqui, Cayambe and Otavalo. Tradition traced them to a sea landing on the Bay of Caráquez; by the tenth century they had moved up the Esmeraldas River into the Andes, speaking a Barbacoan tongue and raising the stepped mounds called tolas, seen at Cochasquí from about 900.

Skilled traders between the Pasto, the Quitu and the Yumbo, they saw wars and marriage alliances with the Quitu ripen into a league against the Incas. Túpac Yupanqui broke the league; a later revolt under Huayna Capac ended at Yahuarcocha, the blood lake, where the Caranqui and Cayambi were slaughtered.

Spaniards overran the region in 1534; epidemic disease and intermarriage dissolved the tribe into the colonial mestizo population, though its language lived on in place names.
zh:
卡兰基人又称卡拉人，是厄瓜多尔最北部高原居民，据有因巴布拉山谷，酋邦在卡兰基、卡扬贝和奥塔瓦洛。传说祖先由海上登陆卡拉克斯湾，10世纪沿埃斯梅拉达斯河上溯安第斯山区，使用巴巴科安语族语言，建造名为托拉的阶梯形土墩，约900年的科查斯基遗址即可见到。

他们善于经商，处在帕斯多人、基多人与云博低地之间；与基多人的战和联姻演变为对抗印加的联盟。图帕克·尤潘基击破联盟，后来他们在瓦伊纳·卡帕克治下再度起义，最终在亚瓦尔科查（意为血湖）与卡扬贝人同遭屠戮。

1534年西班牙人征服该地；疫病和通婚使这个部族消融于殖民时代的梅斯蒂索人口之中，但其语言仍留在地名里。

en:
The Carentouan take their name from the palisaded town of Carantouan on the upper Susquehanna, near the New York border. In 1615 Champlain sent the interpreter Étienne Brûlé to win them as allies against the Haudenosaunee; Brûlé found a fortified town of about four thousand people and roughly eight hundred warriors, its houses and palisades resembling the Wendat's, and Champlain mapped it in 1632. Its name was later glossed as Big Tree.

Most historians identify them with the Susquehannock, called Andaste by the Wendat, who had earlier lived in scattered riverside hamlets before drifting south to Chesapeake Bay. A ruined earthwork at Spanish Hill, South Waverly, is the best-known candidate for the town's site.

They shared the Susquehannock collapse. Overwhelmed by the Haudenosaunee in the mid-1670s and besieged on Piscataway Creek in 1675, they were absorbed into the Haudenosaunee nations from 1677.
zh:
卡伦图安人得名于萨斯奎哈纳河上游、纽约州界附近的栅栏城镇卡伦图安。1615年尚普兰派译员布吕莱争取该镇结盟对付霍迪诺肖尼人；布吕莱见其为约四千居民、近八百战士的设防城镇，房屋栅栏与温达特人的相似，尚普兰1632年绘入地图，镇名后释为“大树”。

多数学者把卡伦图安人等同于萨斯奎哈诺克人（温达特人称其为安达斯特人），此前以分散河畔村落为居，后南迁切萨皮克湾。南韦弗利西班牙山一处倾圮的土垒，是该镇遗址最知名的候选地。

他们同遭萨斯奎哈诺克人的崩溃：17世纪70年代中期被霍迪诺肖尼人击溃，1675年在皮斯卡塔韦溪遭围攻，1677年起被并入霍迪诺肖尼诸族。

en:
The Kalinago, or Island Caribs, were warriors of the Windward Islands, Dominica and southern Leewards in Columbus's time, and gave the Caribbean its name. Long said to be mainland Caribs conquering the Igneri around 1200, they are now understood as islanders fused with smaller South American groups: their everyday tongue was the Igneri Arawakan, while men used a Cariban pidgin marking mainland ties.

The Taíno warned Columbus of these raiders on his arrival in 1492. The Kalinago later fought the Spanish alongside the Taíno of Puerto Rico, destroying a Franciscan church at Aguada in 1579.

French colonization from 1635 squeezed them, and after a failed 1660 Martinique revolt survivors concentrated in Dominica and Saint Vincent. The Saint Vincent community mixed with escaped Africans to become the Garifuna, or Black Caribs, whom the British moved to Roatán off Central America at the end of the eighteenth century; a Kalinago community remained in Dominica.
zh:
卡利纳戈人又称岛屿加勒比人，是哥伦布时代向风群岛、多米尼加与小安的列斯南部尚武族群，加勒比海得名于他们。旧说视其为约1200年征服伊涅里人的大陆加勒比人，今视为岛民与南美小群体融合产物：日常讲承自伊涅里人的阿拉瓦克语，男子另用加勒比语混合语标示大陆渊源。

1492年哥伦布抵达，泰诺人即警告这些袭掠者；卡利纳戈人后来与波多黎各的泰诺人联手对抗西班牙，1579年捣毁阿瓜达的方济各会教堂。

1635年法国殖民紧逼，1660年马提尼克起义失败，残部聚于多米尼加和圣文森特。圣文森特一支与逃亡非洲人融合成加里富纳人（即黑加勒比人），18世纪末被英国迁到中美洲海岸外的罗阿坦岛；多米尼加的卡利纳戈社群存续下来。

en:
The Casma were the people of a chain of coastal valleys in northern Peru, from the Culebras valley to the Chao valley, a stretch about three hundred kilometres long. Their pottery appears from around 700 CE, and they reoccupied and remodelled older Moche centres such as Panamarca and El Castillo, while walls at Santa and Nepena guarded their frontiers.

Between 1000 and 1290 their confederation peaked. It was ruled from El Purgatorio in the Casma valley, with towns at Cerro la Cruz and Ten Ten.

Expansion then brought them against the Chimu Empire: the Punta Lobos massacre has been interpreted as a sacrifice connected with that conquest, and after a final war in the late fourteenth century the Casma state disappeared. At Manchan, Chimu and Casma styles appear together, showing Casma communities lived on under Chimu rule.
zh:
卡斯马人聚居于秘鲁北部一连串沿海河谷，南起库莱布拉斯河谷，北抵乔河谷，沿海岸绵延约三百公里。他们的陶器约在700年前后出现，还重新占据并改造了帕尼亚马卡、埃尔卡斯蒂略等更早的莫切遗址，并在圣塔和内佩尼亚筑墙守卫边界。

1000至1290年间，卡斯马联盟达到极盛，以卡斯马河谷的埃尔普加托里奥为首府，塞罗拉克鲁斯和腾腾也是重要城镇。

此后扩张把他们推向奇穆帝国：蓬塔洛沃斯屠杀被认为与这场征服有关，14世纪末最后一场战争后，卡斯马邦国灭亡。在曼昌，奇穆与卡斯马的风格并存，说明卡斯马社群在奇穆统治下延续下来。

en:
The Castilians are the people of the high northern Meseta around Burgos, whose Romance vernacular grew from Vulgar Latin brought to the peninsula after 210 BC; its first written traces appear in ninth-century Latin glosses. Their land began as a county of the kingdom of León and became a kingdom itself in the 1000s, and after Ferdinand III united Castile and León in 1230 his crown carried the Reconquista down the Guadalquivir to Seville.

Toledo, taken from the Muslims in 1085, became the forge of the written standard: in the 1200s the royal chancery turned the Burgos dialect into the language of law and learning, enriched by thousands of Arabic words.

The marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand in 1469 joined Castile to Aragon, and the fall of Granada in 1492, the same year Columbus sailed under the Castilian flag, opened an American empire that carried Castilian across the Atlantic. The Nueva Planta decrees of 1716 made Castilian the official Spanish of a centralized monarchy.
zh:
卡斯蒂利亚人是北部高原梅塞塔的居民，聚居于布尔戈斯一带；他们的罗曼语方言源自公元前210年后罗马人带到半岛的通俗拉丁语，现存最早的语言痕迹见于9世纪拉丁文注释。此地原是莱昂王国的伯爵领，11世纪成为独立王国；1230年费尔南多三世合并卡斯蒂利亚与莱昂后，王权沿收复失地运动南下，沿瓜达尔基维尔河一直打到塞维利亚。

1085年从穆斯林手中夺取的托莱多成为书面标准的熔炉：13世纪，王室文书处把布尔戈斯方言锤炼成法律与学术语言，并吸收了数以千计的阿拉伯语借词。

1469年伊莎贝拉与费尔南多联姻，卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡合流；1492年格拉纳达陷落，同年哥伦布挂卡斯蒂利亚旗帜出航，开启了把卡斯蒂利亚语带过大西洋的美洲帝国。1716年的《新基本法令》使卡斯蒂利亚语成为中央集权君主制下的官方西班牙语。

en:
The Cataguá, also called Cataguases, were a non-Tupi people of the Brazilian interior and the most numerous indigenous group in later Minas Gerais; their grip on the central and southern grasslands was such that bandeirantes called it the Campos Gerais dos Cataguases, the Country of the Cataguá.

Moving north from southern Brazil, they defeated the Tupi-speaking Carijó and occupied much of their territory, winning fame as warriors, and Portuguese settlers accused them, perhaps unjustly, of devouring war captives.

When the Portuguese crown turned against them around 1670, paulista bandeirantes marched in to enslave or exterminate: Fernão Dias Paes Leme led some six hundred men, and Lourenço Castanho Taques is credited with breaking their power in a campaign remembered as genocide. Surviving bands were absorbed or displaced by the gold rush filling Minas Gerais with miners, and the town of Cataguases still keeps their name.
zh:
卡塔瓜人又称卡塔瓜塞斯人，是巴西内陆的非图皮族群，也是后来米纳斯吉拉斯人数最多的原住民；他们控制中部和南部草原，旗兵遂把那片地区称为卡塔瓜旷野，即卡塔瓜之地。

他们从巴西南部北上，击败说图皮语的卡里若人，占据其大片土地，以善战著称，葡萄牙殖民者指控他们吞食战俘，这一罪名未必属实。

约1670年葡萄牙王室决定对他们用兵，圣保罗旗兵随之进山，掳人为奴或加以剿灭：费尔南·迪亚斯·帕伊斯·莱梅率约六百人攻入，洛伦索·卡斯塔尼奥·塔克斯最终将他们击溃，这场行动被视为种族灭绝。残余群体或被同化，或被涌入米纳斯吉拉斯的淘金潮排挤流散，卡塔瓜塞斯镇仍留存他们的名字。

en:
The Catalans are the people of the eastern Pyrenees and the Mediterranean littoral of the peninsula, whose Romance speech evolved from Vulgar Latin by the 800s and slowly diverged from Old Occitan between the 1000s and the 1300s. When the County of Barcelona broke from the Carolingian Empire in 988 it became the heart of an expanding principality, and conquests of the 1200s carried the language into the new kingdom of Valencia and beyond.

The later Middle Ages were Catalan's golden age: Ramon Llull of Majorca, who died in 1315, wrote philosophy, science and fiction in Catalan, the royal chancery forged a standardized tongue that served as an official language of Sicily and Sardinia, and Martorell's chivalric romance Tirant lo Blanc appeared in 1490.

After the union with Castile in 1479 the court turned to Spanish, and the Nueva Planta decrees of 1714 imposed Castilian in law and administration, while the Treaty of the Pyrenees in 1659 had already left the Catalans of Roussillon under France.
zh:
加泰罗尼亚人聚居于比利牛斯山东段及半岛地中海沿岸，他们的罗曼语在9世纪时已从通俗拉丁语中演化成形，并在11至14世纪间与古奥克语逐渐分化。988年巴塞罗那伯国脱离加洛林帝国，成为日益壮大的公国核心，13世纪的征服把这门语言带到新建立的瓦伦西亚王国等地。

中世纪后期是加泰罗尼亚语的黄金时代：1315年去世的马略卡人拉蒙·柳利用加泰罗尼亚语撰写哲学、科学和小说，王室文书处打造出标准化的书面语，一度成为西西里和撒丁的官方语言；1490年，马托雷利的骑士传奇《骑士蒂朗》问世。

1479年与卡斯蒂利亚联合后，宫廷转而使用西班牙语，1714年的《新基本法令》在法律和行政中强制推行卡斯蒂利亚语；而早在1659年，《比利牛斯条约》已把鲁西永的加泰罗尼亚人划归法国。

en:
The Iswa, 'people of the river' in their Siouan tongue, whom Europeans called the Catawba, dominated the Carolina Piedmont on their namesake river. Earlier Mississippian chiefdoms such as Joara stood there, visited by De Soto in 1540 and by Juan Pardo, builder of Fort San Juan in 1567, whose garrison was wiped out a year later.

As English settlement spread, they absorbed dwindling neighbors and fought the Seneca and Shawnee over hunting grounds, and the Cherokee over their mountain border; colonists brokered talks at Albany in 1721 and the Treaty of Lancaster in 1744.

Smallpox struck in 1738 and again in 1759, when it killed nearly half the nation, and Shawnee raiders killed their chief King Hagler in 1763. South Carolina confirmed a reservation on the Catawba River the same year. They joined the colonists in the Revolutionary War, fleeing to Virginia in 1780 and returning after Guilford Court House to reduced lands.
zh:
伊斯瓦人在苏语中意为“河之人”，欧洲人称其卡托巴人，称雄卡罗来纳皮德蒙特，居同名卡托巴河畔。故地曾有约阿拉等密西西比酋邦：1540年德索托到访，1567年帕尔多建圣胡安堡，一年后驻军被灭。

英国定居者扩张后，他们吸纳衰微邻族，与塞内卡人、肖尼人争猎场，又在山区与切罗基人交战；殖民当局先后于1721年奥尔巴尼会议、1744年《兰开斯特条约》中斡旋。

天花于1738年、1759年两度重创新部，第二次夺去近半人口；1763年肖尼人杀死酋长黑格勒王，同年南卡罗来纳在卡托巴河畔划保留地。独立战争中他们加入殖民者，1780年避往弗吉尼亚，吉尔福德法院之战后返回缩小的土地。

en:
The Caxcan were a partly sedentary, partly nomadic people of the southern Sierra Madre, holding what is now southern Zacatecas and northern Jalisco, with chief towns at Teul, Tlaltenango, Juchipila and Teocaltiche. They lived in competing city-states under elected tlatoani and spoke a Uto-Aztecan tongue often described as an old variant of Nahuatl.

In 1540 their leader Tenamaztle led them into the Mixtón Rebellion beside the Zacatecos; Spanish accounts called the Caxcan the heart of the rising, which was nevertheless crushed in 1542.

They then made peace and, unlike their former allies, fought on the Spanish side through the Chichimeca War of 1550 to 1590, which exposed them to raids by Zacateco and Guachichil bands. Warfare, epidemics and intermarriage over the following colonial centuries gradually merged most Caxcan communities into the mestizo population of Zacatecas and Jalisco.
zh:
卡什坎人是半定居、半游牧族群，活动在西马德雷山脉南段，即今萨卡特卡斯南部与哈利斯科北部，主要城镇有特乌尔、特拉尔特南戈、胡奇皮拉和特奥卡尔蒂切。他们分成相互竞争的城邦，由推举的特拉托阿尼统治，说犹他—阿兹特克语，常视为纳瓦特尔语的古老变体。

1540年首领特尼亚马孙特尔率他们与萨卡特科人加入米斯通起义；西班牙记载称其为起义的心脏，起义1542年被镇压。

此后他们议和，与旧盟友不同，在1550至1590年奇奇梅克战争中站在西班牙一方，因而屡遭萨卡特科和夸奇奇特尔游帮袭击。其后殖民世纪里，战争、疫病和通婚渐把多数卡什坎社区融入萨卡特卡斯与哈利斯科混血人口。

en:
The Cayas were the people of a province on the Cayas River, now the Arkansas, reached by De Soto's expedition in 1541. Tanico held salt-makers who turned salty sand into brine, evaporated it and traded across the Mississippi valley. Tanico later named the Tunica, whose language is regarded as an isolate; linguists count the Cayas among the Tunican chiefdoms of the Mississippian world.

Epidemics and a century and a half of silence followed. When French travelers descended the Mississippi in 1682, the Tunica had left the Arkansas for the Yazoo mouth, old lands held by the Quapaw.

A French mission began among the Tunica around 1700; they prospered as salt and horse middlemen, trading with Caddoan villages to the west. Chickasaw wars and Anglo settlement drove them to the lower Mississippi in 1731 and Louisiana's Red River by the 1790s, where a commissioner counted only about twenty-five Tunica men in 1806.
zh:
卡亚斯是卡亚斯河（今阿肯色河）畔一省，1541年德索托远征队抵达。塔尼科镇居民以制盐为业，把含盐河沙淋成卤水，蒸发为盐销往密西西比河谷。塔尼科一名后来用于图尼卡人，其语言被视为孤立语，语言学家将卡亚斯归入密西西比文化圈图尼卡语酋邦。

西班牙人去后瘟疫接踵，沉寂一个半世纪。1682年法国旅人顺河而下时，图尼卡人已弃阿肯色故地迁亚祖河口，旧地由夸保人散占。

约1700年法国设传教站，图尼卡人做盐马中间商，与西边卡多人贸易致富。奇克索战争与英美移民迫其1731年迁密西西比河下游，1790年代再迁路易斯安那雷德河；1806年美国专员清点，图尼卡男子仅约二十五人。

en:
The Cayubaba are an indigenous people of the Bolivian Amazon, native to the historic Mojos plains of the Beni, west of the Mamoré River and north of Santa Ana del Yacuma, where they lived in large villages of farmers, hunters and fishermen using woven basket traps. Their own Cayubaba tongue is a linguistic isolate, with no demonstrated relatives.

The first European in their territory, the Jesuit Agustín Zapata, counted seven villages in 1693, six of them holding some eighteen hundred people each and one more than two thousand.

In 1704 Father Antonio Garriga gathered them into the Exaltación de la Santa Cruz mission, and the foundations of San Carlos, Concepción and Las Peñas merged the once numerous Cayubaba into the settled mission world of eighteenth-century Mojos, alongside the Movima and other Beni peoples.
zh:
卡尤巴巴人是玻利维亚亚马孙的原住民，世居贝尼地区历史上的莫霍斯平原，在马莫雷河以西、亚库马的圣安娜以北，以大型村落聚居，务农、狩猎、捕鱼，捕鱼用编织的篮篓陷阱。他们本族的卡尤巴巴语是孤立语言，没有确定的亲属语言。

1693年，最先进入其领地的耶稣会士阿古斯丁·萨帕塔清点出七座村庄，其中六座各有约一千八百人，另一座超过两千人。

1704年安东尼奥·加里加神父把他们并入举扬圣十字传教站；此后圣卡洛斯、康塞普西翁、拉斯佩尼亚斯等传教站相继建立，把人口一度众多的卡尤巴巴人纳入18世纪莫霍斯的定居传教世界，与莫维马等贝尼族群共处。

en:
The Cebuano are the largest Visayan subgroup, native to Cebu and spread across Bohol, western Leyte and much of Mindanao. Chinese records of 1225 mention their island port as Suwu, and Visayan tradition traces its rajahnate to Sri Lumay, a half-Malay, half-Tamil settler from Sumatra; the name Sugbu, later rendered Cebu, refers to scorched-earth fires against slave raiders.

Under Rajah Humabon the port traded with Japan, Siam and China, and in 1521 Magellan's expedition arrived; Magellan was killed at the Battle of Mactan by Lapulapu's forces. Humabon's household became the first Filipinos baptized as Christians; the Spanish called these tattooed islanders pintados.

In 1565 Legazpi overthrew Rajah Tupas and made Cebu the first Spanish settlement in the archipelago, and Cebuano auxiliaries marched with the Spaniards at Manila's conquest in 1571. Native and Catholic devotion met in the Sinulog festival of Cebu.
zh:
宿务人是米沙鄢最大支系，原居宿务，后散居保和、莱特西部和棉兰老大片地区。1225年中国文献已将其海岛港口记作束务；米沙鄢传说把拉贾政权归于苏门答腊来的斯里·卢迈，他兼有马来与泰米尔血统，苏格布（后演变为宿务）一名源自抵御掳奴者的焦土之火。

拉者胡马邦治下，港口与日本、暹罗、中国贸易；1521年麦哲伦船队到此，他在麦克坦战役中被拉普拉普部众击杀。胡马邦家眷成为最早受洗的菲律宾基督徒，西班牙人把这些文身岛民称为“平塔多斯”。

1565年莱加斯皮推翻拉者图帕斯，把宿务建成西班牙在群岛的首个据点，宿务辅兵随征1571年马尼拉之役。本土信仰与天主教交融于宿务仙奴诺节。

en: The Chyemdal are an Evenki clan band of the Nepa and Tokma river country in the Katanga taiga, the basin of the Lower Tunguska west of the Lena, living as nomadic reindeer herders and hunters. The Russian advance of the seventeenth century reached this district through its river routes and placed its Evenki clans under Cossack fur-tax administration.
zh: 切姆达尔人是卡坦加泰加林里涅帕河与托克马河一带的鄂温克氏族游群，位于勒拿河以西的下通古斯卡河流域，以游牧养鹿和狩猎为生。17世纪俄国势力沿水路进入这一地区，将当地鄂温克氏族置于哥萨克毛皮税管理之下。

en:
The Cemuhi are the Kanak clans of the north-east coast of Grande Terre in New Caledonia, whose Cèmuhî language, also called Wagap after the coastal district of that name, is spoken around Touho, Koné and Poindimié in the Paici-Camuki customary area. With Paicî it forms the central-northern New Caledonian group, descended from the Austronesian speech brought by Lapita settlers after 1100 BC.

Cèmuhî is a tone language in which three pitch registers distinguish words otherwise sounded alike, giving everyday speech something of the melodic precision of a chant. Society turned on clans and hereditary chiefs, taro irrigation in steep valleys and fishing from outrigger canoes, while the chief's great house and rooftop carving linked the living to the ancestors.

James Cook noted the coast in 1774, yet the steep mountains behind it kept Cemuhi villages effectively beyond European reach through 1837.
zh:
塞穆希人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛东北沿海的卡纳克氏族，其塞穆希语又称瓦加普语（得名于沿海瓦加普地区），通行于帕伊西-卡穆基习俗区内的图奥、科内和普安迪米耶一带。它与派西语共同组成新喀里多尼亚语中北部语组，是公元前1100年后拉皮塔定居者带来的南岛语后裔。

塞穆希语是声调语言，三个音高层级可区分同音词，日常言语带着几分吟唱般精准的旋律。社会以氏族和世袭酋长为核心，在陡峭山谷灌溉芋头，驾舷外架独木舟出海捕鱼；酋长大屋及屋顶雕饰连接生者与祖先。

詹姆斯·库克1774年记录了格朗德特尔岛海岸，但背后的崇山峻岭使塞穆希村落实质上处于欧洲人势力之外，直至1837年。

en:
The Chaima are an Indigenous people of eastern Venezuela, whose villages once spread across later Monagas, Anzoátegui and Sucre, around Maturín and the Cumaná coast. They spoke Chaima, a Cariban tongue of the Itoto Majun group related to Cumanagoto and close to Pemón and Yukpa.

After the Spanish conquest many were gathered into Capuchin missions, notably around Caripe, and by the late eighteenth century nearly all the roughly fifteen thousand Indians in the Capuchin missions of northeastern Venezuela were Chaima; one of their number is said to have led a multi-tribal rising against the Spaniards.

Alexander von Humboldt, visiting around 1800, described their stature and customs. Chaima remained in everyday use in the early nineteenth century, one of the three most spoken Indigenous languages of Cumaná and Barcelona, but then declined without surviving as a community language.
zh:
柴马人是委内瑞拉东部原住民，村落曾分布在后来的莫纳加斯、安索阿特吉、苏克雷三州，即马图林与库马纳海岸一带。其柴马语属加勒比语系伊托托—马洪语群，与库马纳戈托语有亲缘，近于佩蒙语、尤克帕语。

西班牙征服后，许多柴马人被并入嘉布遣会传教区，尤以卡里佩一带为多；18世纪末，委内瑞拉东北部嘉布遣会传教区里约一万五千名印第安人几乎全是柴马人，据说一位柴马人曾率多部起兵反抗西班牙人。

亚历山大·冯·洪堡约1800年到访，记述了他们的身材与风俗。19世纪初柴马语仍是日常用语，曾是库马纳和巴塞罗那使用最广的三种原住民语言之一，此后逐渐衰落，未能作为社群语言留存。

en:
Sa'ktcihuma, rendered Chakchiuma by chroniclers, means red crawfish in Western Muskogean, after their crawfish totem. Late-seventeenth-century French explorers called them a Chicacha nation, sharing Chickasaw and Choctaw origins, in the upper Yazoo country of present-day Mississippi, where Bienville counted four hundred families in 1702.

Earlier, De Soto, wintering among the Chickasaw, had sent a detachment against them. In 1700 Carolina slave traders prompted a Quapaw raid to seize them for sale, but the attack failed.

They fought for the French in the Yazoo War, but chronic warfare cut them to sixty families by 1735, and around 1739 the enraged Chickasaw and Choctaw destroyed their villages, killing warriors and even the village animals. Survivors joined the two neighboring nations: those with the Choctaw formed their own Crawfish clan, and a trader in 1757 found others settled in Chickasaw towns.
zh:
萨克奇胡马（史籍作 Chakchiuma）在西马斯科吉语中意为“红螯虾”，取自螯虾图腾。17世纪末法国探险者称其为奇克察人的一支，与奇克索、乔克托人同源，住在今密西西比亚祖河上游；1702年比安维尔数出四百户。

他们更早见于记载：德索托在奇克索人处过冬时曾派兵攻打。1700年卡罗来纳奴隶贩子唆使夸保人来袭，企图掳贩，却遭失败。

亚祖战争中他们站在法国一方，连年征战到1735年只剩六十户；约1739年，被激怒的奇克索、乔克托人摧毁其村落，杀尽战士连牲畜也不放过。幸存者并入两个邻族：入乔克托的一支组成螯虾氏族，1757年商人发现另一些人定居奇克索村镇。

en:
The Chakma, or Changhma, largest hill people of the Chittagong Hill Tracts, live around Kaptai, Ramu and the southeastern Bengal ridges, with Rakhine kin called Daingnet. They trace to Tibeto-Burman Sak groups moving from upper Myanmar to the Arakan hills from around the tenth century, then the Chittagong hills, where a Chakma raja ruled thirty-one clans.

A historical shift gave them the Indo-Aryan Chakma tongue, close to Chittagonian and written in its own Brahmi-derived script; their life rested on jhum cultivation and Theravada Buddhism.

When Mughal governor Shaista Khan took lowland Chittagong in 1666 the hill kingdom stayed free, and treaties in 1713 and 1715 recognized its internal autonomy in return for tribute. The East India Company inherited the claim in 1761, fought raja Sher Doulat Khan and his son Jan Baksh Khan from 1777 to 1787, then signed a Calcutta treaty leaving the raja to rule his hills as a tributary.
zh:
查克马人又称昌马人，是吉大港山区最大山地民族，住在卡普泰、拉穆及孟加拉东南山岭；若开亲缘群体称代内人。先祖为藏缅语系萨克人，约10世纪起从上缅甸迁入若开山区，再进吉大港山地，后由查克马拉杰统辖三十一氏族。

后来语言转换使他们改说印度—雅利安查克马语，近吉大港方言，用源自婆罗米文的自有文字；生计靠朱姆轮耕，信上座部佛教。

1666年莫卧儿总督沙伊斯塔汗取吉大港平原，山地王国仍保持自由，1713、1715年条约承认其内部自治，条件是纳贡。东印度公司1761年继承宗主权，1777—1787年与拉杰谢尔·道拉特·汗及其子詹·巴克什·汗交战，后在加尔各答签约，保留拉杰纳贡治山之权。

en:
The Chalaghawtha, or Chillicothe, were one of five Shawnee divisions, traditionally supplying the Shawnee confederacy's political leadership. The chief's village shared the name, and each forced move produced a new town called Chillicothe.

From about 1734 the Lower Shawnee Town on the Ohio River grew into a trading hub of over 1,200 people before being abandoned in 1758. On the Scioto, Tecumseh was likely born in a Chillicothe in 1768, and Virginia militia imposed a border settlement after Dunmore's War of 1774.

The Old Chillicothe on the Little Miami, home of war chief Blackfish, held Daniel Boone captive for months in 1778; Blackfish died of a wound in 1779 and George Rogers Clark burned it in 1780. Successive Chillicothes later rose on the Great Miami, St. Mary's and Maumee as the Shawnee retreated before American expansion.
zh:
查拉高萨人英文文献多作奇利科西，是肖尼人五个分支之一，传统上为松散的肖尼联盟提供政治领袖。首领所在村庄也叫奇利科西，每次被迫迁徙，新城仍沿用此名。

约1734年起，俄亥俄河畔下肖尼镇发展成逾一千二百人的贸易重镇，1758年弃守。赛欧托河畔的奇利科西可能是特库姆塞1768年出生地；1774年邓莫尔战争后，弗吉尼亚民兵迫使肖尼人划界。

小迈阿密河畔旧奇利科西是战将黑鱼据点，1778年丹尼尔·布恩被掳村中数月；1779年黑鱼伤重而死，1780年乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克焚镇。随着肖尼人在美国扩张前不断后撤，奇利科西又相继出现于大迈阿密河、圣玛丽斯河和莫米河畔。

en:
The Cham are an Austronesian seafaring people of the central Vietnamese coast, heirs of the Sa Huỳnh culture whose river-mouth settlements reach back to around the first millennium BCE. From the second century CE they built Champa, a league of Indianized port principalities which grew wealthy on the trade routes linking India and China and reached their height in the ninth and tenth centuries.

Hinduism shaped Cham art and its red-brick sanctuaries such as Mỹ Sơn. Contacts with Muslim traders from the eleventh century slowly prepared the conversion that made the ruling dynasty Muslim by the seventeenth century.

In 1337 the Cham held the coastal strip between Đại Việt and the Khmer, but the Vietnamese Nam Tiến pressed southward: Lê Thánh Tông sacked Vijaya in 1471, ending Champa's power, while Panduranga survived as a tributary until the Nguyễn emperor Minh Mạng annexed it in 1832. Cham refugees settled in Cambodia and the Mekong Delta, where descendants still speak Cham and keep matrilineal customs.
zh:
占人是越南中部沿海的南岛语系航海民族，是沙萤文化的继承者，河口定居点可追溯到公元前一千纪左右。从公元2世纪起，他们建立占婆，由印度化港口城邦组成联盟，靠连接印度与中国的商路致富，在9至10世纪达到鼎盛。

印度教塑造了占人的艺术和美山等地的红砖神庙。11世纪起与穆斯林商人的接触为后来的改宗埋下伏笔，到17世纪占人王朝已皈依伊斯兰教。

1337年时，占人据有夹在大越与高棉之间的沿海地带，但越南人的南进不断南下：1471年黎圣宗攻陷毗阇耶，终结了占婆的强势，宾童龙作为附庸存续到1832年，被阮朝明命帝吞并。占人难民流落柬埔寨和湄公河三角洲，后人仍说占语，保留母系习俗。

en:
The Chamoru are the Austronesian people of the Mariana Islands, whose ancestors came from island Southeast Asia around 1500 BC. They built on latte rows and sailed proas called flying canoes, in ranked matrilineal clans under an ancestor-spirit cult. Their tongue is Malayo-Polynesian, not Oceanic.

Magellan reached Guam in 1521, but permanent colonization waited until 1668, when the Jesuit San Vitores opened a mission among about 180 autonomous villages. Chief Hurao besieged Hagåtña in 1670, and in 1672 chief Matå'pang killed San Vitores at Tumon after his daughter's baptism, starting war.

Reprisals burned villages and another rebellion besieged Hagåtña, and Governor Salas forced the people into seven towns. Campaigns on Rota, Saipan and Tinian ended by 1699 with the last northern islanders moved to Guam. War, disease and resettlement broke the old order; by 1837 survivors were Catholic subjects of Spain, their speech full of Spanish loanwords.
zh:
查莫罗人是马里亚纳群岛南岛原住民，祖先约公元前1500年自东南亚海岛地区迁入。他们在拉提石柱上建房，驾飞行独木舟式外架舟，社会为等级化母系氏族，崇祖先神灵；其语属马来—波利尼西亚语族，非大洋洲语族。

麦哲伦1521年抵达关岛，永久殖民迟至1668年，耶稣会士圣维托雷斯在约180个自治村落中建立传教站。1670年酋长胡劳围攻阿加尼亚，1672年酋长马塔庞因女儿受洗在杜梦杀圣维托雷斯，战火遂起。

西班牙人纵火报复，起义者再围阿加尼亚，总督萨拉斯集村并民，归入七镇。罗塔、塞班、天宁战事结束，到1699年最后的北方岛民被迁往关岛。战乱、疫病、迁村瓦解旧秩序；到1837年幸存者已成西班牙天主教臣民，语言满是西语借词。

en:
The Champenois are the people of Champagne, the plains between Paris and the Holy Roman Empire, centred on Troyes, Reims and the Marne valley. Their tongue is an Oïl Romance language with dialects from Ardennais to Langrois, and it holds a real literary heritage: the trouvere Theobald the Songwriter, count of Champagne and king of Navarre, composed in it.

The County of Champagne became a commercial wonder of medieval Europe through its trade fairs, which drew merchants from Flanders, the Rhine, Italy and England and made Troyes a centre of finance and a literary court graced by Chretien de Troyes. The country was also the cradle of the Cistercian order at Clairvaux and sent knights to every crusade between 1095 and 1270.

From 1234 its counts ruled Navarre too, and the marriage of Queen Joan I of Navarre to Philip IV of France carried the county into the French royal domain in the early fourteenth century. After that Parisian French slowly overshadowed the regional speech.
zh:
香槟人生活在巴黎与神圣罗马帝国之间的平原上，以特鲁瓦、兰斯和马恩河谷为中心。他们的香槟语属奥依罗曼语，方言北起阿登、东南至朗格勒，并拥有真正的文学传统：身兼香槟伯爵与纳瓦拉国王的“歌手”蒂博等中世纪特罗维尔诗人便用它写作。

凭借香槟集市，香槟伯国成为中世纪欧洲的商业奇迹，佛兰德斯、莱茵、意大利和英格兰的商人纷至沓来，特鲁瓦既是金融中心，也是克雷蒂安·德·特鲁瓦活跃的文学宫廷。这里还是明谷修道院所在地、西多会的摇篮，1095至1270年间每次十字军都有香槟骑士参加。

1234年起香槟伯爵同时统治纳瓦拉；纳瓦拉女王胡安娜一世与法王腓力四世联姻，伯国遂于14世纪初并入法兰西王室领地，此后巴黎法语逐渐盖过地方方言。

en:
The Chaná were the southern branch of the Chaná-Timbú peoples, riverine groups who in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries occupied the floodlands and islands of the Paraná, from its meeting with the Paraguay to the Río de la Plata and the lower Uruguay. Related bands included the Mbegua, Timbú and Mepene, among others; their riverine ceramic tradition, shaped by Guaraní influences after about 1200, is known as the Goya-Malabrigo culture.

They were semi-nomadic hunters, fishers and gatherers who also planted small plots of corn and manioc, spending much of their lives in dugout canoes and camping along the waterways. Their guttural languages are usually grouped with the Charrúa tongues; the priest Dámaso Larrañaga recorded Chaná in 1823.

Early contact brought smallpox, encomienda levies and raids. During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the Chaná merged or scattered among the Guaraní and Charrúa, disappearing as a distinct people.
zh:
查纳人是查纳-廷布族群集团南缘的一支；16至17世纪，这批滨水民族占据巴拉那河的滩地与岛屿，范围从巴拉那河与巴拉圭河交汇处延伸到拉普拉塔河和乌拉圭河下游。相近支系包括姆贝瓜、廷布、梅佩内等；其制陶传统约1200年后受瓜拉尼人影响，考古学界称之为戈亚-马拉布里戈文化。

他们半游牧，以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，也小片种植玉米、木薯等作物，多栖身独木舟，在水道边扎营。其语言喉音浓重，通常归入查鲁亚语群；神父达马索·拉腊尼亚加曾于1823年记录查纳语。

早期接触带来天花、委托监护征发和军事征伐。16至17世纪间，查纳人或与瓜拉尼人、查鲁亚人融合，或四散流离，不再作为独立民族存在。

en:
The Chancay were the people of a string of river valleys on the central Peruvian coast, from the Fortaleza to the Lurin, their heartland in the Chancay and Chillon valleys. Their civilization arose after the Wari Empire collapsed around 1000 and grew into a centralized state ruled by curacas, whose adobe towns clustered around pyramid mounds.

Farmers watered the desert with reservoirs and canals, fishermen sailed reed canoes, and traders carried Chancay goods into the highlands. They were the first Peruvian culture to organize mass production: specialist workshops turned out mould-made black-on-cream pottery, including standing burial figurines, and painted textiles woven for the dead.

The southern Chancay valleys fell to the Chimu in the early fifteenth century, and by about 1450 Inca armies had occupied the whole region, bringing the independent Chancay state to an end.
zh:
钱凯人居住在秘鲁中部沿海一连串河谷中，北起福塔莱萨河，南至卢林河，核心在钱凯河谷与奇永河谷。其文明约在1000年瓦里帝国崩溃后兴起，发展成酋长统治的集权国家，土坯城镇簇拥着金字塔形土丘。

农民用蓄水池和灌渠开垦荒漠，渔民驾芦苇舟，商人把钱凯货物运往高原等地。他们是第一个实现大规模生产的秘鲁文化：专业作坊大量出产模制黑彩奶白陶器，包括用于墓葬的立式小塑像，以及为死者织造的彩绘织物。

15世纪初，钱凯南部河谷被奇穆征服；到1450年前后，印加军队占领整个地区，独立的钱凯邦国就此终结。

en:
The Chángdé culture belongs to north-western Hunan, on the west shore of Dongting Lake and the lower Yuan River, a region known in antiquity as Wuling. Rice farming here is ancient, for Pengtoushan has yielded the earliest known settled rice village in China, dating back some 8,000 years.

A Han county, Linyuan, was established in the second century BCE; from it the Wuling commandery watched the mountain tribes of western Hunan. The Tang seat was Langzhou, and the name Changde dates from 1117, when the Song created Changde county. Long the gateway to Guizhou and Sichuan, its river markets handled the rice, timber and tung oil of the Yuan basin.

Its speech is a Hunan branch of Southwestern Mandarin, bordering the Xiang dialects, and under the Qing the prefecture passed from Huguang to the new province of Hunan in the 1660s.
zh:
常德文化分布在湖南西北部、洞庭湖滨与沅水下游，古属武陵。这里种稻历史极早，彭头山遗址发现了中国已知最早的定居稻作村落，距今约八千年。

公元前2世纪，汉朝在此设临沅县，武陵郡借此统辖湘西山地诸部；唐代这里是朗州治所，1117年宋朝置常德县，常德之名由此确立。这里长期是通往贵州、四川的门户，沿河市镇集散沅水流域的稻米、木材与桐油。

常德话属于西南官话的湖南分支，与湘语相邻；清代17世纪60年代湖广分省，常德府划归新置的湖南省。

en:
The Changos, also called Camanchacos, were maritime peoples of the desert Pacific coast from Camaná in Peru to northern Chile. Their way of life reached back to the eight-thousand-year-old Chinchorro fishing tradition, famous for its mummies. Chango was not a tribe but a loose Spanish label, used from the mid-seventeenth century for independent coastal communities with shared customs; the Aymara called them Camanchacos after the coastal fog.

They knew no agriculture: families lived off fish and shellfish, salted fish as charqui, and hunted seals for skins stretched over wooden frames into fishing rafts, trading dried fish, guano and shells inland for maize and wool.

Fishing villages stood on the Collasuyo coast when Tiwanaku expanded in the ninth century. Organized in autonomous family bands, they kept much of their old way of life under Inca and Spanish rule; in 1835 Alcide d'Orbigny found Chango raftsmen off Cobija carrying silver to ships.
zh:
昌戈人又称卡曼查科人，是沙漠太平洋沿岸的海洋族群，分布从秘鲁南部的卡马纳延伸到智利北部。其生计可追溯到有八千年历史、以木乃伊闻名的新克罗渔猎传统。昌戈并非一个部落，而是西班牙人自17世纪中叶起对沿海习俗相近、互不统属的社区的笼统称呼；艾马拉人因沿海浓雾称他们为卡曼查科人。

他们不懂农业：家族村落以鱼类和贝类为生，用盐腌鱼成鱼干，捕猎海狮取皮，把皮绷在木架上制成捕鱼筏子，再以鱼干、鸟粪和贝壳向内地交换玉米和羊毛。

9世纪蒂亚瓦纳科扩张时，科利亚苏约沿海已有渔村。他们以自治家族群为单位，在印加和西班牙统治下保留大量旧有生活方式；1835年，阿尔西德·道比尼仍在科维哈近海看到昌戈筏工驾皮筏运银上商船。

en:
The Changpa, whose name means northerners in Tibetan, are the semi-nomadic pastoralists of the Changtang, a high plateau running from Rutok in western Tibet into south-eastern Ladakh. Their country was once part of Zhangzhung, the Bon kingdom of western Tibet, until it was absorbed by the expanding Tibetan Empire around 634.

They herd yaks, sheep and cashmere goats, whose pashmina wool they traded westward to the weavers of Kashmir, and pitch black tents along seasonal migration routes. In Ladakh the nomadic Phalpa move between the Hanle valley and Lato, while the settled Fangpa keep six permanent villages. They speak Changskhat, a dialect of Tibetan, and follow Tibetan Buddhism.
zh:
羌巴人在藏语中意为“北方人”，是羌塘高原的半游牧牧民；羌塘是一片高寒高原，西起西藏西部的日土，延伸至拉达克东南部。其故土曾是西藏西部信奉苯教的象雄王国的一部分，约634年被扩张中的吐蕃帝国吞并。

羌巴人牧养牦牛、绵羊和绒山羊，所产帕什米纳羊绒向西销往克什米尔织工；他们沿季节转场路线支起黑色帐篷。在拉达克，游牧的帕尔巴人往来于汉勒河谷与拉托之间，定居的方帕人保有六个固定村落。他们讲藏语方言昌斯喀特语，信奉藏传佛教。

en:
The Chanka were a warlike people of the central Peruvian Andes, related to the Quechua. Their chiefdoms grew in the Andahuaylas valley and Ayacucho highlands after they migrated from Castrovirreina, and their raids are thought to have helped bring down the Wari state. Their confederation united the Hanan, Urin and Villca under two paramount chiefs; chronicles describe a rich lordship at its height between 1200 and 1438.

Farmers and llama herders, they worshipped a puma deity, painted faces, carried ancestral mummies into battle and made cups from the skulls of slain enemies.

Inca tradition claims the Urin Chanka were subdued around 1230, Mayta Cápac crossing the Apurímac by a hanging bridge; after 1430 the Hanan Chanka besieged Cusco and were crushed at Yawarpampa by the prince Cusi Yupanqui, who took the name Pachacuti. In 1532 the Chanka joined Pizarro's auxiliaries against the Inca; colonial rule brought forced labour.
zh:
昌卡人是秘鲁中部安第斯山区的好战民族，与克丘亚人相近；他们从卡斯特罗维雷纳迁徙到安达韦拉斯河谷和阿亚库乔高原，其袭扰被认为促成了瓦里政权的崩溃。昌卡联盟把上昌卡、下昌卡与维尔卡诸部联合起来，由两位大酋长统辖；史书载1200—1438年间其酋邦富庶强盛。

他们务农并放牧羊驼，崇拜美洲狮神，作战时涂面、肩扛祖先木乃伊，还用被杀敌人的头骨制成饮器。

印卡传说称下昌卡人约1230年被迈塔·卡帕克经吊桥渡过阿普里马克河征服；1430年后，上昌卡人围攻库斯科，在亚瓦尔潘帕被王子库西·尤潘基击溃，后者取名帕查库特克。1532年，昌卡人加入皮萨罗的盟军攻打印卡，殖民统治却带来劳役。

en:
The Chaoui are the Zenata Amazigh people of the Aurès massif in northeastern Algeria, highland shepherds whose name Shawi means shepherd and who speak Tachawit, a Zenati variety of Tamazight.

The Aurès long served as a Berber redoubt: its Christian kingdom, founded by King Masties in the 480s, defied Vandals and Byzantines. When the Arabs conquered the Maghreb the Aurès led the last resistance; after Kusaila fell at Mamma in 690, the Jerawa queen Dihya, known to the Arabs as al-Kahina, united the tribes, won the Battle of Meskiana and ruled as far as Ghadames until she was slain in 703.

In the Islamic era the Zenata clans of the region listed by Ibn Khaldun supplied warriors to the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, while high valleys around Baghai and Constantine kept Berber speech and tribal life through Hafsid and Ottoman centuries.
zh:
沙维亚人是阿尔及利亚东北部奥雷斯山区的泽纳塔系阿马齐格人，以高山放牧为生，沙维一词意为牧人，操塔马齐格特语的泽纳提分支塔沙维特方言。

奥雷斯向来是柏柏尔人的堡垒：480年代马斯提斯王建起基督教王国，抗拒汪达尔、拜占庭。阿拉伯人征服马格里布时，奥雷斯扛起最后的抵抗：690年库赛拉在马马战役阵亡后，杰拉瓦女王迪希亚（阿拉伯人称卡希娜）联合诸部，赢得梅斯基亚纳战役，政权延伸至古达米斯，直至703年战死。

伊斯兰时代，伊本·赫勒敦记载的当地泽纳塔诸部为特莱姆森的扎扬王朝提供战士，巴加伊、君士坦丁一带的高山河谷则在哈夫斯与奥斯曼的数百年间始终保留柏柏尔语言和部落生活。

en:
The Teochew are Han Chinese of the Chaoshan plain, easternmost Guangdong, around Chaozhou, Jieyang and Chaoyang on the lower Han River, speaking Teochew, a conservative Southern Min dialect. Barely touched by the Qin conquest of 214 BC, the coast remained remote Yue country; in 591 the Sui named the prefecture Chaozhou.

Northern families drifted in through Fujian, many sojourning in Putian before entering between the Tang and Ming, giving Teochew its close kinship with Hokkien. In 819 the exiled writer Han Yu governed the prefecture briefly and promoted schools; the city river was later named Han River after him.

Under the Song and Ming the region became a crowded rice country of walled towns, sending traders and coolies overseas from the eighteenth century; by 1819 Teochew planters were already opening gambier estates in Singapore, and Teochew merchants became the largest Chinese group in Siam.
zh:
潮州人是广东最东端潮汕平原上的汉族民系，聚居韩江下游潮州、揭阳、潮阳一带，操闽南语中保守的潮州话。公元前214年秦征岭南时，这片海岸尚属化外，长期是偏远越地；591年隋朝定名潮州。

数百年来北方世家经福建陆续南下，许多人在莆田短暂落脚后，于唐至明代间迁入本区，潮州话因此与闽南语关系极近。819年，被贬的文学家韩愈出任潮州刺史，任内兴学教士，穿城而过的江后来得名韩江。

宋明时期这里发展为城镇林立、人烟稠密的稻米之乡；18世纪起不断有商人与苦力出洋，1819年潮州种植者已在新加坡开辟甘蜜园，潮州商人更成为暹罗最大的华人群体。

en:
The Charca or Charka were a highland people of the central Bolivian Andes, spread across what is now Chuquisaca and northern Potosí; the Charka kingdom of Kollasuyu bound them with neighbours such as the Chuwi and Qhara Qhara. From the east came repeated Ava Guaraní raids, by people they called Chiriguano.

In the late fifteenth century Inca Túpac Yupanqui's armies invaded; after several defeats their leader Copacatiraca persuaded them to submit, and Charca warriors served in the Inca armies. The Portuguese Aleixo Garcia reached them around 1525, and in 1538 they allied with Gonzalo Pizarro's Spaniards. La Plata, later Sucre, was founded on their land in 1540 and gave its name to the Audiencia of Charcas.
zh:
查克拉人即史籍中的查尔卡斯人，是玻利维亚安第斯中部的高原族群，分布在今丘基萨卡、波托西北部等地；科利亚苏尤的查克拉王国将其与丘维、卡拉卡拉等邻近族群联合。东方不断有阿瓦·瓜拉尼人来袭，他们称后者为奇里瓜诺人。

15世纪末，印加王图帕克·尤潘基的军队入侵，连战连败后，首领科帕卡蒂拉卡说服族人归降，查尔卡斯战士随即加入印加军队。葡萄牙人阿莱舒·加西亚约1525年抵达此地；1538年他们与贡萨洛·皮萨罗的西班牙人结盟。1540年，拉普拉塔城（后名苏克雷）在其土地上建立，查尔卡斯检审庭即得名于此。

en:
The Charrúa were semi-nomadic hunter-gatherers of the grasslands around the Río de la Plata, ranging in the sixteenth century between the Paraná and Uruguay rivers and later centred on Uruguay. They summered on the coast fishing, wintered inland hunting deer and rhea with bolas, and once cattle and horses spread across the pampas, livestock raids called malones became central to their life.

Their encounter with Europeans was violent from the start, chroniclers blaming them for the killing of Juan Díaz de Solís in 1515; with the Chaná they long resisted colonial settlement. In the eighteenth century they warred against the Guaraní missions and mingled with the Minuane and others, until writers applied Charrúa to the confederacy.

Their independent life ended in 1831, when Fructuoso Rivera's army carried out the Massacre of Salsipuedes, killing most and selling survivors into service; the remnant dispersed and their language died with them.
zh:
查鲁亚人是拉普拉塔河一带草原上的半游牧狩猎采集族群，16世纪时活动在巴拉那河与乌拉圭河之间，后以乌拉圭为中心。他们夏天到海岸捕鱼，冬天深入内陆，用流星锤猎鹿与美洲鸵鸟；等牛马在潘帕斯草原扩散后，劫掠牲畜的马隆突袭成了他们生活的核心。

他们与欧洲人一接触就兵戎相见，编年史家把1515年胡安·迪亚斯·德索利斯之死记在他们头上；他们又与查纳人联手，长期抵抗殖民定居。18世纪，他们与瓜拉尼传教区交战，并与米努安等族群通婚融合，文献遂把整群部族笼统称为查鲁亚。

1831年，弗鲁克图奥索·里维拉的军队发动萨尔西普埃德斯屠杀，大部分人遇害，幸存者被卖为仆役，残部四散，查鲁亚语也随之消亡。

en:
The Chatot, now more often called Chacato, were a Muskogean-speaking people of the Florida panhandle, occupying the upper Chipola and Apalachicola river basins in the seventeenth century.

The Spanish founded two missions among their villages in 1674, but pressure to adopt full Christian practice sparked a rebellion in which converts tried to kill a missionary; many rebels fled to the Tawasa or joined the Spanish-hostile Chiscas, while the rest resettled in Apalachee Province missions. When Carolinian raiders and Native allies destroyed the Apalachee missions in 1704, surviving Chatot moved west with the Apalachee and settled around Pensacola and Mobile bays, some later absorbed into the Choctaw.

After West Florida passed to Great Britain in 1763, others crossed into Louisiana. Spanish writers called them chato, flat-nosed, perhaps for artificial cranial deformation, and the Choctawhatchee River and Bay may preserve their name.
zh:
查托特人今多称查卡托人，是佛罗里达狭地操穆斯科格语的族群，17世纪占据奇波拉河与阿巴拉契科拉河上游盆地。

1674年西班牙人在其村庄建两座传教站，但强迫遵行基督教仪轨激起叛乱，信徒企图杀死一名传教士；许多叛乱者逃往塔瓦萨人处或投奔与西班牙为敌的奇斯卡人，其余迁入阿巴拉契省传教站。1704年，卡罗来纳袭击者与印第安盟友摧毁阿巴拉契传教区，幸存者随阿巴拉契人西迁，定居彭萨科拉湾、莫比尔湾一带，部分后来并入乔克托人。

1763年西佛罗里达归英后，另一些人渡河西入路易斯安那。西班牙人称他们chato，意为扁鼻，或源于人工改形头颅之俗；乔克托哈奇河与海湾或即保存其族名。

en:
Tsamosan, also called Olympic Salish, is a Salishan branch of western Washington's Southwestern Coast Salish peoples — the Chehalis, Quinault and Cowlitz — villages lining Grays Harbor, Willapa Bay and the Chehalis River around the Olympic Peninsula.

They had no tribes in the political sense: independent villages linked by language and marriage lived on salmon, shellfish and game in cedar-plank longhouses, and the name Chehalis itself means sand, from the main Lower Chehalis village at present-day Westport. Lower Chehalis words also entered the Chinook Jargon.

The sea captain Robert Gray entered Grays Harbor in 1792, the first recorded European contact; after the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Vancouver, the Chehalis became fur-trade middlemen. Malaria epidemics in the 1830s, above all in 1830, emptied villages and merged surviving groups such as the Willapa Bay Lower Chehalis and Lower Chinook.
zh:
察莫萨又称奥林匹克萨利什语，属萨利什语系，为华盛顿州西南海岸萨利什诸族——切哈利斯人、奎诺尔特人和考利茨人——使用；村落分布于奥林匹克半岛周边格雷斯港、威拉帕湾和切哈利斯河沿岸。

他们没有政治意义上的部落，只有以语言和婚姻相联的独立村落，住雪松木板长屋，以鲑鱼、贝类和猎物为生；“切哈利斯”意为沙子，得名于今韦斯特波特的下切哈利斯主村。下切哈利斯语词汇也进入奇努克混合语。

1792年船长罗伯特·格雷驶入格雷斯港，为首次有记载的欧洲接触；哈德逊湾公司建温哥华堡后，切哈利斯人成为毛皮贸易中介。19世纪30年代疟疾，1830年尤烈，整村人口灭绝，幸存者彼此合并，如威拉帕湾的下切哈利斯人与下奇努克人。

en:
The Cheke Holo are an Oceanic-speaking people of Santa Isabel, longest of the Solomon Islands. Their language, also called Maringe, is spoken chiefly in the island's east in two main dialects, Maringe and Hograno; with Bughotu it ranks among the island's principal languages and serves as a local trade tongue.

Santa Isabel was the scene of the first European landing in the Solomon archipelago. On 7 February 1568 the Spanish expedition of Álvaro de Mendaña went ashore here and charted the island as Santa Isabel de la Estrella. They built a settlement and a surveying brigantine, but hunger, sickness and conflict with islanders drove them to abandon the post for Guadalcanal.
zh:
切克霍洛人是所罗门群岛最长岛屿圣伊莎贝尔岛上说大洋洲语的族群。其语言又称马林格语，主要通行于岛东部，下分马林格和霍格拉诺两大方言；它与布戈图语同为岛上主要语言，充当当地贸易通用语。

圣伊莎贝尔岛是欧洲人在所罗门群岛登陆的第一站。1568年2月7日，阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚率西班牙探险队在此上岸，将该岛标为圣伊莎贝尔·德拉埃斯特雷利亚。西班牙人建起定居点和测量用双桅船，但饥饿、疾病及与岛民的冲突迫使他们放弃据点，撤往瓜达尔卡纳尔岛。

en:
The Chelkans, who call themselves Chalkandu, are a small Turkic people of the northeastern Altai taiga, speaking a Northern Altai tongue. They took shape from Turkic clans mingling with Ket, Samoyedic and other indigenous Siberian hunters, a process already under way when the Yenisei Kyrgyz dominated the region.

From the thirteenth to the eighteenth century the area passed under Mongol and later Dzungar rule, and in 1756 the Chelkans submitted to the Russian Empire together with the other Altai peoples.

Hunters rather than herders, they lived by chasing fur game in the mountain forests, adding cedar-nut gathering in the nineteenth century, and made their homes in polygonal log and bark yurts with conical bark roofs. Russian Orthodoxy gradually spread among them, but older shamanic practices remained alive.
zh:
切尔坎人自称“恰勒坎杜”，是阿尔泰东北部泰加林中的小型突厥语族群，讲一种北阿尔泰语。他们由突厥氏族与克特、萨莫耶德等西伯利亚土著狩猎群体混合而成，早在叶尼塞黠戛斯人称雄该地区时这一融合过程已经开始。

13至18世纪，这一带先后处于蒙古和后来准噶尔的统治之下，1756年切尔坎人与其他阿尔泰民族一同归附俄罗斯帝国。

他们以狩猎而非畜牧为生，在山林中猎取毛皮兽，19世纪又增加了采集雪松籽的营生，住房是多边形木架树皮屋、顶覆锥形树皮盖。俄罗斯东正教逐渐在他们中传播，但更古老的萨满习俗仍然留存。

en:
The Giduwa, or Kituwa, are the Cherokee of the Middle Towns of the upper Little Tennessee and Tuckasegee in western North Carolina, speaking the Kituwah dialect of the Iroquoian Cherokee language. They call themselves Anigiduwagi, People from Kituwa, after their mother town, where a mound raised about 1000 marks the townhouse and its sacred fire.

Nikwasi, the Star Place on the Little Tennessee, was another of the seven mother towns. The mountain Cherokee met South Carolina traders in treaty at Nikwasi in 1727, but their towns were repeatedly burned.

James Grant's expedition razed Nikwasi in 1761 during the war between Britain and the Cherokee, and Rutherford's militia destroyed it in 1776. Each time they rebuilt, until in 1819 the United States forced them to cede the valley and withdraw into the Qualla Boundary, where families avoiding the 1830s removals kept the Giduwa dialect alive.
zh:
基杜瓦人（又称基图瓦人）是切罗基人的中城镇之民，聚居北卡罗来纳西部小田纳西河上游与塔卡塞吉河的山地，说易洛魁语系切罗基语基图瓦方言。他们自称阿尼基杜瓦吉，意为“来自基图瓦的人”；基图瓦是他们的母城，约1000年的土墩标示着公共议事屋与圣火。

小田纳西河畔意为“星辰之地”的尼夸西是七大母城之一。山地切罗基人1727年在尼夸西与南卡罗来纳贸易商缔约，城镇却屡遭兵燹。

1761年英国与切罗基交战期间，詹姆斯·格兰特的远征军夷平尼夸西，1776年格里菲思·拉瑟福德的民兵毁城。人们每次都重建家园，直到1819年美国迫使他们割让河谷、退入夸拉边界；在19世纪30年代强制迁徙中留下来的家族，便在那里延续基杜瓦方言。

en:
The Chewa, also called Mang'anja, are a Bantu people of central and southern Malawi and the neighbouring borderlands of Zambia and Mozambique, main surviving branch of the Maravi peoples. Oral tradition traces them to Malambo in Luba country of the Congo, then through northern Zambia into the Malawi highlands.

The first Chewa kingdom arose around 1480; by the sixteenth century its two leading clans, the Banda at Mankhamba and the Phiri at Manthimba, ruled separately, before Maravi unification in the following century. Portuguese traders and missionaries recorded contacts with Maravi chiefs from 1608 to 1667, never reaching the state's heartland.

By 1750 Maravi dynasties ruled central Malawi; the Chewa kept their identity through language, mphini tattoos and the Nyau secret brotherhoods, whose masked Gule Wamkulu dances mark male initiation. Chewa society is matrilineal: land and lineage pass through the mother, guarded by her brothers.
zh:
切瓦人又称曼甘贾人，是班图人一支，居住在马拉维中南部及赞比亚、莫桑比克边境，为马拉维诸族最主要的后裔。口传传统称他们起源于刚果卢巴地区的马兰博，经赞比亚北部迁入马拉维高地。

第一个切瓦王国约1480年建立；16世纪时，班达氏族据曼坎巴、菲里氏族据曼廷巴，各治一方，下一世纪马拉维完成统一。葡萄牙商人与传教士1608至1667年间留有接触马拉维酋长的记录，始终未深入其腹地。

到1750年，数个马拉维王朝统治马拉维中部，切瓦人凭语言、姆菲尼纹身和尼奥秘密兄弟会维系认同，其戴面具的古勒瓦姆库卢舞标志男子成年。切瓦社会行母系制，土地与世系沿母方继承，由舅父守护。

en:
The Chhattisgarhi people inhabit the fertile upper Mahanadi basin of east-central India, a region known in ancient times as Dakshina Kosala and centred on Ratanpur and Raipur. Their language, Chhattisgarhi, is an Eastern Indo-Aryan tongue of the Eastern Hindi group, written in Devanagari and closely related to Hindi.

In the early medieval period Dakshina Kosala was ruled from Sirpur by the Sharabhpuriya and Panduvamshi dynasties, and from the early eleventh century by the Kalachuris of Ratnapura, whose successors ruled as the Haihaiyavanshi kings. Holding the country for roughly seven hundred years, the dynasty split into Ratanpur and Raipur branches in the fourteenth century and later acknowledged Mughal overlordship.

Maratha armies invaded in 1740, and in 1758 the Bhonsles of Nagpur annexed the kingdom. The name Chhattisgarh, traditionally explained as the land of thirty-six forts, first appeared in an official document under Maratha rule in 1795.
zh:
切蒂斯格尔人生活在印度中东部肥沃的默哈讷迪河上游盆地，这一地区古称南憍萨罗，以勒登布尔和赖布尔为中心。他们的语言切蒂斯格尔语属印度-雅利安语族东印地语支，使用天城文，与印地语关系密切。

中世纪早期，南憍萨罗由设里补罗的设罗菩利亚王朝和般度王朝先后统治；11世纪初起，勒登布尔的卡拉丘里王朝掌权，其后裔以海亥耶万西王朝之名继续统治。该王朝立国约七百年，14世纪分裂为勒登布尔与赖布尔两支，后来承认莫卧儿王朝的宗主权。

1740年马拉塔军队入侵，1758年那格浦尔的邦斯勒家族吞并了这个王国。切蒂斯格尔一名通常被解释为三十六座堡垒之地，在马拉塔统治时期的1795年首次见于官方文件。

en:
The Chiapanec, who call themselves Soctón, are an Oto-Manguean people of Chiapas' Central Depression in southern Mexico, centred on Chiapa, now Chiapa de Corzo. Manguean speakers may have entered Chiapas as early as 200; the Chiapanec probably seized the Zoque city of Chiapa in the ninth or tenth century, taking their name from it.

Postclassic Chiapa became a leading regional urban centre, capital of a state holding most of the Central Depression; a priestly oligarchy ruled, choosing two political-military leaders every year, and rivalry over the Tehuantepec trade route kept it at odds with the neighbouring Zoque, Tzotzil and others.

Spanish expeditions came in the early 1520s, and in 1528 Diego de Mazariegos set up the colonial province of Chiapa. Excessive tribute and labour demands drove them to revolt and abandon their towns, their communities dwindling under colonial rule.
zh:
恰帕斯人自称索克顿人，是墨西哥南部恰帕斯中央洼地的奥托-曼格语族群，以恰帕城（今恰帕德科尔索）为中心。曼格语支使用者可能早在200年就已进入恰帕斯，恰帕斯人大概在9至10世纪攻占原属索克人的恰帕城，并以此得名。

后古典期，恰帕发展为当地最大城市中心之一，成为控制中央洼地大部的政权都城；祭司寡头集团统治该城，每年选出两名军政首领，而围绕特万特佩克商路的争夺使他们长期与索克人、佐齐尔人等邻近部族为敌。

16世纪20年代初西班牙远征队穿过这一地区，1528年迭戈·马萨列戈斯设立殖民省份恰帕。过重的贡赋和劳役迫使恰帕斯人弃城反抗，其社群在殖民统治下日渐衰微。

en:
The Chicha, or Checha, were an Andean people of the south-western altiplano, centred on Tupiza in Bolivia's Potosí department, with lands reaching into Jujuy and Salta in Argentina. Towns such as Chilcayoj and Talina stood along the Inca road through Collasuyo; local groups fused into one ethnic identity in the fertile valleys.

The Inca Túpac Yupanqui conquered them around 1478, dispersing many as mitimaes: some went north to repopulate conquered Quito in Ecuador, others to the Calchaquí valleys and Quebrada de Humahuaca against the Chiriguano, and others to Loa and Atacama in Chile. The resettlements began the mixing that later produced the Kolla conglomerate.

Diego de Almagro's expedition crossed Chicha territory in 1536, when Tupiza was called their capital; a Spanish report of 1566 still listed their roadside towns, though Quechua had made deep inroads under Inca rule.
zh:
希沙人又称切查人，是安第斯高原西南部的原住民，中心在玻利维亚波托西图皮萨，领地延伸至阿根廷胡胡伊和萨尔塔。奇尔卡约赫、塔利纳等城镇位于穿越科利亚苏尤的印加大道沿线，地方群体在肥沃山谷中融合为共同族群。

印加王图帕克·尤潘基约1478年征服他们，把许多人作为米特马埃人拆散：一部分北迁厄瓜多尔填补基多人口，一部分迁往卡尔查基河谷和乌马瓦卡峡谷抵御奇里瓜诺人，还有一些送往智利洛阿和阿塔卡马。迁徙开启融合，后来形成科亚人群体。

1536年阿尔马格罗远征队穿过希沙土地，图皮萨当时被称为其首府；1566年西班牙报告仍列出大道旁的希沙城镇，克丘亚语已在印加统治下深入当地。

en:
The Chickasha, or Chickasaw, are a Muskogean people of northern Mississippi and western Tennessee, kin to the Choctaw, splitting in the seventeenth century. Their migration story recalls a journey from west of the Mississippi, archaeology linking their ancestors to the fifteenth-century collapse of Moundville.

Hernando de Soto knew them as the Chicaza, and in 1540 a Chickasaw night raid nearly destroyed his army. From 1670 they acquired firearms from Carolina merchants, and as British allies fought the French and Choctaw through much of the eighteenth century, beating a French attack at Ackia in 1736.

They backed the United States at Fallen Timbers in 1794 and the 1813 to 1814 Creek War, when the Colberts, descendants of a Scots trader and high-ranking Chickasaw women, rose to lead them. Matrilineal, they ceded lands in the 1832 Treaty of Pontotoc Creek and were forced west on the Trail of Tears after 1834.
zh:
奇克索人是马斯科吉语族族群，分布于密西西比北部和田纳西西部，与乔克托人同源，17世纪分为两族。他们的迁徙传说讲述了从密西西比河以西东来的历程，考古学则把其先民与15世纪蒙德维尔的崩溃联系起来。

埃尔南多·德·索托称他们为奇卡萨人，1540年奇克索人夜袭，几乎全歼这支军队。1670年起，他们从卡罗来纳商人手中获得火器；作为英国盟友，他们在18世纪的大部分时间里与法国人和乔克托人作战，1736年在阿基亚之战中击退法军。

他们在1794年鹿寨之战和1813至1814年克里克战争中支持美国，苏格兰商人与奇克索显贵女子后裔科尔伯特家族成为全族领导核心。奇克索人行母系制，1832年依《蓬托托克溪条约》交出土地，1834年后被迫沿眼泪之路西迁。

en:
The Tsilhqot'in, or Chilcotin, are the southernmost Athabaskan-speaking people of British Columbia, whose country Tŝilhqot'in Nen lies along the Chilko and Chilcotin rivers west of the Fraser. Their name means people of the red ochre river, and they call themselves the Nenqayni.

Before contact they were feared warriors whose influence ran from Similkameen to the Pacific coast and the Rocky Mountains, astride an obsidian trade network for arrowheads. They raided all eleven Lillooet bands for captives until defeat in Graveyard Valley checked them.

Goods reached them in the 1780s and 1790s through sea otter trade; by 1808 the North West Company had posts among the Carrier, and in 1821 the Hudson's Bay Company opened Fort Alexandria on the Fraser, becoming the Tsilhqot'in's chief source of metal tools and guns. An 1836 epidemic swept neighbouring Carrier villages, a foretaste of later disease waves.
zh:
齐尔科廷人是不列颠哥伦比亚最靠南的阿萨巴斯卡语民族，家园“齐尔科廷嫩”位于弗雷泽河以西的奇尔科河与奇尔科廷河一带。他们的名字意为“红赭石河之民”，又自称嫩卡伊尼。

接触欧洲人之前，他们是令人畏惧的武士，势力从锡米尔卡明延伸到太平洋海岸和落基山脉，控制着黑曜石贸易网络，用以制作箭头。他们曾袭击利卢埃特人的全部十一个群体、掳走人口，直到墓地谷战败才受阻。

1780至1790年代，货物经海獭贸易传来；到1808年西北公司已在卡里尔人地区设立商站；1821年哈德逊湾公司在弗雷泽河畔开设亚历山大堡，成为齐尔科廷人获取金属工具和枪械的主要来源。1836年疫病席卷邻近的卡里尔人村落，预示随后的疫病浪潮。

en:
The Chillque, also written Chilque, were a highland people whose name was of Aymara origin, divided into Hanan and Urin moieties whose home lay around Lake Titicaca. They were a cluster of small tribes whom the Incas conquered alongside the Aymara, Umasuyu and Cotabamba nations.

The Incas made them trusted mitimaes, resettling loyal Chillque colonies far from the Collao to watch over newly conquered peoples; chroniclers even numbered them among the Inca de Privilegio, and by then they spoke Quechua. Chillque ayllus were planted in the Chili valley behind Arequipa to watch the migrant Yanahuara and Chumbivilca.

After the conquest Francisco Pizarro granted the Chillque, with the Yanahuara and Chumbivilca, to the encomendero Luis de León. Set to work in silver mines and textile workshops and ravaged by disease, the garrison communities shrank fast, with only thirty-two Chillque tributaries recorded in the Arequipa visitation of 1582.
zh:
奇尔克人又译奇尔凯人，族名出自艾马拉语，分上、下两个半边，故土在的的喀喀湖周围。他们是若干小部落的合称，印加人征服艾马拉、乌马苏尤和科塔班巴等族时一并将其征服。

印加人把他们当作可信的米蒂马伊，将效忠的奇尔克殖民群体远迁科利亚奥之外，监视新征服的民族；编年史家甚至把他们列为享有特权的印加民族之一，此时他们已改说克丘亚语。阿雷基帕后方的奇利河谷安插了奇尔克人的艾柳，监视迁徙而来的亚纳瓦拉人和琼比维尔卡人。

征服之后，皮萨罗把奇尔克人连同亚纳瓦拉人、琼比维尔卡人授予委托监护主路易斯·德莱昂。他们被驱入银矿和纺织作坊劳作，又遭疫病摧残，驻防社区人口锐减，1582年阿雷基帕巡查记录里只剩下三十二名奇尔克纳税壮丁。

en:
The Chimbus, or Chimbos, were a pre-Inca people of the Chimbo River valley in the Ecuadorian highlands, closely related to the Puruhá and Tomabela peoples of the surrounding sierra.

During the Inca expansion of the late fifteenth century they resisted the invading armies from Peru: tradition names the chief Chimbo Cando, called the Guaranga, as their leader in the fighting where Guaranda later rose. After the conquest many Chimbus were deported as mitimae settlers to the region of Lake Titicaca, while Inca colonists were brought into their valley.

Spanish rule began in 1534, when Sebastián de Belalcázar established the corregimiento of Chimbo, and Guaranda was founded around 1571. In time the Chimbus merged with Tomabela, Puruhá and Inca communities to form the Waranka people, and their Panzaleo tongue died out during the eighteenth century as Kichwa took its place.
zh:
钦巴斯人又称钦博人，是厄瓜多尔高原钦博河谷的前印加族群，与周围山地的普鲁人、托马贝拉人关系密切。

15世纪末印加扩张时，他们抵抗来自秘鲁的入侵大军；传说酋长钦博·坎多（人称瓜兰加）率领族人在后来兴起瓜兰达城的地方奋战。征服之后，许多钦巴斯人作为米蒂马埃斯移民被强制迁往的的喀喀湖一带，印加殖民者则被迁入他们的河谷。

西班牙人的统治始于1534年，塞巴斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔设立钦博监政区，瓜兰达城约于1571年建立。久而久之，钦巴斯人与托马贝拉、普鲁和印加群落融合，形成瓦兰卡人；他们的潘萨莱奥语在18世纪逐渐消亡，为克丘亚语所取代。

en:
