The Chimú are the people of Chimor, the largest kingdom of Peru's Late Intermediate Period, which arose from the ruins of the Moche around 900 on the north coast. Their capital, Chan Chan near Trujillo, was a city of adobe palaces behind nine-metre walls.

Tradition holds that the founder Taycanamo arrived from the sea on a balsa raft; his descendants widened the kingdom, conquering the Jequetepeque valley around 1320 and absorbing the Sican lands of Lambayeque around 1375. The Chimú worshipped the Moon above the Sun, and at Huanchaco archaeologists have uncovered a mass sacrifice of more than two hundred children, dated 1400 to 1450.

In 1337 they were still expanding, but the Inca emperor Topa Inca Yupanqui conquered Chimor in the 1470s and carried its last ruler, Minchançaman, to Cusco. Their Quingnam tongue, Chimor's official language, declined and was extinct by 1763.
zh:
奇穆人是奇穆王国的居民。该王国约900年在莫切文化的废墟上兴起于秘鲁北部沿海，是当地晚中间期最大的政权。都城昌昌在特鲁希略附近，是高墙环绕的土坯宫殿之城，城墙高达9米。

相传始祖塔伊卡纳莫乘巴尔沙木筏渡海而来，其后代不断扩张，于1320年前后征服赫克特佩克河谷，1375年前后吞并兰巴耶克的西坎故地。奇穆人崇奉月亮甚于太阳；在万查科，考古学家发现了1400年至1450年间献祭两百多名儿童的大型牺牲遗址。

1337年时奇穆仍在扩张，但印加君主图帕克·印卡·尤潘基于1470年代征服奇穆，将末代君主米昌萨曼掳往库斯科。奇穆人的金南语本是王国官方语言，此后日渐衰微，到1763年已经消亡。

en:
The Chincha were a coastal people of the oasis valleys of southwestern Peru, whose kingdom flourished from 900 to 1450 on ground shaped earlier by Paracas, Nazca and Wari. Their name means ocelot in Quechua; they worshipped a jaguar god and claimed feline ancestors.

From the eleventh century they built adobe pyramids and palaces at their capital La Centinela and made their valley the busiest commercial centre on the Peruvian coast. A Spanish chronicle records thirty thousand households: llama caravans carried goods to Cusco and the Collao, while sailing balsa rafts travelled far along the Pacific, perhaps to Central America.

Around 1480 the kingdom was absorbed into Tawantinsuyu, whose Inca rulers gave the name Chinchaysuyu to their northern quarter. Spaniards reached the valley in 1534, but disease and disorder cut its population by an estimated ninety-nine percent within eighty-five years, and Chincha never recovered.
zh:
钦查人是秘鲁西南沿海绿洲河谷的居民，王国在900—1450年间兴盛，此前这片土地曾受帕拉卡斯、纳斯卡与瓦里文化影响。“钦查”在克丘亚语中意为豹猫，崇拜美洲豹神，自称源自猫科动物。

11世纪起，他们在都城拉森蒂内拉修筑土坯金字塔与宫殿，把河谷建成秘鲁海岸最繁忙的商业中心。西班牙史书载当地有三万户：羊驼商队把货物运往库斯科和科利亚奥，带帆的巴尔沙木筏则沿太平洋远航，可能远抵中美洲。

约1480年，该王国被并入塔万廷苏尤，印卡统治者把帝国北部大区命名为钦查苏尤。1534年西班牙人进入河谷，但疾病和动乱使人口在八十五年内估计减少九成九，钦查再未恢复昔日地位。

en:
The Chinook are a group of Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest who speak Chinookan languages and have lived along the Columbia River, from its gorge to its mouth and the adjoining coast, for more than twelve thousand years.

In cedar-plank longhouses, they lived from salmon runs, elk hunting and river trade, and their societies were ranked into nobles, commoners and slaves. Elite families flattened the foreheads of their children as a mark of status, leading early European visitors to call them the Flathead Indians. Their villages made them middlemen between coastal and interior peoples, and the Chinook Jargon, partly based on their language, became the lingua franca of the Northwest fur trade.

The Lewis and Clark Expedition met the Lower Chinook at the mouth of the Columbia in 1805, after which maritime fur traders and repeated epidemics sharply reduced their numbers.
zh:
奇努克人是太平洋西北海岸讲奇努克语族诸语的原住民群体，一万两千多年来定居在哥伦比亚河从峡谷到入海口及邻近海岸一带。

他们住在红雪松木板长屋里，以鲑鱼、猎鹿和河上贸易为生；社会分贵族、平民、奴隶等级，上层家族把幼儿额头压平作为身份标志，早期欧洲来客因此称他们为扁头印第安人。沿河村庄使他们成为沿海与内陆各族的贸易中介，部分以其语言为基础的奇努克混合语，后来成为西北海岸毛皮贸易的通用语。

1805年，刘易斯与克拉克探险队在哥伦比亚河口遇到下游奇努克人；此后海上毛皮商人到来，疫病反复流行，奇努克人口急剧减少。

en:
The Chiribaya were a people of the desert coast of far southern Peru and northern Chile, their heartland the Osmore valley behind the port of Ilo. Their culture took shape around 700 to 900, after Wari and Tiwanaku colonists linked these valleys to the highlands, and its classic phase lasted to about 1360.

Never a unified state, they formed a señorío, a loose network of villages under caciques following the Andean principle of verticality: coastal fishermen and inland farmers of maize and chili peppers at one thousand to two thousand metres, while llamas and alpacas grazed the lomas fog oases, where they even bred a special shepherd dog.

The two zones exchanged food and supplied highland peoples such as the Colla with maize, dried fish and guano. Mid-fifteenth-century Inca expansion absorbed them into the Tawantinsuyu, though coastal villages kept their mixed farming-and-fishing life into the early Spanish decades.
zh:
奇里巴亚人生活在秘鲁最南端与智利北部相接的沙漠海岸及邻近谷地，腹地是伊洛港后方的奥斯莫尔河谷。文化约在700—900年间成形，此前瓦里、蒂亚瓦纳科殖民者已把低海拔谷地与高原联系起来；鼎盛期延续到约1360年。

他们从未形成统一国家，而是由各地卡西克首领分治、联系松散的领主制网络，按安第斯垂直分工原则组织社会：沿海住渔民，内陆海拔一千至两千米处住种植玉米和辣椒的农民，美洲驼和羊驼在洛马斯雾生绿洲放牧，奇里巴亚人甚至培育了一种专门的牧羊犬。

两个区域互通有无，并向科利亚等高原族群供应玉米、鱼干和海岛鸟粪。15世纪中叶，印加扩张把奇里巴亚诸社区并入塔万廷苏尤，但沿海村落农耕兼渔捞的生活延续到西班牙人到来后的最初几十年。

en:
The Chitarero were a Chibcha-speaking people of the eastern Andes on the Colombia-Venezuela border, holding the high country from Táchira to the Pamplona basin, where the Chicamocha marked their southern limit. Their men wore a calabash gourd of maize wine, or chicha, at the waist, and the Spanish took their word for the vessel, chitarero, as the name of the whole people.

They farmed the high valleys and traded with the Muisca and other neighbours. On 27 May 1533 they ambushed the retreating forces of the German conquistador Ambrosius Ehinger, governor of the Welser colony Little Venice; a poisoned arrow struck his neck; he died four days later near Chinácota, one of their settlements.

When Pamplona was refounded in 1549 the region was still said to hold some 200,000 of them, though no separate Chitarero identity survived colonial times.
zh:
奇塔雷罗人是讲奇布查语的族群，住在哥伦比亚与委内瑞拉边境的安第斯山东段，疆域从塔奇拉延伸到潘普洛纳盆地，奇卡莫查河构成南界。男子习惯在腰间挂一只盛玉米酒奇查的葫芦，西班牙人便把他们对这种容器的称呼“奇塔雷罗”当作整个族群的名字。

他们在高山谷地农耕，与穆伊斯卡等邻族贸易。1533年5月27日，他们伏击韦尔泽家族“小威尼斯”殖民地总督、德国征服者安布罗西奥·阿尔芬格撤退中的队伍；一支毒箭射中他的颈部，四天后他在奇纳科塔附近丧命，而奇纳科塔本就是奇塔雷罗人的聚落之一。

1549年潘普洛纳重建时，据说这一地区仍有约20万奇塔雷罗人，但独立的奇塔雷罗族群身份未能留存过殖民时代。

en:
The Chitimacha, whose name means people of the Grand River, are Indigenous people of Louisiana's Atchafalaya Basin and Mississippi Delta, where their ancestors lived for thousands of years. Their Sitimaxa language is an isolate.

In swamps and bayous they built unfortified pole-and-mud villages, grew corn, beans and squash, hunted deer and alligator, and carved cypress dugouts holding fifty people; society was matrilineal. They may have numbered twenty thousand before contact, but epidemics cut them to about four thousand by 1650.

A long war with the French drove them from Bayou Lafourche, and many survivors were sold into slavery; in 1730 the French destroyed the Chawasha, whose remnants joined them. Later in the eighteenth century Acadian settlers occupied much of their land, leading to intermarriage and conversion to Catholicism; unlike most southeastern peoples, they were not removed in the 1830s and remained on their bayous.
zh:
奇蒂马查人意为住在大河之畔的人，是路易斯安那中南部阿查法拉亚盆地与密西西比三角洲的原住民，祖先在此已生活数千年；他们的奇蒂马查语是一门孤立语言。

他们在沼泽与河湾边建起不设防的木柱糊泥村落，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎鹿捕鳄，还把柏木凿成可容五十人的独木舟；社会按母系传承。接触欧洲人前，他们可能有两万人，瘟疫使他们到1650年只剩约四千人。

随后与法国人的长期战争把他们赶出拉福什河湾村落，许多幸存者被卖为奴；1730年法国人消灭乔瓦沙人，其残余并入奇蒂马查。18世纪后期，阿卡迪亚移民占据他们大量土地，两族通婚并改宗天主教；与东南部大多数族群不同，他们在19世纪30年代没有被强制西迁，始终留在河湾之地。

en:
Chitralis are the Kho people of the Hindu Kush valleys of Chitral and Yasin. Their Khowar speech is a Dardic Indo-Aryan language counted among the most archaic living Indic tongues, preserving Sanskrit case inflection.

They spread from upper Chitral under the Rais dynasty, whose first chief, Shah Nadir Rais, is placed around 1320; in the seventeenth century the Khushwaqt branch carried rule east to Yasin and Ghizer. Most Kho converted to Islam from the fourteenth century, becoming Hanafi Sunnis with an Ismaili community in the upper valleys, while their kinsmen the Kalash kept their old animist faith in remote valleys.

The Kator dynasty overthrew the Rais in the seventeenth century and ruled Chitral as mehtars from Chitral town, holding a kingdom stretching at its height from Kunar to Punial. Older customs survived too: polo on high pastures, the pakol hat and folklore thick with mountain fairies.
zh:
吉德拉尔人即科霍人，聚居在兴都库什山的吉德拉尔、亚辛诸河谷，所讲科瓦语属印度-雅利安语系达尔德语支，被认为是现存最古老的印度语言之一，保留大量梵语格变形式。

他们在拉伊斯王朝治下从上吉德拉尔向外扩张，首位首领沙阿·纳迪尔·拉伊斯约在1320年兴起；17世纪，胡什瓦格特分支把统治向东带到亚辛和吉泽尔。多数科霍人从14世纪起皈依伊斯兰教，成为哈乃斐派逊尼穆斯林，上游河谷有伊斯玛仪派社群；近亲卡拉什人则在偏远河谷保留古老的万物有灵信仰。

17世纪卡托尔王朝推翻拉伊斯家族，以吉德拉尔城为都、以“梅赫塔尔”为号统治此地，极盛时疆域从库纳尔延伸到普尼亚尔。吉德拉尔人的生活也保留古老肌理：高山牧场的马球、帕科尔帽，以及充满山灵仙子的民间传说。

en:
Chiyalik is a medieval culture of the Southern Urals of the tenth to fourteenth century, first identified at Chiyalek village on the Sun river. Its forest-steppe was the Magna Hungaria of medieval Latin writers, homeland of the Magyars.

Its carriers were semi-nomadic Ugric tribes, kin of Hungarians who stayed east when the Magyars moved to the Black Sea steppe and the Carpathian Basin. In the 1230s the Hungarian friar Julian reached Volga Bulgaria and found Eastern Hungarians near the Volga and Kama, years before the Mongol conquest.

They wintered in log houses and semi-dugouts, summered in yurts, made round-bottom pottery and fought as light cavalry, graves supplied with arrows, sabres and stirrups. From the middle of the fourteenth century Kipchak Turkic nomads pressed into their lands; the Chiyalik people gradually adopted Islam and were absorbed into the Bashkirs and Volga Tatars.
zh:
奇亚利克是南乌拉尔的中世纪文化，年代为10至14世纪，最早发现于苏尼河畔奇亚列克村旁的遗址。这片森林草原地带被中世纪拉丁文献称作“马格纳·匈牙利”，即马扎尔人的故地。

创造该文化的是半游牧乌戈尔部落，与马扎尔人同源，在马扎尔主体迁往黑海草原、继而进入喀尔巴阡盆地时留在东方。13世纪30年代，匈牙利修士朱利安抵达伏尔加保加利亚，在伏尔加河与卡马河附近发现“东匈牙利人”；数年后蒙古征服即席卷该地区。

他们冬天住木构房屋和半地穴屋，夏天住毡帐，制作圆底陶器，以轻骑兵作战，墓中随葬箭矢、马刀和马镫。从14世纪中期起，钦察突厥游牧民不断涌入，奇亚利克人逐渐改宗伊斯兰教，融入巴什基尔人和伏尔加鞑靼人之中。

en:
The Chahta, anglicized as Choctaw, are a Western Muskogean people of Mississippi, Alabama and Louisiana whose language is close to Chickasaw; the two share an ancestral tradition. They coalesced in the sixteenth century, organized in three divisions: Okla Falaya, Okla Tannap and the southern Okla Hannali of the Six Towns.

Tradition remembers chief Tuscaloosa, who died facing Hernando de Soto at Mabila in 1540, called the first major pitched battle between Europeans and Native Americans in North America.

The Choctaw traded and allied in turn with French, British and Spanish, and after independence fought beside the United States in the War of 1812, where chief Pushmataha made his name. Classed among the Five Civilized Tribes, they lost their lands by treaty; after the 1830 Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek, most were forcibly relocated to Indian Territory in 1831 to 1833.
zh:
乔克托人（自称恰赫塔，乔克托是英语化写法）是密西西比、阿拉巴马、路易斯安那的西马斯科吉族群，语言近于奇克索语，两族共有同源传说。16世纪融合为民族，分三大区域：奥克拉法拉亚、奥克拉塔纳普，及南部六镇的奥克拉汉纳利。

乔克托人铭记首领塔斯卡卢萨，1540年他在马比拉之战抵抗埃尔南多·德·索托战死，此战被称为北美原住民与欧洲人之间第一场大规模对阵战。

殖民年代他们先后与法、英、西班牙贸易结盟；美国独立后，他们在1812年战争中助美作战，酋长普什马塔哈由此成名。虽被列入五大文明部落，土地仍经条约丧失；1830年《舞兔溪条约》后，大部人于1831—1833年被强制西迁印第安领地。

en:
The Chokwe are Bantu people of north-eastern Angola, south-western Congo and north-western Zambia, in savanna between Kasai and upper Zambezi. Their chiefs trace descent from sixteenth-century Lunda migrations, and by the seventeenth century they were one of twelve clans of the Lunda Empire of the Mwata Yanvo.

After disputes and refusals of tribute, they broke from Lunda rule and built wealthy village societies, farming, hunting and trading wax, ivory and copper inland. Matrilineal lineages and mukanda boys' initiation schools ordered their life, and carvers won fame for ancestor figures, ceremonial chairs and masks: the female Mwana Pwo and the royal Chibinda Ilunga of the legendary hunter-prince who married the Lunda queen.

Their trade and numbers grew through the eighteenth century; by the 1830s, when Portuguese caravans first made contact, they were already a rising power amid collapsing Lunda authority.
zh:
乔奎人是分布在安哥拉东北部、刚果盆地西南部和赞比亚西北部的班图人，地处开赛河与赞比西河上游之间的稀树草原。酋长把共同世系追溯到16世纪的隆达迁徙；到17世纪，乔奎人已是姆瓦塔·扬武隆达帝国的十二氏族之一。

在内争和拒绝纳贡之后，他们摆脱隆达统治，建立富庶的村落社会，农耕、狩猎并在内陆贩运蜂蜡、象牙和铜。乔奎社会按母系血缘和男子入会学校穆坎达组织；雕刻师以祖先雕像、礼仪座椅和面具闻名，如女性的姆瓦纳·普沃面具，以及纪念娶了隆达女王的传奇猎手王子奇宾达·伊隆加的王室面具。

整个18世纪，乔奎人的贸易和人口不断增长；到1830年代葡萄牙商队首次直接接触时，他们已成为趁隆达权威瓦解而崛起的强大势力。

en:
The Ch'ol are Maya of the northern Chiapas highlands whose Ch'ol language forms the conservative Cholan branch of Mayan, among the living tongues closest to the Classic Mayan of hieroglyphic inscriptions at Palenque and other cities.

At contact Ch'ol speakers also held the Lacandon Jungle: the Lakandon Ch'ol capital stood at Lakam-Tun on Laguna Miramar. Hernán Cortés first heard of them in 1524 while passing through Kejache lands. Spanish expeditions began in 1559; by century's end the Lakandon Ch'ol had abandoned Lakam-Tun and founded Sac Balam, whose name means white jaguar. From there they raided Guatemalan highlands and traded cacao and achiote for iron tools with Verapaz towns through the seventeenth century.

The Spanish stormed Sac Balam in 1695; other Ch'ol were gathered into reducciones at Palenque and nearby towns, the last independent Lakandon bands being forcibly relocated in 1712 and absorbed into the highland Maya.
zh:
乔尔人是恰帕斯北部高地的玛雅族群，所用乔尔语属玛雅语系中保守的乔尔语支，是最接近帕伦克等城邦碑铭古典玛雅语的活语言之一。

西班牙人到来时，说乔尔语的族群还据有拉坎东丛林：拉坎东乔尔人的都城在米拉马尔湖畔的拉坎通。1524年科尔特斯行经克哈切人之地时首次听说他们。1559年西班牙人开始征讨，到16世纪末拉坎东乔尔人放弃拉坎通，另建都城萨克巴兰，意为“白美洲豹”。整个17世纪，他们从那里袭击危地马拉高地，用可可和胭脂树果与韦拉帕斯的殖民城镇交换铁器。

1695年西班牙人攻陷萨克巴兰；其余乔尔人被集中迁到帕伦克等地的“集村”，最后一批独立的拉坎东残部于1712年被强制迁徙，融入高地玛雅人之中。

en:
The Cholon were rainforest people of the Huallaga's left bank on the forested eastern Andean slope. Cholon was their Spanish name; their Seeptsá tongue named both people and language, and Seeptsá with the related Hibito formed a small family believed once important across the eastern foothills.

They lived by slash-and-burn farming, hunting and fishing; women grew cotton and wove cloth. For centuries the Cholon traded across the Huallaga with highland Hibito, exchanging feathers, wax, honey and herbs for stone and metal axes. A serpent's poisonous fang was their charm against snakebite.

The outside world knew them through missionaries: Franciscans first contacted them and founded mission villages in 1676; in the eighteenth century friar Pedro de la Mata wrote a Seeptsá grammar, the Arte de la Lengua Cholona, and a bishop recorded a word list in 1782 to 1785. Quechua and Spanish then displaced the old language along the Huallaga.
zh:
乔隆人是安第斯山东坡雨林中瓦亚加河左岸的森林族群。乔隆是西班牙人对他们的称呼，他们以本族语自称塞普尔察，语言也叫这个名字；塞普察语与关系很近的希维托语构成一个小语系，学界认为它曾是安第斯东部山麓重要的交际语言。

他们刀耕火种、狩猎捕鱼为生，妇女种棉织布。几百年来乔隆人与瓦亚加河对岸高原的希维托人贸易，用羽毛、蜂蜡、蜂蜜和药材交换石斧与金属斧。他们还把毒蛇毒牙带在身上当护身符，相信能防蛇咬。

外界主要通过传教士了解他们：1676年方济各会首次接触并建立传教村，18世纪修士佩德罗·德拉马塔撰写塞普察语语法《乔隆语的艺术》，一位主教又在1782—1785年间记录了一份乔隆语词汇表。殖民岁月中，克丘亚语和西班牙语沿瓦亚加河取代了这种古老语言。

en:
The Chono of the Ecuadorian lowlands, known to archaeology as the Milagro-Quevedo culture, held the Guayas basin from about 400, navigable waterways formed by the Daule and Babahoyo.

Probably Amazonian in origin and kin to the Omagua, they farmed the floodplain with raised camellones and tola mounds, and their position between coast and Andes made them the region's great middlemen: canoes carried salt, cotton, cacao, Esmeraldas gold and copper axe-money between coast and highland, while potters stamped snake and frog motifs onto ceremonial vessels called cocinas de brujo, witches' kitchens.

The Incas never entered in force, receiving only occasional tribute. After 1534 the chief Guayaquile led fierce resistance and destroyed the first Spanish settlements on the gulf named after him; once subdued, the Chono country was absorbed into the Real Audiencia of Quito, chiefs reduced to tribute collectors under the encomienda.
zh:
低地乔诺人在考古学上称米拉格罗—克韦多文化，约400年起据守瓜亚斯河流域，即道莱河与巴巴奥约河构成的通航水网。

他们可能源自亚马逊，与奥马瓜人有亲缘关系，以卡梅列内斯台田和托拉土墩经营洪泛区农业；地处太平洋沿岸与安第斯山之间的要冲，成为地区大中间商：独木舟把盐、棉花、可可、埃斯梅拉达斯黄金和铜斧币在沿海与高原各族之间转运，陶工还在名为巫师灶的礼器上压印蛇和蛙的纹样。

印加人从未大举进入其地，只得到零星贡赋。1534年之后，酋长瓜亚基莱领导激烈抵抗，摧毁了以他为名的海湾畔最早的西班牙居民点；被征服后，乔诺之地并入基多检审法院，酋长们沦为监护征赋制下的收税人。

en:
The Yoko t'aanob, called the Chontal Maya of Tabasco, are also called the Putun in older chronicles; the name Chontal comes from the Nahuatl word for foreigner. They live in the lagoon-and-river lowlands of Tabasco, once cradle of the Olmecs and later a Maya heartland.

In the Terminal Classic their canoe-borne merchants dominated the river and coastal trade of the Maya lowlands, their homeland neutral ground for merchants of rival powers. On the eve of the conquest they were divided into six provinces, among them Potonchan and Xicalango, Potonchan and Jalapa holding perhaps thirteen thousand people each; cacao, fish and maize made it rich.

The Spanish arrived in 1518 with Juan de Grijalva's voyage, and in 1519 Hernan Cortes met the chief Tabscoob, whose people became the first in New Spain to acknowledge the Spanish emperor and gave Cortes the interpreter La Malinche. Colonial epidemics and ranching emptied most old towns; Nacajuca, where the first church rose in 1614, was the only urban centre to survive the period.
zh:
琼塔尔人习称塔巴斯科的琼塔尔玛雅人，“琼塔尔”一名来自纳瓦特尔语中意为外乡人的词，较早的编年史常称他们为普顿人。他们住在塔巴斯科潟湖河网密布的低地，这里曾是奥尔梅克文明的摇篮，后为玛雅人腹地。

古典期末期，驾独木舟的商人控制了玛雅低地的河道与沿海商路，故土成为敌对强权商人往来的中立贸易场。征服前夕，他们分为波东钱、希卡兰戈等六个行省，波东钱和哈拉帕各有约一万三千人口，可可、鱼和玉米使当地富庶。

1518年，胡安·德·格里哈尔瓦的航船最先抵达；1519年，埃尔南·科尔特斯会见首领塔布斯库布，琼塔尔人成为新西班牙最早承认西班牙皇帝者，并将翻译拉·马林切献给科尔特斯。殖民地时期的疫病和牧牛业使多数旧城凋敝，1614年首建教堂的纳卡胡卡是这一时期唯一幸存城镇。

en:
The Chorotega, also called the Mangue, are an Oto-Manguean-speaking people who at Spanish contact in the sixteenth century occupied the Pacific lowlands of Nicaragua and Honduras and north-western Costa Rica. Linguistic and archaeological evidence suggests their ancestors split from the Chiapanec and moved south out of central Mexico around the seventh century, reaching the Rivas region of Nicaragua by about 800, where Papagayo polychrome ceramics mark their arrival; around 1200 the incoming Nicarao displaced them onto the Nicoya Peninsula.

Their towns were laid out around central plazas with temples and markets, and councils of elders appointed provincial rulers in a kind of elective monarchy. They made the painted Nicoya polychrome ware and farmed maize, cotton and tobacco.

After the Spanish conquest of the sixteenth century many Chorotega were enslaved and shipped to Panama and Callao in Peru, and their communities declined under colonial rule.
zh:
乔罗特加人又称曼格人，讲奥托-曼格语系语言。16世纪与西班牙人接触时，他们分布在尼加拉瓜、洪都拉斯的太平洋低地和哥斯达黎加西北部。语言学和考古证据提示，先民约在7世纪与恰帕斯人分离，自墨西哥中部南迁，约800年抵达尼加拉瓜里瓦斯，帕帕加约彩陶是其到来的标志；约1200年，迁入的尼卡拉奥人把他们赶到尼科亚半岛。

城镇围绕中央广场修建，配有神庙和市场，长老会议以选举君主制方式任命地方统治者。他们制作彩绘尼科亚陶器，种植玉米、棉花和烟草。

16世纪西班牙征服后，许多乔罗特加人被掳为奴，运往巴拿马和秘鲁卡亚俄，社群在殖民统治下衰落。

en:
The Chorti are Maya of the Guatemala-Honduras-El Salvador borderlands, their speech the closest living relative of the Classic Maya of Copan's stelae. Copan was their ancestral city: founded in 426 by king Yax K'uk' Mo', its dynasty ruled nearly four hundred years, making the valley a centre of Maya sculpture, astronomy and writing.

After the Classic collapse they stayed in the hill country, forming a confederacy called the Payaki kingdom on the eve of the Spanish invasion. Leader Copan Galel resisted the conquistadors near Copan's ruins and then at Citala, where defeat forced his surrender and baptism.

Under colonial rule their territory shrank to farming villages in Chiquimula and the Honduran highlands, with a few communities around Tejutla in El Salvador keeping Chorti ancestry. Their old religion honoured earth and wind gods, and music and maize customs survived in former Payaki villages.
zh:
乔尔蒂人是危地马拉、洪都拉斯、萨尔瓦多交界地带的玛雅民族，语言与科潘石碑的古典玛雅语亲缘最近。科潘是他们的祖先名城：亚什·库克·莫于426年建城，王朝统治近四百年，使河谷成为玛雅雕塑、天文和文字中心。

古典期崩溃后他们仍留居丘陵，西班牙入侵前夕组成帕亚基王国联盟。首领科潘·加莱尔先在科潘遗址迎战，又在西塔拉固守，最终战败投降受洗。

殖民统治下，疆域缩小为奇基穆拉和洪都拉斯高地的农耕村落，萨尔瓦多特胡特拉周边少数社群仍存乔尔蒂血统。旧教敬奉地神风神，音乐与玉米习俗在昔日帕亚基村庄延续。

en:
The Chǔ culture is the people of Hubei, the lake and river country of the middle Yangtze around Jiangling and Wuchang. In the Zhou era this was the kingdom of Chu, also called Jingchu, whose capital Ying stood near present-day Jingzhou and whose poets, headed by Qu Yuan, created the Songs of Chu tradition before Qin annexed it in 223 BCE.

After the Mongol conquest it formed the heart of Huguang, a name the Ming kept after driving out the Yuan in 1368. Its river towns grew on the Yangtze and Han waterways, their speech Southwestern Mandarin, spread by the Ming and Qing migrations that repopulated the upper Yangtze.

The late Ming brought devastation as the armies of Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong ravaged Hubei in the 1630s and 1640s; the Qing took control in 1644 and 1645, and in the 1660s split Huguang into Hubei and Hunan. Wuchang and the Han-confluence towns then grew into busy inland trading cities.
zh:
楚文化的主体是湖北人，即长江中游以江陵和武昌为中心、湖河纵横的江汉之民。周代这里是又称荆楚的楚国，郢都就在今荆州一带；公元前223年秦灭楚之前，以屈原为代表的楚国诗人开创了楚辞传统。

蒙古征服后，这一带成为湖广省的核心，1368年明朝驱逐元廷后沿用湖广建制。凭借长江与汉水的水运，沿江城镇日渐兴盛，当地话属西南官话，是明清大移民填充长江上游时扩散开来的。

明末再遭兵燹：17世纪30至40年代，李自成、张献忠的军队蹂躏湖北，清朝在1644至1645年取得控制，17世纪60年代又将湖广分为湖北、湖南两省。此后武昌与汉水汇入长江处的城镇发展为繁忙的内陆商埠。

en:
The Chugashigmuit, also spelled Chugachigmiut or Chugach Sugpiaq, are an Alutiiq people of the southern Alaskan coast, centred on the Kenai Peninsula and Prince William Sound. Their autonym Sugpiaq means real person, and their Chugach dialect of Alutiiq is a Pacific Gulf language of the Yupik family.

For millennia they lived from the sea, hunting sea mammals and fishing from skin boats, trading and fighting by turns with the neighbouring Eyak, Ahtna and Tlingit.

In 1741 they became the first indigenous Alaskans to meet Europeans when Vitus Bering's Russian expedition reached their shores. Russian fur hunters soon drew them into the sea-otter trade of Russian America, and Spanish, British and American explorers visited the sound later in the century.
zh:
楚加奇人又称楚加奇苏格皮克人，是阿拉斯加南岸的阿鲁蒂克族群，以基奈半岛和威廉王子湾为中心。自称“苏格皮克”意为“真正的人”，所说为阿鲁蒂克语楚加奇方言，属尤皮克语族下的太平洋海湾语言。

数千年来他们靠海为生，乘皮艇捕猎海洋哺乳动物、捕鱼，与相邻的埃亚克人、阿特纳人和特林吉特人时而贸易，时而交战。

1741年，维图斯·白令的俄国探险队抵达海岸，楚加奇人由此成为最早接触欧洲人的阿拉斯加原住民。俄国毛皮猎人随后而至，把他们卷入俄属美洲的海獭毛皮贸易，18世纪后期西班牙、英国和美国的探险队也相继到访威廉王子湾。

en:
The Chukchi are aboriginals of the Chukchi Peninsula and the Arctic and Bering shores of far northeastern Siberia, whose ancestors lived on the Chukotka coast since the turn of the third millennium BC. Their self-name Luoravetlan means genuine people; they divide into settled Maritime Chukchi hunting seal and walrus, and nomadic Reindeer Chukchi of the inland tundra, the Russian name coming from their word for rich reindeer owners.

Russians reached the Kolyma in 1643 and built Anadyrsk in 1649, but early eighteenth-century expeditions against them failed. Major Dmitry Pavlutsky ravaged their camps from the 1730s; the extermination war of 1744 to 1747 ended with his 1747 death, his head kept as a trophy.

After conquest failed the empire abandoned Anadyrsk in 1764; annual Anyuy fairs from 1775 and Kolyma fairs from 1788 drew them into the fur economy without subjecting them.
zh:
楚科奇人是西伯利亚极东北楚科奇半岛及北冰洋、白令海沿岸的原住民，先民自公元前3000年之交便居住在楚科奇大陆海岸。他们自称卢奥拉维特兰，意为真正的人，分为沿海定居、捕猎海豹海象的海猎楚科奇人和内陆苔原随鹿群游牧的养鹿楚科奇人；俄语“楚科奇”一名来自他们语言里对养鹿富户的称呼。

俄国人1643年进抵科雷马河，1649年建起阿纳德尔堡，但18世纪初几次出征都告失败。1730年代起，德米特里·帕夫卢茨基少校大肆焚毁营地；1744至1747年的剿灭战争以1747年他战死、头颅被留作战利品告终。

征服失败后，俄国1764年放弃阿纳德尔堡；1775年起在阿纽伊河、1788年起在下科雷马河每年开设集市，把楚科奇人纳入俄国毛皮经济，却始终没有使他们臣服。

en:
The Chumash are a Native American people of California's central and southern coast, their territory from Morro Bay to Malibu and the Northern Channel Islands, ancestors having lived there at least eleven thousand years. Before contact they held over 150 villages of related Chumashan languages, an isolate.

Island craftsmen made olive-shell bead currency for a trade network reaching Arizona, and tomol sewn-plank canoes served fishing, whaling and island-mainland travel; their rock art and basketry rank among California's most elaborate.

Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo made first European contact in 1542, but large-scale colonization awaited the Portolá expedition of 1769. From 1772 to 1817 five Franciscan missions drew nearly all Chumash into the system, disease and forced labour cutting them down. The 1824 Chumash Revolt, begun at Santa Inés, was among Spanish California's largest Native uprisings, and Mexico's 1833 secularization dissolved the missions without restoring land.
zh:
丘马什人是加利福尼亚中南部海岸的原住民，领地从莫罗湾到马利布及北海峡群岛，祖先在此至少生活一万一千年。接触欧洲人前，他们住150多个村落，讲亲属语言丘马什语族诸语，该语族是孤立语系。

岛上工匠把海螺壳制成贝珠货币，贸易网络远达亚利桑那；名为托莫尔的缝合木板独木舟用于捕鱼、捕鲸和海岛大陆往来；岩画和编篮属加利福尼亚最精美工艺之列。

1542年胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略首次与他们接触，大规模殖民到1769年波尔托拉远征后才开始。1772—1817年五座方济各会传教站把几乎所有丘马什人纳入传教体系，疫病苦役使人口锐减。1824年始于圣伊内斯的丘马什起义是西属加利福尼亚最大原住民反抗之一，1833年墨西哥世俗化解散传教站，未归还土地。

en:
The Churajon were the pre-Inca people of the Arequipa region in southern Peru, thought to descend from Aymara-speaking groups who moved from the highlands into the warm coastal valleys in search of farmland. Between roughly 600 and 1400 they settled the Chili and Tambo river valleys and spread into Moquegua and Tacna, building towns and canals and terracing the slopes.

Their development ran from an early phase (800–1200) contemporary with Wari through autonomous rule (1200–1400) to a late phase under Inca influence. They were farmers and herders who grew maize, potatoes and quinoa, and their globular or cylindrical pottery was painted in white, black and red with geometric motifs. Their stone towns housed the cylindrical burial towers called chullpas.

The type site is the ruins of Churajón below the Choquellampa hill. Around 1450 Inca expansion brought the Churajon communities into the empire.
zh:
丘拉洪人是秘鲁南部阿雷基帕地区的前印加族群，一般认为源自讲艾马拉语的群体，从高原下到温暖的沿海谷地寻找耕地。约600年至1400年间，他们在奇利河与坦博河谷地定居，并扩展到莫克瓜和塔克纳一带，修建城镇与灌渠，在山坡上开辟梯田。

其发展经历了与瓦里帝国同时的早期（800—1200年）、自主的中期（1200—1400年）以及处于印加影响之下的晚期。他们农耕畜牧，种植玉米、马铃薯和藜麦；陶器为球形或筒形，以白、黑、红三色绘出几何纹样，石砌城镇中有被称为楚尔帕的筒形墓塔。

代表性遗址是乔克良帕山下的丘拉洪城址。约1450年印加人扩张，丘拉洪诸社区被并入印加帝国。

en:
The Chutia are a Bodo-Kachari people of eastern Assam, settled cultivators who built the foremost tribal state to arise after Kamarupa's fall. Their kingdom, called Sadiya after its upper Brahmaputra capital, took shape in the early thirteenth century and rose in the later fourteenth, its earliest inscriptionally attested king Nandisvara.

The ruling house showed matrilineal traits and claimed descent from the Asuras, while the people worshipped the goddess Kechaikhati, whose Sadiya temple was served by Deori priests. Ahom chronicles record a clash under Sutuphaa (1369–1379) in which the Ahom king was killed, and border wars from 1512 ended in 1523–1524 when the Ahom king Suhungmung conquered Sadiya.

The Chutia were dispersed across Upper Assam and absorbed into Ahom society, their craftsmen famed as gunmakers. In the seventeenth century many joined the Vaishnava Ekasarana movement, and their Tibeto-Burman speech gave way to Assamese.
zh:
久蒂亚人是阿萨姆东部的博多—卡查里系族群，属定居农耕者，建立了迦摩缕波衰落之后诸部族政权中最发达的一个。他们的王国以布拉马普特拉河上游的萨迪亚为都，又称萨迪亚国，13世纪初成形，14世纪下半叶兴起，碑铭中可考的最早国王是南迪什婆罗。

王室带有母系制特征，自称阿修罗后裔；民众信奉凯柴卡蒂女神，萨迪亚女神庙的祭司由代奥里人担任。阿洪编年史记载，1369—1379年苏图法在位期间的冲突中阿洪国王被杀；1512年起的边境战争最终在1523—1524年以阿洪国王苏洪蒙征服萨迪亚告终。

此后久蒂亚人被分散到阿萨姆上游各地，融入阿洪社会，其工匠以造枪闻名。17世纪许多人加入毗湿奴虔信派，藏缅语也逐渐为阿萨姆语取代。

en:
The Chuukese are a Micronesian people of the Chuuk Lagoon and its outer atolls, in the Caroline Islands of the western Pacific, and speak a Chuukic language of the Austronesian family. Their ancestors were Lapita-related Austronesian settlers: excavations show people on lagoon islands by the second and first centuries BC, and a distinct Chuukese culture took shape from the fourteenth century.

The lagoon splits into the western Faichuuk and eastern Namoneas island groups, whose clans combined fishing with taro and banana gardening in thatch-built villages and fought intermittent wars under their own chiefs.

Álvaro de Saavedra made the first recorded European sighting in 1528 and Alonso de Arellano followed in 1565. Spain later counted the lagoon among the Caroline Islands, but no foreign power established control, so in 1837 the Chuukese still governed themselves with only occasional ships passing through.
zh:
楚克人是西太平洋加罗林群岛楚克潟湖及其外围环礁的密克罗尼西亚族群，使用南岛语系的楚克语支语言。他们的祖先是与拉皮塔文化有关的南岛语定居者，考古发掘显示公元前2—前1世纪潟湖岛屿上已有人居，独具面貌的楚克文化到14世纪才正式形成。

潟湖分为西部的法伊楚克与东部的纳莫尼亚斯两组岛群，各氏族在茅草村落中以捕鱼为主，兼种芋艿和香蕉，并在各自酋长率领下断断续续地争战。

1528年阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉留下了欧洲人最早的目击记录，1565年阿隆索·德·阿雷利亚诺再度抵达。西班牙后来把潟湖算作加罗林群岛的一部分，却没有外国势力建立实际统治，因此到1837年，楚克人仍自行管理内部事务，只有偶尔经过的船只。

en:
The Chuvan were a Yukaghir people of the Anadyr basin, roaming the upper tributaries of the Anadyr and the Anyuy in present-day Chukotka. They lived by hunting, fishing and reindeer breeding and spoke their own Yukaghir tongue, of which a word list was taken down in 1821.

In the eighteenth century Chukchi raids broke their clan lands: one part of the people retreated west to the Kolyma, where they gradually adopted Russian speech and ways, while the rest were absorbed by the Koryaks and Chukchi. Mountain and coastal Chuvan groups kept their identity in the Anadyr tundra into the nineteenth century.
zh:
楚万人是尤卡吉尔人的一支，游猎于阿纳德尔河流域，在今楚科奇境内的阿纳德尔河与阿纽伊河上游支流一带。他们以狩猎、捕鱼和养驯鹿为生，说本族的尤卡吉尔语，1821年还有人为这种语言记下了词汇表。

18世纪，楚科奇人的袭扰打散了他们的氏族地：一部分人西撤到科雷马河，逐渐改用俄语、接受俄式生活，其余则被科里亚克人和楚科奇人同化。山地楚万与沿海楚万两个群体在阿纳德尔苔原上把自身认同保持到了19世纪。

en:
The Chuvash are the only surviving people of the Oghur branch of the Turkic family, settled on the Volga around Cheboksary. Their language split from other Turkic tongues more than a thousand years ago, keeping the Oghur sounds r and l where Turks have z and sh, and most scholars trace it to Volga Bulgar speech mixed with Finnic settlers.

They are heirs of Volga Bulgaria: its rulers adopted Islam in 922, but the Mongols sacked it in 1236, and the region then passed to the Golden Horde and later Kazan's khanate.

After Ivan the Terrible took Kazan in 1552 they became Russian yasak taxpayers, and Orthodox missionaries pressed baptism on them. Many fled east to the Bashkirs rather than convert, and old keremet shrines where geese were sacrificed long survived beside the new churches; Chuvash schools and printed literature later emerged.
zh:
楚瓦什人是突厥语族乌古尔语支唯一留存的民族，居住在伏尔加河畔切博克萨雷一带。他们的语言一千多年前便与其他突厥语分流，保留着乌古尔语特有的r和l音，而其他突厥语对应为z和sh；多数学者将其追溯到伏尔加保加尔语与芬兰语族居民融合后的形态。

他们是伏尔加保加利亚的继承者：保加尔统治者于922年改宗伊斯兰教，蒙古人却在1236年洗劫该国，此地先归金帐汗国，后属喀山汗国。

1552年伊凡雷帝攻占喀山后，他们成为缴纳牙萨克贡赋的俄国属民，东正教传教士力推洗礼。许多人东逃投奔巴什基尔人以避受洗，而以鹅献祭的古老克列梅特神祠在新建教堂旁仍长期存留；楚瓦什学校与本族语印刷文学后来也相继出现。

en:
The Chuwi, also spelled Chuis or Chuwis, were one of the Aymara lordships that took shape on the Bolivian altiplano after the collapse of Tiwanaku and flourished between about 1150 and 1477.

Their valleys lay in what are now the departments of Cochabamba and Chuquisaca, around Mizque, and their ayllus formed part of the Charka kingdom of Collasuyu alongside the Chayanta, Sakaka and Qhara Qhara.

First overborne by the expanding Charca, the Chuwi later became their allies; the chronicles place them at Sacaca with the Caracara and Chichas when the highland peoples made their pact with the Spaniards. Like the other Aymara señoríos they were absorbed into the Inca state under Túpac Yupanqui, keeping their dual chiefly structure within it.
zh:
丘维人在史籍中又拼作丘伊斯或丘维斯，是蒂亚瓦纳科崩溃后在玻利维亚高原上形成的艾马拉诸领地之一，兴盛于约1150年至1477年间。

他们的河谷位于今科恰班巴省和丘基萨卡省境内，以米斯克一带为中心，其村社与查扬塔人、萨卡卡人、卡拉卡拉人等共同组成科利亚苏尤的查克拉王国。

丘维人起初被扩张的查尔卡斯人压服，后来反成其盟友；据史籍记载，高原各族与西班牙人缔约时，丘维人曾与卡拉卡拉人、奇查人齐聚萨卡卡。和其他艾马拉领地一样，他们在图帕克·尤潘基时期被并入印加国家，并在其中保留了二元酋长制的社会结构。

en:
The Chúzhōu culture covers the mountainous southwest of Zhejiang, including Longquan and Qingtian in Lishui prefecture, and reaches across the Fujian border to Pucheng. The Sui first set up Chuzhou Prefecture in 589; after centuries under other names, the Yuan made it Chuzhou Route in 1276, and it became Chuzhou Prefecture under the Ming.

Nearly nine-tenths of the land is mountains, and its isolated valleys made the Chuzhou division of Southern Wu one of the most fragmented groups of Wu speech, while the Ou River carried its goods downstream to the port of Wenzhou.

Longquan was one of China's greatest ceramic centers: its green celadon, in large-scale production from the Northern Song, boomed after the Southern Song court moved to nearby Hangzhou, kept high quality through the Yuan and early Ming, and was exported across the eastern seas for five centuries before Jingdezhen blue-and-white displaced it. The same county kept the ancient Longquan craft of sword-making, while Qingtian became known for its carved soapstone.
zh:
处州文化位于浙江西南山区，即丽水一带的龙泉、青田等地，并翻过省界延伸到福建浦城。589年隋朝首次设置处州，此后数度更名，1276年元代改为处州路，明代定为处州府。

这里近九成地面是山地，闭塞的山谷使南部吴语处州片内部分化极大，各县口音彼此难懂；瓯江则把山货顺流送到温州港。

龙泉是中国历史上最大的青瓷产区之一：北宋时已大规模烧造，南宋朝廷迁到邻近的杭州后更是盛极一时，元代至明初仍保持高水平，五百多年间经海路大量外销，最终被景德镇青花瓷挤出市场。龙泉还传承着古老的铸剑技艺，青田则以青田石雕刻闻名。

en:
The Ciboney, or Siboney, were the dominant Indigenous people of central Cuba when the Spanish arrived, and were also found on western Hispaniola and possibly Jamaica. Scholars classing them as Western Taíno note their dialect was mutually intelligible with Classic Taíno, but their society was less centralized than the great chiefdoms of Hispaniola, with no island-wide political structure.

They were the most numerous group on Cuba until around 1450, when Classic Taíno migrants from Hispaniola began occupying eastern Oriente; after the Spanish invasion of Hispaniola refugees flooded in, among them the chief Hatuey, who was captured and burned in Cuba.

Diego Velázquez began the conquest of Cuba in 1511, and within a generation war, enslavement and epidemic had destroyed the island's Native communities, so the Ciboney ceased to exist as a distinct people by the late sixteenth century.
zh:
西沃内人（又译西波内人）是西班牙人到来时古巴中部占主导地位的原住民，在伊斯帕尼奥拉西部、可能还有牙买加也有分布。将其归入西部泰诺的学者指出，西沃内方言与经典泰诺语可以互通，但其社会集权程度低于伊斯帕尼奥拉的大酋邦，没有全岛性的政治组织。

约1450年以前，他们一直是古巴人数最多的族群；此后来自伊斯帕尼奥拉的经典泰诺移民开始占据东部奥连特省，西班牙入侵伊斯帕尼奥拉后更有大批难民涌入，酋长哈图伊便是其中之一，他最终在古巴被逮捕并烧死。

1511年，迭戈·贝拉斯克斯开始征服古巴，短短一代人的时间里，战争、奴役和疫病便摧毁了岛上的原住民社群，到16世纪末，西沃内人已不再作为一个独立族群存在。

en:
The Ciguayo were a non-Taíno people of north-eastern Hispaniola, holding the Samaná Peninsula and the northern mountains called Ciguay. They seem heirs of an older pre-ceramic, pottery-less hunter-gatherer people pushed into this corner by the expanding farming Taíno; Ciguayo itself was a Taíno exonym meaning roughly people of the wild mountain land.

Spanish observers found them taller than the Taíno, their bodies painted black and hair dressed with feathers, and feared them as archers with larger bows and poisoned arrows. Their tongue struck Ramón Pané and Las Casas as wholly unlike the island's common speech, and it was moribund in the sixteenth century, surviving only around Samaná; a single word, tuob for gold, was recorded.

Their last chief, Mayobanex, sheltered the fugitive Taíno cacique Guarionex, but Spanish campaigns overran the country and both men were seized, Guarionex being shipped in chains to Spain in 1502.
zh:
西瓜约人是伊斯帕尼奥拉东北部的非泰诺族群，据有萨马纳半岛和当时名叫西瓜伊的北部山地。他们似乎是更古老的前陶器时代狩猎采集人群的后裔，不制陶器，在务农泰诺人的扩张下被挤压到这个角落；西瓜约本身是泰诺语他称，大意是荒野山地之民。

西班牙观察者发现他们比泰诺人更高大，身涂黑染料，头发饰以羽毛，并畏惧他们的弓箭：其弓更大，箭镞涂毒。拉蒙·帕内和拉斯卡萨斯都注意到西瓜约语与岛上通用语言完全不同，到16世纪已濒临消亡，只在萨马纳一带残存，记录在案的只有一个表示黄金的词tuob。

末代酋长马约瓦内克斯曾收留逃亡的泰诺酋长瓜里奥内克斯，但西班牙征伐踏平了这片土地，两人先后被俘，瓜里奥内克斯于1502年被锁拿装船送往西班牙。

en:
The Circassians, or Adyghe, are indigenous to the Black Sea coast and Kuban basin. Missions made them Christians between the third and fifth centuries; later they were drawn into Alania and Georgian orbits. Called Kassogs, they were driven behind the Kuban by Mongol raids from 1223 and later Golden Horde and Timurid attacks; Timur sacked their lands in 1395.

Circassian mamluks seized Egypt in 1382, founding the Burji dynasty ruling until 1517. Inal the Great united the tribes and created Kabardia in 1434, pushing the Crimean Tatars beyond the Kuban; his sons split the inheritance after 1453.

Sufi preachers and the Russian threat spread Sunni Islam, general by the eighteenth century. The Kabardians shattered a Crimean invasion at Kanzhal in 1708, and the 1739 Treaty of Belgrade recognized Kabardia's independence. From Peter I's time Russian forts crept down the Terek and Kuban, opening a long mountain war of resistance.
zh:
切尔克斯人自称阿迪格，是黑海沿岸和库班河流域原住民。3至5世纪，传教团使他们皈依基督教，后来进入阿兰和格鲁吉亚势力范围。当时称卡索格人，1223年起蒙古入侵，金帐汗国和帖木儿的攻击将他们逐回库班河以南；1395年帖木儿洗劫其土地。

切尔克斯马穆鲁克1382年在埃及夺权，建立存续至1517年的布尔吉王朝。伊纳尔大王统一诸部，1434年建立卡巴尔达，将克里木鞑靼人逐至库班河以北；1453年后其子瓜分遗产。

苏菲传道者和俄国威胁推动逊尼派伊斯兰教传播，18世纪已相当普遍。1708年卡巴尔达人在坎扎尔击败克里木入侵军，1739年《贝尔格莱德条约》承认卡巴尔达独立。彼得一世时，俄国堡垒沿捷列克河和库班河推进，开启山民抗俄战争。

en:
The Coahuilteco, also called Pakawa by the Spanish, were not a single tribe but a loose web of perhaps two hundred small nomadic bands across Coahuila, Tamaulipas and Texas. Most camped along rivers and lagoons, hunting bison and deer and gathering mesquite and agave, with farming only in southern Tamaulipas.

The missionary Damián Massanet in 1690 and 1691 counted thirty-nine groups and found they all spoke the same language; a Coahuilteco worship manual followed in 1760. Once they learned to ride, many bands raided ranches for horses and mules and melted back into the desert.

From the late seventeenth century Lipan Apache expansion drove Coahuilteco refugees into the Spanish missions around San Antonio. As the missions closed from the late eighteenth century, by 1800 only a handful of named bands remained, their identity dissolving into the mission and ranch populations.
zh:
科阿韦尔特科人，西班牙人又称帕卡瓦人，并非单一部落，而是由约两百个游牧小群体结成的松散网络，散布在科阿韦拉、塔毛利帕斯和得克萨斯。他们大多在河流与湖沼畔扎营，猎捕野牛和鹿，采集牧豆和龙舌兰，只有塔毛利帕斯南部略有农业。

传教士达米安·马萨内特在1690和1691年清点出三十九个群体，发现他们讲同一种语言；1760年又有科阿韦尔特科语礼拜手册编成。学会骑马后，许多群体袭击牧场抢夺马匹骡子，再遁入沙漠。

17世纪后期起，利潘阿帕奇人扩张，把科阿韦尔特科难民逐入圣安东尼奥一带的西班牙传教站。18世纪末传教站相继关闭，到1800年只剩寥寥数个仍有名号的群体，其身份逐渐消融在传教站和牧场的居民之中。

en:
The Cochimí were the hunter-gatherer people of the arid central Baja California peninsula, spread from El Rosario to San Javier. With no agriculture or metal, they roamed in autonomous small bands, living on desert game, shellfish and the seasonal pitahaya cactus fruit, whose seeds they recovered and roasted in a second harvest; shamans officiated in capes woven from donated human hair.

Their Cochimí speech forms the Yuman-Cochimí family together with the Yuman languages of the lower Colorado. Spanish seaborne explorers of the sixteenth century made the first fleeting contacts, and from 1699 the Jesuits built a mission chain from San Javier, reaching Santa María by 1767.

When the crown expelled the Jesuits in 1768 the Franciscans and Dominicans took over, but epidemics had already shattered the Cochimí communities, whose surviving families were absorbed into the mission settlements.
zh:
科奇米人是下加利福尼亚半岛中部干旱地带的狩猎采集族群，分布北起埃尔罗萨里奥，南至圣哈维尔。他们没有农业和金属器，以自治小群体游走荒漠，靠沙漠猎物、贝类和季节性的皮特阿亚仙人掌果为生，甚至把仙人掌籽淘出烤熟，称为第二次收获；萨满身披人发编织的斗篷主持仪式。

科奇米语与科罗拉多河下游的尤曼语族共同组成尤曼—科奇米语系。16世纪西班牙海上探险家与他们有过短暂接触；从1699年起，耶稣会修建一连串传教站，以圣哈维尔为起点，到1767年延伸至圣玛丽亚。

1768年王室驱逐耶稣会后，方济各会和多明我会先后接手，但传染病早已重创科奇米社群，幸存家族被并入传教定居点。

en:
The Cocopah, who call themselves Xawiƚƚ Kwñchawaay, the people of the cloudy river, and are also known as Kwapa, are a Yuman people of the lower Colorado River delta, where the river meets the Gulf of California between Arizona, Sonora and Baja California.

Their Patayan ancestors farmed the annual floodplain and combined maize and bean planting with hunting, fishing and gathering, and the historic Cocopah kept this riverine life, paddling tule-reed rafts through the delta and walking upland trails to visit Paipai and Kumeyaay kin.

In 1540 Hernando de Alarcón became the first European to meet them, finding tall warriors armed with clubs and bows who greeted the ships with gifts of shells and food; Oñate's expedition recorded their name in 1605. Their Cocopah language belongs to the Delta-California branch of the Yuman family, within the wider Hokan grouping.
zh:
哈维希‑库尼查瓦伊人即通称的科科帕人，意为云河之民，又称夸帕人，是科罗拉多河下游三角洲的尤曼语族群，家园在科罗拉多河注入加利福尼亚湾的河口地带，横跨亚利桑那、索诺拉和下加利福尼亚三地。

他们的祖先是帕塔扬文化的农人，在每年泛滥的滩地上种植玉米和菜豆，兼营狩猎、捕鱼和采集；历史上的科科帕人延续这种河畔生活，撑着香蒲草筏穿行三角洲，还沿山地古道探望派派人和库梅亚伊人的亲族。

1540年，埃尔南多·德·阿拉尔孔成为第一个见到他们的欧洲人，发现这些高大的武士手持棍棒弓箭，以贝壳和食物相赠；1605年奥尼亚特的探险队记下了他们的名字。科科帕语属尤曼语系的三角洲—加利福尼亚分支，归入更宽泛的霍坎语群。

en:
The Collique, also called Colli, were the lords of the lower and middle Chillon valley on the central Peruvian coast, holding from sea to Chuquicoto on the Canta border. Their polity, flourishing from about 900 to 1470, was ruled by a curaca titled Collicapac from the fortress of Collique.

Warlike, they fought repeated wars over water and farmland, once raiding into the Lima valley; the Huarochiri Manuscript records a war with the Checa and Concha of the Yauyos, in which they lost part of their highland territory, though trading and building irrigation works with the Canta.

When Tupac Yupanqui's army entered the valley they refused to submit, trusting their fortress. The Inca stormed it, killed Collicapac and his warriors, and resettled the survivors; mitimaes colonists were brought in, an Ichma lord placed over the valley, and the fortress replaced by the tambo of Tambo Inga.
zh:
科利克人又称科利人，是秘鲁中部沿海奇永河中下游的统治者，领地从海边延伸到与坎塔接壤的丘基科托。其政权约900至1470年间兴盛，科利卡帕克首领以科利克要塞实行统治。

科利人尚武，为水源和耕地连年征战，一度攻入利马河谷；《瓦罗奇里手稿》记载了他们与尧约斯的切卡人和孔查人的战争，其间失去部分高地领土，但仍与坎塔人通商并共同修建灌溉工程。

图帕克·尤潘基的军队进入河谷时，科利人自恃要塞坚固拒绝臣服。印加人攻克要塞，杀死科利卡帕克和他的战士，迁走幸存者，又迁入米蒂马埃斯移民，任命一位伊奇马首领统辖河谷，要塞则被坦博印加驿寨取代。

en:
The Esto'k Gna, who called themselves Estok, were known to the Spanish as the Comecrudo or Carrizo. They held the Río Bravo delta in northern Tamaulipas and southern Texas, and spoke extinct Comecrudan tongues, grouped within Coahuiltecan but distinct from Coahuilteco.

Seasonally seminomadic, they wintered in canyons and moved each spring to the Sabinas to fish, hunting with bows and a few traded muskets. They enter the written record in 1747, when their leader Captain Santiago answered Escandón's smoke signals and named thirty native bands along the lower river.

A mission was founded near Reynosa in 1749, and in 1750 Escandón counted 149 Comecrudo settled there; when Reynosa moved in 1802 most families stayed on the old bank. They bore Comanche and Kiowa raids from the plains, and an 1827 boundary commission left the last detailed portrait of their daily life.
zh:
埃斯托克纳人自称埃斯托克，西班牙人称他们为科梅克鲁多或卡里索人。他们占据塔毛利帕斯北部与得克萨斯南部的布拉沃河下游三角洲，讲已消亡的科梅克鲁多诸语，归入科阿韦尔特卡语群，但与科阿韦尔特科语不同。

他们过着季节性半游牧生活，冬天在峡谷过冬，春天迁往萨维纳斯河捕鱼，以弓箭和少量交易得来的火枪狩猎。1747年他们首次见于文字记载：首领圣地亚哥上尉响应埃斯坎东的烟火信号，报出沿河三十个土著群体的名号。

1749年雷诺萨附近建立传教站，1750年埃斯坎东清点出当地定居的科梅克鲁多人有149口；1802年雷诺萨城迁移时，大多数家庭仍留在旧河岸。他们承受来自平原的科曼奇人和基奥瓦人袭掠，1827年一支边界考察队留下了关于其日常生活最后一份详细记录。

en:
The Coos are an Indigenous people of the southwest Oregon coast, whose forty to fifty villages clustered around Coos Bay and North Bend. Their combined population has been estimated at about two thousand in 1780.

They spoke two related tongues, Hanis and Miluk, forming the small Coosan family, often grouped with Oregon Penutian; the name Coos may derive from a Hanis word for south or an Athabaskan word for bay. Hunters, fishers and gatherers of the estuaries and forests, they enlivened village life with foot and canoe races and dice games.

They first appear in European records in February 1806, when William Clark, wintering at Fort Clatsop with Lewis and Clark, heard of the Cook-koo-oose nation and met Coos captives held by the Clatsop and Tillamook, noting that they did not flatten their infants' heads as neighbouring peoples did.
zh:
库斯人是俄勒冈西南海岸的原住民，四五十座村庄集中在库斯湾和北本德一带。据估计，1780年两支库斯人合计约有两千人。

他们讲哈尼斯语和米卢克语两种相近语言，组成小小的库斯语族，常归入俄勒冈佩努蒂语群；库斯一名可能来自哈尼斯语意为南方的词，也可能来自阿萨巴斯卡语意为海湾的词。他们在河口湾与森林间狩猎、捕鱼、采集，村落里流行赛跑、独木舟竞速和掷骰游戏。

欧洲人对他们的最早记载在1806年2月：随刘易斯与克拉克探险队在克拉特索普堡过冬的威廉·克拉克听说了库库乌斯族，见到被克拉特索普人和蒂拉穆克人掳获的库斯俘虏，还注意到他们不像邻族那样压平婴儿前额。

en:
The Coosa were a Muskogean-speaking people of the South Appalachian Mississippian culture, whose paramount chiefdom was centered on the Coosawattee River in northwestern Georgia. Their capital, with a plaza and three platform mounds, ruled eight villages and headed a confederation of seven or more smaller chiefdoms stretching some four hundred miles across northern Georgia, eastern Tennessee and Alabama, perhaps fifty thousand people.

Hernando de Soto passed through in 1540 and found fertile gardens and well-stocked towns; Spanish expeditions under Tristán de Luna (1560) and Juan Pardo (1566–1568) followed.

Old World diseases then emptied the countryside: by the late sixteenth century the core lands had been abandoned, and the survivors regrouped in fortified villages on the Coosa River in Alabama. The town of Coosa lived on as one of the four mother towns of the Muscogee Creek confederacy.
zh:
库萨人是操马斯科吉语的南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化族群，其最高酋长国以佐治亚西北部的库萨瓦蒂河为中心。都城设有广场和三座台庙，直辖八座村镇，统领七个或更多小酋长国组成的联盟，绵亘约四百英里，横跨佐治亚北部、田纳西东部与阿拉巴马，总人口可能达五万。

1540年埃尔南多·德·索托经过此地，见到丰饶园圃和储粮充足的村镇；1560年特里斯坦·德·卢纳和1566—1568年胡安·帕尔多的西班牙远征队先后抵达。

此后旧大陆疫病使乡野人口锐减，到16世纪末核心地带已被废弃，幸存者退守阿拉巴马库萨河畔设防的村落。库萨镇后来成为马斯科吉克里克联盟四大母镇之一。

en:
The Copts are Egypt's native Christian people, descended from the ancient Egyptians and settled chiefly in Cairo, Alexandria and the Nile valley, especially Upper Egypt. Their language Coptic is the last stage of ancient Egyptian, written in an alphabet based on Greek; after the Arab conquest of 641 Arabic gradually replaced it in daily life, while Coptic survived in the liturgy.

Christianity reached Egypt in the first century through Saint Mark, and the Egyptian desert birthed Christian monasticism through Anthony and Pachomius. After the Council of Chalcedon in 451 the Egyptian church broke from the empire's to become the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria.

Under the caliphs and later the Mamluks, Copts paid the jizya and endured cycles of tolerance and persecution with repeated tax revolts; they ceased to form a majority after the fourteenth century. Under Ottoman rule they were grouped in the Armenian millet; Muhammad Ali opened army and state service to them in the early nineteenth century, improving their position.
zh:
科普特人是埃及本土的基督教民族，系古埃及人后裔，聚居在开罗、亚历山大及尼罗河谷地尤其是上埃及。他们的传统语言科普特语是古埃及语的最后阶段，用以希腊字母为基础的文字书写；641年阿拉伯征服后，阿拉伯语逐渐取代其日常位置，科普特语则作为礼拜用语留存。

基督教于1世纪由圣马可传入埃及，埃及沙漠还因圣安东尼和帕科缪而成为基督教修道制度的摇篮。451年迦克墩公会议后，埃及教会与帝国教会决裂，发展为亚历山大科普特正教会。

在历代哈里发及后来的马穆鲁克统治下，科普特人缴纳吉兹亚税，在宽容与迫害的交替中数次起义，14世纪以后不再占埃及人口的多数。奥斯曼统治时期他们被归入亚美尼亚米勒特，19世纪初穆罕默德·阿里向他们开放军队和公职，处境有所改善。

en: The Coremas were an Indigenous people of western Paraíba, counted among the Cariri nation and also named in lists of the Tarairiú tribes. They held the valley of the Piancó River, where their principal chief Piancó gave his name to the Vale do Piancó, and the Portuguese village that grew up on their lands became the town of Coremas.
zh: 科雷马斯人是帕拉伊巴西部的原住民，被归入卡里里族，也出现在塔拉伊留联盟诸部的名单中。他们住在皮安科河谷，主要酋长皮安科的名字成为该谷名称皮安科谷的由来；在他们土地上发展起来的葡萄牙村落后来成为科雷马斯镇。

en:
The Cornish, who call themselves Kernowyon, are the Brittonic people of the south-western peninsula, heirs of Dumnonia's Dumnonii. Cut off from the Welsh by the Saxon victory at Deorham, they kept their Brythonic speech, almost mutually intelligible with Breton. Athelstan fixed the Tamar border in 936; by the late tenth century Cornwall had been incorporated into the English kingdom, keeping its own language and customs.

Tin mining shaped life through Stannary courts and parliaments under royal privilege, and in 1337 Edward III made the earldom a duchy for his son the Black Prince.

English advance met resistance: the 1497 rebellion under Michael An Gof and the 1549 Prayer Book Rebellion, whose defeat broke Cornish as a community language. Dolly Pentreath, popularly its last monolingual speaker, died in 1777; Methodist chapels sustained their identity and miners carried their craft abroad.
zh:
康沃尔人自称Kernowyon，是西南半岛的布立吞人，为杜姆诺尼亚的杜姆诺尼人后裔。撒克逊人在迪奥勒姆之战获胜，切断他们与威尔士人的联系，他们便保住布立吞语，这种语言与布列塔尼语几乎可以互通。936年阿塞尔斯坦以塔马河为界，到10世纪末康沃尔被并入英格兰王国，仍保留自己的语言和风俗。

采锡业塑造了当地生活，斯坦纳里法庭和议会在王室特权下治理矿区；1337年爱德华三世把伯爵领升格为公爵领，封给儿子黑太子。

英语的进逼激起反抗：1497年迈克尔·安·戈夫领导的叛乱，以及1549年的祈祷书叛乱；后者被镇压后，康沃尔语作为社群语言崩坏。民间传说中最后只会康沃尔语的多莉·彭特里思于1777年去世；循道宗小教堂维系着他们的认同，矿工也把手艺带到海外。

en:
The Corsicans are the Romance people of the Mediterranean island of Corsica, heirs of the ancient Corsi who gave it its Roman name, later mixed with Roman, Lombard and Frankish settlers. In 1337 the island was held by Genoa, after Pisa's rule; coastal villages suffered centuries of Barbary slave raids, while the pastoral interior kept a society of clan loyalty and vendetta.

Corsicans served as mercenaries and condottieri, fighting at Lepanto in 1571, and Sampiero Corso led French-backed revolts against Genoa in the 1550s. Their Corsu tongue is an Italo-Dalmatian language akin to medieval Tuscan, and Italian long remained the island's written and official language.

In 1755 Pasquale Paoli proclaimed a Corsican Republic, with a constitution and university at Corte, but Genoa sold its rights to France in 1768 and French troops overran the island in 1769, Napoleon Bonaparte's birth year at Ajaccio.
zh:
科西嘉人是地中海科西嘉岛的罗曼语民族，源自古科尔西部落，岛名来自该部落，后来融合罗马人、伦巴第人和法兰克人移民。1337年，该岛在比萨之后落入热那亚统治；沿海村庄数百年间屡遭柏柏尔人掳掠为奴，以牧为生的内陆维持宗族忠诚和血亲复仇的社会。

科西嘉人充当雇佣兵和佣兵队长，参加1571年勒班陀海战；桑皮耶罗·科尔索在16世纪50年代领导法国支持的反热那亚起义。科西嘉语属意大利-达尔马提亚语支，近似中世纪托斯卡纳语，意大利语长期是岛上的书面和官方语言。

1755年，帕斯夸莱·保利宣布成立科西嘉共和国，颁布宪法并在科尔泰创办大学；热那亚1768年把对该岛的权利卖给法国，法军1769年占领全岛，同年拿破仑·波拿巴出生在阿雅克肖。

en:
The Cossacks take their name from Turkic kazak, meaning a free man, and began as bands of runaway serfs, townsmen and adventurers settling from the fifteenth century in the steppe called the Wild Fields, beyond Polish, Lithuanian and Tatar lords. On the lower Dnieper they built the Zaporozhian Sich, whose rada assembly elected an ataman and admitted any newcomer who accepted Orthodox Christianity. Communities on the Don became the Don Host.

In self-governing stanitsas, granted land for frontier service, they guarded against Crimean and Nogai raiders: the Polish crown created the Registered Cossacks in 1572, and Don Cossacks under Yermak opened Siberia's conquest in the 1580s.

Repeated revolts included Bohdan Khmelnytsky's rising of 1648, which created the Hetmanate and brought the 1654 Pereyaslav agreement with Muscovy. After Mazepa's defection and the destruction of the Sich in 1775, their freedoms were curbed, many were resettled to the Kuban and Danube, and hosts became Russian regiments.
zh:
哥萨克的名字来自突厥语卡扎克，意为自由人。15世纪起，逃亡农奴、市民和冒险者在波兰、立陶宛与鞑靼领主势力之外、人称蛮荒原野的草原落脚。他们在第聂伯河下游建起扎波罗热谢契，拉达大会选举阿塔曼，凡接受东正教的来者皆可入伙。顿河聚落发展为顿河军。

哥萨克以自治集镇斯坦尼察编户，以戍边军役换取土地，负责抵御克里米亚与诺盖袭扰：波兰王室1572年设立注册哥萨克，顿河哥萨克则在1580年代随叶尔马克开启征服西伯利亚。

起义屡次发生，其中1648年波格丹·赫梅利尼茨基起义催生盖特曼国，促成1654年与莫斯科的佩列亚斯拉夫协议。马泽帕倒戈、1775年谢契被摧毁后，哥萨克的自由被收束，许多人被迁往库班和多瑙河，诸军屯被改编为俄国军团。

en:
Coweta was a Muscogee town on the lower Chattahoochee River, in what the Spanish called Apalachicola Province, and one of four mother towns of the Muscogee Confederacy. Its valley supported Lamar farming villages with platform mounds from the fourteenth century.

With other Chattahoochee towns, Coweta moved east into central Georgia in the late seventeenth century, where the English called its people Ochese Creek Indians, and returned to the Chattahoochee after the Yamasee War of 1715, becoming a leading Lower Creek market town. Its mico Hoboyetly, Emperor Brim to the British, shifted British, French and Spanish alliances through the war until his death in 1733.

The later Coweta chief William McIntosh signed the Treaty of Indian Springs in 1825, surrendering most of the Muscogees' remaining land, and was executed by men of the Creek National Council the same year, on the eve of forced removal to Indian Territory.
zh:
考维塔是查特胡奇河下游的马斯科吉城镇，地处西班牙人所称的阿巴拉契科拉省，是马斯科吉联盟四大母镇之一。早在14世纪，这一河谷就有带台庙的拉马尔文化农耕村落。

17世纪末，考维塔与查特胡奇河诸镇东迁佐治亚中部，英国人称之为奥切斯溪印第安人；1715年雅马西战争后迁回查特胡奇河，成为下克里克的主要贸易城镇。酋长霍博耶特利（英称皇帝布里姆）在战争中周旋于英、法、西三方之间，直至1733年去世。

后来的考维塔酋长威廉·麦金托什于1825年签署《印第安斯普林斯条约》，割让马斯科吉人残余的大部分土地，同年被克里克全国委员会的人处死，时值强制迁往印第安领地的前夜。

en:
The Crimeans, or Crimean Tatars, are the Turkic people of the Crimean peninsula, forged from the Tauri, Goths, Greeks and Khazars and the Cumans and other Kipchak nomads.

In 1337 Crimea was the Crimean Ulus of the Golden Horde; in the fourteenth century its people largely adopted Islam and Kipchak speech dominated. As the Horde fragmented, clans invited Hacı Giray to the throne in 1441, founding the Crimean Khanate; after the Ottoman conquest of 1475 the khans ruled as vassals. The khanate grew rich on the slave trade through Kefe, while Bakhchisaray became a centre of learning.

Three ways of life shaped them: steppe herdsmen, mountain villagers and Oghuz-speaking coastal dwellers. Defeat in the Russo-Turkish War of 1768 to 1774 ended Ottoman protection; in 1783 Russia annexed the khanate, and by 1800 between one and three hundred thousand Crimeans had fled or been driven into Ottoman exile.
zh:
克里米亚人即克里米亚鞑靼人，是克里米亚半岛上的突厥语族群，由陶里人、哥特人、希腊人、可萨人与库曼人等钦察游牧民融合而成。

1337年，克里米亚是金帐汗国的克里米亚兀鲁思；14世纪，兀鲁思民众大多改宗伊斯兰教，钦察语渐占上风。金帐汗国瓦解后，部落于1441年迎立哈吉·格来为汗，建立克里米亚汗国；1475年奥斯曼征服后，汗成为附庸。汗国凭借克法港的奴隶贸易致富，巴赫奇萨赖则成为学术中心。

三种生活方式塑造了他们：草原牧民、山地村民，以及说乌古斯语的沿海居民。1768年至1774年俄土战争的失败终结了奥斯曼的庇护，俄国于1783年吞并汗国；到1800年，已有十万至三十万克里米亚人逃离或被驱赶到奥斯曼境内流亡。

en:
The Croatan, later also called the Hatteras, were a small Algonquian people of the North Carolina Outer Banks, around Roanoke and Hatteras, perhaps a branch or ally of the Roanoke. Their name may mean council town; werowance chiefs ruled by persuasion and gifts.

They met John White's expeditions of 1585 and 1587, and when White returned in 1590 the abandoned Roanoke settlement held only CROATOAN carved on its palisade, which he read as a sign the colonists had sheltered on Croatoan Island.

They kept the friendship first shown by the guide Manteo, but disease and displacement shrank them to perhaps eighty by 1701. In the Tuscarora War of 1711 they fought on the colonial side and paid heavily, many driven from the islands; by the mid-eighteenth century they had ceased to exist as a separate tribe, their descendants absorbed into neighbouring Algonquian communities and, by uncertain tradition, the Lumbee.
zh:
克洛坦人（后来亦称哈特勒斯人）是北卡罗来纳外滩群岛的阿尔冈昆语小族群，居于罗阿诺克、哈特勒斯诸岛，可能是罗阿诺克人的分支或盟友。族名或意为“议事镇”，首领称维罗安斯，以说服和馈赠治国。

约翰·怀特1585年和1587年两度探险时与他们接触；1590年怀特重返，罗阿诺克定居点的栅栏上只刻着CROATOAN，他据此判断“失落的殖民者”已往克洛阿坦岛避难。

他们延续了向导曼蒂奥结下的友谊，但疫病和流离使他们到1701年可能仅余八十人。1711年塔斯卡洛拉战争中他们站在殖民者一方作战，代价惨重，不少人被逐出岛屿；到18世纪中叶，他们已不再作为独立部落存在，后裔融入邻近的阿尔冈昆社群，又有不确定的传说称其融入卢姆比人。

en:
The Croats are a South Slavic people settling the eastern Adriatic hinterland, Dalmatia and Pannonia in the late sixth and early seventh centuries, absorbing romanized coastal folk. Their dukes accepted Frankish and Byzantine overlordship while keeping their own rulers; Christianity took root early, and in 879 the pope recognized Duke Branimir as an independent prince.

Around 925 Tomislav became the first Croatian king; the Trpimirović dynasty raised the kingdom to its height, with Glagolitic writing preserved on the Baška tablet of about 1100. A succession crisis carried the crown to the Hungarian Árpáds in 1102, yet the kingdom kept the Sabor assembly and Ban viceroy.

In 1337 Croatian nobles held land contested between the Hungarian crown and Venice, holder of Dalmatian cities; the Mongols had sacked Zagreb in 1242. Ottoman conquests after 1463 reduced Croatian lands to a frontier, and after Mohács in 1526 the crown passed to the Habsburgs, under whom the Croats guarded the frontier against the Ottomans for three centuries.
zh:
克罗地亚人是南斯拉夫民族，6世纪末7世纪初定居亚得里亚海东岸腹地、达尔马提亚和潘诺尼亚，融合沿海罗马化居民。公爵先后臣属法兰克和拜占庭，却保留自己的统治世系；基督教很早扎根，879年教皇承认公爵布拉尼米尔为独立君主。

约925年托米斯拉夫成为首位克罗地亚国王，特尔皮米罗维奇王朝把王国推向鼎盛，约1100年的《巴什卡石碑》保留着格拉哥里文字。1102年继承危机使王冠落入匈牙利阿尔帕德王朝，王国保留萨博尔议会和巴安总督。

1337年，克罗地亚贵族治理匈牙利与威尼斯争夺之地，威尼斯已占达尔马提亚城；1242年蒙古人曾洗劫萨格勒布。1463年后奥斯曼扩张把克罗地亚压为防御前沿，1526年莫哈赤战役后王冠归哈布斯堡家族，此后三百年克罗地亚人在边疆对抗奥斯曼人。

en:
The Cueva were the principal Indigenous people of the eastern Panamanian isthmus when Europeans arrived, holding Darién and both coasts from the Atrato to Chame. Rival chiefdoms included Pocorosa, Comagre and Careta on the Caribbean and Chochama on the Pacific.

Cueva was the Spanish name for their speech, now often treated as a lingua franca shared by several groups; its links to the Chibchan, Choco and Arawak families remain debated.

After 1510 settlers including Vasco Nunez de Balboa reached them from Santa Maria la Antigua; at Comagre he heard of a southern sea and reached the Pacific in 1513. War, epidemics, slaving and forced labour broke them within a generation: by the 1530s they had ceased to exist as a people, fugitives taking to the mountains or joining their enemies the Guna, who filled the empty lands in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
zh:
奎瓦人是欧洲人到来时巴拿马地峡东部最主要的原住民，据有达连及两海沿岸，从阿特拉托河直到查梅。彼此争战的酋邦中，加勒比岸有波科罗萨、科马格雷和卡雷塔，太平洋岸有乔查马。

奎瓦是西班牙人对其语言的称呼，晚近不少学者视其为各族群共用的通用语，它与奇布查、乔科、阿拉瓦克三大语系的关系仍无定论。

1510年后，包括巴尔沃亚在内的定居者从圣玛丽亚·拉安提瓜前来；在科马格雷他听说南方有大海，遂于1513年穿越地峡抵达太平洋。战争、疫病、掳奴和苦役在一代人之间摧毁了奎瓦人：到16世纪30年代他们已不再作为独立民族存在，余者或遁入深山，或投奔世敌古纳人；古纳人在17至18世纪间西扩，占据了空置的土地。

en:
The Cuicas were one of the two main branches of the Timoto–Cuica people, the most advanced Indigenous society of the Venezuelan Andes, whose language and ways linked them to the Chibcha world of the Muisca. The Cuicas held the mountains and foothills around Trujillo and the adjacent plains, while their Timote kinsmen centred on Mérida.

They built permanent villages of stone and timber houses ringed by irrigated stone terraces, grew maize, potatoes and sweet yucca, made anthropomorphic ceramics and gold objects, and used cacao beans as currency in trade with Arawak and Carib neighbours.

In 1549 the Cuicas and Timotes forged a war alliance at Escuque, defeated a Spanish column in open battle and drove it back to El Tocuyo. In colonial times their old settlements were reorganized into Indian parishes and few place names kept their original forms.
zh:
奎卡斯人是蒂莫托—奎卡斯人的两大支系之一，后者是委内瑞拉安第斯山区最发达的原住民社会，语言和风习都与穆伊斯卡人的奇布查文化圈相连。奎卡斯人占据特鲁希略一带的山地、丘陵及邻近平原，亲缘的蒂莫特人则以梅里达为中心。

他们的村落由石木房屋构成，四周环绕引水灌溉的石砌梯田，种植玉米、马铃薯和甜木薯，能制作人形陶器和金器，并用可可豆作货币，与阿拉瓦克和加勒比邻族贸易。

1549年，奎卡斯人与蒂莫特人在埃斯库克结成战时同盟，在野战中击败一支西班牙队伍，把他们逐回埃尔托库约。殖民时代，他们的旧聚落被改组为印第安人教区，保留下来的原地名寥寥无几。

en:
The Cuitlatecs were an indigenous people of the Tierra Caliente lowlands of Guerrero, in the Balsas river basin, whose chief towns at the time of the Spanish arrival included Ajuchitlán, Totolapan and Cutzamala.

Their language, Cuitlatec, was a language isolate unrelated to any other surviving Mexican tongue, and some scholars link its speakers to the earlier Mezcala culture of the region. Their name is a Mexica exonym, coined from the Nahuatl word for excrement.

The sixteenth-century Relaciones geográficas still recorded Cuitlatec in Ajuchitlán and Tetela del Río and along much of the Costa Grande, and around 1550 the parish priest Martín de Espinosa y Monzón wrote a grammar of the language while serving at Ajuchitlán.
zh:
奎特拉特克人是格雷罗州火地低地、巴尔萨斯河流域的原住民，西班牙人到来时其主要城镇包括阿胡奇特兰、托托拉潘和库察马拉。

他们的语言奎特拉特克语是孤立语言，与墨西哥其他现存语言都没有亲属关系，有学者认为这支族群与当地更早的梅斯卡拉文化有关。其名字是墨西加人取的外来称谓，源自纳瓦特尔语中意为粪便的词。

16世纪的《地理报告》仍记载阿胡奇特兰、滨河特特拉以及大海岸大部通行奎特拉特克语；约1550年，在阿胡奇特兰任职的神父马丁·德·埃斯皮诺萨-蒙松还编写了一部该语言的语法书。

en:
The Cumans, called Polovtsians by the Rus', were the western branch of the Cuman-Kipchak confederation, Turkic nomads who dominated the Pontic and Caspian steppe for two centuries, trading and fighting with Rus' and Byzantium.

The Mongol advance shattered them: in 1239 Khan Köten led many into Hungary, and after Cuman rule ended in 1241, those who stayed east joined the Golden Horde, while others fled to Bulgaria, Byzantium and Egypt, where Cuman-born Mamluks such as Baybars rose to the sultanate.

In Hungary they settled on the Great Plain in districts called Greater and Little Cumania, keeping chiefs, herds and Kipchak speech; princess Elizabeth became queen in 1270, mother of Ladislaus IV. Later they farmed and spoke Hungarian, yet kept privileges until around 1702, when districts were sold to the Teutonic Order. In 1745 the Cuman and Jasz bought their freedom as free farmers, not serfs.
zh:
库曼人被罗斯人称为波洛韦茨人，是库曼—钦察联盟的西支，属突厥语游牧民，两个世纪里统有黑海至里海的大草原，与基辅罗斯、拜占庭战和交替。

蒙古人摧毁了他们的世界：1239年可汗忽滩率部众迁入匈牙利；1241年库曼草原统治终结，东留的族人并入金帐汗国，另一些人逃到保加利亚、拜占庭和埃及，出身库曼的马穆鲁克人拜巴尔斯在埃及登上苏丹之位。

迁入匈牙利的库曼人安置在大平原上仍称大、小库马尼亚的地区，保留酋长、畜群和钦察语；库曼公主伊丽莎白1270年成为王后，是拉斯洛四世之母。中世纪后期他们渐转定居农耕、改用匈牙利语，仍保有特权，至1702年前后领地被卖给条顿骑士团而丧失；1745年库曼人与雅斯人集体赎回自由，成为自由农而非农奴。

en:
The Cumanagoto were a Cariban people of the Caribbean coast of eastern Venezuela, around the gulf of Cumaná and valleys that became the province of Nueva Andalucía. They farmed maize, manioc and sweet potatoes, kept coca trees, hunted and gathered; they lived in palisaded villages with polygynous chiefs. Like other coastal peoples they worshipped the sun and moon and held the frog lord of waters, keeping frogs as pets but whipping them when rain failed.

Resistance drew Spanish campaigns into the Tuy valleys in 1579 and 1580. Between 1633 and 1654 the Catalan Joan Orpí built his New Catalonia, or Province of the Cumanagotos, on their lands before it merged into Nueva Andalucía in 1654.

Tribal organization broke in the seventeenth century, though a remnant kept its identity: by 1822 only about twenty-six were counted west of Cumaná, their descendants absorbed into the mixed population of Anzoátegui and Sucre.
zh:
库马纳戈托人是委内瑞拉东部加勒比海岸的加勒比语族群，分布在库马纳湾一带以及后来成为新安达卢西亚省的各个河谷。他们种植玉米、木薯和甘薯，栽种古柯，兼事狩猎采集；村庄设有木栅，酋长多妻。和海岸其他族群一样，他们崇拜日月，奉青蛙为水神：平日养蛙为宠，雨水不继时便鞭打青蛙。

他们的反抗引来西班牙征讨，1579和1580年西班牙军两度攻入图伊河谷。1633至1654年间，加泰罗尼亚人胡安·奥尔皮在他们的土地上建立新加泰罗尼亚，又称库马纳戈托省，1654年并入新安达卢西亚。

部落组织在17世纪瓦解，但日渐稀少的遗民仍保持身份：到1822年，库马纳以西登记在册的仅约二十六人，后裔融入安索阿特吉和苏克雷的混血人口。

en:
The Cunco were a coastal branch of the Williche, the southernmost arm of the Mapuche family, holding the rainy forested shore and Chilean Coast Range between Valdivia and the Maullín River.

They spoke Mapudungun, farmed maize, potatoes and quinoa, raised chilihueques, and spent each spring and summer on the coast gathering shellfish, hunting sea lions and fishing from wooden dalca boats, dwelling in large ruca huts under small local chiefs.

After the great Mapuche rising of 1598 they became the most relentless enemies of the Spaniards in Osorno, besieging the city until its settlers abandoned it in 1602 and then destroying it. Through the rest of the seventeenth century they harried every party trying to pass between Valdivia and Chiloé, keeping the forested coast a closed and warlike frontier.
zh:
昆科人是维利切人的一支，而维利切人又是马普切大家庭最南端的支系。他们住在瓦尔迪维亚到马乌林河之间多雨多林的海岸与智利海岸山脉一带。

他们讲马普敦贡语，种植玉米、马铃薯和藜麦，饲养奇利韦克家畜，每年春夏前往海边采集贝类、猎捕海狮，乘木制达尔卡船捕鱼，在地方小酋长治理下的大鲁卡茅屋里聚居。

1598年马普切人大起义后，他们成为奥索尔诺西班牙人最凶悍的对手，长期围城，直到1602年殖民者弃城而走，城市随即被毁。整个17世纪，他们不断截击试图在瓦尔迪维亚与奇洛埃之间往来的西班牙队伍，使这片森林海岸始终是一道封闭而好战的边界。

en: The Cūnhuà, or Gelong, are the people of the lower Changhua River in western Hainan, around present-day Dongfang and Changjiang, who speak Cun, a Kra–Dai language of the Hlai branch. They descend from Han settlers who reached the island after its Western Han garrison in 110 BC and intermarried with the indigenous Li, and are officially counted as Han.
zh: 仡隆人又称村人、哥隆人，聚居于海南岛西部昌化江下游的东方市和昌江黎族自治县一带，说属于壮侗语系黎语支的村话，即仡隆语。他们的祖先是公元前110年西汉在海南岛设治后陆续迁来的汉族移民，与当地黎族通婚融合，所以村话比其他黎语支语言有更多汉语借词，而仡隆人在民族划分上仍被算作汉族。

en:
The Curonians were Baltic sailors and pirates settled on the Baltic coast from the fifth century, in lands still bearing their name: Courland in western Latvia and the Curonian Spit, Grobiņa their early centre. Norse sources record raids on Sweden with Estonians; in 854 they resisted Swedish tribute, defending Apuolė for eight days.

They resisted the Livonian Crusade, attacking Riga in 1210 and again in 1228 with the Semigallians. Northern Curonians made peace in 1230 under ruler Lammekinus, but the south fought on; at Durbe in 1260 Curonian troops deserted the Livonian Order and helped the Samogitians win. Resistance ended in 1266 with Courland divided between the Order and the Archbishop of Riga.

Northern Curonians merged into the Latvians, southerners into the Samogitians; their language was extinct by the sixteenth century, leaving traces in Samogitian and Latvian dialects.
zh:
库罗尼亚人是波罗的部落，擅长航海与劫掠，5世纪起定居波罗的海沿岸，其名留在拉脱维亚西部的库罗尼亚（库尔兰）和库尔斯沙嘴，早期中心为格罗宾。诺斯史料记载他们与爱沙尼亚人联手袭扰瑞典；854年他们抗拒瑞典索贡，在阿普奥莱要塞坚守八天。

立窝尼亚十字军期间他们坚持抵抗，1210年攻打里加，1228年又与塞米加利亚人联手再攻里加。北部库罗尼亚人1230年在首领拉梅基努斯率领下议和，南部继续作战；1260年杜尔贝战役中库罗尼亚士兵临阵脱离立窝尼亚骑士团，助萨莫吉蒂亚人取胜。1266年抵抗失败，库尔兰被骑士团与里加大主教瓜分。

北部库罗尼亚人融入拉脱维亚人，南部融入萨莫吉蒂亚人；库罗尼亚语到16世纪已经消亡，只在萨莫吉蒂亚和拉脱维亚方言中留下痕迹。

en:
The Cusabo were a loose group of tribes, including the Kussoe, living on the South Carolina coast between Charleston and the Savannah River when English colonists arrived. Their language was poorly recorded and matched none of the neighbouring families, suggesting an isolate, dying out in the eighteenth century.

Charles Town was founded in 1670 in their midst: war with the Kussoe broke out in 1671, and after further fighting the Cusabo were forced to cede land and pay tribute in deerskins. They nevertheless became the colony's Settlement Indians, serving as hunters, scouts and slave-catchers and fighting in the Tuscarora War of 1711 to 1712.

A census of 1715 counted them in five villages with fewer than three hundred people. In the Yamasee War later that year they sided with the colonists, after which most drifted away and merged into the Muscogee or the Catawba.
zh:
库萨博人是包括库索人在内的松散部落群体，英国殖民者到来时居住在查尔斯顿到萨凡纳河之间的南卡罗来纳海岸。他们的语言留存记录很少，与邻近各语系都不相同，可能是一门孤立语言，18世纪消亡。

1670年查尔斯镇建在他们的土地中央：1671年殖民地与库索人开战，经过几番冲突，库萨博人被迫割地，以鹿皮纳贡。尽管如此，他们还是成为殖民地的“定居印第安人”，充当猎人、斥候和逃奴追捕者，并在1711—1712年的塔斯卡罗拉战争中为南卡罗来纳作战。

1715年的人口统计显示他们分布在五座村庄，人口不足三百。同年亚马西战争中他们站在殖民者一边，战后大多数人逐渐离去，并入马斯科吉人或卡托巴人。

en:
The Cuyonon are a Visayan ethnolinguistic group from the low-lying Cuyo Islands in the Sulu Sea, who later settled the northern and central coasts of Palawan. Their language is closely related to Kinaray-a of Panay and served for centuries as the lingua franca of Palawan, understood by Tagbanwa, Agutaynen and other island peoples.

Before the Spanish arrived, Cuyo was ruled by Datu Magbanua and Taytay by the Cabaylo royal family, whose people sheltered the survivors of Magellan's fleet after the Battle of Mactan in 1521.

In the early seventeenth century Augustinian Recollect friars opened missions in Cuyo and Taytay, and the Spanish later walled the church towns and posted garrisons against Moro raiders; the sultan of Brunei ceded southern Palawan to Spain in 1749. Long regarded as an elite among Palawan peoples, the Cuyonon became mostly Roman Catholic.
zh:
库约农人是米沙鄢语族群，原居苏禄海中地势低平的库约群岛，后来定居巴拉望的北部和中部海岸。他们的语言与班乃的基纳拉雅语相近，数百年来一直是巴拉望的通用语，为塔格巴努瓦、阿古塔延能等岛民所通晓。

西班牙人到来之前，库约由达图·马格巴努阿统治，泰泰则由卡巴伊洛王室统治；1521年麦克坦战役后，正是泰泰的居民收留了麦哲伦船队的幸存者。

17世纪初，重整奥斯定会修士在库约和泰泰开设传教站，后来西班牙人又给教堂城镇筑起围墙、派驻守军，以抵御摩洛人的袭掠；1749年，文莱苏丹把南巴拉望割让给西班牙。库约农人长期被视为巴拉望诸族中的上层，后来大多成为罗马天主教徒。

en:
The Czechs are a West Slavic people of Bohemia, Moravia and Czech Silesia, whose ancestors settled there in the 500s and 600s, absorbing remaining Celtic and Germanic peoples. Premyslid dukes built Prague Castle around 880 and from 1198 ruled a Bohemian kingdom drawing German settlers from the later 1200s.

In 1337 John the Blind of Luxembourg held the throne; under his son Charles IV, king from 1346 and emperor from 1355, Prague became imperial capital and in 1348 gained the first university north of the Alps. Jan Hus, burned in 1415, reformed Czech spelling and inspired the Hussite movement, whose armies defended the Bohemian Reformation in wars of 1419 to 1434.

The Kralice Bible of 1579 to 1593 fixed the literary language, but after the White Mountain defeat of 1620, Habsburg re-Catholicization and Germanization exiled scholars such as Komensky, and by the 1700s German dominated public life. National revival rebuilt a written standard with Dobrovsky's 1809 grammar and Jungmann's dictionary.
zh:
捷克人是波希米亚、摩拉维亚和捷克西里西亚的西斯拉夫人，先民6至7世纪定居此地，同化残留凯尔特、日耳曼人。普热米斯尔王朝约880年建布拉格城堡，1198年起统治波希米亚王国，13世纪后期德意志人迁入。

1337年卢森堡盲人约翰在位；其子查理四世1346年即位、1355年加冕皇帝，布拉格成帝国都城，1348年办阿尔卑斯山以北首所大学。扬·胡斯1415年被烧死，改革捷克语正字法并启发胡斯运动，后者于1419至1434年间保卫波希米亚宗教改革。

1579至1593年《克拉利采圣经》确立书面语规范，1620年白山战役战败后，哈布斯堡再天主教化、德意志化使夸美纽斯等流亡，18世纪德语主导公共生活。民族复兴以多布罗夫斯基1809年语法书和荣格曼词典重建标准语。

en:
The Daga are a Papuan people of the Bird's Tail, the southeastern peninsula of New Guinea, whose speech, also called Dimuga or Nawp, gives its name to the small Dagan family of Trans–New Guinea languages. The Dagan languages are spoken in the Meneao Range and are the easternmost Papuan languages on the New Guinea mainland.

Daga-speaking villages lie in the Rabaraba country of Milne Bay Province and in the Abau country of neighbouring Central Province, where the Daga share the mountains with related peoples such as the Maiwa.
zh:
达加人是新几内亚东南半岛“鸟尾”地区的巴布亚族群，他们的语言又称迪穆加语或诺普语，小小的达甘语族（属跨新几内亚语系）便因它得名。达甘诸语通行于梅尼奥岭，是新几内亚大陆上位置最靠东的巴布亚语言。

达加人的村落分布在米尔恩湾省的拉巴尔拉巴一带和相邻中央省的阿包一带，与迈瓦人等亲缘族群共居山地。

en:
The Dagbani, self-styled Dagbamba, are a Gur-speaking people of northern Ghana and Togo, their country Dagbon, its court at Yendi.

Kings claim descent from Tohazie, a hunter said to have come from east of Lake Chad; his descendant Naa Gbewaa settled at Pusiga, and his son Sitobu united the southern farming towns and their earth priests, the Tindaamba. Sitobu's son Naa Nyagsi (1416 to 1432) overthrew many Tindaamba and built Yani Dabari; kings took the title Yaa Naa. Gonja wars drove the court to Yendi, where Naa Zanjina, first Muslim Yaa Naa, defeated the Gonja at Sang in the late 1600s.

Wangara and Dyula traders brought Islam, under Zanjina the court religion; in 1700 the Moliyili school was founded, keeping Dagbani manuscripts in an Arabic-based script. Dagbon grew rich on kola and salt; by 1788 Yendi was described as larger than Kumasi, and women held chiefly titles headed by the Gundo Naa.
zh:
达格邦人（英文常称达贡巴人，自称达格班巴）是加纳北部和多哥说古尔语的民族，其国称达贡，王庭在延迪。

王室自称出自猎人托哈齐：据说他从乍得湖以东迁来，后裔纳·格贝瓦阿定居普西加，其子西托布联合南方农耕城镇及其地神祭司廷丹巴。西托布之子纳·尼亚格西于1416—1432年攻灭众多廷丹巴，营建亚尼·达巴里；国王自此称亚阿纳。后来与贡贾人的战争迫使王庭迁至延迪，第一位穆斯林亚阿纳纳·赞吉纳于17世纪末在桑地击败贡贾人。

旺加拉和迪乌拉商人传入伊斯兰教，赞吉纳时代成为宫廷宗教，1700年创办莫利伊利学堂，用阿拉伯字母抄写达格邦文典籍。达贡靠柯拉果和食盐致富，1788年时延迪被认为比库马西大；女性也可拥有酋长头衔，以贡多·纳为首。

en: The Dahalo are a Cushitic-speaking people of the Kenyan coast around the lower Tana River, remnants, with the neighbouring Aweer and Waata, of East Africa's early hunter-gatherer inhabitants. Formerly elephant hunters dispersed among Swahili and Bantu communities with no villages of their own, they retain click sounds from their older speech in their Cushitic tongue, also called Sanye.
zh: 达哈洛人是肯尼亚沿海塔纳河下游一带的库希特语族群，与邻近的阿维尔人、瓦塔人一样，是东非早期狩猎采集居民的孑遗。他们世代以猎象为生，散居在斯瓦希里人和班图人当中，没有自己的村庄；其库希特语又称桑耶语，保留着古老语言的咂舌音。

en:
The Dai are the Chinese name for Southwestern Tai peoples, notably the Tai Lue, ancestors spreading from Yunnan to the Vietnam–Laos borderlands. They settled river valleys, grew wet rice in stilt villages and organized into muang, chiefly principalities.

In the twelfth century the Tai Lue raised Jinghong. Further south the Black Tai built Ngưu Hống, sending tribute to Vietnam as early as 1067 and fighting the Trần in the early fourteenth century. In 1337 these remained independent Tai muang: Ngưu Hống held the upper Black River.

Ming forces subdued the Black Tai in 1416, and after the Vietnamese reconquest Lê Lợi's 1431–1432 campaigns folded their lands into Hưng Hóa; the Yunnan Tai kept hereditary chieftains under tusi rule. The Yunnan Dai adopted Theravada Buddhism in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries; the Black Tai long kept animist rites and their own script.
zh:
傣是汉人对西南台语诸民族的统称，傣泐等支系的先民从云南南迁，进入越南、老挝边境。他们栖居河谷、种植水稻，住干栏竹楼，以“勐”为单位组成头人治理的小邦。

12世纪，傣泐人建立景龙。更南的黑泰人建立牛吼政权，早在1067年就向越南进贡，14世纪初又与陈朝交兵。1337年这里仍是独立泰邦林立的局面：牛吼据有黑河上游。

明军于1416年平定黑泰，越南复国后黎利于1431—1432年用兵，把黑泰土地并入兴化省；云南傣族在土司制度下保留世袭头人，于15至16世纪改奉上座部佛教，而黑泰人长期保留精灵崇拜和本族文字。

en:
The Djangadi, also written Dainggati or Dunghutti, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Macleay Valley on the northern coast of New South Wales, around the town of Kempsey. Their language Dhanggati belongs to the Yuin-Kuric group within the Pama-Nyungan family.

Shell middens at Clybucca, some heaped into mounds two metres high, an ancient fish trap in Limeburners Creek and a bora ring near Crescent Head trace at least four thousand years of continuous occupation.

Outsiders first reached them in the late 1820s, when ex-convict cedar cutters camped at Euroka Creek from 1827 pushed up the valley after red cedar, and in 1835 Enoch Rudder took up the first European land grant in the Kempsey district, opening the country to pastoral settlement as the period closed.
zh:
丹加蒂人（又拼邓胡蒂）是澳大利亚新南威尔士州北部海岸麦克利河谷的原住民，活动在肯普西镇一带。他们的语言丹加蒂语属于帕马-牛雅语系的尤因-库里克语组。

克莱巴卡的贝丘有些堆成两米高的贝壳丘，莱姆伯纳溪的古代鱼梁和克雷森特角附近的博拉环，都证明人类在此至少连续居住了四千年。

19世纪20年代末，外来者第一次进入他们的土地：1827年起，以尤罗卡溪为营地的获释伐木犯为采伐红椿木深入河谷；1835年，伊诺克·拉德在肯普西区取得第一份欧洲人的土地授予，在本时期结束之际为牧业定居打开了大门。

en:
The Daju are a cluster of related Nilo-Saharan peoples, their seven groups straddling the Chad-Sudan border, their oldest home the Daju Hills in Darfur's Marrah range.

A Daju kingdom emerged perhaps in the twelfth century; tradition recalls a war with Christian Dongola around 1100, after which King Ahmed al-Daj moved his court to Meri. In the fourteenth century the Tunjur overthrew the dynasty: the fugitive king led followers to Dar Sila in Chad, while other bands drifted east to Kordofan, some later reaching the Nuba Hills around Lagowa under Messiria and Ngok Dinka pressure.

The Tunjur brought Islam and Arabic administration; in 1596 their last sultan married into the Fur Keira line, producing the Darfur Sultanate. Most Daju were Muslims by the fifteenth century, though Dar Fur Daju long kept the cult of high god Kalge; they remained millet and sorghum farmers.
zh:
达朱人是若干彼此亲缘的尼罗-撒哈拉语系族群的合称，七个支系分布在乍得与苏丹边界两侧，最古老的家园在达尔富尔迈拉山脉的达朱丘陵。

达朱王国或在12世纪兴起：传说1100年前后它与基督教栋古拉王国交战，国王艾哈迈德·达季随后把王廷迁到梅里。14世纪，通朱尔人推翻达朱王朝：逃亡的国王率追随者西走今乍得的达尔西拉，另一些支系东迁科尔多凡，部分人后来在梅西里亚和恩戈克丁卡压力下退入拉戈瓦一带的努巴山区。

通朱尔人带来伊斯兰教和阿拉伯式行政；1596年末代苏丹与富尔凯拉家族联姻，由此产生达尔富尔苏丹国。到15世纪多数达朱人已成为穆斯林，但达尔富尔达朱人长期保留对至高神卡尔格的崇拜；他们仍以种植小米、高粱为生。

en:
The Dakelh, also called the Carrier and known to themselves as the Yinka Dene, are a Northern Athabaskan, or Dene, people of central British Columbia, around Stuart and Babine lakes and the upper Fraser River. Their Carrier and Babine-Witsuwit'en languages belong to the Northern Athabaskan family; the Wet'suwet'en and Babine are Dakelh branches. Their name refers to water travel; Carrier came from French explorers.

Life followed a seasonal round of salmon, hunting and berries in family hunting territories called keyoh under hereditary chiefs; Dakelh parties carried coastal goods along the grease trails into the interior.

Simon Fraser reached them in 1806; the North West Company built Fort St. James on Stuart Lake, later run by the Hudson's Bay Company. Chief Kw'eh (born around 1755) received Fraser and in 1828 spared his prisoner, the young trader James Douglas, later first governor of the Colony of British Columbia.
zh:
达凯尔人又称卡里尔人，自称因卡德内人，是北方阿萨巴斯卡（德内）族群的一支，生活在不列颠哥伦比亚中部内陆，分布于斯图尔特湖、巴宾湖一带与弗雷泽河上游。他们的卡里尔语和巴宾—韦苏韦滕语同属北方阿萨巴斯卡语系，韦苏韦滕人与巴宾人都是其分支。族名与水上出行有关，卡里尔一名来自法国探险家。

传统生计围绕鲑鱼、狩猎和采果按季节轮换，土地按世袭酋长掌管的家族领地凯约划分，族人沿油脂商道把海岸货物运往内陆。

1806年西蒙·弗雷泽抵达此地，西北公司在斯图尔特湖畔建圣詹姆斯堡，后来由哈德逊湾公司经营。约1755年出生的酋长克韦接待了弗雷泽，1828年赦免了被俘的年轻商人詹姆斯·道格拉斯，后者日后成为不列颠哥伦比亚殖民地首任总督。

en:
The Dalmatians are the Romance-speaking heirs of the romanized Illyrian coast, their walled towns surviving the seventh-century Slavic settlement while the hinterland passed to Croatian tribes. From Zadar to Dubrovnik, these city-states kept Latin law, Catholic worship and the vulgar Latin that became Dalmatian, split into Ragusan of Dubrovnik and Vegliote of Krk.

The cities traded with Italy and Byzantium and passed between Byzantine, Croatian and Hungarian overlords as Venice built an Adriatic empire: Zadar and northern towns accepting Venetian rule, Venetian increasingly displacing Dalmatian in business and administration.

Dubrovnik, called Ragusa, became an independent republic, where Ragusan remained the language of law until the late fifteenth century and the Senate in 1472 protected it against Slavic. In 1337 the Dalmatian towns formed a bilingual coastal civilization, Romance in identity and faith yet interwoven with the Slavic hinterland through commerce and intermarriage.
zh:
达尔马提亚人是罗马化伊利里亚沿海居民的罗曼语后裔；7世纪斯拉夫人定居时，其城墙城镇幸存，腹地落入克罗地亚部落之手。从扎达尔到杜布罗夫尼克，这些城邦保留罗马法、天主教和通俗拉丁语，后者演变为达尔马提亚语，分为拉古萨方言和克尔克的维格利奥方言。

诸城与意大利和拜占庭贸易，宗主权在拜占庭、克罗地亚和匈牙利之间易手，威尼斯则建立亚得里亚海霸权：扎达尔等北部城镇接受威尼斯统治，威尼斯语在商业行政中日益取代达尔马提亚语。

杜布罗夫尼克（又名拉古萨）成为独立共和国，拉古萨方言直到15世纪末仍是法律用语，1472年元老院立法抵制斯拉夫语。1337年的达尔马提亚诸城是双语沿海文明，身份与信仰属罗曼传统，又通过贸易通婚与斯拉夫腹地交织。

en:
The Damara, self-styled Daman, are an indigenous people of Namibia speaking the Nama Khoe tongue, though genetic evidence links them to the Bantu Herero and Himba, suggesting ancestors exchanged an earlier Bantu language and way of life for a Khoekhoe one. Their traditions count them with the San among the country's oldest inhabitants, chiefs remembered back to the fourteenth century.

They first lived between the Kunene and Kavango rivers and later drifted south to mountains around Brandberg, Waterberg and Erongo, hunting, herding, growing pumpkins, corn and tobacco and smithing copper and iron.

An invasion about 1600 broke their kingdom, scattering them into named clans, some to the Kalahari sands and others to mountain refuges that gave them the Bergdamara, or mountain Damara, label. As Nama and Herero herdsmen took the central plateau, many Damara lost their land and became household dependents.
zh:
达马拉人自称达曼人，是纳米比亚的原住民；他们使用纳马人的科伊语，但遗传证据显示他们与班图系的赫雷罗人和辛巴人血缘很近，暗示其祖先曾放弃早先的班图语言和生活方式，转而接受科伊科伊文化。口传传统中，达马拉人与桑人并列，是纳米比亚最古老的居民，可追忆的酋长世系早至14世纪。

他们最初生活在库内内河与奥卡万戈河之间，后来南迁至布兰德山、瓦特贝格和埃龙戈一带的山区，以狩猎畜牧为生，兼种南瓜、玉米和烟草，并锻造铜铁。

约1600年的一次入侵瓦解了他们的王国，达马拉人分裂为若干有名号的氏族：一支退入卡拉哈里沙地，另一支遁入群山，山地达马拉之名即由此而来。随着纳马和赫雷罗牧民占据中部高原，许多达马拉人失去土地，沦为依附者。

en:
Dambro (Pak Tai or Southern Thai) is the Southwestern Tai speech of the people of the Thai half of the Malay Peninsula, from Chumphon to the sultanate borderlands. Their country had been the Indianized Buddhist land of Tambralinga, Tai settlers making Nakhon Si Thammarat (Ligor) their chief mueang before the mid-thirteenth century.

Ram Khamhaeng's inscription lists Ligor as Sukhothai's southernmost tributary in the late thirteenth century; after Sukhothai weakened it became the peninsula's dominant Thai state. In 1337 the lands were a frontier between Thai and Malays, Buddhism and Islam; Majapahit recognized Ligor as belonging to Siam in 1365, Ayutthaya making it one of its eight great cities in 1468.

Rich from Portuguese and Dutch trade, Ligor kept its dynasty and vassals and revolted in 1629 and 1688. After Ayutthaya's 1767 fall it was independent until Taksin subdued it in 1769; Rama I made its ruler an appointed governor.
zh:
巴泰人又称南泰人，所说的巴泰语属西南部台语，分布在马来半岛泰人一侧，北起春蓬，南至马来苏丹国边疆。这里曾是印度化佛教古国丹马令的所在，13世纪中叶以前，台语移民已以那空是贪玛叻（洛坤）为首要城邦。

兰甘亨碑铭把洛坤列为13世纪末素可泰最南端属邦；素可泰衰落后它成为半岛最强泰人城邦。1337年这里是泰人与马来人、佛教与伊斯兰教交汇的前沿；1365年满者伯夷承认洛坤属暹罗，1468年阿瑜陀耶将其列为八大城市之一。

凭借与葡萄牙、荷兰贸易致富，洛坤保留王朝和属邦，1629、1688年两度反抗阿瑜陀耶。1767年阿瑜陀耶陷落后它一度独立，1769年被郑信征服，拉玛一世将其统治者降为任命的总督。

en:
The Dan are a Mande-speaking people of the forests along the border of north-western Ivory Coast and Liberia, where they are officially called Yacouba and were once known to outsiders as Gio. Their traditions place their origins in the western Sudan, and by the 700s they were living in the savanna of the northern Ivory Coast.

Political turmoil, population growth and exhausted land drove them south of the Nimba range and into the high forest in the 900s. There they cleared fields each year for rice and staples and became known as fierce warriors, whose chiefs fought long wars against the neighbouring Kru.

Their ritual life centred on the Gle mask ceremonies and on Gor, a men's society named after the leopard and devoted to peacemaking, while their carved masks became the most celebrated art of the region.
zh:
丹人是说曼德语族语言的民族，居住在科特迪瓦西北部与利比里亚交界的森林地带，官方称雅库巴人，外部旧称吉奥人。按其传统，他们的祖源在西苏丹地区，8世纪时已生活在科特迪瓦北部的稀树草原上。

10世纪时，因政局动荡、人口增长和地力耗竭，他们南迁越过宁巴山脉，进入高地森林。在那里他们每年开垦土地种植水稻等作物，并以善战著称，历代酋长同邻近的克鲁人长期交战。

他们的仪式生活以格莱面具典礼和名为戈尔的男性会社为中心，戈尔在丹语中意为豹子，是一个致力于调停争端的组织；丹人雕刻的面具也成为该地区最负盛名的艺术品。

en:
The Southern Tutchone, whose language is called Dan k'e, are an Athabaskan First Nations people of the southwestern Yukon, with country around Kluane and Aishihik lakes and the upper Yukon at Whitehorse; their historic bands include the Kluane Lake and Champagne people.

For some two thousand years they kept seasonal hunting and fishing camps in this lake-and-plateau country, storing food in raised log caches and moving between salmon stations and caribou hunting grounds in small matrilineal bands. They were linked to the Pacific coast by the Chilkat Pass, a rare route through the coastal mountains, along which Tlingit traders brought eulachon oil and, in time, European goods in exchange for furs.
