After the Qing drove out the Dzungars in 1717–1720, the frontier was redrawn along the Jinsha River in 1725–1726, eastern-bank lands becoming imperial territory under tusi chieftains. Famed horsemen, traders and raiders, they kept their fierce pride under whichever distant power claimed their valleys.
zh:
康巴人是康区的藏人。康区是藏族世界的东部边疆，峡谷纵横，传统上称“四水六岗”。7世纪松赞干布的大军将其并入吐蕃帝国；9世纪帝国解体后，康区再未臣服于单一统治者，各河谷形成头人领地与寺院庄园并立的局面，德格、林葱、囊谦、昌都与霍尔诸部各据一方，宁玛、噶举、萨迦寺院与世俗堡垒并立。

1337年时，新龙（雅垄）、理塘、察瓦戎一带仍由本地头人和喇嘛分治。1639年固始汗出兵击灭白利土司，康区被纳入达赖喇嘛的势力范围，1677年其与中原的边界划定，归拉萨管辖。

1717至1720年清军驱逐准噶尔，1725至1726年边界改以金沙江为界，江东土地成为王朝治下的土司辖地。康巴人以善骑、经商、善战闻名，无论名义上的宗主是谁，始终保持强烈的自尊。

en:
The Khandeshi are the people of the Khandesh region, the Tapti River valley in north-western Maharashtra centred on Asirgarh and Burhanpur. Their Indo-Aryan tongue is also called Ahirani after the Ahir herders; the region was known as Abhiradesa in early literature, and the language is written in Devanagari.

In 1295 Ala-ud-din Khalji of Delhi took Khandesh from its Chauhan lord, and in the late fourteenth century Malik Raja founded the independent Farooqui sultanate. Akbar's armies overran the region in 1599, making Burhanpur the seat of a Mughal subah as cotton, indigo and cloth trade brought prosperity. Maratha raids began in 1670, the Peshwa seized Asirgarh in 1760, and in 1818 Khandesh passed to British rule.
zh:
坎德什人是坎德什地区的居民，其地在马哈拉施特拉邦西北部的达布蒂河谷，以阿西尔格尔和布尔汉普尔为中心。他们说的印度—雅利安语又称阿希拉尼语，得名于阿希尔牧人；早期文献称这一带为阿比拉德萨，语言使用天城体书写。

1295年，德里的阿拉乌德丁·哈尔吉从乔汉领主手中夺取坎德什；14世纪末，马利克·拉贾建立独立的法鲁基苏丹国。1599年阿克巴的军队征服此地，布尔汉普尔成为莫卧儿苏巴的治所，棉花、靛蓝和布匹贸易带来了繁荣。马拉地人的袭扰始于1670年，佩什瓦于1760年攻占阿西尔格尔；1818年坎德什落入英国统治。

en:
The Khanty, formerly called Ostyaks by Russians from the Khanty word as-kho, a person of the Ob, are the Ob-Ugric people of the middle and lower Ob and Irtysh, a region known to medieval Novgorod as Yugra. Their language shares its Ugric branch with Mansi and Hungarian.

They descend from woodland Uralic populations between the Kama and the Irtysh; by the eleventh century Novgorodian hunters and merchants knew the tribes of Yugra, each led by its own chief. Some Khanty princedoms were absorbed into the Sibir Khanate between the 1440s and the 1570s, and its capital Qashliq stood in Khanty lands.

The Russian conquest in the 1580s brought yasak tribute, hostage children, destroyed idols and mass baptisms, but Christianity remained superficial. The Khanty kept their nature cults, shamans and Bear Celebration honouring the sky god Torum, alongside fishing, taiga trapping and reindeer herding.
zh:
汉特人过去被俄国人称为奥斯佳克人，名称来自他们自称的阿斯-霍，即鄂毕河人；他们是鄂毕河与额尔齐斯河中下游的鄂毕-乌戈尔民族，所居地区在中世纪诺夫哥罗德文献中称作尤格拉。其语言与曼西语、匈牙利语同属乌戈尔语支。

他们是卡马河与额尔齐斯河之间乌拉尔林地居民的后裔；11世纪，诺夫哥罗德猎人和商人已知道各有首领的尤格拉诸部。15世纪40年代至16世纪70年代，一些汉特小公国并入西伯利亚汗国，都城卡什雷克就在汉特人的土地上。

16世纪80年代俄国征服汗国后，亚萨克贡赋、儿童人质、捣毁神像和集体洗礼随之而来，但基督教化流于表面。汉特人仍保留自然崇拜、萨满和敬拜天神托鲁姆的熊节，以捕鱼、泰加狩猎和养鹿为生。

en:
The Kharchin are a Mongol tribe of the border country between Chifeng and northwestern Liaoning. Their name goes back to the early 1200s, when Kipchak and Qanqli captives famed for brewing black kumis were enrolled in the Mongol imperial guard and called Kharachin; by the 1400s they were a tribe of the Yüngshiyebü tümen.

In 1510 Dayan Khan made them a right-wing tribe, and under his grandson Kundulun they spread east into the lands of the Ming Döyin, or Uriangkhan, Guards, whose herdsmen gradually took the Kharchin name.

Ligdan Khan scattered the old Yüngshiyebü Kharchin in 1628, whereupon the Uriangkhan leader Subudi led the merged tribe to submit to Hong Taiji. In 1636 and 1648, and under the Kangxi emperor, the Qing enrolled them as the three Kharchin banners of the Josotu League; they increasingly settled into agriculture beside Chinese migrants.
zh:
喀喇沁是赤峰与辽西北交界地带的蒙古部落。族名可追溯到13世纪初：当时以酿制黑马奶酒闻名的钦察、康里降人被编入蒙古帝国宿卫，称作喀喇沁；到15世纪，他们已成为永谢布万户的一个部落。

1510年达延汗把喀喇沁编为右翼诸部之一；后来在其孙昆都力哈统领下，他们向东进入明朝朵颜卫，即兀良哈三卫的牧地，当地牧人逐渐袭用喀喇沁之名。

1628年林丹汗击散旧喀喇沁，兀良哈首领苏布地遂率融合后的部众归附皇太极；清朝在1636年、1648年及康熙年间先后把他们编为卓索图盟的喀喇沁三旗，他们也越来越多地在汉族移民旁边定居务农。

en:
The Kharia are a Munda people of the forested uplands where Jharkhand and Odisha meet, centred on the Sundargarh, Simdega and Gumla hills. Their Kharia language forms, together with Juang, its own branch of the Munda languages of the Austroasiatic family. Like other Munda peoples they descend from Austroasiatic settlers who reached the Odisha coast from Southeast Asia by about 1500 BCE.

They are divided into Hill, Delki and Dudh Kharia: the Hill Kharia remained hunters, gatherers and labourers living on game, honey and wild tubers, while the Delki and Dudh sections took to settled plough farming, and many in the plains held land as tenants under zamindars.

Their villages kept close to the forest, and their religion centred on the spirit groves and ancestor cults of the Sarna complex shared with neighbouring tribes.
zh:
卡里亚人是居住在贾坎德与奥里萨交界山林地带的蒙达族群，以孙达尔加尔、辛德加和古姆拉丘陵为中心。卡里亚语与朱昂语共同构成南亚语系蒙达语族下的一个独立语支。和其他蒙达人一样，他们是公元前1500年左右自东南亚抵达奥里萨海岸的南亚语移民的后裔。

卡里亚人分为山地、德尔基和杜德三支：山地卡里亚仍以狩猎、采集和佣工为生，食物取自猎物、蜂蜜和野生块茎，德尔基和杜德两支则转为定居犁耕，平原上的许多人在柴明达尔手下充当佃农。

他们的村落紧靠森林，信仰属邻近诸族共有的萨尔纳体系，以圣林和祖先崇拜为中心。

en:
The Khas are an Indo-Aryan hill people of the western Nepalese Himalayas, whose old Khasa tongue was the ancestor of Nepali. From the eleventh century the Khasa Malla kings held a kingdom centred on Sinja in the Karnali basin, reaching western Tibet as far as Guge and Purang under Prithvi Malla in the mid-fourteenth century.

Ripu Malla marked his 1312 pilgrimage to Lumbini on the Ashokan pillar; the kings' records used an early form of Nepali in Devanagari and mixed Buddhist and Hindu devotion. After Abhaya Malla's death the empire broke into the Baise and Chaubisi hill principalities, which absorbed Rajput immigrants from the plains.

The Khas kept their language and Shaivite Masto cult; when Gorkha absorbed the hill states, their speech spread to become the language of the unified Nepalese kingdom.
zh:
卡斯人是尼泊尔西部喜马拉雅山区的印度雅利安族群，其古卡斯语是尼泊尔语的前身。11世纪起，卡斯·马拉诸王以格尔纳利盆地的辛贾为中心建立王国；14世纪中叶普利特维·马拉在位时，势力西入西藏的古格、普兰。

里普·马拉1312年朝礼蓝毗尼并在阿育王石柱上刻铭；诸王的碑铭使用天城文书写的早期尼泊尔语，兼奉佛教与印度教。阿巴亚·马拉死后，帝国瓦解为二十二国与二十四国山地诸邦，来自平原的拉杰普特移民逐渐融入其中。

卡斯人保留了语言和湿婆派的马斯托信仰；后来廓尔喀吞并山邦，卡斯语随之传播，成为统一后的尼泊尔王国的语言。

en:
The Khasi are an Austroasiatic people of the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya, one of the few Mon-Khmer-speaking communities in South Asia. Oral tradition and linguistics point to a migration from Southeast Asia by way of Upper Burma and the Brahmaputra valley. Their society is matrilineal: property passes to the youngest daughter, and men join their wife's clan after marriage.

They worshipped the supreme creator U Blei Nongthaw in the indigenous Niam Khasi religion, and the War subtribe built living root bridges by training fig-tree roots across streams. The hills were split among about twenty-five chiefdoms alongside the Jaintia kingdom, whose Pnar rulers had split from an older realm in 630.

Jaintia was briefly overrun by the Ahoms in 1707 before recovering, came into contact with the East India Company after its grant of the Diwani of Bengal in 1765, and was annexed by the Company in 1835.
zh:
卡西人是梅加拉亚邦卡西丘陵的南亚语系族群，也是南亚少数孟高棉语社群之一。口传与语言研究显示，其先民自东南亚经上缅甸和布拉马普特拉河谷迁徙而来。卡西社会实行母系制：家产传给最年幼的女儿，男子婚后加入妻子的氏族。

他们在本土的卡尼亚姆·卡西信仰中崇拜至高创世神乌勃黎·农陀；支系瓦尔人把榕树根系牵引跨过溪流，编成活树桥。卡西丘陵分属约二十五个小酋邦，与之并存的是詹塔王国，其普纳尔统治者于630年从一个更古老的政权分出。

詹塔于1707年一度被阿洪姆人攻灭后复国，1765年东印度公司取得孟加拉的迪万财税权后与其接触，1835年被吞并。

en:
The Khmer are an Austroasiatic people of the lower Mekong basin and one of Southeast Asia's oldest settled populations, rice-farming ancestors reaching it by the early second millennium BCE. They built the port kingdom of Funan and successor Chenla, and in 802 Jayavarman II founded the Khmer Empire, the Angkor period.

From hydraulic cities north of the Tonlé Sap, Angkor grew into the world's largest pre-industrial urban complex. Suryavarman II raised Angkor Wat in the early twelfth century; Jayavarman VII added walled Angkor Thom and the Bayon around 1200. Hinduism and Mahayana Buddhism gradually gave way to Theravada Buddhism from the late thirteenth century.

In 1337 the empire was past its peak, weakened by drought, failing waterworks and Siamese wars; in 1431 Ayutthaya sacked Angkor and the court moved to Longvek and then Oudong. Longvek fell to Siam in 1594, and in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Vietnamese settlement of the Mekong Delta detached the lower Khmer, or Khmer Krom, lands from the Cambodian heartland.
zh:
高棉人是湄公河下游的南亚语系民族，也是东南亚大陆最古老的定居族群之一，稻作先民在公元前两千年前后已到达此地。他们先后建立港口王国扶南及其后继者真腊；802年阇耶跋摩二世建立高棉帝国，柬埔寨进入吴哥时代。

以洞里萨湖北部的水利城市为中心，吴哥成为前工业时代世界最大城市综合体：苏利耶跋摩二世12世纪初修建吴哥窟，阇耶跋摩七世1200年前后增建吴哥城和巴戎寺。13世纪末起，印度教和大乘佛教逐渐让位于上座部佛教。

1337年帝国已过鼎盛期，受干旱、水利损毁和暹罗连年战争削弱；1431年阿瑜陀耶攻陷吴哥，王廷南迁洛韦、乌栋。洛韦1594年被暹罗攻占，17至18世纪越南人拓殖湄公河三角洲，把下高棉（Khmer Krom）土地从柬埔寨本土分割出去。

en:
The Khmu, whose endonym means people, speak a Khmuic language of the Austroasiatic family and are considered the aboriginal inhabitants of northern Laos and the surrounding upper Mekong lands, where Khmuic villagers had lived for millennia before the arrival of Tai speakers.

Tai migrations south gathered pace after the Mongol conquest of Yunnan in 1253, and as Lao principalities took the fertile river valleys the Khmu were pushed onto wooded slopes, where they became known as Lao Theung and practised swidden farming. In 1337 their scattered villages still reached west across the Khorat Plateau.

When Fa Ngum founded the Lao kingdom of Lan Xang in 1353, the Khmu entered it as its largest upland people, governed through their own village headmen and remembered in Lao origin legend as the elder brothers of the lowland Lao.
zh:
克木人的自称意为“人”，说南亚语系克木语支的语言，被认为是老挝北部及湄公河上游周边土地的原住民；早在泰语人群到来之前的数千年里，克木语村民就已生活在这里。

泰人南迁在1253年蒙古征服云南后加快，随着佬人城邦占据肥沃的河谷，克木人被挤到林木覆盖的坡地，被称为“老听”，从事刀耕火种。1337年时，他们分散的村落向西仍延伸到呵叻高原。

1353年法昂建立佬人国家澜沧王国时，克木人作为境内最大的山地民族加入，由本村头人管辖，并在佬人的起源传说中被记为低地佬人的兄长。

en:
Khoemana, also called Korana or Griqua, is the South Khoekhoe tongue once spoken along the southern Cape coast and across the Karoo, where clans grazed Nguni cattle and sheep when Dutch ships began calling at Table Bay.

The Dutch East India Company founded its Cape station in 1652; over the following century the Cape Khoekhoe lost grazing land in wars and epidemics and were drawn into the colonial frontier. Survivors merged with settlers, freed slaves, San and Tswana into mounted, gun-using communities including the Korana and Griqua.

The name Griqua is first recorded in 1730; under leaders such as Adam Kok they trekked to the Orange and Vaal rivers, where Klaarwater, later Griquatown, became their gathering place. In the 1820s and 1830s Korana and Griqua commandos raided the highveld; a Griqua commando was destroyed by the Ndebele at Moordkop in 1831.
zh:
科伊马纳语又称科拉纳语或格里夸语，是南部科伊科伊人的语言，曾通行于开普南部海岸和卡鲁高原；荷兰船只开始停靠桌湾时，当地氏族放牧恩古尼牛和绵羊。

1652年荷兰东印度公司在开普建立据点，此后一个世纪，开普科伊科伊人在战争和瘟疫中丧失牧场，被卷入殖民边疆。幸存者与定居者、获释奴隶、桑人和茨瓦纳人融合，形成骑马持枪的群体，包括科拉纳人和格里夸人。

“格里夸”之名最早见于1730年；亚当·科克等首领率众迁至奥兰治河与法尔河畔，克拉尔沃特（后称格里夸敦）成为聚落地。19世纪20—30年代，科拉纳和格里夸民团袭掠高地草原，1831年一支格里夸民团在莫尔德科普被恩德贝莱人歼灭。

en:
The Khon Muang, or Tai Yuan, are the Northern Thai people of the valleys around Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai and Phayao. They called themselves people of the mueang, the settled rice-plain towns.

King Mangrai united the northern Tai principalities from 1259, conquered the Mon kingdom of Hariphunchai around 1292 and in 1296 made Chiang Mai the capital of Lanna, the Land of a Million Rice Fields. From the Mon the Tai Yuan took Theravada Buddhism and the Tai Tham script. In 1337 Mangrai's dynasty ruled Chiang Mai; Lanna reached its zenith under King Tilok in the fifteenth century, fighting Ayutthaya.

In 1558 the Burmese Toungoo conquered Chiang Mai. Lanna nobles allied with Taksin of Siam to throw off the Burmese in 1774; after Chiang Saen fell in 1804 the country passed under Siamese suzerainty.
zh:
傣阮人又称泰沅人，是清迈、清莱和帕尧河谷的北部泰人。他们自称“勐人”，即稻作平原城镇之民。

芒莱王自1259年起统一北部泰人诸邦，约1292年征服孟人王国哈利奔猜，1296年以清迈为兰纳都城；兰纳意为“百万稻田之国”。泰沅人从孟人接受上座部佛教和泰昙文。1337年芒莱王朝统治清迈；兰纳在15世纪滴洛拉王治下鼎盛，与阿瑜陀耶交战。

1558年缅甸东吁攻占清迈。1774年兰纳贵族联合暹罗郑信摆脱缅甸，1804年清盛陷落后归暹罗宗主。

en:
The Khonds are a Dravidian tribal people of the forested Eastern Ghats, chiefly in the highlands of inland Odisha. They speak Kui and Kuvi, tongues closest to Gondi and traditionally written in the Odia script. Their society is organised into totemic clans led by headmen.

Their economy combines hunting and gathering with podu, slash-and-burn cultivation. They worshipped the earth deity Dharni together with mountain and river spirits, and the Meriah rite, in which a purchased victim was sacrificed to secure the fertility of the soil, made them notorious to early British administrators.

During the Company's war against the raja of Goomsur from 1835, the Scottish officer Samuel Charters Macpherson entered the previously unmapped Khond hills in 1837. He recorded their language and institutions, and prepared the reports on which the later campaigns to abolish the sacrifice were based.
zh:
孔德人是生活在东高止山森林中的达罗毗荼语系部族，主要聚居于奥里萨内陆高地。他们使用与贡德语亲缘最近的库伊语和库维语，传统上以奥里亚字母书写；社会按图腾氏族组织，由头人统领。

他们以狩猎采集与当地称“波杜”的刀耕火种为生。他们崇奉大地神达尔尼以及山川神灵，其中为求土地肥沃而献祭买来人牲的梅里亚仪式，令早期英国官员极为震动。

1835年东印度公司对古姆苏尔王公开战后，苏格兰军官塞缪尔·查特斯·麦克弗森于1837年进入此前无人测绘的孔德山区。他记录了孔德人的语言与制度，其报告成为后来废除人祭行动的依据。

en:
The Khorasanis are the Persian-speaking people of western Khorasan, the historic eastern province of Iran, centered on Nishapur, Tus and later Mashhad. Khorasan, meaning the Eastern Land, became a Sasanian province in the sixth century and the cradle of New Persian: after the Arab conquest, literary Persian re-emerged in Khorasan and Transoxiana.

The Mongol conquest of 1221 devastated its cities, but recovery followed under the Ilkhanate. In 1337 the fall of the Ilkhanate had left western Khorasan to the Sarbadars and Kartids, until Timur conquered it at the end of the fourteenth century; recovery continued under the Timurids.

From the sixteenth century the Safavids and the Uzbek khanates fought over Khorasan for two hundred years. Nader Shah made Mashhad his capital in 1736, and after his death the Qajars secured the western half in 1796 while Herat passed to the Afghan Durranis.
zh:
呼罗珊人是西呼罗珊的波斯语居民，其地是伊朗历史上的东方行省，以尼沙普尔、图斯及后来的马什哈德为中心。呼罗珊意为东方之地，6世纪被萨珊设为行省，也是新波斯语的摇篮：阿拉伯征服后，文学波斯语在呼罗珊与河中重新兴起。

1221年蒙古征服重创其城市，伊儿汗国时期有所恢复。1337年伊儿汗国崩溃，西呼罗珊落入萨尔巴达尔、卡尔提德等地方政权之手，14世纪末为帖木儿征服；帖木儿王朝时期继续恢复。

16世纪起，萨法维与乌兹别克诸汗国为争夺呼罗珊交战两百年；纳迪尔沙于1736年以马什哈德为都，他死后卡扎尔王朝1796年取得西半部，赫拉特归入阿富汗杜兰尼王朝。

en:
The Khorezmians of this age are the settled townspeople and farmers of the Khwarazm oasis and Transoxianan cities, from Bukhara to Fergana. Their forebears included Iranian-speaking Khwarazmians and Sogdians, whose Eastern Iranian tongue survived in Khwarazm at least into the thirteenth century before giving way to Persian and Karluk Turkic.

Turkic rule came in the eleventh century with the Muslim Kara-Khanid khans; by the fourteenth century bazaar towns spoke Middle Turkic, wrote in Perso-Arabic script and kept Khwarazmian learning such as al-Biruni's. In 1337 the Transoxianan cities belonged to the fracturing Chagatai Khanate and the Khwarazm oasis to the Golden Horde. Timur later made Samarkand his Timurid capital, covering the region in mosques and madrasas.

From local Middle Turkic arose Chagatai, Central Asia's classical literary language, brought to its height by Ali-Shir Nava'i in the fifteenth century. When Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbek nomads conquered Transoxiana after 1501, they called the settled people Sart; these Karluk-speaking townspeople became the core of the later Uzbek nation under Bukhara, Khiva and Kokand.
zh:
这一时代的花剌子模人是花剌子模绿洲与河中诸城（从布哈拉到费尔干纳）的定居市民和农民。祖先包括说伊朗语的花剌子模人和粟特人，其东伊朗语支的花剌子模语至少留存到13世纪，后让位于波斯语和葛逻禄突厥语。

11世纪喀喇汗可汗带来突厥统治；到14世纪，丝路城镇通用中突厥语，以波斯—阿拉伯字母书写，延续比鲁尼等学者的传统。1337年河中诸城属分裂中的察合台汗国，花剌子模绿洲属金帐汗国；后来跛子帖木儿以撒马尔罕为都，在境内广建清真寺和经学院。

中突厥语发展出察合台语，成为中亚古典文学语言，15世纪经阿里希尔·纳瓦伊推向顶峰。1501年后昔班尼率乌兹别克游牧民征服河中，把定居人口统称撒尔塔人；这些说葛逻禄语的城镇居民在布哈拉、希瓦、浩罕诸汗国治下，成为后世乌兹别克民族核心。

en:
The Khoromboy were a Yukaghir tribal group of the Laptev Sea coast, roaming the lower Omoloy and Yana, where they spoke the Yan, or Detkil, dialect of Yukaghir. According to the ethnographer Boris Dolgikh, their name combines the Yukaghir words koriel, a wolf, and omo, a tribe, so that Khoromboy meant something like the wolf clan.

When Russian parties first met Yukaghir bands on the Yana in the 1630s, the Khoromboy were a small group of about a hundred and ten people, sometimes called Omoloi after their river. Tribute, disease and pressure from reindeer-herding neighbors thinned them under Russian rule, and the Khoromboy eventually dissolved into Evenki and partly Nganasan communities.
zh:
霍龙博伊人是拉普捷夫海沿岸的尤卡吉尔部落，游猎于奥莫洛伊河和亚纳河下游，使用尤卡吉尔语的亚纳（杰特基尔）方言。民族学家鲍里斯·多尔吉赫认为，族名由尤卡吉尔语“科里埃尔”（狼）和“奥莫”（部落）组合而成，意思近似“狼之族”。

17世纪30年代俄国探险队在亚纳河首次遇到尤卡吉尔人时，霍龙博伊人约有110人，有时按河名称他们为奥莫洛伊人。在俄国统治下，贡赋、疫病和邻近养鹿民族的压力使他们不断减员，霍龙博伊人最终融入鄂温克人，还有一部分融入了恩加纳桑人。

en:
The Khwe, also rendered Kxoe or Khwedam, are a San people of the Okavango Delta and the western Caprivi, whose traditional lands reach into Angola, Zambia and Botswana. Their traditions place their ancestors around the Tsodilo Hills. They lived in small semi-nomadic bands without chiefs, moving with the game and seasonal waterholes, and left their mark in the rock art of the Tsodilo Hills.

As Bantu-speaking herders and farmers spread through the region up to the year 1000, the Khwe traded and intermingled with them, and the clicks of their Khoe speech were absorbed into neighbouring Bantu languages.

While Dutch trekboers and their commandos destroyed San bands around the Cape frontier from 1714 to the 1790s, the Okavango country lay far beyond colonial reach, and the Khwe kept their foraging life there undisturbed.
zh:
克韦人（又译克索埃人，其语言也称克韦达姆语）是生活在奥卡万戈三角洲和卡普里维地带西部的桑人一支，传统活动范围延伸到安哥拉、赞比亚和博茨瓦纳。他们的口传传统把祖先之地指向措迪洛山。他们结成没有酋长的半游牧小群，随猎物和季节性水洼迁徙，并在措迪洛山的岩画中留下了自己的印记。

到公元1000年前后，说班图语的牧民和农民已遍布这一地区，克韦人与他们贸易、杂处，自己科伊语里的吸气音也被邻近班图语吸收。

1714年至18世纪90年代，荷兰游牧布尔民及其民团在开普边境摧毁了一支支桑人群体，而奥卡万戈远在殖民势力范围之外，克韦人得以不受打扰地延续狩猎采集的生活。

en:
The K'iche' are one of the principal Maya peoples of the Guatemalan highlands; their name means many trees, and its Nahuatl translation, Cuauhtēmallān, gave Guatemala its name. After the Classic collapse they built a Postclassic kingdom, moving its capital around 1400 to Q'umarkaj, founded by King Q'uq'umatz.

Allied with the Kaqchikel, the K'iche' conquered the K'oja and expanded under Q'uq'umatz's son K'iq'ab, subduing the Mam of Zaculeu. A noble rebellion in 1470 drove out their Kaqchikel allies; after K'iq'ab died around 1475 the kingdom weakened through wars with the Kaqchikel and Tz'utujil. In March 1524 Pedro de Alvarado destroyed their army, killed its commander Tecún Umán and burned Q'umarkaj.

The K'iche' preserved their traditions in writing. The Popol Vuh, with its creation myth and Hero Twins, was set down around 1550 and transcribed and translated by the Dominican Francisco Ximénez in 1701.
zh:
基切人是危地马拉高地的主要玛雅族群之一；其名称意为“许多树”，纳瓦特尔语译作夸乌特马兰，“危地马拉”由此得名。古典期崩溃后，他们建国，约1400年迁都至国王库库马茨所建的库马尔卡赫。

基切人与卡克奇克尔人结盟，征服科哈人，在库库马茨之子基亚布治下扩张，令萨库莱乌的玛姆人臣服。1470年贵族叛乱赶走卡克奇克尔盟友；基亚布约1475年去世后，基切与卡克奇克尔、楚图希尔交战，逐渐衰弱。1524年3月，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多歼灭基切军队，击杀统帅特昆·乌曼，焚毁库马尔卡赫。

基切人以文字保存传统。《波波尔·乌》记载创世神话和孪生英雄，约1550年成文，1701年由多明我会修士弗朗西斯科·希门尼斯转写并翻译。

en:
The Kichesipirini, whose name means men of the great river, were an Algonquin nation of the Ottawa River, known to the French as the Island Indians because their main village stood on Morrison Island beside Allumette Island. The river itself they called Kitchissippi, and their country stretched along both its banks between Ontario and Quebec.

They may have been the first Algonquin people to meet the French: their one-eyed chief Tessouat met Samuel de Champlain in 1603, and Champlain visited the island village again in 1613. Holding the narrows and portages, the Kichesipirini charged tolls on traders and missionaries.

In 1645 they and their Huron allies made peace with the Haudenosaunee, but the settlement collapsed, and by 1650 raiding had driven them from their islands. Their survivors are thought to have taken refuge among the Odawa.
zh:
基切西皮里尼人是渥太华河畔的阿尔冈金民族，族名意为“大河之人”；法国人称他们为“岛上印第安人”，因为主村位于阿吕梅特岛旁的莫里森岛上。他们称渥太华河为“基奇西皮”，地盘沿河流两岸延伸，横跨安大略与魁北克交界一带。

他们可能是最早接触法国人的阿尔冈金民族：独眼酋长泰苏阿于1603年会见萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰，尚普兰又在1613年重访这座岛上村落。由于扼守大河的狭口和转运陆路，基切西皮里尼人向商人和传教士收取通行费。

1645年，他们与休伦盟友同霍德诺索尼人议和，但和议破裂，到1650年时袭扰已把他们逐出各岛。幸存者据认为投奔了奥达瓦人。

en:
The Gija, also spelled Kija or Gidja and known to neighbours as the Lungga, are an Aboriginal people of the East Kimberley in Western Australia, whose country runs from Halls Creek towards Kununurra and takes in most of the striped sandstone domes of the Bungle Bungle Range in Purnululu, bordering Miriwoong lands around Lake Argyle.

Their language belongs to the small Jarragan family of the East Kimberley; the family takes its name from jarrag, the Gija word for language. Gija forms its own Gijic branch alongside the Miriwoongic languages, with Kuluwarrang and Walgi recorded as possible dialects.
zh:
基亚人又拼作吉贾，邻族称之为隆加人，是西澳大利亚东金伯利地区的原住民，领地从霍尔斯克里克延伸到库努纳拉方向，波奴鲁鲁中班古鲁班古山脉的条纹砂岩穹丘大多位于其境内，在阿盖尔湖一带与米里温人的领地相接。

他们的语言属于东金伯利的杰拉甘语系；该语系的名称就来自基亚语中意为“语言”的jarrag。基亚语自成吉亚语支，与米里温语支并列，库卢瓦兰语和瓦尔吉语则被记为它可能的方言。

en:
The Kilivila are the people of the Trobriand Islands, coral atolls off New Guinea, whose largest island is Kiriwina. Speaking Kilivila, an Austronesian language of the Oceanic branch, they live in villages under matrilineal clans that hold the land and arrange marriage and inheritance.

Their economy rests on yam gardening, with yams and pigs serving as stores of wealth and instruments of prestige. Their villages take part in the kula, an inter-island circuit in which red shell necklaces and white shell armshells circulate among lifelong trade partners reached by seagoing canoes.

In 1793 the French expedition of Antoine Bruni d'Entrecasteaux sailed past and named the islands after his officer Denis de Trobriand. In the decades that followed, whalers and other ships called for water and provisions, while the islanders kept their clan system, gardening magic and exchange rites essentially intact.
zh:
基利维拉人是特罗布里恩群岛的居民，这片珊瑚环礁位于新几内亚外海，最大岛屿为基里维纳岛。他们说的基利维拉语属于南岛语系大洋洲语支，村落由母系氏族掌握土地并安排婚姻与继承。

其经济以山药园艺为基础，山药和猪既是财富储备也是声望工具。各岛村落还参与“库拉”岛际交换圈，红色贝壳项链与白色贝壳臂镯在终身贸易伙伴之间流转，人们驾驶远航独木舟前去拜访。

1793年，安托万·布吕尼·当特尔卡斯托率领的法国船队经过此地，并以随船军官德尼·德·特罗布里安之名为群岛命名。此后数十年间，捕鲸船和过往船只常来补给淡水和给养，岛民的氏族制度、园艺巫术和交换仪式基本保持完好。

en:
The Kiliwa, who call themselves Ko'leeu, are an Indigenous people of northern Baja California, whose traditional territory stretched across the peninsula from San Felipe on the Gulf of California to San Quintín on the Pacific.

They lived by hunting and gathering without agriculture: pit-roasted agave was their staff of life, supplemented in the high country by autumn acorns and pine nuts. Rabbits and deer were taken in communal drives into nets.

Their first meeting with Europeans was with Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo's ships at San Quintín in 1542, but serious contact resumed two centuries later, with the Jesuit Wenceslaus Linck in 1766. Dominican friars founded the mission of Santo Domingo in 1775 and San Pedro Mártir in 1794; by the time Mexico won independence in 1821, disease and mission life had reduced the Kiliwa population to a remnant.
zh:
科莱乌人外称基利瓦人，自称“科莱乌”，是下加利福尼亚半岛北部的原住民；他们的传统领地横跨半岛，东有加利福尼亚湾畔的圣费利佩，西抵太平洋沿岸的圣金廷。

他们不事农耕，以狩猎采集为生：坑烤龙舌兰是主食，秋季再到高地采收橡子和松子。兔子和鹿靠众人驱赶、张网围猎。

1542年，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略的船队在圣金廷与他们首次相遇，但此后两个世纪接触寥寥，直到1766年耶稣会士文策斯劳斯·林克到来。多明我会修士于1775年建立圣多明各传教站，1794年又建立圣佩德罗马丁尔传教站；到1821年墨西哥独立时，疫病和传教站生活已使科莱乌人口凋零，只剩残余部众。

en:
The Killaka or Quillacas were one of the Aymara-speaking lordships of the southern Bolivian altiplano, holding the country around present Uyuni and the Aullagas basin south of Lake Poopó, in what is now the department of Oruro. With the Aullagas, Chichas and neighboring groups they belonged to the Charca federation, whose highland ayllus traded with the valleys and stood together against Guaraní raids from the Chaco.

After the Inca conquest their land became the huamani of Quillaca, counted among the twenty-eight provinces of Collasuyo. Under Spanish rule the old chiefdom survived as Hatun Quillacas: the noble José Fernández Collque Inca Guarachi held its caciqueship from 1681 to 1734, and the town of Santuario de Quillacas preserves the people's name.
zh:
基利亚卡人又称基利亚卡斯人，是玻利维亚南部高原讲艾马拉语的族群之一，占据着波波湖以南、今乌尤尼和奥亚加斯盆地一带，即后来的奥鲁罗省境内。他们与奥亚加斯人、奇查人等邻近族群同属查尔卡斯联盟；联盟内的高原村社与河谷贸易，并合力抵御来自查科的瓜拉尼人袭扰。

印加征服后，他们的土地被编为基利亚卡行省，是科利亚苏尤二十八个行省之一。西班牙统治时期，旧酋邦以大基利亚卡之名存续：贵族何塞·费尔南德斯·科尔克·印加·瓜拉奇于1681年至1734年担任其酋长，基利亚卡圣所镇的名字也来自这个族群。

en:
The Killke were the pre-Inca people of the Cusco basin in the Peruvian highlands, whose archaeological culture flourished from about 900 to 1200 during the Late Intermediate Period, before Inca culture arose in the thirteenth century.

Their most important monument is the great fortified complex of Saksaywaman above Cusco, whose first sections Killke builders raised in the twelfth century and which the Inca later expanded and reused. Killke pottery, first described by the archaeologist John Howland Rowe, consists mainly of globular vessels with vertical strap handles and simple geometric line decoration in black or black-on-red over a white slip.

With the rise of Cusco under the early Inca rulers in the thirteenth century, Killke communities were absorbed into the Inca world, which inherited their stoneworking and ceramic traditions.
zh:
基利克人是秘鲁高原库斯科盆地的前印卡居民，其考古文化在约900—1200年的晚中间期兴盛，早于13世纪兴起的印卡文化。

他们最重要的遗迹是库斯科城北的萨克塞瓦曼大型要塞建筑群：基利克工匠在12世纪建起它的最早部分，后来印卡人又加以扩建并继续使用。基利克陶器最早由考古学家约翰·豪兰·罗描述，多为带竖直带状把手的球状容器，白色陶衣上饰以黑色或黑红两色的简单几何线条。

13世纪初印卡统治者在库斯科崛起后，基利克社群融入印卡世界，其石雕与制陶传统也被印卡继承。

en: The Kimaama are a Papuan people of Kolepom Island, the large, flat island off the south coast of New Guinea in present-day South Papua, Indonesia. Their main settlement of Kimaan lies in the island's southeast, and their Kimaghama tongue, together with neighbouring Riantana, forms the Central Kolopom branch of the Trans–New Guinea language family.
zh: 基马马人是科洛庞岛上的巴布亚族群；该岛地处新几内亚岛南海岸外，即今印度尼西亚南巴布亚省，地势低平。他们的主要聚落基马安位于岛的东南部，所说的基马马语与邻近的里安塔纳语共同构成泛新几内亚语系的中科洛庞语支。

en:
The Kindigir are an Evenki clan whose early hunting grounds lay around the upper Lena and the northern shore of Lake Baikal. Dushkachan, on the Kichera river near the lake's northern tip, is described as one of the first settled camps of the Kindigir, and archaeology traces human occupation there to the early first millennium.

The clan entered written history with the Russian conquest of the Lena country in the 1600s, when the Baikal Evenki came under yasak administration. Kindigir lineages, including a Lakshikagir branch, were later counted among the Barguzin Khamnigans, the Mongolized Evenki clans absorbed into the Buryat world east of Baikal.
zh:
金迪吉尔人是鄂温克氏族，早期猎场在勒拿河上游与贝加尔湖北岸一带。贝加尔湖北端基切拉河畔的杜什卡昌被称为金迪吉尔氏族最早的定居营地之一，考古发现表明公元第一个千年初期已有人在此活动。

17世纪俄国征服勒拿河流域时，贝加尔湖沿岸的鄂温克人被纳入雅萨克税贡体系，该氏族也由此见诸文字记载。金迪吉尔的支系（包括拉克什卡吉尔分支）后来被列入巴尔古津哈米尼干人的氏族名单，这些蒙古化的鄂温克氏族在贝加尔湖以东逐渐融入布里亚特世界。

en:
The Waimiri-Atroari, who call themselves Kinja, are a Cariban-speaking forest people of northern Brazil, whose villages lie in the country between the Uatumã, Negro and Branco rivers. Kin of the Kalina, they were known to earlier travellers by a string of other names, and their tongue belongs to the Carib language family.

Spanish and Portuguese expansion up the Amazon reached their rivers in the 1600s, though the first recorded face-to-face contact came only in 1732; in 1775 the Portuguese official Sampaio crossed their territory and left one of the earliest descriptions of it.

The Kinja already had a firm name as warriors, and the wealth of their rivers and forests drew pioneer traders upstream, so through the 1700s and early 1800s they kept their independence by meeting intruders with their bows rather than with trade or missions.
zh:
金雅人是巴西北部使用加勒比语族语言的森林族群，村庄散布在瓦图芒河、内格罗河与布朗库河之间。他们与卡利纳人同源，早年旅人还用一串别的名字称呼他们。

17世纪西班牙和葡萄牙沿亚马逊河的扩张已抵达他们的河道，但有据可查的第一次面对面接触迟至1732年；1775年葡萄牙官员桑帕约穿越他们的领地，留下了最早的记述之一。

金雅人早已享有善战之名，而其河川与林地的丰富物产又引着拓荒商人溯流而上，因此在18世纪至19世纪初，他们不事贸易、不接纳传教，而是以弓箭迎击闯入者，守住了自身的独立。

en:
The Kinugumiut, who call themselves the Kiŋikmiut, are the Iñupiaq people of the Bering Strait tip of the Seward Peninsula, around Port Clarence and Cape Prince of Wales, the site of present-day Wales, or Kiŋigin, the westernmost town on the North American mainland. They speak the Bering Strait dialect of Iñupiaq and belonged to the whaling and sea-mammal hunting culture of the strait, trading across the narrow water with the peoples of Siberian Chukotka.

Captain James Cook named Cape Prince of Wales on his voyage of 1778, and in 1827 a Russian naval report listed their coastal and inland villages by name, making the Kinugumiut one of the best-documented Alaskan Inuit groups of the early contact period.
zh:
基努古缪特人自称基尼基缪特，是苏厄德半岛白令海峡一端的因纽皮亚特人，活动在克拉伦斯港和威尔士王子角一带，也就是北美大陆最西端的城镇威尔士（基尼金）的所在地。他们使用因纽皮亚特语的白令海峡方言，属于海峡地区捕鲸和捕猎海洋哺乳动物的文化圈，还跨过狭窄的海面与西伯利亚楚科奇的民族贸易。

1778年詹姆斯·库克在航行中命名了威尔士王子角；1827年的一份俄国海军报告逐一记录了他们在沿海和内陆的村庄，基努古缪特人也因此成为早期接触时代记载最详尽的阿拉斯加因纽特群体之一。

en:
The Kirati are a cluster of Tibeto-Burman peoples of the eastern Himalaya, including the Rai and Limbu, in eastern Nepal, Sikkim and Darjeeling. Sanskrit texts call these mountain peoples Kirata, and Kirati chiefs were among the earliest rulers of the Kathmandu Valley: according to tradition their king Yalambar founded a Kirat dynasty there before the Licchavi conquest.

In the far east the Limbu country, Limbuwan, was divided into ten kingdoms, of which Morang was the strongest, and the Limbu language acquired its own Sirijunga script in the ninth century. Kirati society was ordered by the oral Mundhum; its people worshipped nature and ancestors through shamans and celebrated the seasonal Sakela festivals.

The independent Kirati kingdoms ended in 1774, when Gorkha armies conquered Limbuwan after seventeen battles; the treaty preserved a measure of local self-rule under the kipat land system.
zh:
基拉特人是喜马拉雅山东段一群藏缅语族群的统称，包括拉伊、林布等分支，聚居在尼泊尔东部、锡金与大吉岭。梵文文献把这一带的山民称为基拉塔人；基拉特首领也是加德满都谷地最早的统治者之一，相传首领雅兰巴尔在那里建立了基拉特王朝，后被离车毗人征服。

在更东边的林布地区林布湾曾分成十个王国，以莫朗最为强大，林布语还在9世纪有了自己的西里琼加文字。基拉特社会以口传经典《蒙德姆》为法度，由萨满主持自然与祖先崇拜，并在季节性的萨克拉节举行仪式。

1774年，廓尔喀军队经十七场战役征服林布湾，独立的基拉特诸王国就此终结；战后条约在基帕特土地制度下保留了一定程度的地方自治。

en:
The Kariri, also written Cariri or Kiriri, are a cluster of Indigenous peoples of the sertão, the dry backlands of northeastern Brazil, spread across the São Francisco River basin and the neighboring backlands. Their name comes from the Tupi word kiri'ri, meaning silent or taciturn, and colonial writers classed them among the non-Tupi peoples generically called Tapuia.

Related tongues formed the Kariri language family within the Macro-Jê trunk. A Dutch governor described the Carirys of the Paraíba interior as early as 1639.

After the Dutch were expelled, the Kariri north of the São Francisco rose in the Confederation of the Cariris, known to the Portuguese as the Guerra dos Bárbaros of 1683 to 1713; the defeated survivors were gathered into missionary aldeias, and their name lives on in the Cariris Velhos and Cariris Novos highlands.
zh:
基里里人（又译卡里里）是巴西东北部干旱腹地塞尔陶的一群原住民，分布在圣弗朗西斯科河流域及邻近腹地。其名来自图皮语 kiri'ri，意为沉默或寡言；殖民地著述把他们归入非图皮族群，泛称为塔普亚人。

数种亲属语言组成大热语系下的卡里里语族。早在1639年，已有荷兰总督描述过帕拉伊巴内陆的卡里里人。

荷兰人被逐出后，圣弗朗西斯科河以北的基里里人组成卡里里联盟起事，被葡萄牙人称为1683至1713年的野蛮人战争；战败的幸存者被集中到传教村落，他们的名字留在卡里里韦柳、卡里里诺武斯等山地地名中。

en:
The Kispoko were one of the five divisions of the Shawnee, an Algonquian-speaking people of the Northeastern Woodlands, and were reckoned the smallest of the five in the eighteenth century. During the Beaver Wars they were driven from their Ohio homeland by the Iroquois Confederacy and were living among the Creek in the Upper South as early as 1650, before returning to Ohio around 1759.

The division supplied the tribe's hereditary war chiefs; Chiksika, elder brother of Tecumseh, was a Kispoko war chief. Kispoko families shared the Shawnee village of Peckuwe with the Pekowi division until it was destroyed after the Battle of Piqua in 1780.

Most of the sept was removed west of the Mississippi in the early nineteenth century, and its descendants formed part of the Absentee-Shawnee in Indian Territory.
zh:
基斯波科人是东北林地阿尔冈昆语民族肖尼人的五大分支之一，在18世纪被认为是五支中人数最少的一支。海狸战争期间，他们被易洛魁联盟赶出俄亥俄故土，早在1650年便寄居南方腹地的克里克人之中，约1759年才返回俄亥俄。

肖尼人的世袭军事首领出自这一分支，特库姆塞的长兄奇克西卡就是基斯波科的战将。基斯波科人与佩科维分支同住肖尼人的佩库韦村，直到1780年皮夸战役后村庄被毁。

19世纪初，该分支大多数人被迁到密西西比河以西，其后裔成为印第安领地缺席肖尼人的一部分。

en:
The Kissi are a West Atlantic people of the forested hills where Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia meet, grouped around towns such as Kissidougou and Kérouané. They speak Kissi, a Mel language of the Niger-Congo family.

Their traditions recall an earlier home in the Upper Niger country south of the Futa Jallon; expelled by the Yalunka, they moved after 1600 into the forests, pushing the Limba before them while living under constant pressure from the Kuranko. Ironworking was ancient in this region and Kissi smiths were famed for their skill, their iron bars serving as trade goods when Portuguese voyagers recorded them in the early sixteenth century.

Their traditional religion centers on ancestor worship and the soapstone figures called pomdo, buried images that the Kissi dig up and consult for guidance.
zh:
基西人是几内亚、塞拉利昂和利比里亚三国交界森林丘陵地带的大西洋语支族群，聚居于基西杜古、凯鲁阿内等城镇周围，讲尼日尔—刚果语系梅尔语支的基西语。

他们的传统记忆把更早的家园指向富塔贾隆以南的尼日尔河上游地区；被雅隆卡人驱逐后，他们于1600年以后迁入森林，一路挤走林巴人，又始终承受着库兰科人的压力。冶铁在这一地区起源甚古，基西铁匠技艺高超，16世纪初葡萄牙航海者的记录里，他们的铁条已被当作贸易货物。

他们的传统宗教以祖先崇拜为核心，供奉被称为“庞多”的皂石造像；这些造像埋在土中，人们会把它们挖出，在疑难时请示指点。

en:
The Kitikiti'sh, meaning raccoon-eyed people for their tattooed eye-rings, are the people better known as the Wichita. They spoke Caddoan tongues and lived in domed grass lodges in settled towns from the Arkansas to the Red River. Their ancestors had farmed the Washita valley from about 900 and later built the Great Bend towns of Kansas.

In 1541 Coronado found the land he called Quivira among them. Epidemics and Apache and Osage pressure thinned them in the seventeenth century, and Apache attacks drove them south to the Red River by 1757.

Allied with the Comanche, they destroyed the San Saba Mission and defeated a Spanish army of five hundred at the Twin Villages. A smallpox epidemic in 1777 and 1778 killed about a third of them, and after 1803 the surviving related bands were increasingly grouped under the single name Wichita.
zh:
基蒂基蒂什人意为浣熊眼之人，得名于眼部的环状文身，外部更熟悉的称呼是威奇塔人。他们讲卡多语系语言，在阿肯色河至雷德河之间的定居城镇里住圆顶草屋。其先民约900年起就在瓦希塔河谷务农，后来又在堪萨斯的大弯一带建起诸镇。

1541年，科罗纳多在他们这里找到了他称作基维拉的土地。17世纪的瘟疫以及阿帕奇人和奥塞奇人的挤压使他们人口锐减，阿帕奇人的袭击又迫使他们在1757年前南撤到雷德河。

他们与科曼奇人结盟，曾摧毁圣萨瓦传教站，并在双子村之战中击败一支五百人的西班牙军队。1777至1778年的天花瘟疫夺去约三分之一人口的生命；1803年后，幸存的各亲缘部落越来越多地被笼统称为威奇塔人。

en:
The Kitkehahki are one of the four bands of the Pawnee, a Caddoan-speaking people of the central Great Plains, and their name means Little Muddy Bottom Village. As the southernmost of the Pawnee South Bands they were often called the Republican Pawnee, after their earth-lodge villages on the Republican River. Their villagers farmed corn, beans and pumpkins in the river valley and left each season to hunt buffalo on the open plains.

In the early eighteenth century the Pawnee together numbered more than twelve thousand, but pressure from the Lakota, Dakota and Cheyenne and repeated epidemics gradually weakened them.

In 1806 Zebulon Pike of an American expedition visited their main village and persuaded the Kitkehahki to accept the American flag, and in 1818 they signed the Treaty of St. Louis as the Pawnee Republic.
zh:
基特凯哈基人是波尼人的四大分支之一，波尼人是中部大平原上说卡多语的原住民；基特凯哈基意为小泥底村。作为波尼南支中位置最靠南的一支，他们在共和河畔建起土屋村落，因此常被称为共和波尼人。村民在河谷种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，每到特定季节还要前往开阔平原猎捕野牛。

18世纪初波尼人总数超过一万二千，但拉科塔人、达科他人和夏延人的挤压加上接连的瘟疫，使他们逐渐衰弱。

1806年，美国探险队的泽布伦·派克到访他们的主营，说服基特凯哈基人接受美国国旗；1818年，他们以波尼共和国的名义签署了《圣路易斯条约》。

en:
The K'itaish, whom French and Spanish scribes wrote down as Kichai, were a Southern Plains people of Texas, Louisiana and Oklahoma. They spoke a Caddoan language and were closest in origin to the Pawnee. French explorers first met them on the Red River in Louisiana in 1701.

Their allegiances shifted with the rivalries of the plains: early colonists called them enemies of the Caddo, and in 1712 they fought the Hainai on the Trinity River, yet they also intermarried with the Kadohadacho and took part in Caddoan confederate alliances.

By 1772 their main villages stood east of the Trinity near the site of present-day Palestine, Texas. In 1837 they defeated a Texas Ranger force at the Battle of Stone Houses, though their own leader fell in the first attack.
zh:
基泰什人是南部平原的印第安部族，活动于得克萨斯、路易斯安那和俄克拉荷马一带，自称基泰什，法国和西班牙文献记作基柴等拼法。他们讲卡多语系的一种语言，族源上与波尼人最近。1701年，法国探险家在路易斯安那的雷德河上首次遇到他们。

他们的立场随平原上的合纵连横而变化：早期殖民者把他们视为卡多人的仇敌，1712年他们还在特里尼蒂河畔与海奈人交战，但同时又与卡多哈达乔人通婚，并加入卡多联盟阵营。

到1772年，他们的主要村落已位于特里尼蒂河以东，靠近今得克萨斯帕勒斯坦一带。1837年，他们在石屋之战中击败了得克萨斯游骑兵，尽管自己的首领在首轮攻击中阵亡。

en:
The Kiwigapawa are the Kickapoo, an Algonquian-speaking people of the Great Lakes; Kickapoo is a French rendering of their word Kiwigapawa, meaning he who moves about, a name fitting their long migrations. French missionaries first met them in southern Wisconsin in 1667, after the Beaver Wars dispersed the lower Great Lakes peoples, and the Kickapoo encountered La Salle's expedition in the Illinois country in 1682.

They later settled along the Wabash and in southern Illinois as members of the Wabash Confederacy, and signed the Treaty of Greenville in 1795. Among the firmest allies of the Shawnee leader Tecumseh, they fought at Tippecanoe in 1811.

The 1819 Treaty of Edwardsville forced the cession of nearly half of Illinois, and under the prophet Kennekuk part of the nation held out before an 1832 land exchange moved the main band from Missouri to Kansas.
zh:
基维加帕瓦人即基卡普人，五大湖地区的阿尔冈昆语民族；Kickapoo是法语对其本族语词Kiwigapawa的转写，意为四处迁徙之人，恰合他们不断迁移的历史。海狸战争打散下五大湖的各族群之后，法国传教士于1667年在威斯康星南部首次见到他们；1682年，基卡普人又与拉萨尔的伊利诺伊探险队相遇。

后来他们作为沃巴什联盟的成员定居沃巴什河沿岸和伊利诺伊南部，并于1795年签订《格林维尔条约》。他们是肖尼人首领特库姆塞最坚定的盟友之一，参加了1811年的蒂珀卡努战役。

1819年的《爱德华兹维尔条约》迫使他们割让近半个伊利诺伊；在先知基内库克带领下，一部分人坚持留守，1832年的土地交换把主体部族从密苏里迁往堪萨斯。

en:
The Koasati, or Coushatta, are a Muskogean people whose earliest known towns stood in the Tennessee River valley of present-day Tennessee, where Hernando de Soto's expedition met them in 1540. Maize farmers and noted basket-makers, they drifted southwest in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, founding towns on the Tennessee before settling at Coosada and joining the Muscogee Creek Confederacy as Upper Creeks, closely intermarried with the Alabama.

After 1763 colonial pressure pushed them further west across Mississippi into Spanish Louisiana and Texas: a Coushatta band reached the Big Thicket of eastern Texas in 1795, while kin who remained in Alabama were swept into the removals to Indian Territory in the 1830s.

Their language belongs to the Muskogean family. Together with Alabama and the extinct Apalachee it forms the family's Apalachee-Alabama-Koasati branch.
zh:
科阿萨蒂人（又称考沙塔）是马斯科吉语族族群，已知最早的城镇在今田纳西州的田纳西河谷，1540年德·索托的探险队曾在那里与他们相遇。他们种植玉米，以编织篮筐闻名；17至18世纪开始向西南迁移，在田纳西河上陆续建镇，最后在科萨达定居，并作为上克里克一支加入马斯科吉克里克联盟，与阿拉巴莫人互通婚姻。

1763年后，殖民压力把他们进一步向西推过密西西比，进入西属路易斯安那和得克萨斯：一支科阿萨蒂人于1795年抵达东得克萨斯的大灌丛，留在阿拉巴马的亲族则在19世纪30年代被强制迁往印第安领地。

他们的语言属于马斯科吉语系，与阿拉巴莫语及已消亡的阿巴拉契语同属阿巴拉契-阿拉巴莫-科阿萨蒂语支。

en:
The Koch are a Tibeto-Burman people of the lower Brahmaputra and North Bengal, organised into nine matrilineal, exogamous clans and speaking a Boro-Garo language, though many groups later adopted Indo-Aryan speech. Muslim chronicles already place them in western Kamrup in the early thirteenth century.

After the Bengal sultan seized Kamata in 1498, the Koch leader Hajo united the tribes, and his grandson Bisu overthrew the Baro-Bhuyan chieftains, took the Hindu name Biswa Singha and founded the Koch kingdom at Kamatapur in 1515. Under Nara Narayan in the mid-sixteenth century it became the strongest power northeast of Bengal and patronised the Vaishnava revival of Sankardev.

The kingdom then split into Koch Bihar and Koch Hajo: Mughal armies conquered Koch Hajo in 1612, the Khaspur branch merged into the Kachari kingdom in 1745, and Koch Bihar survived as a Mughal-aligned state.
zh:
库奇人是布拉马普特拉河下游与北孟加拉的藏缅语族群，分为九个行母系制、实行族外婚的氏族，讲博多—加罗语支的库奇语；后来许多支系改说印度雅利安语。13世纪初的穆斯林史籍已把他们记作迦摩缕波西部的居民。

1498年孟加拉苏丹攻占迦摩陀之后，库奇首领哈乔统一诸部，其孙比苏推翻巴罗—布扬诸首领，取印度教名比斯瓦·辛哈，于1515年在迦摩陀布尔建立库奇王国。16世纪中叶纳拉·纳拉扬治下，该国成为孟加拉东北最强的政权，并赞助了商羯罗提婆的毗湿奴虔信改革。

王国随后分裂为库奇比哈尔与库奇哈乔两支：1612年莫卧儿军队征服库奇哈乔，卡斯普尔一支于1745年并入卡查里王国，库奇比哈尔则作为亲莫卧儿的政权延续下来。

en:
The Kochini, or Malabar Jews, are the oldest Jewish community of India, established on the Kerala coast, where tradition places their first settlers in the generation after the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 CE, at the port of Cranganore. Hebrew signatures on the Kollam copper plates of 849 attest to Jewish traders in the region, and later royal plates made the Jewish leader Joseph Rabban a prince over his community.

In 1341 a flood silted up Cranganore harbour, and the Jews shifted with the pepper trade to Cochin and built their first synagogue there. The Portuguese who arrived in 1500 discriminated against them, and after 1492 Sephardic exiles later called Paradesi Jews joined them and built their own synagogue.

When the Dutch took Cochin in 1663 the community gained a more tolerant ruler. They followed the Sephardic rite and looked above all to the code of Maimonides.
zh:
柯枝犹太人又称马拉巴尔犹太人，是印度最古老的犹太社群，定居在喀拉拉海岸；按他们的传说，最早的定居者是70年第二圣殿被毁之后那一代人，落脚于克兰加努尔港。849年奎隆铜盘上的希伯来文签名证明当时已有犹太商人在此活动，后来的王室铜盘又册封犹太领袖约瑟夫·拉班为社群之长。

1341年一场洪水淤塞了克兰加努尔港，犹太人随胡椒贸易迁往柯枝，并在那里建起第一座会堂。1500年到来的葡萄牙人对他们多有歧视；1492年以后塞法迪流亡者陆续来投，后称帕拉迪西犹太人，建起自己的会堂。

1663年荷兰人攻占柯枝后，社群迎来了较宽容的统治者。他们奉行塞法迪仪轨，最推崇迈蒙尼德的法典。

en:
The Kodava, or Coorgs, are an endogamous Dravidian hill people of Kodagu, the forested Coorg highlands of the Western Ghats in southern Karnataka, where they have lived as land-owning rice farmers and cattle herders for well over a thousand years. Their society is patrilineal and martial, honouring ancestors, nature and weapons, and a Kannada lexicon of 1398 already described them as warriors fond of hunting.

Early medieval Coorg passed between several dynasties and then the Vijayanagara Empire. Around 1600 the Haleri Rajas made the district their own, ruling from Haleri; in the later eighteenth century Raja Dodda Vira Rajendra fought the invading armies of Tipu Sultan.

In 1834 the East India Company defeated the last Haleri raja and annexed Coorg, and a revolt against the new order broke out at Sulya in 1837.
zh:
科达瓦人又称库尔格人，是南卡纳塔克西高止山森林高地——库尔格（科达古）地区实行内婚制的达罗毗荼语山民，千余年来以拥有土地的稻农和牧人身份在此定居。其社会按父系传承，崇尚武艺，敬奉祖先、自然和兵器；1398年的一部卡纳达语辞书已把他们描写为酷爱狩猎的武士。

中世纪早期，库尔格先后在诸王朝与毗奢耶那伽罗帝国治下。约1600年起，哈莱里诸王以哈莱里为中心统治此地；18世纪后期，多达·维拉·拉金德拉王曾抗击提普苏丹的入侵。

1834年，东印度公司击败末代哈莱里王，吞并库尔格；1837年，苏利亚又爆发反抗新秩序的起义。

en:
The Kofan, who call themselves the A'i, are an ancient people of the Amazonian foothills between the Aguarico and Guamués rivers, in what is now northeast Ecuador and southern Colombia. They speak A'ingae, a language isolate, and lived by farming, hunting and river travel in dugout canoes.

When the Spanish reached their country in the mid-sixteenth century, the Kofan may have numbered some fifteen thousand; they resisted fiercely, and late in that century they destroyed the Spanish town of Mocoa and forced the intruders to withdraw. The Jesuit Rafael Ferrer began missionary work among them in 1602, but soldiers and settlers following in his wake drove him out.

Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries sporadic expeditions sought gold, trade and converts, while European diseases steadily cut the population, leaving the Kofan a diminished but unconquered people in their forest homelands.
zh:
科凡人自称阿依人，是阿瓜里科河与瓜穆埃斯河之间亚马孙山麓地带的古老族群，分布在今厄瓜多尔东北部和哥伦比亚南部。他们使用孤立语言科凡语，以农耕、狩猎和乘独木舟在河上往来为生。

16世纪中叶西班牙人抵达时，科凡人可能约有一万五千之众；他们激烈抵抗，在该世纪末摧毁西班牙人的莫科阿镇，迫使入侵者撤退。1602年，耶稣会士拉斐尔·费雷尔开始在他们中间传教，但尾随而来的军人和殖民者又把他赶走。

17至18世纪，零星的远征队不断前来寻求黄金、贸易和皈依者，欧洲传来的疾病则持续削减其人口，使科凡人人数大减，但始终未被征服，仍守在自己的森林家园里。

en:
Kohistani is the collective name for the Dardic Indo-Aryan mountain peoples of Kohistan, the land of steep forests and pastures split between the Indus, Swat and Dir valleys. They speak a cluster of related tongues and stand close to their Shina and Kashmiri neighbours.

Once they ranged far more widely, for the Gibari-speaking Sultans of Swat ruled Swat, Dir, Buner and Malakand until the sixteenth century; between 1510 and 1515 the Yousafzai Pashtuns overran that sultanate and drove most Kohistanis back into the high valleys, where Pashtun settlement and conversion slowly Pashtunized some groups, who lost their old speech for Pashto.

The remaining valleys kept their small languages and their old valley politics, governed by local clans rather than outside kings, and entered the British period as isolated tribal hills.
zh:
科希斯坦是科希斯坦地区达尔德系印度-雅利安山地民族的统称，这片森林茂密、牧场纵横的山地分属印度河、斯瓦特和迪尔河谷。他们讲一族亲缘语言，与邻近的希纳人和克什米尔人关系很近。

他们的分布曾远比现在广阔：讲吉巴里语的斯瓦特苏丹国直到16世纪还统治着斯瓦特、迪尔、布内尔和马拉坎德；1510至1515年间，优素福扎伊普什图人攻灭该苏丹国，把大部分科希斯坦人逼回高山河谷，此后普什图人的定居和传教逐渐使一些群体普什图化，放弃原有语言改用普什图语。

留存下来的河谷则保住了各自的小语言和古老的河谷自治，由本地氏族而非外来君王治理，进入英属时期时仍是闭塞的部落山区。

en: The Koiali are the Mountain Koiari people of the rugged inland ranges of southeastern New Guinea, around the Efogi, Barai and Koiari villages inland from Port Moresby. Their language belongs to the Koiarian family of the Trans–New Guinea phylum and is only distantly related to the Grass Koiari speech of the coastal plains below them.
zh: 科亚利人即山地科亚里人，住在新几内亚东南部内陆崎岖山区，即莫尔兹比港后方的埃福吉、巴赖和科亚里等村落一带。他们的语言属跨新几内亚语系的科亚里安语族，与下方沿海平原的草原科亚里语只有远亲关系。

en: The Kokomini, who called themselves Gugumini, meaning good or intelligible speech, were an Aboriginal Australian people of Queensland, perhaps a loose confederation of tribal groups rather than a single tribe. Neighbouring peoples knew them by the exonym Kookawarra, meaning poor speakers, and their territory bordered the Palmerville country on the upper Palmer River.
zh: 科科米宁人自称古古米尼，意为“清晰好懂的话”；他们是昆士兰的澳大利亚原住民，可能并非单一部落，而是若干部落群体的松散联盟。邻族用以意为“说话差劲者”的他称库卡瓦拉称呼他们，其领地邻近帕尔默河上游的帕默维尔一带。

en: The Kokowara, also called Kuku-Warra or Gugu-Warra, were an Aboriginal people of northern Queensland. The name given them by neighbouring tribes meant rough speech. They held about 1,800 square miles of country on the Normanby River, from Lakefield south to the Laura River, camping chiefly at Daidan on the Deighton River.
zh: 科科瓦拉人又记为库库-瓦拉或古古-瓦拉，是昆士兰北部的澳大利亚原住民。邻族给他们的名字意为“粗话”。他们在诺曼比河一带保有约1800平方英里的土地，南起莱克菲尔德直至劳拉河，主要营地在戴顿河畔的代丹。

en: The Kol people live in Pomio District on the southern side of eastern New Britain. Their language appears to be an isolate, perhaps distantly related to the poorly known Sulka language within the proposed East Papuan grouping.
zh: 科尔人居住在新不列颠岛东部南坡的波米奥区。他们的科尔语看来是一门语言孤岛，或许与记录甚少的苏尔卡语有远亲关系，同属拟议中的东巴布亚语群。

en:
The Qulla or Kolla are the southernmost of the Aymara-speaking peoples of the Altiplano, whose Colla kingdom arose on the Collao plateau around Lake Titicaca after the decline of Tiwanaku, at least by the late twelfth century, and whose dead were buried in stone chullpa towers such as those at Sillustani.

With the other Aymara lordships they were conquered by the Inca Pachacuti around 1450; the Inca named the southern quarter of Tawantinsuyu Qullasuyu, while Qulla families were resettled as soldier-colonists into the southern Andes, including the high puna around Antofalla.

In 1540 the Qulla first met the Spaniards, resisting for years before their lands were taken, and in 1780 the leader Ñusta Willaq led Qulla warriors in the Andean revolt. Their descendants in northwestern Argentina and western Bolivia speak a southern Quechua dialect, though the Titicaca Qulla probably once spoke Puquina.
zh:
科利亚人（又称科亚）是高原艾马拉诸族中分布最南的一支；蒂亚瓦纳科衰落后，他们的科利亚王国至少在12世纪末已兴起于的的喀喀湖周围的科利亚奥高原，死者葬在西卢斯塔尼等地的石造楚尔帕塔墓中。

约1450年，他们与其他艾马拉王国一起被印卡的帕查库特克征服；印卡人将塔万廷苏尤的南部大区命名为科利亚苏尤，同时把科利亚家族作为军人殖民者远迁到安第斯南部，包括安托法亚一带的高寒荒原。

1540年科利亚人首次接触西班牙人，抵抗多年后土地仍被夺去；1780年，首领努斯塔·维利亚克率科利亚战士参加安第斯起义。他们在阿根廷西北部和玻利维亚西部的后裔使用南部克丘亚方言，而的的喀喀地区的科利亚人古时很可能使用普基纳语。

en:
The Kolo are a small Bantu people of the upper Kwango valley, on the borderlands of northern Angola and the Congo, best identified with the Holo, or Baholo, who live along the Kwango next to the Suku.

Holo carvers made figures with rounded faces and helmet masks for circumcision ceremonies, close in style to the work of their Suku neighbours.
zh:
科洛人是宽果河上游的一个班图小族群，分布在安哥拉北部与刚果交界一带，可对应宽果河沿岸、与苏库人为邻的霍洛人（又称巴霍洛人）。

霍洛人的工匠雕刻圆脸的人像和用于割礼仪式的盔式面具，风格与邻近的苏库人相近。

en:
The Kolyma Yukaghirs are the Yukaghir clans of the Kolyma River basin in northeast Siberia, heirs of the Neolithic Ymyyakhtakh culture. They lived by fishing, hunting wild reindeer and elk and breeding reindeer for transport, and spoke the Kolyma, or Odul, variant of Yukaghir, whose wider kinship remains uncertain.

At Russian contact their largest tribe was the Omoki of the lower Kolyma and Omolon, six hundred and twenty people in eleven clans in 1659; the word omok itself means clan or tribe. Tribute, intertribal wars and epidemics reduced them to fifty-four people by 1693.

The upper-Kolyma Kogime, the clan of the Great Raven, fared better, and present-day Upper Kolyma Yukaghirs trace their descent chiefly from them. In the colonial centuries many Kolyma Yukaghirs merged into Yakut, Even and Russian communities, while clan shamanism and the old nomadic hunting life lingered on.
zh:
科雷马尤卡吉尔人是西伯利亚东北部科雷马河流域的尤卡吉尔各氏族，是新石器时代伊米亚赫塔赫文化的后继者。他们以捕鱼、猎取野鹿和驼鹿、饲养驯鹿驮运为生，使用尤卡吉尔语的科雷马（奥杜尔）变体，这一语言与其他语系的亲缘关系始终未定。

俄国人到来时，他们中间最大的部落是住在科雷马河和奥莫隆河下游的奥莫基人：1659年有620人，分十一个氏族，“奥莫克”一词本身就是氏族、部落的意思。贡赋、部族战争和疫病使他们到1693年只剩54人。

上游科雷马的科吉梅人即“大乌鸦之族”处境稍好，后来的上科雷马尤卡吉尔人主要出自这一支。殖民时代里，许多科雷马尤卡吉尔人融入雅库特人、埃文人和俄国人的社区，而氏族萨满信仰和古老的游猎生活仍延续了很久。

en:
The Kombai are a Papuan people of the South Papua rainforest interior, in the Mappi and Boven Digoel river country. Their name comes from khoba, meaning people, and their Kombai language forms the Kombai-Wanggom branch of the Greater Awyu family.

They live in patrilineal clans, each holding a forest territory called mburu with sweet-potato and banana gardens, sago swamps and pig-hunting grounds with dogs; fish are stunned with root poison in dammed streams.

Their most distinctive custom is building treehouses: the sacred ramo dumo of the clan elder stands at the territory's centre, guarded by bowmen, tall walina serve as men's lookouts, and low ibena houses serve women in childbirth and sago-grub feasts binding neighbouring clans. Like other interior Papuans, they descend from populations established on the island long before Austronesian seafarers reached its coasts around 1500 BCE.
zh:
孔拜人是南巴布亚雨林内陆的巴布亚族群，分布在马皮与博文迪古尔的河网地带。族名来自意为“人”的khoba一词，孔拜语属大阿维尤语系的孔拜-旺贡分支。

孔拜人按父系氏族聚居，每个氏族拥有名为姆布鲁的森林领地，园圃种植红薯、香蕉，沼泽经营西谷椰林，并带猎狗猎猪；捕鱼时在溪流筑坝，用有毒根茎把鱼毒晕。

他们最鲜明的习俗是建造树屋：氏族长老的圣树屋拉莫杜莫位于领地中心，由弓箭手守卫；高耸的瓦利纳是男子瞭望台，低矮的伊贝纳供妇女分娩并举办西谷虫宴，以此维系邻近氏族。和其他内陆巴布亚人一样，他们是远早于约公元前1500年南岛语航海者抵达之前就定居该岛的古老族群后裔。

en:
The Komi are a Permian people of the Uralic family in the Vychegda and Kama basins. Their endonym means man; southerners were called Permyaks, after Great Perm, and northerners Zyryans. They and the Udmurts descend from a Proto-Permian people that split in the first millennium BC; by the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the Komi had divided into Kama Permyaks and northern Zyryans.

From the twelfth century Novgorodian fur traders entered the country, while Great Perm's dukes ruled from Cherdyn. In 1365 Moscow sent Stephen of Perm to convert them; he created the Old Permic alphabet, though the shaman Pama resisted and the Permyaks were not fully baptised until Duke Mikhail accepted Christianity in 1470. Moscow seized Cherdyn in 1472 and abolished the duchy in 1505.

They kept hunting and gathering ways and the myth of rivals En and Omöl.
zh:
科米人是乌拉尔语系彼尔姆语支民族，自古住在东欧东北部维切格达河与卡马河流域的森林地带。他们的自称意为“人”；南部科米人被称彼尔姆人，得名于“大彼尔姆”，北部的称兹梁人。他们与乌德穆尔特人同源于公元前一千纪分裂的古彼尔姆人群；到16至17世纪科米人分为卡马河的彼尔姆人和北方的兹梁人。

12世纪起诺夫哥罗德毛皮商人进入此地，大彼尔姆公爵以切尔登为统治中心。1365年莫斯科派彼尔姆的斯蒂芬前来传教，他创制古彼尔姆字母，但萨满帕马起而抵抗，彼尔姆人直到1470年米哈伊尔公爵受洗才整体归信。莫斯科于1472年攻占切尔登，1505年废除公国。

科米人保持狩猎采集的生计，以及恩神与奥默尔神相争的古老神话。

en:
The Komo, also called Kumu and plural Bakomo, are a Bantu people of the northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, living in the forest country around Kisangani and stretching toward the Kivu highlands. Their own tradition records that they moved southwest out of the kingdom of Bunyoro, in present-day Uganda, in the early 1800s. They speak Komo, also called Kikomo, a Bantu language of the Komo-Bira group.

Their traditional religion centers on a creator named Muungu and a demiurge called Nkya, with astral legends explaining the world. Before farming or hunting begins, the Komo hold rituals with sacrifices to the spirits, and belief in magic remains part of daily life.
zh:
科莫人又称库穆人（复数称巴科莫），是刚果民主共和国东北部的班图族群，住在基桑加尼周围并伸向基伍高地的森林地带。他们自己的传说记载，19世纪初从今乌干达境内的巴尼奥罗王国向西南迁徙而来。科莫人使用科莫语，又名基科莫语，属班图语的科莫—比拉语支。

他们的传统宗教以创世神穆翁古和造物主恩基亚为中心，并有星宿神话解释世界。每逢农耕或狩猎开始，都要举行仪式、向神灵献祭，对巫术的信仰也深植于日常生活。

en: The Konbudj, recorded as Ngunbudj or Gonbudj, were an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory whose language was a little-known variety of the Umbugarla–Ngumbur group within the Darwin Region languages, spoken in the western Arnhem Land country. The tongue was virtually undocumented and had died out before the Second World War.
zh: 孔布吉人在文献中记作恩贡布吉或贡布吉，是北领地的原住民，其语言属达尔文地区语群中的翁布加拉-恩贡布尔语支，通行于阿纳姆地西部一带。这种语言几乎没有留下记录，在第二次世界大战前便已消亡。

en: The Kondogir are an Evenki clan of the Lower Tunguska, or Katanga, taiga whose name survived as the Kondogirsky village council of Katangsky district. As reindeer-herding hunters they were made to pay the fur tax, or yasak, which Cossacks secured by taking hostages from leading clans in the seventeenth century.
zh: 孔多吉尔人是下通古斯卡河（卡坦加河）泰加林的鄂温克氏族，其名称在俄国行政建制中保留为卡坦加区的孔多吉尔村苏维埃。作为养鹿狩猎者，17世纪哥萨克以扣留氏族首领人质的方式迫使他们缴纳毛皮税，即雅萨克。

en:
The Kongo, or Bakongo, are the Bantu people who speak the Kikongo cluster of related dialects and live along the Atlantic coast of Central Africa. Around 1390 their dynasties founded the Kingdom of Kongo, ruled from Mbanza Kongo by the Manikongo.

The Portuguese explorer Diogo Cão reached the coast in 1483, and in 1491 King Nzinga a Nkuwu was baptized as João I; under Afonso I, who won the throne in 1509, Catholicism became the religion of the ruling elite. From the sixteenth century the slave trade reshaped Kongo society.

The Manikongo's power collapsed after the defeat and death of King António I at the Battle of Mbwila against Portuguese Angola in 1665. Rival royal houses then fought long civil wars, yet Kongo communities kept their language, clan structure and trading networks along the river routes into the nineteenth century.
zh:
刚果人又称巴刚果人，是讲彼此相近的刚果语各方言的班图人，居住在中非大西洋沿岸。约1390年，他们的王朝建立了刚果王国，由马尼刚果以姆班扎刚果为都进行统治。

1483年葡萄牙航海家迪奥戈·康抵达海岸，1491年国王恩津加·恩库武受洗取名若昂一世；1509年即位的阿方索一世治下，天主教成为统治精英的信仰。从16世纪起，奴隶贸易重塑了刚果社会。

1665年，国王安东尼奥一世在姆布维拉战役中被葡属安哥拉军队击败身亡，马尼刚果的权威随之崩溃。此后对立的王室家族长期内战，但刚果人社群仍保留着语言、氏族制度和沿河商路网络，一直延续到19世纪。

en:
The Konkani are the Indo-Aryan people of the Konkan, the narrow coastal plain between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, centred on Goa and reaching from north of Bombay to Karwar. They speak Konkani, a southern Indo-Aryan language of the Marathi-Konkani group, attested in stone inscriptions from the second century and first named in the verse of the thirteenth-century saint-poet Namadeva.

In 1337 the coast was held by the Muslim sultanates of the Deccan, first the Bahmanis and later Bijapur, whose governors ruled Goa. In 1510 Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa for Portugal and made it the capital of the Portuguese Estado da Índia.

Jesuits such as Thomas Stevens studied and printed the language, while missionary preaching and Portuguese rule drew a large share of the people into Catholicism. Other Konkani speakers migrated along the coast to Surat, Mangalore and Cochin, carrying their dialects beyond Goa.
zh:
康坎人是康坎海岸的印度—雅利安人，那是西高止山脉与阿拉伯海之间的狭长平原，以果阿为中心，北起孟买以北，南到卡尔瓦尔。他们讲康坎语，属印度—雅利安语南支的马拉地—康坎语组，2世纪的石刻铭文已见其形，其名称最早见于13世纪圣诗诗人纳姆德夫的诗篇。

1337年，海岸由德干的穆斯林苏丹国统治，先后是巴赫曼尼和比贾布尔苏丹国，果阿长官由它们委任。1510年阿尔布克尔克为葡萄牙夺取果阿，将其建为葡属印度的首府。

托马斯·史蒂文斯等耶稣会士学习并刊印这种语言，传教活动与葡萄牙统治也使相当多的人皈依天主教。另一些康坎语居民沿海岸迁往苏拉特、门格洛尔和柯钦，把各方言带到果阿之外。

en:
The Kono are a Mande-speaking people whose homeland is the wooded hill country of eastern Sierra Leone, with part living across the border in Guinea. Their traditions describe them as descendants of migrants from the Mali-Guinea region who moved west as peaceful hunters and settled the land that became Kono District in the mid-1500s; they claim to have once been a powerful people in Mali and Guinea.

Later, raids by the related Mende drove them north into Koranko territory, where they were granted farmland; when the Mende shifted further south the Kono returned to their eastern homeland as farmers and hunters under village chiefs.
zh:
孔诺人是说曼德语族语言的民族，家园在塞拉利昂东部的丘陵林地，部分支系住在边界另一侧的几内亚。按其口述传统，他们是马里—几内亚地区移民的后裔，其先民以和平猎人的身份西迁，16世纪中叶定居于后来的孔诺地区，并称自己曾是马里和几内亚一带的强族。

后来同属曼德群体的曼德人来袭，孔诺人北逃到科兰科人的地界，获准在那里耕种；曼德人继续南移后，孔诺人才重返东部家园，在村镇酋长治下务农狩猎为生。

en:
The Koreans are the people of the Korean Peninsula, whose Bronze Age ancestors came from Manchuria and merged with agricultural populations. In 1337 their land was ruled by the Goryeo dynasty of Kaesong, founded in 918, a Buddhist kingdom long overshadowed by Mongol Yuan.

In 1392 the general Yi Seong-gye overthrew Goryeo and founded Joseon, moving the capital to Hanyang, later Seoul, and installing Neo-Confucianism as state ideology; the Hanja-writing yangban elite dominated scholarship and office. King Sejong (1418–1450) ordered the creation of Hangul, proclaimed in 1446, and pushed the border to the Amnok and Tuman rivers against the Jurchens.

Toyotomi Hideyoshi's 1592 and 1598 invasions devastated the peninsula until Yi Sun-sin's turtle ships and Ming intervention turned the tide. Manchu invasions in 1627 and 1636–1637 forced Joseon into brotherhood and then into Qing tributary submission. The eighteenth century brought a scholarly revival under Kings Yeongjo and Jeongjo, but after 1800 Andong Kim corruption and persecution of Catholics accompanied mounting peasant unrest.
zh:
朝鲜人是朝鲜半岛主体民族，青铜时代祖先由满洲南下，与半岛农耕人群融合。1337年统治半岛的是918年建立、以开城为都的高丽王朝，佛教王国长期处在蒙元阴影下。

1392年李成桂推翻高丽建立朝鲜王朝，迁都汉阳（即后来的汉城），程朱理学定为国家意识形态，学问官职由用汉文的两班贵族垄断。世宗（1418—1450年）主持创制谚文，1446年颁布，又对女真用兵，把北界推到鸭绿江、图们江。

1592和1598年丰臣秀吉两度入侵，半岛惨遭蹂躏，李舜臣龟船与明朝援军扭转战局。满洲1627年来攻迫使朝鲜订兄弟之盟，1636—1637年再度来攻，迫使朝鲜向清朝称臣。18世纪英祖正祖时期学术复兴、实学兴起；1800年后安东金氏当道，腐败横行，迫害天主教徒，民变频发。

en:
The Korku are the westernmost Munda-speaking people, isolated in the Satpura hills on either side of the Tapti River in southern Madhya Pradesh and northern Maharashtra. Their name combines koro, person, and ku, alive, and their forebears were hunter-gatherers of the Satpura forests before turning to settled cultivation of millet, pulses and wheat.

They are organised into four subsects, the Mawasi being the largest and formerly given to raiding, and into exogamous clans with tree, animal and river totems. In the Mughal age their hills formed the remote forest fringe of the Handia sarkar under Gond chieftains.

After the Marathas took the country in 1742, Korku bands joined the Pindaris in raiding towns such as Harda, which they attacked in the years after 1801. British forces entered the region during the Third Anglo-Maratha War of 1817.
zh:
科尔库人是分布最西的蒙达语族群，孤居于中央邦南部和马哈拉施特拉邦北部、达布蒂河两岸的萨特普拉山区。“科尔库”由“科罗”（人）和“库”（活的）两词合成。其先民本是萨特普拉森林中的狩猎采集者，后来转为定居农耕，种植小米、豆类和小麦。

他们分为四个支系，以马瓦西一支人数最多，过去以劫掠为生；氏族实行外婚制，以树木、动物、河流等为图腾。莫卧儿时期，这片山地是贡德酋长治下汉迪亚行政区的边远林缘。

1742年马拉塔人夺取该地后，科尔库武装与平达里流寇联手袭击哈尔达等城镇，1801年后仍不断寇掠。1817年第三次英国-马拉塔战争期间英军进入这一地区。

en:
The Koroa, called Akoroa by the French, were a people of the Yazoo River basin in present-day northwest Mississippi, with villages on both banks of the Mississippi River; their speech is believed to have been a dialect of Tunica, a language isolate. They may be the Coligua encountered by Hernando de Soto's expedition near modern Little Rock in 1541.

La Salle twice visited a west-bank Koroa town in 1682 and found their Quinipissa allies there. A French mission under Antoine Davion arrived in 1698; in 1702 the priest Nicolas Foucault was killed among them, though Koroa leaders themselves executed his killers.

European epidemics thinned the tribe, and in 1729 the survivors joined the Yazoo and Natchez in a great revolt against the French; afterwards the Koroa ceased to exist as a separate tribe, absorbed by the Tunica, Chickasaw and Natchez.
zh:
科罗阿人是密西西比河谷亚祖河流域的原住民，住在今密西西比州西北部，大河两岸都有村落，法国人称他们为阿科罗阿；他们的语言被认为是孤立语言图尼卡语的一种方言。他们可能就是1541年埃尔南多·德索托远征队在今小石城附近遇到的科利瓜。

1682年，拉萨尔两次到访西岸的一座科罗阿集镇，发现盟友基尼皮萨人也住在镇里。1698年安托万·达维翁率领的法国传教团来到；1702年神父尼古拉斯·富科在他们中间遇害，不过科罗阿首领亲自处死了凶手。

欧洲瘟疫使该部落人口锐减，1729年幸存者与亚祖人、纳奇兹人联合发动反法大起义；此后科罗阿人不再作为独立部落存在，部众被图尼卡人、奇克索人和纳奇兹人吸收。

en:
The Koryaks are the indigenous people north of Kamchatka, from the Bering Sea coast and Anadyr basin in the north to Tigil in the south, their language belonging with Chukchi to the Chukotko-Kamchatkan family. They follow two ways of life: coastal Nemelan, village dwellers fishing and hunting sea mammals, and inland Chaucu, reindeer-rich herders of the tundra.

Their ancestors shaped the first-millennium Okhotsk culture. The name Koryak, a neighboring word for reindeer people, entered records with Vladimir Atlasov's 1695 Kamchatka campaigns.

Warfare ran from 1708 to 1715, and in 1745 reindeer Koryaks rose with Chukchi and Yukaghir, crushed only in 1757. War and the smallpox epidemic of 1769 to 1770 cut their numbers from ten or eleven thousand in 1700 to four thousand eight hundred by 1800; peace, trade and Russian settlement then slowly transformed their life.
zh:
科里亚克人是堪察加以北的原住民，分布在北起白令海沿岸和阿纳德尔盆地、南至季吉利一带，语言与楚科奇语同属楚科奇—堪察加语系。他们有两种生计：沿海的内梅兰人意为“村居者”，捕鱼猎海兽；内陆的乔夫楚人意为“多鹿者”，在苔原上游牧。

先民塑造了公元1千纪的鄂霍次克文化。“科里亚克”出自邻近语言，意为“拥有驯鹿的人”，见于弗拉基米尔·阿特拉索夫1695年远征堪察加的文书。

1708—1715年战事连绵，1745年养鹿的科里亚克人与楚科奇人、尤卡吉尔人联合起义，1757年才被镇压。战争加上1769—1770年的天花，人口从1700年的一万或一万一千人降到1800年的4800人，此后和平、贸易和俄国移民逐渐改变了他们的生活。

en:
The Kosraeans are the people of Kosrae, a small volcanic island at the eastern end of the Caroline Islands, speaking Kosraean, a core Micronesian language of the Austronesian family. Settled by the early first millennium, the island gave rise to the walled city of Leluh, which flourished from about 1250 as seat of a stratified kingdom of nobles and commoners, with matrilineal clans, shell money and stone burial pyramids for its rulers.

Álvaro de Saavedra made the first recorded European sighting in 1529, sailing from Tidore. Spain later claimed the island without occupying it. The first Europeans to land were the French crew of Louis-Isidore Duperrey's corvette La Coquille, spending ten days at Okat Harbour in June 1824 and recording Leluh's ruins.

Whalers followed, but as late as 1837 Kosrae remained under its own chiefs, untouched by colonial administration.
zh:
科斯雷人是加罗林群岛东端火山小岛科斯雷的居民，使用南岛语系密克罗尼西亚语族核心语言之一的科斯雷语。该岛在公元第一个千年早期已有居民，后来兴起城墙环绕的莱卢城：约1250年起它成为等级森严的王国都城，社会分贵族与平民，氏族按母系传承，使用贝壳货币，统治阶层拥有石造墓葬金字塔。

1529年，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉从蒂多雷返航时留下欧洲人最早的目击记录。西班牙后来声称拥有该岛却从未驻军。真正登岛的第一批欧洲人是路易·伊西多尔·迪佩雷率领的法国护卫舰“科基耶号”船员，1824年6月在奥卡特港停留十天，并记录了莱卢城遗址。

此后捕鲸船相继而来，但直到1837年，科斯雷仍由本族酋长统治，没有任何殖民机构上岛。

en:
Kota Gabun denotes the Bakota, Bantu speakers of the dense north-eastern Gabon forests, chiefly around Makokou and across the Congo border, including the Mahongwe among other groups. Their traditions bring them south from overcrowded northern lands, and their name is said to recall migrants gathering in one bound bundle on a riverbank during the crossing.

They speak iKota, a Bantu language, in patriarchal farming and hunting villages marked by secret circumcision and widow-purification rites. They are famed for their mbulu-ngulu reliquary guardians: stylized wooden faces sheathed in copper plates and lamellae atop baskets holding lineage ancestors' bones, through which the living spoke with the dead, rare copper itself signalling wealth and spiritual power.

Carbon-14 dates surviving Mahongwe examples to around 1600, showing the bwete ancestor cult and its sculpture fully developed by the seventeenth century and flourishing through the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.
zh:
科塔加蓬指巴科塔人，即生活在加蓬东北部马科库一带密林及刚果边境的班图语族群，包括马洪圭等支系。传说先民从北方人口稠密之地南迁，据说族名来自迁徙渡河时众人像捆成一包那样聚在河岸的经历。

他们讲伊科塔语，在父系氏族村落中农耕狩猎，有秘传的割礼和寡妇净化仪式。巴科塔人最负盛名的是姆布卢-恩古卢圣物守护者雕像：风格化的木质面孔覆以铜片铜条，安放在盛放祖先遗骨的篮上，生者借此与死者沟通；稀有的铜本身象征财富与灵力。

碳十四测年把现存马洪圭风格作品断在1600年前后，说明布韦特祖先崇拜及其雕刻在17世纪已完全成熟，并在18世纪至19世纪初持续繁荣。

en:
The Kowoj were a Late Postclassic Maya group and polity of the Petén lakes in northern Guatemala, active from about 1250 to the Spanish conquest. Their traditions traced them to Mayapan in Yucatán; its fifteenth-century collapse sent them south into Petén, where they settled Zacpetén on Lake Salpetén, Ixlu between the Salpetén and Petén Itzá lakes, and Topoxte on the Yaxha lagoon.

Kin to the Itza but political rivals, the Kowoj marked their towns with a distinctive C-shaped plaza temple assemblage inherited from Mayapan; in 1696 a Kowoj attack on the Itza capital Nojpetén burned nine temples. Earlier, in 1518, Juan de Grijalva's expedition clashed with Kowoj fighters at Chakán Putum on the Gulf coast.

With the Itza, the Kowoj held out against the Spanish until 1697, when Nojpetén's fall ended the last independent Maya polities of Mesoamerica.
zh:
科沃伊人是后古典期末期（约1250年起）危地马拉北部佩滕湖区的玛雅族群兼政权。按其传说，先祖来自尤卡坦的玛雅潘，该城15世纪崩解后他们南迁佩滕，在萨尔佩滕湖畔的萨克佩滕、萨尔佩滕湖与佩滕伊察湖之间的伊斯卢和雅克萨潟湖畔的托波斯特建城。

科沃伊人与伊察人同源却长期为敌，用承袭自玛雅潘的独特C形广场神庙群标识城镇；1696年他们攻打伊察都城塔亚萨尔，焚毁九座神庙。更早的1518年，胡安·德·格里哈尔瓦的远征队在墨西哥湾沿岸的查坎普图姆与科沃伊武士交战。

科沃伊人与伊察人一同抵抗西班牙人至1697年，塔亚萨尔陷落，中美洲最后一批独立的玛雅政权告终。

en:
Koyoongkawi is the speakers' own name for Konkow, the Northwestern Maidu language of the Sacramento Valley edge: koyoo means meadow, so the word denotes the speech of the meadow tribe. Its bands held the lower Yuba and Feather River country, where hundreds of small independent villages shared similar customs and lived on acorn meal and the Yuba salmon runs.

Their villages included Yupu or Yubu, whose name was given to the Yuba River, and the Mechoopda, whose main settlement stood near Chico. Like other Maiduan peoples they had no chiefs beyond the leaders of their Kuksu dance societies, and their valley homes put them closer than the mountain bands to Spanish and Mexican travel routes.

In 1833 the malaria epidemic that swept the Sacramento Valley struck these river villages hardest, opening the way for the foreign settlement that followed.
zh:
科永卡维是萨克拉门托谷地边缘的康考语（即西北迈杜语）使用者对本族语言的自称：koyoo意为“草甸”，整个词即“草甸部落之语”。他们的群体据有尤巴河与费瑟河下游一带，数百个独立的小村落习俗相近，以橡子粉和尤巴河的鲑鱼洄游为生。

其村落包括尤普（又称尤布）村——尤巴河后来便得名于此——以及主营地在奇科附近的米乔普达人。和其他迈杜族群一样，他们除库克苏舞社的首领外没有酋长；谷地的住地也使他们比山地群体更接近西班牙和墨西哥人的往来路线。

1833年，席卷萨克拉门托谷地的疟疾对这些河畔村落打击最重，为随后的外来定居者打开了通道。

en:
The Koyukon, who call themselves Denaa and their language Denaakk'e, are an Alaska Native Athabaskan people of the interior, with villages strung along the Yukon and Koyukuk rivers. Archaeological evidence traces their occupation of the region back at least a thousand years.

As hunters and trappers they followed a seasonal round of salmon fishing, caribou and moose hunting and fur taking, trading furs to coastal Iñupiat and Yupik, through whom Russian goods and tobacco reached them before any European arrived. The first Russians ascended the Yukon as far as Nulato in the 1830s, finding that a smallpox epidemic had already devastated the village; introduced diseases would cut deep into the Koyukon population in the years that followed.
zh:
科育空人自称迪纳人，称自己的语言为迪纳阿克语，是内陆的阿拉斯加阿萨巴斯卡族群，村落散布在育空河与科尤库克河沿岸。考古证据显示，他们在这一地区至少已生活了一千年。

他们按季节轮替捕鲑鱼、猎驯鹿和驼鹿、取毛皮，并把毛皮卖给沿海的伊努皮亚特人和尤皮克人，俄国人的货物和烟草也经由此路先于欧洲人到来。1830年代，首批俄国人沿育空河上溯至努拉托，发现一场天花已经重创了村庄；此后外来疫病使科育空人口锐减。

en:
The Kpelle, called the Guerze in Guinea, are a Mande-speaking people of central Liberia and the adjoining forest belt of Guinea. In a country of heavy rainfall and broken ground they farm rice as their staple crop, and their towns were traditionally governed by paramount chiefs and town chiefs.

Their traditions place their ancestors in the Sudanian belt in the sixteenth century, from where they moved westward as the Mali Empire crumbled into tribal wars, clearing forest land for their settlements. In later centuries they traded rice and forest produce with Muslim Vai and Mandinka merchants on the routes to the coast.
zh:
克佩勒人在几内亚被称为格尔泽人，是说曼德语族语言的民族，居住在利比里亚中部和毗邻的几内亚森林地带。他们在多雨崎岖的土地上以种植水稻为生，城镇传统上由最高酋长和城镇酋长治理。

按其口述传统，他们的祖先16世纪时居住在苏丹地带，因马里帝国瓦解后的部落混战向西迁徙，开垦林地定居。此后几个世纪里，他们在通往海岸的商路上与穆斯林瓦伊人和曼丁哥商人交易大米和林产品。

en:
The Kren, known to the Portuguese as Aimoré or Botocudo, from the botoque wooden plugs worn in their lips and ears, are a Macro-Jê people of eastern Brazil. Their own name Krenak means heads or sons of the land, and their language belongs to the Jê family.

In 1532 a Botocudo chief was carried to the court of Henry VIII, and a fort raised at Espírito Santo in 1535 was meant to guard against them. Slave-raiding provoked the long Aimoré War from 1555 onward.

Colonists gradually drove them west over the Serra dos Aimorés into Minas Gerais, where diamond strikes at the end of the eighteenth century brought fresh conflict. The frontier wars of 1790 to 1820, fought with deliberate smallpox contagion and poisoned food, nearly destroyed the eastern Botocudo groups and left the Krenak as their principal survivors.
zh:
克雷纳克人被葡萄牙人称为艾莫雷人或博托库多人，博托库多一名来自他们戴在唇上和耳垂上的木塞。他们是巴西东部的大热语系族群，自称克雷纳克意为“土地之首”或“土地之子”，所说的语言属热语族。

1532年一名博托库多酋长被带到亨利八世的宫廷，1535年葡萄牙人在圣埃斯皮里图修筑堡垒，目的就是防备他们。掳人为奴的劫掠引发了1555年起漫长的艾莫雷战争。

殖民者逐渐把他们向西赶过艾莫雷山脉，逼入米纳斯吉拉斯；18世纪末那里发现钻石，带来新的冲突。1790—1820年的边疆战争中，殖民者故意传播天花、投放毒物，东部的博托库多各群体几近覆灭，克雷纳克人成为他们主要的遗裔。

en:
The Ktunaxa, also called Kutenai or Kootenay, are an Indigenous people of the northern Columbia Plateau whose bands live along the Kootenay River, split into Upper and Lower groups. Their Kutenai language is a language isolate.

One account of their origins holds that they began on the prairies and were pushed across the Rockies by the Blackfoot; each year parties crossed the mountains to hunt bison, and rivalry with the Blackfoot over hunting grounds often turned violent. Plateau villages lived on salmon, game and roots, travelling in distinctive sturgeon-nosed bark canoes.

In the eighteenth century a Lower Kootenay prophet, Shining Shirt, foretold the coming of black-robed missionaries, and by the 1830s Christian elements reached the Ktunaxa through Iroquois voyageurs. The North West Company built Kootanae House among them in 1807, but abandoned it in 1812 under hostility from the Peigan.
zh:
库特内人又称库特奈人，是哥伦比亚高原北部的原住民，各支系沿库特内河而居，分为上、下两支。他们的库特内语是一门孤立语言。

关于其起源，一种说法认为他们原住草原，被黑脚人赶过了落基山脉；此后每年仍有队伍翻山捕猎野牛，围绕猎场与黑脚人的冲突常演变为武力相向。高原上的村落以鲑鱼、野味和根茎为生，出行使用独特的鲟鱼鼻树皮独木舟。

18世纪，下库特内的先知“闪光之衫”预言黑袍传教士即将到来；到19世纪30年代，基督教元素已随易洛魁向导传入库特内人中间。西北公司于1807年在他们那里建起库特内贸易站，但在佩甘人的敌对压力下于1812年将其放弃。

en:
The Kuba, also called Bakuba or Bushongo, are a cluster of about nineteen Bantu-speaking peoples in the heart of the Congo basin, between the Sankuru, Lulua and Kasai rivers. Their ancestors are said to have migrated from the north in the sixteenth century, settling among earlier villagers and Twa foragers.

Around 1625 the outsider leader Shyaam a-Mbul united the rival chiefdoms into the Kuba Kingdom. The kingdom was ruled by a king, the nyim, drawn from the Bushoong clan, who governed through a council representing each subject group.

Maize, cassava, beans and tobacco from the Americas brought wealth, and Kuba nobles patronized embroidered raffia cloth, geometric helmet masks and carved ndop royal figures. During the eighteenth century the nyims extended their power southward along the Kasai, and the kingdom entered the nineteenth century comparatively untouched by the Atlantic slave trade.
zh:
库巴人又称巴库巴人或布尚人，是生活在刚果盆地中心、散库鲁河、卢卢阿河与开赛河之间约十九个班图语族群的统称。据说他们的祖先在16世纪从北方迁来，与更早的村民和特瓦族狩猎采集者混居。

约1625年，外来首领希亚姆·安布尔统一了彼此竞争的诸酋长国，建立库巴王国。王国由布尚氏族出身的国王“尼伊姆”统治，通过代表各臣属族群的议事会治理。

美洲传来的玉米、木薯、豆类和烟草带来了新财富，库巴贵族资助了刺绣酒椰布、几何纹头盔面具和恩多普国王雕像等艺术。18世纪，历任尼伊姆沿开赛河向南扩张，进入19世纪时，王国较少受到大西洋奴隶贸易的冲击。

en:
The Kuchun-deka are the Kuccuntikka, the Buffalo Eaters of the Eastern Shoshone, also called the Plains Shoshone and later the Wind River Shoshone. Their country lay along the upper Green and Wind rivers of western Wyoming, and they kept the largest horse herds of any Shoshone band.

Mounted early, they pushed far north on to the plains of Montana and Alberta until the Blackfoot, armed through the Hudson's Bay trade, drove them back; the surveyor David Thompson found most of that northern territory lost by 1787. Their kinsmen the Comanche had already split off for the southern plains in the late seventeenth or early eighteenth century.

Around the Wind River Range they fought the Crow over prime bison ground, and from the 1820s their camps anchored the Rocky Mountain fur trade's summer rendezvous.
zh:
库春德卡人即库春蒂卡人，是东肖肖尼人的“食野牛者”支群，又称平原肖肖尼人，也就是后来的温德河肖肖尼人。他们的家园在怀俄明西部的格林河上游与温德河一带，拥有所有肖肖尼支群中最大的马群。

他们很早就掌握骑术，向北远抵蒙大拿和阿尔伯塔的平原，直到黑脚人通过哈得孙湾贸易获得火器后将其逐退；测量员戴维·汤普森在1787年记述，北方的故土大多已经丧失。他们的近亲科曼奇人则已于17世纪末或18世纪初分离，南迁到大平原南部。

在温德河岭一带，他们为争夺优良的野牛猎场与克罗人交战；从19世纪20年代起，他们的营地还成为落基山毛皮贸易夏季集会的依托之地。

en:
The Kuhtsutuuka, whose name means Bison Eaters and was written Kotsoteka in Spanish documents, were a Shoshone-speaking division whose ancestors lived as hunter-gatherers in the Wyoming mountains. They were probably among the first of the Shoshonean groups to break away: during the sixteenth century the proto-Comanche crossed the Rocky Mountains, and after the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 they became mounted bison hunters on the southern plains.

In the late 1770s their leader Cuerno Verde, who had inherited his father's green-tinted horned headdress, led raids on Spanish settlements. Governor Juan Bautista de Anza marched against him with Ute, Apache and Pueblo auxiliaries and killed him in a running battle in Colorado in September 1779.

Through the early nineteenth century the Kotsoteka remained one of the strongest Comanche divisions, until the Cheyenne and Arapaho advance of the 1830s severed their last links with the Shoshone of Wyoming.
zh:
库楚图卡人名字意为食野牛者，西班牙文献写作科措特卡。他们的先祖是怀俄明山区讲肖肖尼语的狩猎采集者，而且很可能是最早分离出去的肖肖尼群体之一：16世纪，原科曼奇人越过落基山脉；1680年普韦布洛起义后，他们变成南部平原上骑马猎野牛的人。

18世纪70年代末，战将绿角继承了父亲那顶染绿的角饰头饰，并率部劫掠西班牙定居点。总督安萨联合犹他人、阿帕奇人和普韦布洛人出兵征讨，于1779年9月在科罗拉多的连续追击战中将他杀死。

19世纪初，库楚图卡人仍是科曼奇人最强的分支之一，直到1830年代夏延人和阿拉帕霍人推进，切断了他们与怀俄明肖肖尼人的最后联系。

en: The Kuiba were a little-documented Indigenous people of the western Venezuelan interior around Aricagua, on the margin between the Andean foothills and the llanos. Their language is known only from colonial and later ethnographic name lists, which group it speculatively with the extinct Jirajaran tongues of Lara and Falcón; no grammar or texts survive to confirm the link.
zh: 奎巴人是委内瑞拉内陆西部阿里卡瓜一带、安第斯山麓与平原交界地带的原住民，记载稀少。他们的语言只散见于殖民时代及后世的民族志名录，学者推测它与拉腊和法尔孔一带已消亡的希拉哈拉诸语同类，但没有语法或文本存世，这一归属无法证实。

en:
The Kuikuro are a Cariban-speaking people of the upper Xingu River in Mato Grosso, one of the interconnected Upper Xingu tribes. They are regarded as the descendants of the builders of the archaeological towns now called Kuhikugu, whose palisaded villages, plazas, bridges and radial roads housed perhaps ten thousand people by around 1400.

These settlements were abandoned around four hundred years ago, probably after epidemics introduced through European contact shattered the old network. Surviving Kuikuro communities kept the village-otomo way of life, combining fishing, manioc farming and ritual exchange with their Xingu neighbors.

Their cosmology centers on the sun Giti and moon Alukuma as creators and on the Itseke spirits of water and forest, dealt with by initiated shamans who diagnose illness and misfortune. Portuguese slave-raiding bandeirantes entered their oral memory long before peaceful European visits, leaving disease and disruption.
zh:
库伊库罗人是马托格罗索州兴古河上游使用加勒比语族语言的族群，属上兴古诸部之一。他们被认为是考古遗址库希库古城建造者的后裔：那些设有木栅、广场、桥梁和放射状道路的村镇，在1400年前后可能容纳了上万人。

这批聚落在约四百年前被废弃，很可能是欧洲人接触带来的疫病摧毁了旧有网络。幸存群体保留了“奥托莫”村落生活方式，以捕鱼、木薯种植和与兴古邻族的礼仪交换为生。

他们的宇宙观以太阳神吉蒂和月神阿卢库马为创世者，并崇信水中与林间的伊采凯精灵，由入会后的萨满沟通、诊断疾病与灾祸。早在欧洲人和平到来之前，葡萄牙猎奴远征队就已进入他们的口述记忆，留下疫病与破坏。

en:
The Kukakma are the Cocama, who call themselves Kukama, a Tupi-Guarani people of the upper Amazon floodplain; the Spaniards knew them together with their kin as Omaguas or Cambeba. They held the island-dotted channels and banks of the lower Huallaga, Ucayali and Marañón, where they farmed terra preta soils and orchards, fished, and were acknowledged as the finest canoemen on the great river.

The name Cambeba refers to their custom of flattening children's foreheads with boards as a mark of distinction. Their Cocama language is closely related to Omagua and travelled with them upriver from Brazil; by the sixteenth century they had reached the Ucayali.

They first allied with the Spanish missions, but rose against them in 1662 and were crushed in 1666; epidemics and forced recruitment into Spanish armies then thinned their villages.
zh:
库卡克马人即科卡马人（自称库卡马），是上亚马孙河漫滩的图皮-瓜拉尼语族群，西班牙人把他们与同族统称为奥马瓜人，亦称坎贝瓦人。他们据有瓦亚加河下游、乌卡亚利河和马拉尼翁河上沙洲罗布的河道与河岸，在亚马孙黑土和果园中耕作、捕鱼，并被公认为大河上最出色的船夫。

坎贝瓦一名得自他们用木板压平幼儿前额的习俗，以此作为身份标志。他们的科卡马语与奥马瓜语近亲，随族人从巴西溯河而上，到16世纪已进抵乌卡亚利河。

他们起初与西班牙传教站结盟，却于1662年起义，1666年被镇压；此后疫病流行，加上被强征入西班牙军队，村落人口大为减少。

en: The Kukatj, also rendered Kukatji or Gugadj, are an Aboriginal people of the southern Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, whose traditional lands lie around Normanton on the lower Gulf of Carpentaria. Their Kukatj language belonged to the Paman branch of the Pama-Nyungan family and has since become extinct.
zh: 库卡特吉人又拼作库卡吉或古加吉，是昆士兰州约克角半岛南部的原住民，传统领地位于卡奔塔利亚湾下游的诺曼顿一带。他们的库卡特吉语属帕马—牛雅语系的帕曼语支，该语言已经消亡。

en:
The Kukra were a Misumalpan-speaking people of the Ulua branch of the Sumu family, whose home was the coast around present-day Kukra Hill and the Kukra River in southern Nicaragua, south of the Ulwa settlements. Their tongue is counted among the Sumo dialects, alongside Panamahka and Tawahka.

In the second half of the seventeenth century Kukra communities began mixing with Africans brought to the coast as slaves, but their independence ended with the rise of the Miskito: allied with English privateers, Miskito war parties subjugated them, and English influence over the shore lasted until Britain recognized Spanish sovereignty over Mosquitia in 1796.

By the end of the eighteenth century the Kukra had been absorbed into the dominant Miskito, leaving only place names such as Kukra Hill and the Kukra River to mark their former territory.
zh:
库克拉人是苏莫语族乌尔瓦支系的一支米苏马尔潘语族群，故地在尼加拉瓜南部加勒比沿海、今库克拉希尔和库克拉河一带，位于乌尔瓦人聚落以南。他们的语言与帕纳马卡语、塔瓦卡语同属苏莫语的方言。

17世纪下半叶，库克拉社群开始与被贩运到海岸的非洲人混血；但他们的独立随着米斯基托人的崛起而终结：与英国私掠者结盟的米斯基托武装征服了他们，英国对这片海岸的影响一直持续到1796年英国承认西班牙对莫斯基蒂亚的主权。

到18世纪末，库克拉人已被占主导地位的米斯基托人同化，只有库克拉希尔、库克拉河等地名还标示着他们昔日的领地。

en:
The Kuku-Yalanjin are an Aboriginal Australian rainforest people of Far North Queensland, whose traditional territory of some two thousand two hundred square miles covered the headwaters of the Palmer River, running east from Palmerville to Mount Lukin and across the southern and western slopes of the Dividing Range as far as the upper Mitchell River.

They had made the rainforest their home for at least four thousand years, living at high population density in semi-permanent bark huts called gunyahs and ordering the year into five seasons.

Their staple carbohydrate was the toxic seed of the cycad Cycas media, soaked to leach out the poison before cooking, supplemented by yams, bitter walnuts and candlenuts. Their traditional language was Guugu Yalandji, and they are closely related to the Wulpura people of the Mount Windsor rainforest plateau.
zh:
库库‑亚兰吉人是昆士兰远北地区的热带雨林原住民，传统领地约两千二百平方英里，覆盖帕尔默河上游，东起帕默维尔、西至卢金山，横跨大分水岭的南坡与西坡，一直延伸到米切尔河上游。

他们在雨林中至少生活了四千年，人口密度较高，住在半永久性的树皮棚屋“古尼亚”里，并把一年划分为五个季节。

他们的主食是有毒的媒质苏铁种子，须先用水浸出毒素再烹煮，此外还食用山药、苦核桃和石栗。他们的传统语言是古古‑亚兰吉语，与栖息在温莎山雨林台地上的乌尔普拉人亲缘密切。

en: The Kumalu are the people of the Kumalu area in the inland ranges of Morobe Province, New Guinea. Their speech forms the Dambi–Kumalu end of the Mumeng dialect chain, an Austronesian linkage of the South Huon Gulf group whose varieties share only partial mutual intelligibility.
zh: 库马鲁人住在新几内亚莫罗贝省内陆山区的库马鲁一带，所说的方言构成穆孟方言链的丹比-库马鲁一端。穆孟方言链属南岛语系南休恩湾语群，链内各方言只能部分互通。

en:
The Kumandins, who call themselves Kumandy, are a Turkic people of the northern Altai foothills, living along the Biya and lower Katun rivers and speaking a Northern Altai language. Ethnographers treat them as a federation of seok clans of mixed descent: Kipchak-Cuman steppe herders, taiga hunters and Nenets reindeer breeders.
