zh: 伍努马拉人即瓦努马拉人，是昆士兰西北部的澳大利亚原住民，领地覆盖弗林德斯河流域，包括里士满和基努纳；里士满附近的奎彭布拉可能是他们北部的一支游群。他们说的瓦努马拉语又称马伊库兰语，属帕马—牛雅语系的马伊语群，与邻近的恩加温语关系密切。

en:
The Wurundjeri are a Woiwurrung-speaking people of the Kulin nation and, with the Boonwurrung, the traditional owners of the Yarra River valley, the country they call Naarm. Their clans camped along the Yarra and at Bolin Bolin lagoon, taking eels, fish and possum; firestick farming kept open plains thick with murnong yam daisies, the staple starch root.

They worked the Mount William greenstone quarry, whose axe heads were traded as far as New South Wales and Adelaide, and joined Kulin assemblies for ceremony, trade and marriage.

In 1835 John Batman met their ngurungaeta chiefs, including Bebejan and Billibellary, at Merri Creek and, after a tanderrum ceremony, obtained the agreement later called Batman's Treaty. The colonial government annulled it, yet the treaty was used to seize some 600,000 acres, and within a few years most of the Wurundjeri river country had been taken.
zh:
伍伦杰里人是库林联盟中讲沃伊武朗语的族群，与布武朗人同为雅拉河谷的传统主人，他们称这片土地为纳姆。各氏族在雅拉河沿岸和博林博林潟湖一带宿营，捕捉鳗鱼、鱼和负鼠；他们用火耕维持开阔的草原，上面长满作为主要淀粉来源的穆尔农山药菊。

他们开采威廉山的绿石矿场，其石斧毛坯远销新南威尔士和阿德莱德；他们也参加库林诸族的集会，举行仪式、贸易和联姻。

1835年，约翰·巴特曼在梅里溪会见比比扬、比利贝拉里等恩贡加塔首领，在坦德鲁姆仪式之后达成了后来所称的巴特曼条约。殖民政府宣布条约无效，它却被用来侵占约六十万英亩土地，几年之内伍伦杰里人的河畔故土便大半易主。

en:
The Wuthathi, also recorded as the Mutjati or Otati, were an Aboriginal people of the eastern shore of the northern Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, whose country centred on the white silica dunes and coastal rivers of Shelburne Bay on the Coral Sea. Their language was a dialect of Uradhi in the Paman branch of the Pama-Nyungan family.

They were one of the Kawadji, or sandbeach people, who kept camps along the shore and lived mainly by fishing in the ocean and the river mouths, gathering shellfish and seasonal foods along the beach. Captain Cook charted this coastline in 1770.
zh:
伍塔西人（也记作穆贾蒂人或奥塔蒂人）是昆士兰约克角半岛北部东岸的原住民，家园以珊瑚海畔谢尔本湾的白色硅沙沙丘和入海河流为中心。他们的语言是乌拉迪语的一种方言，属帕马-牛雅语系的帕马语组。

他们属于“沙滩人”群体，沿海岸设有营地，主要在海洋和河口捕鱼，在滩涂上采集贝类与时令食物。1770年库克船长测绘了这条海岸线。

en:
The Munduruku, who call themselves Wuyjuyu, “our people”, are a Tupi-speaking people of the Brazilian Amazon whose homeland is the Tapajós river valley. Their familiar name was given them by their enemies the Parintintin and means “red ants”, after their habit of attacking in great swarms; colonists called them head-cutters, for they dried and shrank enemy heads as ritual trophies.

When recorded contact with the Portuguese began in the second half of the 1700s, the Munduruku dominated the Tapajós and drove the Mura of Madeira to seek shelter with the colonists. The Portuguese switched to alliance: in 1788 the Munduruku all but destroyed the Mura.

After 1803 the Munduruku lived at peace with the Brazilians, supplying food and rubber while keeping broad autonomy. The revolt that swept Pará from 1835 brought persecution again, and many communities withdrew deeper into their territory.
zh:
蒙杜鲁库人自称乌伊朱尤，意为“我们的人”，是巴西亚马逊地区使用图皮语族语言的族群，故土在塔帕若斯河流域。蒙杜鲁库这个名字来自敌人帕林廷廷人，意为“红蚁”，形容他们成群蜂拥扑向敌军的战法；殖民者则称他们为“砍头者”，因为他们将敌人的头颅晒干缩制成仪式战利品。

18世纪下半叶葡萄牙人首次留下与他们接触的记载，当时蒙杜鲁库人称雄塔帕若斯河流域，逼得马代拉河的穆拉人投奔殖民者求生。葡萄牙人转而采取结盟策略：1788年蒙杜鲁库人大败穆拉人。

1803年后蒙杜鲁库人与巴西人和平相处，为其提供粮食和橡胶，同时保留了很大的自主权。1835年席卷帕拉的起义使他们再遭迫害，许多社群退入领地深处。

en:
The Wùzhōu culture fills the Jinqu basin of central Zhejiang, around Jinhua and its satellite towns of Lanxi, Dongyang, Yiwu, Yongkang and Wuyi. A county existed here from the second century BC, and in 589 the Sui created Wuzhou Prefecture with its seat at Jinhua; the Tang later split off Quzhou to the west, and after passing through the Wuyue kingdom and the Song, Wuzhou became Wuzhou Route under the Yuan in 1276. Jinhua's present walled city dates to 1352.

Its people speak the Wuzhou division of Southern Wu, a chain of related but distinct county varieties spread across the basin. The Wu River links the prefecture through the Qiantang to the southern end of the Grand Canal, making Jinhua a collecting center for rice, bamboo and forest goods.

Its cured ham has been famous since the Song, and the broad-halled, horse-head-gabled merchant residences built here in the Ming and Qing form the distinctive Wu-school of architecture.
zh:
婺州文化位于浙江中部的金衢盆地，以金华为中心，包括兰溪、东阳、义乌、永康、武义等卫星城邑。早在公元前2世纪这里就已设县，589年隋朝置婺州，州治设在金华；唐代又从婺州析置西边的衢州，其后历经吴越国和两宋，1276年元代升为婺州路。今天金华的城墙城制可追溯到1352年的元末。

当地人说的是南部吴语婺州片，盆地内各县方言相近却各有特点。婺江经钱塘江把州城与大运河南端的水运网连在一起，使金华成为稻米、竹木等农林物产的集散中心。

金华火腿自宋代起远近闻名，盆地里明清商人宅第厅堂宏敞、马头墙高耸，构成别具一格的婺派建筑。

en:
The Halchidhoma, who call themselves Xalychidom Piipaa, meaning the people who live toward the water, were a river people of the lower Colorado around its junction with the Gila. In 1604 and 1605, the Spanish expedition of Juan de Oñate met the Alebdoma on the lower Colorado; when the missionary Eusebio Kino returned in 1700, the tribe had shifted about a hundred miles upriver.

In the warfare of the Colorado tribes, the Halchidhoma sided with the Maricopa and Cocopa against the Quechan and Mohave. In the 1820s the Mohave and Quechan drove them from the river, and they took refuge with the Maricopa on the middle Gila.

Some families moved on to Lehi on the Salt River and kept a separate identity, while the rest merged into the Maricopa; their abandoned Colorado lands were taken over by the Chemehuevi.
zh:
哈利奇多姆人自称“哈利奇多姆·皮皮”，意为“临水而居的人”，是科罗拉多河下游与希拉河汇流一带的河畔族群。1604—1605年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特率领的西班牙远征队在科罗拉多河下游遇到了“阿莱布多马人”；1700年传教士尤西比奥·基诺再访此地时，发现该部已向上游迁移约一百英里。

在科罗拉多河诸部的战事中，哈利奇多姆人与马里科帕人、科科帕人结盟，对抗夸特桑人和莫哈维人。19世纪20年代，莫哈维人与夸特桑人把他们逐出科罗拉多河，他们投奔希拉河中游的马里科帕人。

此后一部分家族迁到盐河的利希并保持独立认同，其余则融入马里科帕人；他们在科罗拉多河畔弃守的土地被切梅惠维人占据。

en:
The Cxam are the ǀXam, the San people of the dry Karoo and Bushmanland in South Africa's Northern Cape. Their language belonged to the ǃUi branch of the Tuu click family and was closely related to Nǁng. Like other San they had no chiefs, moved seasonally between springs and pans, and painted hunting scenes and trance visions on rock shelters.

After the Dutch founded their Cape station in 1652, trekboer pastoralists pushed into the Karoo from 1714, occupying waterholes and shooting game. Resistance and stock-raiding brought punitive commandos, whose raids became general along the frontier from the 1770s.

In 1777 the Dutch East India Company formally endorsed the extermination of the San. By the end of the century thousands had been killed or bound to frontier farmers, and the independent ǀXam bands of the Karoo had been broken.
zh:
卡姆人是生活在南非北开普省干旱卡鲁和布须曼兰地区的桑人。他们的语言属图语系ǃUi语支，与努语近亲。和其他桑人一样，他们没有酋长，随季节在泉眼和盐沼间迁徙，在岩棚里留下狩猎与出神幻象的壁画。

1652年荷兰人在开普建立据点后，游牧布尔民从1714年起涌入卡鲁，占去水洼，射杀猎物。反抗和劫掠牲畜招来报复性民团，其袭击从18世纪70年代起在整个边境蔓延。

1777年，荷兰东印度公司正式认可对桑人的剿灭政策。到该世纪末，数以千计的桑人被杀或被迫为农场服役，卡鲁地区独立的卡姆人小群已被打散。

en:
The Xaracuu are the Kanak people of south-central Grande Terre in New Caledonia, their Xârâcùù language often called Canala after its chief town. Xârâcùù forms, with Xârâgurè, a distinct branch of the southern New Caledonian languages, heirs to the Austronesian speech of Lapita villagers who first occupied these coasts between 1100 BC and AD 200.

Xârâcùù numerals carry special classifiers, prefixes and suffixes that sort counted things by kind. Shell money, yam stores and ceremonial gifts fixed every clan's rank, and Xaracuu chiefs ruled from great houses topped with the carved flèche faîtière, overseeing taro terraces, lagoon fishing fleets and cycles of feast and feud.

James Cook sailed past in 1774 without landing, and for two generations more the only Europeans seen were passing whalers. Well into the 1830s the Xaracuu valleys still ran by their own clan politics.
zh:
哈拉库人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛中南部的卡纳克人，其哈拉库语常以重镇得名而称卡纳拉语。哈拉库语与邻近的哈拉古雷语共同构成新喀里多尼亚南部语群中的独立分支；南部语群承继了公元前1100年至公元200年间最早占据这些海岸的拉皮塔村民所使用的南岛语。

哈拉库语的数词带有特殊的量词、前缀和后缀，按类别区分所数之物。贝币、山药储备和仪式礼物决定着氏族的等级，哈拉库酋长在屋顶竖着雕花矛饰的大屋里发号施令，统辖芋头梯田、潟湖捕鱼船队以及宴饮与仇杀交替的周期。

詹姆斯·库克于1774年途经此地但并未登陆，此后两代人见到的欧洲人只有路过的捕鲸者。直到19世纪30年代，哈拉库各山谷仍依照自己的氏族规则运转。

en:
The Xauxa were the Quechua-speaking people of the southern Mantaro Valley in the Peruvian highlands, belonging before the Incas to the Xauxa-Wanka confederation. They submitted to Túpac Yupanqui, and the Incas built Hatun Xauxa as an administrative center on the road between Cusco and Quito.

In the Inca civil war the Xauxa sided with Huascar, whose generals used the city as headquarters until Atahualpa's general Challco Chima stormed it and took reprisals against the loyalist population. The captive Huascar was held in its fortress before being drowned in the Andamarca River.

The Xauxa welcomed the Spaniards as liberators: Francisco Pizarro made Santa Fe de Hatun Xauxa the first Spanish capital of Peru in April 1534, though Lima supplanted it the next year. Jauja later declined into dependence on Tarma; between 1742 and 1756 its mountains were swept by the indigenous rebellion of Juan Santos Atahualpa.
zh:
豪哈人是秘鲁高原曼塔罗河谷南部讲克丘亚语的族群，在印加人到来之前属于豪哈-万卡联盟。他们归顺图帕克·尤潘基，印加人修建大东豪哈作为行政中心，位于连接库斯科与基多的道路旁。

印加内战中，豪哈人站在瓦斯卡尔一边，其将领以该城为大本营，直到阿塔瓦尔帕的大将查尔库奇马将其攻陷并报复效忠派居民。被俘的瓦斯卡尔关押在城中要塞，后来被溺死在安达马卡河。

豪哈人把西班牙人当作解放者迎接：1534年4月，皮萨罗将圣菲-德大东豪哈定为西属秘鲁的第一个首府，不过次年利马便取代了它。豪哈城后来日渐衰落，依附于塔尔马；1742年至1756年间，其周围山区卷入胡安·桑托斯·阿塔瓦尔帕领导的印第安人起义。

en: The X'xegwi are the ǁXegwi, San foragers of the high grasslands around Lake Chrissie in eastern South Africa, close to the Swazi border. Their extinct Batwa tongue was an ǃKwi language of the Tuu family; they called themselves Tlouʼeʼthle, ‘people of rock and water’, while Nguni neighbours called them Abatwa and the Sotho Baroa.
zh: 泽格维人是南非东部高地草原、邻近斯威士兰边界的克里西湖一带的桑人狩猎采集者。他们已消亡的语言又称巴特瓦语，属图语系的克维语支；他们自称 Tlouʼeʼthle，意为“岩石与水之民”，恩古尼邻族称其为阿巴特瓦人，索托人则称巴罗阿人。

en: The Xetá are a Tupi-Guarani people of the Serra dos Dourados in northwestern Paraná, whose traditional lands lay along the Ivaí River and its tributaries. Their men wore wooden lip discs after the initiation ritual, which earned them the colonial label of Botocudo, and through the whole colonial period they remained almost entirely beyond Portuguese observation.
zh: 谢塔人是巴拉那州西北部多拉达山的图皮-瓜拉尼语族群，传统领地位于伊瓦伊河及其支流一带。他们的男子在成年礼后佩戴木制唇盘，因而得到博托库多这一殖民地称呼；整个殖民时期，他们几乎都处在葡萄牙人的视野之外。

en:
The Xhosa are the southernmost Nguni people, Bantu-speaking agropastoralists who have held the Eastern Cape since at least the seventh century, absorbing San and Khoekhoe. Oral tradition traces the Xhosa kingdom to Tshawe, who before the fifteenth century overthrew his brother and united Nguni and Khoekhoe clans under the royal amaTshawe.

Their language belongs to the Nguni branch of Bantu and carries roughly fifteen percent Khoisan vocabulary along with click consonants adopted from the same contact. The Dutch foundation of the Cape in 1652 began colonial pressure eastward, and by the later eighteenth century the Xhosa chiefdoms were fighting the Cape frontier wars.

During the mfecane upheavals of the early nineteenth century they sheltered refugees fleeing the Zulu kingdom, incorporating them as the amaMfengu. In 1823 missionaries produced the first printed works in isiXhosa at the Lovedale press.
zh:
科萨人是恩古尼各族中分布最南的一支，是说班图语的农牧民。至迟从7世纪起，他们便占据东开普，并同化了桑人和科伊科伊人。口传传统把科萨王国追溯到首领察韦：他在15世纪以前推翻兄长，把恩古尼和科伊科伊氏族并入以王室阿姆察韦氏族为核心的政权。

科萨语属班图语系恩古尼语支，约有百分之十五的词汇来自科伊桑语，还在接触中吸收了吸气辅音。1652年荷兰人在开普建殖民地，开始东扩；到18世纪后期，科萨各酋邦投入开普边境战争。

19世纪初的姆费卡内大乱中，他们收容逃离祖鲁王国的难民，将其编为姆芬古人。1823年，传教士在洛夫代尔印刷所印出了最早的科萨语出版物。

en:
Xiangxi denotes the Ji-Xu, or Chen-Xu, branch of Xiang Chinese, scattered through the Wuling mountains along the middle Yuan River in western Hunan. It stands apart from both New and Old Xiang, keeping only some of the Middle Chinese voiced initials, and sits beside the Miao and Tujia languages of the same hills.

Chinese rule reached the region with the expansion of the state of Chu in the third century BCE, and Han and later dynasties kept only a loose hold on its valleys.

Under the Yuan and the Ming after 1368 the native Tujia and Miao chieftains, or tusi, governed much of the area; the Qing court later replaced them with appointed officials in its gaitu guiliu reforms, tightening imperial control.
zh:
湘西指湘语的吉溆片（亦称辰溆片），散布在湖南西部武陵山区、沅水中游。它既不同于新湘也不同于老湘，只保留了部分中古汉语浊声母，与同一片山区里的苗语、土家语并存。

公元前3世纪楚国扩张，把统治延伸到这一地区；汉代以后的历代王朝对这些山谷控制松弛。

元代以及1368年建立的明代，当地的土家族、苗族土司统辖着大部分地方；清代推行改土归流，以流官取代土著首领，朝廷控制加强。

en: The Xindonga is a collective name for four small Bantu groups of southeastern Angola's Cuando Cubango country, the Cusso or Mbukushu, Dilico, Sambio and Maxico, living by subsistence farming, fishing and hunting along the Kavango and upper Zambezi. The Mbukushu, the best known of them, formed one of the five Kavango kingdoms and were famed as rain-makers.
zh: 欣东加是对安哥拉东南宽多-库邦戈地区四个班图小族群的统称，即库苏（姆库舒）、迪利科、桑比奥和马希科，他们在卡万戈河与赞比西河上游一带靠自给农业、渔猎为生。其中最知名的姆库舒人是卡万戈五王国之一，以祈雨之术闻名。

en:
The Xinghua, or Putian people, are the Han Chinese of the Xinghua plain on the central Fujian coast, speaking Pu-Xian, a Coastal Min tongue midway between the Eastern Min of Fuzhou and the Southern Min of Quanzhou.

Putian county was first set up under the Chen dynasty in 568; in 979 the Song created the separate Xinghua military prefecture, after which its dialect developed on its own, taking in Eastern Min features while keeping a Southern Min core.

Lin Moniang, a shamaness of Meizhou Island born in 960, was worshipped after her death in 987 as Mazu, goddess of the sea. Song emperors recognised her temple from 1123, Zheng He earned her a new title in 1409, and after the Qing campaign against Taiwan in 1683 she was promoted to Heavenly Empress.
zh:
兴化人又称莆田人，是福建中部沿海兴化平原上的汉族民系，操莆仙话，一种介于福州闽东语与泉州闽南语之间的沿海闽语。

莆田县最早设于568年的陈朝；宋朝于979年另设兴化军，此后方言独立发展，在闽南语底子上吸收了闽东语的特点。

湄洲岛巫女林默娘生于960年，987年去世后被奉为海神妈祖。1123年起宋朝皇帝敕封其庙，1409年郑和为她请得新封号，1683年清军平定台湾后她又被晋封为天后。

en:
The Xīnhuì are the people of the lower Tan River in the south-western Pearl River Delta, whose speech, with the Huicheng accent as its standard, is one of the representative dialects of the coastal Siyi or Four Counties branch of Yue.

Settled on land silted up at the confluence of the Tan and West Rivers, Xinhui was the scene of the Battle of Yamen in 1279, when the last Song fleet was destroyed by the Yuan navy and the boy emperor Zhao Bing perished in the sound.

Under the Ming it produced Chen Baisha, born in 1428; his Baisha school of Neo-Confucianism shaped Lingnan thought for generations. The county also gave its name to Xinhui chenpi, the dried mandarin peel prized across China in cooking and medicine.
zh:
新会人聚居在珠江三角洲西南部潭江下游，所说新会话以会城腔为标准音，属粤语沿海支系四邑方言，是四邑话的代表之一。

新会地处潭江与西江交汇处的冲积平原，1279年这里的崖门海面爆发崖门海战，南宋最后的水师被元朝海军歼灭，幼帝赵昺殉海。

明代这里诞生了生于1428年的陈献章，世称陈白沙，他开创的白沙学派塑造了此后数代的岭南理学。新会还以特产新会陈皮闻名，这种晒制的柑橘皮在中国饮食和医药中长期被视为佳品。

en:
The Xinka are a non-Mayan people of southeastern Guatemala, possibly among the earliest inhabitants of the region, predating both the Maya and the Pipil. Their Xincan languages form an isolated family with many Mayan loanwords. Before the Spanish arrival they shared the eastern Pacific plain with the Pipil.

In 1524 Pedro de Alvarado met them at Guazacapán and stormed their principal city of Atiquipaque, near Taxisco, on 26 May, against warriors fighting with spears and poisoned arrows. The survivors paid tribute in cacao, cotton, salt and vanilla, and many were enslaved and marched off to the conquest of El Salvador, which gave Los Esclavos near Cuilapa its name.

After 1575 deportations emptied whole towns, and by the time Archbishop Cortés y Larraz visited the diocese of Taxisco in 1769 the Xincan tongue survived in only a few communities.
zh:
辛卡人是危地马拉东南部的非玛雅族群，可能是当地最早的居民之一，比玛雅人和皮皮尔人更早来到这里。他们的辛卡语是一个孤立语系，吸收了大量玛雅语借词。西班牙人到来之前，他们与皮皮尔人分据东部太平洋平原。

1524年，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多进至瓜萨卡潘，于5月26日攻占他们位于塔克西斯科附近的首要城市阿蒂基帕克，守城武士以长矛和毒箭抵抗。幸存者以可可、棉花、盐和香草纳贡，许多人被掳为奴，押去参加征服萨尔瓦多的战事，奎拉帕附近的洛斯埃斯克拉沃斯便由此得名。

1575年之后，人口流放使整座城镇空虚，到1769年科尔特斯·伊·拉腊斯大主教视察塔克西斯科教区时，辛卡语只在少数社群中残存。

en:
New Xiang, or Chang-Yi, is the northern and eastern branch of the Xiang languages, centred on Changsha on the lower Xiang River. Xiang speech descends from the Nanchu dialect formed when Chu migrants settled among the Ba, Nanman and Baiyue peoples of Hunan in the Warring States period; the Han scholar Yang Xiong recorded this Southern Chu speech in his Fangyan.

Northern migrants under the Tang brought Middle Chinese forms, and after the Mongol conquest of the Song in the thirteenth century devastated Hunan, large numbers of Jiangxi settlers arrived under the Ming after 1368, bringing Gan influence.

In the speech of Changsha and the eastern lowlands this contact effaced the voiced initials of Middle Chinese, marking New Xiang off from the older dialects of the interior, which retained them.
zh:
新湘又称长益片，是湘语偏北、偏东的一支，以湘江下游的长沙为中心。湘语源于战国时代楚人迁入湖南、与当地巴人、南蛮、百越诸族融合而成的南楚方言，汉代扬雄的《方言》已记载这种南楚话。

唐代北方移民带来中古汉语的成分；13世纪蒙古灭宋之战使湖南人口锐减，1368年明朝建立后，大批江西移民迁入，带来赣语影响。

在长沙及东部低地的口音里，这种接触使中古汉语的浊声母完全消失，新湘由此与内陆保留浊音的老湘区分开来。

en:
The Xixime were a people of the Sierra Madre Occidental, between Sinaloa and Durango, living in extended-family villages around stone cliff towns. They grew crops and traded with coastal peoples; Spanish scouts in Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán's 1530 expedition thought their stone settlements made them more civilized than their neighbors.

Colonial reports claim they ate captured enemies in rites meant to secure the maize harvest, though modern historians suspect such stories were exaggerated. Their feud with the Acaxee ran across the sixteenth century. When Jesuit missions pushed into the sierras the Xixime rose in 1610, calling churches temples of disease and attacking the Acaxee for refusing to join.

Francisco de Urdiñola marched in with Spanish soldiers and native allies and broke the revolt by October. The Xixime later backed the larger Tepehuán Revolt of 1616.
zh:
希希梅人是西马德雷山脉的族群，活动在锡那罗亚与杜兰戈之间，以大家族为单位居住在石砌崖镇周围的村落里。他们种植作物，与沿海居民交易；1530年尼尼奥·贝尔特兰·德·古斯曼远征队的西班牙斥候认为，他们的石砌定居点比邻族更为文明。

殖民文献记载，希希梅人会在祈求玉米丰收的仪式上食用俘虏，不过近代史家怀疑这类说法被夸大了。他们与阿卡塞人的世仇贯穿整个16世纪。耶稣会传教站深入山区后，希希梅人在1610年发动起义，称教堂为“疫病之庙”，并攻打拒绝加盟的阿卡塞人。

弗朗西斯科·德·乌尔迪尼奥拉率西班牙士兵和原住民盟友进山，于当年10月镇压了起义。希希梅人后来又支持了规模更大的1616年特佩万起义。

en:
The Xllang are the people of the Sican, or Lambayeque, culture, which occupied the river valleys of the north Peruvian coast around Chiclayo from about 750 to 1375. Succeeding the Moche, they farmed the irrigated valleys of the La Leche and Lambayeque rivers and spoke Muchik.

Between 900 and 1100 their religious capital at Batán Grande presided over a florescence of adobe temple mounds, fine black ceramics and arsenical-bronze and gold metallurgy; elite tombs held gold masks and tumbaga ornaments. A generation-long drought around 1020 shattered the old order.

The temples of Batán Grande were burned and abandoned between 1050 and 1100, and a new capital rose at Túcume, where twenty-six great mounds were built around La Raya mountain. In 1337 the Lambayeque polities still ruled their valleys, but the expansion of Chimor ended their independence around 1375.
zh:
什扬人即西坎（又称兰巴耶克）文化的居民，约750年至1375年间生活在秘鲁北部沿海奇克拉约一带的河谷中。他们继承莫切文化，在拉莱切河与兰巴耶克河的灌溉谷地务农，使用穆奇克语。

900年至1100年，宗教中心巴丹格兰德进入鼎盛期，土坯神庙、精美黑陶以及砷青铜和黄金冶铸盛极一时，贵族墓葬出土了黄金面具和通巴加金饰。1020年前后持续约三十年的大旱动摇了旧秩序。

巴丹格兰德的神庙在1050年至1100年间被焚毁废弃，新的中心土库美在拉亚山旁建起26座大土墩。1337年时兰巴耶克诸邦仍据有各自的河谷，但奇穆王国的扩张在1375年前后终结了他们的独立。

en:
The Xocó, also recorded as Shocó, Chocó or Ceocose, were an Indigenous people of the lower São Francisco River whose villages in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries ranged from Sergipe north to southern Ceará. They lived largely itinerant lives, repeatedly slipping away from the mission settlements where the Portuguese tried to concentrate them.

In the late seventeenth century Capuchin friars founded the missions of São Pedro de Porto da Folha and Caiçara in Sergipe, gathering the Xocó together with other peoples, and in 1700 the Portuguese Crown granted the mission Indians a square league of land. At São Pedro, the Xocó kept their Toré ritual alive in secret after the missionaries forbade it.
zh:
肖科人（文献中又作绍科、乔科或塞奥科塞）是圣弗朗西斯科河下游的原住民，17至18世纪时村落分布从塞尔希培向北延伸到塞阿拉南部。他们长期过着流动生活，一再逃离葡萄牙人试图集中安置他们的传教村。

17世纪末，嘉布遣会修士在塞尔希培建立圣佩德罗-迪波尔图达福利亚和凯萨拉传教站，把肖科人与其他族群集中在一起；1700年，葡萄牙王室向传教站的印第安人授予一平方里格的土地。在圣佩德罗，传教士禁止托雷仪式后，肖科人仍秘密举行这一仪式。

en: The Qxoon are the ǃXoon, San foragers of the Kalahari in Botswana and Namibia who call their language Taa or ǃXóõ. Taa is a Tuu click language with one of the largest sound inventories, most basic words beginning with a click. It forms a west-to-east dialect continuum, and some communities call themselves ʼNǀohan rather than ǃXoon.
zh: 昆人是博茨瓦纳和纳米比亚卡拉哈里的桑人狩猎采集者，把自己的语言称作 Taa（宏语，又名 ǃXóõ）。宏语属图语系，是已知音位数量最多的语言之一，大部分基本词以吸气音开头。它是一条自西向东分布的方言连续体，部分社群自称 ʼNǀohan，而不用昆人之名。

en:
The Xuānzhōu culture covers the hilly country of southern Anhui between the Tianmu range and Mount Huangshan, centered on Xuancheng and taking in Wuhu, Dangtu, Ningguo and Jingxian. In the Spring and Autumn period it passed between Wu, Yue and Chu; the Qin made it Zhang Commandery in the third century BC, and in 109 BC the Han reorganized it as Danyang Commandery with its seat at Wanling, the future Xuancheng, which became Xuancheng Commandery's seat in 281 and remained the regional center.

Its speech is the Xuanzhou division of Wu, or Western Wu, the most internally diverse Wu branch, carrying strong Jianghuai Mandarin influence and sound innovations of its own.

Through the Yuan, Ming and Qing it was known for crafts rather than politics, above all Xuan rice paper, writing brushes and inkstones sold across China, while the southern hills bordered the merchant country of Huizhou.
zh:
宣州文化地处皖南山地，夹在天目山与黄山之间，以宣城为中心，范围包括芜湖、当涂、宁国、泾县等地。春秋时期这片土地在吴、越、楚之间几经易手；公元前3世纪秦设鄣郡，公元前109年汉改置丹阳郡，郡治宛陵即后来的宣城，281年又设宣城郡，此后一直是区域行政中心。

当地宣州片吴语又称西吴语，是吴语各片中内部分化最复杂的一支，既受北方江淮官话强烈影响，又有自身语音创新。

元明清三代，这片州府以物产而非武功闻名，尤以宣纸、宣笔和砚台享誉全国，宣纸之名即得自宣州；群山之南与徽商故里相接。

en:
The Xumani, better known in Spanish records as the Jumanos, were the people of La Junta, where the Río Conchos meets the Río Bravo. Cabeza de Vaca may have met them near La Junta in 1535, and Antonio de Espejo first used the name Jumano in 1582 for its farming villagers, while related bands hunted bison on the Pecos River.

They traded in hides, meat and salt. In the seventeenth century drought and advancing Lipan and Mescalero Apache drove them to seek Spanish missions and alliances, and the chief Juan Sabeata built trade and Christian ties in the 1680s.

Their language is unrecorded, with Uto-Aztecan, Tanoan and Athabascan all proposed. By 1729 the Spanish spoke of Apache Jumanos, and by 1750 the nation had dissolved, its remnants absorbed by Apache, Caddo and Wichita bands after epidemics, slaving raids and war.
zh:
舒马尼人在西班牙文献中更常见的名字是胡马诺人，活动在孔乔斯河与布拉沃河交汇处的拉洪塔。卡韦萨·德巴卡可能于1535年在拉洪塔附近遇到过他们；1582年，安东尼奥·德埃斯佩霍首次用胡马诺一名称呼当地务农的村人，而与他们同源的队伍则在佩科斯河上猎捕野牛。

他们以兽皮、肉食和盐贸易为生。17世纪，干旱和南下的利潘、梅斯卡莱罗阿帕奇人迫使他们求助于西班牙传教团并寻求同盟，酋长胡安·萨维亚塔在17世纪80年代建立贸易与基督教联系。

他们的语言没有留下记录，犹他—阿兹特克、塔诺和阿萨巴斯卡三种归属都有人主张。到1729年，西班牙人已改称他们为阿帕奇胡马诺人；到1750年，这个民族已在疫病、奴隶猎捕和战争中解体，余众被阿帕奇、卡多和威奇塔诸部吸收。

en: Xuukhoe, meaning ‘people left behind’, is the self-name of the Tsʼixa-speaking San community of Mababe, on the eastern edge of the Okavango Delta in Botswana. Tsʼixa belongs to the Kalahari Khoe branch of the Khoe-Kwadi family, the name is also used by some Khwe speakers, and its speakers are foragers classed by Bantu neighbours as Basarwa. Related Shua dialects such as Deti are spoken around the nearby Makgadikgadi pans.
zh: 乌科伊意为“被留下的人”，是博茨瓦纳奥卡万戈三角洲东缘马巴比村讲茨克萨语的桑人社群的自称，部分克韦语使用者也用这个称呼。茨克萨语属科伊-夸迪语系的卡拉哈里科伊语支，这些人以狩猎采集为生，被班图邻族笼统归入巴萨尔瓦（即桑人）。与它相近的舒阿语方言（如代蒂方言）通行于附近的马卡迪卡迪盐沼一带。

en:
The Yadhaigana, also called Yadhaykenu, were an Aboriginal tribe of the eastern coast at the northern tip of the Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, whose country lay north of the Wuthathi around the later site of Bamaga. Their tongue was a dialect of Uradhi, a Paman language of the Pama-Nyungan family.

Their name was given them by Torres Strait Islanders, in whose language it means talkers or chatterers, a trace of the long maritime trade and contact between the peninsula peoples and the islanders of the strait.

They were the traditional enemies of the Gudang at Cape York's tip and were counted among the warlike tribes of the far north. European ships began sailing the adjacent Torres Strait after the Spanish passage of 1606, and Captain Cook rounded Cape York in 1770.
zh:
亚代加纳人是昆士兰约克角半岛北端东海岸的原住民部落，领地在伍塔西人以北、今巴马加一带。他们的语言是乌拉迪语的一种方言，属帕马-牛雅语系的帕马语组。

亚代加纳这个名字来自托雷斯海峡岛民的语言，意为“话多的人”，折射出半岛族群与海峡岛民之间长期的海上贸易与往来。

他们与半岛最尖端的古当人世为仇敌，被视为极北地区好战的部落之一。自1606年西班牙人首次航过邻近的托雷斯海峡后，欧洲船只开始出入这一带；1770年库克船长绕过约克角。

en: The Yagalingu, also spelt Jagalingu, were an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland whose country covered the headwaters of the Belyando River, from the Great Dividing Range east to the Drummond Range. Their language is poorly recorded and has been tentatively counted as a dialect of Bidjara, and their local groups included the Auanbura, Owanburra, Wakelbara and Kokleburra.
zh: 亚加林古人又拼写为贾加林古，是昆士兰中部的澳大利亚原住民，领地覆盖贝利安多河源头，西起大分水岭、东抵德拉蒙德山脉。他们的语言留存记录很少，曾被暂定为比贾拉语的一种方言，其地方群包括安布拉、奥万布拉、瓦克尔巴拉和科克尔布拉。

en:
The Yahgan, also called Yámana, were the southernmost people on Earth, occupying the islands and channels south of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego as far as Cape Horn in five canoe-borne groups. Their language, Yámana, is an isolate.

They were nomadic hunter-gatherers who lived almost entirely from the sea: men harpooned sea lions from bark canoes, women dived for shellfish, and everyone gathered berries, mushrooms and the meat of stranded whales. They went mostly naked beside fires, slept in domed huts and kept Fuegian dogs.

Ferdinand Magellan sighted their fires in 1520, but sustained contact came only in the nineteenth century. In 1830 Robert FitzRoy of HMS Beagle seized four Yahgan, including the youth Jemmy Button, carried them to England and presented them at court, then brought them home on the voyage of 1832 that carried Charles Darwin.
zh:
雅甘人又称亚马纳人，曾是地球上分布最南的居民，占据大火地岛以南、一直延伸到合恩角的岛礁与水道，分为五个操舟游动的群体。他们的雅甘语是孤立语言。

他们是游猎采集族群，生计几乎全靠海洋：男子乘树皮独木舟猎捕海狮，女子潜水捡拾贝类，全体成员还采集浆果、蘑菇并取食搁浅的鲸鱼。他们常在篝火旁近乎赤身露体，睡在狭小的圆顶棚屋里，并驯养火地犬。

1520年斐迪南·麦哲伦曾望见他们的篝火，但持续接触要到19世纪才出现。1830年贝格尔号船长罗伯特·菲茨罗伊带走四名雅甘人，其中包括少年杰米·巴顿，把他们带到英国并带入宫廷觐见，随后又在1832年搭载查尔斯·达尔文的那次航行中把他们送回故乡。

en:
The Yaka are a Bantu people of the forest and savanna between the Kwango and Wamba rivers in the southwestern Congo basin, close to the Angola border, and speak Kiyaka, an offshoot of Kikongo. The name Yaka was originally a Kongo title for warriors.

Yaka society was organized under paramount chiefs and matrilineal clans, and its craftsmen made upturned-nose masks, mbwoolo figurines and the mukoku slit drum used in ritual dances.

In the seventeenth century Lunda migrants moving west under a leader named Kabamba founded the Yaka kingdom, blending with local Kongo-speaking groups such as the Mbala and Tsamba. An older Yaka polity had been subdued by the expanding Lunda Empire in the 1730s, and the reorganized kingdom long resisted Portuguese penetration.
zh:
雅卡人是生活在刚果盆地西南部宽果河与万巴河之间森林和稀树草原地带的班图人，西临安哥拉边境，操基孔戈语的分支基亚卡语。“雅卡”本是刚果人对武士的称号。

雅卡社会在最高酋长和母系氏族体系下组织起来，工匠制作翘鼻大面具、姆沃洛人像和仪式舞蹈中使用的穆科科缝鼓。

17世纪，向西迁徙的隆达人在首领卡班巴率领下建立雅卡王国，与姆巴拉、昌巴等当地孔戈语族群融合。更早的雅卡政权在18世纪30年代被扩张中的隆达帝国征服，重组后的王国长期抵御葡萄牙势力的渗透。

en:
Mamachatpam is the self-name of the Lower Yakama, the largest of the five or six Sahaptin-speaking bands that outsiders gathered under the name Yakama. Their villages held the lower Yakima River east of the Cascade Range, and they were also called Pa'kiut'lĕma, people of the gap, after their main village in the Union Gap.

Their upriver cousins were the Kittitas or Upper Yakama, and the related Wanapum kept the Columbia about Priest Rapids, where they cut more than three hundred petroglyphs into the basalt cliffs. All spoke Ichishkíin, a Sahaptin language of the Plateau Penutian family, and lived on Columbia salmon, camas roots and game.

In 1805 the Wanapum chief Cutssahnem welcomed the Lewis and Clark Expedition with food and dancing. In 1805 or 1806 the corps met the Yakama bands themselves at the river confluences of their country.
zh:
马马查特帕姆是下雅卡马人的自称，而雅卡马本是外界对五六个萨哈普廷语支派的统称，下雅卡马是其中最大的一支。他们的村社占据喀斯喀特山脉以东的亚基马河下游；按其在联合隘口的主村，他们又被称为帕基乌特雷马人，意为“隘口之民”。

上游的近亲是基蒂塔斯人，又称上雅卡马人；同语的瓦纳普姆人则守着普里斯特急流一带的哥伦比亚河，在玄武岩崖壁上凿下了三百多幅岩画。他们都说伊奇什金语，即高原佩努蒂语系的萨哈普廷语的一支，以哥伦比亚河的鲑鱼、卡马夏百合球茎和猎物为生。

1805年，瓦纳普姆首领库察内姆以食物和歌舞迎接刘易斯与克拉克探险队。1805或1806年，探险队又在雅卡马人土地上的河流交汇处见到了雅卡马诸支派。

en: The Yalarrngan are the Yalarnnga, an Aboriginal Australian people of north-western Queensland, whose country lay around Dajarra and Cloncurry, inland from the Gulf of Carpentaria. They spoke a Pama-Nyungan language of the Kalkatungic branch, grouped by linguists with the neighbouring Kalkatungu, and early records also use variant names such as Jalanga and Yellunga.
zh: 雅拉恩加人是昆士兰西北部的澳大利亚原住民，领地位于卡奔塔利亚湾内陆的达贾拉与克朗克里一带。他们的语言属帕马—牛雅语系卡尔卡通语支，语言学家将其与邻近的卡尔卡通语划为一类；早年文献中该族也有贾兰加、耶隆加等异写。

en:
The Yamasee were a multiethnic confederation forged in the seventeenth century from survivors of Georgia chiefdoms shattered by disease and Westo slave raids. Spanish documents first called them the Yamasis in 1663, when they lived on the Georgia and South Carolina border. Their speech was close to Muskogean.

In the 1680s they settled by the Savannah River and Port Royal Sound and became South Carolina's foremost Indian ally, selling captives at Charles Town and forming the core of the militia that fought the Tuscarora War.

Abuses by traders, debts and colonial hunger for their rice lands drove them to revolt in 1715. Joined by others, they nearly destroyed the colony before the Cherokee switched sides and the war ended in 1717. The defeated Yamasee dispersed to Spanish Florida and the Creek towns and ceased to exist as an independent people.
zh:
亚马西人是17世纪形成的多族群联盟，成员来自佐治亚酋邦在疫病和韦斯托人奴隶劫掠中崩溃后的遗民。1663年西班牙文献首次称他们为亚马西人，当时他们住在佐治亚与南卡罗来纳边界。他们的语言与马斯科吉语相近。

17世纪80年代，他们在萨凡纳河与罗亚尔港湾一带定居，成为南卡罗来纳最重要的印第安盟友，把俘虏卖到查尔斯镇，并构成参加塔斯卡罗拉战争的民兵主力。

商人的欺压、债务以及殖民者对其稻田的觊觎，促使他们于1715年起兵。在许多部族响应下，他们险些摧毁这个殖民地，直到切罗基人倒戈，战争于1717年结束。战败的亚马西人四散，有的投奔西属佛罗里达，有的加入克里克城镇，作为独立族群的亚马西人就此消亡。

en:
The Yampara are an Andean people of the valleys of Chuquisaca in central Bolivia, who gave their name to the province of Yamparáez. They may have been resettled in the region as Inca mitimaes, and by the late fifteenth century they shared the fate of the neighboring Charca when the armies of the Inca Túpac Yupanqui reached their valleys.

In 1538 their cacique Kuysara built the alliance that brought Gonzalo Pizarro's Spaniards into the region, leading to the founding of the city that became Sucre. During the independence wars Yampara fighters joined the revolutionaries and helped defeat royalist troops at the battle of Jumbate in 1816.
zh:
扬帕拉人是玻利维亚中部丘基萨卡河谷的安第斯族群，扬帕拉埃斯县因他们得名。他们可能是被印加迁居到此的米蒂马埃斯殖民村社；到15世纪末，印加王图帕克·尤潘基的军队进入他们的河谷，扬帕拉人与邻近的查尔卡斯人同遭征服。

1538年，其首领奎萨拉促成联盟，把贡萨洛·皮萨罗的西班牙人引入此地，日后发展为苏克雷的城市由此兴建。独立战争期间，扬帕拉战士加入革命军，在1816年的洪巴特战役中协助击败保王派军队。

en:
Yān culture belongs to the old Yan lands around present-day Beijing, from Jizhou towns to the Bohai coast. Yan, northernmost of the Warring States, kept its capital Ji on Beijing's site; its people were frontier fighters, generals including Qin Kai fought the Donghu and Gojoseon, and Yan's wall and five commanderies guarded lands where knife money passed between farmers and nomads.

Tang Youzhou was where An Lushan rebelled in 755 and proclaimed a rebel Yan. Khitan Liao made the city of Ji southern capital Nanjing in 938, Jurchen Jin central capital Zhongdu in 1153; after Mongols razed Zhongdu in 1215, Kublai built nearby Dadu in 1264–1293 as Yuan capital. In 1337 Yan people were Yuan subjects, linked to the Yangzi delta by the Grand Canal.

The Ming took Dadu in 1368 and renamed it Beiping; the Yongle Emperor, once Prince of Yan, rebuilt it as Beijing and moved the capital there in 1420; the Qing kept it after 1644, banner garrisons by the old townspeople.
zh:
燕文化属于古燕地之民，即以今北京为中心、从蓟州军镇到渤海之滨的北部边疆。燕国是战国最北的诸侯国，都城蓟在今北京一带；燕民以边地战士著称，燕将秦开东征东胡和古朝鲜，燕国长城与五郡护卫着农耕汉人与草原游牧民之间以刀币交易的商路。

唐代这里是幽州，755年安禄山在此起兵叛乱，建立僭号燕国。938年契丹辽朝把蓟城定为南京，1153年女真金朝立为中都；1215年蒙古摧毁中都后，忽必烈1264—1293年在附近建大都为元朝都城。1337年燕人是元朝京畿臣民，凭大运河与长江三角洲相连。

1368年明军攻占大都，改名北平；曾为燕王的永乐帝重建为北京，1420年迁都于此，清朝1644年后继续以此为都，在旧城居民旁驻扎八旗。

en: The Yandan are the Yanda, an Aboriginal Australian people of western Queensland, whose country lay at the headwaters of the Hamilton River, north of Warenda and beside the Pitta Pitta lands. Their language is known only from a single word list, and linguists judge it to have been a Pama-Nyungan tongue close to the neighbouring Guwa.
zh: 阳达人是昆士兰西部的澳大利亚原住民，领地在沃伦达以北的汉密尔顿河源头，与皮塔皮塔人的土地相邻。他们的语言仅靠一份词汇表流传，语言学家判断它属帕马—牛雅语系，与邻近的古瓦语十分接近。

en:
The Yandin were a Yukaghir tribal group of the far northern Siberian tundra, living between the lower Lena and the Yana along the Omoloy River, where they spoke the Yan, or Detkil, variant of Yukaghir. Their name may derive from the Yukaghir word yande, a goose, or from a local prince called Uyanda.

By about 1650 Russian tribute books counted fifty tribute-paying Yandin men, perhaps two hundred people in all, under the label of the stone Yukaghirs. Epidemics, feuds with neighboring Even and Evenki bands and the burden of fur tribute thinned them during the colonial period. The Yandin eventually vanished from the records as a separate group, their descendants absorbed into surrounding peoples.
zh:
扬丁人是西伯利亚极北苔原的尤卡吉尔部落，活动在勒拿河下游与亚纳河之间的奥莫洛伊河一带，使用尤卡吉尔语的亚纳（杰特基尔）变体。他们的族名可能来自尤卡吉尔语“扬德”，意为鹅，也可能得名于当地酋长乌扬达。

到1650年前后，俄国贡赋册籍登记了50名纳税的扬丁男子，总人口约200人，册中称他们为“石地”尤卡吉尔人。殖民时代，疫病、与邻近埃文人和鄂温克人的冲突，加上毛皮贡赋的重压，使扬丁人不断衰减。他们最终作为独立群体从记载中消失，后裔融入周围各族。

en:
The Yandyr, also recorded as Yandygir, were a small Yukaghir clan group of the Yana and Omoloy country in the far northern Siberian tundra, closely bound to the Yandin and speaking the same Yan, or Detkil, variant of Yukaghir. Their shared name is traced to the Yukaghir word for a goose, or else to the local prince Uyanda.

Russian fur-tribute records of the mid-1600s list them among the stone Yukaghirs of the Lena-Yana tundra, a few hundred strong at most. Smallpox, feuds with Even and Evenki neighbors and the pressure of tribute broke the group up within a few generations, and its families were absorbed into the surrounding tundra peoples.
zh:
扬德尔人（文献中又作扬达吉尔）是西伯利亚极北苔原、亚纳河与奥莫洛伊河一带的尤卡吉尔小氏族群体，与扬丁人关系密切，使用同一种尤卡吉尔语亚纳（杰特基尔）变体。他们共同的族名可追溯到尤卡吉尔语里的“鹅”，也有人认为源自酋长乌扬达。

17世纪中叶的俄国毛皮贡赋册籍把他们归入勒拿河与亚纳河之间苔原的“石地”尤卡吉尔人，总人口至多几百。天花、与邻近埃文人和鄂温克人的仇杀，加上贡赋的重压，在几代人之间就瓦解了这个群体，其家户最终融入周围的苔原各族。

en:
The Yanesha, also called Amuesha, are an Arawak-speaking people of the central Peruvian rainforest, whose villages lie along the Palcazu, Pichis and Pachitea rivers. Yanesha is their own name for themselves; they lived by hunting, fishing and subsistence agriculture, and their language belongs to the Maipurean, or Arawak, family.

Mercedarian friars first entered their country in the later sixteenth century, but stable contact came only in the early eighteenth century, when the Franciscan Francisco de San José founded reducciones at Cerro de la Sal and Quimiri. The indigenous rebellion led by Juan Santos Atahualpa in 1742 destroyed these missions and kept the region closed to outsiders for several decades.
zh:
亚内沙人又称阿梅沙人，是秘鲁中部雨林的阿拉瓦克语族群，村落沿帕尔卡苏河、皮奇斯河和帕奇特亚河分布。亚内沙是他们的自称，传统上以狩猎、渔捞和自给农业为生，其语言属迈普雷（阿拉瓦克）语系。

16世纪下半叶，仁慈会修士最早进入他们的地界，但稳定的接触要到18世纪初：方济各会的弗朗西斯科·德·圣何塞在盐山和基米里建起归化村。1742年，胡安·桑托斯·阿塔瓦尔帕领导的印第安人起义摧毁了这些传教站，使该地区向外界封闭了数十年。

en: The Yanga, also spelt Jangaa or Janga, were an Aboriginal Australian people of Queensland whose lands lay around the headwaters of the Copperfield River. They spoke the Yanga language, mutually intelligible with neighbouring Mbara, and were also known as the Purkaburra; they may have been the same people as the Yukulta and Ganggalida of the Gulf country.
zh: 阳加人又拼写为詹加或詹加尔，是昆士兰的澳大利亚原住民，土地位于科珀菲尔德河源头一带。他们使用的阳加语与邻族姆巴拉语可以互通，别名普尔卡布拉；他们可能与海湾地区的尤库尔塔人和冈加利达人是同一群人。

en: The Yangga, also spelt Jangga, were an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, distinct from the similarly named Yanga people of the Gulf country. Their language was recorded by Norman Tindale as Jangga and counted among the dialects of Biri, and settlers also knew them as the Durroburra.
zh: 阳甘人又拼写为詹加，是昆士兰中部的澳大利亚原住民，与名字相近、住在海湾地区的阳加人并非同一群体。诺曼·廷代尔把他们的语言记为詹加语，归入比里语的方言之一；定居者还称他们为杜罗布拉人。

en:
The Yángjiāng are the Yue people of the Moyang River basin on the Guangdong coast, around Yangjiang and Yangchun, whose speech belongs to the Gao-Yang branch of Yue. It is not intelligible with Guangzhou speech and keeps a lateral fricative shared with Zhuang and Li.

That sound and place names beginning with na, dong and ma record the language of the ancient Li who lived here when Central Plains refugees arrived during the late Han and Three Kingdoms troubles; the settlers led local sinicization while their speech absorbed Li elements.

The land became the seat of Gaozhou in 527 and gained its name with Yangjiang county in 598. In 1048 its prefecture was renamed Nan'en, the name it bore around 1337, until the Ming merged it into Zhaoqing in 1368. The coastal county became known for knives, lacquerware and fermented black beans.
zh:
阳江人是广东沿海漠阳江流域的粤语人群，聚居在阳江、阳春一带，阳江话属粤语高阳片。它与广州话无法互通，还保留了与壮语、黎语共有的边擦音声母。

这个声母连同那、洞、麻字头的地名，都是汉末三国战乱中中原移民初到时，当地俚人留下的语言痕迹；移民主导了当地汉化，自己的话也吸收了俚语成分。

这里527年成为高州治所，598年新设阳江县，阳江之名由此而始。1048年所在的恩州改称南恩州，1337年前后这片地区仍以南恩为名，直到1368年明朝将其并入肇庆府。这座州县还以小刀、漆器和豆豉闻名。

en:
The Yangman were an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory whose country was centred on the lands around the later town of Larrimah, south-east of Katherine, and reached towards Mataranka and the Elsey country; they had occupied the area for over 40,000 years. They held that the Dreaming tracks of the Storm Bird, the channel-billed cuckoo, shaped the local landscape, and the name Larrimah means meeting place in their tongue.

Their language, together with Wardaman and Dagoman, makes up the Yangmanic group of non-Pama-Nyungan languages, once classified within Gunwinyguan but now treated as a family apart.
zh:
阳曼人是北领地的澳大利亚原住民，领地以凯瑟琳东南、后来的拉里马镇所在一带为中心，延伸至马塔兰卡和埃尔西地区；他们在这片土地上已生活四万多年。阳曼人认为风暴鸟（沟嘴鹃）的梦创足迹塑造了当地地貌，“拉里马”在他们的语言中意为集会之地。

阳曼语与瓦达曼语、达戈曼语共同构成非帕马-牛雅语的阳曼语组，该语组曾被划入贡温古语，后来被视为独立语族。

en:
The Yanyuwa are a saltwater Aboriginal people of the southern Gulf of Carpentaria in the Northern Territory, holding the coast around and opposite the Sir Edward Pellew Group of Islands near the mouth of the McArthur River.

Their tongue is a Pama-Nyungan language of the Ngarna group, unusual in maintaining distinct men's and women's dialects; boys grew up speaking the women's form and switched to men's speech at initiation.

From the 1720s Makassan trepangers from Sulawesi visited their shores, arriving with the December north-westerlies and leaving on the April south-easterlies. Trade relations were close enough that Yanyuwa men sometimes sailed back with the prau fleets and stayed for months at Makassar; many Gulf peoples used Makassan as a trade lingua franca and its words entered their languages.
zh:
雅纽瓦人是澳大利亚北领地卡奔塔利亚湾南岸的“海水民族”，领有麦克阿瑟河口附近爱德华·佩柳爵士群岛及其对岸的海岸。

雅纽瓦语属帕马—牛雅语系纳尔纳语支，独特之处在于保留着男女有别的两种方言；男孩自幼说女性方言，到成年礼时才改说男性方言。

从18世纪20年代起，苏拉威西的望加锡海参商人到访他们的海岸，乘着12月的西北风而来，顺着4月的东南风而归。双方贸易关系密切，雅纽瓦男子有时随帆船船队回访，在望加锡一住数月；湾岸许多族群把望加锡语作为贸易通用语，望加锡词汇也进入了他们的语言。

en:
The Yao, largest branch Iu Mien, are southern China highlanders speaking Mienic languages of the Hmong–Mien family. Their traditions trace them to Dongting Lake and Changsha in Hunan, venerating Panhu, legendary dog-ancestor, as their clans' forefather. Between 200 BCE and 900 CE they drifted south of the Yangtze into Hunan, Guangxi and Guangdong hills, clearing slopes by slash-and-burn farming; under the Tang they appear as the Mo Yao, highlanders excused from forced labor.

From the tenth to thirteenth centuries imperial rule reached them through the loose jimi and tusi systems, tribute paid through hereditary headmen. In 1337 Yao communities were thickest around Guangxi's Guilin hills and northern Guangdong's Lianzhou.

Ming and Qing tightened control, replacing headmen with tax officials, and the Yao rose with the Miao in 1370s and 1449 rebellions; each defeat pushing communities deeper into the mountains or south, by about 1700 first Mien migrants had crossed into northern Laos, others settling in Vietnam and Thailand.
zh:
瑶族是中国南方的山地民族，最大的支系自称优勉，语言属苗瑶语系的勉语支。其传说把祖源追溯到湖南洞庭湖、长沙一带，奉传说中的盘瓠为各姓始祖。公元前200年至公元900年间，瑶人逐渐南迁长江以南，进入湖南、广西、广东山岭，刀耕火种；唐代文献称他们为莫徭，是免服徭役的山民。

10至13世纪，王朝通过松散的羁縻、土司制度统辖瑶族，由世袭头人纳贡。1337年，瑶人聚落最密处是广西桂林山地和粤北连州一带。

明清强化控制，以流官取代头人征税，瑶人在14世纪70年代和1449年与苗人联合起事；历次失败把瑶人逼进更深的大山或更南之处，到约1700年第一批勉人已进入老挝北部，另有一些定居越南、泰国。

en:
The Yao are a Bantu people whose traditional homeland lies between the Rovuma and Lugenda rivers, in the Niassa highlands of northern Mozambique, with later settlements around the southern end of Lake Malawi. They speak Chiyao, a Bantu language of the Rufiji-Ruvuma group.

Farmers and fishermen, they turned to long-distance trade as Arab and Swahili merchants developed the southeastern coast, carrying ivory, grain and slaves to the coast in exchange for cloth, beads and firearms. Their caravans and chiefly seats made them a power in the hinterland of Kilwa and Mikindani, and around the 1830s groups began moving east of Lake Malawi. Through coastal contacts Islam gradually reached them, mingling with older local beliefs.
zh:
亚奥人是班图人的一支，传统家园在鲁伍马河与卢任达河之间，即莫桑比克北部的尼亚萨高地，后来也有支系在马拉维湖南端一带定居。他们操齐亚奥语，属班图语系的鲁菲吉—鲁武马语支。

他们务农并兼事渔捞，随着阿拉伯和斯瓦希里商人开发东南非海岸，亚奥人转而经营长途贸易，把象牙、粮食和奴隶运往海边，换回布匹、珠饰和火器。商队和酋长领地使他们成为基尔瓦、米金达尼腹地的一股势力；到19世纪30年代，成批亚奥人开始迁入马拉维湖以东地区。通过与沿海的往来，伊斯兰教逐渐传入，与当地旧有信仰交融。

en:
The Yapese are the people of the Yap Main Islands in the western Caroline Islands. They speak Yapese, an Oceanic language that forms its own branch apart from the other Micronesian languages. Settled roughly two thousand years ago by voyagers from Melanesia, Yap developed a stratified society, with at least seven ranked castes and villages whose rank rose or fell through warfare and tribute.

Yapese sailors navigated by stars and swells without a compass, and the island built a dominion over surrounding atolls. Its stone money consisted of giant calcite disks quarried chiefly in Palau and rafted home at great risk, whose worth lay in their size and the story of their transport.

Álvaro de Saavedra sighted Yap in 1528, and Ruy López de Villalobos charted it in 1543. Spain never ruled Yap; in 1837 its villages governed themselves.
zh:
雅浦人是西加罗林群岛雅浦主岛的居民。他们使用的雅浦语属大洋洲语，却独立于其他密克罗尼西亚语言之外、自成一支。约两千年前，来自美拉尼西亚的航海者定居于此，发展出等级森严的社会：至少七层种姓式等级，村落的名次随战争胜负和纳贡关系升降。

雅浦水手不靠罗盘，仅凭星象和涌浪远航，并建立了对周边环礁的宗主权。雅浦石币是巨大的方解石圆盘，主要产自帕劳，人们冒极大风险用木筏运回家，价值取决于石盘大小和运输经历。

1528年阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉望见雅浦，1543年鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·比利亚洛沃斯将其绘入海图。西班牙从未实际统治雅浦，1837年时这些等级分明的村落仍自行治理。

en:
The Yapahruka, whose name means Root Eaters and was later recorded by the Spanish as the Yamparika, were a Shoshone-speaking people of the Wyoming mountains and the northernmost division that became the Comanche. In the fourteenth century they were foot-borne hunter-gatherers; by 1500 some had crossed the Rocky Mountains to hunt bison on the Great Plains.

After the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 made Spanish horses available, they took to mounted life and drifted south. By the 1750s they generally lived north of the Arkansas River. Around 1790 pressure from the Cheyenne and Arapaho pushed some bands into the North Canadian River valley, where their later chief Ten Bears grew up.

In 1820 Ten Bears was a key figure in making peace between the Comanche and the Ute. Through the 1830s Cheyenne and Arapaho pressure broke their ties with the Shoshone of Wyoming, leaving them a southern-plains people.
zh:
亚帕赫鲁卡人名字意为食根者，后来被西班牙人记作扬帕里卡人。他们原是怀俄明山区讲肖肖尼语的族群，也是后来科曼奇人各分支中位置最北的一支。14世纪时他们仍是徒步的狩猎采集者；到1500年，已有群体越过落基山脉到大平原猎捕野牛。

1680年普韦布洛起义后西班牙马群流入，他们转为骑马生活，逐渐南下。1750年代他们多住在阿肯色河以北。约1790年，在夏延人和阿拉帕霍人的压力下，部分营地迁到北加拿大河谷，后来的首领十熊就在这里长大。

1820年，十熊在科曼奇人与犹他人的议和中扮演了关键角色。到1830年代，夏延人和阿拉帕霍人持续南压，切断了亚帕赫鲁卡人与怀俄明肖肖尼人的旧有联系，使他们成为南部平原族群。

en: Yapen denotes the peoples of Yapen, a large mountainous island in Cenderawasih Bay off northern New Guinea, among them the Serui and Ansus communities of the coast; the island is unusually mixed in language, home both to Austronesian Yapen languages and to the Papuan Yawa tongues of its central districts. The Spanish navigator Álvaro de Saavedra made the first recorded European landing there in 1528 while sailing back from Tidore.
zh: 亚彭指亚彭岛上的诸族群，该岛是新几内亚岛北岸极乐鸟湾中的多山大岛，沿海居民包括塞鲁伊人、安苏斯人等社群；岛上语言格局格外混杂，既通行南岛语系的亚彭诸语言，中部地区又使用巴布亚语系的亚瓦诸语言。1528年，西班牙航海家阿尔瓦罗·德·萨韦德拉从蒂多雷返航途中首次有记载地登上该岛。

en: The Yaqay, also spelled Yakhai or Jaqai and known to neighbouring peoples as the Yaghai, are a Papuan people of the south coast of Mappi Regency in South Papua, Indonesia, settled along the Obaa River. Their Yaqay language, with Oba-Miwamon among its dialects, forms the Yaqay branch of the Marind-Yaqai family within the Anim languages of Trans-New Guinea.
zh: 雅凯人又拼作亚凯或贾凯，邻族称其为雅盖人，是印度尼西亚南巴布亚省马皮摄政区南海岸的巴布亚族群，沿奥巴河而居。他们的雅凯语（含奥巴-米瓦蒙等方言）构成跨新几内亚语系阿尼姆语族马林德-雅凯语系中的雅凯分支。

en:
The Yaqui, who call themselves Yoeme, are the agricultural people of the lower Yaqui River valley in Sonora. In 1533 Diego de Guzman's expedition met warriors whose old chief drew a line in the dirt and ordered them not to cross. Forty years of fighting followed.

In 1608 the Yaqui and Mayo allies beat the Spanish, and after the peace of 1610 they invited Jesuits in 1617. The missions kept settlers at arm's length: the Yaqui accepted Christianity while keeping their lands and unity. Encroachment by miners sparked the Yaqui and Mayo revolt of 1740, and the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 handed the missions to Franciscans the Yaqui never trusted.

After Mexican independence the leader Juan Banderas tried to unite the Yaqui, Mayo, Opata and Pima in an autonomous state, rising in 1825 until his capture and execution in 1833.
zh:
亚基人自称约梅人，是索诺拉亚基河下游的农耕民族。1533年，迭戈·德·古斯曼的远征队遇到一队战士，年迈的首领在地上划了一条线，命令对方不得越过。此后四十年战事不断。

1608年，亚基人与马约盟友击败西班牙人；1610年议和后，他们于1617年主动请来耶稣会士。传教站把移民挡在远处：亚基人接受基督教，同时保住了土地与族群团结。矿主的侵入引发1740年亚基—马约起义；1767年耶稣会被驱逐，传教站转给亚基人始终不信任的方济各会。

墨西哥独立后，首领胡安·班德拉斯试图联合亚基、马约、奥帕塔和皮马诸族建立自治政权，于1825年起兵，最终被俘，1833年被处决。

en: The Yareba are a Papuan people of the Musa River country in the Bird's Tail of New Guinea. Their speech, also called Middle Musa, belongs to the small Yareban or Musa River family of Trans–New Guinea languages, whose members also include Moikodi and Aneme Wake.
zh: 亚雷巴人是新几内亚“鸟尾”穆萨河流域的巴布亚族群。他们的语言又称中穆萨语，属跨新几内亚语系下小小的亚雷班语族（又称穆萨河语族），同语族还包括莫伊科迪语和阿内姆韦克语。

en:
The Yariguí were a Cariban-speaking people of the middle Magdalena valley in western Santander, Colombia. Nomadic hunters and gatherers, they were split into independent clans, each led by a cacique.

At the Spanish arrival in 1536 the Yariguí may have numbered some 50,000, and met the invaders with poisoned darts and ambushes. By 1570 four chiefs led attacks on boats carrying settlers and goods along the rivers.

The most celebrated leader was Pipatón, captured by the Spaniards in 1601 and maimed by having his heels cut, who escaped to fight on before surrendering late in life and dying in a Bogotá convent after 1612; his wife Yarima also led resistance. Colonial settlement and imported diseases cut the population sharply during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, though the clans kept their forest independence long after the surrounding lands had been pacified.
zh:
亚里吉人是说加勒比语的族群，生活在哥伦比亚桑坦德省西部马格达莱纳河中游。他们游猎采集，分成若干互不统属的氏族，各由一名酋长统领。

1536年西班牙人初到时，亚里吉人可能约有五万人，随即以毒镖和伏击迎战入侵者。到1570年，四位酋长率众袭击河上运送移民与货物的船只。

最著名的首领是皮帕通：他于1601年被俘并被挑断脚跟，却逃脱后继续领导抵抗，晚年才投降，1612年之后死于波哥大的一座修道院；他的妻子亚里马也曾率众抗敌。由于殖民点不断扩张，加上传入的疫病，亚里吉人口在17、18世纪急剧减少，但周围地区被平定之后很久，这些氏族仍保持着林中的独立。

en:
The Yaro, also remembered as the Yarowilcas, were a pre-Inca people of the high Andes of central Peru, formed from communities that broke away when the Wari Empire collapsed around the eleventh century. Their nation dominated the Bombon plateau around Lake Chinchaycocha, and Yaro remains have been dated to as early as the ninth century.

Around 1200 they built the citadel of Gonicutac, a three-storey complex of stone and mud with residential, agricultural and religious quarters. From the thirteenth century their territory reached north into the Huallanca district and the lands later called Yarowilca, near Huanuco. The Yaro entered the Inca Empire as a confederated nation, keeping their own lords under Cuzco's overlordship.
zh:
亚罗人又称亚罗维尔卡人，是秘鲁中部安第斯高原的前印加居民，源自11世纪前后瓦里帝国崩溃时脱离出去的村社。他们的邦国统治着钦查伊科查湖畔的邦邦高原，亚罗人的遗存最早可追溯到9世纪。

约1200年，他们修建了戈尼库塔克堡垒城寨，这是一座石泥砌筑的三层建筑群，兼有居住、农事和祭祀功能。13世纪起，其领土向北扩展到瓦良卡地区以及瓦努科附近后来被称为亚罗维尔卡的地方。亚罗人以结盟邦国的身份加入印加帝国，在库斯科的宗主权下保留了自己的首领。

en:
The Yaros were an Indigenous people of the lower Uruguay River. When the Spanish arrived they held the western bank, until the Charrúa pushed them south between the Negro and San Salvador rivers.

They lived without agriculture, pottery or the bow: they fished, hunted and gathered honey, pine nuts and carob pods, brewing a drink from pine seeds. Their only shelters were woven windbreaks.

The Yaros fought alongside the Charrúa against the Spaniards. Chronicles as early as 1612 record them, under the name Chayos, killing Captain Juan Ramón, an explorer sent up the Uruguay by Sebastián Cabot. Jesuits tried to settle them at the Yapeyú reduction from 1627 and founded San Andrés de Yaros in 1657, but its people walked away within a year, preferring nomadic life. Between the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries the Yaros were broken and absorbed by the Charrúa.
zh:
亚鲁斯人是乌拉圭河下游的原住民。西班牙人到来时，他们占据西岸，后来被查鲁亚人向南挤到内格罗河与圣萨尔瓦多河之间。

他们不事农耕，也没有陶器和弓箭，以捕鱼、狩猎和采集蜂蜜、松子、角豆荚为生，还用松籽酿酒。他们唯一的栖身设施是编织的防风障。

亚鲁斯人曾与查鲁亚人并肩对抗西班牙人。早在1612年的编年史就记载，他们被称作查约人，杀死了塞瓦斯蒂安·卡伯特派往乌拉圭河探险的胡安·拉蒙船长。耶稣会从1627年起试图把他们安置在亚佩尤传教区，又于1657年建立圣安德烈斯-德亚罗斯，但居民不出一年便离去，宁愿继续游牧生活。17世纪末至18世纪初，亚鲁斯人被查鲁亚人击溃并吸收。

en:
The Yat Tindé are the Plains Apache, also called the Kiowa Apache, a small Southern Athabaskan people of the Great Plains whose names for themselves include Ná'ishą and γát dìndé, the cedar people. Their oral tradition says they split from the Tsuut'ina, another Athabaskan group of the Canadian prairies, and they had taken to plains life by the sixteenth century, moving south until the Lakota allowed them land south of the Black Hills.

In the early eighteenth century they lived near the upper Missouri in a permanent alliance with the Kiowa, whose language was entirely unlike their own, so the two peoples conversed in Plains Indian Sign Language.

Their population was estimated at only about four hundred in 1780. Around 1800 they followed the Kiowa south onto the Southern Plains, hunting bison along the eastern face of the Rocky Mountains.
zh:
亚特廷德人即平原阿帕奇人，又称基奥瓦阿帕奇人，是大平原上一支人数不多的南阿萨巴斯卡族群；他们的自称还有Ná'ishą和γát dìndé，后者意为“雪松之人”。据其口传历史，他们从加拿大草原上另一支阿萨巴斯卡群体楚蒂纳人中分离出来，16世纪时已适应平原生活，随后南移，直到拉科塔人允许他们在黑山以南居住。

18世纪初，他们生活在密苏里河上游附近，与语言完全不同的基奥瓦人结成永久同盟，双方靠平原印第安手语交谈。

1780年总人口估计仅有约四百人。1800年前后，他们随基奥瓦人南迁进入南部平原，沿落基山脉东麓猎捕野牛。

en: The Yaur, also recorded as Jaur, are an Austronesian-speaking people of the eastern shore of Cenderawasih Bay, in the country that is now Nabire Regency of Central Papua. Their language belongs to the Cenderawasih Bay branch of Austronesian and, together with Iresim, descends from the reconstructed Proto-Yaur-Yerisiam, while Umar is a more distant relative within the same branch.
zh: 尧尔人（又记作扎乌尔人）是极乐鸟湾东岸的南岛语族族群，地在今中巴布亚省纳比雷县一带。其语言属南岛语系极乐鸟湾语支，与伊雷辛语同由拟构的原始尧尔-耶雷辛语分化，与同语支的乌马尔语关系则更远。

en:
The Yavapai are the Upland Yuman people of west-central Arizona. Archaeologists trace them to Patayan groups who moved east from the Colorado River and emerged as a distinct people around 1300; their name, given by the Mojave, means people of the sun.

They lived in four roaming bands, gathering wild foods and raiding in shifting alliances, often with the Western Apache against the Akimel O'odham and Maricopa. Hopi guides led the Spanish explorer Antonio de Espejo to their copper-bearing mountains in 1583, and Juan de Onate crossed their lands in 1598 and 1604.

Smallpox carried off perhaps a quarter of them in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and the Franciscan Francisco Garces lived among them in 1776, by which time horses, metal tools and cattle raiding had reshaped their old way of life.
zh:
亚瓦派人是亚利桑那中西部的高地尤曼语族群。考古学家认为他们源自从科罗拉多河向东迁徙的帕塔扬人，约1300年发展为独立民族；亚瓦派这个名字由莫哈维人所起，意为太阳之人。

他们分为四个游荡游群，以采集野生食物为生，并在变幻的结盟中外出袭掠，常与西阿帕奇人联手对付阿基梅尔·奥奥德姆人和马里科帕人。1583年，霍皮向导带领西班牙探险家安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍来到他们产铜的山地；胡安·德·奥尼亚特于1598年及1604年两度穿过其土地。

17—18世纪，天花可能夺去四分之一人口，方济各会士弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯于1776年在他们中间生活，那时马匹、金属工具和盗牛活动已重塑了他们的旧日生活。

en:
The Yawyu were the highland people of the upper Cañete valley, southeast of Lima, whose early culture fused Kauki and Aymara roots and whose language belonged to the Aymaran family. They formed a confederation led by four towns known as Hatun Yauyos, with their paramount lord at Ñaupahuasi.

Around 1450 the prince Túpac Yupanqui, son of the Inca Pachacuti, brought them into the Inca Empire through an alliance. Yawyu auxiliaries afterward marched with the Incas against the Chimú and Huarco, while Yawyu mitimaes were resettled among the Huanca.

When Francisco Pizarro asked for their submission in 1534 they refused, so Hernando de Soto and Diego de Agüero routed their army with cavalry. The Yawyu later joined Manco Inca's siege of Lima before being broken into Spanish repartimientos and, from 1571, gathered into reductions such as Santo Domingo de Yauyos.
zh:
亚维尤人是利马东南山区、卡涅特河上游谷地的高原族群，其早期文化由考基与艾马拉两种传统融合而成，语言属于艾马拉语族。他们组成部落联盟，由合称大亚维尤的四座城镇为首，最高首领驻于尼亚瓦帕瓦西。

约1450年，印加王帕查库特克之子图帕克·尤潘基以结盟方式将他们并入印加帝国。此后亚维尤援军随印加人出征奇穆和瓦尔科，部分亚维尤移民也被安置到万卡人的土地上。

1534年皮萨罗要求他们归顺遭到拒绝，埃尔南多·德·索托和迭戈·德·阿圭罗遂率骑兵击溃其军队。亚维尤人后来又参加了曼科·印加围攻利马的大战，最终被划入西班牙人的委托监护区，并从1571年起被集中迁入圣多明各-德亚维尤等归化镇。

en:
The Yazoo were a small tribe of the lower Yazoo River in the Mississippi Delta, kinsmen and neighbours of the Tunica, Koroa and Tiou. Their lost language is thought to have belonged with Tunica, a language isolate.

French missionaries reached them at the end of the seventeenth century, but they leaned toward English traders, and in 1702 helped the Koroa kill the priest Nicholas Foucault and his companions. A French fort and a Jesuit mission under Jean Rouel followed in 1718 and 1722.

In 1729 the Yazoo and Koroa joined the Natchez revolt, killing Rouel and overwhelming the French garrison after the Natchez destroyed Fort Rosalie. The French and their Choctaw allies crushed the rising: survivors were sold into slavery on Caribbean plantations or captured and traded away by the Chickasaw, and the tribe disappeared as a separate people, its remnants merging with the Chickasaw and others.
zh:
亚祖人是密西西比三角洲亚祖河下游的小部落，与图尼卡人、科罗阿人和提乌人同族相邻。他们失传的语言被认为与孤立语言图尼卡语同属一类。

法国传教士在17世纪末来到他们中间，但亚祖人倾向于英国商人，并于1702年协助科罗阿人杀死神父尼古拉斯·富科及其同伴。法国随后在1718年和1722年分别建起堡垒和让·鲁埃尔主持的耶稣会传教站。

1729年，亚祖人与科罗阿人加入纳奇兹起义：纳奇兹人摧毁罗莎莉堡后，他们杀死鲁埃尔并歼灭了法国驻军。法国人与乔克托盟友镇压了起义，幸存者被卖到加勒比种植园为奴，或被奇克索人掳走转卖，这个部落就此不复为独立族群，残余者融入奇克索人等民族之中。

en:
The Ychsma, more often called Ichma, were the people of the kingdom of Pachacamac on the central Peruvian coast. Their polity arose around 1100 from the ruins of the Wari Empire, covering the Lurin and Rimac valleys south and east of Lima. Their name, recorded as ychma in the earliest Quechua dictionaries, meant the vermilion colour made from cinnabar.

In a desert land they extended the irrigation canals first built by the Lima culture, watering orchards and fields. At Pachacamac they raised at least sixteen truncated adobe pyramids with great access ramps, and other walled sanctuaries studded the Lima plain.

Around 1470 the armies of Tupac Yupanqui, acting for his father Pachacutec, annexed the kingdom. Local lords kept their rank after swearing obedience, and the Incas enlarged Pachacamac with a temple of the Sun and a house of chosen women.
zh:
伊奇斯马人常称伊奇马人，是秘鲁中部沿海帕查卡马克王国的居民。他们的政权约在1100年瓦里帝国崩溃后的废墟上兴起，领有利马城东南的卢林河谷与里马克河谷。他们的名字在最早的克丘亚词典中写作ychma，意为用朱砂制成的朱红色。

在这片荒漠土地上，他们扩建了利马文化最早开凿的灌溉渠网，滋养果园和田地。他们在帕查卡马克修建了至少十六座带巨大坡道的截顶土坯金字塔，利马平原上还有其他围墙圣所。

约1470年，图帕克·尤潘基奉其父帕查库特克之命率军吞并了这个王国。地方首领宣誓效忠后保留了地位，印加人还在帕查卡马克增建太阳神庙和选女之宫。

en: The Yei are a Marind sub-tribe of the lowlands along the upper Maro River near the Papua New Guinea border, in South Papua. Originating in the Fly River country, they speak a Yam, or Morehead–Maro, language closer to Papua New Guinean tongues than to Marind, and live by fishing, hunting and sago gathering in Upper and Lower Yei villages.
zh: 耶伊人是马林德人的一支，住在南巴布亚省马罗河上游、邻近巴布亚新几内亚边界的低地。他们发源于东部的弗莱河流域，所说的耶伊语属亚姆语系，又称莫尔黑德-马罗语系，与巴布亚新几内亚诸语言的关系比马林德语更近；他们分上耶伊、下耶伊两组村落，以渔捞、狩猎和采集西谷椰为生。

en:
The Yela are the people of Rossel Island, a mountainous island ringed by coral reefs at the eastern end of the Louisiade Archipelago off New Guinea. Linguists treat their language, Yélî Dnye, as an unclassified language isolate, with a large inventory of doubly articulated consonants and a special women's speech in which words connected with the sea are avoided.

The islanders occupied small villages along the coast and fertile valleys, keeping largely to themselves behind the dangerous reefs. Europeans first sighted the island in 1606, when the Spanish expedition of Luís Vaez de Torres charted it together with Tagula as the Land of Saint Bonaventure; the French d'Entrecasteaux expedition named it after the officer Élisabeth-Paul-Édouard de Rossel in the 1790s.
zh:
耶拉人是罗塞尔岛的居民，该岛多山，四周环绕珊瑚礁，位于新几内亚外海路易西亚德群岛最东端。语言学家将耶利多涅语视为系属未定的孤立语言，该语言有大量双重调音辅音，女性用语还避讳与海有关的词语。

岛民在沿海和肥沃谷地的小村落中生活，凭借危险的礁障与外界保持相当距离。1606年，路易斯·巴埃斯·德·托雷斯率领的西班牙探险队首次见到此岛，把它与塔古拉岛一并绘入地图，称作圣波拿文都拉之地；18世纪90年代，法国当特尔卡斯托探险队以军官伊丽莎白-保罗-爱德华·德·罗塞尔之名为岛命名。

en: The Yelmek are a Papuan people of the lowlands west of Merauke in South Papua, settled in villages between the Digul and Mbian rivers, among them Wanam and Bibikem. Their language, also called Jelmek or Yabega, belongs with nearby Maklew to the proposed Trans-Fly–Bulaka River family, and its Wanam variety may be a distinct language.
zh: 耶尔梅克人是南巴布亚马老奇以西低地的巴布亚族群，聚居于迪古尔河与姆比安河之间的瓦南、比比肯等村落。他们的语言又称耶尔米克或雅贝加，与邻近的马莱乌语同属拟议中的跨弗莱-布拉卡河语系，其中瓦南方言可能本身就是一门独立语言。

en:
Yemenis are the Arab people of south-western Arabia, around Sanaa, Taiz and the ports Mocha and Aden. They speak Yemeni Arabic; Mehri and Soqotri survive in the far east and on Socotra, society built around tribes, northern highlands following Zaydi Islam, lowlands the Sunni Shafi'i school. Land of Sabaean and Himyarite kingdoms, Yemen accepted Islam in the seventh century, the Zaidi imamate founded at Saada in 897.

Rasulid sultans ruled from Zabid and Taiz in 1229–1454, growing rich on Red Sea trade. In 1337 Sultan al-Mujahid Ali held the lowlands, the Zaydis keeping the northern mountains after retaking Sanaa in 1324. Tahirids followed in 1454 until the Mamluk conquest of 1517 and then the Ottomans; Ottoman armies took Aden in 1538 and made Zabid seat of Yemen Eyalet.

Qasimid imams expelled the Ottomans by 1636, Mocha becoming coffee emporium of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries with English, Dutch, French factories. In the later eighteenth century the imamate fragmented into principalities such as Lahej, Mocha's coffee trade drifting to newer ports.
zh:
也门人是阿拉伯半岛西南部阿拉伯人，聚居高原城市萨那、塔伊兹及摩卡、亚丁等港。讲也门阿拉伯语，马赫里语、索科特拉语仍在东部边陲和索科特拉岛通行；社会围绕部落，北高原奉栽德派，低地奉沙斐仪派。也门为赛伯伊、希木叶尔故土，7世纪归信伊斯兰，897年栽德派伊玛目政权建于萨达。

1229—1454年拉苏勒苏丹都扎比德、塔伊兹，靠红海贸易致富。1337年穆贾希德·阿里控低地，栽德派保北山，1324年夺回萨那。1454年塔希尔王朝代之，1517年后历经马穆鲁克和奥斯曼征服；奥斯曼军1538年取亚丁，扎比德为也门省治所。

卡西姆伊玛目到1636年逐走奥斯曼人，摩卡成17、18世纪咖啡港，港内挤满英荷法商馆。18世纪后期伊玛目政权分裂为拉赫季等小邦，摩卡咖啡贸易转往新港。

en:
Yerle Qalıq, meaning older inhabitants, is the self-name of the indigenous Siberian Tatars, distinguishing them from later Volga Tatar settlers. This Turkic population between the Urals and the Yenisei formed from hunters Turkified by Kipchaks from the eleventh century, later absorbing Tatar clans.

From 1242 the country belonged to the Golden Horde; on its breakup the Taibugid khans founded the Khanate of Sibir, ruling from Chimgi-Tura and then Qashliq. Kuchum seized the throne in 1563 and tried to enforce Islam; his raids drew the Cossack Yermak into Siberia. Kuchum was beaten at Chuvash Cape in 1582 and routed on the Ob in 1598, opening the Russian conquest of Siberia.

The Yerle Qalıq became the tsar's yasak-paying subjects, living by hunting and horse breeding. Sunni Islam, adopted from the fourteenth century and general by the late eighteenth, sat alongside shamanic customs.
zh:
“叶尔喀勒”意为老住户，是土著西伯利亚鞑靼人的自称，用以区别后来迁入的伏尔加鞑靼移民。乌拉尔山与叶尼塞河之间的猎人从11世纪起被钦察人突厥化，后吸收鞑靼氏族，形成这一突厥语族群。

1242年起该地归属金帐汗国；汗国瓦解后，泰布吉德系汗王建立失必儿汗国，先后定都奇姆吉-图拉和卡什雷克。1563年库楚姆夺位并强推伊斯兰教，他的袭击招致哥萨克叶尔马克进军西伯利亚。1582年库楚姆在楚瓦什角战败，1598年在鄂毕河畔被击溃，俄国征服西伯利亚的序幕由此拉开。

叶尔喀勒人成为向沙皇缴纳亚萨克税的属民，以狩猎和养马为生。他们从14世纪起皈依、18世纪末普遍信奉逊尼派伊斯兰教，仍保留萨满习俗。

en:
The Yi, self-named Nuosu, with branches called Nisu, are Tibeto-Burman highlanders of Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou and Guangxi, speaking Loloish languages close to Burmese and keeping their own syllabic script. Their Wuman ancestors of eastern Yunnan supplied Nanzhao's warrior caste in 738–902, then lived under Bai-ruled Dali until the thirteenth-century Mongol conquest.

Under the Yuan the Yi were governed through chieftainships, while Yi clans had already established their own states; Guizhou's Mu'ege lasted to 1279 and survived as Shuixi chiefdom to 1698. In 1337 southern Sichuan Yi held the Jianchang and Huili valleys in what is now Liangshan, Black Yi aristocrats ruling commoners and captives in a rigid caste order that kept imperial officials at bay for centuries.

Ming reforms replaced hereditary chieftains with appointed officials, and the 1621–1629 She-An Rebellion briefly set up a breakaway kingdom before defeat. Ortai's 1720s campaigns broke remaining chiefdoms and pressed assimilation on Yi near Kunming, but Liangshan was never fully subdued, keeping its clan order after the rest of the southwest came under direct rule.
zh:
彝族自称诺苏，另有尼苏等支系称呼，是云南、四川、贵州、广西山区的藏缅语民族，讲与缅甸语相近的彝语支，保有本民族音节文字。先民是滇东乌蛮，曾为738—902年南诏国武士阶层，后为白族大理国臣民，直到13世纪蒙古征服。

元代以土司治理彝区，彝族各支此前已自建政权，贵州慕俄格国至1279年，后身水西土司延续到1698年。1337年川南彝人据有建昌、会理河谷，即后来的凉山地区，黑彝贵族在严格等级制下统治平民与奴仆，数百年间把王朝官吏拒之山外。

明代改土归流，1621—1629年奢安之乱曾建短暂割据政权，终被镇压。雍正年间鄂尔泰用兵摧毁残余土司，强令昆明附近彝人同化；但凉山始终未被真正征服，西南其余地区纳入流官治理后仍保家支制度。

en:
The Yidinjdjin, or Yidiny, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the lowland rainforests around Cairns in Far North Queensland. Their lands ran from Deeral north to the Barron River, inland to Mount Hypipamee and east to the Prior Range. To their north lay the coastal Djabugay, while to the south their borders met the Ngajanji and the Mamu.

They were divided into clans, including the Gimuy, custodians of the Cairns area, and the Walubara. They spoke Yidiny, a Pama-Nyungan tongue of the Yidinic branch closely akin to Djabugay.
zh:
伊丁吉人又称伊迪尼人，是昆士兰远北地区凯恩斯一带低地雨林的澳大利亚原住民。他们的领地从迪拉尔向北延伸到巴伦河，内陆至希皮帕米山，东抵普赖尔岭；北邻沿海的贾布盖人，南与恩甘詹吉人和马穆人接壤。

他们分成若干氏族，包括守护凯恩斯一带的吉穆伊人和瓦卢巴拉人。所说的伊迪尼语属帕马-牛雅语系伊迪尼语支，与贾布盖语十分接近。

en:
The Yiiji, also spelt Yeidji, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Kimberley region of Western Australia, closely bound up with the people called Gwini or Kwini; the groups around the Forrest River are often treated as one people, which also includes the Miwa. Their speech, also called Yiiji, is a dialect of Wunambal within the Worrorran family.

Their territory covered about 2,600 square kilometres between Cambridge Gulf and the Milligan ranges. From the eighteenth century they were drawn into the Makassan trepang trade: Makassan visitors, whose landfalls on the Kimberley coast began between 1669 and 1763, exchanged dugout canoes and trade goods for the sea cucumber cured on their beaches.
zh:
伊吉人（又作耶吉）是西澳大利亚州金伯利地区的澳大利亚原住民，与格维尼或奎尼人关系密不可分：福里斯特河一带的群体常被视为同一个群体，米瓦人也包括在内。伊吉语是武南布尔语的方言，属沃罗拉语系。

其领地在剑桥湾与米利根山脉之间，约2600平方公里。从18世纪起，他们被卷入望加锡人的海参贸易：1669—1763年间开始登陆金伯利海岸的望加锡客商，用独木舟和杂货交换他们在海滩上加工好的海参。

en: The Yilba, also written Ilba or Jilba, were an Aboriginal Australian people of Queensland whose speech was counted among the dialects of Biri, the language of the coast between Mackay and Townsville. Their recorded local groups, or hordes, included the Yukkaburra, Pegulloburra and Munkeeburra.
zh: 伊尔巴人（异写吉尔巴）是昆士兰的澳大利亚原住民，所说的语言被归入比里语的方言，比里语通行于麦凯与汤斯维尔之间的海岸地区。有记载的地方群包括尤卡布拉、佩古洛布拉和蒙基布拉。

en:
The Yinggardan are an Aboriginal people of the Gascoyne region of Western Australia, their country lying between the Gascoyne and Wooramel Rivers and running inland from the northern edge of Shark Bay. Their Kartu language had a northern and a southern dialect.

The Mandi called them and their neighbours the Baiyungu and Maia by the shared name Kakarakala, meaning easterners, while the Nhantan held them in awe as rain-making sorcerers. They entered European records through the Dutch ship Batavia, wrecked on the Houtman Abrolhos in 1629: the survivors' journal mentions the mainland people, and two convicted mutineers marooned on the coast may have ended their lives among local groups.
zh:
英加尔达人是西澳大利亚加斯科因地区的原住民，家园夹在加斯科因河与伍拉梅尔河之间，从鲨鱼湾北缘向内陆伸展。他们的卡尔图语分北方、南方两种方言。

曼迪人把他们与邻近的白云古人、马亚人统称为“卡拉卡拉”，意为“东方人”；恩汉塔人则敬畏他们，把他们视作能呼风唤雨的巫师。欧洲文献首次提到他们，与荷兰商船巴达维亚号有关：该船于1629年在豪特曼阿布罗柳斯群岛失事，幸存者的航海日志提到了大陆上的居民，两名被流放海岸的叛变水手或许最终就老死在当地族群之中。

en: The Yinwumi are the Yinwum, also written Jinwum, an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, neighbours of the Yupangathi groups near the peninsula's western tip. They spoke a Paman language of the North Cape York group, noted by linguists for unusual sound changes that set it apart from its relatives.
zh: 因伍姆人又译金伍姆人，是昆士兰约克角半岛北部的澳大利亚原住民，与半岛西端附近的尤潘加提诸群体相邻。他们的语言属北约克角帕曼语群，语言学家注意到它经历过一些罕见的音变，在同语群中显得与众不同。

en:
The Yir-Yoront are an Aboriginal people of the south-western Cape York Peninsula in northern Queensland, whose country lay along rivers and coastal flats facing the Gulf of Carpentaria. The sandridges there give their name its second element, yorront. Their language belongs to the Pama-Maric group, and their society was built on patrilineal clans divided into two moieties, with each person assigned clan land through a conception totem.

Because their territory had little usable stone, even stone axes reached them only through long-distance trade. They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering across the seasonal wetlands.

In 1623 a Dutch expedition under Jan Carstenszoon landed on their coast to trade; the logbook noted that the people knew nothing of metals or spices, and of the Dutch goods only the iron pieces failed to enter their everyday use.
zh:
伊尔约朗特人是昆士兰北部约克角半岛西南部的原住民，家园位于注入卡奔塔利亚湾的河流与沿海平原一带。那里沙脊纵横，他们名称的后半部分“约朗特”便与沙地有关。他们的语言属帕马-马里克语组，社会以父系氏族为基础，分为两个半偶族，每个人凭出生图腾分得氏族领地。

由于境内缺少可用的石材，就连石斧也要靠长途贸易辗转获得。他们在随季节变化的湿地上以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生。

1623年，扬·卡斯滕松率领的荷兰探险队在其海岸登陆交易，航行日志记载当地人对金属和香料一无所知，而荷兰人给出的货物里，唯有铁器没有进入他们的日常生活。

en: The Yirandhali are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Flinders River country in Queensland, around Hughenden in the Shire of Flinders. Their language is assigned to the Maric branch of the Pama–Nyungan family, their neighbours along the river included the Mbara, Gugu-Badhun and Wanamara, and the same people are recorded as the Dalleburra in the Hughenden area.
zh: 伊兰达利人是昆士兰弗林德斯河流域的澳大利亚原住民，活动在弗林德斯郡的休恩登一带。他们的语言被归入帕马-牛雅语系的马里语支，沿河的邻族包括姆巴拉人、古古-巴敦人和瓦纳马拉人；在休恩登地区，同一群人又被记作达利布拉人。

en:
The Yitha Yitha are an Aboriginal people of the lower Murray and lower Lachlan river country of south-western New South Wales. Their speech belongs with Kureinji and Dadi Dadi to the Lower Murray group of Pama-Nyungan, and their name is a reduplication of their word for no, jita, like the names of many Riverine tribes.

Each community kept a gnalla wattow, or postman, who understood every dialect within a hundred and fifty miles and whose person was sacred even among feuding tribes; these envoys arranged trade between the river peoples.

Charles Sturt's whaleboat expedition of 1830, descending the Murrumbidgee and following the Murray to the sea, passed through this country, opening it to the overlanders and squatters who came after.
zh:
伊塔伊塔人是新南威尔士州西南部墨累河下游与拉克伦河下游河乡的澳大利亚原住民。他们的语言与库雷因吉语、达迪达迪语同属帕马-尼永加语系的下墨累语组；族名和许多滨河族群一样，由意为“不”的吉塔一词重叠而成。

每个群落都设有一名称为格纳拉瓦托的“信使”，他通晓方圆一百五十英里内的各种方言，人身即使在敌对部落之间也被视为神圣不可侵犯，负责安排滨河诸族之间的贸易。

1830年，查尔斯·斯特尔特的捕鲸船探险队沿马兰比吉河而下，再顺墨累河入海，穿过这片土地，也为随后而来的陆路旅行者和牧场主打开了通道。

en:
The Karitiana are a Tupian people of the western Amazon in Rondônia, Brazil, occupying lands south of Porto Velho on tributaries of the Madeira. They lived by farming, fishing and hunting in villages that long remained beyond European reach.

Their language, Karitiâna, belongs to the Arikém branch of the Tupi family and is its only surviving member, the related Arikém and Kabixiâna tongues having since died out. The first Western contacts with them are thought to date to the 1600s, but no lasting or recorded contact followed for centuries.
zh:
卡利吉亚纳人是巴西朗多尼亚州西亚马逊地区的图皮语族群，住在韦柳港以南、马代拉河支流一带，以农耕、渔猎为生，村落长期处在欧洲人的势力范围之外。

他们的卡利吉亚纳语属图皮语系的阿里肯语支，是该语支仅存的语言，近亲的阿里肯语和卡比克西亚纳语都已消亡。一般认为西方人与他们的最早接触发生在17世纪，但此后数百年间都没有留下持续往来的记录。

en:
The Yoli, whom the Spanish called the Conchos after the shell-littered Río Conchos, were seminomadic bands in northern Mexico. They held the Río Conchos basin in Chihuahua northward to the Río Bravo and included the Chinarra and Chiz. Their Uto-Aztecan language was so close to Tarahumara that some scholars treat it as a dialect of that language.

They hunted deer and rabbits with bows, fished with nets, gathered plants and farmed, dwelling in huts of wooden frames covered with hides or grass. Franciscan missionaries entered their valleys. In 1684 a Concho headman testified before a Spanish court that he had led dozens of local bands, pointing to loose political ties, while the Chiz stood apart as allies of the Jumanos.
zh:
约利人是墨西哥北部一群半游牧部族，西班牙人因贝壳遍布的孔乔斯河而称他们为孔乔人。他们占据奇瓦瓦的孔乔斯河流域，向北直到布拉沃河，包括奇纳拉人、奇斯人等部落。他们的语言属犹他—阿兹特克语系，与塔拉乌马拉语极为相近，有学者认为它只是后者的一种方言。

约利人用弓箭猎鹿捕兔、撒网捕鱼，采集植物，也从事农耕，住在木架蒙兽皮或茅草的棚屋里。方济各会传教士进入他们的谷地传教。1684年，一名孔乔首领在西班牙法庭上供述自己曾统领数十个当地部落，可见各部落之间存在松散的政治联合，与舒马尼人结盟的奇斯人则不在其中。

en:
The Yolngu are Aboriginal Australian clans of north-eastern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory; their name means person in the Yolngu Matha languages, and every clan belongs to either the Dhuwa or the Yirritja moiety. Their customary law, the Maḏayin, governs land ownership, trade and ceremony through song cycles and sacred sites.

They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, obtained boomerangs through trade routes reaching Central Australia, and passed messages between distant clans with message sticks carried hundreds of kilometres.

From about the 1500s, Macassan trepang fishermen from Sulawesi anchored off their coasts each monsoon season, exchanging metal tools, cloth and tobacco for pearlshell and labour. The Yolngu word for a European, Balanda, derives from this contact through the Malay term for a Dutchman. Through the early 1800s these voyages remained their main link with the outside world.
zh:
雍古人是澳大利亚北领地阿纳姆地东北部若干原住民氏族的合称，在雍古玛萨诸语言中，“雍古”意为“人”，每个氏族都分属杜瓦或伊里查两大半偶族。他们的习惯法“玛达因”以歌组和圣地规范土地归属、贸易与仪式。

雍古人以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，通过远达澳大利亚中部的商路换取回旋镖，并由信使带着信息杖跋涉数百公里，在遥远的氏族间传递消息。

约从16世纪起，苏拉威西的望加锡海参渔民每年季风时节停泊在他们的海岸，用金属工具、布匹和烟草交换珍珠贝和劳力。雍古人称呼欧洲人的“巴兰达”一词便来自这一接触，源自马来语中对荷兰人的称呼。直到19世纪初，这种航行仍是他们与外部世界的主要联系。

en:
The Yombe are a Bantu people of the Kongo group, at home in the forested Mayombe hills that straddle the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of the Congo and Cabinda, where they speak Kiyombe, a dialect of the Kongo language. With the Vili and neighbouring peoples they formed one of the ethnic components of the Kingdom of Loango from its rise in the 1500s, and their clans also lived within the wider world of the Kingdom of Kongo.

Their carvers produced royal and funerary figures, phemba maternity statues and nkisi nkonde nail fetishes. Their cosmology placed the high god Ngoma Bunzi above earth and river spirits approached through ancestor shrines.
zh:
永贝人是刚果族群中的班图人，居住在横跨刚果（金）、刚果（布）和卡宾达的马永贝山林地带，说刚果语方言基永贝语。他们与维利人等周边族群一道，是16世纪兴起的罗安果王国的族群组成部分，其氏族也生活在刚果王国更广阔的世界中。

永贝工匠制作王室与墓葬雕像、称为“彭巴”的母性雕像以及“恩基西恩孔德”钉子神像。在他们的宇宙观里，至高神恩戈马·本齐高居天上，人们通过祖先神龛与大地神灵、河流神灵相通。

en:
Yongzhou denotes the Yong-Quan branch of Xiang Chinese, strung along the Hunan-Guangxi corridor from Qidong near Hengyang through the Lingling basin to Quanzhou and Xing'an across the Guangxi border; its main varieties include the speech of Yongzhou and Qiyang.

The region was ancient Lingling, where the Xiao and Xiang rivers meet. The Sui made it the prefecture of Yongzhou in the late sixth century, and in 805 the exiled Tang writer Liu Zongyuan settled here; his travel essays made its rivers and hills famous.

Yong-Quan dialects retain many voiced initials of Middle Chinese under heavy contact with Southwestern Mandarin. Under the Ming, Quanzhou was transferred to Guangxi, but its people kept their Xiang speech, so the branch still straddles both provinces.
zh:
永州指湘语的永全片，沿湘桂走廊分布，东起衡阳附近的祁东，穿过零陵盆地，西抵广西境内的全州、兴安等地，主要方言有永州话、祁阳话等。

这一带是古零陵之地，潇水与湘江在此汇合。6世纪末隋代改置永州；805年，遭贬的唐代文人柳宗元谪居于此，写下的游记使这里山水闻名。

永全片方言保留较多中古汉语浊声母，又深受西南官话影响。明代全州改隶广西，当地居民仍说湘语，这一支方言因此横跨两省。

en:
The Yorta Yorta are an Aboriginal people of the riverine country where the Goulburn River joins the Murray, spanning north-eastern Victoria and the opposite bank in New South Wales, including the wetlands around Barmah. Like several Murray basin peoples, their name is a reduplication of their word for no. Their dialect continuum and Yabula Yabula form the Yotayotic branch of Pama-Nyungan, possibly an isolate within the family.

The river provided fish, waterfowl and routes for bark canoes, and the people lived in a network of related clans sharing the one speech. European overlanders first crossed their country in the 1830s, and pastoral runs were taken up along the rivers soon afterwards.
zh:
约塔约塔人是古尔本河汇入墨累河一带河乡的澳大利亚原住民，地跨维多利亚州东北部与新南威尔士州对岸，包括巴马周围的湿地。和墨累河流域的几个族群一样，他们的名字由本族语言中意为“不”的词重叠而成。他们的方言连续体与亚布拉亚布拉语同属帕马-尼永加语系的约塔约特语支，在语系内可能是孤立语言。

河流提供鱼、水禽和树皮独木舟的航路，约塔约塔人以共用同一语言的亲属氏族网络而居。19世纪30年代，欧洲陆路旅行者首次穿过他们的土地，此后沿河地带很快出现了牧场。

en:
The Yoruba are one of West Africa's most urban peoples, organized since medieval times into walled city-states across Yorubaland's forest and savanna in southwestern Nigeria and adjoining Benin and Togo. Their spiritual homeland is Ile-Ife, founded by the middle of the first millennium BCE and seat of the Ife Empire at its height around 1200 to 1420, whose artists made naturalistic brass and terracotta heads.

Yoruba dynasties trace descent from the semi-legendary Oduduwa; each state was ruled by an oba, checked by chief councils. From the fifteenth century the Oyo Empire, with its cavalry and capital Oyo-Ile, overshadowed Ife and built a dominion from the Niger to the coast, drawing tribute from Dahomey and Nupe.

Oyo's power crumbled in the early nineteenth century under Fulani pressure and the loss of Ilorin; Ibadan and Abeokuta then rose as rival states. Traditional Yoruba religion centres on the high god Olodumare and orisha such as Shango and Ogun, whose worship spread with the Atlantic slave trade into Santeria and Candomble.
zh:
约鲁巴人是西非城市化程度最高的民族之一，中世纪起便在约鲁巴兰——今尼日利亚西南部及毗邻贝宁、多哥的森林与稀树草原地带——建立起一座座有城墙的城邦。他们的精神故土是伊费，早在公元前一千纪中期即已形成，1200年至1420年前后作为伊费帝国的都城达到鼎盛，其工匠创作了高度写实的黄铜和赤陶头像。

约鲁巴诸王朝都把世系追溯到半传说的始祖奥杜杜瓦；各城邦由奥巴统治，受酋长会议制衡。15世纪起，拥有骑兵、定都奥约-伊莱的奥约帝国盖过伊费，建立起北起尼日尔河、南至海岸的霸权，向达荷美、努佩等索取贡赋。

19世纪初，在富拉尼人的压力和伊洛林失守后，奥约霸权瓦解，伊巴丹和阿贝奥库塔作为相争的约鲁巴城邦崛起。约鲁巴传统信仰以至高神奥洛杜马雷和奥里沙神祇为核心，香戈、奥贡等神祇的崇拜随大西洋奴隶贸易外传，融入桑特里亚和坎东布雷。

en:
The Yshyr, who call themselves Ishír, meaning “person”, are a Zamuco-speaking people of the Gran Chaco, whose homeland lay along the Paraguay River and in the forests behind it. They were divided into the river-dwelling Ebytoso and the forest Tomáraho, each speaking its own dialect.

They lived as hunter-gatherers, moving with the resources of the Chaco scrub, and the Tomáraho long kept their boys' initiation ceremonies and shamanic traditions. Jesuit missionaries studied and described their language during the 1700s, leaving its earliest written record, while the Yshyr remained in the riverine woods beyond colonial settlements.
zh:
伊希尔人是大查科草原上操萨穆科语族语言的族群，自称伊希尔，意为“人”，家园在巴拉圭河沿岸及其后方森林。他们分为临河而居的埃比托索人和住在森林深处的托马拉霍人，各说一种方言。

伊希尔人以狩猎采集为生，随大查科灌丛中的资源迁徙，托马拉霍人长期保留着男子成丁仪式和萨满传统。18世纪，耶稣会传教士研究并记录了他们的语言，留下了最早的文字记载，而伊希尔人仍在殖民据点之外的河岸林地中生活。

en:
The Yuanga are a Kanak people of the far north of Grande Terre in New Caledonia. Their language belongs to the extreme-northern group of New Caledonian languages and was spoken around Kaala-Gomen and the inland districts of Bondé and Paimboa. These tongues share the Austronesian inheritance of Lapita navigators, whose pottery first appears on Grande Terre around 1100 BC.

Yuanga clans grew taro and yam on the ridges, gathered shellfish and speared fish along the reef, and bound rival lineages through ceremonial exchanges under their chiefs.

James Cook reached northern Grande Terre in September 1774, anchoring near Balade among neighbouring Kanak clans and trading before sailing on. Later visitors such as the Comte de Lapérouse in 1788 were rare, and the Yuanga hills kept their customary clan life intact through 1837.
zh:
尤安加人是新喀里多尼亚格朗德特尔岛最北端的卡纳克族群。他们的语言属新喀里多尼亚诸语的极北语组，通行于卡拉戈门及邦代、潘博阿等内陆地区。这些语言共同承继着拉皮塔航海者的南岛语遗产，拉皮塔陶器约在公元前1100年首次出现于格朗德特尔岛。

尤安加氏族在山脊上种植芋头和山药，沿礁岩采集贝类、叉鱼，并在酋长治下通过仪式交换联结相互竞争的世系。

1774年9月，詹姆斯·库克抵达格朗德特尔岛北端，在邻近的巴拉德一带停泊，与当地卡纳克氏族交易后继续航行。此后访客稀少，1788年拉彼鲁兹伯爵的途经是少数例子，尤安加山区的氏族习俗生活完整保持到1837年。

en:
The Maaya, or Yucatec Maya, are the Maya people of the Yucatán Peninsula; their tongue, Máaya t'áan, belongs to the Mayan language family. Their ancestors built the Classic-period cities of Chichen Itza and Coba; after the tenth-century upheavals the peninsula's political centre shifted north. In about 1221 regional lords overthrew Chichen Itza and made Mayapan their capital, led by the Cocom family with the Xiu and other houses sharing government; the league united northern Yucatán for over two centuries.

In 1337 Mayapan still dominated the peninsula, but in 1441 an Xiu revolt sacked and burned the city, and Yucatán broke into rival city-states, sixteen still standing when the Spanish arrived.

Europeans first landed in 1508; shipwrecked in 1511, Gonzalo Guerrero married into a Maya lord's family. Spanish conquest and the encomienda system followed in the 1520s, and introduced diseases carried off many people. The Maya kept their language and communal identity through colonial rule until Mexico's independence in 1821.
zh:
玛雅人（这里指尤卡坦玛雅人）是尤卡坦半岛的玛雅民族，所说的玛雅语自称 Máaya t'áan，属玛雅语系。先民建起奇琴伊察、科巴等古典期大城；10世纪动荡后，政治中心北移。约1221年，各地领主推翻奇琴伊察，定都玛雅潘，由科科姆家族主导，希乌等家族共治；联盟统合尤卡坦北部两百多年。

1337年玛雅潘仍是半岛霸主，但1441年希乌家族起兵攻破并焚毁玛雅潘，尤卡坦分裂为互相争战的城邦，西班牙人到来时仍有十六个。

欧洲人最早于1508年登陆；1511年沉船幸存者贡萨洛·格雷罗入赘玛雅首领之家。1520年代起西班牙发动征服并推行监护征赋制，外来疫病夺去大量人口。殖民统治下玛雅人保留语言和社群认同，直至1821年墨西哥独立。

en:
The Yuè culture occupies the Qiantang River basin and the southern shore of Hangzhou Bay around Hangzhou and Shaoxing in northern Zhejiang. It descends from the ancient State of Yue, whose capital Kuaiji stood at modern Shaoxing; under King Goujian, Yue annexed its rival Wu in 473 BC and dominated the lower Yangtze until Chu overran it in 333 BC.

The Yue were famed for bronze swords, a navy and a distinct native speech, often taken as the substrate of later Wu dialects. Under the Qin's Kuaiji Commandery, Han settlement and sinification deepened. In 1132 the Song court, driven south by the Jurchen, made Lin'an, modern Hangzhou, its capital; northern migrants gave the Hangzhou dialect its northern flavor and the region a literary reading layer.

Through the Yuan, Ming and Qing, Hangzhou remained the Grand Canal's southern terminus and a commercial city, while Shaoxing supplied examination graduates and the famed Shaoxing legal secretaries, and gave its name to Yue opera.
zh:
越文化地处钱塘江流域与杭州湾南岸，以杭州、绍兴为中心，即浙北临绍一带。它源自古代越国：都城会稽就在今绍兴，越王勾践卧薪尝胆，于公元前473年攻灭世仇吴国，称霸长江下游，至公元前333年被楚国吞并。

越人以青铜宝剑、水军和独特的本土语言闻名，古越语通常被视为后世吴语的底层成分。秦代设会稽郡，汉人移民迁入，中原化日益加深。1132年宋廷为避女真人南下，以临安（今杭州）为行在，大批北方士民随行，使杭州话带上北方色彩，也为当地方言添了文读系统。

元、明、清三代，杭州始终是大运河的南端终点和商业巨邑；绍兴则通过科举向朝廷输送人才，绍兴师爷遍布衙门，越剧也发源于此。

en:
The Yuèhǎi are Yue Chinese of the Pearl River Delta around Guangzhou; their speech is the main branch of Yue, whose Guangzhou dialect is the prestige form, Cantonese. Their Lingnan homeland south of the Nanling was Baiyue territory until the Qin conquest of 214 BC brought Han migrants via the Lingqu Canal; after Qin fell it became the kingdom of Nanyue, absorbed by the Han in 111 BC.

Refugee waves after the Han, Tang and Song collapses blended northern speech with the indigenous Tai-related vernacular, yielding a language conservative in Middle Chinese final consonants and tones.
