official_raw.zh: [ShowGodName('quetzalcoatl_god')]是美索美洲众神中的生命、风和智慧之神。

en: Ratovantany, also called Andriantompo, was self-created, and his creation myth is known across Madagascar. He shaped human beings from soil and takes back the corpse at death to decompose it. The soul belongs to Zanahary and goes to the sky or the sun. Unlike Zanahary, Ratovantany does not appear to have been a prominent deity to any Malagasy people.
zh: 拉托万塔尼又称安德里亚恩托姆波，是自生之神，他的创世神话流传于马达加斯加全岛。他用泥土塑成人的身体，人死后收回遗体使其腐化。灵魂则属于扎纳哈里，去往天空或太阳。与扎纳哈里不同，拉托万塔尼似乎没有成为任何马达加斯加族群崇奉的显要神明。

official_raw.en: $ratovantany_god$ is an earth god of the [ShowReligionAdjective('fomba_gasy_religion')] pantheon that made a pact with [ShowGodName('zanahary_god')] to create humanity.
official_raw.zh: $ratovantany_god$是[ShowReligionAdjective('fomba_gasy_religion')]中的地神，与[ShowGodName('zanahary_god')]立约创造人类。

en: Rep-un-kamuy was one of the spirits that the Ainu of the coasts of Hokkaidō, Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands looked to for their living.
zh: 北海道、库页岛和千岛群岛沿海的阿伊努人，要仰仗海鲸神威赐予生计。

official_raw.en: $rep_un_kamuy_god$ is the god of the sea of the [ShowCultureName('ainu_culture')] people.

en: Sakhua is also the name the Mizo of northeast India gave to their traditional faith, and in the view of the writer Zairema it is the guardian spirit of a clan, representing its identity. The word joins sa, the clan or family a person is born into, with khua, the village.
zh: 萨库阿也是印度东北部米佐人对其传统信仰的称呼，在作家扎伊雷马看来，它同时是氏族的守护灵，代表这个氏族的身份。这个词由“萨”和“库阿”组成，前者指人出生所属的氏族或家族，后者指村落。

official_raw.en: $sakhua_god$ is the god of the family of the [ShowCultureName('zo_culture')] people.

en:
Sakpata is worshipped among the Fon, Ewe, Adja and other Gbe-speaking peoples, from the west of present-day Nigeria to the Volta Region. He is the Dahomean form of the Yoruba Sopona, god of smallpox, and can both heal and inflict illness and madness.

Oral history says smallpox decimated their ancestors at Adja Tado until a Yoruba man called Torgbui Anyi cured them. Sakpata is one of the most worshipped of their gods.
zh:
萨克帕塔受丰人、埃维人、阿贾人及其他格贝语民族崇拜，这些民族分布在今尼日利亚西部到沃尔特地区一带。他是约鲁巴天花神索波纳在达荷美的形态，既能治病，也能降下疾病和疯狂。

口述历史说，天花曾在阿贾塔多使他们的祖先大批死去，直到一位名叫托格布伊·安伊的约鲁巴人把他们治好。萨克帕塔是他们崇拜最广的神之一。

official_raw.en: $sakpata_god$ is the god of earth and disease of the [ShowReligionAdjective('vodun_religion')] pantheon.

en: The name Śakti comes from the Sanskrit root meaning to be able. Beside Shiva she appears as Uma, Durga, the terrifying Kali and the motherly Parvati; beside Vishnu, as Lakshmi. In nondualist thought Shiva and Shakti are one inseparable being. The name Shakta became popular from the ninth century.
zh: 沙克蒂的名称出自意为“能够”的梵语词根。在湿婆身边，她化为乌玛、杜尔迦、可怖的迦利和慈母般的帕尔瓦蒂；在毗湿奴身边则是拉克什米。在不二论的思想中，湿婆与沙克蒂是不可分割的一体。“沙克塔”之名自9世纪起流行。

official_raw.en: $shakti_god$ is a major [goddess|e] in [ShowReligionName('hindu')], revered as the fundamental cosmic energy. She is worshiped as the supreme [goddess] or Devī in [ShowPolicyName('shaktism')], and many other [goddesses] are worshiped as different aspects of $shakti_god$. Some of them can even take many other forms themselves.
official_raw.zh: $shakti_god$是[ShowReligionName('hindu')]中的重要[goddess|e]，被视为宇宙的根本能量。在[ShowPolicyName('shaktism')]中，她被尊为“提毗”，即至高[goddesses]，许多其他[goddess]也被视为$shakti_god$的不同化身，有些甚至能变化为多种形态。

en:
Śiva is also called Mahadeva, the Great God. He is the yogi who lives an ascetic life on Mount Kailasa, patron of meditation and the arts, and also a householder with his wife Parvati and sons Ganesha and Kartikeya.

His emblems are the trident, the crescent moon, the river Ganga in his matted hair and a third eye that burns what it looks on. He is mostly worshipped as the lingam.
zh:
湿婆又称大自在天，即“伟大的神”。他是在凯拉萨山过着苦行生活的瑜伽行者，冥想与艺术的庇护者，又是与妻子帕尔瓦蒂和儿子犍尼萨、鸠摩罗同住的家主。

他的标志是三叉戟、新月、发髻中流出的恒河，以及睁开时会烧毁眼前一切的第三只眼。人们大多以林伽的形式崇拜他。

official_raw.en: $shiva_god$ is one of the main [gods|e] of [ShowReligionName('hindu')], and the supreme being in [ShowPolicyName('shaivism')]. He is the patron of asceticism and yoga.
official_raw.zh: $shiva_god$是[ShowReligionName('hindu')]的主要[gods|e]之一，也是[ShowPolicyName('shaivism')]的至高存在。他是苦行与瑜伽的庇护者。

en: A male sky god often rules the pantheon as a sky father, paired with an earth mother. In Greek myth the primordial sky god Uranus was succeeded by Zeus, who ruled from Mount Olympus.
zh: 男性天神往往统领诸神，成为“天父”，并与“地母”配对。希腊神话中，原初天神乌拉诺斯被宙斯取代，后者在奥林匹斯山上统治天界。

official_raw.en: The $sky_god$ represents the omnipresent force that watches over and protects humanity.
official_raw.zh: $sky_god$象征无处不在的守护之力，庇佑人间。

en: The ethnographer Sidney Endle lists Song Bwrai with Bathoubwrai and Mainao among the prominent gods of the Boro. He is worshipped at an altar inside the house called the dham, chiefly by women, and the offerings made to him are afterwards laid at the sijou tree of Bathou.
zh: 民族志学者悉尼·恩德尔把宋布赖与巴图布赖、买瑙并列为博罗人的主要神灵。人们在屋内名为“丹”的祭坛上祭拜他，主要是妇女，供品事后还要摆到象征巴图的西久树下。

official_raw.en: $song_bwrai_god$ is a household god of the [ShowCultureName('bodo_culture')] people.

en:
Sumnima is worshipped by the Rai, a Kirati people of eastern Nepal, as the goddess of nature, fertility, agriculture, forests and rivers. She is the wife of the sky god Paruhang.

The two together stand for the union of heaven and earth in the Kirat Mundhum. The Rai make offerings to Paruhang and Sumnima at the Sakela festival of sowing and harvest.
zh:
松米玛受尼泊尔东部基拉特民族莱人崇拜，是自然之神，主管生育、农耕、森林和河流。她是天神帕茹夯的妻子。

两位神合起来象征门顿传统中天与地的结合。在播种和收获时的萨克拉节上，莱人要向帕茹夯和松米玛献祭。

official_raw.en: $sumnima_god$ is the supreme god and Mother Earth of the [ShowCultureName('kirati_culture')] people.

en:
Supay was an ambivalent spirit of the Quechua, Aymara and Inca who ruled the Uku Pacha. He stood for shadow, night, darkness and the inevitable passage of death. The word comes from supa, meaning shadow, illness or death.

In its early form the name was neutral: the 1560 Quechua–Spanish dictionary of Friar Domingo de Santo Tomás lists a good spirit, allisupa, and a bad one, manaallisupa. Under Spanish rule Supay was turned into the Christian devil.
zh:
苏帕伊是克丘亚人、艾马拉人和印加人信仰中亦善亦恶的灵，统治着内界乌库·帕查。他代表阴影、黑夜、黑暗和死亡的必然降临。这个词出自“苏帕”，意为阴影、疾病或死亡。

这个名字起初是中性的：1560年多明各·德·圣托马斯修士编的克丘亚语—西班牙语词典，既列出了善灵，也列出了恶灵。西班牙人统治时期，苏帕伊被改造成基督教的魔鬼。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('supay_god')] is the god of the underworld for the people of the [ShowRegionName('andes_region')].

en:
In Hindu texts Sūrya is a male god, counted among the five equivalent deities of the Smarta tradition, and is shown riding a chariot drawn by seven horses. The oldest Vedic hymns, such as Rigveda 1.115, revere him as the rising sun; in the medieval period he was worshipped with Brahma by day, Vishnu at noon and Shiva in the evening.

His worship declined greatly around the thirteenth century, perhaps because Muslim invaders destroyed Sun temples in northern India. He was increasingly merged with Vishnu and Shiva.
zh:
在印度教文献中，苏利耶是男神，位列斯马尔塔传统中地位对等的五位神祇之一，形象是驾着七匹马拉的战车。最古老的吠陀颂歌（如《梨俱吠陀》1.115）崇敬升起的太阳；中世纪时，人们白天与梵天同祭，正午与毗湿奴同祭，傍晚与湿婆同祭。

13世纪前后，对他的崇拜大幅衰落，也许是因为北印度的太阳神庙被穆斯林破坏。他越来越多地被并入毗湿奴和湿婆。

official_raw.en: $surya_god$ is the Sun [goddess|e] in [ShowReligionName('hindu')], and one of the main deities of [ShowPolicyName('smartism')].
official_raw.zh: $surya_god$是[ShowReligionName('hindu')]中的太阳[goddess|e]，也是[ShowPolicyName('smartism')]的主要神祇之一。

en:
Takhar, or Taahkarr, is a demi-god of the Serer of Senegal, the Gambia and Mauritania. Serer appeal to him against injuries, oppression and evil magic.

He is worshipped at the foot of the tallest trees of a sacred forest, where he and his adversary Tiurakh, god of wealth and property, are believed to dwell. His high priests, the Saltigues, are old men from notable families who judged theft and witchcraft, relying on fear of Takhar more than on the non-lethal poison they gave the accused.
zh:
塔卡尔又作塔阿卡尔，是塞内加尔、冈比亚和毛里塔尼亚塞雷尔人的半神。塞雷尔人向他申诉所受的伤害、压迫和邪恶巫术。

人们在神圣森林里最高的树脚下祭拜他，相信他和他的对手财富与财产之神提乌拉赫就住在那里。他的大祭司萨尔蒂格是出身名门的老人，审理盗窃和巫术案件，靠的是人们对塔卡尔的畏惧，多于给被告喝的不致命毒药。

official_raw.en: $takhar_god$ is the god of justice and vengeance of the [ShowReligionAdjective('odinala_religion')] pantheon.

en:
Tano, whose true name is Ta Kora, is also a god of strife, and among the Asante of thunder and lightning. He is counted the highest of the abosom, the lesser gods, many of whom are his sons.

He is pictured as a large armed warrior who can change shape, and baboons are said to guard his shrine. Fish are his children, and the Asante do not eat the river's fish.
zh:
塔诺的真名是塔·科拉，也是纷争之神，在阿散蒂人那里还是雷电之神。他被视为阿博松，也就是诸次级神灵中地位最高者，许多阿博松是他的儿子。

他的形象是身材高大、手持兵器的战士，能变换形体，据说狒狒守卫着他的神龛。鱼是他的孩子，阿散蒂人不吃这条河里的鱼。

official_raw.en: $tano_god$ is the gof of war of the [ShowReligionAdjective('akan_religion')] pantheon, he represents the Tano river.

en:
Kök Teŋri, the Eternal Blue Sky, was judge and source of life, eternal and supreme. His oldest recorded form is the Chinese transcription Cheng-li, used of the Xiongnu in the fourth century BC.

He was the chief god of the steppe ruling classes in the sixth to ninth centuries. The Orkhon inscriptions of the early eighth century say that Tengri creates death, and a khagan called himself ‘Tengri-like, Tengri-born’. The Uighur khagans’ adoption of Manichaeism in the eighth century cost his cult its place at court.
zh:
长生天（腾格里）即永恒的蓝天，是审判者和生命之源，永恒而至高。他最早的记载是汉文史书的音译“撑犁”，用于公元前4世纪的匈奴。

6至9世纪，他是草原统治阶层的主神。8世纪初的鄂尔浑碑铭说腾格里创造死亡，毗伽可汗自称“如天、天生”。8世纪回鹘可汗改奉摩尼教，使他的崇拜在宫廷里失去了地位。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('tengri_god')] is the god of heaven of the [ShowCultureGroupName('turkic_group')] people.

en:
Tepeu, a K’iche’ Maya word meaning ‘sovereign’, was a creator god of the K’iche’ of the Guatemalan highlands. According to the Popol Vuh, he made the world and humanity together with the Feathered Serpent Q’uq’umatz, and was a god of lightning and fire.

The two were held to be the mythical ancestors of the K’iche’ nobility in the male line. The Popol Vuh was recorded in K’iche’ around 1550, after the Spanish conquest.
zh:
特佩乌在基切玛雅语中意为“君主”，是危地马拉高地基切人的创世神。据《波波尔·乌》所述，他与羽蛇古库马兹一同创造了世界和人类，并被视为闪电与火之神。

这两位神被认为是基切贵族男系的神话始祖。《波波尔·乌》在西班牙征服之后，于1550年前后用基切语记录下来。

official_raw.en: $tepeu_god$ is the sovereign god of the [ShowLanguageName('maya_language')] speaking people.

en:
Tezcatlipoca, ‘Smoking Mirror’, was a central god of the Aztecs, linked to the night sky, obsidian, hurricanes, conflict and divination; the name alludes to the obsidian mirrors used in prophecy. He was one of four sons of the primordial pair Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, and his animal form was the jaguar.

He was Quetzalcoatl’s rival in the myth of the Five Suns and in the legends of Tollan. His festival was Toxcatl, and a new king fasted and prayed to him at his enthronement.
zh:
特斯卡特利波卡意为“冒烟的镜子”，是阿兹特克的核心神祇之一，与夜空、黑曜石、飓风、冲突和占卜相关；名字指占卜时用的黑曜石镜。他是原初配偶奥梅特库特利和奥梅西瓦特尔的四个儿子之一，兽形是美洲豹。

在五个太阳的神话和托兰城的传说里，他都是魁札尔·科亚特尔的对手。他的节日是托什卡特尔，新王登基时要向他斋戒祈祷。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('tezcatlipoca_god')] is the god of providence, the invisible and darkness in the Mesoamerican pantheon.
official_raw.zh: [ShowGodName('tezcatlipoca_god')]是美索美洲众神中的黑暗无常之神。

en: Thunder gods have been imagined by peoples in many cultures. In Indo-European religions the thunder god is often male and chief of the gods, as with Indra in Hinduism, Zeus in Greece, Perkunas among the Balts and Perun among the Slavs.
zh: 许多文化中的人们都设想过雷神。在印欧人的宗教里，雷神往往是男性，并且是诸神之首，例如印度教的因陀罗、希腊的宙斯、波罗的人的佩尔库纳斯和斯拉夫人的佩伦。

official_raw.en: The $thunder_god$ represents the immediacy and indiference of fate.
official_raw.zh: $thunder_god$象征命运无常的威严与雷霆骤降的裁决。

en:
Tláloc was also the Aztec god of water and earthly fertility, feared for his hail, thunder and lightning. He is shown with fangs and a forked tongue, often holding a vessel of water. A storm god was already worshipped at Teotihuacan, and his great rites were held on the mountain called Cerro Tláloc.

Those killed by drowning or lightning went to his paradise, Tlálocan. At Tenochtitlan his shrine stood beside Huitzilopochtli’s on the Great Temple.
zh:
特拉洛克也是阿兹特克的水与大地丰饶之神，人们敬畏他降下的冰雹、雷鸣和闪电。他的形象长着獠牙和分叉的舌头，常捧着盛水的容器。特奥蒂瓦坎早已奉祀风暴之神，他最盛大的祭仪在特拉洛克山上举行。

死于溺水或雷击的人会去他的乐园特拉洛坎。在特诺奇蒂特兰，他的神殿与维齐洛波奇特利的并立在大神庙上。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('tlaloc_god')] is the rain god of the Mesoamerican pantheon.

en:
Thor was the hammer-wielding Germanic god of strength, patron of farmers, son of Odin and husband of Sif. He drove a cart drawn by two goats, and his great foe was the world serpent Jörmungandr, with whom he was fated to die at Ragnarök.

In the Viking Age, hammer pendants and names beginning with Þórr were worn in defiance of Christian missionaries. In the 11th century Adam of Bremen described his statue at Uppsala, and a 12th-century runic stick from Bergen still calls on him and Odin.
zh:
托尔是日耳曼人手持战锤的力量之神，是农夫的守护神，奥丁之子，西芙的丈夫。他驾着两只山羊拉的车，大敌是世界之蛇耶梦加得，诸神黄昏时两者注定同归于尽。

维京时代，人们佩戴锤形吊坠、取以托尔为首的名字，以此对抗基督教传教士。11世纪，不来梅的亚当描述了乌普萨拉的托尔神像；12世纪卑尔根的一根卢恩木棍上，还在向他和奥丁求助。

official_raw.en: $tor_god$ is a member of the Aesir, who is worshipped as the God of thunder, storms, protection and free people.
official_raw.zh: $tor_god$是阿萨神族中的重要神祇，被尊为雷神与风暴之神，同时也是人类的保护者及自由民的守护神。

en:
In Norse sources Týr fed the wolf Fenrir. When the gods bound the monster, Týr put his right hand in its mouth as a pledge and lost it when Fenrir found himself tricked. At Ragnarök the dog Garmr is foretold to devour him.

The Romans equated him with Mars, and a third-century inscription names ‘Mars of the Assembly’, linking him with the Germanic thing. His name is the Old English Tiw, and some scholars think he once stood nearer the centre of the Germanic gods.
zh:
在诺斯资料里，提尔饲养着巨狼芬里尔。诸神缚住这头怪物时，提尔把右手放进它口中作担保，芬里尔发觉受骗，咬断了他的手。诸神黄昏时，据预言他将被恶犬加姆吞噬。

罗马人把他等同于战神马尔斯，3世纪的一块拉丁铭文称“议事会的马尔斯”，说明他与日耳曼人的议事会有关。他的名字在古英语里是提乌；有学者认为他早先在日耳曼诸神中地位更为核心。

official_raw.en: $tyr_god$ is a member of the Aesir, and is the feeder of wolfs, and the battle god.
official_raw.zh: $tyr_god$是阿萨神族的一员，饲狼者以及战神。

en: In Khasi tradition U Blei Nong-thaw, the Lord Master, first divided humankind into sixteen heavenly families, of which seven were left on earth.
zh: 卡西人的传说称，乌勃黎·农陀，即主宰，最初把人类分成十六个天上的家族，其中七家被留在人间。

official_raw.en: $u_blei_nong_thaw_god$ is the creator god of the [ShowReligionAdjective('ka_niam_khasi_religion')] pantheon.

en: The Khasi faith held that one formless supreme creator, U Blei Nongthaw, stood above all such deities.
zh: 卡西人的信仰认为，独一无形的至高创世主乌勃黎·农陀位在所有这些神灵之上。

official_raw.en: $ulei_longspah_god$ is the god of wealth of the [ShowReligionAdjective('ka_niam_khasi_religion')] pantheon.

en: The Khasis lived in about twenty-five independent states, each ruled by a chief called the syiem.
zh: 卡西人生活在约二十五个独立的邦里，各由一位称作“西姆”的酋长治理。

official_raw.en: $ulei_muluk_god$ is the god of the state for the [ShowCultureName('khasi_culture')] people.

en: Every Khasi village traditionally kept a sacred grove to appease the forest spirit, and the religion was handed down by word of mouth.
zh: 传统上，每个卡西村庄都有一片圣林，用来安抚森林之灵；卡西人的宗教靠口耳相传。

official_raw.en: $ulei_umtang_god$ is the god of drinking water of the [ShowReligionAdjective('ka_niam_khasi_religion')] pantheon.

en:
Ülgen, from the Old Turkic words for ‘rich’ and ‘magnificent’, is a creator god believed to be without beginning or end. He is usually distinct from Tengri, though sometimes identified with him.

He has seven sons, the White Boys, and nine daughters who inspire shamans. In Altai tradition he is the brother of Erlik, lord of the underworld, and both were created by Kayra; Erlik opposed the upper realm of light and was imprisoned in the ninth layer of the earth.
zh:
于尔根的名字出自古突厥语中的“富有”和“壮丽”，是创世神，被认为无始无终。他通常与长生天有别，有时又被等同于长生天。

他有七个儿子，称为白衣少年，还有九个女儿，她们是萨满灵感的来源。在阿尔泰传统里，他是冥界之主尔力克的兄弟，二者都由凯尔拉所造；尔力克与光明的上界为敌，被囚禁在大地的第九层。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('ulgen_god')] is the god of goodness of the [ShowCultureGroupName('turkic_group')] people.

en:
Umay was protector of women, mothers and children. The word umay meant the placenta. She lived in heaven, unseen, and kept the souls of unborn babies on a mount called Ymay-tas. When she left a child for long it fell ill, and shamans called her back.

The Kül Tigin inscription of the eighth century compares the khagan’s mother to her, and the khagans’ wives were themselves called Umay. She is especially honoured by the Khakas.
zh:
乌迈守护妇女、母亲和孩童。乌迈一词原指胎盘。她住在天上，不被常人看见，把未出生婴儿的灵魂保存在一座叫伊迈石的山上。她若久久离开孩子，孩子就会生病，要请萨满把她唤回。

8世纪的阙特勤碑把可汗的母亲比作乌迈，可汗的妻子也被称作乌迈。哈卡斯人尤其敬奉她。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('umay_god')] is the goddess of fertility of the [ShowCultureGroupName('turkic_group')] people.

en:
Urpihuachac, also written Urpayhuáchac, appears in the Huarochirí Manuscript as the wife of the god Pachacamac and one of five sisters. They had two daughters who lived on islands off the coast.

According to the manuscript, fish once existed only in her care, until they were cast into the sea and multiplied. She was pictured with the features of both bird and fish, and at San Francisco de Mangas some clans asked her for rain in the form of a dove carved of bone.
zh:
乌尔帕伊·瓦查克，又作乌尔皮瓦查克，在《瓦罗奇里手稿》中是神明帕查卡马克的妻子，五姐妹之一。两人有两个女儿，住在近海的岛上。

据手稿所述，鱼起初只由她饲养，后来被抛入海中，才繁衍起来。她的形象兼有鸟和鱼的特征；在圣弗朗西斯科·德·曼加斯，一些氏族以骨头刻成的鸽子向她求雨。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('urpihuachac_god')] is the mother of birds and fish for the people of the [ShowRegionName('andes_region')].

en: Uscovilca was also the title of the chief of the Hanan Chanka, a farming people of Andahuaylas in the Peruvian highlands. The Chanka were defeated by the Inca at Cusco in 1438.
zh: 乌斯科维尔卡也是秘鲁高地安达瓦伊拉斯农耕民族昌卡人中上昌卡首领的称号。昌卡人于1438年在库斯科被印加击败。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('uscovilca_god')] is the creator god of the [ShowCultureName('chanka_culture')] people.

en:
Wiraqucha was the supreme god in pre-Inca and Inca belief. Pictured as a bearded man, he is said to have ordered the building of Tiwanaku, made the sun, moon and stars, and set time in motion by commanding the sun to cross the sky. Under the Inca he was the most important deity, followed by Inti.

One account has him make humanity on an island in Lake Titicaca, teach people how to live, then hand them over to lesser gods and vanish.
zh:
维拉科查是印加以前和印加时代信仰中的至高神。他的形象是一位有胡须的男子；据说他下令修建了蒂瓦纳库，创造了日月星辰，并命令太阳越过天空，由此启动了时间。在印加人那里，他是最重要的神，其后才是因蒂。

一种说法称，他在的的喀喀湖的一座岛上造出人类，教人们如何生活，然后把人类交给较低的神灵，自己隐去。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('viracocha')] is the creator god of the people of the [ShowRegionName('andes_region')].

en:
Viṣṇu’s name means All Pervasive, and in the Trimurti he is the Preserver beside Brahma and Shiva. Little prominent in the Vedas, he rose to importance in the last centuries BCE, when he was identified with Vasudeva-Krishna and Narayana.

Whenever evil and chaos threaten the world he descends as an avatar to restore order and protect dharma. Of the ten Dashavataras, Rama and Krishna are the most worshipped.
zh:
毗湿奴的名字意为“无所不在者”，在三相神中与梵天、湿婆并列，担任守护者。他在吠陀中并不突出，到公元前最后几个世纪才变得重要，被等同于瓦苏提婆—克里希那和那罗衍那。

每当邪恶与混乱威胁世界，他就化身下凡，恢复秩序，护持正法。十大化身中，罗摩和克里希那最受崇拜。

official_raw.en: $vishnu_god$ is one of the main [gods|e] of [ShowReligionName('hindu')], and the main one in [ShowPolicyName('vaishnavism')]. He is regarded as the supreme being, manifesting himself on earth in the form of his ten [avatars|e].
official_raw.zh: $vishnu_god$是[ShowReligionName('hindu')]的主要[gods|e]之一，也是[ShowPolicyName('vaishnavism')]的至高存在。他被视为至高存在，并以十种[avatars|e]的形式显现在地球上。

en:
Waaq, or Waaqa, is a sky god of the Horn of Africa. The word still means God in Oromo, and survives in Konso, Rendille and other Cushitic languages.

Among the Oromo he is Waaqa Tokkicha, the one God, who acts through the ayyaana, intermediary spirits. After Islam arrived, the Somali largely replaced the name with the Arabic Allaah, but it lives on in the Jidwaaq clan and the town of Ceelwaaq.
zh:
瓦格又作瓦加，是非洲之角的天神。这个词在奥罗莫语中仍意为“神”，在孔索语、伦迪勒语等库希特语言里也仍可见到。

奥罗莫人称他为瓦格·托基查，即唯一的神，他通过阿亚纳，即居间传话的灵行事。伊斯兰教传入后，索马里人大多改用阿拉伯语的安拉称呼神，但这个词仍保留在吉德瓦格氏族和埃勒瓦格镇等名称里。

official_raw.en: $waaq_god$ is the creator god of the [ShowLanguageName('east_cushitic_language')] speaking people.
official_raw.zh: $waaq_god$是库希特族群信奉的创世神。

en: War gods are common in polytheistic religions. The Greek Ares embodied both the courage and the brutality of battle, while his sister Athena stood for strategy and generalship.
zh: 战神在多神宗教中十分常见。希腊的阿瑞斯既体现战斗中的勇气，也体现其中的残暴，而他的姐姐雅典娜则代表谋略与统兵之道。

official_raw.en: The $war_god$ represents the strength and creativity brought by conflict, but also its devastation and calamity.
official_raw.zh: $war_god$既赋予冲突中的力量与创造，也带来其导致的毁灭与浩劫。

en: Water deities are most prominent among peoples for whom the sea or a great river mattered. Chinese tradition knows Hebo, god of the Yellow River, and Mazu, goddess of the sea and protector of seafarers.
zh: 水神在依赖大海或大河的民族中尤为重要。中国传统中有黄河之神河伯，以及海上女神、航海者的保护者妈祖。

official_raw.en: The $water_god$ represents the strength and rejuvenation brought by rain and river.
official_raw.zh: $water_god$象征雨水与河流所赐予的力量与复苏。

en: Many polytheistic religions have one or more wind gods. A wind god may double as an air god, and many are linked with one of the four seasons.
zh: 许多多神宗教都有一位或几位风神。风神可以兼任空气之神，许多风神还与四季中的某一季相联。

official_raw.en: The $wind_god$ represents the freedom and wonder of youth.
official_raw.zh: $wind_god$象征无拘无束的自由与奇迹般的气息。

en:
Xiuhtecuhtli, ‘Turquoise Lord’ or ‘Lord of Fire’, was the Aztec god of heat, day and the year, lord of volcanoes and one of the oldest gods of Mesoamerica. He was usually shown young, though sometimes identified with the ‘Old God’ Huehueteotl; his wife was Chalchiuhtlicue.

A small fire burned at the centre of every home in his honour, and the first mouthful of each meal was thrown into the hearth. The Aztec emperors were regarded as his living embodiment at their enthronement.
zh:
修特库特利意为“绿松石之主”或“火之主”，是阿兹特克的热、昼和年岁之神，是火山之主，也是中美洲最古老的神祇之一。他通常被画成年轻人的样子，有时又被等同于“老神”韦韦特奥特尔；他的妻子是恰尔丘特利奎。

每家每户的中心都燃着一小堆火来供奉他，每顿饭的第一口食物要投进灶火里。阿兹特克的皇帝在登基时被视为他的化身。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodName('xiuhtecuhtli_god')] is the god of fire in the Mesoamerican pantheon.

en:
Yuma Sammang, also called ‘Grandmother’, is revered by the Limbu, or Yakthung, of eastern Nepal. She is the female form in which the supreme power Tagera Ningwaphuma appears on earth, her male form being Theba Sammang, and the Limbu regard her as a maternal figure.

Her worship is carried by the oral Mundhum. In the 1770s the Limbu confederation Limbuwan fell to Gorkha, but the Limbu kept their culture and Mundhum alive.
zh:
玉玛桑芒又称“祖母”，受尼泊尔东部林布人，即雅克通人崇奉。至高力量塔格拉·宁瓦普马在人间以她为女性形态，男性形态则是特巴桑芒；林布人把她看作母亲一般的神。

对她的崇拜靠口传的《门顿》流传。18世纪70年代，林布人的林布旺联盟被廓尔喀并吞，但林布人仍保存着自己的文化和《门顿》。

official_raw.en: $yuma_sammang_god$ is the supreme god and Mother Earth of the [ShowCultureName('limbu_culture')] people.
official_raw.zh: $yuma_sammang_god$是[ShowCultureName('limbu_culture')]民族的至高神和大地之母。

en:
Zanahary is the personified sky and supreme god of Malagasy belief, usually thought of as male. With the earth god Ratovantany he made humanity: at death the soul rises to the firmament and the body returns to the earth, which ties him closely to the soul and to ancestor worship.

He is a national god of the Merina people of the central highlands. A missionary account records Malagasy saying that he made people's hands and feet, then left them to themselves.
zh:
扎纳哈里是马达加斯加信仰中人格化的天空与至高神，通常被想象为男性。他与大地神拉托万塔尼共同创造了人类：人死后灵魂升向苍穹，身体回归大地，因此他与灵魂和祖先崇拜关系密切。

他是中部高地梅里纳人的民族神。一份传教士的记录说，马达加斯加人讲述他造出人的手脚之后便离去，任凭人类自行生活。

official_raw.en: $zanahary_god$ creator god and sky father of the [ShowReligionAdjective('fomba_gasy_religion')] pantheon.

en:
Zeus was the son of Cronus and Rhea and the supreme god of the ancient Greeks. He was honoured as a sky father: even gods who were not his children called him Father. His symbols were the thunderbolt and the eagle, and he was married to Hera.

Greek worship had long died out by 1337. In the fifteenth century the philosopher Plethon placed Zeus at the head of his proposed pagan order.
zh:
宙斯是克洛诺斯与瑞亚之子，古希腊人的至高神。他被尊为天父，就连并非他亲生的神也称他为父亲。他的象征是雷霆和鹰，妻子是赫拉。

到1337年，希腊人的旧信仰早已消亡。15世纪，哲学家卜列东在他设想的异教秩序中，把宙斯置于首位。

official_raw.en: [ShowGodNameWithNoTooltip('zeus_god')] is the king of the Olympian gods, ruler of the sky, thunder, law, and cosmic order.
official_raw.zh: [ShowGodNameWithNoTooltip('zeus_god')]是奥林波斯诸神的神王，天空、雷霆、律法和宇宙秩序的统治者。

en:
Ahobilam was a pilgrimage town in the Nallamala hills of Andhra Pradesh and the chief centre of worship of Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu. Nine shrines line a steep gorge at Upper Ahobilam, while Lower Ahobilam holds the Prahladavarada temple, dedicated to his mild form. The Tamil saint Thirumangai Alvar praised the place in the ninth-century Periyatirumozhi, and it was counted among the 108 Divya Desams, the Vaishnava holy places.

The Kakatiya and Reddi dynasties patronised the shrines in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, followed by the Vijayanagara kings. Krishnadevaraya came on pilgrimage in the sixteenth century, and the Ahobila Matha monastic seat grew up around the same time.

After the decline of Vijayanagara the temple was sacked in 1579 by Murahari Rao, a commander of the Golconda Sultanate, who carried its jewelled idol away.
zh:
阿霍比拉姆是安得拉邦纳拉马拉丘陵中的朝圣城镇，也是崇拜毗湿奴的人狮化身那罗辛哈的首要中心。上阿霍比拉姆的陡峭峡谷中排列着九座神龛，下阿霍比拉姆则有供奉其温和面相的帕拉拉达瓦拉达神庙。9世纪泰米尔圣徒蒂鲁芒盖·阿尔瓦尔在《佩里亚蒂鲁莫利》中赞颂此地，它被列为毗湿奴教一百零八座圣庙之一。

13至14世纪，卡卡提亚王朝和雷迪王朝曾资助这些神龛，随后毗奢耶那伽罗诸王继之。克里希纳德瓦拉亚于16世纪前来朝圣，阿霍比拉修道院也在这一时期兴起。

毗奢耶那伽罗衰落后，神庙于1579年遭到戈尔孔达苏丹国将领穆拉哈里·拉奥的洗劫，镶宝神像被掠走。

en:
Masjid al-Kazimiyya is a Twelver Shia mosque and shrine in the Kadhimiya suburb north of Baghdad. It stands on the Quraysh cemetery laid out with the Round City by the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur in 762.

The seventh Imam Musa al-Kadhim was buried there in 799 after his death in Abbasid custody, and his grandson the ninth Imam Muhammad al-Jawad followed him in 834. The two tombs gave the quarter its name and made it one of the holiest grounds of Shiism.

The Safavid Shah Ismail I rebuilt and adorned the shrine between 1502 and 1524. After the Ottomans took Baghdad in 1534, Suleiman the Magnificent added further ornament, and in 1611 Sultan Ahmed I granted hereditary custodianship of the shrine to the al-Jamali family.
zh:
卡济米耶圣陵是巴格达北郊卡济米耶区的十二伊玛目派清真寺与陵墓，其地本是762年阿拔斯王朝哈里发曼苏尔营建圆城时划出的古莱什墓地。

799年，第七任伊玛目穆萨·卡齐姆在阿拔斯人的囚禁中去世后安葬于此；834年，其孙第九任伊玛目穆罕默德·塔基·贾瓦德也葬在这里。两座圣墓使这片城区得名，也使它成为什叶派最神圣的场所之一。

萨法维王朝沙阿伊斯玛仪一世于1502—1524年重建并装饰了圣陵。1534年奥斯曼人攻占巴格达后，苏莱曼大帝又加以增饰；1611年，苏丹艾哈迈德一世将圣陵的世袭监护权授予贾马利家族。

en:
Tradition holds that Mark the Evangelist founded the church of Alexandria in the first century and was martyred there. The Council of Chalcedon in 451 split the ancient see in two: the patriarch Dioscorus was deposed for his Miaphysite teaching, the Copts kept their own non-Chalcedonian popes, and a Greek-speaking minority formed the Melkite patriarchate.

After the Arab conquest of 642 both communities lived as dhimmis. In 828 or 829 Venetian merchants smuggled the body of Saint Mark, minus the head, to Venice. In the eleventh century the Coptic popes moved their residence from Alexandria to Cairo.

Under Mamluk rule, attacks in 1321 destroyed churches and monasteries across Egypt, and the riots of 1354 drove mass conversions. Under Ottoman rule the Copts faced heavy taxation and Catholic missionary pressure, while the Greek patriarchate survived as a small community.
zh:
相传福音书作者马可于1世纪创立亚历山大教会并在此殉道。451年的迦克墩公会议把这座古老牧座一分为二：牧首狄奥斯库若因基督合性派主张被废，科普特人保留了自己的非迦克墩教宗，希腊语少数派则组成麦勒基牧首区。

642年阿拉伯征服后，两个群体都作为迪米人生活。828或829年，威尼斯商人把圣马可的遗体（头部除外）偷运往威尼斯。11世纪科普特教宗们把驻地从亚历山大迁往开罗。

马穆鲁克统治下，1321年的袭击摧毁了埃及各地的教堂和修道院，1354年的暴乱引发大规模改宗。奥斯曼统治下科普特人承受重税和天主教传教的压力，而希腊牧首区作为小社群存续。

en:
Alexandria, on the Egyptian coast, was founded in 331 BC by Alexander the Great and became the capital of the Ptolemaic kingdom, famed for the Pharos lighthouse and the Great Library. It was also a chief city of early Christianity and the seat of one of the five patriarchates.

Its Catechetical School, led by Clement of Alexandria and later by Origen, made the city a center of biblical theology. Gnostic teaching also took root here: Basilides taught his dualist doctrines between roughly 117 and 161, and his followers remained active in the Nile Delta into the late fourth century.

Arab forces under Amr ibn al-As took Alexandria in 641 after a fourteen-month siege. It passed to the Ottomans in 1517 and regained some of its trade after the Mahmoudiyah Canal linked it to the Nile in 1820.
zh:
亚历山大位于埃及海岸，公元前331年由亚历山大大帝建立，后来成为托勒密王国的首都，以法罗斯灯塔和大图书馆闻名。它也是早期基督教的主要城市之一，是五大牧首区之一的所在地。

城中的教理学校由亚历山大的克雷芒主持，后来又由俄利根领导，使亚历山大成为圣经神学中心。灵知派教义也在此扎根：巴西里德约于117—161年传授他的二元论学说，其追随者在尼罗河三角洲一直活动到4世纪末。

641年阿姆鲁·本·阿斯率领阿拉伯军队围攻十四个月后拿下亚历山大。1517年它转入奥斯曼帝国手中，1820年马赫穆迪亚运河将城市与尼罗河连通后，它的贸易地位有所恢复。

en: The Amamangalam Maha Vishnu Temple at Kakkur in Kerala's Kozhikode district houses Vishnu in his tortoise avatar, worshipped as Kurmavataram. Local legend counts it among the major Dashavatara temples of the Malabar coast consecrated by the warrior-sage Parashurama, who in the Keralolpathi reclaimed Kerala from the sea.
zh: 阿马曼加拉姆摩诃毗湿奴神庙位于喀拉拉邦科泽科德县卡库尔，供奉毗湿奴的龟化身“俱利摩下凡”。当地传说把它列为马拉巴尔海岸的十化身大庙之一，相传由圣仙持斧罗摩亲自开光；据《喀拉拉源流》所载，持斧罗摩曾投斧入海，从波涛中辟出喀拉拉之地。

en:
The Anantheshwara Temple at Udupi, in Tulu Nadu on the south-western coast, is dedicated to Parashurama, the axe-wielding avatar of Vishnu, worshipped here as a linga on a silver seat.

Legends tell how Parashurama is said to have reclaimed the land from the sea and King Ramabhoja venerated him here; Sanskrit texts call the town Rajata Pitha, the silver seat. The shrine was founded around the 700s under the Alupa dynasty and was among the oldest temples of Tulu Nadu.

Madhvacharya (traditionally 1238-1317), founder of the Dvaita school of Vedanta, composed many of his Tattvavada works in the temple and taught his disciples here. The temple later came under the Puttige Matha, one of the eight monastic orders of Udupi, whose Madhva Brahmins conducted its rituals according to Madhvacharya's ordinances.
zh:
阿南特什瓦拉神庙位于西南海岸图卢纳德地区的乌度比，供奉毗湿奴持斧化身持斧罗摩；他以银座之上的林伽形象受人敬拜。

传说持斧罗摩从大海中索回这片土地，国王罗摩博阇曾在此敬拜他；梵文典籍把这座城市称为罗阇塔皮塔，意为银座。神庙约建于8世纪阿卢帕王朝治下，是图卢纳德最古老的神庙之一。

吠檀多二元论学派的创立者摩陀婆阿阇梨（传统纪年1238—1317年）在庙中写下多部真实论著作，并向弟子讲道。神庙后来归入乌度比八大道场之一的普蒂盖摩特管辖，该道场的摩陀婆婆罗门依照摩陀婆阿阇梨制定的仪轨主持祭祀。

en:
The Mosque of the Andalusians stands in Fes el-Bali, the old medina of Fez, in the quarter settled by refugees from Cordoba who fled to Morocco in 818 after a failed uprising. It was founded in 859 or 860 by Maryam al-Fihri, with money from the Andalusi families whose name it bears.

In 933 the Fatimid governor of Fez transferred the Friday sermon to it, making it the chief mosque of the Andalusian quarter. The building was almost entirely reconstructed between 1203 and 1207 on the orders of the Almohad caliph Muhammad al-Nasir, who added the northern gate and a water channel feeding its ablutions house.

Marinid sultans kept up the work: Abu Ya'qub Yusuf repaired it in 1295, and Abu Sa'id Uthman III founded its library in 1415, confirming it as the second mosque of Fez after the Qarawiyyin mosque.
zh:
安达卢西亚人清真寺位于非斯老城巴利区，所在街区聚居着818年科尔多瓦起义失败后逃到摩洛哥的难民。859年或860年，麦尔彦·菲赫里修建了这座清真寺，安达卢西亚难民家庭也出资相助，清真寺便由他们得名。

933年，非斯的法蒂玛王朝总督把周五讲道移到这里，使它成为安达卢西亚人区的主麻清真寺。1203—1207年，穆瓦希德哈里发穆罕默德·纳西尔下令几乎将全寺重建，增修了北门和向净仪房供水的水道。

马林王朝的苏丹们继续经营：阿布·叶尔孤卜·优素福于1295年加以修缮，阿布·赛义德·奥斯曼三世于1415年敕建图书馆，使它成为非斯仅次于卡拉维因清真寺的第二大清真寺。

en:
Angamaly, in the Malabar hinterland behind Kochi, was the ecclesiastical heart of the Saint Thomas Christians. They hold that the Apostle Thomas landed at Muziris in 52 and founded seven churches along the Kerala coast before his martyrdom.

Under Patriarch Timothy I around 800 the community became the Province of India of the Church of the East, governed by bishops from Mesopotamia and a hereditary archdeacon. Their seat came to rest at Angamaly, which in 1565 gave its name to the renewed Archdiocese of India.

Mar Abraham, who died in 1597, was the last East Syriac prelate to rule the undivided community. Two years later the Portuguese-run Synod of Diamper suppressed his see and imposed the Latin rite. The reforms provoked the Coonan Cross Oath of 1653, after which the Saint Thomas Christians split between East and West Syriac traditions.
zh:
安加马利位于科钦后方的马拉巴尔内陆，是圣多马基督徒的教务中心。该群体相传使徒多马于52年在穆济里斯登陆，在喀拉拉沿海建立七座教堂，最后殉道。

约800年，牧首提摩太一世将这个社群组建为东方教会的印度教省，由美索不达米亚派遣的主教与世袭的总执事共同治理。主教驻地最终设在安加马利，1565年重建的印度总教区也以它命名。

1597年去世的马尔·亚伯拉罕是统治这个尚未分裂社群的最后一任东叙利亚教长。两年后，葡萄牙人主持的戴佩尔公会议取缔了他的牧座并强行推行拉丁礼仪。改革激起了1653年的“弯十字架誓约”，圣多马基督徒此后分裂，分别遵奉东叙利亚和西叙利亚传统。

en:
Angkor Wat was a vast temple complex at Yaśodharapura, the capital of the Khmer Empire. King Suryavarman II built it as his state temple dedicated to Vishnu and, most likely, as his own mausoleum; work began around 1122 and ended in 1150. Its moat, galleries and central towers reproduce Mount Meru, and unlike other Angkorian temples it faces west.

After the Chams sacked Angkor in 1178, Jayavarman VII restored the empire from nearby Angkor Thom, and Angkor Wat was gradually converted to Buddhist worship.

When Ayutthaya brought down the Khmer Empire in 1431 the temple was not abandoned: monks maintained its ponds, and seventeenth-century inscriptions record Japanese Buddhist pilgrims settling beside Khmer villagers, one of whom celebrated the Khmer New Year there in 1632. It remained a Theravada monastery long after the capital moved south.
zh:
吴哥窟是高棉帝国都城耶输陀罗补罗的巨型寺院建筑群。苏利耶跋摩二世将它建为供奉毗湿奴的国寺，很可能也是他自己的陵庙；工程约始于1122年，1150年完工。护城河、回廊与中央塔群象征须弥山，与其他吴哥寺院不同，它朝向西方。

1178年占城攻陷吴哥后，阇耶跋摩七世在附近的吴哥通王城复兴帝国，吴哥窟也逐渐转为佛寺。

1431年阿瑜陀耶灭亡高棉帝国后，寺院并未被废弃：僧人持续维护寺内池塘，17世纪的碑铭记载日本佛教巡礼者与高棉村民比邻而居，其中一人于1632年在此庆祝高棉新年。国都南迁之后很久，它仍是一座上座部寺院。

en:
The ancient patriarchate of Antioch, where disciples were first called Christians, was fractured by the Council of Chalcedon in 451. In 512 the Miaphysite Severus became patriarch, only to be deposed six years later; his Syriac followers were organized by the sixth-century bishop Jacob Baradaeus, after whom they were called Jacobites, while the Greek-speaking Melkites held the Chalcedonian patriarchate.

In 1165 Emperor Manuel I forced Prince Bohemond III to restore the Orthodox hierarchy, allowing Patriarch Athanasius I to reside at the cave Cathedral of Saint Peter. Mamluk conquests scattered both flocks: in 1293 the Syriac Orthodox patriarchs settled at Mor Hananyo monastery near Mardin, and in 1342 the Greek patriarch moved to Damascus.

The disputed election of Cyril VI Tanas split the Greek patriarchate in 1724. Pope Benedict XIII recognized his Catholic line in 1729 as the Melkite Greek Catholic Church.
zh:
安条克是古老的牧首区，门徒最早在此被称为“基督徒”，451年迦克墩公会议使其分裂。512年，基督合性派塞维鲁登位为牧首，六年后被废；他的叙利亚语信众由6世纪的主教雅各·巴拉德乌斯组织，因他得名“雅各派”，操希腊语的麦勒基派则掌握迦克墩派牧首区。

1165年曼努埃尔一世迫使博希蒙德三世恢复东正教教阶，牧首亚他那修一世得以入驻洞穴式的圣伯多禄主教座堂。马穆鲁克征服打散两支会众：1293年叙利亚正教牧首定居马尔丁附近的哈南约修道院；1342年，希腊牧首迁往大马士革。

1724年西里尔六世·塔纳斯的选举之争使希腊牧首区分裂。教宗本笃十三世于1729年承认其天主教一脉为麦勒基希腊天主教会。

en:
Antioch, on the Orontes River in northern Syria, was founded around 300 BC by Seleucus I Nicator and served as the Seleucid capital. One of the earliest strongholds of Christianity, it was where the New Testament records that the followers of Jesus were first called Christians; Saint Peter is said to have preached in its cave church.

Paul of Samosata, patriarch from 260 to 268, taught an adoptionist, nontrinitarian doctrine, and later Byzantine writers linked the Paulician sect to his name. Constantine began the Great Church in 327.

Arab armies took Antioch in 637 and the Byzantines recovered it in 969. The First Crusade captured it in 1098 after an eight-month siege and made it the seat of the Principality of Antioch. Mamluk forces under Baibars sacked it in 1268, ending Latin power in northern Syria; the Ottomans absorbed it in 1516.
zh:
安条克位于叙利亚北部的奥龙特斯河畔，约公元前300年由塞琉古一世·尼卡托建立，曾为塞琉古都城。它是基督教早期重镇，《新约》记载耶稣的追随者最早在这里被称为基督徒；相传圣伯多禄曾在城中的洞穴教堂讲道。

260—268年任牧首的萨摩萨塔的保禄主张嗣子论的非三位一体教义，后来的拜占庭作者把保禄派的名称与他联系起来。君士坦丁于327年动工修建大圣堂。

637年阿拉伯军队攻占该城，969年拜占庭将其收复。1098年第一次十字军围攻八个月后攻下该城，使它成为安条克公国的中心。1268年拜巴尔斯率领马穆鲁克军队洗劫城市，终结拉丁势力在叙利亚北部的统治；1516年奥斯曼帝国吞并安条克。

en:
Anuradhapura Maha Viharaya was the great Theravada monastery of Anuradhapura, the royal capital of ancient Sri Lanka. King Devanampiya Tissa founded it in the third century BCE, and its monks became the island's oldest and most orthodox Buddhist fraternity.

It long rivaled the Abhayagiri and Jetavana monasteries. The chronicle Mahavamsa records its demolition under King Mahasena in the fourth century, though the Chinese pilgrim Faxian found three thousand monks there around 406. In the fifth century the scholar Buddhaghosa composed his Visuddhimagga and commentaries on the Tipitaka there, defining Theravada doctrine.

In the twelfth century King Parakramabahu I supported the Mahavihara, dissolved the rival fraternities and united the sangha under its lineage, which from Sri Lanka went on to shape the Theravada Buddhism of Southeast Asia.
zh:
阿㝹罗陀补罗寺是古代斯里兰卡王都阿努拉德普勒的上座部大寺，由天爱帝须王于公元前3世纪创建，寺中僧人组成岛上最古老、最严守传统的佛教僧团。

它长期与无畏山寺、祇园寺鼎立。《大史》记载它在4世纪被摩诃斯那王拆毁，但中国求法僧法显约在406年见到寺中仍有三千僧人。5世纪，学者觉音在此撰写《清净道论》和三藏注疏，奠定了上座部佛教的教义体系。

12世纪，波罗迦罗摩巴忽一世支持大寺，取缔对立僧团，将僧伽统一在大寺法脉之下；这一法脉又从斯里兰卡传出，塑造了东南亚的上座部佛教。

en:
The Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple stands on the southern bank of the Pamba River in central Kerala and honours Krishna as Parthasarathy, the charioteer of Arjuna in the Mahabharata. It is one of the five ancient Pandava shrines of the Chengannur region; Arjuna is said to have built this one to atone for slaying the unarmed Karna. The place takes its name from the bamboo raft, made of six pieces, that carried its image to the site.

Counted among the hundred and eight Divya Desams, Vishnu temples glorified by the Tamil Alvar saints, it is built in the Kerala style and preserves wall paintings from the early 1700s.

It guards the golden Thanka Anki vestment of Ayyappan, presented by the rulers of Travancore and carried each year to Sabarimala; its riverside steps host the Aranmula snake-boat race every Onam season.
zh:
阿兰穆拉的阿周那之御者神庙坐落在喀拉拉中部潘巴河南岸，供奉《摩诃婆罗多》中担任阿周那御者的奎师那，即“帕塔萨拉斯瓦米”。它是琴加努尔一带五座古老的般度族神庙之一，相传本庙为阿周那忏悔诛杀手无寸铁的迦尔纳之罪而建。地名源于运送神像的六根竹筏。

该庙被列为一百零八座迪维亚·德萨姆之一，即泰米尔阿尔瓦尔派圣徒歌颂的毗湿奴神庙，采用喀拉拉建筑风格，庙墙保存着18世纪初的壁画。

庙中珍藏着阿亚潘的金衣“坦加安吉”，由特拉凡哥尔王公奉献，每年送往萨巴里马拉；河边石阶则在每年欧南节期间举办阿兰穆拉蛇船赛。

en:
The Arasavalli Sun Temple is a shrine of Surya, the sun god, in Arasavalli on the northern coast of Andhra Pradesh. Wall inscriptions ascribe its founding to Devendra Varma of the Eastern Ganga dynasty of Kalinga in the 600s CE, making it one of the oldest surviving sun temples in India.

The Padma Purana credits the sage Kashyapa with installing the Surya image, while a local sthalapurana tells how Indra, struck blind by the sun god after an affront to Shiva's gatekeeper Nandi, regained his sight by worshipping the icon here.

The temple is built in the rekha deula form of Kalinga architecture. It later fell into ruin and was reconstructed in 1778 by Elamanchili Pullaji Panthulu, with further repairs paid for by the Dusi family. At the Ratha Saptami festival, pilgrims greet the rising sun at the temple gate.
zh:
阿拉萨瓦利的太阳神庙供奉太阳神苏利耶，位于安得拉邦北部沿海的阿拉萨瓦利村。庙墙铭文记载，神庙由羯陵伽东恒伽王朝的提婆因陀罗·瓦尔摩于7世纪创建，是印度现存最古老的太阳神庙之一。

《莲花往世书》称迦叶波仙人安立了苏利耶像；当地的圣地往世书则讲述，因陀罗冒犯湿婆的守门神牛南迪，被太阳神灼瞎双眼，在此供奉神像后重获光明。

神庙采用羯陵伽建筑的雷卡德乌拉式，后来倾圮，1778年由埃拉曼奇利·普拉吉·潘图卢重建，杜西家族又捐资修缮。一年一度的拉特萨普塔米节上，香客们在庙门迎接初升的太阳。

en:
Armagh in Ulster is the ecclesiastical capital of Ireland and the seat of the archbishop who bears the title Primate of All Ireland. The hill above the town had been a pagan sanctuary, named Ard Mhacha, the height of Macha, after a Gaelic goddess, before Saint Patrick founded his principal church there in 445.

By the seventh century its monastery and school were foremost in northern Ireland, and in the early ninth century its scribes produced the Book of Armagh. Vikings first raided Armagh in 832, but the high king Brian Boru was buried there after Clontarf in 1014. A national synod confirmed Armagh's primacy in 1111.

The cathedral was rebuilt in 1268, but the Tudor conquest left the town in ruins by 1601. The church passed to the Protestant Church of Ireland, which rebuilt it under Archbishop Christopher Hampton.
zh:
阿尔斯特的阿马是爱尔兰的教会首府，驻节于此的大主教拥有全爱尔兰首席主教头衔。镇旁的山丘本是异教圣地，以盖尔女神玛查之名称为阿尔德·瓦卡，即玛查之丘；445年圣帕特里克在此建立主要教堂。

到7世纪，这里的修道院和学校已是爱尔兰北部首屈一指的学术中心。9世纪初抄写员完成《阿马书》。维京人于832年首次洗劫阿马，但至高王布赖恩·博鲁在1014年克朗塔夫战役后安葬于此；1111年的全国宗教会议确认了阿马的首席地位。

座堂于1268年重建，但都铎王朝的征服使该镇到1601年沦为废墟。教堂转入新教的爱尔兰教会手中，后由大主教克里斯托弗·汉普顿主持重建。

en:
The Artemision at Ephesus, on the coast of Ionia, was the great temple of Artemis and one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world. The marble temple begun around 550 BC by the architect Chersiphron and paid for by Croesus of Lydia made the sanctuary famous.

In 356 BC Herostratus burned it down to immortalise his name, an act that tradition placed on the night Alexander the Great was born. The Ephesians refused Alexander's offer to pay for its rebuilding; after his death in 323 BC they raised a larger temple with more than a hundred and twenty-seven columns.

Gothic raiders destroyed it in 262 AD. Worship of Artemis lingered until about 401, but the temple was never restored; by the later Middle Ages only foundations remained beside the village at Selçuk.
zh:
阿耳忒弥斯神庙位于爱奥尼亚海岸的以弗所，是供奉阿耳忒弥斯的大庙，也是古代世界七大奇迹之一。约公元前550年建筑师凯尔西弗龙主持、吕底亚国王克洛伊索斯出资兴建的大理石神庙，使圣地闻名。

公元前356年，赫洛斯特拉特为使自己的名字不朽而纵火烧庙，传说此事正发生在亚历山大大帝出生的当夜。以弗所人婉拒亚历山大出资重建的提议，在他于公元前323年去世后建起更宏伟的新庙，立柱超过一百二十七根。

262年哥特袭掠者摧毁了神庙。对阿耳忒弥斯的崇拜延续到约401年，神庙却再未修复，到中世纪后期只剩下地基，旁侧是塞尔丘克的聚落。

en:
The Arulmigu Koniamman Temple lies on the northern bank of the Noyyal River in Coimbatore, in Kongu Nadu, and is dedicated to Koniamman, a form of Parvati honoured as the city's guardian goddess. Local tradition derives both goddess and place from the chieftain Kovan: his tutelary deity Koyamma became Koniamman, while his settlement Koyampuththoor grew into Coimbatore.

Kovan's descendants are said to have built the shrine in the 1000s; Tamil sources instead credit the Irula forest people with raising it around the 1200s. After the rule of those tribal chiefs the temple declined, until in the 1700s a king of Mysore restored it and installed the goddess in her Mahishasura Mardini form, the slayer of the buffalo demon.
zh:
阿卢利弥具‑拘尼阎曼神庙位于孔古纳德地区哥印拜陀的诺伊尔河北岸，供奉帕尔瓦蒂的化身拘尼阎曼，她被尊为城市的守护女神。当地传说把女神和城市的由来都系于首领科万：他供奉的保护神科亚姆玛演变为拘尼阎曼，而他的居留地科扬普图尔发展为哥印拜陀。

相传此庙由科万后裔于11世纪建造；泰米尔资料则说它是13世纪前后伊鲁拉尔林中部族所建。部族首领的统治结束后神庙一度衰落，18世纪一位迈索尔国王将其重修，并以斩杀牛魔王的杜尔加形象安奉女神。

en:
The Temple of Jupiter Heliopolitanus at Baalbek, in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, was the greatest sanctuary of Roman Syria and the empire's largest temple dedicated to Jupiter. Baalbek had long been a cult centre of Baal Haddu, whom Romans equated with Jupiter.

After Augustus planted a colony there around 16 BC, work began on the temple and its Great Court, largely complete by AD 60. Its fifty-four Corinthian columns were nearly twenty metres tall, and the podium stood on the Trilithon, three blocks of about eight hundred tonnes each. Emperors consulted its oracle.

Earthquakes and Christian spoliation damaged the temple, and Justinian carried eight columns to Constantinople for Hagia Sophia. After the Arab conquest the ruins became fortifications, rebuilt by the Mamluk sultan Qalawun in the thirteenth century after a Mongol raid. Three columns collapsed in the earthquakes of 1759.
zh:
朱庇特·赫利奥波利斯神庙位于黎巴嫩贝卡谷地的巴勒贝克，是罗马叙利亚最宏伟的圣所，也是帝国境内献给朱庇特的最大神庙。巴勒贝克早就是巴阿勒·哈达的崇拜中心，罗马人将他等同于朱庇特。

约公元前16年奥古斯都在此建立殖民地后，巨庙及大庭院动工，公元60年左右主体落成。神庙的54根科林斯柱高近20米；台基建在三块巨石之上，每块重约800吨。历代皇帝来此求问神谕。

地震与基督徒的拆取损害了神庙，查士丁尼又将八根石柱运往君士坦丁堡修建圣索菲亚大教堂。阿拉伯征服后，废墟被纳入防御工事，蒙古军破坏之后，马穆鲁克苏丹嘉拉温于13世纪加以重修。1759年的地震震塌了三根石柱。

en:
Badrinath on the Alaknanda river in the Garhwal Himalayas is the northernmost of the four Char Dham shrines . Its black stone image of Vishnu as Badrinarayan sits beneath a badri tree. Lakshmi is said to have sheltered the meditating Vishnu as a badri, or jujube, tree, giving the shrine its name.

Tradition credits Adi Shankara with founding the pilgrimage in the ninth century, recovering its image from the Tapt Kund springs . Garhwal kings installed the image in the temple in the sixteenth century; after the earthquake of 1803 the King of Jaipur rebuilt much of it.

Snow closes the shrine for half the year, when the deity is notionally moved to the Narasimha temple at Jyotirmath and a ghee lamp left burning. In summer the annual fair drew pilgrims north from Haridwar.
zh:
伯德里纳特位于加瓦尔喜马拉雅山区的阿拉卡南达河畔，是印度教四大圣地中位置最北的一座。庙里黑石雕成的毗湿奴化身巴德里纳拉扬像坐于巴德里树下。传说吉祥天女曾化作巴德里树，即枣树，为入定的毗湿奴遮寒，神庙因此得名。

传统认为9世纪的阿迪·商羯罗开创了这场朝圣：他从塔普特昆德泉中找回神像。16世纪加瓦尔国王把神像迁入神庙；1803年地震后，斋浦尔王公主持重建了大部分庙宇。

大雪每年封山半年，期间神像被象征性地迎往焦蒂尔马特的那罗辛哈神庙，庙中留一盏酥油灯长明。夏季一年一度的节会吸引朝圣者从赫里德瓦尔北上。

en:
The patriarchal see of the Church of the East was fixed in 410 at the Council of Seleucia-Ctesiphon; the patriarch ruled from Kokhe in the Sasanian capital. When the caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad nearby in 762, the patriarch was compelled to move there, and the city became the heart of a church stretching from Mesopotamia to India, Central Asia and Tang China.

The Mongol sack of 1258 at first spared the Christians: Hulagu's wife Doquz Khatun interceded for them, and Patriarch Makkikha II was granted the caliphal palace as a church.

The Ilkhan Ghazan's conversion to Islam in 1295 ended this favor, and Timur's storm of Baghdad in 1401 shattered the community. In the fifteenth century the patriarchs withdrew to Alqosh near Mosul. The schism of 1552 produced a rival Chaldean Catholic line when Yohannan Sulaqa was consecrated in Rome; by 1830 two patriarchates had settled into lasting separation.
zh:
410年的塞琉西亚-泰西封公会议确立了东方教会的牧首座堂，牧首驻在萨珊首都的科赫区。762年哈里发曼苏尔在附近兴建巴格达后，牧首被迫迁入新城，巴格达成为教会的核心，教会从美索不达米亚延伸到印度、中亚乃至唐代中国。

1258年蒙古人攻陷巴格达时，基督徒起初得以幸免：旭烈兀之妻脱古思可敦为他们求情，牧首马基哈二世获赐哈里发宫殿作为教堂。

1295年伊尔汗合赞改宗伊斯兰教，这种优待随之终结；1401年帖木儿攻破巴格达，社群受到重创。15世纪间牧首们退居摩苏尔附近的阿尔科什。1552年的大分裂产生了竞争的迦勒底天主教一脉，约哈南·苏拉卡在罗马受祝圣；到1830年，两个牧首体系形成了持久并立的局面。

en:
The Bajreshwari Mata Temple stands at Kangra, the hill fortress town of Nagarkot in the Punjab Himalayas, seat of the Katoch Rajput kings of Trigarta. Its goddess Vajreshwari, whose name means Lady of the Thunderbolt, is a fierce form of Durga who is said to have slain the demon Kalikala with a divine vajra.

The shrine is among the fifty-one Shakta Pithas, for tradition places the falling of Sati's left breast here. The temple, reputedly wealthy, drew pilgrims and plunderers: Mahmud of Ghazni is said to have sacked it in 1009, though Kangra fort was regarded as impregnable until the Mughal emperor Jahangir took it in 1622.

The Katoch rajas recovered the fortress after his death. Gurkha troops seized it in 1806, a Sikh-Katoch alliance retook it in 1809, and Ranjit Singh annexed Kangra in 1810.
zh:
婆折丽湿伐梨神庙坐落于旁遮普喜马拉雅山区的冈格拉，即古称讷格尔果德的山城要塞，特里加尔塔的卡托奇拉杰普特诸王以此为都。主神伐折丽湿伐梨之名意为金刚杵女神，是难近母的忿怒化身，相传以神赐金刚杵诛杀恶魔迦里迦罗。

该庙位列五十一处性力佩特，传说萨蒂的左乳坠落于此。神庙久负富庶之名，既吸引朝圣者也招来劫掠：据说伽色尼的马哈茂德于1009年洗劫此庙，而冈格拉要塞被视为坚不可破，直到1622年才被莫卧儿皇帝贾汉吉尔攻克。

他死后卡托奇王公收复要塞。廓尔喀军队于1806年占据此地，锡克与卡托奇联军在1809年将其夺回，兰吉特·辛格于1810年吞并冈格拉。

en:
The Bhu Varaha Swamy Temple at Srimushnam in northern Tamil Nadu is dedicated to Vishnu's boar avatar Varaha, seated with Lakshmi as Ambujavalli Thayar. Legend says Varaha slew the asura Hiranyaksha here, and that his sweat formed the temple tank Nithya Pushkarani; the central icon turns its boar face south toward the fallen demon while its human body faces the worshippers.

Chola inscriptions record gifts by Virarajendra Chola in 1068 and a village granted by Kulothunga Chola I around 1100. The Vijayanagara emperors added the seven-storey gateway, and their vassals the Thanjavur Nayaks rebuilt and expanded the temple. Achuthappa Nayak, who ruled from 1560 to 1614, raised the sixteen-pillared Purushasuktha Mandapa.

The temple became a stronghold of Madhva teaching: Madhvacharya repeatedly stayed here and kept his four-month vows on the site, and later saints including Vyasatirtha and Raghavendra Tirtha also resided here.
zh:
布筏罗诃斯瓦米神庙位于泰米尔纳德邦北部斯里穆什纳姆，供奉毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃，吉祥天女以安布贾瓦利·塔亚尔之名同祀。传说筏罗诃在此诛杀阿修罗王金目，他的汗水汇成尼提亚·普什卡拉尼圣池；主像猪脸朝南望向伏诛的妖魔，人形身躯面向信众。

铭文记载1068年毗罗罗贞陀罗·朱罗的布施，以及约1100年俱卢通伽·朱罗一世献上的村庄。毗奢耶那伽罗皇帝增建七层门楼，藩属坦贾武尔纳亚克王朝重建扩建神庙。1560—1614年在位的阿丘塔帕·纳亚克修建了十六柱的原人颂柱厅。

神庙成为摩陀婆派的重镇：摩陀婆阿阇梨多次驻锡，守四月安居誓，毗阿萨提尔塔、罗伽文德拉提尔塔等圣徒也居停于此。

en:
The Biraja Temple at Jajpur, called Jajnagar in Muslim chronicles, is the ancient shrine that gave the place its older name of Biraja Kshetra, the field of the goddess Viraja. Tantric texts teach that the navel of Sati fell here in the old Utkala kingdom.

The present Deula-style temple was raised around the 1000s, though Jajpur had been a capital under the Somavanshi king Yayati Keshari from 473 and later under the Buddhist Bhauma-Kara dynasty of the 700s. The town remained a centre of Tantric worship.

Its two-armed Durga spears Mahishasura while pulling his tail, one foot on her lion and the other on the buffalo demon. A sacred well named Nabhi Gaya draws pilgrims for rites for the dead, and an annual sixteen-day Durga Puja culminates in the animal sacrifice of Bali Dana.
zh:
毗罗阇神庙位于贾贾普尔，穆斯林编年史称其为贾杰纳加尔；这座古庙使该地得旧名毗罗阇之野，意为女神毗罗阇的领域。密典记载萨蒂的肚脐落在古乌特卡拉王国的此处。

现存德乌拉风格建筑约建于1000年代，而贾贾普尔自473年起便是索马万什国王耶耶迪·凯沙里的王都，700年代又为佛教婆摩-迦罗王朝的都城。这座城镇始终是密教崇拜的中心。

庙中双臂难近母一足踏狮、一足踩水牛魔，一手持矛刺向摩西沙修罗、一手拽其尾巴。圣井脐伽耶吸引信众前来举行超度先人的仪式；每年长达十六天的难近母节以兽祭巴利达那收尾。

en:
Bodh Gaya on the Phalgu River in Magadha, known as Uruvela in the Buddha's lifetime, is where Siddhartha Gautama, after six years of asceticism and rice milk offered by the village woman Sujata, sat beneath a sacred fig tree, found the Middle Way and attained enlightenment. The tree became the Bodhi Tree. Nearby shrines recall the seven weeks he spent in the area after enlightenment.

The Chinese pilgrims Faxian in the 400s and Xuanzang in the 600s recorded a thriving monastic centre. From the 1000s to the 1200s the Pithipati rajas of Magadha protected it.

Turkic invasions around the end of the 1100s shattered that Buddhist world, and the ruined site passed centuries in obscurity. The name Bodh Gaya came into use in the 1700s, while pilgrims from Sri Lanka, Tibet, Nepal and Myanmar kept its memory alive.
zh:
菩提伽耶位于摩揭陀的帕尔古河畔，佛陀在世时称优楼频螺。悉达多·乔达摩在此经历六年苦行，又接受村女善生供养的乳糜，最后坐在神圣的榕树下证得中道、觉悟成佛。那棵树后称菩提树。周边圣迹对应他成道后在此停留的七周。

5世纪的法显与7世纪的玄奘都曾记载这座繁盛的僧院中心。11至13世纪，摩揭陀的皮蒂帕蒂王公守护此地。

12世纪末前后突厥人的入侵摧毁了这一佛教世界，荒废的遗址沉寂了数百年。菩提伽耶这一名称直到18世纪才通行，斯里兰卡、西藏、尼泊尔和缅甸的朝圣者维系着对圣地的记忆。

official_raw.en: The Mahābodhi Mahāvihāra marks the spot where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree. Originally built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BC, it has undergone several restorations over time. Its distinctive brick structure is one of the earliest examples of $buddhist_ADJ$ temple architecture in India.
official_raw.zh: 摩诃菩提大寺标志着释迦牟尼在菩提树下证悟成佛的所在地。它最初由阿育王于公元前3世纪建造，随着时间推移，已经经历了数次修复工程。其独特的砖结构属于印度$buddhist_ADJ$寺庙建筑最早期的范例之一。

en:
B'olon Yej Te' Naah, the House of the Nine Sharpened Spears, is the largest pyramid at Palenque, a Maya city-state in the Chiapas lowlands. It was raised as the funerary monument of K'inich Janaab' Pakal, who ruled Palenque from 615 to 683; his son K'inich Kan Bahlam II finished it shortly after 683.

Three tablets carry 617 glyphs chronicling Pakal's reign. A hidden stairway descends to the burial chamber, where the king lay in a carved sarcophagus whose lid shows him sinking into the jaws of the underworld beneath the cosmic tree, wearing a jade mosaic death mask. Five sacrificed attendants were placed at the crypt's entrance.

Palenque's last dated monuments fall around 799. Within a generation the city collapsed and the jungle closed over the temple, its hidden burial chamber left undisturbed beneath the roots.
zh:
九锐矛铭文神庙意为九支磨尖长矛之屋，是恰帕斯低地玛雅城邦帕伦克最大的金字塔。它是为615—683年统治帕伦克的金尼奇·贾纳布·巴加尔修建的陵墓，其子金尼奇·坎·巴拉姆二世在683年稍后完工。

庙内三块铭文板刻有617个象形文字，记述巴加尔的统治。一条隐秘阶梯通往墓室，国王安卧于雕刻石棺之中，棺盖刻画他在宇宙树下沉入冥界之口的形象，脸上戴着玉片镶嵌的死亡面具。墓室入口还殉葬了五名侍从。

帕伦克最后的纪年碑刻约在799年。此后不出一代人城邦便告崩溃，丛林吞没了神庙，隐秘的墓室在树根之下未被惊扰。

en:
Borobudur is a ninth-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in the Kedu Plain of Central Java, raised under the Sailendra dynasty. Its nine platforms climb to a central dome ringed by seventy-two Buddha statues inside perforated stupas; among its 2,672 relief panels, 1,460 narrative scenes guide pilgrims upward toward enlightenment.

Inscriptions of 824 and 842 record the inauguration and endowment of the sanctuary, which fused the Buddhist path to nirvana with older Javanese ancestor veneration. By the fourteenth century, as the courts of Java turned to Islam, the temple was abandoned and slowly buried under volcanic ash and jungle.

The court poet Mpu Prapanca still mentioned a holy place at Budur in 1365. In 1814 the British administrator Thomas Stamford Raffles, told of its location by local people, ordered the site cleared and surveyed.
zh:
婆罗浮屠寺是9世纪的大乘佛教寺院，坐落在中爪哇的克杜平原，由夏连特拉王朝建成。九层平台之上是中央穹顶，周围环绕着72尊镂空佛塔中的佛像；2672块浮雕板中有1460块叙事浮雕，引导朝圣者拾级而上，走向觉悟。

824年和842年的铭文记载了这座圣所的落成与赐地，它把佛教的涅槃之道与爪哇古老的祖先崇拜融为一体。14世纪，随着爪哇诸宫廷改宗伊斯兰教，寺院被弃置，逐渐被火山灰和丛林掩埋。

宫廷诗人普拉潘查在1365年仍提到布杜尔有一处圣地。1814年，英国殖民官员托马斯·斯坦福德·莱佛士从当地人口中得知其位置，下令清理和勘测遗址。

en:
The Brihadisvara Temple, named Rajarajesvaram by its founder and called the Big Temple of Thanjavur, stands on the south bank of the Cauvery. It was the supreme monument of Chola architecture, praised as the Dakshina Meru, the Meru mountain of the south.

The Chola emperor Rajaraja I built it of granite between 1003 and 1010, raising a towering vimana above a sanctum holding one of India's largest lingams. Its walls carry Chola frescoes and the bronze Nataraja, Shiva as lord of the dance, first cast for this shrine.

After the Chola age the temple suffered in wars between the sultans of Madurai and the Hindu rulers of Thanjavur. The Nayakas of the 16th and 17th centuries added the Parvati, Murugan and Nandi shrines and fort-like walls; the Maratha kings of Thanjavur later kept the temple in repair.
zh:
婆利诃地湿伐罗神庙由建造者命名为罗阇罗阇湿婆罗，俗称坦贾武尔大庙，位于高韦里河南岸。它是朱罗建筑的最高典范，被誉为南方的须弥山。

朱罗皇帝罗阇罗阇一世于1003—1010年间以花岗岩建成此庙，高耸的维马纳塔楼下供奉着印度最大的林伽之一。庙壁存有朱罗壁画和舞王纳塔罗阇铜像，即湿婆舞蹈之主的形象，最初为这座神庙铸造。

朱罗时代之后，神庙在马杜赖苏丹与坦贾武尔印度教王公的战争中受损。16至17世纪的纳亚克诸王增建帕尔瓦蒂、穆卢干和南迪神祠，并修筑堡垒般的围墙；其后的坦贾武尔马拉塔国王持续维护神庙。

en:
Burgos Cathedral, dedicated to the Virgin Mary, stands in the former royal capital of Castile on the pilgrim road to Santiago de Compostela. Burgos became a bishopric in 1075 under Alfonso VI, succeeding the older Visigothic see of Oca, and a first Romanesque cathedral was finished there in 1096.

The present Gothic church was begun in 1221, when King Ferdinand III and Bishop Maurice laid the first stone; a French master builder modelled it on the cathedrals of Paris and Reims, and it was consecrated in 1260.

In the fifteenth century Juan de Colonia raised the openwork spires of the west front; the lantern dome and Chapel of the Constable followed in the late fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Eighteenth-century sacristies and chapels completed the ensemble.
zh:
布尔戈斯主教座堂奉圣母马利亚为主保，坐落在卡斯蒂利亚旧日的王都，正处在前往圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉的朝圣路上。1075年，阿方索六世设立布尔戈斯主教区，承接更古老的西哥特奥卡教区；第一座罗马式主教座堂于1096年落成。

现存的哥特式教堂始建于1221年，由国王费尔南多三世和主教莫里斯共同安放奠基石，一位法国建筑师以巴黎和兰斯主教座堂为蓝本设计，教堂于1260年祝圣。

15世纪，胡安·德·科洛尼亚竖起西立面镂空的双塔尖；15世纪末至16世纪又增建灯笼式穹顶和治安官小堂。18世纪添建的圣器室和小堂为整组建筑收尾。

en:
Canterbury Cathedral in Kent is the seat of the archbishop of Canterbury, the foremost prelate of the English Church. It was founded in 597 by Augustine, leader of the Gregorian mission.

After the Norman Conquest the cathedral was rebuilt between 1070 and 1077 under Archbishop Lanfranc, and rebuilt again in the Gothic style after a fire in 1174. Its greatest claim to sanctity was the shrine of Thomas Becket, the archbishop murdered before the altar by knights of Henry II in 1170; pilgrims flocked to it for the next three and a half centuries. In 1538 Henry VIII dissolved the priory and destroyed Becket's shrine during the English Reformation, though the cathedral church itself survived.
zh:
位于肯特的坎特伯雷座堂是坎特伯雷大主教的驻节地，而大主教是英格兰教会地位最高的教士。597年，格里高利传教团首领奥古斯丁建立了这座座堂。

诺曼征服后，座堂于1070—1077年间在大主教兰弗朗克主持下重建，1174年火灾后又按哥特风格重建。它最负盛名的圣迹是托马斯·贝克特圣龛：这位大主教于1170年被亨利二世的骑士杀死在祭坛前，此后三个半世纪里朝圣者纷至沓来。1538年，亨利八世在英格兰宗教改革中解散了附属修道院并捣毁贝克特圣龛，不过座堂建筑本身得以保存。

en:
The Capitolium was the greatest temple of the Roman state, on the Capitoline Hill above the Forum, housing Jupiter, Juno and Minerva. Traditionally dedicated in 509 BC, the first year of the Republic, its foundations yielded a human head read as a promise that Rome would head a great empire.

The wooden temple burned in 83 BC, taking the Sibylline Books with it; the replacement, dedicated in 69 BC, reused columns Sulla had carried off from Athens. After murdering Caesar in 44 BC, Brutus and the conspirators barricaded themselves within it. Fire destroyed it again in 69 and 80 AD; Vespasian and then Domitian rebuilt it.

Theodosius I closed it in 392; the Vandals stripped its bronze tiles in 455. The last ruins were demolished in the sixteenth century when the Palazzo Caffarelli was raised over the podium.
zh:
卡庇托林神庙是罗马国家最崇高的神庙，雄踞广场上方的卡庇托林山，供奉朱庇特、朱诺和密涅瓦三神。传统上认为它于公元前509年、即共和国建立的第一年落成；奠基时挖出的人头被解读为罗马将成为帝国之首的预兆。

木构神庙于公元前83年失火，寄存其中的《西卜林书》一同化为灰烬；重建的神庙于公元前69年落成，复用了苏拉从雅典掠来的石柱。公元前44年恺撒遇刺后，布鲁图斯等密谋者曾把自己关在庙中。神庙又于公元69年和80年两度焚毁，韦斯巴芗和图密善先后重建。

392年，狄奥多西一世关闭神庙；455年汪达尔人剥走了铜瓦。16世纪，卡法雷利宫建在神庙台基之上，最后的残迹也被拆毁。

en:
The sanctuary of the Vera Cruz stands in the castle above Caravaca, near the old frontier with Granada, and guards a fragment believed to come from the True Cross.

Tradition places its origin in 1231 or 1232, when the captive missionary Gínes Pérez Chirinos was made to say Mass before the Muslim ruler Zeyt-Abuzeyt: as the priest lamented the lack of a crucifix, two angels were said to bring a cross down from heaven, and the ruler and his family converted and asked for baptism.

The relic, venerated as the double-barred Caravaca Cross flanked by angels, was guarded by the Knights Templar from 1266 and, after 1344, by the Order of Santiago. After 1492 Franciscan friars carried copies to the Americas. The medieval chapel was replaced by a Baroque basilica-sanctuary, built between 1617 and 1703.
zh:
真十字圣殿矗立在卡拉瓦卡城堡的高地上，邻近旧时与格拉纳达接壤的边地，堂内供奉着一块被认为取自真十字架的木片。

相传此事源于1231或1232年：被俘的传教士希内斯·佩雷斯被迫在穆斯林统治者宰特·阿布·宰特面前主持弥撒，正当神父叹息没有十字架时，两位天使自天而降送来十字架，统治者全家因而皈依并请求受洗。

这件圣物以双横杠、两侧有天使相伴的卡拉瓦卡十字造型受人敬拜，1266年起由圣殿骑士团守护，1344年后改由圣地亚哥骑士团看管。1492年之后，方济各会修士把复制品带到了美洲。中世纪小堂后来被一座巴洛克式圣殿取代，新堂建于1617—1703年。

en:
The Cave of the Patriarchs stands in the Old City of Hebron over the cave that the Book of Genesis says Abraham bought as a family tomb. Tradition holds it to contain the graves of Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, and Jacob and Leah.

The rectangular enclosure above it was raised by Herod the Great between 31 and 4 BCE. The Sasanian Persians sacked it in 614, and after the Arab conquest of 637 it was roofed and turned into a mosque.

Crusaders made it a church after taking Hebron in 1100, and in 1119 a monk reopened the buried cave and claimed to find the patriarchs' bones, drawing pilgrims of all three Abrahamic faiths. Saladin retook the city in 1188 and restored it as a mosque, in which form it passed through Mamluk and Ottoman rule.
zh:
列祖之洞位于希伯伦老城。据《创世记》记载，亚伯拉罕买下这里的岩洞作为家族墓地，相传洞中葬有亚伯拉罕与撒拉、以撒与利百加、雅各与利亚三对夫妇。

洞上的长方形围墙由大希律王于公元前31年至前4年修建。614年萨珊波斯人洗劫了此地，637年阿拉伯人征服后将其加盖屋顶、改为清真寺。

1100年十字军攻占希伯伦后把它改成教堂，1119年一名修士重新打开被掩埋的岩洞，声称发现列祖遗骨，吸引三大亚伯拉罕宗教的朝圣者。1188年萨拉丁收复该城，恢复其清真寺身份，此后它先后经历马穆鲁克和奥斯曼的统治。

en:
The Chamundeshwari Temple stands on the Chamundi Hills near Mysore in Karnataka, dedicated to Chamundeshwari, a form of Durga whom Mysore adopted as its tutelary goddess.

Hindu tradition holds that Durga slew the buffalo demon Mahishasura on this hill, and the demon's capital below came to be called Mahishuru, the name from which Mysore derives. The shrine is counted among the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas, said to mark where a lock of Sati's hair fell.

The original sanctum was built in the twelfth century under the Hoysala dynasty, its tower was probably raised by Vijayanagara rulers in the seventeenth century, and in 1659 a staircase of a thousand steps was cut up the hillside. Dodda Devaraja Wodeyar of Mysore installed the colossal granite Nandi on the path in 1664, and the Wodeyar maharajas remained the temple's chief patrons.
zh:
占闷提湿伐梨神庙位于卡纳塔克迈索尔附近的占蒙迪山，供奉杜尔迦的化身占蒙迪湿伐梨；迈索尔奉她为守护女神。

印度教传说杜尔迦在这座山上斩杀牛魔摩西沙修罗，山下魔王的都城因此得名摩西沙乌鲁，迈索尔之名即由此而来。该庙被列为十八处大性力圣地之一，相传萨蒂的一缕头发坠落于此。

圣所原建于12世纪曷萨拉王朝时期，高塔大概是17世纪毗奢耶那伽罗统治者所加；1659年山腰凿出千级石阶。1664年迈索尔的多达·提婆罗阇·沃德亚尔在山道上安置了巨型花岗岩神牛南迪像，此后沃德亚尔诸土邦主一直是神庙的主要供养人。

en:
The Changu Narayan Temple crowns a hilltop in Bhaktapur district east of Kathmandu in Nepal, and is dedicated to Vishnu in his Narayan form. Tradition places its foundation in the fourth century; a legend derives its name from Champak, daughter of a Kashmiri king given in marriage to a prince of Bhaktapur.

Its most treasured monument is a Sanskrit pillar inscription set up by the Lichhavi king Manadeva, who ruled from 464 to 505, one of the earliest surviving inscriptions in the country and a key source for early Nepalese history. The temple was repeatedly restored after fires and earthquakes, and its courtyards gathered metalwork, woodcarvings and sculptures spanning many centuries of Nepalese art.
zh:
昌古纳拉扬神庙坐落在尼泊尔加德满都以东巴克塔普尔县的山顶，供奉毗湿奴的纳拉扬相。传说其始建于4世纪；另有传说称庙名来自一位克什米尔国王嫁给巴克塔普尔王子的女儿占芭格。

庙中最珍贵的文物是梨查维王朝国王马纳提婆（464—505年在位）所立的梵文石柱铭文，这是尼泊尔现存最早的铭文之一，也是研究该国早期历史的关键史料。神庙历经多次火灾与地震后一再重修，院内汇集了尼泊尔艺术多个世纪的金属器、木雕与造像。

en:
Chartres, southwest of Paris, is the cathedral of Our Lady on a hill that has held a bishop's church since the fourth century. In 876 Charles the Bald presented the Sancta Camisa, held to be the Virgin Mary's tunic, and pilgrims began to converge on the town. Bishop Fulbert rebuilt after the fire of 1020 and made Chartres a leading cathedral school.

Fire struck again in 1194, leaving the crypt, towers and Royal Portal; the High Gothic cathedral rose between 1194 and 1220, with stained glass, flying buttresses and a floor labyrinth. It was reconsecrated in 1260 before King Louis IX.

During the French Revolution the church became state property and worship was suspended, but townspeople protected the sculpture and a local architect dissuaded the revolutionary committee from blowing the building up. It survived until services resumed under Napoleon.
zh:
沙特尔位于巴黎西南，城中的圣母大教堂建在一座山丘上，自4世纪起这里就设有主教教堂。876年秃头查理献上圣衣，相传是圣母玛利亚所穿的束腰外衣，朝圣者从此络绎而来。1020年火灾后，富尔贝主教重建教堂，并把沙特尔办成一流的主教学校。

1194年大火再临，仅存地下室、双塔与皇家门廊；盛期哥特式大教堂于1194—1220年建起，配有彩色玻璃窗、飞扶壁和地面迷宫。1260年教堂在路易九世面前重新祝圣。

法国大革命期间教堂收归国有、礼拜中止，但市民保护了雕塑，当地建筑师又劝阻革命委员会不要炸掉建筑。教堂得以保存，直到拿破仑时期恢复礼拜。

en:
The Chausath Yogini Temple at Hirapur, near Bhubaneswar in Orissa, is a circular, roofless tantric shrine devoted to the sixty-four yoginis, the goddess-like attendants of Durga. Local priests relate that Durga took the form of sixty-four demi-goddesses to overcome a demon and afterwards asked to be commemorated in a temple.

It was built around 864 by Queen Hiradevi of the Bhauma dynasty and is regarded as the oldest of India's few surviving Chausath Yogini temples. Its low sandstone ring has niches for sixty-four yogini images surrounding a central figure of Kali standing on a human head; fifty-six of the dark stone statues survive.

In the sixteenth century the temple is said to have been sacked and its images broken by Kalapahad, the Muslim convert general remembered as the destroyer of the Jagannath and Konark temples.
zh:
六十四瑜伽女神庙位于奥里萨布巴内斯瓦尔附近的希拉普尔，是一座圆形无顶的怛特罗神庙，供奉侍奉杜尔加的六十四位瑜伽女。当地祭司相传，杜尔加曾化身为六十四位女神击败恶魔，战后女神们要求立庙纪念。

此庙约于864年由博马王朝王后希拉德维主持修建，被视为印度现存为数不多的六十四瑜伽女庙中最古老的一座。低矮的砂岩环墙上有六十四尊瑜伽女像的壁龛，环绕着中央踩在人头上的迦梨女神像，现存56尊深色石像。

16世纪，改宗伊斯兰教的将领卡拉帕哈德据说曾劫掠此庙、打碎神像，他也以摧毁贾格纳特神庙和科纳克太阳神庙而闻名。

en:
The Chhinnamasta Temple at Rajrappa, in the Hazaribagh country of Jharkhand, is a Tantric pilgrimage centre dedicated to Chhinnamasta, the self-decapitated goddess counted among the ten Mahavidyas.

It sits on a hillock at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi rivers beside the Rajrappa falls, a setting read by Tantric worshippers as an image of the reversed union described in the goddess's meditation verse.

The object of worship is a natural rock sheathed in an eight-metal alloy cover; local tribes venerated the spot long before it became a Chhinnamasta centre by the 1700s, and pilgrims offer kheer and animal sacrifice. The main temple is surrounded by smaller shrines to the other Mahavidyas and to Surya, Hanuman and Shiva, and draws devotees from Bihar, Bengal and the Nepal hills as well as tribals who immerse ashes in the Damodar below.
zh:
献首女神庙位于贾坎德邦赫扎里巴克地区的拉杰拉帕，是一座怛特罗朝圣中心，供奉十大明妃之一、自行断首的女神旗那摩斯塔。

庙建在达莫达尔河与拜拉维河汇流处的小丘上，旁临拉杰拉帕瀑布，怛特罗信众把这一地势看作女神观想偈中逆向交合意象的体现。

受拜的神体是一块外包八金属合金罩的天然岩石；早在18世纪这里成为旗那摩斯塔信仰中心之前，当地部落已在此礼拜，香客供奉乳粥与杀牲献祭。主庙周围环绕着供奉其余明妃以及太阳神、哈奴曼、湿婆的小庙，香客来自比哈尔、孟加拉、尼泊尔山区，也有部民把骨灰撒入脚下的达莫达尔河。

en:
The Chintaman Ganesh Temple is the largest temple dedicated to Ganesha in Ujjain, the old Malwa city in Madhya Pradesh, standing on the Kshipra river. The image enshrined there is held to be swayambhu, self-manifested rather than consecrated by human hands, and Ganesha is worshipped under the name Chintaman, the remover of worries, flanked by his two consorts, Riddhi and Siddhi.

The stone building is dated to the 1000s and 1100s, when the Paramara dynasty ruled Malwa, while a local legend pushes its origins back to the age of the Ramayana and credits Sita with establishing the shrine. Its assembly hall is lined with finely carved stone pillars, and the sanctuary draws pilgrims seeking relief from their anxieties.
zh:
除障者伽内什神庙是中央邦摩腊婆古城乌贾因规模最大的伽内什神庙，坐落在希普拉河畔。庙中神像相传为自行显现的自生像，而非人工安立；伽内什在此以“钦塔曼”——意为消除忧虑者——之名受奉，两侧配祀他的两位配偶哩迪与悉迪。

这座石庙的历史可上溯至11—12世纪帕拉玛拉王朝统治摩腊婆之时，当地传说更把其渊源推到《罗摩衍那》时代，称神龛由悉多建立。庙内集会厅排列着雕工精细的石柱，神龛吸引着祈求解忧的香客前来。

en:
Cholollan, the place of refuge, was one of the holiest cities of central Mexico, and its pyramid was called Tlachihualtepetl, the hand-made mountain, by later Nahuatl speakers. Six building campaigns from the third century BC to the ninth century AD wrapped one adobe-brick pyramid inside another, producing the largest pyramid on earth by volume, facing the snow-capped volcano Iztaccihuatl.

The city may have held 100,000 people at its height, but in the eighth century the population collapsed and the pyramid was abandoned, though the devout went on burying their dead around it. In the twelfth century Toltec-Chichimeca invaders seized the city and built a temple to Quetzalcoatl elsewhere.

In 1594 the Spanish crowned the tree-covered monument with the church of Our Lady of Remedies, turning the sanctuary into a place of Catholic pilgrimage while native rites continued on its slopes.
zh:
乔卢兰意为避难之地，是墨西哥中部最神圣的城市之一；后世说纳瓦特尔语的人把城中的大金字塔称作特拉奇瓦尔特佩特尔，即人造之山。从公元前3世纪到公元9世纪，六次营建把一座土坯金字塔层层包裹在另一座之中，形成世界体积最大的金字塔，朝向积雪覆盖的伊斯塔西瓦特尔火山。

城市极盛时或有10万人口，但8世纪人口骤减，金字塔被弃置，信徒仍继续在周围安葬死者。12世纪托尔特克-奇奇梅卡入侵者夺取城市后，另择地点新建了一座魁札尔科亚特尔神庙。

1594年，西班牙人在树木丛生的金字塔顶建起雷梅迪奥斯圣母教堂，把圣所变为天主教朝圣地，而本土仪式仍在山坡上延续。

official_raw.en: The Great Pyramid of [ShowLocationName('cholollan')] was built in successive stages during hundreds of years. Dedicated to the deity [ShowGodName('quetzalcoatl_god')], it is the largest pyramid in the region. Even after the city's decline, it remained a sacred and cultural site for local inhabitants.
official_raw.zh: [ShowLocationName('cholollan')]大金字塔历经数百年分阶段建造而成，供奉羽蛇神[ShowGodName('quetzalcoatl_god')]，是该地区规模最宏大的金字塔建筑。即便在城市衰落后，它依然是当地居民心中的圣地与文化象征。

en:
Cologne, on the Rhine, has held a bishop's church since late Roman times; the Carolingian Hildebold Cathedral was consecrated in 870. In 1164 Archbishop Rainald of Dassel brought the relics of the Three Wise Men from Frederick Barbarossa's Milanese spoils; the gilded Shrine of the Three Kings drew pilgrims from across Europe.

To house it, Archbishop Konrad von Hochstaden laid the foundation stone of the Gothic cathedral in 1248. The choir was consecrated in 1322, but work ceased in 1473 with the south tower raised only to belfry level, its crane a landmark for centuries.

French revolutionary troops occupied Cologne in 1794; the cathedral served as a stable and warehouse, while the shrine was hidden and returned in 1804. Reduced to a parish church in 1803, the cathedral regained its rank in 1821 under Prussian patronage and became a symbol of German nationhood.
zh:
科隆位于莱茵河畔，自罗马时代晚期起就建有主教教堂；加洛林时代的希尔德博尔德主教座堂于870年祝圣。1164年，大主教达塞尔的赖纳尔德把东方三博士的圣骨带到科隆，它们是腓特烈·巴巴罗萨攻占米兰后的战利品；鎏金的三王圣龛吸引了全欧洲的朝圣者。

为安置圣龛，大主教康拉德·冯·霍希施塔登于1248年为哥特式主教座堂奠基。唱诗班席于1322年祝圣，但工程在1473年停顿，南塔只建到钟楼高度，塔上的起重机成为数百年来的城市标志。

1794年法国革命军队占领科隆，教堂被用作马厩和仓库，三王圣龛被藏起，1804年才迎回。1803年主教座堂被降为教区教堂，1821年在普鲁士扶持下恢复主教座堂地位，并成为德意志民族的象征。

en:
The see of Constantinople grew with the capital refounded by Constantine in 330; the council of 381 ranked its bishop second in honor only to Rome. Justinian's Hagia Sophia was consecrated in 537, and the breach with Rome opened there in 1054. Latin clergy held it under Crusader occupation from 1204 to 1261.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1453 turned Hagia Sophia into a mosque, Mehmed II in 1454 invested the monk Gennadius as patriarch and ethnarch of Orthodox Christians under the millet system. The Miaphysite Armenians received their own patriarchate in 1461 under Hovakim I, whose millet also embraced the Syriac Orthodox.

Moscow was recognized as a fifth patriarchate in 1589. The Greek throne moved in 1597 to Saint George in the Phanar, rebuilt after fires, while the Church of Greece broke away as autocephalous in 1833.
zh:
君士坦丁堡牧座随330年君士坦丁重建首都而兴起，381年的公会议将其主教位列罗马之后、尊荣第二。查士丁尼的圣索菲亚大教堂于537年祝圣，1054年与罗马的决裂在此拉开。1204—1261年十字军占领期间大堂由拉丁神职人员主持。

1453年奥斯曼征服后圣索菲亚被改为清真寺，穆罕默德二世于1454年立修士根纳迪乌斯为牧首，让他在米利特制度下担任东正教徒的民族领袖。基督合性派的亚美尼亚人于1461年获得自己的宗主教区，由霍瓦基姆一世主持，其米利特还统辖叙利亚正教会。

莫斯科于1589年被承认为第五个牧首区。希腊人的牧座1597年迁入法纳尔区的圣乔治教堂，该堂历经大火后重建，而希腊教会在1833年自立为自主教会。

en:
Constantinople, on the Bosporus between Europe and Asia, was refounded by Constantine in 330 on Byzantium and became the Byzantine capital. Its greatest shrine was Hagia Sophia.

A first Great Church was consecrated in 360, and after it burned the domed basilica was built under Justinian I between 532 and 537 as the patriarch's seat. In 1054 the papal envoy delivered there the excommunication that opened the East-West Schism, and from 1204 to 1261 Catholic clergy served the cathedral under the Latin Empire.

Paulician communities broken by imperial warfare were resettled in Thrace from the late ninth century, and in 970 John I Tzimiskes moved some two hundred thousand of them to the region of Philippopolis, where their dualist teaching helped feed the later Bogomil movement. When Ottoman troops stormed the city in 1453, Hagia Sophia was converted into a mosque.
zh:
君士坦丁堡地处欧亚之间的博斯普鲁斯海峡，330年由君士坦丁在拜占庭的基础上重建，成为拜占庭帝国的首都。城中最伟大的圣地是圣索菲亚大教堂。

360年首座大教堂祝圣启用，后来毁于火灾，穹顶巴西利卡由查士丁尼一世于532—537年修建，是牧首的座堂。1054年，教宗特使在此递交绝罚令，引发东西教会大分裂；1204—1261年拉丁帝国时期，大教堂由天主教神职人员主持。

9世纪末起，被帝国战争击垮的保禄派信众被陆续迁往色雷斯，970年约翰一世·齐米斯凯斯又将约二十万人迁到菲利普波利斯一带，他们的二元论教义后来滋养了鲍格米勒派运动。1453年奥斯曼军队攻陷城市后，圣索菲亚大教堂被改为清真寺。

en:
The Sanctuary of Daphne stood on a wooded plateau of springs and waterfalls south of Antioch. Seleucus I Nicator, founder of the Seleucid dynasty, built there the Daphneion, an Apollo temple housing a statue by the sculptor Bryaxis and a renowned oracle.

Further temples were raised to Zeus Olympios, Artemis, Aphrodite and Isis, and Antiochus IV held a military review at Daphne in 166 BC. Under Roman rule Titus built a theatre from the spoils of Jerusalem.

In 351 the Caesar Constantius Gallus placed a church holding the relics of Saint Babylas beside the temple. When the emperor Julian restored the shrine in 362 he blamed the relics for silencing the oracle and had them removed; days later fire destroyed the temple and statue, and the temple was never rebuilt. Khosrow I's Persian army sacked Daphne in 540, and after the Arab conquest of the seventh century the site was gradually abandoned.
zh:
达佛涅圣所位于安条克以南一处林木繁茂、遍布泉水与瀑布的高地上。塞琉古王朝的建立者塞琉古一世在此修建了供奉阿波罗的达佛涅翁神庙，庙内有雕刻家布拉克西斯制作的神像和一处著名神谕所。

此后这里又建起供奉奥林匹斯宙斯、阿尔忒弥斯、阿佛洛狄忒和伊西斯的神庙；公元前166年，安条克四世在达佛涅举行阅兵。罗马统治时期，提图斯用耶路撒冷战利品修建了剧场。

351年，副帝君士坦提乌斯·加卢斯在神庙旁修建了安放圣巴比拉遗骨的教堂。362年，重启圣所的尤利安皇帝认为遗骨使神谕缄默，下令迁走，然而数天后一场大火焚毁了神庙与神像，此后再未重建。540年，霍斯劳一世的波斯军队洗劫了达佛涅；7世纪阿拉伯征服后，这片圣地逐渐被废弃。

en:
Delos is an island at the centre of the Cyclades, held sacred as the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, whom Leto bore beneath Mount Cynthus. It was a pilgrimage centre of the Ionians. In 426 BC the Athenians removed the dead and forbade births and burials on the island, which hosted the Delian games.

After the Persian Wars it became the treasury of the Delian League, founded in 478 BC, until Pericles moved it to Athens in 454 BC. Rome made Delos a free port in 166 BC, and it grew into the busiest slave market in the eastern Mediterranean.

Assaults by the forces of Mithridates in 88 and 69 BC broke its prosperity. Trade shifted elsewhere, and by the second century AD Pausanias found only temple custodians on the island; it was abandoned altogether around the eighth century.
zh:
提洛岛是基克拉泽斯群岛中心的小岛，被尊为阿波罗与阿耳忒弥斯的诞生地——勒托在岛上的基斯诺斯山下生下这对孪生神。它最初是爱奥尼亚人的朝圣中心。公元前426年雅典人迁走岛上全部遗骸，并禁止在岛上出生和下葬，提洛运动会随后在此举办。

希波战争后，它成为公元前478年成立的提洛同盟的金库所在地，直到公元前454年伯里克利把金库迁往雅典。罗马于公元前166年将提洛辟为自由港，它发展成东地中海最繁忙的奴隶市场。

公元前88年和公元前69年米特拉达梯军队的两次进攻摧毁了它的繁荣。商路改道后，2世纪保萨尼阿斯见到的岛上只剩神庙看守人；约8世纪它被彻底放弃。

en:
Delphi was the sacred precinct of Apollo on Mount Parnassus in central Greece, and the seat of the Pythia, the Hellenic world's most authoritative oracle. The Greeks held it to be the centre of the earth, marked by the omphalos in Apollo's temple; myth told how the god slew the serpent Python.

On a tripod above the chasm the priestess delivered prophecies that shaped colonial ventures, laws and wars. City-states lined the Sacred Way with treasuries, the Athenian one commemorating Marathon in 490 BC; the Pythian Games were held every four years from 586 BC.

Sulla plundered the sanctuary in 86 BC and Nero in AD 66; it was closed under Theodosius I in 381. The antiquary Cyriacus of Ancona recorded its ruins in 1436, an earthquake did further damage in 1500, and Byron visited in 1809.
zh:
德尔斐是阿波罗的圣域，位于希腊中部的帕尔纳索斯山，也是皮提亚女祭司的驻地，即希腊世界最具权威的神谕所。希腊人认为这里是大地的中心，阿波罗神庙中的翁法罗斯石标示着这个中心；神话讲述阿波罗杀死了巨蛇皮同。

女祭司坐在裂隙上方的三足凳上传达预言，影响殖民建邦、立法征战。各城邦沿圣道修建宝库，雅典人的宝库即为纪念公元前490年的马拉松之战而建；皮提亚竞技会自公元前586年起每四年举行一次。

苏拉于公元前86年、尼禄于公元66年先后洗劫此地，圣域最终在381年狄奥多西一世治下被关闭。古物学家安科纳的奇里亚科于1436年记录了残存遗迹，1500年的地震又加破坏，拜伦在1809年到访。

en:
Deo Patan on the coast of Saurashtra is the site of the Somnath temple, the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva. Tradition says the moon god Soma bathed here to recover his radiance, giving the shrine its name Someshvara, lord of the moon.

The Chaulukya king Mularaja built the first stone temple before 997, but in 1026 Mahmud of Ghazni sacked it. The Chaulukya king Kumarapala rebuilt it around 1169, only for Ulugh Khan's army to sack it in 1299; the Chudasama king Mahipala rebuilt it in 1308 and his son Khengara reinstalled the lingam between 1331 and 1351.

Zafar Khan, the Delhi governor who founded the Gujarat Sultanate, destroyed it in 1395, Mahmud Begada desecrated it in 1451, and Aurangzeb ordered its demolition and conversion into a mosque in 1706. In the later eighteenth century Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore built a smaller shrine beside the ruins so that worship could continue.
zh:
德奥帕坦位于萨乌拉施特拉海岸，索姆纳特神庙坐落于此，是湿婆十二处究提林迦中的第一处。相传月神苏摩曾在此沐浴，恢复光辉，神庙因此得名苏摩湿婆罗，即月之主。

遮娄其国王穆拉罗阇在997年之前建起第一座石庙，但1026年伽色尼的马哈茂德劫掠此庙。遮娄其国王鸠摩罗波罗约于1169年重建，1299年乌鲁格汗的军队再次将其洗劫；朱达萨摩国王摩希波罗于1308年重修神庙，其子肯伽罗在1331—1351年间重新安立林伽。

德里总督、古吉拉特苏丹国的开创者扎法尔汗于1395年再度毁庙，马哈茂德·贝加达1451年又加以亵渎，奥朗则布在1706年下令拆庙改建清真寺。18世纪后期，印多尔的阿希莉娅芭伊·霍尔卡在废墟旁另建一座小庙，使香火得以延续。

en:
The Deo Surya Mandir, also called Devark, is a sun temple dedicated to Surya in Deo, Bihar, and the principal shrine of the Chhath sun-festival. Unusually, it faces west, towards the setting sun.

Historians place its first building between the 500s and the 700s, and tradition numbers it among the twelve sun temples raised by Samba, son of Krishna. An inscription of 1437 records King Bhairavendra's dedication of the temple and its restoration by Hindu chieftains after Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji's invasion of Bengal in the early 1200s.

Some scholars argue it had first been a Buddhist temple. Built of carved stone in a blend of Nagara, Dravidian and Vesara forms, it is crowned by a dome bearing a golden urn, and draws its greatest crowds at the Chhath Puja and on Sundays.
zh:
代奥的苏利耶神庙又名代瓦尔克，是比哈尔邦代奥镇的一座太阳神苏利耶神庙，也是恰特普迦太阳神祭的首要圣地。与一般太阳神庙不同，它朝西面向落日。

史家推断其最初建于6—8世纪，传统则把它列为奎师那之子商波所建十二座太阳神庙之一。1437年的铭文记载国王拜拉文德罗为神庙举行奉献，也记载了巴赫蒂亚尔·卡尔吉于13世纪初入侵孟加拉后，当地印度教酋长修复神龛的事迹。

部分学者认为它最初可能是一座佛寺。神庙以石雕建成，融合纳加拉、达罗毗荼与毗萨拉三种样式，顶部穹隆上安放金罐；每逢恰特普迦节和周日，前来的香客最多。

en:
The Dewa Sanzan are the three sacred mountains of Dewa Province in the far north of Honshu, Mount Haguro, Mount Gassan and Mount Yudono, each with its own shrine. The chief shrine on Haguro venerates the deities of all three.

Tradition dates their opening as a religious centre to 593, when Prince Hachiko, son of the murdered Emperor Sushun, fled the Soga clan to Dewa and spent his life in devotion to the mountain god Haguro Gongen.

The mountains became a training ground of Shugendō mountain asceticism. In summer yamabushi and ordinary pilgrims trekked north to their shrines. Mount Haguro, the only one approachable all year, has a five-storey wooden pagoda in its cedar groves, and the poet Matsuo Bashō later joined the pilgrims climbing its stone path.
zh:
出羽三山是本州极北出羽国的三座圣山——羽黑山、月山和汤殿山，各有神社，羽黑山顶的总社同时供奉三山之神。

相传593年崇峻天皇遇弑后，皇子蜂子为躲避苏我氏逃到出羽，终生奉祀山神羽黑权现，三山由此开辟为宗教之地。

这里后来成为修验道的修行场。每年夏天山伏与普通信众跋涉北上，登山朝拜。羽黑山是三山中唯一全年可登的一座，杉林中矗立着木造五重塔；诗人松尾芭蕉后来也沿石阶上山朝圣。

en:
Didyma was the oracle sanctuary of Apollo in the territory of Miletus on the Ionian coast, where a priestess spoke over a sacred spring and the priestly family of the Branchidae interpreted her words. The Persians burned the temple after the battle of Lade in 494 BC and carried its bronze Apollo to Ecbatana; the site lay in ruins until Alexander freed Miletus in 334 BC.

The Milesians raised a vast Ionic temple with an open court; Seleucus I brought the statue back from Persia around 300 BC. Galatian raiders sacked the sanctuary in 277 BC, and pirates in 67 BC, yet Roman emperors patronised it; Hadrian came as prophet in 129 AD.

The oracle ended when Theodosius I closed the pagan temples; a Byzantine bishopric and village lingered on the site until an earthquake in 1493 toppled the temple and drove the inhabitants away.
zh:
迪迪玛是爱奥尼亚海岸米利都境内的阿波罗神谕圣地，女祭司在圣泉之上宣示神谕，再由布兰基代祭司家族解读。公元前494年拉德海战之后，波斯人焚毁神庙，把青铜阿波罗像劫往埃克巴坦那；遗址沦为废墟，直到公元前334年亚历山大解放米利都。

米利都人随后建起一座带露天内院的爱奥尼式大庙；约公元前300年，塞琉古一世把神像从波斯迎回。公元前277年加拉太人洗劫圣地，公元前67年海盗又来一次，但罗马皇帝仍眷顾此地；129年哈德良亲任先知。

狄奥多西一世关闭异教神庙后，神谕就此终结；一处拜占庭主教区和村落在此延续，直到1493年的地震震塌神庙，居民四散离去。

en:
The Dilwara Temples stand in the forested hills above Mount Abu in southern Rajasthan, among the five great Svetambara pilgrimage places of the Jains. Five white-marble shrines were raised between the 1000s and 1500s, their plain exteriors giving way to lace-like marble carving.

The earliest and largest, the Vimal Vasahi dedicated to Rishabhanatha, was built around 1026 by Vimal Shah, minister of the Chaulukya king Bhima I. The Luna Vasahi, honouring Neminatha, was completed by 1230 under the minister brothers Vastupala and Tejpal.

Alauddin Khalji's army sacked the temples in 1311 and they were repaired from 1321 onward. The Pittalhar temple was then built, the three-storey Parshvanatha temple followed in 1458 and 1459, and the Mahavira temple was added in 1582; Sirohi painters decorated it in 1764.
zh:
地利缚罗寺坐落在拉贾斯坦南部阿布山上方的林丘间，是耆那教白衣派五大圣地之一。五座白色大理石神殿建于11至16世纪，外墙朴素，内部却布满近乎镂空织锦般的石雕。

最早也最大的是供奉勒舍婆那陀的毗摩罗瓦西寺，约1026年由遮娄其国王毗摩一世的大臣毗摩罗沙兴建。供奉涅弥那陀的卢那瓦西寺，则在大臣兄弟瓦斯图波罗与泰阇波罗主持下于1230年前完工。

1311年阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉的军队洗劫神庙，1321年起陆续修复。此后皮陀罗诃寺、三层楼高的巴湿伐那陀寺（1458—1459年）和大雄寺（1582年）相继落成；锡罗希画师于1764年为大雄寺绘制壁画。

en:
Dodona, in the mountains of Epirus, was the oldest oracle in Greece, where priests read the will of Zeus in the rustling leaves of a sacred oak. In the Iliad Achilles prays to Zeus of Dodona before Troy; the goddess Dione was honoured beside him.

Around 290 BC Pyrrhus made it his kingdom's religious capital, rebuilding the Temple of Zeus and adding a theatre and games. The Aetolians burned it in 219 BC and Philip V of Macedon restored it, but raiders in the pay of Mithridates sacked it around 88 BC.

Pilgrims came in Roman times: Pausanias saw the sacred oak in the second century, and the emperor Julian consulted the oracle in 362. In 391 or 392 Theodosius I closed the pagan temples and had the oak cut down, though a Christian bishopric survived into the fifth century.
zh:
