多多纳位于伊庇鲁斯的群山之中，是希腊最古老的神谕所，祭司通过倾听圣橡树叶的沙沙声解读宙斯的旨意。《伊利亚特》中阿喀琉斯在特洛伊城下向多多纳的宙斯祈祷；女神狄俄涅在宙斯身旁同受供奉。

约公元前290年，皮洛士把它定为王国的宗教首都，重建宙斯神庙，并增设剧场和赛会。公元前219年埃托利亚人将其焚毁，马其顿的腓力五世又加以修复；约公元前88年受米特拉达梯雇用的袭击者洗劫此地。

罗马时代仍有朝圣者前来：2世纪保萨尼阿斯见过圣橡树，362年皇帝尤利安曾求问神谕。391—392年间，狄奥多西一世关闭异教神庙并砍倒古橡树，不过基督教主教区一直延续到5世纪。

en:
The Dwarkadhish Temple stands at Dwarka, on the Saurashtra coast of Gujarat, and houses Krishna as Dwarkadhish, the Lord of Dwarka. Hindu tradition holds that Krishna built the city on land reclaimed from the ocean and made it his capital after leaving Mathura.

The five-storey shrine, also called the Jagat Mandir, is raised on 72 pillars and counted among the Char Dham and the Sapta Puri. Adi Shankara visited it in the eighth century and founded the nearby Dvaraka Pitha; archaeological evidence traces a temple here to around 200 BCE.

In 1473 the Gujarat sultan Mahmud Begada sacked Dwarka and destroyed the shrine and its idol. The present building was raised in the sixteenth century and the image installed in 1559. The poet-saint Mirabai is said to have vanished into the image, and Vallabha made Krishna Janmashtami a regular observance.
zh:
德瓦尔格之主奎师那神庙位于古吉拉特萨乌拉施特拉海岸的德瓦卡，供奉以德瓦卡之主之名受拜的奎师那。印度教传统认为，奎师那离开马图拉后在填海得来的土地上建成此城，立为都城。

这座五层神庙又称世界之庙，以72根石柱撑起，位列印度教四大朝圣圣地与七圣城之一。8世纪阿迪·商羯罗曾来此朝拜，并在附近建立德瓦卡寺；考古证据显示，公元前200年前后此地已有神庙。

1473年，古吉拉特苏丹马哈茂德·贝加达洗劫德瓦卡，捣毁神庙与神像。主体建筑建于16世纪，神像于1559年安立。相传诗人圣女米拉巴伊在此融入神像，伐拉巴则把奎师那诞辰节确立为庙中的常例庆典。

en:
Ek' Balam was a Yucatec Maya city in the northern lowlands, northeast of Chichen Itza, whose kings ruled from around the start of the Common Era until its slow abandonment in the Postclassic. Its golden age ran from 770 to 840 under Ukit Kan Lek Tok', who reigned from 770 to about 800 and was buried in the great Acropolis.

His tomb temple, El Trono, opens through a jaguar-maw doorway and preserves fine Maya plaster sculpture. Two concentric walls ringed the city, while a rough inner wall across the Great Plaza suggests a desperate last defence before the population collapsed and the site was emptied.

A late sixteenth-century Spanish Relacion Geografica recorded local memory of the kingdom of Talol. It was said to have been founded by a chief named Ek' Balam from the east, before the Cupul family dominated the district.
zh:
埃克巴拉姆是尤卡坦北部低地上的玛雅城市，位于奇琴伊察东北，其国王约自公元初年起统治此地，直到后古典期城市逐渐被弃。它的黄金时代在770—840年间，国王乌基特·坎·莱克·托克于770年至约800年在位，死后葬入大卫城。

他的陵庙“王座”以美洲虎巨口为门，保存着精美的玛雅灰泥雕塑。两道同心城墙环绕全城，大广场上仓促补筑的粗糙内墙暗示城破前曾有过拼死防守，随后人口锐减，城址沦为空城。

16世纪末西班牙人的《地理报告》记录着当地对塔洛尔王国的记忆。传说它由一位来自东方、名叫埃克·巴拉姆的首领建立，后来库普尔家族成为这一地区的主宰。

en:
Enryaku-ji overlooks Kyoto from the border of Ōmi Province. With Emperor Kanmu's backing, Saichō brought Chinese Tiantai teachings to Japan from here; in 807 he ordained a hundred disciples for twelve years of secluded study.

At its height the complex held some three thousand sub-temples. In the tenth century a succession feud split Tendai into the Mountain Order at Enryaku-ji and the Temple Order at Mii-dera, and armed monks repeatedly marched on Kyoto. The monastery trained the men who later founded the Pure Land, Shinshū, Sōtō Zen and Nichiren schools.

In 1571 Oda Nobunaga stormed Mount Hiei, burned the buildings and put the monks to the sword; only the thirteenth-century Ruri-dō survived. Reconstruction followed, and Tokugawa Iemitsu rebuilt the main hall in 1642.
zh:
延历寺坐落于近江国边境，俯瞰京都。最澄在桓武天皇支持下，由此将中国天台教义传入日本；807年他为百名弟子授戒，令其闭关修行十二年。

极盛时山内有约三千座子院。10世纪，天台宗因法统之争分裂为以延历寺为本山的山门派和以三井寺为本山的寺门派，武装僧众多次入京强诉。后来开创净土宗、净土真宗、曹洞宗和日莲宗的祖师，都曾在此修行。

1571年，织田信长攻入比睿山，焚毁堂舍、屠戮僧众，只有13世纪的琉璃堂幸免。此后寺院逐步重建，德川家光于1642年再建正殿。

official_raw.en: Founded in 788 AD on Mount Hiei by the monk Saichō, $enryaku_ji$ became the headquarters of the $SECT_TENDAI_NAME$ school of Japanese [ShowReligionGroupName('buddhist')]. It was a powerful monastic center that housed thousands of warrior monks and influenced the affairs of [ShowLocationName('kyoto')].
official_raw.zh: $enryaku_ji$由最澄和尚于公元788年在比睿山建造，成为日本[ShowReligionGroupName('buddhist')]$SECT_TENDAI_NAME$的总本山。这是一座强大的寺院，拥有数千名武僧，影响着[ShowLocationName('kyoto')]的事务。

en:
Epidauros was a small polis on the Argolid peninsula facing the Saronic Gulf. It claimed to be the birthplace of Asclepius, the healer son of Apollo, whose sanctuary arose from the sixth century BC and became the most celebrated medical centre of the Greek world.

The sick slept in a great dream-dormitory, trusting the god to prescribe a cure in a dream. A temple and a theatre famed for its acoustics served the sanctuary. Sulla plundered it in 87 BC and pirates again before 67 BC, beginning a long decline.

Hadrian's visit in 124 revived its fortunes: he reformed the priesthood and games, and Antonine patrons added baths and a temple of Hygieia. Goths raided it in 395, yet in the middle of the fifth century the healing centre still drew patients under Christian management.
zh:
厄庇道洛斯是阿尔戈利斯半岛上濒临萨罗尼科斯湾的小城邦。此地相传是阿波罗之子、医神阿斯克勒庇俄斯的出生地，公元前6世纪起他的圣所兴起，后来成为希腊世界最负盛名的医疗中心。

病人在大寝殿中睡卧祈梦，相信医神会在梦中指点疗方。圣所内有神庙和以音响效果著称的剧场。公元前87年苏拉洗劫此地，公元前67年之前海盗又来一次，圣所由此长期衰落。

124年哈德良亲临后再度振兴，他改革祭司制度与赛会，安敦尼王朝的赞助人又增建浴场和许癸厄亚神庙。395年哥特人来袭，但直到5世纪中叶，疗愈中心仍在基督教管理下接待病人。

en:
The metropolitan see of Fars stood at Rev Ardashir, the port refounded by the Sasanian king Ardashir I in the third century. Tradition held that Persian merchants converted in Edessa first brought Christianity to the region.

By 424 Fars ranked as the sixth metropolitan province of the Church of the East; around 540 its metropolitan gained authority over Bahrain, Oman and Socotra. Maʿna of Pars, installed in 540, translated the Psalms and Syriac liturgy into Pahlavi for churches as far away as India.

Islamization after the Arab conquests eroded these communities, and the last known metropolitan, ʿAbdishoʿ, is recorded in 1138. By the Mongol era few Christians remained on the mainland, though a community at Hormuz is mentioned into the sixteenth century and Socotra sent a bishop to the enthronement of Yahballaha III in 1281.
zh:
法尔斯教省的都主教驻地在雷夫阿尔达希尔，即3世纪萨珊国王阿尔达希尔一世重建的港口城市。相传是在埃德萨归信的波斯商人最早把基督教带到这一地区。

到424年法尔斯已位列东方教会第六个都主教教省；约540年，其都主教又管辖巴林、阿曼和索科特拉岛。540年就任的法尔斯的马纳把《诗篇》和叙利亚语礼仪译成巴列维语，供远至印度的教会使用。

阿拉伯征服后的伊斯兰化使这些社群萎缩，有史可考的末任都主教阿卜迪绍见于1138年的记载。蒙古时代大陆上的基督徒已所剩无几，但霍尔木兹的社群直到16世纪仍有记载，索科特拉人还在1281年派主教参加雅巴拉哈三世的登位典礼。

en:
The Fatima Masumeh Shrine in Qom, Persia, is the mausoleum of Fatima bint Musa, daughter of the seventh Shia Imam and sister of the eighth Imam Ali al-Rida. In 816 she set out from Medina to join her brother in Khorasan, but her caravan was attacked at Saveh; poisoned and ill, she was carried to Qom, where she died and was buried.

Her tomb, first sheltered by a bamboo canopy, received a domed building about fifty years later at the request of Sayyida Zaynab, daughter of the ninth Imam. The shrine drew pilgrims and seminaries, and Qom grew into a centre of Shia learning.

In 1519 Tajlu Khanum, wife of Shah Ismail I, added an iwan and two minarets and rebuilt the tomb chamber as a domed octagon. Under the Qajars, Fath-Ali Shah merged the courtyards in 1795 and restored the gilded dome in 1803.
zh:
纯洁者法蒂玛圣陵位于波斯的库姆，安葬着什叶派第七任伊玛目之女、第八任伊玛目阿里·里达之妹法蒂玛·马苏梅。816年，她从麦地那动身前往呼罗珊投奔兄长，商队却在萨韦遇袭；她中毒染病，被送往库姆，在那里去世并下葬。

她的坟墓起初只有竹棚遮盖，约五十年后，第九任伊玛目之女赛义达·宰纳卜主持修建了穹顶建筑。圣陵吸引了朝圣者和经学院，库姆也由此成为什叶派学术中心。

1519年，沙阿伊斯玛仪一世之妻塔吉鲁·汗努姆增建了伊万拱门和两座宣礼塔，并把墓室重建为穹顶八边形。卡扎尔王朝时期，法特赫-阿里沙于1795年合并庭院，又在1803年重修鎏金穹顶。

en:
The sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia at Praeneste, modern Palestrina east of Rome, was Latium's grandest oracular shrine. Six vast terraces climbed the hillside to a round temple holding a gilded bronze statue of the goddess as a young warrior. Matrons brought their first-born children to her for protection, and pilgrims consulted her oracle by drawing wooden lots.

The complex took its monumental form around 120 BC, and Sulla enlarged it after making Praeneste a colony about 80 BC. The oracle survived into Christian times until Constantine and Theodosius I forbade lot-divination and closed the temple.

In the Middle Ages the hill belonged to the Colonna: Pope Boniface VIII razed the town in 1298 and Eugenius IV destroyed it again in 1437. After the Barberini bought Palestrina in 1630, their palace rose over the ancient temple-theatre, preserving the round shrine within its walls.
zh:
头生子之神福尔图娜的圣所位于罗马以东的普莱内斯特，即今帕莱斯特里纳，是拉丁姆最宏伟的神谕圣地。六座台地沿山坡升至圆形神庙，庙中供奉着女战神形象的镀金青铜女神像。已婚妇人把头生孩子带来祈求护佑，朝圣者则抽取木签求问神谕。

建筑群约在公元前120年形成宏伟形制；苏拉约于公元前80年在普莱内斯特设立殖民地后扩建圣所。神谕延续到基督教时代，最终君士坦丁和狄奥多西一世禁止抽签占卜并关闭神庙。

中世纪时此山归科隆纳家族所有：1298年教宗波尼法爵八世将城镇夷为平地，1437年教宗恩仁四世再度将其摧毁。1630年巴尔贝里尼家族买下帕莱斯特里纳后，在古神庙剧场上方建起宫殿，把圆形神庙保存在宫墙之内。

en:
Fushimi Inari Taisha is the head shrine of Inari, the kami of rice and agriculture, standing in Yamashiro Province south of Kyoto at the foot of Mount Inari. Founded in 711 by the immigrant Hata clan, it grew from their tutelary shrine into the centre of the nationwide Inari cult.

In 816 the shrine was moved to its present site at the request of the monk Kūkai, and in 965 Emperor Murakami numbered it among the shrines receiving imperial offerings.

The main hall dates from 1499, and the two-storey tower gate was donated by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. From the Edo period onward merchants and guilds dedicated thousands of vermilion torii gates to Inari, increasingly honoured as the patron of trade; the rows called the Senbon Torii climb the mountain behind the shrine, while branch Inari shrines multiplied across Japan.
zh:
伏见稻荷大社是稻荷神的总本社，位于山城国京都以南、稻荷山麓。稻荷神司掌稻米与农业，神社于711年由渡来豪族秦氏创建，从秦氏的氏社发展为全国稻荷信仰的中心。

816年应僧人空海之请迁至现地；965年村上天皇将它列入接受朝廷币帛的神社。

本殿建于1499年，两层楼门由丰臣秀吉捐建。江户时代以来，商人与行会献上数以千计的朱红色鸟居，在社后山腰排成“千本鸟居”；稻荷神也越来越被视为商业守护神，稻荷神社随之遍布日本各地。

en:
Gelati Monastery crowns a hill above the Tskaltsitela Gorge near Kutaisi, seat of the medieval Georgian kings in Imereti. King David IV the Builder founded it in 1106 as both a monastery and an academy. Its main Church of the Blessed Virgin was completed in 1130 under his successor Demetrius I, who placed the gates carried off from Ganja in 1138 at its entrance. David himself was buried there.

The Gelati Academy gathered theologians and philosophers who had studied at houses such as the Mangana in Constantinople. Ioane Petritsi wrote commentaries on Proclus, Arsen Ikaltoeli compiled the Aristotle-influenced Dogmatikon, and scribes copied manuscripts, so that contemporaries called the house a new Hellas and a second Athos.
zh:
格拉特修道院位于伊梅列季库塔伊西附近、俯瞰特斯卡尔齐特拉峡谷的山丘上，库塔伊西曾是中世纪格鲁吉亚国王的都城。1106年，大卫四世（建设者）在此同时兴建修道院与学院；主教堂圣母堂于1130年在继任者德米特里一世治下完工，1138年从占贾掠来的城门安放在教堂入口，大卫四世本人也安葬于此。

格拉特学院汇聚了曾在君士坦丁堡曼加纳修道院等地求学的神学家和哲学家。约阿内·彼得里齐为普罗克洛斯作注，阿尔森·伊卡尔托埃利编成受亚里士多德影响的《教义集》，抄写员传抄典籍，时人把这里称为“新希腊”和“第二阿索斯”。

en:
The Gnana Saraswati Temple stands on the Godavari at Basar in Telangana, one of the subcontinent's most celebrated shrines of Saraswati, goddess of knowledge and learning. Tradition connects it with the sage Vyasa, who after the Kurukshetra war settled here for prayer; his abode was called Vasara, later becoming Basara in Marathi speech.

The temple is credited to Bijialudu, a Karnataka king who ruled Nandagiri from Nanded in the 500s. It is one of three temples near the Manjira and Godavari confluence. After Muslim invaders destroyed its images in the medieval period a Nandagiri chieftain reinstalled the idols in the 1600s.

Saraswati occupies the sanctum with Lakshmi and Mahakali nearby, making Basara an abode of the goddess trinity. Families bring young children for the Akshara abhyasam, in which they trace their first letters before the goddess.
zh:
智慧辩才天女庙坐落于特伦甘纳巴萨尔镇的戈达瓦里河畔，是次大陆最著名的萨拉斯瓦蒂神庙之一，萨拉斯瓦蒂是主管知识与学问的女神。相传俱卢之战后，仙人毗耶娑在此长期祈祷，他的住处称“瓦萨拉”，后来受马拉地语影响读成巴萨尔。

史家一般认为，此庙是6世纪以楠德德为都、统治南达吉里的卡纳达国王比贾卢杜所建，也是曼吉拉河与戈达瓦里河汇流处附近的三座神庙之一。中世纪穆斯林入侵者毁坏神像后，17世纪一位南达吉里首领重新安奉了神像。

圣室中萨拉斯瓦蒂居中，旁有吉祥天女和大迦梨像，巴萨尔因此被尊为三位女神同居之地。家长们带幼童来此举行识字礼，让孩子在女神面前写下人生第一个字母。

en:
The Guruvayur Temple stands in Guruvayur in central Kerala and is dedicated to Guruvayurappan, a four-armed form of Krishna-Vishnu carved from shaligram stone. Tradition holds that after Krishna's death and the drowning of Dvaraka his disciple Uddhava brought the idol south. Brihaspati, the guru of the gods, and Vayu, the wind god, installed it on a spot chosen by Shiva; the place takes its name from Guru and Vayu.

A fourteenth-century Tamil poem calls it Kuruvayur, and by the end of the sixteenth century it was a leading Kerala pilgrimage centre. Melpathur Narayana Bhattathiri popularised its Sanskrit name.

In 1716 Dutch raiders looted it and burned its western tower, rebuilt in 1747. Hyder Ali spared it for ransom in 1766, and in 1789 Tipu Sultan's invasion forced the priests to hide the idol at Ambalappuzha until its reinstallation in 1792.
zh:
古鲁瓦尤尔神庙位于喀拉拉中部的古鲁瓦尤尔镇，供奉以页岩化石雕成的四臂立像古鲁瓦尤尔阿潘，即奎师那与毗湿奴的合一之相。相传奎师那升天、德瓦卡城沉入海中后，其弟子优陀婆将神像带往南方，由天神之师祭主仙人与风神伐由在湿婆指定之地安立，地名取自祭主与伐由的名字。

14世纪的泰米尔语诗篇已称此地为库鲁瓦尤尔，到16世纪末它已是喀拉拉重要的朝圣中心。梅尔帕图尔·纳拉亚纳·巴塔蒂里使它的梵文化名字广为流传。

1716年，荷兰入侵者洗劫神庙、烧毁西门楼，门楼于1747年重建。1766年海德尔·阿里在索取赎金后放过神庙；1789年蒂普苏丹来犯，祭司被迫把神像转移到安巴拉普扎，直到1792年才重新安立。

en: Hamp'atu is a high peak of the puna grasslands in southern Peru, venerated as an apu, one of the Andean mountain spirits whose cult reaches back to the early second millennium BCE. Its Quechua name means toad, the same word behind the volcano Ampato, and like other sacred peaks it received offerings from nearby herding communities.
zh: 安帕图圣山是秘鲁南部普纳草原的一座高峰，被尊为安第斯山神“阿普”，这一山峰崇拜可追溯至公元前第二千年纪早期。其克丘亚语名意为“蟾蜍”，安帕托火山之名也出自同一个词；与其他圣峰一样，它接受附近放牧社群的献祭。

en:
Haridwar stands where the Ganges enters the northern plain. Ancient Sanskrit texts call it Gangadvara, the gate of the Ganges; its later name means gateway to Hari, the god Vishnu. Puranic legend counts it among the four places where drops of amrita fell from the gods' pitcher.

Its twelve-yearly bathing fair appears to be the original Kumbh Mela, named for the zodiacal sign Kumbha, or Aquarius, under which it is held. The earliest surviving texts to use that name, from 1695 and 1759, apply it only to Haridwar.

Timur sacked the town in 1398 and massacred pilgrims on its banks. Under Mughal rule the fair became a great religious and commercial gathering, but armed ascetics often fought over bathing precedence: a clash in 1760 left thousands dead. After the Marathas ceded the region in 1804, the East India Company disarmed the orders and policed the ghats.
zh:
赫里德瓦尔地处恒河进入北部大平原之处。梵文古籍称其为“恒河门”，后来的名字意为“诃利之门”，诃利即毗湿奴。往世书传说中，长生不老的甘露从众神的壶中洒落四处，此地便是其中之一。

这里十二年一度的沐浴节会似乎是最早的大壶节，以举行时刻对应的宝瓶宫命名。现存最早使用“大壶节”一名的文献分别出自1695年和1759年，都只用它称呼赫里德瓦尔的节会。

1398年帖木儿洗劫此城，屠杀聚集河畔的朝圣者。莫卧儿时期，节会成长为盛大的宗教与商业集会，但武装苦行僧团常为谁先沐浴相争，1760年的冲突造成数千人死亡。1804年马拉塔人割让此地后，东印度公司解除了僧团的武装，接管河坛治安。

en:
The Humcha temples stand in the Malenadu hills of Karnataka, the greatest southern centre of the cult of Padmavati, attendant of Parshvanatha. Tradition relates that the Jain prince Jinadatta Raya fled Mathura carrying her golden image and was told in a dream to found his capital where it rested. He established Pombuccapura, later Humcha, set up a Bhattaraka seat in the 600s or 700s, and made it the Santara dynasty's first capital.

Vira Santara raised the Padmavati temple in 1061. Chattaladevi built the largest monument, the five-shrined Panchakuta Basadi, in 1077, with its forty-foot pillar.

The Santaras made Humcha a feudatory centre of Vijayanagara and spread Digambara Jainism through the Tulu and Malenadu lands. An inscription of 1530 records a viceroy of Srirangapatna converting to Jainism here under the acharya Vidyananda.
zh:
颔遮寺坐落于卡纳塔克的马拉纳德丘陵，是南印度耆那教巴湿伐那陀护法钵特摩婆蒂信仰最大的中心。相传耆那王子耆那达多·罗耶背负女神金像从秣菟罗出逃，梦中受指点在金像停歇之地建都。他建立蓬布遮补罗，即后来的颔遮，于7至8世纪设立巴达罗迦教座，并使其成为桑塔拉王朝的第一个都城。

钵特摩婆蒂殿由毗罗·桑塔拉于1061年建成。1077年，查多罗提毗修建了当地最大的五殿式五峰寺，并立起四十英尺高的荣誉柱。

桑塔拉人使颔遮成为毗奢耶那伽罗的藩属中心，把天衣派耆那教传播到图卢与马拉纳德各地。1530年的铭文记载室利楞伽帕特纳的一位总督在阿阇梨吠陀难陀影响下于此改宗耆那教。

en:
Ich Kaan Ti'Ho was the old name of the city archaeologists call Dzibilchaltun, whose name means the place of writing on flat stones, north of Merida in Yucatan. Settled from about 600 BC, it became a regional power of more than 25,000 people between 800 and 1000, before declining around 1100.

Its most sacred building was the Temple of the Seven Dolls, named for seven small clay figures beneath its floor. At the equinoxes the sun rises through its eastern and western doorways; a long white stone road links it to the Great Plaza and Cenote Xlacah. The deep waterhole became a cult place for offerings of vases, carved bones and wood.

The settlement outlived its monuments. After the Spanish conquest a sixteenth-century open chapel was raised among the old stones, where the Maya still lived around the cenote.
zh:
七子之像神庙所在古城的古名为Ich Kaan Ti'Ho，考古学家称其为齐比尔查尔通，意为“扁石上有文字之处”，位于尤卡坦的梅里达以北。城址约自公元前600年有人居住，在800—1000年的鼎盛期发展为人口逾2.5万的区域强权，1100年前后衰落。

城中最神圣的建筑是七子之像神庙，因地面下供奉的七尊小泥像而得名。春分、秋分时，旭日恰好穿过它东西两门升起，一条长长的白色石砌大道将神庙与大广场和什拉卡天然井相连。深井后来成为祭祀场所，人们向井中投献陶罐、刻纹骨器和木器。

聚落的寿命比纪念碑更长久。西班牙征服之后，16世纪的一座露天礼拜堂建在古石之间，玛雅人仍围绕着天然井居住。

en:
The Imam Ali Shrine at Najaf, near Kufa in Iraq, is the foremost Shia sanctuary, holding the tomb of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, fourth Rashidun caliph and first Shia Imam. Ali was assassinated in Kufa in 661 and buried in secret at the desert spot that grew into Najaf. In 786 the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid raised the first domed shrine over his grave.

The caliph al-Mutawakkil destroyed the sanctuary in 850, but the Hamdanids rebuilt it in 923 and the Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla enlarged it in 979. Fire gutted the shrine in 1354 and it was rebuilt around 1358.

The Safavid shah Abbas I began reconstruction in 1623, finished under Shah Safi in 1632. In 1742 Nader Shah gilded its dome and minarets, giving it the golden skyline that drew Shia pilgrims from across the region.
zh:
伊玛目阿里圣陵位于伊拉克库法附近的纳杰夫，是什叶派最重要的圣所，安葬着穆罕默德的堂弟兼女婿、第四位正统哈里发、什叶派第一位伊玛目阿里·本·阿比·塔利卜。661年，阿里在库法遇刺，秘密安葬在后来发展为纳杰夫的沙漠之地。786年阿拔斯哈里发哈伦·拉希德在墓上建起第一座带穹顶的圣陵。

850年哈里发穆塔瓦基勒拆毁圣所，923年哈姆丹王朝将其重建，979年白益王朝埃米尔阿杜德·道莱又加以扩建。1354年圣陵毁于大火，1358年前后重建。

萨法维王朝的阿拔斯一世于1623年启动重修，1632年由萨非完成。1742年纳迪尔沙为穹顶和宣礼塔贴金，金色的天际线吸引着各地的什叶派朝圣者。

en:
The Imam Husayn Shrine in Karbala, Iraq, marks the tomb of Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of Muhammad and the third Shia Imam. He was killed with his family and some seventy followers at the Battle of Karbala in 680 after rising against the Umayyad caliph Yazid I. His martyrdom, commemorated on Ashura, made Karbala one of Shia Islam's holiest cities.

The Abbasid caliph al-Saffah raised the first substantial shrine in the 750s, but in 850 al-Mutawakkil had the tomb demolished and its pit flooded, until his successor al-Muntasir allowed pilgrims to return. The Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla rebuilt and fortified it in 981, and it was restored after a fire in 1016.

In 1802 Wahhabi raiders from Najd sacked Karbala, massacred its people and tore down the dome. The Qajar shah Fath-Ali Shah then funded the rebuilding of the shrine.
zh:
伊玛目侯赛因圣陵位于伊拉克卡尔巴拉，安葬着穆罕默德的外孙、什叶派第三位伊玛目侯赛因·伊本·阿里。680年，侯赛因起兵反抗伍麦叶哈里发耶齐德一世，在卡尔巴拉战役中与家人及约七十名追随者一同被杀。他的殉难在阿舒拉节受到纪念，卡尔巴拉也因此成为什叶派最神圣的城市之一。

阿拔斯哈里发萨法赫在8世纪50年代建起第一座圣陵，850年穆塔瓦基勒却下令毁墓、向墓坑灌水，直到其继任者蒙塔塞尔放行朝圣者。981年白益埃米尔阿杜德·道莱重建并加固圣所，1016年火灾后再度修复。

1802年，来自内志的瓦哈比武装洗劫卡尔巴拉、屠杀居民并捣毁穹顶。事后卡扎尔王朝的法塔赫-阿里沙出资重建了圣陵。

en:
The Imam Reza Shrine in Mashhad, in Khorasan in northeastern Iran, holds the tomb of Ali al-Rida, the eighth Shia Imam. In 818 the caliph al-Ma'mun had Reza poisoned near Tus, and the grave grew into Mashhad, whose name means the place of martyrdom.

In 993 the Ghaznavid ruler Sebuktigin sacked the town and halted pilgrimage, until Mahmud of Ghazni restored the shrine after 1009. After the Mongol devastation of Khorasan in 1220 the Ilkhanid ruler Öljaitü renovated it. In 1418 the Timurid empress Goharshad built her mosque beside the sanctuary.

With the Safavid adoption of Twelver Shiism in 1501 the shrine became a royal pilgrimage centre. Shah Abbas I walked from Isfahan to Mashhad and gilded the dome between 1601 and 1607; the Qajar shahs enlarged the complex in the early nineteenth century.
zh:
伊玛目礼萨圣陵位于伊朗东北部呼罗珊的马什哈德，安葬着什叶派第八位伊玛目阿里·礼萨。818年，哈里发马蒙在图斯附近毒杀礼萨，墓地周围逐渐发展成马什哈德，其名意为“殉道者之地”。

993年伽色尼统治者塞布克特勤洗劫城镇、禁止朝觐，1009年后伽色尼的马哈茂德重修圣陵。1220年蒙古人蹂躏呼罗珊后，伊儿汗国统治者完者都修缮圣陵。1418年，帖木儿王朝皇后高哈尔绍德在圣所旁建起以她命名的清真寺。

1501年萨法维王朝立十二伊玛目派为国教，圣陵成为皇家朝觐中心。阿拔斯一世从伊斯法罕徒步前往马什哈德，并于1601—1607年为穹顶贴金；19世纪初卡扎尔诸沙进一步扩建了圣陵建筑群。

en:
The Inti Wak'a at Chan Chan marks the sun shrine within the greatest city of the Peruvian coast. In Quechua a wak'a is a revered place, rock or monument where Andean communities invoked spirits.

From about 900 Chan Chan was the capital of Chimor, whose palace-mausoleums, ceremonial pyramids and plazas formed a sacred landscape devoted above all to the royal ancestors and to the Moon, which the Chimú ranked above the Sun. The city kept its own solar cult, until the Inca emperor Túpac Yupanqui besieged it in 1470, cutting the aqueducts and incorporating Chimor into the Inca Empire.

Inca rule drew the local wak'a into the state cult of Inti, the sun god and divine ancestor of the ruling dynasty. When the Chimú rebelled around 1500, Huayna Cápac sacked and partly burned the city, but the adobe shrines among its ruins continued to be venerated.
zh:
昌昌的因蒂圣所标志着秘鲁沿海最宏大城市中的太阳祭祀场所。在克丘亚语中，wak'a（瓦卡，即圣所）指受人敬拜的地点、岩石或纪念建筑，安第斯社群在此呼请神灵。

约从900年起，昌昌成为奇姆王国的都城，城内宫殿-陵墓、仪式金字塔和广场构成的神圣景观主要侍奉王室祖先与月亮，奇姆人认为月亮的地位高于太阳。城中仍保有自己的太阳崇拜，直到1470年印加皇帝图帕克·尤潘基围攻昌昌，切断灌溉渠，将奇姆并入印加帝国。

此后印加统治者把当地圣所纳入太阳神因蒂的国家崇拜之中，因蒂也是王朝的神圣祖先。约1500年奇姆人反叛，瓦伊纳·卡帕克洗劫并部分焚毁了昌昌，但废墟中的土坯圣所仍受到敬奉。

en:
The Ise Grand Shrine in Shima province is the holiest place of Shintō, built around the Naikū that houses the Yata no Kagami, the sacred mirror of the sun goddess Amaterasu, and the Gekū dedicated to the food goddess Toyouke. Tradition says the princess Yamatohime chose Ise as the goddess's dwelling, and Emperor Tenmu raised the first shrine hall between 678 and 686; his widow Empress Jitō carried out the first ceremonial rebuilding in 692.

The Shikinen Sengū renewed every hall every twenty years, alternating between two adjacent sites and preserving the shinmei-zukuri style of plain cypress joined without nails.

In the Edo period the Okage mairi pilgrimage became a mass movement: in 1625 some 3.6 million pilgrims came within fifty days, and in 1829 more than a million arrived in three days for the great festival.
zh:
伊势神宫位于志摩地区，是神道教最神圣的场所，核心为供奉天照大神、收藏其神镜八咫镜的内宫，以及供奉食物女神丰受大神的外宫。相传倭姬命选定伊势作为天照大神的居所，天武天皇于678至686年间建起第一座神殿，其皇后持统天皇又于692年主持了首次式年迁宫。

此后每隔二十年，所有殿舍都在相邻的两块地基上交替重建，使不用一钉、以素朴桧木构建的神明造古制得以传承。

江户时代，“御荫参”朝圣演变为全民运动：1625年约有360万朝圣者在50天内涌入，1829年的大祭期间，三天之内便有上百万人到访。

en:
Isthmia was the sanctuary of Poseidon on the Isthmus of Corinth, famous for the Isthmian Games, one of the four great Panhellenic festivals. Legend traced the games to funeral rites held by Sisyphus of Corinth for the boy Melicertes, and the historical festival was constituted in 582 BC.

After Chaeronea in 338 BC Philip II of Macedon formed the League of Corinth there, and after the Second Macedonian War the Roman general Flamininus proclaimed the freedom of the Greeks before the festival crowd. When Rome destroyed Corinth in 146 BC the sanctuary was sacked and the games passed to Sicyon, returning after Julius Caesar refounded Corinth in 44 BC.

Nero performed at the games in 67 AD, but the Temple of Poseidon was later abandoned and its stones reused in the Hexamilion wall. Isthmia fell permanently to the Turks in 1458.
zh:
伊斯米亚是科林斯地峡上的波塞冬圣地，以伊斯米亚运动会闻名，这是希腊四大泛希腊赛会之一。传说赛会源于科林斯的西西弗斯为少年墨利刻耳忒斯举行的葬礼竞技，历史上的赛会则确立于公元前582年。

公元前338年喀罗尼亚战役后，马其顿的腓力二世在此组建科林斯同盟；第二次马其顿战争后，罗马将领弗拉米尼努斯在赛会人群前宣告希腊人的自由。公元前146年罗马毁灭科林斯，圣地被洗劫，赛会移交西库翁，直到公元前44年尤利乌斯·恺撒重建科林斯后才回归。

67年尼禄在赛会中登台表演，但波塞冬神庙后来遭废弃，石材被拆去修筑赫克萨米利翁城墙。伊斯米亚于1458年永久落入土耳其人手中。

en:
Izumo Taisha on the Sea of Japan coast is among the oldest shrines of Shintō, dedicated to Ōkuninushi, the god who builds the land and binds people in marriage. The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki tell that Ōkuninushi yielded Izumo to the heavenly grandson Ninigi, whereupon Amaterasu ordered a palace built for him with colossal pillars, and that palace became this shrine.

Its hall gave its name to the taisha-zukuri style; a Heian record of about 950 describes it as roughly forty-eight metres high. The hall was shortened around 1200 and reconstructed in 1744 to twenty-four metres.

In the tenth lunar month the kami of Japan were believed to gather here to arrange marriages, births and deaths, so Izumo calls it the month with gods, while elsewhere it is the month without gods. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, it became a pilgrimage destination.
zh:
出云大社位于日本海沿岸，是神道教最古老的神社之一，供奉经营国土、掌管人间姻缘的大国主大神。《古事记》和《日本书纪》记载，大国主将出云之地让给天孙琼琼杵尊，天照大神遂下令以巨柱为他营建宫殿，这座宫殿便是出云大社。

它的本殿为大社造建筑样式命名；约950年的平安时代记录称，本殿高约48米。1200年前后本殿被改建缩小，1744年又重建为24米高。

相传每逢阴历十月，日本的神祇聚集于此商议姻缘、生育与死亡，因此出云称十月为神在月，其他地方则称神无月。18至19世纪，出云大社成为朝圣目的地。

en:
The Jagannath Temple at Puri, on the Odisha coast, is dedicated to Jagannath, a form of Vishnu, and ranks among the four great pilgrimage sites of Hinduism. A shrine already stood there when Adi Shankara founded the Govardhan Math in the ninth century; the present temple was raised from the early twelfth century by Anantavarman Chodaganga of the Eastern Ganga dynasty after his conquest of Utkala in 1112.

His successor Anangabhima Deva III dedicated the kingdom to Jagannath. The wooden images of Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are replaced every twelve or nineteen years, and each summer the deities ride through town on cars in the Ratha Yatra.

In 1568 the Bengal general Kalapahar sacked Puri and burned the images; Ramachandra Deva I of Khurda installed new images in 1575. After taking Odisha in 1803 the East India Company taxed pilgrims until ordered to withdraw from temple affairs in 1833.
zh:
普里的世主奎师那神庙位于奥里萨海岸，供奉毗湿奴的化身札格纳特，是印度教四大朝圣圣地之一。9世纪阿迪·商羯罗在此建立戈瓦尔丹寺时，这里已有神庙；现存建筑由东恒伽王朝的阿南塔跋摩·朱达恒伽提婆在1112年征服乌特伽罗后，于12世纪初起修建。

其继任者阿南加比马·提婆三世把王国献给札格纳特。庙中札格纳特、巴拉巴德拉和苏婆德拉三尊木像每隔12或19年更换；每年夏天神像乘坐神车穿城而过，举行乘车节。

1568年孟加拉将领卡拉帕哈尔洗劫普里、焚毁神像，库尔达的罗摩旃陀罗·提婆一世于1575年重立新像。1803年英国东印度公司夺取奥里萨后向朝圣者征税，直到1833年才奉命退出神庙事务。

en:
The Jal Mandir, the Water Temple, rises from a lotus-covered tank at Pawapuri, the sinless town of ancient Magadha, and marks the place where Mahavira, the twenty-fourth Tirthankara, was cremated. In 527 BCE, Mahavira passed his final chaturmas at Pawapuri and attained nirvana there on the night of the Dipawali festival, which Jains commemorate at every Diwali.

Pilgrims carried away so much soil from his funeral pyre that the spot became a pit and filled with water, and Mahavira's elder brother Nandivardhan is said to have raised the first shrine within the pond.

The present white-marble temple is shaped like a vimana chariot and houses the foot impression of Mahavira; a stone bridge six hundred feet long joins it to the bank.
zh:
水上神殿（贾尔曼迪尔）矗立在古摩揭陀波婆补罗——意即“无罪之城”——一方莲花满塘的水池中央，标志着第二十四代祖大雄火化之处。公元前527年，大雄在波婆补罗度过最后一次夏安居，并于排灯节之夜在此涅槃，耆那教信众每逢排灯节都要纪念此事。

香客纷纷取走焚化圣址的泥土，竟在原地掘出大坑、积水成塘，相传大雄的兄长难提伐弹那遂在塘中建起第一座神龛。

现存殿宇以白色大理石建成，形如神车维摩那，内奉大雄的足印圣迹，一条六百英尺长的石桥把神殿与塘岸相连。

en:
Jerusalem stood at the heart of East Syriac piety, and monks of the Church of the East regarded a pilgrimage to the Holy Sepulchre as the highest of callings. Around 1275 two Chinese monks, Rabban Bar Sauma and his pupil Markos, later the patriarch Yahballaha III, set out from Khanbaliq on such a pilgrimage, only to be turned back by warfare in Syria.

An East Syriac community endured through the Mamluk age: Franciscan records show a Nestorian presence at the Holy Sepulchre between 1348 and 1575, and in 1482 the Dominican pilgrim Felix Fabri listed Nestorians among the rites in Jerusalem.

The contraction of the Church of the East after Timur's campaigns and the schism of 1552 thinned these congregations. After the later sixteenth century the Nestorian altars vanish from pilgrim accounts, absorbed or abandoned as larger denominations divided the shrines.
zh:
耶路撒冷处于东叙利亚虔诚信仰的核心，东方教会的僧侣把前往圣墓教堂朝圣视为最高志向。约1275年，两名中国修士拉班·扫马和他的学生马尔谷，即后来的牧首雅巴拉哈三世，从汗八里出发踏上朝圣之旅，却因叙利亚的战事受阻而返。

马穆鲁克时代，城中维持着东叙利亚社群：方济各会记述显示，1348—1575年间圣墓教堂里有聂斯脱里派存在；1482年，多明我会朝圣者法布里仍把聂斯脱里派列为耶路撒冷的仪轨群体之一。

帖木儿征战之后东方教会萎缩，1552年又发生大分裂，这些会众日益稀薄。16世纪后期以后，朝圣文献中不再见到聂斯脱里派祭台的记载，它们在各大教派分割圣地时被吞并或遭废弃。

en:
The bishopric of Jerusalem, which tradition traces back to James the brother of Jesus, was raised to a patriarchate by the Council of Chalcedon in 451. In 637 Patriarch Sophronius surrendered the city to the caliph Umar under a covenant guaranteeing Christian protection; the following year the Armenian Apostolic Church began appointing bishops in Jerusalem, whose see grew into the Armenian Patriarchate of Saint James.

When the crusaders took the city in 1099 the Orthodox patriarch was driven out and a Latin patriarch installed. Greek patriarchs were elected in Constantinople until Saladin's victory of 1187 allowed their return.

Under Mamluk and Ottoman rule the Greek Brotherhood of the Holy Sepulchre guarded its rights in the Holy Sepulchre and the Church of the Nativity against the Franciscans. In 1439 the Armenians lost and then bargained back their rights at the Golgotha chapel.
zh:
耶路撒冷主教区传统上溯至耶稣的弟兄雅各，451年迦克墩公会议将其升格为牧首区。637年，牧首索弗罗尼乌斯在保证基督徒受保护的协约下把城市交给哈里发欧麦尔；次年亚美尼亚使徒教会开始在耶路撒冷自派主教，其座堂发展为圣雅各亚美尼亚牧首区。

1099年十字军攻占城市后，东正教牧首被驱逐，拉丁牧首取而代之。希腊牧首仍在君士坦丁堡继续选举，直到1187年萨拉丁获胜后牧首区才得以回归。

马穆鲁克和奥斯曼时期，希腊人的圣墓兄弟会在圣墓教堂和圣诞教堂守护自身权利，与方济各会抗衡。1439年亚美尼亚人失去各各他小堂的权利后又通过谈判取回。

en:
Around 135 the emperor Hadrian buried the tomb beneath what became the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, under a temple of Aphrodite; after Constantine's bishops cleared the site, three crosses were unearthed nearby, one taken for the True Cross, and the basilica was consecrated in 335.

In 614 Sassanid troops burned the church and carried the True Cross away, and Heraclius restored both in 630. The Fatimid caliph al-Hakim ordered the building demolished in 1009, and reconstruction was completed in 1048. Crusaders rebuilt it, finishing under Queen Melisende in 1149 and uniting the chapels under one roof.

Saladin's forces occupied the church in 1187 yet soon admitted pilgrims again. The Status Quo of 1757 fixed the denominations' rights, and after the fire of 1808 the rotunda and tomb shrine were rebuilt in 1809 to 1810.
zh:
约135年，皇帝哈德良把受尊崇的墓穴埋在后来的圣墓教堂之下，其上建起阿佛洛狄忒神殿；君士坦丁的主教们清理场地后，在附近发掘出三个十字架，其中一个被认定为真十字架，新的巴西利卡于335年祝圣。

614年，萨珊军队焚毁教堂并掠走真十字架，630年希拉克略将二者恢复。1009年，法蒂玛哈里发哈基姆下令拆毁教堂，重建工程于1048年完工。十字军重建教堂，工程在梅利桑德女王治下的1149年完成，把小堂统一在同一屋顶之下。

1187年萨拉丁的军队占领教堂，但很快重新允许朝圣。1757年的现状协定确定了各教派的权利；1808年大火之后，圆形大厅与墓穴圣龛于1809—1810年重建。

official_raw.en: Built in the 4th century under Emperor Constantine, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in $jerusalem$ encompasses both Golgotha and the tomb of Christ. It became the holiest site in [ShowReligionGroupName('christian')] and its most important pilgrimage center. Despite periods of destruction and reconstruction, it has remained in shared $christian_ADJ$ custody.
official_raw.zh: $jerusalem$圣墓教堂建于4世纪君士坦丁大帝时期，建筑群涵盖各各他山与基督墓穴，自此成为[ShowReligionGroupName('christian')]世界的至高圣地与核心朝圣中心。虽历经多次损毁与重建，这座圣殿始终由$christian_ADJ$各教派共同守护。

en:
Al-Quds, Jerusalem, is the third holiest city of Islam after Mecca and Medina, its sanctity concentrated on the Haram al-Sharif. Muslims believe Muhammad was carried there by night from Mecca and ascended to heaven from the rock at its heart; Jerusalem was the first direction of Muslim prayer before the Kaaba.

After the Arab conquest of 637 the caliph Umar founded a prayer house on the platform, and in 691 to 692 the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik raised the Dome of the Rock over the holy rock. The neighbouring Al-Aqsa Mosque was rebuilt by the Fatimid caliph al-Zahir after the earthquake of 1033.

Crusaders turned the sanctuary into a church and the Knights Templar headquarters after 1099, until Saladin retook Jerusalem in 1187 and restored Muslim worship. Ayyubid, Mamluk and Ottoman rulers then maintained it.
zh:
古德斯即耶路撒冷，是伊斯兰教仅次于麦加和麦地那的第三大圣城，其神圣性集中于谢里夫圣地。穆斯林相信穆罕默德夜间从麦加被带到此地，并从圣地中央的岩石登霄；在克尔白成为礼拜朝向之前，耶路撒冷曾是最早的礼拜朝向。

637年阿拉伯人征服后，哈里发欧麦尔在台地上建起礼拜所；691—692年，伍麦叶哈里发阿卜杜勒-马利克在圣石之上修建岩石圆顶寺。相邻的阿克萨清真寺在1033年地震后由法蒂玛哈里发扎希尔重修。

1099年后十字军把圣地改为教堂和圣殿骑士团总部，直到1187年萨拉丁收复耶路撒冷、恢复穆斯林礼拜。此后阿尤布、马穆鲁克和奥斯曼的统治者相继维护这处圣所。

en:
The Jogulamba Temple at Alampur stands near the confluence of the Tungabhadra and Krishna rivers in the northern Deccan. Jogulamba, whose name means Mother of Yogis in Telugu, is shown seated on a corpse with a scorpion, frog and lizard above her head.

Her shrine is counted fifth among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas; tradition holds that the upper teeth of Sati fell here when Vishnu dismembered her body. It shares its enclosure with the nine Navabrahma Shiva temples, raised in the seventh and eighth centuries under the Badami Chalukyas.

In 1390 Bahmani armies sacked and largely destroyed the temple, although the Vijayanagara emperor Harihara Raya II counter-attacked and fortified the complex. The priests had already carried Jogulamba's image to the nearby Bala Brahma temple, where it was worshipped in a secluded chamber for more than six centuries.
zh:
乔古兰巴神庙位于德干北部的阿拉姆普尔，靠近栋格珀德拉河与克里希纳河汇流之处。乔古兰巴之名在泰卢固语中意为瑜伽士之母，女神坐于尸体之上，头侧刻有蝎子、青蛙和蜥蜴。

其神庙位列十八处大性力佩特的第五处，相传毗湿奴肢解萨蒂遗体时，萨蒂的上齿落在此地。神庙与九座纳瓦婆罗贺摩湿婆庙同处一院，后者建于7至8世纪的巴达米遮娄其王朝时期。

1390年，巴赫马尼军队洗劫并严重摧毁了神庙，维查耶纳伽罗皇帝诃里诃罗二世随后发兵反击并加固庙区。祭司们事先已将乔古兰巴神像转移到附近的婆罗·婆罗贺摩庙，在密室中供奉达六个多世纪。

en:
Jyotisar is a shrine on the Jyotisar Sarovar tank, west of Thanesar in the Kurukshetra region, where Hindu tradition places the opening of the battle of the Mahabharata. Its name means the lake of light.

On the first day of fighting, Krishna is said to have answered the doubts of Arjuna, who shrank from killing his own kin, with the sermon that became the Bhagavad Gita, and to have revealed his universal form beneath a banyan tree. A banyan venerated as an offshoot of that tree rises at the water's edge.

In the 700s the Hindu scholar Adi Shankara identified Jyotisar as the exact spot of the discourse. An old Shiva temple on the site is said to have been worshipped at by both the Kauravas and the Pandavas, and the shrine forms one of the stops on the 48-kos circumambulation of Kurukshetra.
zh:
殊帝萨是坦内萨尔以西、库鲁克谢特拉地区殊帝萨池畔的一处圣所，印度教传统把《摩诃婆罗多》大战的开端放在这一带。殊帝萨意为光之池。

相传开战首日，阿周那不愿向同族挥兵，奎师那在此为他释疑，说出了后来成为《薄伽梵歌》的教言，并在一棵榕树下向他显现宇宙相；池畔的榕树被视为那棵神树的分枝。

8世纪时印度教学者阿迪·商羯罗确认这里正是宣说《薄伽梵歌》的确址。当地还有一座古老的湿婆庙，相传俱卢族与班度族都曾在此礼拜，这座圣所也是环库鲁克谢特拉48科斯巡礼路线上的一站。

en:
The Kaaba, which Muslims hold to be the House of God, was raised by Ibrahim and his son Ismail. Before Islam it was a Qurayshi sanctuary housing 360 idols; after Muhammad entered Mecca the idols were destroyed and the shrine rededicated to God.

Fire gutted the building during the Umayyad siege of 683, and in 693 the caliph Abd al-Malik rebuilt it on Qurayshi foundations, giving it a cube form. In 930 the Qarmatians carried off the Black Stone and held it until 952; after the floods of 1626 the Ottoman sultan Murad IV rebuilt the walls.

Circling the Kaaba seven times is the central rite of the hajj and umrah pilgrimages, and the kiswah that covers it is renewed every year.
zh:
穆斯林认为克尔白是真主之屋，由易卜拉欣与其子易斯马仪修建。前伊斯兰时代，这里是古莱什人的圣所，供奉着360尊偶像；穆罕默德进入麦加后捣毁偶像，将圣殿重新奉献给真主。

683年伍麦叶军队围攻麦加时大火焚毁殿身，693年哈里发阿卜杜勒-马利克在古莱什旧基上重建，奠定了克尔白的立方体形制。930年卡尔马特派劫走黑石，直到952年才将其归还；1626年洪水毁墙后，奥斯曼苏丹穆拉德四世加以重修。

环绕克尔白绕行七圈是朝觐和副朝的核心仪式，覆盖殿身的罩幕每年更换。

official_raw.en: Located in [ShowLocationName('mecca')] and most commonly known as al-Ka'ba, the $kaaba$ is the most sacred shrine of [ShowReligionGroupName('muslim')]. Covered by a black cloth known as Kiswah, it defines the direction of prayer (qibla) for all $muslim_ADJ$ prayers.
official_raw.zh: $kaaba$位于[ShowLocationName('mecca')]，更广为人知的名字叫做克尔白天房，其上覆盖着被称为罩幕的黑色锦幔，是[ShowReligionGroupName('muslim')]最神圣的圣地。所有$muslim_ADJ$信徒祷告时都要面朝这里。

en:
The Kalaram Temple stands in the Panchavati quarter of Nashik on the Godavari, the forest where the Ramayana says Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spent more than two years of their fourteen-year exile. It takes its name from its black stone image of Rama, kala meaning black, flanked by black images of Sita and Lakshmana.

A shrine stood here in the Rashtrakuta period of the seventh to eleventh centuries, and during the early Turkish invasions its Brahmins hid the idol in the Godavari. Around 1700 the Maratha sardar Rangarao Odhekar, guided by a dream, recovered the image and rebuilt the temple and reconsecrated the deity.

The building has fourteen entrance steps recalling the years of exile, eighty-four pillars, and a black Hanuman facing Rama's sanctum. The rebuilt temple became one of the principal Rama pilgrimage places of the Maratha Deccan.
zh:
黑罗摩神庙位于纳西克的潘查瓦蒂区、戈达瓦里河畔；《罗摩衍那》中，罗摩、悉多与罗什曼那流放十四年，曾在此林中居住两年有余。庙名来自罗摩的黑石像，“卡拉”意为黑色，悉多与罗什曼那的黑色神像与之并立。

此地早有古庙，历史可追溯至7至11世纪的罗湿陀罗拘陀时期；早期突厥入侵时，庙中婆罗门将神像沉入戈达瓦里河藏起。约1700年，马拉塔的萨达尔朗加拉奥·奥德卡尔受梦境指引，从河中打捞出神像，重建神庙并重新为神像开光。

庙宇入口有十四级台阶，象征流放的十四年，全庙立有八十四根石柱，还有一尊黑色哈奴曼像正对罗摩圣所。重建后的黑罗摩神庙成为马拉塔德干最重要的罗摩朝圣中心之一。

en:
The Kalighat Kali Temple stands on a ghat of the old Bhagirathi channel in the Bengal delta, its name combining Kali with the river landing where she is worshipped. The shrine is counted among the Shakta Pithas, for the Puranas teach that the toes of Sati's right foot fell here when Vishnu dismembered her body.

A place of goddess worship on this bank is named in the Bengali poem Mansar Bhasan of the 1400s and Kavi Kankan's Chandi of the 1600s. The temple was built in the Bengal ath-chala style, its eight-sloped roof imitating a thatched village hut.

Santosh Roy Chowdhury began work in 1798 and it was completed in 1809; Kashinath Roy added the Nat Mandir hall in 1835. Pilgrims bathe the image in the Snan Yatra. Kali Puja and the new moon nights draw the greatest crowds.
zh:
迦梨女神庙坐落在孟加拉三角洲古婆吉罗提河道的一处河坛上，庙名由迦梨女神与受祀的河坛合成。此庙位列性力佩特，往世书称毗湿奴肢解萨蒂遗体时，其右足脚趾坠落于此。

1400年代的孟加拉长诗《摩萨尔跋娑》和1600年代的《诗人坎坎·禅迪》提到这处河岸边的女神道场。庙宇采用孟加拉阿特-查拉风格，八面坡顶模仿乡村茅草屋。

桑托什·罗伊·乔杜里于1798年动工，1809年落成，卡西纳特·罗伊于1835年增建纳特曼迪尔乐舞殿。信众举行圣浴节为神像沐浴。迦梨普迦和各朔日之夜最是人潮汹涌。

en:
The Kalika Mata Temple crowns Pavagadh Hill above Champaner in eastern Gujarat. The goddess is venerated as Mahakali in the form of Durga or Chandi, and a Kali Yantra in the sanctum is dated to the 900s or 1000s. Counted among the Shakta Pithas, the hill is hallowed as the place where a toe of Sati's right foot fell.

Pavagadh was also a Jain pilgrimage: from 1113 the Svetambara Achalgacch honoured Mahakali as its protecting deity. The shrine long served both Jain and Hindu devotees.

In 1484 Mahmud Begada of Gujarat stormed the Pavagadh fort after a twenty-month siege and built his capital of Muhammadabad, the later Champaner, below; Humayun scaled the cliffs and took the fortress in 1535. Through these conquests the goddess kept her pilgrims, who gathered in thousands for the fair of Chitra Sud 8.
zh:
伽利伽·摩多神庙位于古吉拉特东部尚庞上方帕瓦加德山的顶峰。女神以摩诃迦梨的身份受祀，显现为难近母或禅底形态；殿中迦梨曼陀罗可断代至900—1000年代。此庙位列性力佩特，圣山被视为萨蒂右足脚趾坠落之地。

帕瓦加德也是耆那教朝圣中心：1113年起白衣派阿恰尔伽阇尊摩诃迦梨为该派护法神。神祠长期服务于耆那教与印度教信众。

1484年，古吉拉特苏丹马哈茂德·贝伽达经二十个月围攻攻陷帕瓦加德要塞，在山下营建新都穆罕默达巴德，即后来的尚庞；1535年胡马雍攀越悬崖夺取此堡。历经兵燹，女神香火不绝，每逢质多罗月白分八日的庙会，有数千信众朝山。

en:
Kamakhya crowns the Nilachal hills above Guwahati in Assam and is a centre of Tantric Hinduism, counted among the four oldest of the fifty-one Shakta Pithas, where the yoni of Sati is believed to have fallen. The underground sanctum holds no image but a natural rock fissure shaped like a yoni, fed by a perennial spring and worshipped as the goddess herself.

The cult grew from Kirata and tribal worship before the Mlechchha kings of Kamarupa adopted the shrine in the 9th century. Ruined during Hussein Shah's invasion in 1498, the temple was restored by the Koch dynasty: Vishwasingha revived worship and his son Nara Narayan completed its rebuilding in 1565 under his brother Chilarai.

The Ahoms took Kamrup by 1658 and secured it after the Battle of Itakhuli in 1681. The Ambubachi Mela celebrates the goddess's menstruation and draws Tantric pilgrims from Bengal and Assam.
zh:
卡马基雅寺高踞阿萨姆古瓦哈蒂的尼拉查尔山，是怛特罗印度教中心，位列五十一处性力派圣地中最古老的四处；相传萨蒂的约尼（女阴）坠落于此。地下密室中不立神像，只有一道天然岩石裂成约尼之形，底下常年泉水涌出，信众将其奉为女神本身。

这种崇拜源自基拉塔人与部落的信仰，9世纪迦摩缕波的蔑戾车王朝将神庙纳入王室护持。1498年侯赛因沙入侵时神庙被毁，科赫王朝的毗湿瓦辛哈恢复香火，其子那罗·那罗延在兄弟奇拉莱主持下于1565年完成重建。

阿洪姆人至1658年已夺取迦摩缕波，又在1681年伊塔胡利之战后控制此地。安布巴奇节庆祝女神的月事，吸引孟加拉与阿萨姆各地的怛特罗朝圣者。

en:
The Kamakshi Amman Temple lies in Kanchipuram, south-west of Chennai, and is dedicated to Kamakshi, a supreme form of the goddess Adi Shakti. The Pallava kings founded the shrine between the fifth and eighth centuries, and it is counted among the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas; its Varaha shrine is also honoured by Tamil Vaishnavas.

The goddess is seated in the lotus pose holding a noose, goad, sugarcane bow and flower arrow, with a Sri Yantra before her that tradition credits to Adi Shankara. The temple was enlarged in the 1300s and 1600s.

After the fall of Vijayanagara in 1565 the golden image of Kamakshi was carried from place to place for safety, and kept at Tiruvarur from 1739 to 1781. It was finally installed in a rebuilt Kanchipuram temple in 1783, under the care of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham.
zh:
爱目母神庙坐落于金奈西南的甘吉布勒姆，供奉至尊女神阿迪·夏克提的化身迦摩刹。帕拉瓦诸王于5—8世纪创建此庙，它被列为十八处大性力圣地之一；庙中的筏罗诃神龛也受泰米尔毗湿奴派尊崇。

女神像结莲花坐，手持套索、刺棒、甘蔗弓与花箭，像前供奉着相传由阿迪·商羯罗安置的室利坛城。神庙在14世纪和17世纪两度扩建。

1565年毗奢耶那伽罗沦落后，为安全起见，金铸的迦摩刹像被辗转迁移，1739—1781年间安奉于提鲁瓦鲁尔。1783年神像最终迎回重建的甘吉布勒姆神庙，由甘吉迦摩科提道场照管。

en:
Kanchipuram, the City of a Thousand Temples on the Palar river in Tamil Nadu, ranks among the seven Sapta Puri holy cities where Hindus seek liberation. From the sixth century it was the capital of the Pallavas; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang found in 640 a seat of Hindu, Buddhist and Jain learning.

The Cholas took the city about 890; Malik Kafur's invasion disrupted it in 1311. The Vijayanagara general Kumara Kampana conquered it in 1361 and restored Hindu worship.

After the Vijayanagara empire fell, rival powers fought over the city, and priests carried its temple idols south to safety between 1688 and 1707. It then passed to the Nawabs of the Carnatic and the East India Company. Fifteen of the 108 Vaishnava Divya Desam temples stand here, alongside the Shaiva temple of Ekambareswarar and the Kamakshi Amman shrine.
zh:
甘吉布勒姆位于泰米尔纳德的巴拉尔河畔，有千庙之城之称，也是印度教七圣城萨帕塔普里之一，信徒相信在此可求得解脱。6世纪起它成为帕拉瓦王朝的都城；640年中国求法僧玄奘到访时，这里是印度教、佛教与耆那教的学问中心。

约890年朱罗人攻占此城，1311年马利克·卡富尔的入侵使地方陷入混乱。1361年毗奢耶那伽罗将领库马拉·坎帕纳攻克此地，恢复印度教祭祀。

毗奢耶那伽罗帝国崩溃后，各方轮番争夺此城，1688—1707年间祭司们把神庙神像南运避难。此后它归卡纳蒂克纳瓦卜与英国东印度公司统治。毗湿奴派108处圣域中有15处在此，此外还有湿婆派的埃坎巴雷什瓦拉尔大庙与迦摩克希·安曼神庙。

en:
The Karpaka Vinayakar Temple is a rock-cut cave shrine dedicated to Ganesha in Pillayarpatti village, Sivaganga district of Tamil Nadu. Its earliest datable layer is a cave temple cut around 650 CE and attributed to the ruler Narasimhavarma; an archaic inscription suggests parts of the site may be a few centuries older.

The six-foot bas-relief of Ganesha in the sanctum has only two arms, his trunk curves to the right, giving him the local name Valampuri Vinayagar, and his left tusk is broken. The walls carry inscriptions from the 1000s to the 1200s.

The temple is one of the nine ancestral shrines of the Nagarathar merchant community, whose tradition dates its ties with the place to 714 CE. Later centuries added the gopuram, mandapams and temple tank, and the annual Brahmothsavam chariot festival and Vinayaka Chaturthi draw pilgrims.
zh:
羯波迦‑频那夜迦神庙是一座凿岩而成的伽内什石窟神庙，坐落在泰米尔纳德邦西瓦甘加县的皮莱亚尔帕蒂村。现存最早、可断代的部分是约650年凿成的石窟，相传由统治者纳拉辛哈瓦尔摩主持；一则更古的铭文说明遗址部分建筑可能还要早几个世纪。

殿内六英尺高的伽内什浮雕只有双臂，象鼻向右卷曲，当地人因而称其为瓦兰普里·毗那夜迦，左牙则已折断。庙墙保留着11—13世纪的铭文。

这座神庙是纳加拉塔尔商人群体的九大祖庙之一，该群体与神庙的渊源按其传统可追溯到714年。后世增建了瞿布罗高塔、厅堂和庙池；每逢一年一度的婆罗摩节神车游行与伽内什节，都有香客前来。

en:
Kashima Shrine is a Shintō shrine in Hitachi Province, east of the Kantō plain, dedicated to Takemikazuchi, a kami of thunder, war and the martial arts. Its cult dates to at least the seventh century, when a ritual hall was rebuilt in 649 on ground where the local kami was believed to have descended.

The Nakatomi clan, ancestors of the Fujiwara, made it a base for extending Yamato rule over the east and for campaigns against the Emishi, and its treasury kept a bucket said to be a trophy taken from the Emishi leader Aterui.

Minamoto no Yoritomo endowed it with estates, and the early Tokugawa shōguns rebuilt its halls: Ieyasu in 1605, Hidetada in 1619, and the tower gate given by Yorifusa in 1634. In 1687 the poet Matsuo Bashō recorded a pilgrimage there in his travel journal Kashima Kikō.
zh:
鹿岛神宫是位于常陆国、关东平原以东的神道教神社，祭祀雷神、战神与武术守护神建御雷神。其信仰至少可追溯到7世纪：649年当地在传为神明天降之处重建了祭殿。

中臣氏即藤原氏的前身，以神社为据点扩张大和朝廷在东国的统治、征讨虾夷，社中宝藏保存着据称取自虾夷首领阿弖流为的桶。

源赖朝向神社寄进庄园，德川幕府初期又由历代将军重建社殿：家康建于1605年，秀忠于1619年再建本社，赖房捐建的楼门成于1634年。1687年，诗人松尾芭蕉到此参拜，并在《鹿岛纪行》中记下这段旅程。

en:
The sun temple at Katarmal, a village in the Kumaon hills above Almora, is one of the rare Surya shrines built in the medieval Himalayas. It was raised in the ninth century by Katarmalla, a king of the Katyuri dynasty, whose masons bonded the stones with a mixture of lime and lentil paste.

Around the main sanctuary of the sun god, worshipped here as Burhadita or Vraddhaditya, stand forty-four smaller temples, with further shrines to Shiva and Parvati and to Lakshmi-Narayana. Its walls and carved wooden doors and panels carry the sculpture of the Katyuri school, blending north Indian plains traditions with local Himalayan forms.

After the Katyuri collapse the region was reunited by the Chand dynasty, who moved their capital to Almora in 1563. In 1791 Kumaon was absorbed by the expanding Kingdom of Nepal.
zh:
迦吒罗末罗太阳神庙坐落在阿尔莫拉上方库马翁山区的同名村庄，是中世纪喜马拉雅山区少见的苏利耶神庙之一。它由9世纪迦吒里王朝国王迦吒罗末罗兴建，工匠用石灰与豆糊混合成黏合剂砌石。

主殿供奉被称为布里哈迪塔或弗利达迪蒂亚的太阳神，周围环绕四十四座小庙，还有湿婆与帕尔瓦蒂、吉祥天女与那罗延的神龛。庙墙与雕花木门、木板上留有迦吒里流派的雕刻，融合了北印度平原传统与当地喜马拉雅风格。

迦吒里王朝衰落后，昌德王朝重新统一该地区，并于1563年迁都阿尔莫拉。1791年库马翁被扩张中的尼泊尔王国兼并。

en:
The Katas Raj complex in northern Punjab surrounds a sacred pond held to be fed by Shiva's tears when Sati died. Its name comes from the Sanskrit kataksha, tearful eyes.

The Chinese pilgrim Faxian described a temple here in the 4th century, and Xuanzang in the 7th century saw a Buddhist stupa attributed to Ashoka's age. The surviving Hindu temples were raised from the late 6th century under the Shahi kings of Gandhara and the Odi Shahi dynasty. Temple B dates to the late 500s, and the principal Temple A to the 900s.

Later Sikh rulers added a fort and haveli. Ranjit Singh came on pilgrimage in 1806, 1818 and 1824, and the Maha Shivaratri fair made Katas Raj a Hindu gathering place of western Punjab.
zh:
北旁遮普的迦多娑罗阇神庙群环绕着一方圣池；相传萨蒂死后湿婆流下的眼泪汇聚成池。其名来自梵语“迦多刹”，意为含泪的双眼。

4世纪中国求法僧法显记述过这里的一座神庙，7世纪玄奘见过一座传为阿育王时代的佛塔。现存印度教神庙由犍陀罗的夏希诸王与奥迪夏希王朝自6世纪末起陆续兴建：“B庙”可溯至500年代末，主庙“A庙”建于900年代。

后来的锡克统治者增建了堡垒与宅邸。兰吉特·辛格于1806、1818和1824年前来朝觐，大湿婆夜节的庙会使迦多娑罗阇成为西旁遮普的印度教聚地。

en:
Katori Shrine is the ichinomiya of Shimōsa Province and the head of some four hundred branch shrines, dedicated to Futsunushi, a kami of swords and lightning. The early eighth-century Hitachi Fudoki knew the shrine, whose guardians the Ō clan had migrated from Kyushu and allied with the Nakatomi of neighbouring Kashima.

As a tutelary of the Fujiwara it supplied the second deity of Kasuga Taisha when that shrine was founded in Nara. The Engishiki of 927 names it a myōjin taisha, one of only three shrines styled Jingū alongside Ise and Kashima.

Minamoto no Yoritomo and Ashikaga Takauji were among its samurai patrons, while its estates drew income from fishing rights and toll barriers. The Tokugawa shogunate rebuilt the shrine in 1607 and again in 1700, the latter rebuild giving the precinct its shape into the nineteenth century.
zh:
香取神宫是下总国一宫，也是约四百座香取神社的总本社，祭祀剑与雷之神经津主神。8世纪初的《常陆风土记》已提到这座神社，世代奉祀的多氏从九州迁来，与邻近鹿岛的中臣氏结盟。

香取神宫是藤原氏的守护神社，奈良春日大社创建时从这里分灵，供奉经津主神为第二祭神。927年的《延喜式》将它列为名神大社，是与伊势神宫、鹿岛神宫并列、仅有的三座称“神宫”的神社。

源赖朝、足利尊氏等武家先后寄进，神社还凭借渔业权和关卡关税获得收入。德川幕府于1607年、1700年两次重建社殿，后一次重建奠定了此后至19世纪的社域格局。

en:
The Kattu Narasimhaperumal Temple, also called the Azhagiya Singar temple, stands in Srirangam, the temple island in the Kaveri river. Its presiding god is Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu, known here as Varaprasadhi, the granter of boons. Though not counted among the 108 Divya Desams, it is ranked among the foremost Abhimana Sthalams, temples especially dear to Vishnu.

An inscriptional tradition attributes its construction in the ninth century to the Pandyan king Vallabadevan, while local legend claims the shrine is older than the Ranganathaswamy temple, with some dating it to the fifth century.

In the twelfth century the Vaishnava teacher Pillai Lokachariar delivered his discourses on the secrets of the Sri Vaishnava doctrine here. In the fifteenth century Manavala Mamunigal took charge of the temple's administration at the request of the Pandyan ruler Srisindarapandian, who provided for its upkeep.
zh:
卡图那罗辛哈佩鲁马尔神庙又称阿扎吉亚·辛加尔神庙，坐落在高韦里河中的神庙之岛斯里兰加姆。庙中主神是毗湿奴的人狮化身那罗辛哈，名号瓦拉普拉萨迪，意为赐福者。它不属于108座毗湿奴圣地迪维亚·德萨姆，却被列为最重要的阿比马纳斯塔拉姆之一，即毗湿奴格外眷顾的圣地。

据铭文传统，神庙是9世纪潘地亚国王瓦拉巴提婆所建；当地传说称这座神龛比兰加纳塔斯瓦米神庙还要古老，有人将其年代上推至5世纪。

12世纪，毗湿奴派导师皮莱洛卡查里亚尔曾在此宣讲室利毗湿奴派教义的秘要。15世纪，马纳瓦拉·马穆尼加尔应潘地亚统治者斯里辛达拉潘地亚之请接管庙务，国王则出资供养神庙。

en:
Kesariyaji Tirth, known as the Rishabhdeo temple, lies in the hills of Mewar in southern Rajasthan on the old trade road from Gujarat's seaports into the interior, drawing merchant patronage. Its holiest object is a black stone image of the first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha, called Kesariyaji from the legend of a devotee who offered saffron, kesar, equal to the weight of his son in thanksgiving.

The temple was raised in 874 under the Mewar ruler Rawal Khuyan, and an inscription of 1422 records repairs through the 1300s and 1400s. Merchants commissioned marble replicas that carried the cult into Svetambara temples across western India.

Digambara and Svetambara Jains and Vaishnava Hindus honoured the idol and contended for control from the fourteenth century through the favour of Mewar's rulers. In 1654 a statue of Marudevi, Rishabhanatha's mother, seated on an elephant was added before the sanctum.
zh:
吉娑哩耶圣所通称勒舍婆提婆神庙，坐落于拉贾斯坦南部梅瓦尔的丘陵中，处在从古吉拉特港口通往内陆的古商道上，得到商人供养。寺中最神圣的是黑石第一代祖师勒舍婆那陀像，通称吉娑哩耶，得名于一位信徒献上与儿子等重藏红花（kesar）谢神的传说。

神庙于874年梅瓦尔君主拉瓦尔·库扬在位时兴建，1422年的铭文记载了14至15世纪间的修缮。商人订制的大理石复刻像把信仰带到了西印度各地的白衣派寺庙。

天衣派与白衣派耆那教徒和毗湿奴派印度教徒都尊崇此像。从14世纪起，三派信众借梅瓦尔统治者的恩宠争夺神庙管理权；1654年，神殿前增设了勒舍婆那陀之母摩卢提毗乘象的造像。

en:
The Kichakeshwari Temple stands at Khiching in northern Odisha, the ancient capital of the Bhanja rulers. It honours Kichakeshwari, a form of Chamunda or Kali who was the family goddess of the Bhanja dynasty and the state deity of the Mayurbhanj chiefs.

The original shrine was raised in the 700s, built of black chlorite in the Kalinga style. Its hundred-foot rekha tower rises on a high platform behind carved walls, though vandalism left it in ruins for long periods.

The sanctum holds a ten-armed skeletal image of Chamunda-Kali with sunken belly and protruding ribs, wearing a garland of skulls and seated on a corpse. The compound also preserves an early brick shrine called the Itamundhi.
zh:
吉遮鸡湿伐梨神庙位于奥里萨北部的基青，这里曾是班阇统治者的古都。神庙供奉吉遮鸡湿伐梨，即旃蒙达（迦梨）的一种化身，她是班阇王朝的家族守护神，也是马乌尔班杰首领的国家女神。

原庙建于8世纪，以黑绿泥石筑成，属羯陵伽风格。百尺高的雷塔式圣塔立于高台之上，外壁雕有纹饰，但神庙曾遭破坏，长期沦为废墟。

圣所中是一尊十臂枯骨形旃蒙达—迦梨像：腹部凹陷、肋骨外露，颈挂骷髅花环，坐于一具尸身之上。庙院内还保留着一座名为伊塔蒙迪的早期砖殿。

en:
The Kodandarama Temple of the Belur country survives at Hiremagalur, near Chikkamagaluru in the Malnad hills, the old Hoysala heartland. Kodandarama means Rama bearing his bow, the kodanda, and the sanctum holds Rama with Sita on his right and Lakshmana on his left, posed as a wedding scene called Kalyana-rama; Hanuman shares their pedestal, though the scene precedes his first meeting with Rama.

Thought to be India's oldest continuously used Rama temple, it grew in stages: the sanctum and idol follow Ganga or Chola forms, the navaranga hall was added in the 1300s and the entrance hall in the 1500s.

Local tradition says Rama humbled Parashurama here, and Parashurama then asked to witness the wedding scene; the village was called Bhargavapuri, the town of Bhargava, where nine siddhas are said to have practised penance. A one-day temple yatra is held each February or March.
zh:
拘檀陀‑罗摩神庙现存于马尔纳德丘陵中的希雷马加卢尔，地近奇克马加卢尔，与贝卢鲁同属曷萨罗故地。“拘檀陀罗摩”意为持弓的罗摩：圣所中罗摩居中，悉多立于其右、罗什曼那立于其左，呈婚礼场景，称“吉祥罗摩”；哈奴曼像同处一座台基，尽管所表现的时刻尚在他与罗摩初遇之前。

它被认为是印度持续使用的最古老罗摩神庙，建造历经数阶段：圣所与神像为西恒伽或朱罗风格，14世纪增建聚会厅，16世纪又加前门厅。

当地传说称，罗摩曾在此折服持斧罗摩，后者遂请求一见婚礼景象；该村古称波尔加瓦普里，意为“婆罗伽瓦之城”，传说曾有九位悉达仙人在此苦修。每年二三月间还会举行为期一天的游神朝圣。

en:
The Kola Valvill Ramar Temple stands at Tiruvelliyangudi in the Kaveri delta of the Tamil country. Vishnu is worshipped here reclining as Kola Valvill Ramar, with Lakshmi as Maragathavalli; the shrine is among the 108 Divya Desams praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham of the Alvar saints between the sixth and ninth centuries.

Built in the Dravidian style, its brick shrines and two tanks are enclosed by granite walls and entered through a multi-tiered gopuram. Legend says Vishnu appeared here to the sage Markandeya.

The place is linked to Vishnu's dwarf avatar: legend says that when the demon preceptor Sukracharya took the shape of an insect to block King Bali's ritual gift of land, Vishnu blinded him with a spear point; Sukracharya did penance here to recover his eye, and his lamp is still honoured as the Nethra Deepam. The sage Parasara is also said to have worshipped here.
zh:
拘缡伐鼻利‑罗秣神庙坐落于泰米尔地区高韦里河三角洲的蒂鲁韦利扬古迪。庙中毗湿奴以侧卧的拘缡伐鼻利·罗秣之相受人敬拜，其配偶吉祥天女名为玛拉伽塔瓦利；它是毗湿奴派一百零八座圣庙之一，6至9世纪阿尔瓦尔圣徒的《四千圣诗》曾加以赞颂。

神庙为达罗毗荼风格，砖砌神龛与两处圣池外绕花岗岩围墙，入口是多层瞿布罗门楼。传说毗湿奴曾在此向摩根德耶仙人显圣。

此地又与毗湿奴的侏儒化身有关：相传阿修罗之师苏揭罗化作虫豸，阻挠巴利王行献地之礼，毗湿奴以矛尖刺瞎其目；苏揭罗在此苦行复明，他的明灯仍被尊为“眼灯”。相传仙人波罗娑罗也曾在此礼拜。

en:
The Konark Sun Temple is a vast thirteenth-century shrine of Surya on the Odisha coast, about thirty-five kilometres north-east of Puri. King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, who reigned from 1238 to 1264, built it around 1250 on the site of an older sun temple, whose image was re-consecrated within the new building. Conceived as Surya's colossal chariot, the stone complex carries twenty-four carved wheels nearly four metres across and is drawn by seven galloping horses, the twelve pairs of wheels matching the twelve months of the Hindu calendar. Rising perhaps sixty-nine metres in its prime, it was the summit of Kalinga architecture, its walls covered in divine figures and erotic mithuna reliefs; its name joins the Sanskrit words kona, angle, and arka, the sun.

An inscription of 1384 and the Akbar-era Ain-i-Akbari both describe a complete, flourishing temple, but the great sanctuary tower collapsed in the late 1500s; Kalapahar, a general of the Bengal sultanate, is believed to have sacked Konark around 1568. European sailors called the ruin the Black Pagoda, a Bay of Bengal landmark recorded as early as 1676 beside Puri's White Pagoda. In the last quarter of the 1700s Maratha rulers moved the Aruna pillar from its entrance to the Lion's Gate of the Jagannath temple in Puri, after which the site lay deserted in coastal forest until the East India Company took Odisha in 1803 and began its conservation. The annual Chandrabhaga Mela kept pilgrims coming through the centuries of decay.
zh:
科纳克太阳神庙是奥里萨海岸一座规模宏大的13世纪苏利耶神庙，位于补梨东北约三十五公里处。东恒伽王朝的那罗辛诃·提婆一世（1238—1264年在位）于约1250年在一座更古老太阳神庙的旧址上建成此庙，旧庙神像被重新开光后迎入新殿。整座石构建筑群被设计成苏利耶的巨型战车：二十四只直径近四米的精雕车轮、七匹奔腾的石马牵引战车，十二对车轮对应印度教历的十二个月。神庙盛时高约六十九米，是羯陵伽建筑艺术的巅峰，墙上布满神像与男女欢爱的米图纳浮雕。庙名由梵语“科纳”（角）与“阿尔迦”（太阳）二字合成。

1384年的一方铭文和阿克巴时代的《阿克巴则例》都还记载着一座完整兴盛的神庙，但宏伟的主殿高塔在16世纪末倒塌；一般认为，孟加拉苏丹国将领卡拉帕哈尔约在1568年洗劫了科纳克。欧洲水手把这片废墟称作“黑塔”，早在1676年的记载中它已是孟加拉湾上的航标，与补梨的“白塔”遥遥相对。18世纪最后二十五年，马拉塔统治者把庙门口的阿楼那石柱迁到补梨札格纳特神庙的狮门之前，此后遗址便荒废在沿海丛林中；直到1803年英国东印度公司取得奥里萨，保护工作才开始。一年一度的旃陀罗跋伽庙会则让香客们在庙宇残破的数百年间仍持续前来朝拜太阳神。

en:
Koneswaram crowns Konesar Malai at Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's east coast. Foremost among the island's five Pancha Ishwaram Shiva shrines, it was honoured as Dakshina Kailasam, the Kailash of the south. Its name goes back to the Sanskrit Gokarnesvara.

Pallava craftsmen built its thousand-pillared hall between 537 and 668. Pallava, Pandya and Chola dynasties gave to the shrine, which reached its greatest age under the Cholas and the Sinhalese king Gajabahu II, its benefactor from 1131 to 1153.

Between 1622 and 1624 the Portuguese sacked the complex, threw its images into the sea and built Fort Fredrick from its stones. Some surviving idols were transferred in 1632 to a new temple inland, while a single pillar remained on Swami Rock above the bay; the annual Ther chariot festival kept its name alive among the Tamils of the east coast.
zh:
亭可马里寺雄踞斯里兰卡东海岸亭可马里的科内萨尔山角，是岛上五大湿婆圣庙“潘查伊湿婆罗”中地位最高的一座，被尊为“南凯拉斯”。其名可追溯至梵语“戈卡尔纳湿婆罗”。

537年至668年间，帕拉瓦工匠建起千柱大厅。此后帕拉瓦、潘地亚与朱罗三朝施舍神庙，它在朱罗时代和僧伽罗国王迦阇巴忽二世（1131—1153年间护持神庙）的支持下进入鼎盛。

1622年至1624年，葡萄牙人洗劫庙群，将神像投入大海，并用庙石修建了弗雷德里克堡。部分幸存神像于1632年迁至内陆的新庙，旧庙仅余一根石柱立在海湾上方的斯瓦米岩上；一年一度的神车节让科内斯瓦拉姆之名在东海岸泰米尔人中流传。

en:
The Kothandaramaswamy Temple stands at Dhanushkodi on Pamban Island. Dedicated to Rama, it takes its name from his bow, the kothandam held by the main idol, grouped with images of Lakshmana, Sita, Hanuman and Vibhishana. It is among the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of the Vaishnava tradition.

Tradition identifies this shore as the place where Vibhishana, Ravana's younger brother, fled from Lanka and surrendered to Rama after his warning to return Sita was rejected. Rama welcomed him despite his vanara army's suspicions and, after Ravana's fall, crowned him king of Lanka here, a story painted on the shrine's inner walls.

Probably raised between the tenth and fifteenth centuries, the temple shared the island's fortunes. Malik Kafur's forces raided Rameswaram in 1311, the island passed to Vijayanagara in 1520, and the Sethupati rajas of Ramanathapuram later patronised its pilgrim shrines.
zh:
拘旦陀‑罗摩斯瓦米神庙位于班本岛的达那斯科迪。庙奉罗摩，得名于主神手中所持的弓“拘旦陀”，神像与罗什曼那、悉多、哈奴曼和维毗沙那并列；它位列毗湿奴派一百零八座阿比摩纳圣地之一。

相传这片海岸正是维毗沙那投奔罗摩之处：罗波那的幼弟维毗沙那劝兄归还悉多未果，逃离楞伽前来归降。猴军虽有疑虑，罗摩仍接纳了他；罗波那败亡后，罗摩又在此为维毗沙那举行楞伽王位的灌顶礼，这段故事绘在神庙内壁之上。

神庙可能建于10至15世纪，与海岛共历变迁。1311年马利克·卡富尔的军队洗劫拉梅斯沃勒姆，1520年海岛转入毗奢耶那伽罗治下，后来拉马纳塔普拉姆的塞图帕蒂王公又资助了岛上的朝圣神庙。

en:
The Kutubiyya is the largest mosque of Marrakesh, standing in the southwestern medina near the Jemaa el-Fnaa square. Its name, the Booksellers' Mosque, comes from the book vendors who once crowded the souk at its walls.

It was founded in 1147 by the Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min after he took Marrakesh from the Almoravids, whose mosques he condemned as wrongly oriented and demolished. He rebuilt it around 1158, and its seventy-seven-metre minaret was probably finished under Ya'qub al-Mansur around 1195. Abd al-Mu'min also moved here the Almoravid minbar commissioned in 1137 by Ali ibn Yusuf from a Cordoba workshop, fitted with a mechanism that made it glide forward for prayers.

The Kutubiyya supplied the model for the Giralda of Seville and the Hassan Tower of Rabat. After neglect in the seventeenth century, it was restored in the eighteenth.
zh:
库图比亚清真寺是马拉喀什规模最大的清真寺，坐落在老城西南、杰马夫纳广场附近。它的名字意为“书商清真寺”，得名于曾云集在寺墙下集市里的书商。

1147年，穆瓦希德王朝哈里发阿卜杜勒·慕敏从穆拉比特王朝手中夺取马拉喀什后修建此寺；他宣称前朝清真寺的礼拜方向有误而将其拆毁。他于1158年前后重建此寺，高77米的宣礼塔可能约在1195年雅各布·曼苏尔在位时完工。阿卜杜勒·慕敏还把穆拉比特王朝的敏拜尔讲经坛移到这里：它是阿里·伊本·优素福于1137年委托科尔多瓦工匠制作的，配有机械装置，礼拜时能自行滑出。

库图比亚为塞维利亚的吉拉达钟楼和拉巴特的哈桑塔提供了蓝本。17世纪它一度荒废，18世纪得到修缮。

en:
The Krishna Janmasthan at Mathura marks the prison cell where Hindu tradition says Krishna was born to Devaki and Vasudeva, who were held captive by Krishna's uncle Kamsa, the king of Mathura. Krishna's great-grandson Vajranabh is credited with the first shrine on the spot.

The Gupta emperor Chandragupta II rebuilt a temple there around 400. Mahmud of Ghazni plundered Mathura in 1017 and burned its temples, and an inscription of 1150 records a new white Vishnu temple raised by Jajja. Sikandar Lodi of Delhi destroyed the shrines early in the sixteenth century, yet the saints Chaitanya and Vallabhacharya came to worship at the birthplace.

In 1618 Raja Vir Singh Deo of Orchha built an octagonal Keshavdeva temple in red sandstone. Aurangzeb had it demolished in 1670 and raised the Shahi Eidgah mosque on its foundations; Mathura passed to British control in 1804.
zh:
奎师那诞生地位于马图拉，相传奎师那在这里的一间囚室中降生：他的父母提婆吉和婆苏提婆被奎师那的舅父、马图拉国王刚沙囚禁。相传奎师那的曾孙瓦吉拉纳巴最先在此立庙。

约400年，笈多皇帝旃陀罗笈多二世在此重建神庙。1017年，加兹尼的马哈茂德劫掠马图拉、焚毁诸庙；1150年的铭文记载，贾贾又建起一座洁白的毗湿奴神庙。16世纪初，德里苏丹锡坎达尔·洛迪捣毁神庙，但柴坦尼亚和伐拉巴阇利耶等圣人仍来诞生地朝拜。

1618年，奥尔切土王维尔·辛格·德夫建起一座红砂岩筑成的八角形凯舍瓦提婆神庙。1670年，奥朗则布下令拆毁神庙，在原址上修建皇家会礼清真寺；1804年，马图拉转入英国控制之下。

en:
The Kukkuteswara Temple stands in the ancient town of Pithapuram in Andhra, called Pishtapura in the Gupta emperor Samudragupta's pillar inscription of about 350. Dedicated to Shiva as Kukkuteswara, the Lord of the Rooster, it houses a self-manifested crystal linga and a Nandi carved from a single stone.

Its enclosure also contains the shrine of Puruhutika Devi, among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas, so the complex is revered in both the Saivite and the Shakta traditions. The Skanda Purana praises Pithapuram as a holy place, and in the fourteenth century it was the birthplace of the saint Sripada Sri Vallabha.

After the rule of the Velanati Chodas and local Pitapuram Chalukyas in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, the town passed under the Reddi kings and later Muslim rulers. The temple remained a pilgrimage goal, drawing crowds for Maha Shivaratri and Navaratri.
zh:
库库特斯瓦拉神庙位于安得拉古城毗多补罗；约350年笈多皇帝沙摩陀罗·笈多的石柱铭文称此地为毗什多补罗。神庙供奉以雄鸡形象显现的湿婆库库特斯瓦拉，内有自生水晶林伽和整石雕成的难迪牛。

庙院之中还有普鲁胡胡提卡女神殿，位列十八处大性力佩特，因此整个建筑群受到湿婆派和性力派尊崇。《塞建陀往世书》称美毗多补罗为圣地，14世纪的圣人室利波陀·室利·瓦拉巴也诞生于此。

12至13世纪，此地先后由韦拉那提·朱罗和本地的毗多补罗遮娄其统治，其后归入雷迪国王与穆斯林政权。神庙仍是朝圣目标，湿婆夜和九夜节吸引大批信众。

en:
Kulpakji, also called the Kolanupaka Temple, is a Svetambara Jain temple at Kolanupaka in Telangana. Jain tradition traces the site back roughly two millennia and credits the legendary king Bharata Chakravartin with its founding, while the surviving temple took shape from the ninth century, when the Kalachuri ruler Shankaragana granted twelve villages for its upkeep.

It flourished as a Jain centre under the Rashtrakutas and Western Chalukyas: a Kannada inscription of the Chalukya king Someshvara III dated 1125 records its teachers and monasteries. The temple enshrines images of Rishabhanatha, Neminatha and Mahavira, the last a green-stone figure famed as Manikyaswami, which the fourteenth-century monk Jinaprabhasuri celebrated in his pilgrimage work Vividha Tirtha Kalpa.
zh:
屈禄波耆寺又称科拉努帕卡寺，是特伦甘纳邦科拉努帕卡村的一座白衣派耆那教寺庙。耆那教传统将该地上溯约两千年，相传为传说中的婆罗多转轮王所建；现存庙宇则成形于9世纪，当时迦罗珠利君主商羯罗伽纳曾拨赐十二座村庄供养。

罗湿陀罗拘陀与西遮娄其时期，这里发展为耆那教重镇：1125年西遮娄其国王索梅什瓦拉三世的一方卡纳达语碑铭记载了当地的导师与寺院。寺内供奉勒舍婆那陀、尼弥那陀和大雄三尊祖师像，其中大雄像以绿石雕成，号称“摩尼格湿瓦米”；14世纪僧人金波罗婆苏利在其朝圣著作《诸圣地纪》中曾专门记述此像。

en:
The Kumano Sanzan are the three great shrines of the Kii peninsula, Hongū, Hayatama and Nachi, whose kami were worshipped together as the Kumano Gongen, buddhas and native gods fused into one faith. The Nachi waterfall drew hermits of Shugendō.

The first imperial pilgrimage was made by Emperor Uda in 908, and over the next 374 years emperors and retired emperors came ninety-four times. Pilgrims followed the Kumano Kodō trails, resting at the ninety-nine Oji shrines built between the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, seeking healing and rebirth in this world and the next.

In the Muromachi period the flow of samurai and peasants became so constant it was called the ant pilgrimage. Under the Tokugawa it joined the Ise pilgrimage as a mass devotion, while more than three thousand branch shrines carried the cult across Japan.
zh:
熊野三山是纪伊半岛的三座大社——熊野本宫大社、熊野速玉大社与熊野那智大社，三地神祇合称熊野权现，是佛教诸佛与日本本土神灵融为一体的信仰。那智瀑布吸引着修验道的隐士。

908年，宇多天皇开启了首次天皇熊野参拜；此后374年间，天皇与上皇共巡幸94次。朝圣者沿熊野古道跋涉，在12至13世纪修建的九十九座王子社沿途歇脚，祈求身心疗愈与来世解脱。

室町时代，武士和平民的参拜队伍连绵不绝，被称为“蚂蚁的熊野参拜”。德川治下，它与伊势参拜并列为群众性的信仰活动，三千余座熊野分社也把这一信仰播撒到日本各地。

en: The Kurma Varadaraja Swamy Temple is an ancient Vishnu shrine at Kurmai near Palamaner in present-day Andhra Pradesh, where the god is worshipped in his tortoise avatar Kurma as Varadarajaswamy; it is one of only five Kurma temples in India, and local tradition credits the Pallava kings with its foundation and a local chief, Chenge Gowda, with its rebuilding.
zh: 拘利摩‑伐罗陀罗阇斯瓦米神庙是一座古老的毗湿奴神庙，位于今印度安得拉邦帕拉马内尔附近的拘利摩村，供奉以龟化身俱利摩显现、号为伐罗陀罗阇斯瓦米的毗湿奴，是全印仅有的五座俱利摩神庙之一；当地传说它由帕拉瓦诸王始建，后经地方首领琴盖·高达重建。

en:
The Kurmanathaswamy Temple at Srikurmam, on the Kalinga coast of Andhra Pradesh, is dedicated to Kurma, the tortoise avatar of Vishnu. It is the only known Indian temple built before the fourteenth century for that form. The sanctum houses a tortoise image and an anthropomorphic Vishnu with Lakshmi.

It originally stood as a Shiva shrine, but in 1113 the Eastern Ganga king Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva converted it into a Vaishnava temple, an event recorded in its earliest inscriptions. Its walls and processional corridor were raised in a fusion of Kalinga and Dravidian styles, with later additions by King Anangabhima Deva III.

Srikurmam became a centre of Vaishnavism in medieval Kalinga and the guru-pitha of the Ganga kings of Utkala. Naraharitirtha, a disciple of Madhvacharya, made it a seat of Madhwa activity and defended it against raids from the forest-dwelling Sabaras.
zh:
俱利摩神庙位于安得拉邦羯陵伽海岸的斯里俱利摩村，供奉毗湿奴的龟化身俱利摩，是已知唯一一座在14世纪以前为这一化身修建的印度神庙。圣所中同时供奉龟形神像以及与吉祥天女相伴的人形毗湿奴像。

它最初是湿婆神庙，1113年东恒伽王朝国王阿南塔跋摩·朱达恒伽提婆将其改为毗湿奴派神庙，此事见于庙中最早的铭文。庙墙和绕行廊以羯陵伽与达罗毗荼混合风格建成，阿南加比马·提婆三世时期又有增建。

中世纪时，斯里俱利摩成为羯陵伽重要的毗湿奴派中心，也是乌特伽罗恒伽诸王的祖师道场。摩陀婆阿阇梨的弟子那罗哈利提尔塔后来把它建成摩陀婆派的活动中心，并抵御了森林土著萨巴拉人的袭击。

en:
The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, the Monastery of the Caves, overlooks the Dnipro in Kyiv. In 1051 the monk Anthony settled in a cave and gathered disciples; Prince Iziaslav I gave the hill to the monks, who built their monastery with architects from Constantinople.

It became a religious and cultural centre of Kyivan Rus, where monks wrote the Primary Chronicle and the Kyiv Caves Patericon. Its wealth drew repeated attacks: the Cumans plundered it in 1096, Batu Khan's Mongols stormed it in 1240, and Tatar raids of 1416 and 1482 burned it.

Rebuilt each time, it won stauropegion rights directly under the Patriarch of Constantinople in the later sixteenth century and took the title of lavra. After the Union of Brest, the Ostrogski family secured it for Orthodoxy in 1613; its printing house, opened in the 1620s, and its school made Kyiv a centre of Orthodox learning.
zh:
基辅洞窟修道院坐落于基辅，俯瞰第聂伯河。1051年，修士安东尼在山中洞穴定居，身边聚集起一批弟子；伊贾斯拉夫一世将山丘赐给修士，修道院由来自君士坦丁堡的建筑师修建。

它成为基辅罗斯的宗教与文化中心，修士们在此撰写《往年纪事》和《基辅洞窟修士传》。财富也引来反复攻掠：1096年库曼人劫掠，1240年拔都的蒙古军攻陷，1416年和1482年又两度被鞑靼人焚毁。

修道院屡毁屡建，16世纪下半叶获得君士坦丁堡牧首授予的直属特权，改称“拉夫拉”。布列斯特联合后，1613年经奥斯特罗格斯基家族支持才确保留在东正教会手中；1620年代开办的印刷所和修道院学校使基辅成为东正教的学术中心。

en:
Kykkos Monastery stands in the Troodos Mountains in Cyprus and is the island's richest Orthodox house. It was founded in the late eleventh century under Emperor Alexios I Komnenos, after the hermit Esaias, according to tradition, persuaded the governor Manuel Boutoumites to fetch from Constantinople an icon of the Virgin held to have been painted by the Apostle Luke. According to the tradition, the emperor's daughter was healed as the icon sailed to Cyprus.

The icon has been veiled ever since, its covering said to blind anyone who looks upon it. The Patriarch of Alexandria Gerasimos was the last man recorded to have seen it, in 1669.

Fire destroyed the church three times, and the church dates from 1745. In 1760 Cypriots credited the veiled icon with delivering the island from a plague of locusts, while pilgrims carried its fame across the Orthodox world.
zh:
基科斯修道院坐落在塞浦路斯特罗多斯山脉，是岛上最富有的东正教修道院。它建于11世纪末阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁皇帝在位时：相传隐修士以赛亚说服总督曼努埃尔·布图米特斯，从君士坦丁堡请来相传为使徒路加亲手所绘的圣母圣像。相传圣像运往塞浦路斯途中，皇帝之女的病也因此痊愈。

这尊圣像一直被遮盖，传说窥视者会失明。有记载最后见过它的人是1669年的亚历山大牧首格拉西莫斯。

教堂三次毁于火灾，现存教堂建于1745年。1760年，塞浦路斯人相信是这尊蒙面圣像使全岛躲过蝗灾；朝圣者则把它的名声传遍了东正教世界。

en:
The Lakshmi Narasimha Temple stands at the foot of Mangalagiri, the Auspicious Hill, in Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh, and is counted among the eight great Narasimha shrines of India. It is the lowest of three Narasimha temples on the hill, the others standing on its slope and summit. Tradition holds that the Pandava Yudhishthira discovered the shrine.

The Vijayanagara kings were its patrons: Krishnadevaraya visited in the sixteenth century, and a pillar inscription dated 1520 records grants of villages. After long rule by the Golconda Nawabs, the town survived a raid by Hyder Jung in 1780 and Pindari looting in 1816.

The temple's landmark, an eleven-storeyed gopuram 153 feet high, was raised in 1807 to 1809 by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu of Amaravati.
zh:
拉克什米‑那罗辛哈神庙坐落在安得拉邦贡土尔县曼加拉吉里，即吉祥山的山脚下，被列为印度八大那罗辛哈神庙之一。山上共有三座那罗辛哈神庙，另外两座分别在山坡和山顶。相传神龛是般度族长子坚战发现的。

毗奢耶那伽罗诸王是神庙的施主：克里希纳德瓦拉亚于16世纪亲临此地，一根1520年的石柱铭文记录了村庄的施赠。在戈尔孔达纳瓦布长期统治之后，此地又经历了1780年海德尔·忠格的袭击和1816年平达里匪帮的劫掠。

神庙的标志——高153英尺、共十一层的戈普拉姆门楼，是阿马拉瓦蒂的王公瓦西雷迪·文卡塔德里·奈杜在1807—1809年间修建的。

en:
The Lakshmi Temple is a small shrine in the Western Group at Khajuraho, the temple city raised by the Chandela dynasty. It was built around 930 to 950, but its name is a misnomer: it began as the Garuda shrine of the neighbouring Lakshmana Temple, for the bird mount of Vishnu is traditionally housed in a small pavilion directly facing his master's sanctum.

The modest square plan, plain side walls and tiny sanctum are typical of such a vahana shrine, whose main image showed Garuda seated with Vishnu. In later centuries the doorway carvings were defaced and the statues beheaded, and a damaged image of the goddess Brahmani was placed inside, which devotees then took to worshipping as Lakshmi.
zh:
吉祥天女神庙是昌德拉王朝所建神庙之城克久拉霍西庙群中的一座小殿。它约建于930至950年，但名字是后世误称：它最初是相邻拉克什曼纳神庙的迦楼罗神龛，按照传统，毗湿奴的坐骑迦楼罗要安奉在正对主神圣殿的小亭里。

朴素的方形台基、素面无饰的侧墙和狭小的圣室，都是这类坐骑神龛的典型形制，龛中主像原是与毗湿奴同坐的迦楼罗。后来门楣雕刻被毁、神像遭砍头，一尊破损的婆罗诃弥女神像被移入殿中，信众便把她当作吉祥天女礼拜。

en:
The Lakshminarasimha Temple at Haranhalli, not far from the Hoysala capital of Dvarasamudra, is a triple-shrine Vishnu temple in the Vesara style. It and the nearby Someshvara Temple, dedicated to Shiva, were completed in the 1230s at the expense of three brothers, Peddanna Heggade, Sovanna and Kesanna.

Inscriptions show that the temple was first named after Keshava, a form of Vishnu, and only later took the name Lakshminarasimha. Its three sanctums hold images of Venugopala, Keshava and Lakshminarasimha. The building blends late Chalukya and early Hoysala features: a platform serving as a circumambulation path, a single tower over the central shrine, and walls lined with Vaishnava reliefs and miniature towers.
zh:
哈兰哈利的拉克什米那罗辛哈神庙距曷萨拉都城德瓦拉萨穆德拉不远，是一座维萨拉风格的三圣所毗湿奴神庙。它与附近供奉湿婆的索梅什瓦拉神庙一样，都是13世纪30年代由佩达纳·赫加德、索万纳和凯萨纳三兄弟出资建成的。

铭文显示，神庙最初以毗湿奴的化身凯沙瓦命名，后来才改名拉克什米那罗辛哈。三间圣所中分别供奉维努戈帕拉、凯沙瓦和拉克什米那罗辛哈像。建筑融合了遮娄其晚期与曷萨拉早期的特征：台基兼作绕行通道，中央圣所上耸立独塔，墙面布满毗湿奴教浮雕和微型塔。

en:
Llullaillaco is a dormant stratovolcano in the Puna de Atacama, above Antofagasta; its Quechua name joins llulla, false or deceitful, and yaku, water, because the snowmelt vanishes into the dry earth instead of feeding streams.

The high peaks were apus, sacred ancestors and wak'as in Inca religion, and between 1470 and 1532 the Inca Empire made the summit a stage for the capacocha rite.

Children chosen from communities across the empire were brought to Cusco and then led along straight ceque pilgrimage routes to the mountain, prepared for months with coca leaves and chicha and buried near the summit as offerings to the apu, to intercede for harvests, weather and the cohesion of the empire. A capacocha performed here between the 1460s and the early 1500s took three children, whose bodies the freezing, rainless peak preserved along with their finery.
zh:
尤耶亚科山是阿塔卡马高原上一座休眠的层状火山，雄踞安托法加斯塔之上。其克丘亚语名由llulla（虚假、欺瞒）与yaku（水）组成，因为融水渗入干涸的土地，并不汇成溪流。

在印加宗教中，高峰是阿普——神圣的祖先与圣所；1470年至1532年间，印加帝国把山顶作为卡帕科查祭祀的舞台。

帝国各社群选出的孩童先被带往库斯科，再沿笔直的塞克朝圣路线登上高山；他们经数月准备，服食古柯叶、饮用奇恰酒，最后被安放在近峰顶处献祭给阿普，为丰收、天时与帝国的凝聚祈福。15世纪60年代至16世纪初，这里举行的一场卡帕科查献祭了三名孩童；寒冷无雨的峰顶将他们的遗体与华服一同保存下来。

en:
The Maa Dewri Temple lies in Diuri village near Tamar, Jharkhand, where the Munda and Bhumij tribes worshipped the goddess in a sacred grove known as Dewri Diri, the sacred stone of Diuri.

Tradition dates the stone temple to about 1300, when Kera, a king of Singhbhum, is said to have prayed here after losing a battle and, having regained his kingdom with the goddess's blessing, raised a shrine of interlocking stones without mortar and installed the sixteen-armed image of Maa Dewri.

The raja of Tamar later adopted her worship and brought a Brahmin priest, giving the temple its custom of six days of ritual led by the tribal Pahan and one day by a Brahmin Panda. Devotees tie red and yellow threads on bamboo for the fulfilment of vows, returning to untie them when their prayers are answered.
zh:
提乌梨神庙位于贾坎德塔马尔附近的迪乌里村；蒙达和布米吉部落在一处名为提乌梨·迪里的圣林中敬拜这位女神，意为迪乌里的圣石。

相传约1300年，辛格布姆国王凯拉战败后在此祈祷，蒙女神庇佑而复国，遂不用灰浆、以石块交错咬合砌成石庙，并供奉十六臂的提乌梨女神像。

塔马尔的王公后来也皈依女神，带来婆罗门祭司，由此形成一周六天由部落祭司帕汉主持仪轨、一天由婆罗门潘达主持的制度。信众在竹架上系上红黄丝线许愿，愿望达成后再回来解开丝线。

en:
The Mahadev Temple at Deobaloda, near Durg in Chhattisgarh, is a sandstone Shiva shrine raised in the 1200s under the Kalachuris of Ratnapura, a Haihaya dynasty. Local legend holds that it was completed in only six months, giving it the nickname six-month temple.

Facing east, the building pairs a square sanctum with a pillared Navaranga hall, though its Nagara-style spire has not survived. The sanctum keeps a lingam; the temple walls bear divine figures and scenes of hunting and bull-fighting, while a stone Nandi watches before the entrance.

Beside the temple lies a stepped kund, said in folk tale to hide a tunnel to the ancient temple town of Arang. The shrine remained a place of pilgrimage under the later Haihaya rajas, whose kingdom accepted the suzerainty of the Marathas of Nagpur in 1740, and villagers still gather there for the fair of Maha Shivaratri.
zh:
大天神庙位于恰蒂斯加尔杜尔格附近的德奥巴罗达，是1200年代海诃耶系的拉特纳普拉卡拉楚里王朝治下兴建的砂岩湿婆神庙。当地相传它仅用六个月便告竣工，因而得了“六月庙”的别称。

神庙朝东，方形密室与柱厅那瓦朗伽相配，那伽罗式塔尖已不存。密室中供着林伽；神庙墙面上雕有神像、狩猎和斗牛场景，一尊石牛南迪在门前守望。

庙旁有一座阶梯圣池，民间传说池底藏着一条通往古城阿兰格的隧道。在后来的海诃耶罗阇治下，此庙仍是朝圣场所；该王国于1740年接受那格浦尔马拉塔人的宗主权，周围乡村的百姓每逢大湿婆夜节仍聚集于此赶庙。

en:
Mahakaleshwar is a Shiva temple in the ancient city of Ujjain, on the Shipra river in Malwa, and one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. Ujjain was the capital of Avanti and a sacred city of Hinduism, where the Simhastha Kumbh Mela is held every twelve years.

The lingam is held to be self-manifested, and the presiding image faces south as Dakshinamurti, a feature unique among the Jyotirlingas; the shrine is also counted among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas, where Sati's upper lip is said to have fallen.

The temple was destroyed during Iltutmish's raid on Ujjain in 1234 and 1235, when the lingam was dismantled and thrown into a neighbouring pond. It was rebuilt in the eighteenth century under Maratha rule by the diwan Ramachandra Sukthankar. A great fair gathers here for Maha Shivaratri, with worship lasting through the night.
zh:
摩诃迦丽湿伐罗神庙坐落在摩腊婆希普拉河畔的古城乌贾因，供奉湿婆，是十二处究提林迦之一。乌贾因曾是阿般提国的都城，也是一座印度教圣城，每十二年举办一次僧伽斯塔壶节。

庙中的林伽相传为自生显现；主神作南面相的达克希纳穆尔蒂之形，这在十二处究提林迦中独一无二。此庙也被列为十八处大性力派圣地之一，相传萨蒂的上唇便坠落于此。

1234—1235年伊勒杜迷失劫掠乌贾因时神庙被毁，林伽被拆投入邻近的池塘。18世纪马拉塔统治时期，迪万罗摩旃陀罗·苏克坦卡尔将其重建。每逢大湿婆夜节，庙旁都有大型庙会，信众通宵祭拜。

en:
The Mahalakshmi Temple, also called the Ambabai Mandir, is the great shrine of Kolhapur in southern Maharashtra, dedicated to Mahalakshmi, the consort of Vishnu. Local legend tells that the goddess slew the demon Kolhasur, whose dying wish gave the city its name. The shrine was counted among the principal Shakti Peethas.

The temple is said to have been built in 634 by the Chalukya king Karnadeva. The historian Paul Dundas, following the twelfth-century poet Brahmashiva, argues that it began as a Jain temple of the tirthankara Chandraprabha and was converted to Hindu worship amid medieval religious tensions.

Its black-stone image of the crowned goddess stands before a stone lion with a Shri Yantra carved on the wall behind. In 1707 the Maratha queen Tarabai made Kolhapur the capital of her own state, and the temple remained the spiritual centre of the kingdom.
zh:
大吉祥天女神庙又称安巴巴伊庙，是南马哈拉施特拉戈尔哈布尔的大庙，供奉毗湿奴的神妃大吉祥天女。相传女神曾诛杀恶魔迦罗修罗，魔王临终请求以自己的名字命名此地，戈尔哈布尔因而得名。此庙被列为主要性力圣地之一。

相传此庙由遮娄其国王卡尔纳提婆建于634年。史学家保罗·邓达斯依据12世纪诗人婆罗门湿婆的记载提出，它最初是供奉耆那教祖师旃陀罗波罗跋的耆那庙，在中世纪的宗教纷争中改为印度教神庙。

庙中黑石女神像头戴宝冠，身前置石狮，背后墙壁刻有室利坛城。1707年，马拉塔女王塔拉巴伊以戈尔哈布尔为自己国家的都城，这座神庙始终是王国的精神中心。

en:
The Mahavinayak Temple is one of the oldest Ganesha shrines in Odisha, standing at Chandikhole in Jajpur district. Five gods, Ganesha, Shiva, Vishnu, Durga and Surya, are worshipped together as a single deity inside one sanctum. It was raised in the 1100s under the Keshari, or Somavamshi, kings of Odisha.

A legend explains the fivefold cult: when Rati, wife of the love god Kamadeva, prayed here for her husband's release from Shiva's curse, five hands reached out for her offering, and Brahma told her the five gods had accepted it together; a granite stone then rose from the earth, holding their combined power.

Local tradition also claims this is where Ganesha's severed head fell, and links the Baruna hill beside the temple with the Pandava king Yudhishthira, whose palace ruins are said to face the shrine.
zh:
大毗那夜迦神庙是奥里萨最古老的伽内什神庙之一，坐落在贾贾普尔县的昌迪科尔；圣室中将伽内什、湿婆、毗湿奴、杜尔迦和苏利耶五位神祇当作一位合体之神供奉。神庙于12世纪由奥里萨的凯沙里（索马瓦姆希）王朝诸王修建。

当地传说解释了这种五神合一的信仰：爱神伽摩之妻拉提在此祈祷，求湿婆解除对丈夫的诅咒，献祭时五只手伸出来接她的供品，梵天告诉她五位神祇一同受了她的供奉；随后一块花岗岩从地中涌出，蕴含着五神的合力。

当地还相传伽内什被砍落的头颅便坠落于此，神庙旁的巴鲁纳山又与般度族国王坚战有关，据说他宫殿的遗迹正对着神庙。

en:
The Mallikarjuna Temple crowns the hills of Srisailam, above the Krishna river in the Deccan, and is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, worshipped beside his consort Bhramaramba. Its name comes from the Telugu word mallika, jasmine, with which the lingam is said to have been adorned.

The complex is also counted among the Shakta Pithas, where Sati's neck is believed to have fallen. Inscriptions show a shrine here under the Satavahanas in the 2nd century, and the innermost sanctum dates to the 7th century. The Reddi kings of the 13th and 14th centuries cut the Pathala Ganga stairway of more than eight hundred steps down to the Krishna.

Most halls and four gateways were built under Vijayanagara emperors, beginning with Harihara I, who reigned from 1336 to 1355. Pilgrims worship at the temple and bathe in the river below.
zh:
末利迦阿周那神庙位于德干高原室利势罗的山巅，下临克里希纳河，是湿婆十二处究提林迦之一；湿婆在此与配偶婆罗摩兰巴同受供奉。庙名来自泰卢固语“末利迦”，即茉莉花，相传林伽曾以茉莉花装点。

此庙也被列入性力派圣地，相传萨蒂的颈部坠落于此。铭文显示，2世纪百乘王朝时期这里已有神祠，最内殿可追溯至7世纪。13—14世纪的雷迪诸王凿出八百余级的帕塔拉恒河石阶，直通克里希纳河。

主要殿堂和四座瞿布罗门楼大多由维查耶纳伽罗帝国皇帝修建，始于1336—1355年在位的诃利诃罗一世。朝圣者在此礼拜之余，还会下到河水里沐浴。

en:
The Martand Sun Temple is a ruined Hindu shrine dedicated to Surya, called Martanda in Sanskrit, on a plateau above the Kashmir Valley near Anantnag. The chronicler Kalhana records that it was commissioned in the eighth century by Lalitaditya Muktapida, the most powerful king of the Karkota dynasty.

Its colonnaded courtyard was ringed by eighty-four smaller shrines around a central sanctuary that probably carried a pyramidal roof; its carvings blended Gandharan and Gupta forms with influences from China and the Byzantine world.

The sanctuary stood for some six centuries until the reign of Sikandar Shah Miri, from 1389 to 1413, when it was pulled down during his campaign to bring the valley's Brahmanical institutions under state control. Earthquakes later damaged what remained, leaving the broken colonnade overlooking the valley.
zh:
马坦德太阳神庙是供奉太阳神苏利耶（梵语称马坦达）的印度教神庙遗址，坐落在克什米尔山谷阿嫩德纳格附近的高原上。史家卡尔哈纳记载，神庙由卡尔科塔王朝最强盛的国王拉利塔迪蒂亚·穆克塔皮达在8世纪敕建。

柱廊院内的中央主殿周围环绕八十四座小神龛，主殿屋顶可能为金字塔形；殿中雕刻融合了犍陀罗、笈多乃至中国和拜占庭世界的风格。

神庙屹立约六个世纪，直到1389—1413年西坎达尔·沙·米里在位期间，在他将山谷内婆罗门教机构纳入国家控制的行动中被拆毁。此后地震又损毁了残存建筑，只剩断裂的柱廊俯瞰山谷。

en: The Matsya Narayana Temple on the Omkar Hills in southern Bangalore is the only Karnataka shrine dedicated to Vishnu's fish avatar Matsya, first of his ten incarnations. As told from the Shatapatha Brahmana onward, Matsya guides Manu's ship through the great deluge and slays the demon Hayagriva to recover stolen Vedas, his icon joining Vishnu's four-armed torso to fish's body.
zh: 摩蹉那罗延神庙位于班加罗尔南部的奥姆卡尔山，是卡纳塔克邦唯一供奉毗湿奴鱼化身摩蹉的神庙，摩蹉为毗湿奴十大化身之首。从《百道梵书》起流传的神话说，摩蹉引导摩奴之舟渡过灭世大洪水，又诛杀恶魔诃耶羯哩婆夺回被盗的吠陀，造像为四臂毗湿奴上身接鱼身。

en:
Mayapan, whose name means the standard of the Maya people, was the walled capital of the Yucatan Maya in the Late Postclassic, southeast of Merida, with more than four thousand buildings and perhaps 17,000 people. After the revolt against Chichen Itza in 1221, lords led by the general Hunac Ceel built the city and gave the throne to the Cocom family, who ruled through a council of nobles for more than two hundred years.

Its principal sanctuary was the Temple of Kukulcan, a four-sided, nine-terraced pyramid modelled on the Castillo of Chichen Itza and set beside the Cenote Ch'en Mul, with serpent balustrades.
