In 1441 Ah Xiu Xupan of the rival Xiu family rose against the Cocom and slaughtered nearly the whole lineage; the capital was sacked and burned. By about 1461 the city was empty and Yucatan had split into warring city-states.
zh:
玛雅潘意为“玛雅人的旗帜”，是后古典期晚期尤卡坦玛雅人的有城墙都城，位于梅里达东南，城内有4000多座建筑，人口或达1.7万。1221年反抗奇琴伊察的起义之后，各地领主在将领胡纳克·塞尔主持下兴建新都，把王位交给科科姆家族；此后两百多年间，科科姆家族通过贵族议事会统治。

城中首要圣所是库库尔坎神庙，这座四面九级的金字塔仿照奇琴伊察的卡斯蒂略金字塔而建，矗立在琴穆尔天然井旁，栏杆雕有羽蛇。

1441年，敌对的休家族的阿·休·苏潘起兵反抗科科姆家族，几乎将其满门屠灭；都城遭洗劫焚毁。到1461年前后城市已空无一人，尤卡坦分裂为互相攻战的城邦。

en:
The Meenakshi Temple stands on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, dedicated to Meenakshi, the fish-eyed form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar, a form of Shiva.

The oldest surviving masonry was raised under the Pandya king Sadayavarman Kulasekaran I around 1190 to 1216 and enlarged by his successors. In 1311 the Khalji general Malik Kafur sacked Madurai, destroyed the temple and carried its treasure to Delhi; under the ensuing Madurai Sultanate the idols were hidden and the complex lay abandoned for some sixty years.

The Vijayanagara prince Kumara Kampana reconquered the city in 1378, rebuilt the walls and reconsecrated the images. His Nayak governors expanded the shrine. Under the Madurai Nayaks, above all Vishwanatha Nayak, it took its present form with fourteen gopurams, a thousand-pillared hall and the golden lotus pond.
zh:
鱼目女神庙坐落于马杜赖的韦盖河南岸，供奉鱼目的米纳克希，即帕尔瓦蒂的化身，以及她的配偶、湿婆化身孙达雷什瓦拉。

现存最早的石构建筑由潘地亚国王萨达亚瓦尔曼·库拉塞卡兰一世在约1190—1216年间修建，后继诸王又加以扩建。1311年，卡尔吉王朝将领马利克·卡富尔劫掠马杜赖，摧毁神庙并把财宝运往德里；随后的马杜赖苏丹国时期，神像被藏起，庙群荒废约六十年。

1378年，毗奢耶那伽罗王子库马拉·坎帕纳收复此城，重建围墙并重新安奉神像。他麾下的纳亚克诸将扩建神庙；到马杜赖纳亚克王朝、尤其是维什瓦纳塔·纳亚克统治时，神庙形成今日的格局，有14座塔门、千柱厅和金莲池。

en:
The Meteora are sandstone pillars rising from the Thessalian plain near Trikala, whose summits hold an Orthodox monastic complex. Hermit monks lived in the rocks by the ninth century, and by the eleventh century they had formed the Skete of Stagoi.

Permanent monasteries came in the fourteenth century, as Turkish raids drove monks to the inaccessible pinnacles. In 1344 Athanasios the Meteorite arrived from Mount Athos, and between 1356 and 1372 he built the Great Meteoron under the local ruler Simeon Uroš's protection; Simeon's son John Uroš abdicated to die as a monk there in the 1420s.

More than twenty houses were founded, reachable only by jointed ladders and hauling ropes, said to be replaced only when they broke. Theophanes built the monastery of Varlaam in 1517, keeping the finger of Saint John and the shoulder blade of Saint Andrew.
zh:
迈泰奥拉是色萨利平原特里卡拉附近的砂岩巨柱群，柱顶建有东正教修道院群。9世纪时隐修士已在岩石中栖身，11世纪组成斯塔戈伊隐修区。

14世纪土耳其人不断袭扰，修士们才在难以攀援的岩柱上修建常住修道院。1344年，“流星者”阿塔纳修斯从阿索斯山而来，1356—1372年在当地领主西美昂·乌罗什庇护下创建大迈泰奥拉修道院；西美昂之子约翰·乌罗什后来退位出家，15世纪20年代在该院去世。

这里先后建起二十多座修道院，只能靠拼接的长梯和吊绳网篮上下，据说绳索断了才更换。1517年，狄奥法内斯修建瓦尔拉姆修道院，院内藏有圣约翰的手指和圣安德烈的肩胛骨。

en:
Mile was a medieval church site in the Visoko basin in central Bosnia. It first appears in written sources in 1244 as the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian, and in 1340 the Bosnian ruler Stephen II Kotromanić built there the Franciscan friary of Saint Nicholas, the first of its order in Bosnia.

The estate was a meeting place of the Stanak, the assembly of Bosnian nobility, and served as the coronation and burial church of the kings of Bosnia.

Stephen II, who died in 1353, arranged to be buried there, and Tvrtko I was crowned king at Mile in 1377 when the Banate of Bosnia became a kingdom. When the Ottomans overran the Kingdom of Bosnia in 1463, the friary's role as the ceremonial heart of the Bosnian monarchy came to an end.
zh:
米列是波斯尼亚中部维索科盆地的中世纪教堂遗址。它最早于1244年见诸文献，当时是圣科斯马斯与达米安教堂；1340年，波斯尼亚统治者斯特凡二世·科特罗马尼奇在此修建圣尼古拉方济各会修道院，这是该修会在波斯尼亚的第一座修道院。

这里是波斯尼亚贵族会议“斯坦纳克”的召开地之一，也是波斯尼亚诸王的加冕与安葬教堂。

1353年去世的斯特凡二世安排自己葬在此地，1377年特夫尔特科一世在米列加冕为王，波斯尼亚班国由此升级为王国。1463年奥斯曼攻灭波斯尼亚王国，这座修道院作为波斯尼亚君主制礼仪中心的历史也随之终结。

en:
The Benedictine abbey of Santa Maria de Montserrat clings to a serrated mountain in Catalonia, inland from Barcelona. It enshrines the Virgin of Montserrat, a late twelfth-century Romanesque wooden Madonna and Child known as La Moreneta, the little dark one, one of Europe's Black Madonnas.

Tradition says the image was hidden on the mountain around 718 as Saracen armies invaded; a cult grew around its discovery, and Abbot Oliba of Ripoll founded the monastery in 1025. Ignatius of Loyola laid down his soldier's arms before the statue on 25 March 1522, before founding the Society of Jesus.

The abbey's press printed its first book in 1499. French troops sacked and burned the abbey in 1811 and 1812, and in 1835 it was closed during monastic confiscations, its monks dispersed and buildings left to decay.
zh:
圣马利亚·德·蒙特塞拉特本笃会修道院依傍加泰罗尼亚的锯齿状山峰，位于巴塞罗那内陆。院中供奉蒙特塞拉特圣母像，这尊12世纪末的罗马式木雕圣母子被称为“拉·莫雷内塔”，即小黑女，是欧洲的黑圣母像之一。

相传718年前后撒拉森人入侵时，圣像被藏匿于山中；圣像被发现后信仰渐盛，里波尔的修道院长奥利瓦于1025年在此创建修道院。依纳爵·罗耀拉于1522年3月25日在圣像前放下军人的兵器，此后创立了耶稣会。

修道院的印刷所于1499年印出第一本书。1811—1812年法国军队洗劫并焚毁修道院；1835年，在没收修道院产业的浪潮中它被关闭，修士散去，建筑荒废。

en:
The Mosque of Uqba, the Great Mosque of Kairouan in central Tunisia, was founded in 670 by the Arab conqueror Uqba ibn Nafi when he laid out the city. It became a model for later Maghrebi mosques.

The first building was destroyed around 690 when Berbers under Kusaila took Kairouan, and the general Hasan ibn al-Nu'man rebuilt it in 703. The Umayyad governor Bishr ibn Safwan enlarged it between 724 and 728 and began the square minaret.

Its present form dates to the Aghlabid emirs: Ziyadat Allah I rebuilt the mosque in 836, giving it a hypostyle prayer hall, marble courtyard and early horseshoe arches; Ibrahim II enlarged it in 875. Scholars teaching in its halls made Kairouan a centre of learning until the city's decline from the mid-eleventh century, when intellectual life shifted to the Zaytuna mosque in Tunis.
zh:
乌克巴大清真寺即突尼斯中部的凯鲁万大清真寺。670年，阿拉伯征服者奥卡巴·伊本·纳菲在营建凯鲁万城的同时修建了这座清真寺，它成为马格里布清真寺的范本。

原建筑约在690年库塞拉率柏柏尔人攻占凯鲁万时被毁，将领哈桑·伊本·努阿曼于703年将其重建。倭马亚总督比什尔·伊本·塞夫万在724—728年扩建，并动工修建方形宣礼塔。

清真寺现存的面貌主要来自阿格拉布王朝的埃米尔们：齐亚达特·安拉一世于836年重建，建成多柱式礼拜殿、大理石庭院和早期马蹄形拱门；易卜拉欣二世又在875年扩建。寺中学者使凯鲁万成为学术重镇，直到11世纪中叶该城衰落，学术生活转向突尼斯宰图纳清真寺。

en:
The shrine of Moulay Idris stands in the town of Moulay Idriss Zerhoun, below Mount Zerhoun near Meknes. It holds the tomb of Idris I, a descendant of Muhammad who fled Abbasid rule after the Battle of Fakh and in 789 allied with the Berber Awraba at Oualili, founding the first Islamic state in Morocco.

He died in 791, possibly poisoned at the caliph Harun al-Rashid's order, and was buried under a domed qubba; his posthumous son Idris II took power in 803 and later built Fez. The Marinids revived the Idrisid legacy after the alleged rediscovery of Idris I's remains in 1318, when the annual August moussem took shape.

The Alaouite sultan Moulay Ismail had the mausoleum rebuilt between 1719 and 1721 and established its mosque as the town's Friday mosque. Sultan Abd al-Rahman enlarged it again in 1822.
zh:
扎尔洪的穆莱·伊德里斯圣陵坐落在梅克内斯附近扎尔洪山脚下的同名小镇。陵中安葬着穆罕默德的后裔伊德里斯一世，法赫战役后他逃离阿拔斯王朝，789年在瓦利利与柏柏尔奥乌拉巴部落结盟，建立摩洛哥首个伊斯兰政权。

他于791年去世，可能是被哈里发哈伦·拉希德派人毒杀，葬在穹顶拱北之下；遗腹子伊德里斯二世于803年亲政，后来兴建非斯。马林王朝时期对伊德里斯家族的尊崇复兴：1318年相传重新发现伊德里斯一世的遗骸，八月穆塞姆节庆也在此时成形。

阿拉维王朝苏丹穆莱·伊斯梅尔1719—1721年重建圣陵，将清真寺定为全镇的主麻清真寺。苏丹阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼又于1822年扩建。

en:
Mount Athos, the easternmost prong of the Chalkidiki peninsula in Macedonia, is the foremost monastic centre of Eastern Orthodoxy, known in Greek as the Holy Mountain. Christian hermits had settled its forests by the fourth century, and tradition holds that the Virgin Mary was blown ashore there and consecrated the mountain as her garden.

Organised monasticism took shape in the ninth century, and in 963 Athanasius the Athonite, backed by Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, founded the Great Lavra. Byzantine emperors and Orthodox rulers endowed further houses, and the community came under the direct jurisdiction of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople.

After the fall of Constantinople in 1453 the monasteries kept their rights under Ottoman rule, and nineteenth-century donations from Russia, Serbia and Romania funded a revival. By tradition and later by law, women are barred from entering the peninsula.
zh:
阿索斯山是马其顿哈尔基季基半岛最东端的岩石岬角，是东正教最重要的修道中心，希腊语称“圣山”。4世纪时基督教隐修士已在山林中定居；传统称圣母玛利亚曾被风浪吹到此处，将这座山祝圣为自己的园子。

9世纪起形成有组织的修道生活，963年阿索斯的阿塔纳修斯在皇帝尼基弗鲁斯二世·福卡斯支持下创建大劳拉修道院。此后拜占庭皇帝及正教统治者又捐资兴建修道院，修院共同体直属君士坦丁堡普世牧首。

1453年君士坦丁堡陷落后，各修道院在奥斯曼统治下保留了特权；19世纪，来自俄罗斯、塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的捐助推动了修道复兴。依照传统和后来的法律，女性不得进入这一地区。

en:
Mount Emei rises 3,099 metres on the western rim of the Sichuan basin near Jiading, the highest of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains and the bodhimanda of Samantabhadra, known in Chinese as Puxian. Tradition places the first Buddhist temple in China on its slopes in the first century.

Its oldest enduring foundation is Wannian Temple, established by the monk Huichi under the Eastern Jin as Puxian Temple. Rebuilt in 876 by Huitong and renamed Baishui Temple, then restored in 980 by Maozhen, it acquired a bronze image of Samantabhadra riding his white elephant, cast under the Northern Song.

After a Wanli-era fire the Ming court rebuilt the temple from 1600, adding the timberless Brick Hall crowned with five small pagodas. Ming and Qing patronage supported seventy-six monasteries, from Baoguo Temple to the Golden Summit, joined by a fifty-kilometre pilgrim path.
zh:
峨眉山位于四川盆地西缘，邻近嘉定，海拔3099米，为中国四大佛教名山之最高者，是普贤菩萨的道场。相传1世纪时中国最早的佛寺即建于山中。

现存最古老的开山祖庭是万年寺，东晋僧人慧持创建时原名普贤寺。876年慧通重建后改称白水寺，980年僧人茂真重修，寺中有北宋铸造的普贤骑白象铜像。

明代万历年间寺院遭火，朝廷于1600年起敕令重建，增建不用寸木的无梁砖殿，殿顶饰以五座小塔。明清两代的护持使山间寺院达76座，从报国寺到金顶，由50公里的朝山小径串联。

en:
Mount Fanjing, the highest peak of the Wuling range in Tongren, Guizhou, rises 2,570 metres. Its name shortens Fantian Jingtu, the Brahma Pure Land, and Chinese Buddhism holds it as the bodhimanda of Maitreya, the future Buddha.

Buddhism reached the mountain in the Song, when Xiyan Temple was founded in 965. The early Ming made it a Buddhist centre and named it Fanjing; after local tusi warfare, the court incorporated the region into Guizhou in 1413.

The Bozhou rebellion of Yang Yinglong wrecked the shrines in 1599, and in 1618 the Wanli emperor charged the monk Miaoxuan with restoring the Gold Peak. Under the Qing, the Kangxi reign enlarged the network to forty-eight hermitages, drawing pilgrims from Sichuan, Huguang and Jiangnan. Twin halls of Sakyamuni and Maitreya crown the New Gold Peak; repairs in 1822 and 1832 renewed the Maitreya sanctuary.
zh:
梵净山是贵州铜仁武陵山脉的主峰，海拔2570米。山名是“梵天净土”的简称，汉传佛教以之为未来佛弥勒菩萨的道场。

佛教在宋代传入，965年建成西岩寺。明初这里成为佛教中心，正式定名梵净山；当地土司争战之后，朝廷于1413年将这一带纳入贵州省。

1599年播州土司杨应龙之乱使梵刹残破，1618年明神宗委派僧人妙玄主持重建金顶。入清之后，康熙年间脚庵增至48座，吸引四川、湖广和江浙的朝山者。新金顶之巅并立释迦、弥勒二殿；1822年与1832年又两度重修弥勒道场。

en:
Mount Fuji, the snow-capped volcano between Suruga and Kai, is Japan's highest peak and one of its Three Holy Mountains. In Shintō belief it is the dwelling of Konohanasakuya-hime, wife of Ninigi, and Sengen shrines were built at its foot to pacify its eruptions.

In early times the mountain was worshipped from afar; when eruptions quietened in the Heian period, Shugendō ascetics made it a centre of mountain religion, and the monk Matsudai Shōnin founded a temple on the summit in the early twelfth century. The Hōei eruption of 1707 to 1708 buried nearby villages in ash.

The Edo period saw the rise of Fuji-kō, the pilgrim movement founded by the ascetic Hasegawa Kakugyō, whose followers climbed the cone seeking rebirth and purification. In the 1830s Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji carried its image across the country and beyond.
zh:
富士山位于骏河与甲斐之间，是一座积雪火山，也是日本最高峰和三灵山之一。神道教认为它是琼琼杵尊之妻木花之佐久耶姬的居所，人们在山麓修建浅间神社以镇抚火山喷发。

古时人们在远处遥拜这座山；平安时代火山活动平息后，修验道山伏把它当作山岳信仰的中心，12世纪初僧人末代上人又在山顶建起寺院。1707—1708年的宝永大喷发使附近村落被火山灰掩埋。

江户时代，苦行僧长谷川角行开创的朝圣团体“富士讲”兴起，信众攀登火山口以求重生与净化。19世纪30年代，北斋的《富岳三十六景》把富士的形象传遍日本乃至海外。

en:
Mount Girnar, called Raivata or Ujjayanta in ancient texts, rises above Junagadh in southern Gujarat and has drawn Jain pilgrims since before 250 BCE. It is sacred to Neminatha, the twenty-second Tirthankara, who is said to have gained omniscience in the Sahsavan grove and attained nirvana on the mountain's highest peak.

Some sixteen temples stand near the summit, reached by thousands of stone steps; most belong to the Svetambara sect, though Digambara Jains also venerate the hill. The principal Neminatha temple was rebuilt in 1129 by Sajjana, governor of Saurashtra, and the Chudasama ruler Mandalika I covered it with gold plates in 1364.

Other shrines include the Vastupala-vihara, completed in 1232, and the Adabadji Adinatha temple, with a slab carved with the twenty-four Tirthankaras in 1442. Girnar numbers among the five great Svetambara pilgrimage mountains of India.
zh:
耆栗那罗山古称赖伐多山或乌阇衍多山，耸立在古吉拉特南部的朱纳格特，早在公元前250年以前便有耆那教香客前来朝拜。此山为第二十二祖涅弥那陀的圣地：相传他在萨婆斯梵林证得一切智，又在最高峰上涅槃。

山顶附近有约十六座庙宇，需攀登数千级石阶方可抵达；其中多数属白衣派，天衣派也尊奉此山。主殿涅弥那陀寺于1129年由萨乌拉施特拉总督萨阇那重建，1364年朱达萨马王朝的曼达利迦一世又为它覆上金板。

其他殿宇包括1232年建成的瓦斯图波罗精舍，以及1442年刻有二十四祖师像石板的阿陀巴吉·阿底那特寺。耆栗那罗山同列印度白衣派五大朝圣名山。

en:
Mount Haku is a 2,702-metre volcano on the border of Kaga and the neighbouring provinces, its snow lingering long after lower peaks have thawed; with Mount Fuji and Mount Tate it is counted among Japan's Three Holy Mountains. Its summit was first reached in 717 by the Shugendō monk Taichō, who built a chapel there.

Shirayama Hime at its foot was reckoned the ichinomiya of Kaga and heads some two thousand Hakusan shrines; it first appears in court records in 853 and prospered through the Kamakura and Muromachi periods.

The Kaga ikki rising of 1455 cost it its estates and fire destroyed the buildings in 1480, leaving the cult in ruins for more than a century until Maeda Toshiie, lord of Kaga, restored it under Tokugawa rule. The volcano's last recorded eruption was in 1659.
zh:
白山是矗立于加贺国与邻国边界、海拔2702米的火山，积雪比周围群峰存留更久；它与富士山、立山并称日本三灵山。717年，修验道僧人泰澄首次登顶并在山顶建堂。

山麓的白山比咩神社被视为加贺国一宫，统辖约两千座白山神社；它最早见于853年的朝廷记录，镰仓至室町初期盛极一时。

1455年加贺一向一揆使神社失去庄园，1480年社殿又毁于火灾，信仰荒废了一个多世纪，直到加贺藩主前田利家在江户初期加以复兴。火山最后一次有记载的喷发在1659年。

en:
Mount Hiei rises northeast of Kyoto, the direction held to be the demon gate through which misfortune entered the capital. At its eastern foot stands Hiyoshi Taisha, whose Sannō Gongen faith fused the mountain's Shintō cult with Buddhism.

In 788 the monk Saichō founded Enryaku-ji on the summit with the backing of Emperor Kanmu, and it became the headquarters of the Tendai sect: Hōnen, Shinran, Dōgen and Nichiren studied there before founding their own schools. At the temple's height its warrior monks more than forty times carried Hiyoshi's portable shrine into Kyoto to enforce their demands.

In 1571 Oda Nobunaga stormed the mountain, burned the halls and slaughtered the monks, ending that power; Toyotomi Hideyoshi rebuilt the shrine from 1586, and the Tokugawa shoguns restored Enryaku-ji, its main hall rising again in 1642.
zh:
比叡山耸立于京都东北方，东北在方位信仰中被视为灾祸侵入都城的“鬼门”。山东麓的日吉大社以山王权现信仰把山岳神道与佛教融为一体。

788年，僧人最澄在桓武天皇支持下于山顶创建延历寺，这里后来成为天台宗总本山：法然、亲鸾、道元、日莲都曾在此求学，而后各自开宗立派。鼎盛时期，僧兵曾四十余次抬着日吉的神轿进入京都强诉。

1571年，织田信长发兵攻山，焚毁堂舍、屠戮僧众，终结了这股势力；丰臣秀吉从1586年起重建神社，德川幕府又恢复延历寺，其正殿于1642年再度落成。

en:
Mount Jiuhua, one of China's four great Buddhist mountains, rises in Qingyang county in southern Anhui. Under the Han it was called Mount Lingyang and under the southern dynasties Mount Jiuzi; the Tang poet Li Bai renamed it after celebrating its nine lotus-like peaks in verse.

In 719 Kim Gyo-gak, a prince of Silla who had taken monk's vows, came to the mountain and meditated there for seventy-five years; when he died at ninety-nine his body did not decay, and the monks took him for an incarnation of the bodhisattva Dizang, making Jiuhua his Chinese bodhimanda.

Huacheng Temple and the shrine that holds the incorrupt body, Roushen Temple, became the heart of the pilgrimage. The Ming and Qing saw the mountain's golden age, when as many as three hundred and sixty monasteries sheltered four to five thousand monks and nuns.
zh:
九华山是中国四大佛教名山之一，位于安徽南部青阳县。汉代名陵阳山，南朝称九子山；唐代诗人李白赋诗盛赞九峰如莲花绽放，将山改名为九华。

719年，新罗王族金乔觉舍俗出家，来此结庐苦修，前后山居75年，世寿99岁，入灭后肉身不坏，僧众认定他是地藏菩萨的化身，九华山由此成为地藏菩萨的根本道场。

化城寺与安奉不坏肉身的肉身殿成为朝山信众的中心。明清两代迎来鼎盛，寺院一度多达360座，常住僧尼四五千人。

en:
Mount Kōya is a wooded basin in the Kii range, ringed by eight peaks like the petals of a lotus, where the monk Kūkai founded the headquarters of esoteric Shingon Buddhism in 819. Local Shintō deities, the hunter Kariba and the goddess Niu, were said to have guided him there with white and black dogs.

Kūkai spent his last years on the mountain and, when he died in 835, was entombed without cremation at Okunoin; the faithful hold that he entered eternal samadhi and waits there in meditation for Maitreya, the future Buddha. Around the Danjō Garan sanctuary grew a monastic town of over a hundred sub-temples, from which Kūkai's disciples spread Shingon across Japan.

Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Seigan-ji there in 1593 in memory of his mother, and the Tokugawa shoguns patronised its head temple Kongōbu-ji.
zh:
高野山是纪伊山脉中的林间盆地，八峰环绕，形如莲花八瓣；819年，僧人空海在此建立密教真言宗的总本山。相传当地神祇狩场明神与丹生明神曾以白犬、黑犬引路，带空海寻得此地。

空海在山上度过晚年，835年去世时未经荼毗，葬于奥之院；信众相信他进入永恒的定境，在冥想中等待未来佛弥勒降世。以坛上伽蓝为中心，山上逐渐形成拥有上百座子院的寺院町，空海的弟子由此把真言宗传遍日本。

丰臣秀吉于1593年为纪念亡母在山上修建青岩寺，德川幕府也护持总本山金刚峰寺。

en:
Mount Lu, anciently called Kuanglu, rises above the Yangtze river and Poyang lake near Jiujiang in Jiangxi. Between 386 and 402 the monk Huiyuan built Donglin Temple on its slopes and taught the chanting of Amitabha's name, founding the Pure Land school of Chinese Buddhism.

Daoist temples were added under the Tang, and in 940 the White Deer Grotto Academy was founded at the mountain's foot; the Song scholar Zhu Xi rebuilt it into a celebrated Confucian academy. Tao Yuanming lived and was buried nearby, and Su Shi wrote that no one could see Lushan's true shape while standing inside it. Buddhist, Daoist and Confucian shrines continued to share its peaks and grottoes through the Qing.
zh:
庐山古称匡庐，耸立于江西九江之侧，北临长江、东濒鄱阳湖。386—402年间，僧人慧远在山中创建东林寺，倡念阿弥陀佛之名，开汉传佛教净土宗之源。

唐代兴修道观；940年，白鹿洞书院创立于山麓，宋代儒者朱熹将其重建为著名的儒家书院。陶渊明曾在附近隐居并安葬于此，苏轼则留下“不识庐山真面目，只缘身在此山中”的名句。入清以后，佛、道、儒三教的寺观书院仍并存于峰峦岩洞之间。

en:
Mount Misen is the 535-metre sacred peak at the heart of Itsukushima, the island in Aki Province also called Miyajima, whose soil was guarded by strict taboos of ritual purity.

In 806 the monk Kūkai climbed the mountain, founded the Daisho-in temple and lit the Kiezu-no-hi, an eternal fire kept burning there; his iron staff was said to have taken root as a plum tree, one of the seven wonders of the peak.

The mountain drew pilgrims of the Shugendō mountain cult, while Taira no Kiyomori's patronage of Itsukushima Shrine from 1168 turned the island into one of the great cult centres of the Inland Sea. The taboo on bloodshed was broken in 1555 when Mōri Motonari defeated Sue Takafusa on the island, after which Motonari rebuilt the shrine hall in 1571.
zh:
弥山是安艺国严岛（又称宫岛）中央的圣山，海拔535米；整座岛屿被视为神域，受严格的清净禁忌保护。

806年，僧人空海登上此山，开创大圣院，并点燃此后一直由寺僧守护的“不灭之火”；传说他的锡杖就地生根长成梅树，是弥山七大奇景之一。

弥山吸引修验道的行者前来修行，而平清盛自1168年起营建严岛神社，使该岛成为濑户内海的重要信仰中心之一。1555年毛利元就在岛上击败陶晴贤，打破了岛上不得流血的禁忌，战后又于1571年重建神社正殿。

en:
Mount Nantai, also called Mount Futara, is a 2,486-metre volcano above Nikkō in Shimotsuke Province, whose cone was worshipped from the Yayoi period as a go-shintai, a mountain itself housing the kami.

In the eighth century the Kegon monk Shōdō Shōnin made the first recorded ascent, founding Futarasan Shrine in 767 and its summit chapel, the Oku-no-miya, in 782; the old mountain cult merged with Buddhist Shugendō. The Engishiki of 927 records its shrine, and a middle shrine was raised on Lake Chuzenji in 1096.

After Sengoku warfare cost Futarasan Shrine its estates, the nearby Nikkō Tōshō-gū, mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, brought Tokugawa patronage: Hidetada rebuilt the main shrine in 1617, and the lakeside halls were rebuilt in 1699.
zh:
男体山又名二荒山，是耸立在下野国日光、海拔2486米的火山。自弥生时代起，山容本身就被当作神灵依代的御神体而受崇拜。

8世纪，华严宗僧人胜道上人首次有记载地登上此山，于767年开创二荒山神社，又在782年于山顶建立奥宫；古老的山岳信仰与佛教修验道合流。927年的《延喜式》载有这座神社；1096年，中禅寺湖畔又建起中宫。

战国战乱中神社失去庄园，邻近祭祀德川家康的日光东照宫兴起后，神社得到德川家庇护：秀忠于1617年重建本社，湖畔殿堂也于1699年再建。

en:
Mount Putuo is a small island in the Zhoushan archipelago off Ningbo in Zhejiang, its name taken from Potalaka, the sacred mountain of Avalokitesvara in Indian scripture; Chinese Buddhism regards it as the bodhimanda of Guanyin. Its cult began in 916, when the Japanese monk Hui'e, bearing a Guanyin image from Mount Wutai, was driven back by storms and left the statue with an islander surnamed Zhang; the shrine became the Temple of the Unwilling Guanyin.

In 1080 Emperor Shenzong of the Song refounded it as the Baotuo Guanyin Temple. Ming coastal evacuations twice emptied the island, with temples burned in 1386 under Tang He and again in 1553; monks returned from the 1570s.

The three great monasteries of Puji, Fayu founded in 1580 and Huiji founded in 1793 arose here, making Putuo one of Chinese Buddhism's four sacred mountains.
zh:
普陀山是浙江宁波外海舟山群岛中的一座小岛，山名取自印度经典中观自在菩萨的圣山补怛洛伽，汉传佛教以之为观音菩萨的道场。其香火始于916年：日本僧人慧锷从五台山请得观音像东归，遇风浪不能成行，便将圣像留在岛民张氏家中，由此发展出的庵堂称“不肯去观音院”。

1080年，宋神宗赐额改建为宝陀观音寺。明代海禁迁海，此山两度遭劫：1386年汤和焚毁寺院，1553年再次毁寺；1570年代起僧人陆续重返。

普济、法雨（1580年始建）、慧济（1793年始建）三大寺由此次第崛起，使普陀山跻身中国四大佛教名山。

en:
Mount Tate is a 3,015-metre peak in Etchū Province and with Mount Fuji and Mount Haku one of Japan's Three Holy Mountains. Tradition places its opening in 701, when the hunter-ascetic Saeki no Ariyori founded the cult of Tateyama Gongen; Emperor Monmu declared the summit a sacred domain, and Oyama Shrine later became the ichinomiya of Etchū.

The mountain god appears in a Man'yōshū poem of 747 by Ōtomo no Yakamochi. Under the Kamakura and Muromachi shogunates the halls drew warrior patronage: the Kamakura bakufu began raising them in 1185, and Ashikaga Yoshiki sent offerings in 1492.

In the Etchū campaign of 1585 Hashiba Hideyoshi burned the precinct, but Maeda Toshiie of Kaga rebuilt it and made the shrine a prayer centre of his domain; the Shugendō order Tateyama Shugen maintained the mountain cult through the Edo centuries.
zh:
立山是越中国境内、海拔3015米的高峰，与富士山、白山并称日本三灵山。相传701年，猎人出身的修行者佐伯有赖开创立山权现信仰，文武天皇将山顶划为灵域；雄山神社后来成为越中国一宫。

山神在747年大伴家持收入《万叶集》的和歌中已经出现。镰仓、室町两朝，社殿受到武家庇护：镰仓幕府于1185年起兴建社殿，足利义稙在1492年寄进供品。

1585年越中征伐中，羽柴秀吉烧毁社域，战后加贺藩主前田利家加以重建，将神社定为藩内祈愿所；修验道法团立山修验在江户时代维系着山岳信仰。

en:
Mount Wutai in northern Shanxi is a ring of five flat-topped mountains. Chinese Buddhism counts it first among the four great bodhisattva mountains, the bodhimanda of Manjushri; monks identified it with the clear cold mountain named as Manjushri's abode in the Avatamsaka Sutra, giving it the older name of Mount Qingliang.

By the seventh century pilgrims from India and Central Asia were travelling there, and Tang patronage left two of the oldest surviving timber buildings in China, the main hall of Nanchan Temple of 782 and the East Hall of Foguang Temple of 857.

Over the following dynasties Han Buddhist monasteries and Tibetan Buddhist lamaseries grew side by side on its terraces, among them Xiantong Temple, Tayuan Temple and Pusading, drawing imperial visits and endowments down to the Qing.
zh:
五台山位于山西北部，由五座峰顶平阔的山峰环抱而成。汉传佛教以五台山为四大菩萨名山之首，是文殊师利的道场；古人依据《华严经》中“清凉山”为文殊所居的记载将其比定于此，五台山也因此旧称清凉山。

早在7世纪，印度与中亚的巡礼者已远道而来；唐代的护持留下了中国现存最古老的两座木构建筑，即782年的南禅寺大殿和857年的佛光寺东大殿。

此后历代，汉传青庙与藏传黄庙在山间台地上并立，显通寺、塔院寺、菩萨顶等屡获历朝皇帝巡幸施赐，香火延续至清代。

en:
Mount Yoshino is an eight-kilometre ridge in Yamato Province running south from the Yoshino River into the Ōmine range, its slopes studded with the temples and shrines of the Kinpusen cult. In the seventh century the ascetic En no Gyōja opened the mountain and founded Kinpusen-ji, seat of Zaō Gongen and headquarters of Kinpusen Shugendō, and blazed the trail linking Yoshino with the Kumano shrines of Kii.

Cherry wood served to carve images of Zaō Gongen, and believers donated saplings: from the Heian period four groves of a thousand trees clothed the ridge.

Prince Ōama watched for omens at the Yoshino palace before seizing the throne in the Jinshin War of 672. In 1336 the dispossessed Southern Court made Yoshino its mountain capital, and four of its emperors kept court among the temples until the rival courts were reunited in 1392.
zh:
吉野山是大和国境内一条八公里长的山脊，自吉野川南岸向南延伸入大峰山脉，山坡上遍布金峰信仰的寺院与神社。7世纪，修行者役行者开辟此山，开创供奉藏王权现的金峰修验总本山金峰山寺，并踏出连接吉野与纪伊熊野三山的道路。

藏王权现的造像以樱木雕成，信众供奉树苗：自平安时代起，山脊上形成四处各千株的樱树林。

大海人皇子曾在吉野行宫观望征兆，随后在672年的壬申之乱中夺取皇位。1336年，失势的南朝以吉野为山间王都，四位南朝天皇在众寺之间维持朝廷，直到1392年南北两朝合一。

en:
Muktagiri, also called Mendhagiri, is a Jain pilgrimage centre in the forested hills on the border of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. Known as a Siddha Kshetra, a place where liberated souls are said to have attained nirvana, it holds fifty-two temples around a waterfall, reached by six hundred steps.

The oldest sanctuary is a rock-cut cave raised between roughly 1200 and 1400, its arched entrance carved with lotuses and small tirthankara figures and its inner hall holding some fifty-six Jain images, including a seated Mahavira at the gate.

Among the later numbered shrines, the twenty-sixth temple is famed for its seven-hooded image of Parshvanatha. Pilgrims gather for the annual fair held at Diwali.
zh:
穆羯帝耆梨寺又称门达吉里，是中央邦与马哈拉施特拉邦交界山林中的耆那教朝圣中心。此地被尊为“成就地”，相传有解脱者在此证得涅槃；52座寺院环绕瀑布分布，需登六百级石阶抵达。

最古老的圣所约为13至14世纪开凿的石窟，拱门雕有莲花与小型祖师像，内殿保存约56尊耆那教造像，窟门正中为结跏趺坐的大雄像。

在依次编号的后世祠庙中，第26寺以七头华盖的巴湿伐那陀像著称。每年排灯节期间，信众在此举行庙会朝山。

en:
Muktinath lies at 3,800 metres in the Mustang valley beneath the Thorong La pass, and its sanctity is shared by Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus know it as Mukti Kshetra, the place of liberation, one of Nepal's Himalayan dhams and a self-manifested Vishnu shrine; in Shaktism it is counted among the fifty-one Shakta Pithas, where the head of Sati is said to have fallen.

Tibetan Buddhists call the place Chumig Gyatsa, the Hundred Waters, rank it among the twenty-four tantric abodes of the dakinis and venerate the Vishnu icon as Avalokiteshvara. The copper image dates to the late 1500s.

The Newari-style pagoda with its three-tiered roof was raised in 1814 or 1815 under Queen Subarna Prabha Devi of Nepal, replacing an older clay temple of the Jumla kings; its courtyard is ringed by the hundred and eight bull-headed Mukti Dhara spouts and two sacred ponds.
zh:
穆克蒂纳特位于木斯塘谷地、通拉山口脚下，海拔3800米，由印度教徒与佛教徒共同尊奉。印度教徒称其为“解脱之地”穆克蒂克舍特拉，是尼泊尔喜马拉雅圣地之一，也是一座毗湿奴自显圣庙；在性力派传统中，它位列五十一处性力圣地，相传萨蒂女神的头颅坠落于此。

藏传佛教徒称此地为“楚米嘉察”，意为“百水”，将其列为二十四处空行母密乘圣地之一，并把毗湿奴像视为观世音菩萨的化现。铜制圣像可追溯至16世纪末。

三层尼瓦尔式宝塔于1814年或1815年由尼泊尔王后苏巴尔纳·普拉巴·德维在久姆拉诸王旧黏土庙的原址上兴建，庭院四周环绕着一百零八个牛头造型的“解脱水口”和两座圣池。

en:
The Mundeshwari Temple crowns a hill of the Kaimur plateau in the Bhojpuri country of Bihar, with a rare octagonal stone plan, an example of Nagara architecture. It houses a four-faced Shiva linga while the presiding deity is Mundeshwari, a ten-armed Durga riding a buffalo; her Tantric worship marks this as an early eastern Indian centre of the goddess cult.

Local tradition and a religious trust claim a foundation in 108, but historians date the surviving sculptures and an inscription of the raja Udayasena to about 570 to 590, showing an important temple settlement from the 600s.

The shrine was probably built or rebuilt in the 1500s or 1600s from the doorways and mouldings of ruined seventh-century temples, and its tower has fallen. Rites continued without interruption, with pilgrims gathering for Rama Navami, Shiva Ratri and the Navaratra fair.
zh:
蒙提湿伐罗神庙位于比哈尔博杰普尔地区凯穆尔高原的山丘之上，采用罕见的八角石构平面，是纳加拉风格建筑的实例。殿中供奉四面湿婆林伽，主神则是骑乘水牛的十臂难近母蒙提湿伐罗；其密教化的祭祀方式表明这里是东印度较早的女神崇拜中心。

当地传统和宗教信托机构声称庙宇始建于108年，但史学家据现存雕刻与乌达耶犀那王铭文判断，遗物年代约在570至590年，说明600年代山上已有重要的寺院聚落。

殿宇大约是1500至1600年间利用7世纪废庙的门框和线脚重建或改建而成，塔顶早已倾圮。庙里的祭祀从未中断，每逢罗摩诞辰、湿婆夜和九夜节庙会，信众云集于此。

en:
Nachiyar Koil, properly the Thirunarayur Nambi Temple, is a Sri Vaishnava shrine at Thirunarayur near Kumbakonam in the Thanjavur country, and one of the 108 Divya Desams hymned by the Alvar saints. Vishnu is worshipped here as Srinivasa Perumal and Lakshmi as Nachiyar, the presiding deity.

Legend says the sage Medhavi raised the goddess, found as a girl named Vanjulavalli beneath a vanjula tree, and gave her to Vishnu on the condition that she always take primacy, so in every procession her image comes first. The shrine is attributed to the early Chola king Kochengat Cholan of the late 200s and was enlarged under the medieval Cholas and the Vijayanagara kings.

Its granite enclosure and five-tiered gopuram house the Kal Garuda image, said to grow miraculously heavier as it is carried through each gate during the Brahmotsavam festival.
zh:
那止抴神庙的正式名称为蒂鲁纳鲁尔·南比庙，是坦贾武尔一带贡伯戈讷姆附近蒂鲁纳鲁尔村的一座室利毗湿奴派神庙，也是阿尔瓦尔圣徒颂诗所赞美的108处毗湿奴圣地之一。庙中毗湿奴以斯里尼瓦萨·佩鲁马尔之名受拜，吉祥天女则以“那止亚尔”为主神。

相传仙人梅达毗在万朱拉树下捡到女婴万朱拉瓦利并收为养女，她实为吉祥天女；仙人将她许配毗湿奴时约定女神永远居于首位，所以每次出游行神，女神的神像都走在前面。此庙传为3世纪末早期朱罗国王科琴加特所建，后经中世纪朱罗诸王和毗奢耶那伽罗历代国王扩建。

花岗岩围墙内立着五层塔门，庙中黑迦楼罗像在大节出巡时，据说每过一道门都会奇迹般变重。

en:
Nageshvara, the lord of serpents, is the Jyotirlinga of the Darukavana forest, where the Shiva Purana says Shiva overcame the demon Daruka and settled as a pillar of light. Two shrines claim the title: Nageshwar at Dwarka in Gujarat and Aundha Nagnath in Marathwada, honoured in Maharashtra tradition as the eighth Jyotirlinga.

The present Aundha Nagnath building dates to the 13th century and the Yadavas of Devagiri, built in the mortar-free Hemadpanti style, with the lingam in a basement sanctum. The poet Namdev, who lived from about 1270 to 1350, is said to have been turned away by priests while singing, whereupon the temple rotated to face him, leaving Nandi at the rear.

Damaged in the Delhi Sultanate's invasions of the Deccan, the temple was repaired in the 18th century under Ahilyabai Holkar, who rebuilt the spire; its chariot fair at Maha Shivaratri draws pilgrims.
zh:
纳格什瓦拉意为“蛇之主”，是达鲁迦林森林的究提林迦。《湿婆往世书》说，湿婆降服魔王达鲁迦后，以光柱之形永驻于此。两座神庙争夺这一名号：古吉拉特德瓦尔卡的纳格什瓦尔庙和马拉特瓦达的奥恩达·纳格纳特庙，马哈拉施特拉传统将后者尊为第八处究提林迦。

现存的奥恩达·纳格纳特建筑建于13世纪德瓦吉里亚达瓦王朝时期，采用不用灰浆的赫马德潘蒂风格，林伽安放在地下密室中。相传诗人那摩提婆（约1270—1350年）唱颂时被祭司驱赶，神庙转向他的方向，神牛南迪像因而立于庙后。

神庙在德里苏丹国入侵德干时受损，18世纪阿希莉娅芭伊·霍尔卡加以修缮，重建塔尖；每逢大湿婆夜节，这里的战车庙会吸引朝圣者。

en:
The Nainativu Nagapooshani Amman Temple stands on Nainativu, an island in Palk Bay off the Jaffna peninsula of Sri Lanka, dedicated to Parvati as Nagapooshani, also called Bhuvaneswari, with Shiva worshipped beside her as Nayinaar. The island was known as Manipallavam and its Naga people were serpent worshippers, which gave the goddess her name.

Tamil classics speak of the shrine, and a Tamil inscription from the reign of the Sinhala king Parakramabahu I, between 1153 and 1186, was found in the precinct; it is an edict to his Tamil officials in Jaffna on how to treat shipwrecked foreign traders.

The temple was destroyed by the Portuguese in 1620 and rebuilt between 1720 and 1790. It remained a pilgrimage focus of the Jaffna Tamils, whose sixteen-day summer Mahostavam draws worshippers from across the region.
zh:
奈那底乌·那伽布沙尼女神神庙位于斯里兰卡贾夫纳半岛外、保克湾中的奈那底乌岛，供奉帕尔瓦蒂的化身那伽布沙尼（又名布瓦内湿伐梨），湿婆在此称奈伊纳尔。该岛古称摩尼波罗瓦姆，岛上的那伽人崇奉蛇神，女神之名即由此而来。

泰米尔古典文学已提到这座神庙，庙院内还发现过泰米尔铭文，内容是僧伽罗国王波罗迦罗摩巴忽一世（1153—1186年在位）就如何处置遇险外国商人向贾夫纳当地泰米尔官员颁发的敕令。

旧庙于1620年被葡萄牙人摧毁，1720—1790年间重建。它是贾夫纳泰米尔人的朝圣中心，每年夏季为期16天的大节吸引着各地信众。

en:
Nanto Shichi Daiji is the collective name of the seven great imperial temples of Nara, the old Heijō-kyō capital: Daian-ji, Gangō-ji, Hōryū-ji, Kōfuku-ji, Saidai-ji, Tōdai-ji and Yakushi-ji. Founded by imperial decree in the eighth century, they were the headquarters of the six Nara schools of Buddhism.

Tōdai-ji, made head of the provincial temple system under Emperor Shōmu, housed the great bronze Vairocana Buddha consecrated in 752; the Chinese monk Ganjin ordained clergy there in 754. Kōfuku-ji, the Fujiwara temple, kept its wealth and warrior monks after the court moved to Kyoto in 794.

In 1180 Taira forces burned Kōfuku-ji and Tōdai-ji in the Nara siege, and Minamoto no Yoritomo entrusted the monk Chōgen with their rebuilding, producing the Great South Gate and the giant guardian figures of Unkei and Kaikei; the Great Buddha Hall rose again in 1709.
zh:
南都七大寺是故都平城京奈良七座皇家大寺的合称，即大安寺、元兴寺、法隆寺、兴福寺、西大寺、东大寺和药师寺。它们建于8世纪的天皇诏令之下，是日本佛教南都六宗的总本山。

圣武天皇在位时，东大寺被定为国分寺的总本山，寺内供奉752年开眼供养的巨型毗卢遮那铜像；754年唐朝僧人鉴真在此授戒。藤原氏的氏寺兴福寺在794年朝廷迁都京都后，仍保有财富与僧兵武装。

1180年，平氏军队在南都烧讨中焚毁兴福寺与东大寺；源赖朝命僧人重源主持重建，南大门以及运庆、快庆塑造的巨型金刚力士像便诞生于这一时期，而大佛殿于1709年再度落成。

en:
The Narasimhaswamy Temple is a rock-cut shrine excavated into the Namagiri hill at Namakkal, near Sendamangalam in the Tamil country, and is dedicated to Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu. Legend tells how Hanuman entrusted a shaligrama stone to Lakshmi in disguise; when she set it down it grew into this hill, and Narasimha came to dwell in the image.

Historians date the cave to the sixth to eighth centuries and the Adiyaman kings; one inscription names a king Gunasila around the year 500. In 1500 the Kannada Haridasa Purandarasa, called the grandfather of Carnatic music, visited and sang a hymn to Namagiri Narasimha.

A fort was later raised over the same rock, passing through the hands of the Madurai Nayaks, the Sultans of Bijapur and Golconda, the kings of Mysore and finally the British in 1768.
zh:
纳拉辛哈斯瓦米神庙是凿于纳马卡尔纳马吉里山岩中的石窟神龛，位于泰米尔地区森达曼加拉姆附近，供奉毗湿奴的人狮化身那罗辛哈。相传哈奴曼曾把一块夏利格拉摩圣石托付给化身隐身的拉克什米保管，她将石头放下后，石头便长成了这座山丘，那罗辛哈从此驻于神像之中。

学者判断石窟建于6至8世纪的阿迪亚曼诸王时期；一条铭文提到约500年在位的国王古纳希拉。1500年，被誉为卡纳提克音乐之祖的卡纳达哈里达萨圣徒普兰达拉达萨到此参拜，并为纳马吉里·那罗辛哈赋诗一首。

后来山丘上建起城堡，先后历经马杜赖奈克、比贾普尔与戈尔孔达苏丹、迈索尔君王之手，最终于1768年落入英国人手中。

en:
The Narasingam temple is a Pandya rock-cut shrine at the foot of the Yanaimalai, or Elephant Hill, near Madurai, its Narasimha image carved out of the living rock. Inscriptions record that work began in 770 under Maran Kari, a minister of the Pandya king, and was finished by his brother Maran Eyinan, who added the entrance hall and consecrated the shrine.

Its sthalapurana tells that the sage Romasa performed penance here to see Vishnu in his man-lion form; the ferocious Ugra Narasimha was softened by Prahlada's prayers and by Lakshmi, who took her place in him as Narasingavalli, yielding the serene Yoga Narasimha.

The Thiruvilaiyadal Purana adds that the Elephant Hill was once a magic elephant sent against the Pandya king and turned to stone by the Narasimha mantra. Pandya-period halls and a separate shrine of the goddess Narasingavalli frame the cave.
zh:
纳拉辛加姆神庙是一座潘地亚石窟神庙，坐落在马杜赖附近的亚奈马莱山，即象山的山脚，那罗辛哈像从原生岩石中凿出。铭文记载，工程于770年由潘地亚国王的大臣马兰卡里主持开工，后由其弟马兰·埃伊南续成，他增建门厅并为神龛举行开光仪式。

当地圣传称，仙人罗摩萨在此苦行，以求一见毗湿奴的人狮化身；忿怒的乌格拉·那罗辛哈因帕拉拉达的祈祷和拉克什米的到来而平息，拉克什米化身为纳拉辛加瓦利安住其身，那罗辛哈由此成为安详的瑜伽那罗辛哈。

《蒂鲁维莱亚达尔往世书》还说，这座象山本是敌方用来对付潘地亚国王的神象，被那罗辛哈咒语化为石头。石窟之外，潘地亚时期的厅堂和女神纳拉辛加瓦利的独立神龛环绕四周。

en:
Nashik, on the Godavari in Maharashtra, is known in the Ramayana as Panchavati, where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana passed part of their exile. Lakshmana cut off the nose of the demoness Shurpanakha, from which the city's name is popularly derived.

At Trimbak, the Godavari springs beside the Trimbakeshwar temple, a Jyotirlinga shrine of Shiva with a three-faced linga of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. Aurangzeb destroyed the medieval temple and the Maratha Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao rebuilt it.

Every twelve years, when Jupiter enters Leo, the Simhastha bathing fair draws pilgrims to the Godavari. Until 1789 it was held only at Trimbak, but that year Shaivite sanyasis and Vaishnavite bairagis fought over bathing order; a Peshwa copperplate claims twelve thousand ascetics died. The Peshwa moved the Vaishnavites' bathing place to the Ram Kund in Nashik, splitting the festival between the two towns.
zh:
纳西克位于马哈拉施特拉的戈达瓦里河畔，在《罗摩衍那》中称般查瓦提，是罗摩、悉多与罗什曼那流放时的栖居之处。罗什曼那在此割下罗刹女巨爪的鼻子，民间认为城名便源于此。

在特里姆巴克，戈达瓦里河从特里姆巴克什瓦尔神庙旁涌出；神庙是湿婆的究提林迦圣地，林伽兼具梵天、毗湿奴、湿婆三面。中世纪神庙被奥朗则布拆毁，马拉塔佩什瓦巴拉吉·巴吉·拉奥重建了它。

每隔十二年，当木星进入狮子座，狮子座节沐浴大会便吸引朝圣者来到戈达瓦里河畔。1789年以前节会只在特里姆巴克举行；那一年湿婆派遁世僧与毗湿奴派拜拉吉为沐浴次序大打出手，佩什瓦的铜匾铭文称有一万两千名苦行僧丧命。佩什瓦随后把毗湿奴派的沐浴地迁到纳西克的罗摩池，节会从此分在两地举行。

en:
The Navlakha Temple stands at Ghumli, below the Barda hills in western Saurashtra. The Jethwa rulers built this shrine to the sun god Surya in the eleventh or twelfth century, making it the oldest surviving sun temple in Gujarat. Its name, meaning nine lakhs, recalls the vast sum spent on its construction.

Built in the Maru-Gurjara or Solanki style, it has the largest temple platform in the region, an entrance once crowned by a Kirti Toran arch and an eight-pillared assembly hall. Its niches contain images of Brahma and Savitri, Shiva and Parvati, and Lakshmi-Narayana.

The Jethwa ruler Rana Shiyaji made Ghumli his capital again in 1220, but in 1313 the Jadeja chieftain Barmaniyaji sacked the city and drove the Jethwas to Ranpur, leaving the temple among the ruins.
zh:
纳夫拉卡神庙位于萨乌拉施特拉西部巴尔达山麓的古姆利。杰特瓦统治者在11或12世纪修建了这座供奉太阳神苏利耶的神庙，它也是古吉拉特现存最古老的太阳神庙。庙名意为“九万”，据说来自建庙耗费的巨额资金。

神庙采用马鲁-古吉拉风格，又称索兰基风格，拥有当地最大的庙台；庙门上方曾有一座“光荣门”拱门，会堂由八根立柱支撑。壁龛中分别刻有梵天与萨维特丽、湿婆与帕尔瓦蒂、吉祥天女与那罗延的造像。

1220年杰特瓦君主拉纳·希亚吉再次定都古姆利，但1313年贾德贾首领巴尔马尼亚吉攻陷并摧毁了这座城市，杰特瓦人逃往兰布尔，神庙便留在废墟之中。

en:
The crater lake of Nemi south of Rome was ringed by the sacred grove and sanctuary of Diana Nemorensis, Diana of the Wood. From the sixth century BC the grove was a common holy place of the Latin cities; the temple was built around 300 BC.

Legend traced the cult to Orestes and Iphigenia, who were said to have brought the image of the Tauric Diana to Italy. A runaway slave who broke a branch from the sacred oak might challenge the priest to mortal combat, and if he killed him became king of the grove.

Each August the festival of the Nemoralia drew pilgrims who garlanded their boats with flowers on the lake. Caligula built two enormous floating pleasure palaces on the lake, later sunk and forgotten.
zh:
内米湖是罗马以南的火山口湖，湖畔环绕着林中狄安娜（狄安娜·内莫伦西斯）的圣林与圣所。从公元前6世纪起，这片圣林就是拉丁诸城共同的圣地；约公元前300年，这里建起了神庙。

传说这套崇拜由俄瑞斯忒斯和伊菲革涅亚创立，据说他们把陶里斯的狄安娜神像带到了意大利。逃亡奴隶只要折下圣橡树的一根枝条，就有权向祭司发起生死决斗，若能杀死对方便成为圣林之王。

每年8月的内莫拉利亚节，朝圣者乘船游湖，用花环装点船只。卡利古拉在湖上建造了两艘巨大的游乐浮宫，后来沉没并被人遗忘。

en:
The Nithyakalyana Perumal Temple at Thiruvidandai in Tamil Nadu is dedicated to Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu, worshipped as Nithyakalyana Perumal with Lakshmi as Komalavalli Thayar. It is among the 108 Divya Desams, Vishnu shrines glorified in the Tamil hymns of the Alvar saints.

Its name means the eternal bridegroom. In the legend, after Varaha slew the asura Hiranyaksha and lifted the drowned earth on his tusks, the sage Kalava asked him to marry his three hundred and sixty daughters; Lakshmi took that many forms and wedded him in a fresh shape each day of the year.

The Pallavas raised the original shrine in the seventh century. Chola epigraphs credit Raja Raja I with founding the Panguni Uthiram festival in 1003 and Rajadhiraja with additions in 1052. Built in the Dravidian style, the temple follows the Tenkalai mode of worship.
zh:
尼搋羯耶那·闭卢末神庙位于泰米尔纳德的蒂鲁维丹代，供奉毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃：主神称尼搋羯耶那·闭卢末，配偶吉祥天女称科马拉瓦利·塔亚尔。它是108处迪维亚·德萨姆圣地之一，受到阿尔瓦尔圣徒的泰米尔语赞歌颂扬。

庙名意为“永远的新郎”。相传筏罗诃诛杀阿修罗王金目，用獠牙把沉没的大地托出海面；仙人迦罗伐恳求他迎娶自己的三百六十个女儿，吉祥天女便化出三百六十种身形，一年中每天以一副新容貌与他成婚。

神庙最初由帕拉瓦王朝于7世纪修建。朱罗碑刻记载罗阇罗阇一世于1003年创设潘古尼·乌蒂拉姆节，罗贾迪罗阇于1052年扩建神庙。神庙为达罗毗荼风格，遵腾卡莱仪轨。

en:
Olympia is a sanctuary of Zeus in Elis, where the Olympic Games were held every four years. Tradition dates the first games to 776 BC, and the sacred precinct was called the Altis.

The Temple of Hera was built around 600 BC, and the mid-fifth-century BC Temple of Zeus housed the gigantic chryselephantine statue of the god made by Pheidias. The games drew crowds under the protection of an Olympic truce.

Under Rome the festival was opened to all citizens of the empire, but the last ancient Olympiad was celebrated in 393 AD, shortly before the Christian emperor Theodosius I banned pagan cults; the Temple of Zeus was destroyed around 426, and floods buried the site in the seventh century. The English antiquarian Richard Chandler rediscovered it in 1766, and French and German excavators uncovered the ruins from 1829 onward.
zh:
奥林匹亚是伊利斯境内供奉宙斯的圣地，奥林匹克运动会每四年在此举行。传统上把首届赛会定在公元前776年，圣区名为阿尔提斯。

赫拉神庙建于约公元前600年，公元前5世纪中叶的宙斯神庙中安放着菲狄亚斯制作的巨型黄金象牙宙斯像。赛会在奥林匹克休战的庇护下吸引各地人群前来。

罗马统治时期，节庆向帝国所有公民开放，但最后一届古代奥运会于393年举行，不久基督教皇帝狄奥多西一世下令禁止异教崇拜；宙斯神庙约于426年被毁，7世纪的洪水又将遗址埋没。1766年英国古董商理查德·钱德勒重新发现此地，1829年起法国和德国的考古队相继发掘出这片废墟。

en:
Mount Olympos is the great massif on the ancient border of Thessaly and Macedonia, whose highest summit, Mytikas, rises to nearly three thousand metres, the highest peak in Greece. In Greek belief it was the home of the Twelve Olympian gods and the throne of Zeus above the clouds.

Pilgrims climbed the peaks to sacrifice, and pottery, coins and ashes dated to around 400 BC have been found on the summit. At the eastern foot lay Dion, the sacred city of the Macedonians, dedicated to Zeus and the Twelve, which flourished from the fifth century BC to the fifth century AD.

Under Ottoman rule the mountain became a refuge of klephts and armatoloi, and in the sixteenth century the chapel of Prophet Elias was built on one of its high peaks.
zh:
奥林波斯山是横亘在色萨利与马其顿古边界上的巨大山体，最高峰米蒂卡斯峰海拔近三千米，为希腊第一高峰。在希腊人的信仰中，这里是奥林匹斯十二主神的居所，是宙斯凌驾云端的王座。

朝圣者攀上山峰献祭，山顶已发现约公元前400年的陶器、钱币和灰烬。东麓的迪翁是马其顿人的圣城，供奉宙斯和十二主神，从公元前5世纪一直兴盛到公元5世纪。

奥斯曼统治时期，此山成为山贼克莱夫特和民兵武装阿尔马托利的藏身之地；16世纪，人们又在一座高峰上建起了先知以利亚礼拜堂。

en:
The oracle of Amun stood in the remote Siwa Oasis of Egypt's Western Desert. The Greeks called it Ammonium and equated the ram-headed Egyptian god with Zeus. Greek settlers from Cyrene contacted the sanctuary in the seventh century BC.

About 525 BC the Persian king Cambyses II sent fifty thousand men across the desert to subdue it; according to Herodotus the force vanished in a sandstorm. In 331 BC Alexander the Great crossed the desert, supposedly guided by birds, and the priests greeted him as the god's son and confirmed him as legitimate pharaoh of Egypt.

Under the Ptolemies the sanctuary retained its prestige, but its influence later waned. With the Christianisation of the late Roman Empire the oracle fell silent, leaving the ruined temple among the oasis palms.
zh:
阿蒙神谕所坐落于埃及西部沙漠深处的锡瓦绿洲。希腊人称这里为阿摩尼乌姆，把长着公羊头的埃及神等同于宙斯。公元前7世纪，来自昔兰尼的希腊定居者与圣所建立了联系。

公元前525年前后，波斯国王冈比西斯二世派遣五万人横穿沙漠前去征服神谕所；据希罗多德记载，这支军队在沙暴中全军覆没。公元前331年，亚历山大大帝据称由飞鸟引路穿过沙漠，祭司们以神之子的身份迎接他，并确认他为埃及的合法法老。

托勒密王朝时期圣所仍保有威望，但其影响力后来衰落。随着罗马帝国晚期基督教化，神谕终告沉寂，只剩神庙残迹立于绿洲的棕榈树间。

en:
The cathedral of the Holy Saviour in Oviedo is the great shrine church of Asturias in northern Spain. King Fruela I founded it in 781, and his son Alfonso II made Oviedo the Asturian capital, enlarged the church after 802 and established the see in 810.

Alfonso raised the Cámara Santa to hold relics carried north from Toledo when the Moors overran the south in 718. These included the bloodstained Sudarium, venerated as the cloth that covered Christ's head and kept in the silver-bound Arca Santa. In 1075 Alfonso VI, his sister and the Cid opened the relic chest after days of fasting.

Bishop Pelagius restored the church in the twelfth century. The Gothic cathedral was begun in 1388 under Bishop Gutierre; its tower went up in 1528 and was finished with an octagonal spire in the mid-sixteenth century.
zh:
奥维耶多的圣救主主教座堂是西班牙北部阿斯图里亚斯的重要圣所。781年，弗鲁埃拉一世国王创建了它；其子阿方索二世把奥维耶多定为阿斯图里亚斯王国的都城，802年后扩建教堂，并于810年设立主教区。

阿方索建起圣室，收藏718年摩尔人席卷南方时从托莱多北运的圣物。其中有被敬为基督裹头之巾、带血渍的圣巾，安放在包银的圣柜之中。1075年，阿方索六世、他的妹妹和熙德在数日斋戒后共同开启了圣物箱。

12世纪时，佩拉吉乌斯主教修缮了教堂。哥特式主教座堂于1388年在古铁雷主教主持下动工，高塔建于1528年，并在16世纪中期装上八角形尖顶后竣工。

en:
Pagan, on the Irrawaddy in central Burma, was the capital of the first kingdom to unite the lands that became Myanmar. Burman settlers from Nanzhao founded the walled city in the ninth century; from 1044 it served as the seat of the Pagan kings.

From the mid-eleventh century the rulers patronised Theravada Buddhism. Over two and a half centuries they and their wealthy subjects raised more than ten thousand stupas, temples and monasteries across the plain. Pagan became a centre of Pali learning, although Mahayana, Hindu and nat traditions continued alongside Theravada.

Mongol invasions from 1277 brought the kingdom down in 1287, and in 1297 Pagan ceased to be the capital of Upper Burma. It lived on as a pilgrimage town: great temples such as Ananda and Shwezigon kept their devotees, and Konbaung kings sponsored renovations.
zh:
蒲甘城位于缅甸中部伊洛瓦底江畔，是首个统一缅甸诸地的王国——蒲甘王国的都城。9世纪，从南诏南迁的缅人建起这座城墙环绕的城市；1044年起，它成为蒲甘诸王的王都。

11世纪中叶起，诸王扶持上座部佛教。在两个半世纪里，王室与富有的臣民在平原上修建了上万座佛塔、寺院与僧院。蒲甘成为巴利语学术中心，大乘佛教、印度教与本土纳特信仰仍与上座部并存。

1277年起蒙古军队入侵，蒲甘王国于1287年崩溃，1297年蒲甘不再是上缅甸的都城。此后它作为朝圣城镇延续下来：阿难陀寺、瑞喜宫塔等大寺香火不断，贡榜诸王还出资重修。

en:
The Palitana temples crown the twin ridges of Shatrunjaya hill above Palitana in southern Gujarat, forming the holiest pilgrimage complex of Svetambara Jainism. Jains hold that the first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha, or Adinatha, preached here and that twenty-three of the twenty-four Tirthankaras visited the hill. His first disciple Pundarika attained nirvana here, giving the hill its older name of Pundarikgiri.

The earliest shrines date to the eleventh century, and a marble image of Pundarika was consecrated in 1120. The principal Adinatha temple's hall was renovated in 1157, while the four-faced Chaumukh temple was raised in 1616.

Nearly nine hundred white marble temples cluster along the ridges in nine fortified enclosures called tuks. Repeated damage and rebuilding, especially from the sixteenth century, shaped the complex. No one, priest or pilgrim, may spend the night on the sacred hill.
zh:
波利多拿寺坐落于古吉拉特南部巴利塔纳镇上方沙特伦贾亚山的两道山脊上，是耆那教白衣派最神圣的朝圣建筑群。信众相信，第一代祖师勒舍婆那陀（又称阿底那特）曾在此传道，二十四祖中有二十三位曾登临此山。他的首弟子蓬达哩迦在此证得涅槃，此山因而旧名蓬达哩迦山。

山上最早的殿宇可追溯至11世纪，1120年有蓬达哩迦大理石像开光。主殿阿底那特寺的拜殿于1157年重修，四面造像的朝穆基寺则建于1616年。

近九百座白色大理石庙宇沿山脊密布，分成九座带围墙的图克群。神庙屡遭损毁又反复重建，尤其是在16世纪以后。无论祭司还是朝圣者，皆不得在圣山上过夜。

en:
The Pandava Thoothar Perumal Temple, also called Thirupadagam, stands in Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu and honours Krishna as the Pandavas' envoy. Its legend retells the Mahabharata episode in which Krishna went to the Kaurava court to negotiate for the Pandavas: when Duryodhana tried to seize him from a pit hidden beneath his seat, Krishna revealed his cosmic vishvarupa form to the court and the blind king Dhritarashtra.

One of the hundred and eight Divya Desams sung by the Alvar saints between the 6th and 9th centuries, it ranks among Kanchipuram's three oldest Vishnu temples and was probably built under the Pallavas in the late 700s.

Chola inscriptions of the 1000s record gifts of lamps, cows and gardens, and later Vijayanagara rulers added to its halls. The Dravidian temple has a four-tiered gopuram, and its chief festival is Krishna Janmashtami.
zh:
般度族闭卢末神庙又名“底鲁帕达加姆”，位于泰米尔纳德的甘吉布勒姆，供奉作为般度族使者的奎师那。其传说重述了《摩诃婆罗多》中奎师那出使俱卢族朝堂为般度族斡旋的情节：难敌在座位下暗设陷阱企图擒拿他，奎师那当朝向盲王持国及群臣显现了宇宙相“毗湿瓦鲁帕”。

该庙是6至9世纪阿尔瓦尔派圣徒颂唱的一百零八座迪维亚·德萨姆之一，也是甘吉布勒姆最古老的三座毗湿奴庙之一，可能建于8世纪末的帕拉瓦王朝时期。

庙墙上留有11世纪朱罗铭文，记载信众布施灯油、牛只和园林之事，后来的维查耶纳伽尔统治者又增建了殿宇。整庙为达罗毗荼风格，立有四层门楼，最重要的节庆是奎师那诞辰节。

en:
The Panniyur Sri Varahamurthy Temple at Kumbidi, near Ponnani in northern Kerala, is dedicated to Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu, enthroned with the earth goddess Bhumi. It is counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethras of the Vaishnava tradition.

Kerala tradition calls it the first temple of the land: after Parashurama reclaimed the country from the sea, Vishnu bade him worship his boar form, and he consecrated the image with his own hands. The shrine is said to have held primacy from roughly 800 BC to 600 AD; stone engravings record the thousand-member Panniyuraayiram, which ran its rites and festivals.

In Kerala folklore the master carpenter Perumthachan rebuilt the sanctum. When the work was done he cast down his chisel and measuring rod, which were kept at the temple as relics.
zh:
般尼逾剌室利筏罗诃化身神庙位于喀拉拉北部蓬纳尼附近的昆比迪，供奉毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃，主神与大地女神布弥并坐。它被列为毗湿奴派108处阿比摩纳圣地之一。

喀拉拉传统称它是本地第一座神庙：相传持斧罗摩从海中辟出此地后，毗湿奴命他敬拜自己的野猪化身，他便亲手为神像开光。传说从约公元前800年到公元600年，这座神庙在喀拉拉居于首位；石刻还记载千人团体般尼逾罗伊拉姆负责操办神庙祭仪与节庆。

喀拉拉民间传说中的木匠祖师佩鲁姆塔昌重修了圣所。完工后他弃凿尺而去，这两件工具后来作为圣物珍藏庙中。

en:
Parshuram Kund is a Hindu shrine and sacred bathing pool on the Lohit River in the eastern Himalayan foothills, near Sadiya, which in 1337 lay at the heart of the Chutia kingdom. It is dedicated to Parashurama, the axe-wielding sixth avatar of Vishnu; pilgrims hold that a dip in its waters washes away sin.

The annual gathering takes place at Makar Sankranti in January, when devotees and sadhus travel there from Assam, Manipur and Nepal. Brahmanical Vaishnavism took root at the Chutia court in the late fourteenth century, and the shrine kept drawing pilgrims after the Ahom kingdom overran Sadiya in 1523 and 1524, when the region passed under Ahom rule.
zh:
持斧罗摩池桥是洛希特河畔的印度教圣地与圣沐浴池，地处喜马拉雅山东麓、萨地亚附近，1337年时这里是楚蒂亚王国的核心地带。它供奉毗湿奴的第六化身、手持战斧的持斧罗摩；信众相信在池水中沐浴可涤除罪业。

每年一月的马克尔桑克兰蒂节期间举行集会，来自阿萨姆、曼尼普尔和尼泊尔的信众与苦行僧远道而来。14世纪末，婆罗门教的毗湿奴信仰在楚蒂亚宫廷扎根；1523—1524年阿洪姆王国攻占萨地亚，此地归入阿洪姆治下，而这座神庙仍持续吸引朝圣者。

en:
The Parthasarathy Temple stands in Thiruvallikeni, the lily-pond quarter of Madras, and is dedicated to Krishna as the charioteer of Arjuna in the Mahabharata. Its image bears a moustache, unique among Vishnu icons, and the wound left by Bhishma's arrow at Kurukshetra.

A Pallava foundation of the sixth century, traditionally credited to King Narasimhavarman I, it was enlarged under the Cholas. The Alvar saints sang of it, and it ranks among the 108 Vaishnava Divya Desams. Vijayanagara rulers added halls and sub-shrines in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries; a restoration in 1564 gave the temple much of its form.

After Madras passed to the East India Company, the village was leased in the 1670s to its merchant Kasi Viranna. From 1789 the Board of Revenue supervised temple funds, until Regulation VII of 1817 and an order of 1821 withdrew the collector from its management.
zh:
阿周那之御者奎师那神庙位于马德拉斯的提鲁瓦利凯尼，意为百合池塘，供奉在《摩诃婆罗多》中为阿周那驾车的奎师那。庙中神像留着胡须，在毗湿奴神像中独一无二，身上还带有俱卢之野战场上毗湿摩箭矢留下的伤痕。

神庙始建于6世纪，相传为帕拉瓦国王纳拉辛哈跋摩一世所建，朱罗时期扩建。阿尔瓦尔圣人歌咏此庙，它也位列毗湿奴派108座圣庙之一。15—16世纪，毗奢耶那伽罗诸王增建厅堂与配殿；1564年的大修奠定了神庙的大部分格局。

马德拉斯落入东印度公司之手后，村落于17世纪70年代租给公司商人卡西·维兰纳。1789年起税务委员会监管庙产，直到1817年第七号条例和1821年的命令使税务官退出庙务管理。

en:
The Parthenon is the temple of Athena on the Acropolis of Athens. An earlier temple begun after the Battle of Marathon was unfinished when the Persians sacked Athens in 480 BC. The present building was raised under Pericles between 447 and 438 BC; its cella housed Pheidias' colossal chryselephantine Athena Parthenos, and the rear chamber held the Delian League treasury.

In the final decade of the sixth century AD it became a church of the Virgin Mary, and under Latin rule a Catholic church. After the Ottoman conquest of Athens in 1458 it became a mosque with a minaret.

On 26 September 1687 a Venetian mortar shell ignited the Turkish gunpowder store and blew the centre apart. Lord Elgin removed about half the surviving sculptures between 1801 and 1812; after Greece took Athens in 1832 the minaret and later additions were cleared away.
zh:
帕特农神庙是雅典卫城上供奉雅典娜的神庙。马拉松战役后动工的早期神庙尚未完工，便在公元前480年波斯人洗劫雅典时被毁。现存建筑建于伯里克利执政时期，公元前447年开工、前438年落成；内殿安放菲狄亚斯制作的巨型黄金象牙雅典娜·帕特农像，后殿储存提洛同盟的金库。

6世纪最后十年，它被改为供奉圣母马利亚的教堂，拉丁人统治时期又成为天主教堂。1458年奥斯曼征服雅典后，它被改建为清真寺并添建宣礼塔。

1687年9月26日，威尼斯炮弹引爆土耳其火药库，炸塌建筑中央。1801—1812年，埃尔金伯爵运走约半数幸存雕刻；1832年希腊收复雅典后，宣礼塔和后世添建的建筑被清除。

en:
The Pathirakali Amman Temple is a Hindu shrine in Trincomalee on the east coast of Sri Lanka, dedicated to Bhadrakali, a fierce form of the goddess Kali. It forms the Kali temple of the ancient Koneswaram compound. Tamil tradition counts it among the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas, marking the place where the goddess's waist fell.

Pilgrims visited before the eleventh century, and the Chola emperor Rajendra I enlarged the shrine early in that century, leaving an inscription on the premises. Together with Koneswaram it takes part in the annual Ther Thiruvillah procession.

When the Portuguese destroyed the Koneswaram complex between 1622 and 1624 and built a fort from its rubble, some of the original idols were installed in a new temple built in 1632, while the Amman shrine continued to be venerated as the seat of the peetha.
zh:
贤迦梨母神庙位于斯里兰卡东海岸的亭可马里，供奉迦梨女神的凶相化身巴德拉迦梨，是古代科内斯瓦拉姆神庙群中的迦梨神殿。泰米尔传统把它列入十八处大性力圣地，传说女神的腰肢坠落于此。

11世纪以前已有香客前来，朱罗皇帝拉金德拉一世在11世纪初扩建此庙，留下的铭文陈列庙中。它每年与科内斯瓦拉姆神庙共同举行提鲁维拉节游行。

1622—1624年间葡萄牙人摧毁科内斯瓦拉姆庙群，并用其残料修建堡垒，部分原始神像被移入1632年新建的庙宇，而这座安曼神殿仍作为性力圣地受人礼拜。

en:
Pella, in Lower Macedonia beside the Thermaic Gulf, became the Macedonian capital under Archelaus I around 400 BC; Aigai remained the royal burial ground. Philip II was born here in 382 BC and Alexander the Great in 356 BC.

The Argead kings claimed descent from Heracles and ultimately Zeus and acted as high priests and patrons of the kingdom's cults. Temples of Aphrodite, Cybele and Demeter stood in the city, whose pebble mosaics show Dionysus riding a leopard. Pella remained the seat of Philip V and Perseus in their wars with Rome.

After the defeat at Pydna the Romans sacked Pella in 168 BC. An earthquake around 90 BC destroyed much of it, though the Via Egnatia kept the rebuilt town alive. It became a colony between 45 and 30 BC and shrank in Byzantine times to a fortified village.
zh:
佩拉位于下马其顿、濒临塞尔迈湾，约公元前400年在阿奇拉一世治下成为马其顿都城；埃盖继续作为王室陵寝所在地。腓力二世于公元前382年、亚历山大大帝于公元前356年出生于此。

阿吉德王朝自称是赫拉克勒斯的后裔、最终可上溯至宙斯，国王兼任最高祭司与王国各崇拜的赞助人。城中建有阿佛洛狄忒、西布莉和得墨忒耳的神庙，卵石镶嵌画描绘着骑豹的狄俄尼索斯。佩拉也是腓力五世和珀尔修斯对罗马作战时的都城。

皮德纳战败后，罗马人于公元前168年洗劫佩拉。约公元前90年的地震摧毁大半城市，但埃格纳提亚大道使重建的城镇维持生机。公元前45—前30年它成为殖民地，到拜占庭时代缩为一处设防村落。

en:
The Altar of Zeus at Pergamon stood on a terrace of the acropolis of the Attalid capital in Asia Minor. King Eumenes II raised it in the first half of the second century BC, after the Treaty of Apamea of 188 BC made Pergamon the chief power of western Anatolia under Roman protection.

Its base, more than thirty-five metres wide, carried a high-relief frieze showing the Olympian gods battling the Giants. A second frieze in the inner court depicted the life of Telephus, son of Heracles and legendary founder of the city.

The fire altar ceased to be used with the rise of Christianity. In the seventh century the acropolis was fortified against the Arabs, and the monument was partly dismantled for building stone before the Arabs took the city in 716. In 1625 agents of the Earl of Arundel carried two frieze panels to England.
zh:
帕加马的宙斯祭坛位于小亚细亚阿塔罗斯王朝都城的卫城台地上，由国王欧迈尼斯二世建于公元前2世纪上半叶。公元前188年的《阿帕米亚条约》使帕加马在罗马庇护下成为安纳托利亚西部的首要强国。

祭坛宽逾35米的基座上环绕着高浮雕饰带，刻画奥林匹斯诸神与巨人厮杀；内院第二道饰带讲述赫拉克勒斯之子、城市传说建立者忒勒福斯的生平。

随着基督教兴起，祭坛上的圣火祭祀停止。7世纪时卫城为抵御阿拉伯人而加固城防，祭坛在716年阿拉伯人攻陷城市前被部分拆毁，石材挪作他用。1625年，阿伦德尔伯爵的手下将两块浮雕饰板运回英格兰。

en:
The Polali Rajarajeshwari Temple is a goddess shrine at Polali on the Tulu-speaking coast of Karnataka, where the river bends sharply beside the town. Local inscriptions date the temple around its clay icon to the 700s; tradition names King Suratha as its builder, said to have offered his jewelled crown to the goddess, known in early records as Porala Devi.

The Persian envoy Abdul Razzak, visiting in 1448, described a temple of molten brass on four platforms with a five-to-six-foot image whose eyes were red rubies. The principal image is a ten-foot stucco Rajarajeshwari modelled from clay mixed with herbal compounds.

Every twelve years the idols are freshly coated with medicinal earth in the Lepashta Gandha rite. The wooden roof of the entrance hall is carved with figures of the gods, while the other roofs are sheeted in copper.
zh:
波罗利·罗阇罗誓湿伐梨神庙位于卡纳塔克讲图卢语的沿海地带，河水流经镇旁急转。当地铭文显示，环绕泥塑神像的庙宇建于8世纪；传说建庙者是苏拉陀王，据说他曾把镶满宝石的王冠献给女神，早期文献中女神被称为波罗罗提毗。

1448年波斯使节阿卜杜勒·拉扎克到访时，记载此庙以熔铜筑成、立于四层台基之上，五六尺高的神像双目嵌有红宝石。主像是一尊10尺高的罗阇罗誓湿伐梨灰泥像，以拌有草药的黏土塑成。

每隔12年，神像要在勒帕什塔·甘陀仪式中用药泥重新敷身。门厅木顶雕满诸神形象，其余殿顶则覆以铜板。

en:
Prayag, later called Allahabad, lies beside the confluence of the Ganges, Yamuna and mythical Sarasvati. Its Sanskrit name means place of sacrifice, for tradition holds that Brahma performed the first sacrifice there. The Mahabharata and Puranas praise bathing there in Magha as washing away sin and winning heaven.

The annual Magh Mela is the oldest of the great Indian bathing festivals. The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang described in 644 King Harsha's quinquennial assembly, with crowds bathing at the river junction. The later twelve-yearly Kumbh gathering grew out of this festival.

Through the sultanate and Mughal periods the fair continued, and Akbar built his Allahabad fort overlooking the sangam. By the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries it was organised by the akharas, armed bands of Hindu ascetics, whose rival claims to bathe first sometimes ended in bloody clashes.
zh:
普拉亚格后称安拉阿巴德，城旁是恒河、亚穆纳河与神话中的萨拉斯瓦蒂河汇流处。其梵语名意为“祭祀之地”，相传梵天曾在此举行第一场祭祀。《摩诃婆罗多》和诸往世书称，摩伽月在此沐浴可洗清罪孽、得升天界。

河畔一年一度的摩伽节是印度最古老的大型沐浴节会。644年，中国求法僧玄奘记载了戒日王在此每五年举行的大会，以及成群朝圣者在河口沐浴的盛况。后世十二年一度的大壶节由此发展而来。

苏丹国与莫卧儿时期节会依旧延续，阿克巴在俯瞰汇流处修建了安拉阿巴德城堡。到17、18世纪，节会由印度教苦行僧的武装僧团“阿哈拉”主持，各僧团为争取最先沐浴而相争，有时酿成流血冲突。

en:
The Prophet's Mosque in Medina is the second holiest site of Islam after the Sacred Mosque of Mecca. Muhammad built it in 622, after the hijra; the original open-air building of palm trunks and beaten clay served as a place of prayer, a law court and a school.

The Umayyad caliph al-Walid I rebuilt it between 705 and 715, bringing the graves of Muhammad and of the first two caliphs, Abu Bakr and Umar within its walls.

In 1279 the Mamluk sultan Qalawun raised a wooden dome over the prophet's tomb, rebuilt in stone under Qaitbay in the fifteenth century and again under the Ottoman sultan Mahmud II in 1817; this is the Green Dome, the mosque's most famous landmark. When Wahhabi forces held Medina between 1805 and 1813 they stripped the tomb of its ornaments but spared the dome.
zh:
先知清真寺位于麦地那，是伊斯兰教仅次于麦加禁寺的第二大圣寺。622年穆罕默德迁徙麦地那后兴建此寺；最初是棕榈木梁柱、夯土屋顶的露天建筑，兼作礼拜场所、法庭和学校。

伍麦叶哈里发瓦利德一世于705—715年重建清真寺，将穆罕默德以及前两任哈里发阿布·伯克尔、欧麦尔的陵墓纳入寺内。

1279年马穆鲁克苏丹嘉拉温在先知墓上建起木构穹顶，15世纪卡伊特拜时期改为石构，1817年奥斯曼苏丹马哈茂德二世再次重建，这便是寺内最著名的标志绿穹顶。1805—1813年瓦哈比派占据麦地那期间，墓上装饰被剥除，但穹顶得以幸免。

en:
The Pyramid of the Magician is the tallest monument of Uxmal, a great Maya city of the Puuc Hills in western Yucatan. Work on the first temple pyramid began in the sixth century, and for four hundred years successive builders wrapped older temples inside new ones, giving the structure its unusual elliptical base and steep, rounded sides.

Its upper temples blend Puuc and Chenes styles, their doorways framed by giant masks of the rain god Chaac. Maya legend recorded after the Spanish conquest told of a dwarf hatched from an egg who built the pyramid overnight to save his life and then ruled Uxmal.

The city's great building age ended around 1000, after which the pyramid fell into ruin. During the Spanish conquest of Yucatan it was looted and left to the forest, its old cult long silent.
zh:
魔法师金字塔是乌斯马尔最高的建筑。乌斯马尔是尤卡坦西部普克丘陵的玛雅大城。最早的神庙金字塔于6世纪动工，此后四百年间，历代建造者把旧神庙层层包裹在新建筑之内，形成独特的椭圆形底座和陡峭圆弧形侧面。

上层神庙融合普克风格与切内斯风格，门道由雨神恰克的巨大面具环绕。西班牙征服后记录下来的玛雅传说讲，一个从蛋中孵出的矮人为保命连夜建起金字塔，随后统治了乌斯马尔。

乌斯马尔的大兴土木时代在1000年前后终结，金字塔随之倾颓。西班牙征服尤卡坦期间它遭劫掠，被弃于丛林之中，古老的崇拜早已沉寂。

en:
Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez began as a mosque founded in 857 or 859 by Fatima al-Fihri, whose family had migrated from Kairouan, which gave the institution its name. In 919 or 933 the Friday sermon was transferred to it, making it the chief mosque of the city; it grew into a leading centre of learning.

The Almoravids expanded the building, and the earliest clear evidence of regular teaching there dates to 1121. Under the Almohad sultan Muhammad al-Nasir, between 1199 and 1213, it received a great bronze chandelier for its prayer hall.

The Marinid period marked its intellectual apogee: a chandelier cast from a church bell brought from Gibraltar was installed in 1337, and Sultan Abu Inan founded its library in 1349. Besides the Quran and Maliki law, its curriculum covered medicine, mathematics and astronomy, drawing students from Morocco and Muslim West Africa.
zh:
非斯的卡拉维因最初是一座清真寺，857年或859年由法蒂玛·菲赫里出资修建，她的家族从凯鲁万迁来，这座学府也因此得名。919年或933年，周五聚礼的讲道转移到此，它由此成为全城的主麻清真寺，并逐步成长为重要的学术中心。

穆拉比特王朝扩建了建筑，关于寺内常规教学最早的明确记载出现在1121年。穆瓦希德王朝苏丹穆罕默德·纳西尔在位期间（1199—1213年），礼拜殿添置了巨大的青铜吊灯。

马林王朝时期是它学术上的巅峰：1337年安装了用从直布罗陀带回的教堂铜钟改铸的吊灯，苏丹阿布·伊南于1349年敕建了图书馆。除《古兰经》和马立克派教法外，其课程还涵盖医学、数学和天文，吸引着摩洛哥和穆斯林西非的学生。

en:
Nevado Queva, or Quewar, is a volcano in the Andes of northwestern Argentina, rising to 6,140 metres. Its summit crater holds a large stone platform raised by the Incas after the southern Andes were drawn into the province of Qullasuyu. Topa Inca Yupanqui, who ruled from 1471 to 1493, subdued the Qulla people, and the Argentine northwest was fully absorbed under his successor Huayna Capac.

In Andean religion high peaks were venerated as apu, mountain spirits held to protect communities and receive offerings. The Inca state placed shrines on their summits to anchor its rule. Quewar's crater sanctuary belongs to this cult of sacred mountains, which also practised high-altitude child sacrifice on its most revered peaks.
zh:
奎瓦尔圣山是阿根廷西北部安第斯山脉中的一座火山，海拔6140米。山顶火山口内留有巨型石砌平台，由印加人在南部安第斯并入科利亚苏尤行省后修筑。1471—1493年在位的图帕克·印卡·尤潘基征服了科利亚人，阿根廷西北部则在其继承人瓦伊纳·卡帕克治下被彻底吞并。

在安第斯传统中，高山被尊为“阿普”，即护佑社群、接受献祭的山神。印加政权在山顶营建神龛，以巩固统治。奎瓦尔的火山口圣所属于这一圣山崇拜，该崇拜还会在最受尊崇的山峰上举行高空童祭。

en:
Quri Kancha, meaning golden temple in Cusco Quechua, was the foremost sanctuary of the Inca Empire and the principal shrine of Inti, the sun god and divine ancestor of the Inca dynasty, at the heart of Cusco.

The emperor Pachakuti rebuilt it in the fifteenth century, facing its curved walls with gold and filling its courtyard with golden statues and life-size golden plants. The mummies of seven Incas sat on a golden bench attended by the cloistered Mama-cunas. Its precisely cut stone blocks were fitted without mortar.

When the Spanish held Atahualpa for ransom in 1533, much of the gold they demanded came from Quri Kancha. The conquerors demolished the temple and raised the Church and Convent of Santo Domingo on its foundations, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1650. The Inca stonework survived while the colonial building above it cracked.
zh:
库里坎查在库斯科克丘亚语中意为“黄金神庙”，是印加帝国最重要的圣所，也是太阳神、印加王朝神圣祖先因蒂的主庙，坐落在库斯科中心。

15世纪，皇帝帕查库特克重建此庙，弧形墙面贴满金板，庭院中摆满金像与真人大小的黄金植物。七具印加君主的木乃伊安坐在黄金长凳上，由隐居的“妈妈库纳”侍奉。神庙石块经精心琢凿，不用灰浆即严丝合缝。

1533年西班牙人囚禁阿塔瓦尔帕索取赎金时，所敛黄金有很大一部分来自库里坎查。征服者拆毁神庙，在其地基上建起圣多明我教堂与修道院，并在1650年地震后重建。殖民建筑屡屡开裂，印加石墙却安然无恙。

en:
The Radha Damodar Temple lies at the foot of the Girnar hills near Junagadh in southern Gujarat, beside the sacred Damodar Kund, where pilgrims bathe and scatter the ashes of the dead in the hope of moksha. Its black-stone image of Damodar, a four-armed form of Krishna, stands with Radha at his side, and Vaishnavas regard Damodar as the presiding lord of the whole Girnar pilgrimage.

Tradition credits the first installation of the idols to Vajranabha, Krishna's grandson, and a Suryavanshi ruler named Chandraketpur is said to have built the early shrine; it was renovated in 462 under the Gupta emperor Skandagupta.

The present pink-sandstone complex, with its inner sanctum and two spires, also houses sub-shrines. In the fifteenth century the Gujarati poet-saint Narsinh Mehta came to bathe in the tank and composed his morning hymns on its banks.
zh:
拉妲奎师那神庙位于古吉拉特南部朱纳格特附近的吉尔纳尔山脚下，紧邻圣湖达莫达尔池，朝圣者在此沐浴、撒下逝者骨灰，以求灵魂解脱。庙中黑石神像为四臂达莫达尔，即奎师那的名号之一，身旁伴立拉妲；毗湿奴信徒奉达莫达尔为整个吉尔纳尔朝圣地的主神。

相传神像最早由奎师那之孙瓦吉拉纳巴安立，日族国王旃陀罗吉德布尔修建了早期祠庙，462年笈多皇帝塞建陀笈多又加以重修。

现存建筑群以粉红砂岩筑成，内有圣所和两座尖塔，还有附属祠庙。15世纪时，古吉拉特语诗人圣女纳尔辛赫·梅赫塔常来池畔沐浴，并在湖边写下他的晨祷诗篇。

en:
The Rajagopalaswamy Temple stands at Mannargudi in the Tamil country south of Nagapattinam, and is dedicated to Rajagopalaswamy, Krishna as the royal cowherd; Hindus also call it Dakshina Dwaraka, the Southern Dwarka, and rank it first among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams.

A stone inscription credits the original shrine to Kulothunga Chola I, who reigned from 1070 to 1122. Later Chola kings, including Rajaraja III and Rajendra III, enlarged it, and Hoysala inscriptions and Vijayanagara grants record continued patronage.

The Thanjavur Nayaks made it their dynastic shrine: Vijayaraghava Nayak, who ruled from 1634 to 1673, built the present temple, its thousand-pillared hall, the 47-metre main gopuram and the granite enclosure wall. The vast Haridra Nadhi tank beside it is among the largest temple tanks in India, and Maratha records show the shrine remained richly endowed in later centuries.
zh:
牧童主奎师那神庙位于纳加帕蒂南以南泰米尔地区的曼纳古迪，供奉牧童国王形象的奎师那，尊号罗阇戈帕拉斯瓦米；印度教徒又称它为南德瓦卡，并把它列为108座自重圣地之首。

据石刻记载，最早的祠庙由1070至1122年在位的库洛通加·朱罗一世修建。其后罗阇罗阇三世、罗贞陀罗三世等朱罗国王相继扩建，曷萨拉铭文和毗奢耶那伽罗的赐地文书都记载了持续的供奉。

坦贾武尔纳亚克王朝把它立为王室家庙：1634至1673年在位的维贾亚拉加瓦·纳亚克建成现存神庙、千柱厅、47米高的正门门楼和花岗石围墙。庙旁的哈里德拉池是印度最大的庙池之一，马拉塔人的档案也显示这座神庙在其后的世纪里仍拥有丰厚庙产。

en:
Ram Janmabhoomi, traditionally held to be the birthplace of Rama, lies within the old fortress of Ramkot at Ayodhya, on the Sarayu river in Awadh. The Ramayana presents Ayodhya as the capital of Kosala and the city where Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, was born.

The settlement was known as Saketa in the early centuries and took the name Ayodhya under the Guptas. In 1337 the city belonged to the Delhi Sultanate, passing in 1394 to the Sharqi rulers of Jaunpur.

In 1528 and 1529 Mir Baqi, a commander of the emperor Babur, built the Babri Masjid on Ramkot; Hindu tradition holds that it replaced a temple marking Rama's birthplace, and devotees continued to worship Rama at a platform beside the mosque. The site remained one of the great Vaishnava pilgrimage goals of northern India under the Nawabs of Awadh.
zh:
罗摩降诞处位于阿瓦德阿约提亚的罗摩科特古堡之内，地处萨拉育河畔，相传是罗摩的诞生地。《罗摩衍那》称阿约提亚为拘萨罗的都城，也是毗湿奴第七化身罗摩降生之城。

这座城市早期名为娑枳多，笈多王朝时期改称阿约提亚。1337年该城属德里苏丹国，1394年转归江布尔的沙尔吉王朝。

1528—1529年，皇帝巴布尔的将领米尔·巴基在罗摩科特修建巴布里清真寺；印度教传统认为它取代了一座标记罗摩诞生地的神庙，信众仍在寺旁的平台上敬拜罗摩。在阿瓦德的纳瓦卜们治下，此地始终是北印度毗湿奴派最重要的朝圣目的地之一。

en:
The Ramanathaswamy Temple occupies the island of Rameswaram at the tip of Tamil Nadu, where the Ramayana says Rama set up and worshipped a Shiva lingam before building his bridge to Lanka, asking the god to remain there as the lord of Rama, Rameshvara.

The shrine is therefore one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, a Char Dham pilgrimage destination. The Pandya kings enlarged it in the 1100s and the Sri Lankan ruler Parakrama Bahu aided its sanctum, but in 1311 Malik Kafur's Delhi army sacked the island and destroyed its temples.

The Jaffna kings Jeyaveera and Gunaveera Cinkaiariyan rebuilt the sanctum between 1380 and the early 1400s, ferrying stone from Trincomalee, and the present structure took shape in the 1600s under the Ramnad Sethupathi rajas, whose builders gave it the longest pillared corridor of any Hindu temple in India.
zh:
拉马纳塔斯瓦米神庙位于泰米尔纳德南端的拉梅斯沃勒姆岛。《罗摩衍那》记载，罗摩在此架设通往楞伽的大桥之前，亲手安设并敬拜了一座湿婆林伽，请湿婆永驻此岛，是为“罗摩之主”拉梅什瓦拉。

该庙因此位列湿婆十二处林伽圣地、印度教四大朝圣圣地之一。12世纪潘地亚诸王扩建神庙，斯里兰卡国王波罗迦罗摩巴忽也曾助建圣所；但1311年马利克·卡富尔率领的德里军队洗劫该岛、毁坏神庙。

1380年至15世纪初，贾夫纳国王贾亚维拉·辛凯阿里扬与继任者古纳维拉重修圣所，甚至从亭可马里渡海运来石材；现存神庙主要成型于17世纪拉姆纳德的塞图帕蒂王公治下，其修建者为它打造了印度所有印度教神庙中最长的柱廊。

en:
The Ramapuram Sree Rama Temple is an ancient Vishnu shrine in Ramapuram village near Pala, in the Kerala hinterland, believed to be roughly a thousand years old and counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of the Vaishnavite tradition.

Its circular sanctum, roofed in copper with a golden finial, houses a four-armed image of Rama facing east, cast in panchaloha, an alloy of five sacred metals.

Tradition holds that Rama rested and meditated here during his exile from Ayodhya while searching for Sita, and that his three brothers settled nearby: Lakshmana at Koodapulam, Bharata at Amanakara and Satrughna at Methiri. Their four shrines form the Nalambalam complex, and a circuit of them in the Karkidaka month is known as Nalambala Darshanam. Three Nambudiri Brahmin houses have long managed the temple's lands and worship.
zh:
拉默布勒姆的罗摩神庙是喀拉拉内陆帕拉附近拉默布勒姆村的一座古老毗湿奴神庙，相传已有约千年历史，被列为毗湿奴派传统的108座自重圣地之一。

圆形圣所覆以铜顶、上立金宝瓶，其中供奉面朝东方的四臂罗摩像，神像以五种圣金属合成的五合金铸成。

相传罗摩被逐出阿约提亚、寻找悉多时在此歇息禅修，他的三个弟弟也在附近定居：罗什曼那在库达普拉姆，婆罗多在阿默纳卡拉，设睹卢祇那在梅蒂里。四座神庙合称四庙群，在卡尔基达卡月巡拜四庙的活动称为四庙朝觐。庙产与祭祀长期由三个南布迪里婆罗门家族管理。

en:
The Ramchaura Mandir stands at Rambhadra in Hajipur, on the north bank of the Ganga opposite Patna. Its central object of worship is a set of footprints: local tradition holds that Rama passed this way on the road to Janakpur in Mithila, where he would win Sita as his bride, and left his footprints here.

The name pairs Rama with chaura, the Bhojpuri word for orchid, and the shrine has been tended for centuries by the Bari Sangat, a monastic math. Pilgrims gather above all for Rama Navami, the birthday of Rama, when a fair is held.

In 1337 Hajipur was a ferry village of the Delhi Sultanate's Tirhut; it was fortified and renamed by Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah of Bengal in the mid-fourteenth century, and the armies of Akbar twice stormed it, in 1572 and 1574, while subduing the Karrani rulers of Bengal.
zh:
罗摩兰花神庙位于哈吉普尔的兰巴德拉，哈吉普尔坐落在恒河北岸、与巴特那隔河相望。庙中最重要的崇拜对象是一组足印：当地传说罗摩前往弥萨罗的贾纳克布尔、去赢得悉多为妻的途中经过此地，留下了足印。

庙名由“罗摩”与博杰普尔语中意为兰花的“乔拉”组成；数百年来，神庙由名为巴里桑伽特的修道道场管理。朝圣者最看重罗摩诞辰节，届时会举办庙会。

1337年时，哈吉普尔还是德里苏丹国蒂尔胡特境内的一处渡口村落；14世纪中叶，孟加拉的沙姆斯丁·伊利亚斯·沙阿在此筑城并以自己的名字为其命名，阿克巴的军队又在1572和1574年两度攻破此城，以征服孟加拉的卡拉尼王朝统治者。

en:
Srirangam, an island town between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers near Tiruchirappalli, holds the foremost of the 108 Vaishnava Divya Desams: the temple of Ranganatha, Vishnu reclining on the serpent Shesha.

From the eleventh century the teachers Nathamuni, Yamunacharya and especially Ramanuja made it the headquarters of the Sri Vaishnava tradition. Disaster came with the Delhi Sultanate: Malik Kafur's raid of 1311 carried off the golden image, and the invasion of Muhammad bin Tughluq in 1327 left the temple deserted; in 1337 the Ranganatha icon was being carried secretly from village to village.

Only after Kumara Kampana's Vijayanagara forces overthrew the Madurai Sultanate was the image reinstalled in 1371. Vijayanagara kings and their Nayaka governors then fortified and enlarged the complex over two centuries, adding gopurams, the thousand-pillared hall and granaries.
zh:
斯里兰加姆是蒂鲁吉拉伯利附近、高韦里河与科利达姆河之间的岛上城镇，拥有毗湿奴派108处圣域中地位最高的一座：兰加纳塔神庙，供奉倚躺在神蛇舍沙身上的毗湿奴。

11世纪起，导师纳塔穆尼、亚穆纳查里雅，尤其是罗摩奴阇，把这里建成室利毗湿奴派的大本营。灾难随德里苏丹国而来：1311年马利克·卡富尔的劫掠把金像掳走，1327年穆罕默德·宾·图格鲁克的入侵又使神庙荒废；1337年时，兰加纳塔神像正被人秘密辗转于各村之间。

直到库马拉·坎帕纳率领毗奢耶那伽罗军队推翻马杜赖苏丹国，神像才于1371年重新安奉。此后两百年间，毗奢耶那伽罗诸王与其纳亚卡总督修筑城墙、扩建庙宇，增建瞿布罗塔门、千柱厅和粮仓。

official_raw.en: The Ranganathaswamy Temple in Srirangam is one of the largest and holiest $hindu_ADJ$ temple complexes in India. Dedicated to the god $vishnu_god$ as Ranganatha, it dates at least from the early Chola period, with later extensions by the Pandya and Vijayanagara rulers. By 1337, it is a major pilgrimage center in Southern India, known for its vast precincts, imposing gopurams, and rich religious endowment.
official_raw.zh: 斯利兰加姆的兰加纳塔斯瓦米神庙是印度规模最宏大、地位最神圣的$hindu_ADJ$寺庙建筑群之一，供奉以兰加纳塔化身形态呈现的$vishnu_god$神。其起源至少可追溯至朱罗王朝早期，后期由潘地亚与毗奢耶那伽罗统治者进行扩建。截至1337年，该庙已成为南印度主要朝圣中心，以其广阔院落、宏伟的瞿布罗塔门和丰厚的宗教捐赠而闻名。

en:
Rila Monastery lies in a valley of the Rila Mountains south of Sofia, founded around the cave of the hermit Ivan of Rila, who died in 946. His disciples built the first houses near his retreat, and the tsars of the Second Bulgarian Empire endowed it until it became the spiritual centre of medieval Bulgaria.

The feudal lord Hrelja rebuilt it on its present site in the 1330s and 1340s, leaving a fortified tower of 1334–1335 and a church of 1343.

Ottoman raids at the end of the fourteenth century ended in its destruction in the mid-fifteenth, but it was rebuilt at the century's close by three brothers from Dupnitsa, and Ivan's relics were brought from Tarnovo in 1469. After a fire of 1833 the whole complex was rebuilt from 1834 in the style of the Bulgarian National Revival.
zh:
里拉修道院位于索非亚以南里拉山脉的山谷中，围绕隐修士里拉的伊万的洞穴而建；伊万于946年去世，弟子们在他的隐修处旁建起最早的房舍，第二保加利亚帝国历代沙皇不断捐资，使它成为中世纪保加利亚的精神中心。

14世纪30至40年代，封建领主赫雷利亚在现址重建修道院，留下1334—1335年的防御塔和1343年的小教堂。

14世纪末奥斯曼入侵后劫掠不断，修道院于15世纪中叶被毁；15世纪末，杜普尼察地区的三兄弟将其重建，伊万的圣骨也于1469年从特尔诺沃迁来。1833年大火后，全院自1834年起按保加利亚民族复兴风格重建。

en:
The Rome Patriarchal See is the most venerable of the Christian bishoprics, traditionally founded by Saint Peter, who was martyred in Rome under Nero and buried on the Vatican hill. As the see of the former imperial capital, it stood first among the five patriarchates of the early Church.

Constantine the Great raised a basilica over Peter's tomb between 318 and 322. For twelve centuries Old St. Peter's was the principal shrine of western Christendom: popes were crowned there, and Charlemagne was crowned emperor in it in 800. Saracens sacked the basilica in 846, after which Pope Leo IV enclosed the Vatican with the Leonine Wall.

The see broke communion with Constantinople in the schism of 1054. By the fifteenth century the old church was structurally unsafe; the Renaissance basilica was built from 1506 and consecrated in 1626.
zh:
罗马牧座是基督教最古老的主教座，相传由圣彼得创立；他在尼禄治下于罗马殉道，葬在梵蒂冈山。罗马是帝国旧都，其主教座在早期教会五大牧首区中位列首席。

君士坦丁大帝于318—322年间在圣彼得墓上建起一座大殿。此后一千二百年间，老圣彼得大殿一直是西方基督教的首要圣所：教皇在此加冕，800年查理曼也在此加冕为帝。846年撒拉森人洗劫大殿，教皇利奥四世随后修筑利奥城墙将梵蒂冈围住。

1054年教会大分裂，罗马与君士坦丁堡断绝共融。到15世纪，老教堂已岌岌可危；文艺复兴式大殿于1506年动工，1626年祝圣。

en:
Rome, on the Tiber in central Italy, was the capital of the Roman Empire and became one of the principal holy cities of Christianity. Tradition holds that the apostles Peter and Paul were martyred there under Nero after the Great Fire of 64.

Early heterodox teachers were drawn to the capital as well: the Gnostic Valentinus founded a school in Rome around the middle of the second century, and Marcion of Sinope, who distinguished the God of Jesus from the creator of the world, was excommunicated by the Roman church in about 144.

Pope Boniface VIII proclaimed the first Christian Jubilee in 1300, but from 1309 to 1377 the papacy resided at Avignon and Rome fell into neglect; after the Western Schism, Renaissance popes rebuilt the city and began the new Saint Peter's Basilica.
zh:
罗马位于意大利中部的台伯河畔，曾是罗马帝国的首都，后来成为基督教的主要圣城之一。相传64年罗马大火之后，宗徒圣伯多禄与圣保禄在尼禄治下殉道于此。

早期的异端教师也被帝国首都吸引：灵知派的瓦伦廷约在2世纪中叶于罗马创办学派，而区分耶稣之上主与创世造物主的锡诺普人马吉安，约在144年被罗马教会革出教门。

1300年教宗卜尼法斯八世宣布首个基督教禧年，但1309—1377年教宗迁居阿维尼翁，罗马日渐荒废；西方教会大分裂之后，文艺复兴时期的教宗们重建城市，并动工修建新的圣伯多禄大殿。

en:
Saint Catherine's Monastery stands at the foot of Mount Sinai in Egypt, on the site where Moses is said to have seen the burning bush. Empress Helena, mother of Constantine the Great, built a chapel over the bush in the fourth century, and between 548 and 565 Emperor Justinian I enclosed it within a great fortified monastery.

The supposed body of Catherine of Alexandria, martyred in the early fourth century, was later brought there, and her relics made it a major pilgrimage centre, after which the house was renamed in her honour. Its library became one of the richest in Christendom, holding the fourth-century Codex Sinaiticus.

A Fatimid mosque was built within its walls in 1106. Under Ottoman rule the once multiethnic community became almost entirely Greek, sustained from the 1480s by alms from the princes of Wallachia.
zh:
圣埃卡特里纳修道院坐落在埃及西奈山脚下，相传这里就是摩西见到燃烧荆棘的地方。4世纪时，君士坦丁大帝之母海伦娜皇后在荆棘之上修建小堂；548—565年间，查士丁尼一世下令将其围入一座防御坚固的大修道院。

后来，4世纪初殉道的亚历山大的凯瑟琳的遗骸据传被移送到此，她的圣骨使这里成为重要的朝圣中心，修道院也以她的名字命名。院内藏书是基督教世界最丰富的收藏之一，藏有4世纪的《西奈抄本》。

1106年院内建成一座法蒂玛王朝清真寺。奥斯曼时期，这个曾经多民族的共同体几乎完全希腊化，从1480年代起靠瓦拉几亚王公的施舍维持。

en:
Samarkand, the Sogdian city on the Silk Road, met Christianity early: some of its quarters were Christian by the fourth century, a Nestorian see was created in the fifth, and early in the eighth century it was raised to a metropolitanate of the Church of the East.

The Arab conquest of about 712 under Qutayba ibn Muslim brought persecution, and many believers fled or converted to Islam. A vision of Mar Sergius of Samarkand, a saint of the Church of the East, was credited with the conversion of the Kerait Turks around 1007.

Under Mongol rule after 1220 Christian bishoprics were again permitted, and between 1329 and 1359 a Catholic eparchy served believers after the Chagatai khan Eljigidey accepted baptism. Islam soon reasserted itself, and as Timur made Samarkand his capital in 1370 the old East Syriac congregations had dwindled to isolated remnants that died out in the following centuries.
zh:
丝绸之路上的粟特城市撒马尔罕很早就接触了基督教：4世纪时城中部分城区已有基督徒，5世纪设立聂斯脱里派主教座，8世纪初更升为东方教会的都主教教省。

约712年屈底波·伊本·穆斯林率阿拉伯军队征服此地，带来迫害，许多信徒逃亡或改宗伊斯兰教。约1007年克烈部突厥人归信被归于撒马尔罕的东方教会圣徒马·薛里吉思的显现。

1220年蒙古统治之后，教会再度获准建立主教区；1329—1359年间，随着察合台汗燕只吉台受洗，城中有一个天主教教区。但伊斯兰教很快重新占据上风，1370年帖木儿定都撒马尔罕时，古老的东叙利亚会众已萎缩为零星残余，并在随后几个世纪里绝迹。

en:
The Sanctuary of the Great Gods on Samothrace, off the Thracian coast, was the principal seat of the mystery cult of the Cabeiri, chthonic deities whose secret names initiates were forbidden to divulge and who were invoked as protectors of sailors.

Its rites drew worshippers from across the Greek world: the historian Herodotus and the Spartan commander Lysander were initiates. Plutarch records that Philip II of Macedon met Olympias while both were being initiated.

After Alexander the Great the Ptolemies and Antigonids vied to embellish the sanctuary, building the rotunda of Arsinoe II and, around 325 BC, the Hieron. The Winged Victory of Samothrace was dedicated there in the second century BC. The sanctuary was closed during the late-Roman persecution of pagan cults.
zh:
色雷斯沿海萨摩色雷斯岛上的众神圣殿，是卡比里秘仪的主要中心。卡比里是一组冥土神祇，受秘仪者不得泄露他们的秘名，水手们奉其为保护神。

仪式吸引了整个希腊世界的信众，历史学家希罗多德和斯巴达统帅莱山德都曾入教。普鲁塔克记载，马其顿的腓力二世正是在受秘仪时结识了奥林匹亚丝。

亚历山大大帝之后，托勒密王朝和安提柯王朝竞相装点圣殿，兴建了阿尔西诺伊二世圆厅，以及约公元前325年建成的众神殿。公元前2世纪，萨摩色雷斯的胜利女神像被敬献于此。罗马帝国晚期迫害异教崇拜时，这座圣殿终被关闭。

en:
Santiago de Compostela, in Galicia in northwestern Spain, is the shrine where the apostle Saint James the Great is said to be buried. Tradition holds that in 814 the hermit Pelagius saw strange lights above the Libredon forest; Bishop Theodomirus identified the spot as the apostle's tomb, King Alfonso II of Asturias built a chapel and came as its first pilgrim, and churches followed in 829 and 899.

In 997 the Cordoban commander Al-Mansur burned the church, though he left the tomb itself untouched and carried its gates and bells to Córdoba, from where Ferdinand III returned them after taking the city in 1236.

The present Romanesque cathedral was begun in 1075, and was consecrated in 1211; Master Mateo completed its sculpted Pórtico da Gloria in 1188. In 1492 Pope Alexander VI ranked Compostela among the three great pilgrimages of Christendom with Rome and Jerusalem.
zh:
圣地亚哥‑德孔波斯特拉位于西班牙西北部的加利西亚，相传是宗徒大圣雅各伯安葬的圣所。传说814年隐士佩拉吉乌斯看见利布雷东森林上空有异光，主教特奥多米罗认定此处为宗徒之墓，阿斯图里亚斯国王阿方索二世在此修建小堂并成为第一位朝圣者，829年和899年又先后建起教堂。

997年，科尔多瓦统帅阿尔曼苏尔焚毁教堂，但没有触动墓穴本身，还把堂门和铜钟掠往科尔多瓦；1236年费尔南多三世攻占该城后才将它们运回。

现存的罗曼式大教堂1075年开工，1211年祝圣；马特奥大师于1188年完成雕刻精美的荣耀门廊。1492年教宗亚历山大六世把圣地亚哥与罗马、耶路撒冷并列为基督教世界三大朝圣地。

en:
The monastery of Santo Toribio de Liébana lies near Potes in northern Spain. A community was established there in the sixth century, when a cleric named Turibius retired with companions to follow the Benedictine rule; first dedicated to Saint Martin of Tours, the house took its name in the eleventh century.

Its Lignum Crucis is said to be the largest surviving fragment of the True Cross, brought from Jerusalem by Saint Turibius of Astorga in the fifth century and carried to the valley for safety in the eighth. In that century the monk Beatus of Liébana wrote and illustrated his Commentary on the Apocalypse at the monastery.

The church was built in 1256, and in 1512 Pope Julius II granted the house a jubilee year, its Door of Forgiveness opening to pilgrims alongside Rome, Jerusalem and Santiago. In 1837 the Mendizábal confiscations drove the monks out.
zh:
圣托里比奥修道院坐落在西班牙北部波特斯附近。6世纪时，教士托里比奥带着同伴退隐于此，遵行本笃会规，修道团体就此建立；修道院最初奉图尔的圣马丁为主保，11世纪改用圣托里比奥之名。

院内供奉的真十字架木段相传是现存最大的真十字架残片，5世纪由阿斯托尔加的圣托里比奥从耶路撒冷带回，8世纪为避乱转运到山谷。同在8世纪，修士列瓦纳的比亚图斯在此撰写并手绘《启示录注》。

教堂建于1256年；1512年，教皇尤利乌斯二世授予该院禧年特权，宽恕之门向朝圣者开启，使它与罗马、耶路撒冷和圣地亚哥并列。1837年，门迪萨瓦尔的没收法令把修士们逐出了修道院。

en:
The Serapeum of Alexandria was the chief temple of Serapis, a Graeco-Egyptian god formed from Osiris-Apis. Ptolemy I Soter promoted the cult to bind his subjects; the sanctuary was built mainly under Ptolemy III Euergetes between 246 and 222 BC.

The temple housed a daughter collection of the Library of Alexandria, and subterranean galleries served the mysteries of Serapis. Damaged in the Kitos War of AD 116, it was restored under Hadrian and rebuilt by the Romans around 181 to 217; the column misnamed Pompey's Pillar was erected for Diocletian between 298 and 302.

The Serapeum became the last great stronghold of pagan Alexandria. In 391, after Theodosius I banned temple visits, Christians led by Bishop Theophilus stormed it; the sanctuary was sacked and closed in 392, and a church and the Monastery of Metanoia later rose among its ruins.
zh:
亚历山大塞拉比斯神庙是塞拉比斯神的主庙。塞拉比斯是由奥西里斯—阿皮斯融合而成的希腊化埃及神，托勒密一世·索塔尔为凝聚臣民而推行其崇拜；神庙主要建于托勒密三世·尤厄格忒斯在位期间，即公元前246—前222年。

庙中藏有亚历山大图书馆的分馆藏书，地下长廊用于举行塞拉比斯秘仪。神庙在公元116年的基托斯战争中受损，哈德良时期修复，罗马人又在181—217年前后重建；被误称为“庞贝柱”的巨柱是298—302年间为戴克里先所立。

这座神庙成了异教亚历山大最后的大本营。391年狄奥多西一世禁止参拜神庙后，主教提阿非罗率领基督徒攻入庙中，圣所遭洗劫并于392年关闭，后来废墟上建起了教堂和梅塔诺亚修道院。

en:
