The Shankari Devi Temple at Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's eastern coast is the goddess shrine of the Koneswaram complex, crowning Swami Rock above the Indian Ocean. Worshipped as Ambal or Shankari Devi, the consort of the Shiva of Koneswaram, she is counted among the eighteen Maha Shakta Pithas, and the hymn attributed to Adi Shankara names this seat Sri Sankari Pitham.

Koneswaram, one of the island's five ancient Ishwarams, is mentioned in the Vayu Purana around the fourth century and was enlarged under Tamil dynasties; the Chola prince Kulakottan rebuilt the shrine and its endowments.

Between 1622 and 1624 the Portuguese destroyed the temples and raised a fort from their stones, but the goddess's idols were rescued and installed in a new temple in the town in 1632.
zh:
商羯丽女神庙位于斯里兰卡东海岸的亭可马里，是雄踞斯瓦米岩、俯瞰印度洋的科内斯瓦兰神庙群中的女神殿。女神被尊为安巴尔或商羯丽·提毗，即科内斯瓦兰湿婆的神妃，位列十八处大性力佩特之一，托名商羯罗的圣地颂称此地为斯里·商羯里佩特。

科内斯瓦兰是岛上五大古湿婆神庙之一，4世纪前后的《风神往世书》已有记载，后经泰米尔诸王朝扩建，朱罗王子库拉科坦曾重修神庙及其供养田产。

1622—1624年间，葡萄牙人捣毁诸庙，用庙石修建堡垒，但女神神像被抢救出来，于1632年安置在城中新建的庙宇。

en:
The Shankhapur Temple is the Svetambara Jain tirtha of Shankheshwar in northern Gujarat, near Radhanpur, known in early Jain literature as Shankhpur. It is dedicated to Parshvanatha, whose white seated image is counted among the hundred and eight foremost Parshvanatha idols of the Svetambara tradition.

A temple stood on the Rupen river by 1098, when Sajjan Shah rebuilt it, and the minister brothers Vastupala and Tejpal renovated it in 1229. Destroyed in the fourteenth century during the raids of Alauddin Khalji, it was rebuilt in the sixteenth century and consecrated anew in 1703; the present temple rose in 1811.

Under the Mughals Shah Jahan granted the village to the Ahmedabad banker Shantidas Jhaveri. For Svetambara pilgrims its rank stands second only to Mount Shatrunjaya at Palitana.
zh:
商羯罗补罗寺是古吉拉特北部商凯什瓦尔的白衣派耆那教圣地，邻近拉丹布尔，在早期耆那教文献中名为商羯罗补罗。寺院供奉巴湿伐那陀，白色坐像被列为白衣派最重要的一百零八尊巴湿伐那陀像之一。

鲁彭河畔早有寺院，1098年由萨詹·沙阿重建；1229年，大臣兄弟瓦斯图帕拉与泰杰帕拉加以修葺。14世纪阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉入侵时寺院被毁，16世纪重建，1703年重新安像，现存寺院建于1811年。

莫卧儿时期，沙贾汗曾将此村封赐给艾哈迈达巴德的银行家尚蒂达斯·贾维里。在白衣派信众心中，其地位仅次于帕利塔纳的沙特伦贾亚山。

en: The Shankhodara Temple stands on Bet Dwarka, also called Shankhodhar, the conch-shell island two kilometres off Okha in Gujarat and counted among the lands of Krishna's legendary Dvaraka. It is one of India's few prominent shrines dedicated to Matsya, Vishnu's fish avatar, who guided Manu through the great flood and recovered the Vedas from the demon Hayagriva.
zh: 商拘陀罗神庙位于贝特德瓦尔卡岛（又称商拘达尔岛，意为海螺之岛），距古吉拉特奥卡港两公里，被视为黑天神传说中的德瓦尔卡疆域的一部分。它是全印为数不多的著名摩蹉神庙之一，供奉毗湿奴的鱼化身摩蹉——正是它引导摩奴渡过大洪水，并从恶魔诃耶羯哩婆手中夺回吠陀。

en:
Sharada Peeth, the seat of Sharada, as Saraswati is called in Kashmir, is a ruined temple and temple-university in the Neelum Valley. From the sixth to the twelfth century its library drew scholars; the Sharada script takes its name from the place, and Kashmir was known as Sharada Desh.

As one of the great Shakti Peethas it marks where Sati's right hand is said to have fallen. The stone temple is plausibly a work of the Karkota emperor Lalitaditya Muktapida, who reigned from 724 to 760; by the eighth century pilgrims came from as far as Bengal.

In 1422 the Kashmiri sultan Zain-ul-Abidin visited to seek a vision of the goddess, and in the sixteenth century Abu'l-Fazl described the temple as greatly venerated. Under later Mughal and Afghan rule the valley passed to local Muslim chiefs and the pilgrimage dwindled.
zh:
辩才天女庙的“沙尔达”是克什米尔对萨拉斯瓦蒂的称呼，这座已成废墟的神庙兼古代庙学位于尼勒姆河谷。6—12世纪间，藏书楼吸引学者前来；沙尔达字母得名于此，克什米尔也被称作“沙尔达之国”。

这里是大性力圣地之一，相传萨蒂的右手坠落于此。石庙很可能出自卡尔科塔王朝皇帝拉利塔迭多·穆克塔毗达之手，他在位时间为724—760年；到8世纪时，远自孟加拉的香客已来到此地。

1422年，克什米尔苏丹扎因·乌勒·阿比丁亲来求见女神；16世纪，阿布勒·法兹勒称此庙备受尊崇。后来在莫卧儿和阿富汗统治下，河谷落入地方穆斯林首领之手，巡礼逐渐衰微。

en:
Śikharjī, also called Sammed Śikhar, rises on Parasnath hill in Jharkhand and is the most exalted Jain pilgrimage place, honoured by the Digambara and Svetambara sects. Its name means the venerable peak of concentration: tradition holds that twenty Tirthankaras attained moksha here, including Parshvanatha, whose liberation is placed in 772 BCE and gives the hill its name.

The site is named as a tirth in the Jnatrdharmakatha. In the thirteenth century Vastupala, minister of the Vaghela kings, built a temple housing twenty Tirthankara images. Akbar entrusted the hill to the Jain community in 1583 and forbade killing animals nearby.

The Jagat Seth bankers became patrons from 1725; Mahtabchand rebuilt the temples in 1768, and in 1825 Kushalchand consecrated the twenty liberation sites. Both sects worship the summit's idols.
zh:
尸佉罗时又称三密陀尸佉罗，耸立于贾坎德邦的波尔史伐陀山，是耆那教天衣派与白衣派共同尊奉的最高朝圣圣地。其名意为“可敬的禅定之峰”，相传有二十位祖师在此证得解脱，其中巴湿伐那陀于公元前772年涅槃，此山也因此得名。

《若提陀法经》已将此地列为圣地。13世纪，瓦盖拉王朝的大臣瓦斯图波罗建庙，供奉二十尊祖师像。阿克巴于1583年将山体交由耆那教团体管理，并禁止在附近杀生。

1725年起，银行世家贾格特·塞特家族成为护法：马赫塔卜昌德于1768年重建殿宇，1825年库沙尔昌德为二十处解脱圣地举行开光。山顶神像由两派共同奉祀。

en:
Shikoku Henro is the Buddhist pilgrimage of Japan's island of Shikoku, a circuit of eighty-eight temples linked to the monk Kūkai, posthumously called Kōbō Daishi, who was born at Zentsū-ji in 774 and founded the esoteric Shingon school after returning from study in Tang China. Popular tradition holds that he visited or founded many of the temples himself.

The route winds through Shikoku, and its stages mirror the path to enlightenment. Pilgrims, known as henro, walk in white robes with sedge hats and staffs, chanting the Heart Sutra at each temple, while local people give them alms along the way.

Monks from Mount Kōya spread the Kōbō Daishi cult and its legends, and under the Edo shogunate pilgrims travelled with permits and temple-stamp books. By the eighteenth century smaller copies of the circuit had appeared across Japan.
zh:
四国遍路是日本四国岛上的佛教巡礼路线，由八十八所与空海有关的寺院组成。空海谥号弘法大师，774年生于岛上的善通寺，曾入唐求法，回国后开创密教真言宗；相传他曾亲身巡拜或开创了其中许多寺院。

路线环绕四国，各段象征觉悟之路。巡礼者称遍路，身穿白衣、头戴菅笠、手持金刚杖，每到一寺诵《般若心经》，沿途居民常向他们施舍。

高野山的僧人四处弘扬弘法大师信仰及其传说；江户幕府时代，遍路须持通行许可、携带纳经帐沿路盖印。到18世纪，日本各地已出现规模较小的仿制巡路。

en:
Shravanabelagola is a Jain pilgrimage town in Karnataka in southern India, set between the Chandragiri and Vindhyagiri hills. Tradition holds that the sage Bhadrabahu and his pupil Chandragupta Maurya, founder of the Mauryan empire, meditated on Chandragiri, where the former emperor is said to have died around 298 BCE after taking Jain ascetic vows.

On Vindhyagiri stands the fifty-eight-foot monolithic statue of Gommateshwara, also called Bahubali, commissioned in 981 by Chavundaraya, general of the Western Ganga kings of Talakad.

Under Western Ganga and later Hoysala patronage the town accumulated more than five hundred Jain inscriptions, as well as temples including the Akkana Basadi and the Chandragupta Basadi. Every twelve years devotees gather for the Mahamastakabhisheka, anointing the statue with water, turmeric, sandalwood paste and gold and silver flowers.
zh:
室罗伐拿白泽是印度南部卡纳塔克的耆那教朝圣城镇，坐落在旃陀罗山与温迪亚山之间。相传祖师婆达罗巴忽与弟子、孔雀帝国开创者旃陀罗笈多·孔雀曾在旃陀罗山修行，这位退位帝王约于公元前298年立下耆那教出家誓愿后在此离世。

温迪亚山上矗立着高约18米的整块岩石雕像戈玛特什瓦拉，又称巴霍巴利，由西恒伽王朝塔拉卡德的将领查蒙达罗阇于981年出资开凿。

在西恒伽及后来曷萨拉诸王的护持下，此地积累了五百多方耆那教碑铭，以及阿迦那寺、旃陀罗笈多寺等庙宇。每隔十二年，信众齐聚举行大灌顶盛典，以清水、姜黄、檀香膏和金银花朵为大像涂油供奉。

en:
The Shri Idagunji Maha Ganapati Temple is a Hindu shrine dedicated to Ganesha at Idagunji in Karnataka on India's west coast, near the Sharavathi river. It is one of six celebrated temples on the Ganesha Coast.

A local legend tells how the sage Valakhilya, his penance beset by obstacles, was advised by Narada to invoke Vighneshwara, the remover of hindrances. Ganesha left Kailasha to dwell in the Sharavathi valley, the divine architect Vishwakarma carved his icon, and devotees raised a temple around it in the 400s or 500s CE.

The stone image is unusual: Ganesha has two tusks and only two arms, with a granite bell at his waist and no serpent around his belly. The icon is popularly reckoned to be more than two thousand years old, and pilgrims meditate before its serene face.
zh:
室利伊陀郡时‑摩诃伽那波底神庙供奉伽内什，位于印度西海岸卡纳塔克的伊陀郡时，靠近舍拉沃蒂河。它是“伽内什海岸”六大名庙之一。

相传仙人瓦拉吉利耶苦行时屡遭障碍，那罗陀建议他祈请除障之神毗那夜迦。伽内什离开凯拉萨山驻留舍拉沃蒂河谷，神匠毗首羯磨为其雕造神像，信徒们约在4—5世纪绕像建庙。

石像造型罕见：伽内什长着两根象牙，只有双臂，腰悬花岗岩石铃，腹上没有盘蛇。民间认为此像已有两千多年历史，香客们在它宁静的面容前冥想祈愿。

en:
Shri Mayureshwar Mandir is a Hindu temple dedicated to Ganesha in Morgaon, near Pune in Maharashtra. Its name means Lord of the Peacock: the Ganesha Purana tells how Ganesha incarnated as the six-armed, white-skinned Mayuresvara, rode a peacock and slew the demon Sindhu.

Morgaon is the foremost seat of the Ganapatya sect and the starting and ending point of the Ashtavinayaka pilgrimage of eight Ganesha temples around Pune.

The temple's origins are tied to the saint Morya Gosavi, whose lifetime is variously placed between the 1200s and the 1600s; the poet-saint Samarth Ramdas (1608–1682) composed his arati Sukhakarta Dukhaharta before its icon. In the 1700s the Peshwa rulers of the Maratha Empire, who honoured Ganesha as their family deity, donated land and money to the shrine.
zh:
孔雀之主神庙供奉伽内什，位于马哈拉施特拉邦浦那附近的莫尔冈。庙名意为“孔雀之主”：《伽内什往世书》记载，伽内什曾化身为六臂白肤的摩由雷湿婆罗，骑孔雀诛杀恶魔信度。

莫尔冈是伽那帕提亚教派最首要的圣地，也是浦那周边阿什塔维纳亚克八座伽内什神庙巡礼的起点与终点。

神庙的兴起与圣徒摩利亚·戈萨维有关，此人的生活年代有13—17世纪之间的多种说法；诗人圣徒萨马尔特·拉姆达斯（1608—1682）在庙中神像前写下敬神歌《苏尔迦尔多·杜克尔赫尔多》。18世纪，以伽内什为家族保护神的马拉塔帝国佩什瓦们向神庙捐赠土地与钱财。

en:
Shwedagon Pagoda is the gilded stupa on Singuttara Hill at Dagon, later known as Yangon, in Lower Burma, and the country's most sacred Buddhist site. Tradition holds that two merchant brothers received eight hairs from the Buddha and that the local king enshrined them with relics of the three earlier Buddhas; archaeology instead points to a Mon foundation between the sixth and tenth centuries.

The pagoda enters the royal chronicles in 1362, when King Binnya U of Hanthawaddy rebuilt it to a height of eighteen meters. Queen Shin Saw Pu raised it to forty meters in the fifteenth century and covered it in gold.

By the early sixteenth century it was Burma's most celebrated pilgrimage destination. Earthquakes repeatedly damaged it, and the quake of 1768 threw down its spire; King Hsinbyushin rebuilt the top in 1775.
zh:
大光金塔是矗立在下缅甸大光（后来的仰光）丁固达拉山上的鎏金窣堵坡，也是缅甸最神圣的佛教圣地。相传两位商人兄弟从佛陀处求得八根头发，当地国王将其与过去三佛的圣物一同供奉在山上；考古学家则认为它建于6至10世纪，出自孟族之手。

1362年，罕达瓦底的频耶陀努王重修此塔，将其加高到18米，这是它首次见于王室编年史。15世纪，女王信绍布又把塔加高到40米并全身贴金。

到16世纪初，它已成为缅甸最负盛名的朝圣地。此后地震屡有破坏，1768年的地震震塌塔尖，1775年辛标信王重建塔顶。

en:
This shrine preserves the tomb of Abu Said ibn Khalaf al-Tamimi al-Baji, known as Sidi Bou Said, an Arab Sufi saint of Tunisia born in 1156.

Trained in the school of the Andalusian mystic Abu Madyan, he left Beja to study in Syria and made the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1207, returning to Tunisia in 1210.

He gave up worldly life for prayer and meditation in Tunis, drawing disciples including Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili, founder of the Shadhili order. Sidi Bou Said used to withdraw to a lighthouse on the hill above Carthage, and when he died in 1231 he was buried there; his sanctuary gave the surrounding settlement its name and became a venerated Sufi pilgrimage place in the Tunis region.
zh:
这座圣陵安放着突尼斯阿拉伯苏菲圣徒阿布·赛义德·伊本·赫莱夫·塔米米·巴吉的陵墓，他通称西迪·布·赛义德，生于1156年。

他出自安达卢西亚神秘主义者阿布·马德扬门下，后离开贝贾赴叙利亚求学，1207年前往麦加朝觐，1210年返回突尼斯。

此后他弃绝世俗，在突尼斯城祈祷与冥想，吸引了沙兹里教团创始人阿布·哈桑·沙兹里等弟子。西迪·布·赛义德常到迦太基附近山上的灯塔隐修，1231年去世后葬于此；他的圣所使周边聚落得名西迪布赛义德，并成为突尼斯地区受尊崇的苏菲朝圣地。

en:
The Abu Madyan shrine is a complex of mosque, madrasa, mausoleum and hammam at al-Ubbad outside Tlemcen in western Algeria, built around the tomb of the Andalusian Sufi master Abu Madyan Shu'ayb. Born near Seville around 1126, he studied mysticism in Fez and Mecca, then settled at Bougie, where disciples such as Ibn Arabi gathered around him.

His fame alarmed the Almohad authorities, and when Caliph Ya'qub al-Mansur summoned him to Marrakesh he died on the journey in 1198 and was buried at al-Ubbad.

Tlemcen adopted him as its patron saint, and Caliph Muhammad al-Nasir raised a mausoleum over his grave. In the fourteenth century the Marinid rulers of Tlemcen founded the mosque in 1339 and its madrasa eight years later, where Ibn Khaldun once taught.
zh:
阿布·迈迪安圣陵是阿尔及利亚西部特莱姆森郊外欧巴德的建筑群，由清真寺、经学院、圣陵和浴室组成，围绕安达卢西亚苏菲大师阿布·迈迪安·舒艾卜的坟墓而建。他约1126年生于塞维利亚附近，在非斯和麦加研习神秘主义，后定居贝贾亚，伊本·阿拉比等弟子云集其门下。

他的声望引起穆瓦希德当局忌惮，哈里发雅各布·曼苏尔召他前往马拉喀什，他却在1198年途中去世，葬于欧巴德。

特莱姆森民众奉他为守护圣徒，哈里发穆罕默德·纳西尔在他墓上建起圣陵。14世纪马林王朝于1339年建起清真寺，八年后又建经学院，伊本·赫勒敦曾在此讲学。

en:
Sonagiri, the golden mountain, known in older texts as Swarnagiri, is a Digambara Jain pilgrimage place in the Datia district of central India. White temples have covered its hill from the 800s onward; seventy-seven shrines stand on the hill and more than a hundred belong to the whole tirth.

Jain tradition holds that the eighth Tirthankara Chandraprabha seventeen times held his Samavasarana, the divine preaching assembly, here. The acharya Shubh Chandra and the sage Bhartrihari are said to have practised austerities, attained nirvana and composed religious works here.

The principal shrine is temple number fifty-seven, which houses an eleven-foot image of Chandraprabha called Bade Baba, with a column of honour and a model of the Samavasarana. Pilgrims gather each spring for the chariot festival after Holi and the replacement of the golden flag on the main spire.
zh:
苏那耆梨意为“金山”，古称苏伐那耆梨，是印度中部德蒂亚地区的一处天衣派耆那教圣地。自9世纪起，白色庙宇陆续布满山头：山上有七十七座神龛，整个圣所的庙宇超过一百座。

耆那教传统认为，第八代祖师旃陀罗波罗跋曾十七次在此召开神圣讲法集会萨摩婆萨罗那。阿阇梨输旃陀罗与仙人婆利睹梨诃利相传也在此苦修、证得涅槃并撰写宗教典籍。

主殿是第五十七号神庙，内供十一英尺高的旃陀罗波罗跋像，昵称“大巴巴”，殿前立有荣誉柱，另有萨摩婆萨罗那的模型。每年春天洒红节之后，香客云集参加乘车节，并举行更换主塔金旗的仪式。

en:
The Sreevaraham Lakshmi Varaha Temple stands in Thiruvananthapuram, near the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, patron shrine of the kings of Travancore. Its principal image is Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu, seated with Lakshmi on his lap; the temple is one of only three Varaha temples in Kerala. Local tradition claims the site is ancient, though no early building records survive.

With the rise of Travancore the city's Vishnu shrines received royal patronage: Marthanda Varma dedicated his kingdom to Padmanabha in 1750, and in 1795 Dharma Raja moved the capital to Thiruvananthapuram.

The Kerala-style temple has a round copper-roofed sanctum and a square outer nalambalam. Priests attending the Murajapam at Padmanabhaswamy took ritual baths in its tank, while boat races are held there during Onam. Its annual festival falls in Meenam, alongside the neighbouring temple's Painguni festival; Varaha Jayanti is celebrated in the same month.
zh:
斯里瓦拉哈姆吉祥天女·筏罗诃神庙位于特里凡得琅，邻近特拉凡哥尔王室的护法神庙帕德马纳巴史瓦米庙。主神是毗湿奴的野猪化身筏罗诃，吉祥天女坐于其膝上；这座神庙是喀拉拉仅有的三座筏罗诃庙之一。当地传说该庙极为古老，但早期营建记录已无存。

随着特拉凡哥尔崛起，城内毗湿奴神庙受到王室护持：1750年马尔坦达·瓦尔马把王国献给帕德马纳巴，1795年达尔马罗阇将都城迁至特里凡得琅。

庙宇为喀拉拉风格，圆形圣所覆以铜板顶，方形外圈纳兰巴兰环绕。参加帕德马纳巴史瓦米庙穆拉贾帕姆诵经法会的祭司在圣池沐浴，欧南节时池中举行赛船。神庙大节在米纳姆月，与邻庙潘古尼节同期，同月还庆祝筏罗诃诞辰。

en:
The Sri Sharadamba Temple stands in Sringeri in Karnataka, on the banks of the Tunga river, and is dedicated to Sharadamba, the local form of Saraswati, goddess of learning.

Tradition holds that Adi Shankara founded the shrine in the eighth century and built beside it his first monastery, the Sringeri Sharada Peetham, the southern of the four cardinal mathas he established across India, with his disciple Sureshvaracharya as its first pontiff.

The matha preserved Sanskrit manuscripts and Advaita Vedanta scholarship through an unbroken line of Jagadgurus. In 1791, during the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Pindari raiders sacked and destroyed the temple; Tipu Sultan, ruler of Mysore, wrote letters of condolence to the Shankaracharya and sent money, gifts and armed protection so that the shrine could be rebuilt.
zh:
斯灵盖里辩才天女庙位于卡纳塔克的斯灵盖里镇、栋格河畔，供奉辩才天女萨拉斯瓦蒂的当地化身夏拉丹巴。

相传8世纪时阿迪·商羯罗创建此庙，并在庙旁建立了他的第一座寺院——斯灵盖里夏拉道场，即他在印度所立四大道场中主管南方的一座，其弟子苏雷什瓦拉查亚为首任方丈。

历代祖师传承不断，道场长期保存梵文写本、研习不二吠檀多。1791年第三次英迈战争期间，平达里流寇洗劫并摧毁了神庙；迈索尔统治者提普苏丹致函商羯罗查尔雅慰问，并拨款、献礼、派兵护卫，使神庙得以重建。

en:
Studenica Monastery lies in the wooded hills of central Serbia, the mother church of Serbian temples. Stefan Nemanja, founder of the medieval Serb state, began it in the late twelfth century and took monastic vows there on abdicating in 1196 before retiring to Hilandar, where he died in 1199. His son Rastko, later Saint Sava, brought Nemanja's relics back, and Studenica became the political and spiritual centre of the Nemanjić realm.

Its white-marble Church of the Virgin, frescoed in 1208–1209, blends Romanesque and Byzantine forms in the Raška School style; King Milutin built the smaller King's Church in 1314.

After the Ottoman conquest of Serbia in 1459 the house suffered repeated assaults. A restoration in 1569 renewed its frescoes, but an earthquake and fire in the early seventeenth century destroyed much of its archive.
zh:
斯图代尼察修道院位于塞尔维亚中部的林木丘陵中，是塞尔维亚教堂的母堂。中世纪塞尔维亚国家的缔造者斯特凡·涅曼雅于12世纪末兴建此院，1196年退位时在此发愿修道，之后退隐希利安达里乌修道院，1199年在那里去世。他的儿子拉斯特科，即后来的圣萨瓦，将涅曼雅的圣骨迎回，斯图代尼察成为涅曼吉奇王朝的政治与精神中心。

白色大理石砌成的圣母堂于1208—1209年绘制壁画，融合罗马式与拜占庭风格，即后来所称的拉什卡学派；米卢廷国王于1314年修建了较小的国王堂。

1459年奥斯曼征服塞尔维亚后，修道院屡遭攻掠。1569年的大修重绘了壁画，但17世纪初的地震和火灾毁坏了大量档案。

en:
Sumela Monastery clings to a sheer cliff in the Pontic Mountains south of Trebizond, above the Altındere valley. Tradition places its foundation around 386 by two Athenian monks, Barnabas and Sophronios; it was famed for an icon of the Theotokos believed to have been painted by the Apostle Luke.

The Byzantine general Belisarius restored and enlarged it in the sixth century on Justinian's orders. The monastery took its present form in the thirteenth century, and Emperor Alexios III, whom legend says the Virgin saved from a storm, confirmed its freedom and tax exemptions in 1365.

After the Ottoman conquest of Trebizond in 1461, Mehmed II took the monastery under his protection and later sultans renewed its privileges. From 1682 it housed the Phrontisterion of Trapezous, a Greek school of the Black Sea coast; the monastery drew monks and pilgrims for centuries.
zh:
苏梅拉修道院嵌在特拉比松以南本都山脉的绝壁上，俯瞰阿尔滕代雷山谷。相传它由雅典修士巴拿巴和索夫罗尼奥斯于386年前后创建，以一幅传说出自使徒路加之手的圣母圣像闻名。

6世纪，拜占庭将军贝利萨留奉查士丁尼之命修复并扩建修道院。修道院在13世纪形成今天的格局，传说曾被圣母从风暴中救下的皇帝阿莱克修斯三世于1365年确认其自治权和免税特权。

1461年奥斯曼征服特拉比松后，穆罕默德二世将修道院置于保护之下，此后历代苏丹延续了它的特权。1682年起，院内设有黑海沿岸的希腊学府特拉比松学园；数百年间，修道院吸引着修士与朝圣者。

en:
Sumiyoshi Taisha is the head shrine of the Sumiyoshi cult and the ichinomiya of Settsu Province, beside the old port of Suminoe no Tsu. Its founding in 211 is attributed to the local magnate Tamomi no Sukune, acting on an oracle given to Empress Jingū, who is enshrined beside the three Sumiyoshi kami, protectors of seafarers and gods of war on the sea.

The shrine guarded Yamato embassies sailing to China, and its hereditary priests of the Tsumori clan boarded those ships. As Jingū was mother of the deified Emperor Ōjin, it also ranks as an ancestor shrine of Hachiman and protector of the Kawachi Minamoto line.

In 965 Emperor Murakami numbered it among sixteen shrines receiving imperial offerings. Its honden, built in the Sumiyoshi-zukuri style of raised pillars and plank walls, is the oldest surviving example of the form.
zh:
住吉大社是住吉信仰的总本社、摄津国一宫，坐落于古港住吉津旁。相传211年，当地豪族田裳见宿祢奉神功皇后所得神谕创社，神功皇后与住吉三神合祀于此；住吉三神是航海者的保护神、海上的战神。

神社庇佑大和遣华使船，世袭神职的津守氏也随船同行。由于神功皇后是神格化的应神天皇之母，住吉大社又被视为八幡神的祖社、河内源氏一脉的守护神。

965年，村上天皇将它列入十六座接受朝廷币帛的神社。本殿采用立柱、板壁的“住吉造”样式，是这一样式现存最古老的实例。

en:
Suryanar Kovil is a Hindu temple dedicated to Surya, the sun god, standing in the Kaveri delta near Kumbakonam in Tamil country. It is one of the nine Navagraha temples of Tamil Nadu and the only one with separate shrines for all nine planetary deities, the other eight shrines facing the central shrine of Surya and his consorts, Usha and Chhaya.

An inscription records that the stone building was raised under the Chola king Kulottunga I, who reigned from 1070 to 1120, and was first named Kulottungachola-Marttandalaya; later rulers of Vijayanagara added to it.

Built in the Dravidian style behind a five-tiered gopuram, the temple draws pilgrims who come to appease the planets believed to govern their horoscopes. In the early nineteenth century the Carnatic composer Muthuswami Dikshitar wrote a hymn to its sun deity.
zh:
苏利耶纳尔神庙是供奉太阳神苏利耶的印度教神庙，坐落在泰米尔地区贡伯戈讷姆附近的高韦里河三角洲。它是泰米尔纳德九大九曜神庙之一，也是其中唯一为九位星神各设神龛的一座：其余八座神龛都朝向中央苏利耶与其配偶乌莎、恰雅的神龛。

庙中铭文记载，石构建筑由朱罗国王库洛通加一世（1070—1120年在位）兴建，最初名为库洛通加朱罗-马坦达罗耶，后经毗奢耶那伽罗统治者增建。

神庙为达罗毗荼风格，门前立有五层瞿布罗高塔，朝圣者前来安抚据说掌管个人星命的诸星。19世纪初，卡纳提克作曲家穆图斯瓦米·迪克西特尔为庙中的太阳神写下了一首颂歌。

en:
The Suryavinayak Temple is a Ganesha shrine on a forested hill south of Bhaktapur in Nepal's Kathmandu Valley, and one of the valley's four principal Ganesha temples. Its name, the temple of the rising sun, comes from the eastward-facing image.

Local tradition carries its origins back to the Licchavi period, around the 500s CE, when King Vishnu Dev Barma is said to have founded it. The present brick temple in the shikhara style is much younger: an inscription records that it was completed in 1833.

Inside the sanctum rests a stone Ganesha adorned with metalwork, fronted by a pillar carved with his mouse mount. Pilgrims gather here especially on Tuesdays and in the month of Magha, holding that worship of Suryavinayak brings good fortune and sound judgment.
zh:
苏利耶毗那夜迦神庙是尼泊尔加德满都谷地的一座伽内什神庙，坐落在巴克塔普尔以南的林木山丘上，是谷地四大伽内什神庙之一。庙名意为“旭日之庙”，因神像面朝东方而得名。

当地传统把其渊源追溯到约6世纪的李查维时期，相传由毗湿奴·提婆·巴尔马国王肇建。现存的悉卡罗式砖庙则晚得多：庙中铭文记载它于1833年落成。

圣室中供奉着以金属工艺装饰的石雕伽内什，庙前立有雕着其坐骑神鼠的石柱。香客尤其爱在每周周二和摩伽月前来，相信敬拜苏利耶毗那夜迦能带来好运与明辨之心。

en:
Svetitskhoveli Cathedral rises in Mtskheta, the old capital of Kartli, where Saint Nino founded the first Georgian church after King Mirian III made Christianity the state religion in 337.

Georgian tradition holds that Elias, a Jew of Mtskheta, brought Christ's mantle from Jerusalem, and his sister Sidonia was buried holding it. A cedar grew from her grave, and its wood became a pillar that hung in the air until Nino's prayers brought it down, shedding healing liquid. The cathedral's name means the life-giving pillar.

King Vakhtang Gorgasali built a basilica there in the late fifth century. The present cathedral was raised in 1010–1029 by the architect Arsukidze under Catholicos Melchizedek I. It became the burial church of Georgian kings, was wrecked by Tamerlane at the end of the fourteenth century and rebuilt in the fifteenth, and received its defensive wall in 1787 under King Erekle II.
zh:
生命之柱主教座堂矗立在卡特利王国旧都姆茨赫塔。337年米利安三世立基督教为国教后，圣尼诺在此建立了格鲁吉亚第一座教堂。

按格鲁吉亚传统，姆茨赫塔犹太人埃利亚斯从耶路撒冷带回基督的外衣，他的妹妹西多尼亚抱着圣衣下葬；墓上长出的雪松被制成柱子，悬在空中，经圣尼诺祈祷才落下，并流出能治病的液体，教堂因此得名“生命之柱”。

5世纪末，瓦赫坦·戈尔加萨利王在此修建巴西利卡；现存教堂由建筑师阿尔苏基泽于1010—1029年在卡托利科斯科斯梅尔基塞德克一世主持下建成。这里后来成为格鲁吉亚国王的安葬地，14世纪末被帖木儿摧毁，15世纪重建，1787年又在埃雷克勒二世治下修筑了防御墙。

en:
Swayambhu, the self-arisen one, crowns a hill west of Kathmandu and is among the oldest Buddhist stupa complexes in Nepal. Hindus also worship there, and the resident monkeys earned it the nickname the Monkey Temple. The Swayambhu Purana tells how the bodhisattva Manjushri drained the lake in the Kathmandu valley, revealing a self-sprung flame which King Prachandadev of Gauda enshrined beneath a stupa.

Tradition brings Ashoka here in the 200s BCE, and a damaged inscription records building works ordered by the Licchavi king Vrsadeva in 640. In the 1400s the Indian abbot Sariputra rebuilt the dilapidated stupa with a Malla king's support.

The Tibetan master Tsangnyon Heruka restored it in 1504, and Pratap Malla of Kathmandu added the eastern stairway in the 1600s. Its white dome, four-eyed Buddha cube and gilded thirteen-tier spire embody the Vajrayana cosmos of Newar Buddhism.
zh:
四眼天神庙本名“斯瓦扬布”，意为“自生者”，位于加德满都以西，是尼泊尔最古老的佛塔建筑群之一。印度教徒也来礼拜，庙中群猴聚居，又称“猴庙”。《斯瓦扬布往世书》称，菩萨文殊师利排干加德满都谷地的湖水，使自生之光显露，高尔国王普拉昌达戴夫便在光上建塔供奉。

相传阿育王在公元前3世纪来朝礼，残碑记载离车毗国王弗栗沙提婆于640年下令兴修工程。15世纪，印度上座沙利子经在马拉国王支持下重建佛塔。

1504年藏地大师仓央·海如伽再次修缮，17世纪加德满都的普拉塔普·马拉增修东山门石阶。白色覆钵、绘有佛陀四面慧眼的方台和鎏金十三层相轮，体现了尼瓦尔佛教的密教宇宙观。

en:
The Tara Tarini Temple crowns the Kumari hills above the Rushikulya river in Odisha, and is dedicated to sister goddesses Tara and Tarini, worshipped as forms of Adi Shakti. Puranic legend identifies it as the Sthana pitha where the breasts of Sati fell when Vishnu dismembered her body.

The sanctum holds two stone faces of the goddesses adorned with gold and silver ornaments, and an image of the Buddha, reflecting the shrine's role as a cradle of the Buddhist Tara cult. Hindi and Odia traditions present the goddess as the patron of ancient Kalinga and of merchants who sailed to Java and Sumatra.

The nine hundred and ninety-nine stone steps climbing the hill are said to have been paid for by a merchant saved from shipwreck. Each spring the Chaitra Jatra draws crowds who bring their children for the auspicious first tonsure.
zh:
多罗·多梨尼神庙坐落在奥里萨勒湿俱利亚河畔的库马里山上，供奉姐妹女神多罗与多梨尼，二者被视为阿迪·夏克提的化身。往世书传说认定这里是毗湿奴分解萨蒂遗体时其双乳坠落之地，称“双乳圣地”。

圣所中供着两尊饰有金银妆奁的女神石面，还有一尊佛像，反映出此庙也是佛教多罗女神信仰的发源地之一。印地语与奥里雅语传统把女神奉为古代羯陵伽和远航爪哇、苏门答腊的海商的守护神。

通往山顶的九百九十九级石阶，相传是一位遇海难生还的商人捐资修建的。每年春季的遮伊陀罗节期间，香客云集，纷纷带孩子来此行吉祥的首次剃发礼。

en:
Tarapith is a Tantric pilgrimage village on the Dwarka river in Birbhum district of Bengal, famed for its temple of Tara and the cremation ground beside it. The shrine is recognised as both a Shakti pitha and a Siddha pitha: Puranic works hold that the third eye of Sati fell here, making it one of the fifty-one seats of the goddess.

Tradition makes the sage Vashistha its first worshipper. A legend in the Rudrayamala relates how he travelled beyond the Himalayas to learn the left-handed kaula rites, after which Tara appeared as a mother suckling Shiva and turned into the stone image venerated in the sanctum.

At the adjoining cremation ground, ascetics seek enlightenment amid funeral pyres on the model of Vashistha's austerities. The temple remains one of the three great Shakta centres of Bengal alongside Kalighat and Nabadwip.
zh:
多罗比他寺是孟加拉比尔布姆县德瓦尔卡河畔的一座怛特罗朝圣村落，以多罗女神庙及庙旁的火葬场闻名。该圣地同时被视为性力圣地与成就圣地；往世书认为，萨蒂的第三只眼坠落于此，使它成为五十一处女神圣地之一。

相传仙人婆私吒是此地最早的礼拜者。《楼陀罗耶密罗》中的传说讲述他远赴喜马拉雅山外学得左道俱洛仪轨，女神才化为哺乳湿婆的母亲形象现身，并变成圣所中供奉的石像。

毗邻的火葬场中，修行者效仿婆私吒的苦行，在焚尸烟火之间寻求觉悟。多罗比他寺与迦利卡特、诺博迪维普并列为孟加拉三大性力派中心之一。

en:
The Telesterion was the initiation hall at Eleusis in Attica, the centre of the Eleusinian Mysteries held in honour of Demeter and Persephone. A hall stood on the site by the seventh century BC, and each year the nine-day festival brought thousands of initiates, who were shown sacred relics and forbidden to reveal what they had seen.

The Persians burned the building in 480 BC; it was rebuilt under Pericles from a design by Iktinos, the architect of the Parthenon, and Philon added a Doric portico around 318 BC. Sacked by the Costoboci in 170 AD, it was rebuilt on a larger scale by Marcus Aurelius, the only layman admitted to its innermost shrine.

The emperor Theodosius I closed the mysteries in 392, and in 396 the Goths of Alaric sacked Eleusis and destroyed the Telesterion, which was never rebuilt.
zh:
泰勒斯台里昂神庙是阿提卡厄琉息斯的入会大厅，也是祭祀得墨忒耳与珀耳塞福涅的厄琉息斯秘仪的中心。早在公元前7世纪此地已有会堂，每年为期九天的节庆吸引数以千计的入会者，他们瞻仰圣物，并发誓不得透露所见。

公元前480年波斯人焚毁了建筑，后来在伯里克利主持下按帕特农神庙建筑师伊克蒂诺斯的设计重建；约公元前318年，菲隆又增建了一座多立克式门廊。170年它被科斯托博克人洗劫，马可·奥勒留将其按更大规模重建，他也是唯一获准进入最内殿的俗人。

392年皇帝狄奥多西一世取缔了秘仪，396年阿拉里克率领的哥特人洗劫厄琉息斯并摧毁了泰勒斯台里昂神庙，此后它再未重建。

en:
The Temple of the Great Jaguar rises on the east side of the Great Plaza of Tikal, in the Peten rainforest of northern Guatemala. Dated to about 732, this limestone step pyramid is crowned by a towering roof comb and takes its name from a carved lintel showing its king enthroned on a jaguar seat.

The ruler buried within was Jasaw Chan K'awiil I, who took the throne in 682 and broke the power of rival Calakmul in a battle of 695. Temple II across the plaza held the tomb of his queen, Lady Lahan Unen Mo'.

His son Yik'in Chan K'awiil carried on the dynasty, but Tikal's fortunes faded with the Classic collapse. Building ceased, the palaces were burned, and by the end of the tenth century the jungle had swallowed the empty city and the jaguar temple.
zh:
大美洲虎神庙矗立在危地马拉北部佩滕雨林中的蒂卡尔大广场东侧。这座石灰岩阶梯金字塔约建于732年，顶端高耸着屋顶冠饰，因一块雕有国王端坐美洲虎王座的门楣而得名。

葬在庙中的国王是贾索·昌·卡维尔一世，他于682年登上王位，并在695年的战役中击溃宿敌卡拉克穆尔。广场对面的二号神庙安葬着他的王后拉汉·乌嫩·莫。

他的儿子伊金·昌·卡维尔延续了王朝，但随着古典期崩溃，蒂卡尔逐渐衰落。营造停止，宫殿被焚，到10世纪末丛林已吞没这座空城，也吞没了美洲虎神庙。

en:
The Temple of K'uk'ulkan is the great step pyramid at Chichen Itza in the northern Yucatan lowlands, raised to the Maya Feathered Serpent deity K'uk'ulkan. An inner temple was built between about 600 and 800, and the pyramid took its final form around the ninth to eleventh centuries.

Stairways climb all four sides; each has ninety-one steps, and counting the top platform they add up to three hundred and sixty-five, the days of the Maya solar year. At the equinoxes the setting sun casts shadows that seem to make a serpent crawl down the northern balustrade.

Chichen Itza had declined as a regional power by 1100, and colonial Maya chronicles credit Hunac Ceel of Mayapan with its conquest in the thirteenth century, yet pilgrims still came to its cenote. Spaniards under Montejo the Younger briefly held the ruins in 1532 and 1534 before being driven out.
zh:
羽蛇神庙是尤卡坦北部低地奇琴伊察的大阶梯金字塔，供奉玛雅人的羽蛇神库库尔坎。内层神庙约建于600—800年，金字塔在9至11世纪前后形成最终形制。

金字塔四面各有一道阶梯，每道91级，加上顶部平台合计365级，正合玛雅太阳历的一年天数。春分、秋分时夕阳投下的阴影，仿佛羽蛇正沿北阶梯栏杆爬行而下。

奇琴伊察在1100年之前已不再是地区强国，殖民地时期的玛雅编年史称玛雅潘的胡纳克·塞尔于13世纪征服了它，但朝圣者仍前往城中的圣井。1532年和1534年，小蒙特霍率领的西班牙人曾短暂占据废墟，随后被赶走。

en:
The Temple of Confucius stands on the site of Confucius's house, which the Duke of Lu made a shrine soon after his death in 479 BC. Emperor Gao of the Han offered sacrifices there in 205 BC, setting an imperial precedent.

The original house was replaced during a Sui rebuilding of 611; after a fire of 1214 under the Jin, the Yuan had restored the complex by 1302, and in 1331 it was enclosed by walls modelled on the imperial palace. The Ming rebuilding after another fire in 1499 gave the temple its scale, its nine courtyards and great Dacheng Hall echoing the Forbidden City.

Qing repairs following the fire of 1724 were completed by 1730. Together with the Kong Family Mansion and the Cemetery of Confucius, the temple drew scholars and officials to venerate the master and his teachings.
zh:
孔庙建于孔子故宅之上，公元前479年孔子去世后不久，鲁君便将故宅辟为祭祀之所。公元前205年汉高祖亲临曲阜祭孔，开创了皇帝祀孔的先例。

原来的故宅在611年隋代重建时被拆除；1214年金朝时庙毁于火，到1302年元代已将建筑修复，1331年又仿照皇宫修筑围墙。1499年再遭火灾后，明代重建奠定了规模，九进院落和大成殿都仿效紫禁城。

1724年火灾后的清代修缮于1730年完工。孔庙与孔府、孔林吸引历代士人官员前来瞻仰先师及其学说。

official_raw.en: The $temple_of_confucius$ in [ShowLocationName('qufu')], was originally built in 478 BC to honor the philosopher Confucius. Expanded repeatedly during successive dynasties, it became one of the largest temple complexes in China.
official_raw.zh: [ShowLocationName('qufu')]的$temple_of_confucius$最初建于公元前478年以纪念孔夫子。历朝不断扩建，使它成为了中国最大的寺庙建筑群之一。

en:
Teotihuacan, in the Valley of Mexico, was the greatest city of ancient Mesoamerica, settled from about 100 BC and a religious centre by the first century. Around 450 it held perhaps 100,000 people, along the Avenue of the Dead; the Temple of the Feathered Serpent was ringed with sculpted serpent heads.

Its influence reached the Maya world, where a Teotihuacan king called Spearthrower Owl installed his dynasts at Tikal in 378. Droughts linked to the climate crisis of 535 and 536 brought famine, and around 550 temples and palaces were burned in an uprising and the city collapsed.

Centuries later the Aztecs named the ruins Teotihuacan, the birthplace of the gods, and came as pilgrims. In 1409 the resettled town received a ruler; from 1427 it passed under the Aztec Empire as an Acolhua vassal.
zh:
特奥蒂瓦坎位于墨西哥谷地，是古代美索美洲最伟大的城市，约自公元前100年起有人定居，1世纪时已是宗教中心。450年前后，城中可能有10万人口，城市沿死者大道展开，羽蛇神庙外墙环绕着雕刻的蛇头。

它的影响远及玛雅世界，378年，一位被称为“掷矛者猫头鹰”的特奥蒂瓦坎君王在蒂卡尔扶立了自己的王族。535—536年气候剧变引发旱灾和饥荒，约550年，神庙宫殿在起义中被焚，城市就此崩溃。

数百年后，阿兹特克人将废墟命名为特奥蒂瓦坎，意为“众神诞生之地”，并前来朝圣。1409年，重新有人聚居的城镇获封统治者；1427年起作为阿科卢阿人的附庸并入阿兹特克帝国。

en:
Saint Peter's stands on the west bank of the Tiber, on the site of the former Circus of Nero. Constantine I's first basilica was built between 318 and 322. Charlemagne was crowned emperor there in 800.

In 846 Saracen raiders sacked the shrine and damaged the apostle Peter's tomb, prompting Pope Leo IV to build the Leonine Walls. By the fifteenth century the old church was unsound, and Nicholas V and then Julius II decided on replacement.

Work on the Renaissance basilica began in 1506 under Donato Bramante; Michelangelo took over the design in 1547 and gave the church its great dome, and the building was completed in 1626. Gian Lorenzo Bernini furnished it with the bronze baldachin over the papal altar and the colonnaded square in front.
zh:
圣伯多禄大殿坐落在台伯河西岸，建在昔日尼禄竞技场的遗址上。君士坦丁一世的首座大殿建于318—322年。800年查理曼在此加冕为帝。

846年撒拉森袭掠者洗劫圣所、破坏宗徒伯多禄的陵墓，促使教宗利奥四世修筑利奥城墙。到15世纪，老堂结构已岌岌可危，尼古拉五世继而尤利乌斯二世决定彻底重建。

文艺复兴式大殿于1506年在多纳托·布拉曼特主持下开工；米开朗基罗1547年接掌设计，为教堂留下宏伟穹顶，整座建筑于1626年完工。随后詹洛伦佐·贝尼尼为教堂配上教宗祭坛上方的青铜华盖和殿前带柱廊的广场。

official_raw.en: The original Papal Basilica of Saint Peter in the Vatican in [ShowLocationName('rome')] was commissioned by Emperor Constantine in the 4th century over the tomb of Saint Peter, the first $catholic_pope$. It became the principal church of Western [ShowReligionGroupName('christian')] and the seat of papal authority. It also is one of the main centers of pilgrimage for [ShowReligionName('catholic')].
official_raw.zh: 最初的[ShowLocationName('rome')]梵蒂冈圣伯多禄宗座圣殿由君士坦丁皇帝于公元4世纪在首任$catholic_pope$圣伯多禄的陵墓上建造。它成为了西方[ShowReligionGroupName('christian')]最重要的教堂，以及教宗权威的所在地。它也是[ShowReligionName('catholic')]的主要朝圣地之一。

en:
Thirukkadigai, also called Sholingapuram, is a Vishnu temple at Sholinghur in the Tamil country, counted among the 108 Divya Desams. Its name comes from the belief that worship lasting a kadigai, about twenty-four minutes, is enough to win the deity's blessing; the sage Vishwamitra is said to have earned the title of Brahmarishi here.

Three shrines occupy twin hills: Yoga Narasimha on the larger hill, reached by more than 1,300 steps, Bhaktavatsala Perumal at its foot, and Hanuman on the smaller hill. Inscriptions record gifts from Kulothunga Chola III and other rulers, and the teacher Manavala Mamunigal is said to have expounded the Thirupavai here.

The temple follows the Tenkalai tradition. In July 1781 the hills around it were the scene of the Battle of Sholinghur, fought between the British and Hyder Ali of Mysore.
zh:
蒂鲁卡迪盖又名绍林加普兰，是泰米尔地区绍林古尔的一座毗湿奴神庙，位列一百零八座圣庙。其名源于一种信仰：在此礼拜仅需一卡迪盖，约二十四分钟，便可获得神祇赐福；相传众友仙人正是在此证得梵仙之号。

两座山丘上分布着三处神龛：大山丘上是需攀登1300余级台阶的瑜伽那罗辛哈，山脚是巴克塔瓦察拉·佩鲁马尔，小山丘上则有哈奴曼。铭文记载了库洛通加·朱罗三世等统治者的布施，宗师马纳瓦拉·马穆尼加尔相传曾在此宣讲《蒂鲁帕瓦伊》。

神庙遵行滕卡莱派仪轨。1781年7月，神庙周围的丘陵成为绍林古尔战役的战场，英军与迈索尔的海德尔·阿里在此交锋。

en:
Thirukkavalampadi, also called the Gopalakrishna Perumal Temple, is a Vishnu shrine at Thirunangur near Sirkali on the Tamil Nadu coast. Vishnu is worshipped here as the cowherd Krishna, Gopalakrishna, flanked by Rukmini and Satyabhama. The place takes its name from a legend in which Krishna rescued an elephant, kavalam meaning elephant and padi a place.

It is one of the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams, said to mark the eleven forms Vishnu assumed to calm Shiva's furious dance after the death of Sati. It is glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the canon of the Alvar saints compiled from the 600s to the 800s, above all by Thirumangai Alvar.

Built in the Dravidian style with a three-tiered gopuram, the temple joins the other ten shrines each year in the Thai-month Mangalasasana festival, when their festival images are carried together on Garuda mounts.
zh:
底禄迦伐蓝波地又称“戈帕拉克里希纳·佩鲁马尔神庙”，是泰米尔纳德沿海锡尔卡利附近蒂鲁南古尔村的毗湿奴神庙。庙中毗湿奴以牧童奎师那（戈帕拉克里希纳）之像受供，鲁格米尼与萨蒂亚芭玛分立两侧。庙名源于奎师那拯救大象的传说，“迦伐兰”意为大象，“波地”意为地方。

它是蒂鲁南古尔十一座迪维亚·德萨姆之一，相传标记着毗湿奴为平息湿婆在萨蒂死后狂舞而化现的十一种形象。6至9世纪阿尔瓦尔派圣徒编成的《四千圣咏》对此庙有所歌颂，尤以提鲁芒盖·阿尔瓦尔的颂诗为多。

神庙为达罗毗荼风格，建有三层门楼。每年泰历泰月的“曼加拉萨萨纳”节上，它与同组十座神庙的节庆神像乘迦楼罗舆驾会聚。

en:
The Thiruvallam Sree Parasurama Temple stands on the Karamana River outside Thiruvananthapuram. It is the only temple in Kerala dedicated to Parashurama, the sixth avatar of Vishnu, who in legend hurled his axe into the sea and made the waters retreat from Gokarna to Kanyakumari. Brahmins are said to have raised the shrine in gratitude after he granted them the reclaimed land.

Counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams of the Vaishnava tradition, it honours Shiva with equal standing and is one of the few Hindu temples where Brahma also receives worship. The structure was last renovated between the 1100s and 1200s.

The temple draws pilgrims for the ancestor-rite of Balitharpanam on the new-moon day of the Malayalam month of Karkidakam. Devotees bathe in the river before offering homage to their forefathers.
zh:
耻卢伐蓝‑室利持斧罗摩神庙坐落在特里凡得琅城外的卡拉马纳河畔。它是喀拉拉唯一一座供奉持斧罗摩的神庙；持斧罗摩是毗湿奴的第六化身，传说他把战斧掷入大海，令海水从戈卡尔纳退到坎尼亚库马里，又将新生的土地施予婆罗门，婆罗门感念其恩，据说建起了这座庙。

它位列毗湿奴派108座阿比摩纳圣地之一，庙中湿婆享有同等尊位，还是少数同时供奉梵天的印度教神庙。建筑最后一次重修是在12至13世纪。

每逢马拉雅拉姆历卡尔基达卡月的新月日，神庙吸引朝圣者前来行巴利塔尔帕南祭祖之礼。信众先在河中沐浴，再追荐先人。

en:
Thommanon is a Hindu temple east of the Victory Gate of Angkor Thom, opposite Chau Say Tevoda on the road to Ta Keo. Most scholars attribute it to Suryavarman II, who reigned from 1113 to 1150 and built Angkor Wat, though a few place its devata carvings as early as Jayavarman VI around 1100. It was dedicated to both Shiva and Vishnu.

Built of sandstone on a single-towered plan, the temple opens east through a gopura and a mandapa into the central sanctuary. Unlike Chau Say Tevoda, its upper structure used no wood beams encased in stone, helping it survive in better repair.

Its devatas, divine female figures, wear flowered crowns and pleated skirts, their fingers held in a mudra also seen at Angkor Wat. The enclosure walls and separate library have vanished, leaving the gateways and central tower above the forest floor.
zh:
塔玛侬神庙是一座印度教神庙，坐落在吴哥通胜利门东侧，在通往塔凯奥的路上与周萨神庙相对。多数学者认为它建于吴哥窟建造者苏利耶跋摩二世（1113—1150年在位）时代；也有少数学者根据飞天浮雕把它提早到约1100年阇耶跋摩六世在位时。神庙同时供奉湿婆与毗湿奴。

整庙以砂岩建成，采用单塔布局：朝东依次经过瞿布罗和曼达波，进入中央密室。与周萨神庙不同，它的上部结构没有使用外石内木的梁架，因此保存得更为完好。

庙中提婆妲女神像头戴花冠、身着褶裙，手指摆出吴哥窟中也能见到的独特手印。围墙与独立的经藏已湮没无存，只余门楼和中央塔矗立在林地之上。

en:
The Thrikkakara Vamanamoorthy Temple, near Kochi in Kerala, is one of India's principal shrines dedicated to Vamana, the dwarf avatar of Vishnu, and is counted among the 108 Divya Desams. Tradition ascribes its founding to the sage Parashurama.

The main icon shows Vamana about to set his foot on the Asura king Mahabali. Legend tells how Vamana was granted three paces of land, grew to gigantic size and strode across earth and heaven; Bali offered his head for the third step and was granted the underworld for his humility.

Onam, Kerala's harvest festival, welcomes Bali's annual return. The temple is its ceremonial centre, and its records preserve the earliest known mention of the festival, dated to 861. In the eighteenth century, after Marthanda Varma of Travancore and the East India Company annexed the territory from the Kingdom of Kochi, local chiefs conducted celebrations under the Maharaja of Travancore.
zh:
特里卡卡拉的筏摩那穆尔蒂神庙位于喀拉拉的科钦附近，是印度供奉毗湿奴侏儒化身筏摩那的主要神庙之一，位列108座迪维亚·德萨姆圣地。相传神庙由仙人持斧罗摩开创。

主尊塑像表现筏摩那正准备把脚踏在阿修罗王钵利身上。传说筏摩那向钵利求赐三步之地，应允之后便化身为巨人，跨过大地和天国；钵利献出头颅供他迈第三步，筏摩那嘉其谦卑，命他统治阴间。

喀拉拉丰收节欧南节迎请钵利每年归来。神庙是欧南节的礼仪中心，庙中档案保存着已知最早的欧南节记载，年代为861年。18世纪，特拉凡哥尔的玛尔坦达·瓦尔马与英国东印度公司从科钦王国夺取此地后，各地首领在特拉凡哥尔大君主持下共同举办庆典。

en:
Outside Tibur, on the Via Tiburtina through the Aniene gorge to Rome, stood the sanctuary of Hercules Victor, the greatest Italic shrine of the hero god. Hercules was the town's patron, worshipped as the warrior Invictus after victory over the Aequi and as protector of the quarries.

The complex was raised between the 160s and 82 BC, its terraces modelled on the sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia at Praeneste. The road passed through a vaulted via tecta, and the old bridge toll became offerings and tithes to the god.

Warehouses, banks, inns and an oracular pool made it a wealthy pilgrimage and market centre. The temple with its colossal Hercules statue and yellow roof was visible from Rome. Augustus often judged cases under its arcades, and the theatre was completed in his reign.
zh:
赫拉克勒斯·维克托圣所位于蒂布尔城外，控扼提布尔提那大道沿阿涅内河峡谷通往罗马的要道，是意大利本土最大的英雄神圣所。赫拉克勒斯是城市的保护神：人们因战胜埃魁人而奉他为战神“无敌者”，又奉他为采石场的保护神。

建筑群建成于公元前2世纪60年代至前82年，台地仿效普拉埃内斯特的头生子之神福尔图娜圣所。大道经由拱顶的“有顶之路”穿过圣所，原先的过桥税改为供物和什一税。

仓库、钱庄、客栈和神谕池使这里成为富有的朝圣与贸易中心。神庙中矗立着赫拉克勒斯巨像，黄色屋顶在罗马城都能望见。奥古斯都常在柱廊下审理案件，剧场也在他在位时完工。

en:
The Great Mosque of Tinmal stands in the High Atlas village of Tinmal. Tinmal was the first capital of the Almohad movement, where Ibn Tumart settled his followers in 1124 or 1125 and made his base for war on the Almoravids. When he died in 1130 he was buried there, and his tomb became a sanctuary and place of pilgrimage.

A first mosque was raised at once. After the conquest of Marrakesh the caliph Abd al-Mu'min built the present mosque in 1148, some traditions giving 1153 or 1154. Its hypostyle plan and mihrab style resembled the Kutubiyya, and later Almohad rulers were laid to rest beside it.

Tinmal also served as the dynasty's last redoubt: when the Marinids overran Morocco, the remaining Almohad leaders made their final stand here until they were defeated and captured in 1275.
zh:
廷马尔大清真寺坐落在大阿特拉斯山区的廷马尔村。廷马尔是穆瓦希德运动的第一个都城：1124年或1125年，伊本·图马特把追随者安置在这里，以此为基地向穆拉比特王朝开战。他于1130年去世后葬在此地，坟墓逐渐发展为圣所和朝圣地。

当时便建起了第一座清真寺。穆瓦希德人攻占马拉喀什后，哈里发阿卜杜勒·慕敏于1148年修建了现存的清真寺，也有史料将始建年代记作1153年或1154年。它的多柱式布局和米哈拉布风格与库图比亚清真寺相同，后来的穆瓦希德君主也安葬在寺旁。

廷马尔还是王朝最后的据点：马林王朝席卷摩洛哥时，残余的穆瓦希德首领在此坚守，直到1275年兵败被俘。

en:
Titi'kaka is the Aymara name of the Island of the Sun in southern Lake Titicaca, held by the Incas to be the birthplace of the sun god Inti. One origin myth recorded by the chronicler Bernabé Cobo tells of the Sun rising from behind the island's rock, Titi Qala. Manco Cápac, first of the Incas and son of Inti, was said to have issued from the same rock.

Settlement reached back to the third millennium before Christ, and a Tiwanaku ritual centre stood above the crag before the Inca conquest in the fifteenth century. After the conquest, Titi Qala became a pilgrimage destination, ranked with Pachacamac.

The tenth Inca, Túpac Yupanqui, who reigned from about 1471 to 1493, built a temple at the sacred rock, a convent for chosen women and an inn for pilgrims. Their boats crossed the lake from towns such as Pomata.
zh:
Titi'kaka是太阳岛的艾马拉语名称。这座岛屿位于的的喀喀湖南部，印加人相信太阳神因蒂诞生于此。编年史家贝尔纳韦·科博记录的一则起源神话讲述太阳从岛上圣岩蒂蒂卡拉后方升起。印加初代君主、因蒂之子曼科·卡帕克据说也从这块岩石中走出。

岛上定居史可追溯至公元前第三个千年，在印加于15世纪征服之前，圣岩上方已有一处蒂亚瓦纳科仪式中心。征服之后，蒂蒂卡拉成为朝圣地，地位堪比帕查卡马克。

第十代印加图帕克·尤潘基（约1471—1493年在位）在圣岩旁修建神庙，又为圣女建了修道院、为朝圣者建了旅舍。朝圣者的船只从波马塔等城镇出发，横渡湖水而来。

en:
The cathedral of Saint Mary of the Assumption in Toledo is the senior church of Spain, its archbishop holding the title Primate of the Spains granted by Pope Urban II in 1088. A Visigothic cathedral stood here by 587, when King Reccared abjured Arianism. After the Muslim conquest it was replaced by the great mosque, which Alfonso VI converted to Christian use on reconquering Toledo in 1085.

The Gothic building was begun in 1226 under Ferdinand III on the mosque's footprint. The nave's vaults were closed in 1493 under the Catholic Monarchs.

Known as Dives Toletana, the Rich Toledan, it houses the Mozarabic Chapel preserving the Hispano-Mozarabic rite and the gilded monstrance made by Enrique de Arfe between 1517 and 1524 for Cardinal Cisneros, carried in the Corpus Christi procession. Several kings of Castile lie buried in its chapels.
zh:
托莱多的圣母升天主教座堂是西班牙地位最高的教堂，大主教拥有教皇乌尔班二世于1088年颁赐的“西班牙首席主教”头衔。587年，雷卡雷多国王在此弃绝阿里乌斯派，至迟那时此地已有西哥特主教座堂。穆斯林征服后，教堂被大清真寺取代，阿方索六世于1085年收复托莱多后将其改为基督教堂。

哥特式建筑1226年在费尔南多三世治下于旧清真寺基址动工，拱顶于1493年天主教双王时期合拢。

它有“富庶的托莱多人”之称，莫萨拉布小堂保留西班牙-莫萨拉布礼仪；恩里克·德·阿尔费于1517—1524年为西斯内罗斯枢机打造的镀金圣体光，在基督圣体节游行时抬出。多位卡斯蒂利亚国王葬于小堂。

en:
Tōllān, the site of Tula northwest of Mexico City, was known in Nahuatl as Tollan Xicocotitlan and rose after the decline of Teotihuacan as the capital of the Toltecs. Tula Chico flourished from about 650 to 900, and the ceremonial center of Tula Grande reached its height between 900 and 1150, housing perhaps sixty thousand people.

Its most sacred monument was the Pyramid of Quetzalcoatl, crowned by basalt columns carved as Toltec warriors. Drought and pressure from migrating Chichimeca groups undermined the city, whose ceremonial center was burned and abandoned in the twelfth century.

Later peoples remembered Tollan as the legendary city of wisdom and craftsmanship linked to the priest-king Ce Acatl Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl. When the Spanish arrived, scribes and feather workers still lived among its ruins, and the Aztecs traced their royal legitimacy back to its Toltec rulers.
zh:
图拉圣城即墨西哥城西北的图拉遗址，纳瓦特尔语名为托兰-希科科蒂特兰，在特奥蒂瓦坎衰落后崛起，成为托尔特克人的都城。小图拉约兴盛于650—900年，礼仪中心大图拉在900—1150年达到鼎盛，约有六万居民。

城中最神圣的建筑是羽蛇神金字塔，塔顶矗立着雕成托尔特克武士形象的玄武岩柱。干旱和南下的奇奇梅卡诸部的压力削弱了城市，礼仪中心在12世纪被焚毁废弃。

后世各民族把图拉传颂为与祭司王塞·阿卡特·托皮尔钦·魁札尔科亚特尔相连的传说中的智慧与工艺之城。西班牙人到来时，仍有书吏和羽毛工匠居住在废墟之间，阿兹特克人也将王权的合法性追溯到这里的托尔特克统治者。

en:
Trichambaram Temple is a Krishna shrine at Taliparamba in northern Kerala, founded around the 900s under the Mushika dynasty and praised in the eleventh-century Sanskrit court poem the Mūṣikavaṃśa. Its central image shows Krishna in his ferocious Raudra posture after slaying the tyrant Kamsa, and the temple counts among the Abhimana Kshethrams, esteemed Vaishnavite shrines.

The sanctum walls carry carvings and murals from the 1400s and 1500s. A Durga shrine stands in the middle of a temple tank, one of the hundred and eight Durgalayas of ancient Kerala, while smaller shrines honour Shiva, Ganesha, Shasta and the serpent deities.
zh:
多梨占婆蓝神庙是北喀拉拉塔利帕兰巴的一座奎师那神庙，约建于10世纪穆希卡王朝时期，11世纪的梵语宫廷史诗《穆希迦世系》曾加以称颂。庙中主像呈现奎师那诛杀暴君刚沙之后的愤怒相，该庙也被列入毗湿奴派尊崇的圣庙名录。

圣所墙壁上保留着15至16世纪的雕刻与壁画。庙中水池中央有一座杜尔迦神龛，是古代喀拉拉一百零八座杜尔迦庙之一；周围的小庙供奉湿婆、象头神、夏斯塔和蛇神。

en:
The Krishna Matha at Udupi, on the Karnataka coast, was established in 1285 by Madhvacharya, founder of the Dvaita, or dualist, school of Vedanta. Tradition holds that he brought the image of Krishna from Dwarka hidden inside a block of gopichandana clay and installed it here.

The deity faces west and is viewed through the nine-holed silver window called the Navagraha Kindi. An outer window, the Kanakana Kindi, commemorates the 16th-century devotee-poet Kanakadasa.

Madhvacharya also founded eight surrounding monasteries, the Ashta Mathas, whose swamis take turns to run the shrine: under the paryaya system, worship and administration pass from one matha to the next every two years, making Udupi the enduring centre of the Madhva Vaishnavite tradition and one of South India's busiest pilgrimage kitchens.
zh:
乌杜比的奎师那神庙位于卡纳塔克沿海，1285年由吠檀多二元论学派（德瓦伊塔）的奠基人摩陀伐建立。相传他把从德瓦尔卡迎来的奎师那像藏在戈皮旃檀泥块中带来并安奉于此。

神像面朝西方，信众须通过名为“九曜窗”的九孔银窗瞻仰。外侧的“迦纳迦窗”纪念16世纪的虔信诗人迦纳迦达萨。

摩陀伐还在周边建立了八座修道院，即“八马特”；八院的斯瓦米依照“帕里亚亚”制度每两年轮流接管神庙的祭祀与行政，使乌杜比长期成为摩陀伐毗湿奴派传统的中心，也是南印度最繁忙的朝圣供餐地之一。

en:
The Ulagalantha Perumal Temple, also called the Trivikrama Temple, stands at Tirukkoyilur in the Tamil country. Vishnu is worshipped here as Ulagalantha Perumal, the lord who measured the world, with Lakshmi as Poongothai. The shrine is among the 108 Divya Desams glorified by the Alvar saints.

First raised by the medieval Cholas, it was later enriched by the kings of Vijayanagara and the Nayaks of Madurai. Its eleven-tiered tower rises fifty-nine metres. The image, carved from tharu wood with one foot raised, depicts Vamana as the giant Trivikrama, who humbled the Asura king Bali by striding over the three worlds.

The temple is revered as the place where the first three Alvars, Poigai, Bhoothath and Pey, attained salvation. Tradition holds that the shrine was originally dedicated to Krishna as Gopalan, from which Tirukkoyilur takes its name.
zh:
乌拉加蓝塔佩鲁马尔神庙又称三步神毗讫罗摩神庙，坐落在泰米尔地区的蒂鲁科伊尔卢尔。庙中毗湿奴以“丈量世界之主”乌拉加蓝塔·佩鲁马尔的形象受祀，拉克什米则称蓬戈泰。神庙位列阿尔瓦尔圣徒赞颂的108座迪维亚·德萨姆圣地。

神庙最初由中世纪的朱罗人兴建，后经毗奢耶那伽罗诸王和马杜赖纳亚克家族增饰。十一层的门楼高达五十九米。主尊像以塔鲁木雕成，一足抬起，表现筏摩那化身为巨人毗讫罗摩，跨越三界以折服阿修罗王钵利。

神庙被尊为最早三位阿尔瓦尔圣徒波伊盖、布塔特和佩伊获得解脱之处。相传神龛最初供奉的是号为戈帕兰的黑天，蒂鲁科伊尔卢尔之名便由此而来。

en:
The Umayyad Mosque, or Great Mosque of Damascus, stands on a site sacred since the Iron Age: an Aramean temple of Hadad, then a Roman temple of Jupiter, then a Christian cathedral under Theodosius I. After the Muslim conquest of Damascus in 634 part of the cathedral served as a prayer house.

Between 706 and 715 the Umayyad caliph al-Walid I replaced the church with a mosque built by craftsmen from Byzantine lands and famed for its golden mosaics. Christians and Muslims venerate it as the resting place of the head of John the Baptist; its Minaret of Isa is named for the tradition that Jesus will descend there at the end of days.

Fire damaged the mosque in 1069 and 1479; the Mamluk sultan Qaitbay added his namesake minaret in 1488. The earthquake of 1759 ruined part of its northern arcade.
zh:
伍麦叶清真寺又称大马士革大清真寺，所在之地自铁器时代起便是崇拜场所：先是阿拉米人的哈达德神庙，后成为罗马人的朱庇特神庙，狄奥多西一世时期又改建为基督教堂。634年穆斯林征服大马士革后，教堂一部分被辟为礼拜所。

706—715年，伍麦叶哈里发瓦利德一世将教堂拆除，征调拜占庭地区的工匠建成清真寺，以金色镶嵌画闻名。基督徒和穆斯林都相信施洗约翰的头颅安葬于此；尔撒宣礼塔则得名于尔撒在末日降临于此的传说。

1069年和1479年清真寺两度遭火，1488年马穆鲁克苏丹卡伊特拜在灾后增建了以他命名的宣礼塔。1759年的地震又毁坏了部分北侧拱廊。

en:
Usa Hachiman Jingūji is a shrine-temple complex at Usa in Buzen on Kyushu, dedicated to Hachiman, the deified Emperor Ōjin and tutelary god of warriors. Founded in the Wadō era of 708–714, it was the first Hachiman shrine and ranked second only to the Ise Shrine.

In 749 its portable shrine carried Hachiman's spirit to Nara to protect the casting of the Great Buddha at Tōdai-ji. An oracle from Usa was invoked in the dispute over the monk Dōkyō's claim to the throne under Empress Shōtoku. In 779 Miroku-ji was built beside the shrine, creating what is regarded as Japan's first jingū-ji, a combined shrine and temple.

Usa's branches included Iwashimizu Hachimangū in 859 and Tsurugaoka Hachimangū in 1063. In the sixteenth century the Funai lord Ōtomo Yoshishige repeatedly attacked the shrine; his wife, the priestess Lady Nata, helped defend it.
zh:
宇佐八幡神宫寺位于九州丰前国宇佐，祭祀被神化为八幡神的应神天皇，即武士的守护神。神社建于和铜年间（708—714年），是最早的八幡神社，地位仅次于伊势神宫。

749年，这里的神轿将八幡神灵迎往奈良，护持东大寺大佛的铸造。称德天皇在位时，僧人道镜觊觎皇位，宇佐降下的神谕被用于这场风波。779年弥勒寺在神社旁落成，形成被视为日本最早的神宫寺，即神社与佛寺合一的复合建筑。

宇佐神社衍生出859年的石清水八幡宫、1063年的鹤冈八幡宫等分社。16世纪，府内领主大友义镇多次攻击此地，而义镇之妻、神职奈多夫人曾参与抵抗。

en:
The Vamana Temple at Khajuraho, in the Chandela kingdom of central India, is dedicated to Vamana, the dwarf avatar of Vishnu who in legend took three strides across the world to humble the demon king Bali.

It was raised between about 1050 and 1075 under the Chandela dynasty, whose kings built the Khajuraho complex in the Nagara style during the tenth and eleventh centuries. The shrine stands in the eastern group of monuments, its outer walls carrying the carved divine figures characteristic of Chandela art.

Khajuraho's temples remained in active worship until the late twelfth century; after the Delhi Sultanate under Qutb-ud-din Aibak overran the Chandela kingdom in the thirteenth century the complex was largely abandoned, although the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta could still visit the shrines around 1340.
zh:
瓦玛纳神庙位于中印度昌德拉王国境内的克久拉霍，供奉毗湿奴的侏儒化身瓦玛纳；传说他以三步丈量天地，降服了魔王巴利。

神庙建于约1050—1075年，是昌德拉王朝在10至11世纪以纳加拉风格营建的克久拉霍建筑群的一部分。神庙属于古迹群的东群，外墙布满昌德拉艺术特有的神像雕刻。

克久拉霍诸庙的香火一直延续到12世纪末；13世纪德里苏丹国的库特布丁·艾伊拜克攻灭昌德拉王国后，建筑群大多荒废，不过摩洛哥旅行家伊本·白图泰在约1340年仍曾到此巡礼。

en:
The Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Temple stands on the Simhachalam hills north of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, and is dedicated to Vishnu in a form uniting his boar and man-lion avatars. Legend relates that the devotee Prahlada asked the god to appear as Varaha and Narasimha together. The icon has a boar's head and lion's body, attended by Lakshmi, and is coated in sandalwood paste except at Akshaya Tritiya.

The earliest inscription dates to 1087 under the Chola king Kulottunga I. Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I raised the building in the thirteenth century; his son Bhanudeva I consecrated it in 1268. The Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya set up a victory pillar during his Kalinga campaigns of 1516 to 1519.

Worship was interrupted after 1564 under the Qutb Shahi sultans until a grant of 1604 restored the rites. Simhachalam was a Vaishnavism stronghold in the eastern Deccan.
zh:
室利筏罗诃·吉祥天女·那罗辛哈神庙坐落在安得拉邦维沙卡帕特南北郊的辛赫恰拉姆山上，供奉合野猪化身与人狮化身为一体的毗湿奴。相传虔信者波罗诃罗陀祈求神灵同时显现筏罗诃与那罗辛哈两副化身。主像为猪首狮身、吉祥天女随侍之形，除阿克夏亚·特里蒂亚节外终年裹以檀香膏。

庙中最早的铭文属1087年朱罗王俱卢通伽一世时期。建筑为13世纪东恒伽王纳拉辛哈德瓦一世所建，1268年由其子巴努德瓦一世主持开光。毗奢耶那伽罗统治者克里希纳德瓦拉亚在1516—1519年远征羯陵伽时于此立胜利柱。

1564年以后，受库特布沙希苏丹国统治，庙中仪轨中断，直到1604年的施地令才恢复常祭。辛赫恰拉姆是东德干毗湿奴派的重镇。

en:
The Varaha Temple at Khajuraho houses a colossal monolithic sandstone boar, 2.6 metres long, honouring Varaha, the third avatar of Vishnu. The temple stands in the Western Group of temples raised by the Chandela kings of Jejakabhukti, and dates to about 900 to 925, making it one of the oldest shrines in the complex.

Its myth tells how the asura Hiranyaksha dragged Bhudevi, the earth goddess, to the bottom of the cosmic ocean. Varaha fought him for a thousand years before slaying him and lifting the earth on his tusks. Rows of miniature gods cover the image, with Saraswati bearing her veena between the boar's nose and mouth.

The shrine is an oblong sandstone pavilion on a high plinth, with fourteen plain pillars supporting a pyramid of receding tiers. It faces the Lakshmana Temple and adjoins the Lakshmi shrine.
zh:
克久拉霍的筏罗诃神庙供奉一尊整块砂岩雕成的巨型野猪像，长2.6米，表现毗湿奴的第三化身筏罗诃。神庙属于杰贾卡布蒂的昌德拉诸王兴建的寺庙西群，约建于900—925年，是建筑群中最古老的神祠之一。

神话讲述阿修罗金目把大地女神布德维拖入宇宙之海的海底，筏罗诃与之鏖战千年，终将其诛杀，用獠牙把大地托出海面。巨像通体布满一排排小型神像，猪的口鼻之间还雕有怀抱维纳琴的萨拉斯瓦蒂。

神祠是一座高台上的砂岩长方形亭阁，十四根素面石柱承托层层内收的金字塔式屋顶。它与拉克什曼神庙遥遥相对，紧邻吉祥天女神庙。

en:
The Sri Varahaswamy Temple, also called Bhu Varahaswamy, stands on the Tirumala hills at Tirupati, beside the Venkateswara Temple. It is believed to be older than that shrine; the hills are therefore known as Adi Varaha Kshetra, the first field of Varaha. Varaha is Vishnu's boar avatar, who slew the asura Hiranyaksha and lifted the drowned earth on his tusks.

The Skanda Purana tells how the boar rested by the Swami Pushkarini tank. The hunter Vasu tracked him to an anthill, and Varaha spoke through him to order King Tondaman to raise a temple. Another legend says Varaha granted this land to Venkateswara in return for the right of first worship, so pilgrims worship Varaha first.

The rock shrine follows the Vaikhanasa Agama and was renovated in 1535 by Pedda Tirumalacharya. Varaha Jayanti is celebrated beside the tank each year.
zh:
室利筏罗诃斯瓦米神庙又称布筏罗诃斯瓦米神庙，坐落在蒂鲁帕蒂的蒂鲁马拉山上，位于温卡特斯瓦拉神庙旁。相传它比后者更古老，群山也因此得名“原初筏罗诃之地”。筏罗诃是毗湿奴的野猪化身，诛杀阿修罗金目，用獠牙把大地从海底托起。

《室犍陀往世书》记载，野猪在斯瓦米·普什卡里尼圣湖岸边安息。猎人瓦苏追猎野猪来到蚁冢前，筏罗诃借他之口传令，命通达曼王在此建庙。另一则传说称，筏罗诃把土地让给温卡特斯瓦拉，后者回报以首祭之权，因此朝山者先礼拜筏罗诃。

这座岩石神庙依《毗坎那萨阿笈摩》举行仪轨，1535年由佩达·蒂鲁马拉查里亚重修。每年湖畔都庆祝筏罗诃诞辰。

en:
Varanasi, also called Benares or Kashi, stands on the Ganges and was the capital of the ancient Kingdom of Kashi in the first millennium BCE. Hindu tradition holds that Shiva founded this holy city, where death and cremation are believed to release the soul from rebirth. Pilgrims bathe from its ghats; the Kashi Vishwanath temple is one of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva.

The Ghurid ruler Muhammad of Ghor sacked Varanasi in 1194 and destroyed the original Vishwanath temple. Rebuilt under Akbar, it was demolished by Aurangzeb in 1669, who raised the Gyanvapi Mosque on its site. The Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar built the present temple nearby in 1780.

The Bhakti saints Kabir and Ravidas were born here. As Mughal power weakened, the Kingdom of Benares emerged under Balwant Singh in 1740 and passed to the East India Company in 1775.
zh:
瓦拉纳西又称贝拿勒斯或迦尸，坐落于恒河畔，公元前一千纪时曾是古代迦尸国的都城。印度教传统认为这座圣城由湿婆神建立，相信在此死去、火化可使灵魂脱离轮回。朝圣者沿河坛步入恒河沐浴；湿婆金庙是供奉湿婆的十二处究提林迦圣地之一。

1194年，古尔王朝的穆罕默德·古尔洗劫瓦拉纳西，摧毁了最早的威斯瓦纳特神庙。该庙在阿克巴时期重建，却又在1669年被奥朗则布拆毁，原址建起吉扬瓦皮清真寺。1780年马拉塔女王阿希莉亚拜·霍尔卡在邻近地点修建现存的神庙。

虔诚派圣徒迦比尔和拉维达斯都出生于此。随着莫卧儿势力衰落，贝拿勒斯王国于1740年在巴尔万特·辛格治下兴起，并于1775年转归英国东印度公司。

en:
Vazelon Monastery was built in the Pontic Mountains, about forty kilometres south of Trebizond, in the Maçka valley. Dedicated to John the Baptist, it was founded in Roman times, around 270 or 317, making it one of Anatolia's oldest monasteries.

In the sixth century Sassanid raiders sacked it and killed its monks; in 565 Emperor Justinian I ordered it repaired. After the Fourth Crusade shattered Byzantium in 1204, the emperors of Trebizond endowed Vazelon, and its surviving buildings date from a rebuilding of 1410.

The monastery held authority over surrounding villages, and its church was decorated with frescoes of Heaven, Hell and the Last Judgement. Through the Ottoman conquest of 1461 and the centuries that followed, Vazelon remained a centre of Greek Orthodox worship, and its archive became a source for the history of Byzantium and Trebizond.
zh:
瓦泽隆修道院建于特拉比松以南约40公里的马奇卡山谷，地处本都山脉。它供奉施洗约翰，始建于罗马时代的270年或317年前后，是安纳托利亚最古老的修道院之一。

6世纪时，萨珊波斯入侵者洗劫修道院并杀害修士，565年查士丁尼一世下令修复。1204年第四次十字军东征瓦解拜占庭后，特拉比松帝国皇帝厚赐瓦泽隆，现存建筑则建于1410年的重建。

修道院管辖着周围村庄，教堂内绘有天堂、地狱和最后的审判壁画。经历1461年奥斯曼征服之后的数百年间，瓦泽隆始终是希腊正教的礼拜中心，其档案成为研究拜占庭与特拉比松历史的资料。

en:
The Vedadri Narasimha Temple stands on the bank of the Krishna River and is one of the Pancha Narasimha Kshetras, the five great shrines of the man-lion god. Its sthalapurana tells that the demon Somakasura stole the Vedas from Brahma and hid them in the ocean, whereupon Vishnu appeared as Narasimha, rescued the sacred texts and turned them into the hill of Vedadri.

Five forms of Narasimha are worshipped here, including Vira, Jwala and Yoga Narasimha. The temple rose to prominence under the Kakatiya Empire, and the Telugu saint-composer Narayana Tirtha was a frequent visitor. In the nineteenth century the zamindar Vasireddy Muktiswara Prasad Nayudu renovated it, renewing the flagstaff and building 108 steps down to the Krishna.
zh:
韦达德里的那罗辛哈神庙屹立在克里希纳河畔，是五大人狮神神庙之一。当地圣传称，阿修罗索摩阿修罗从梵天处盗走吠陀经并藏于海中，毗湿奴遂化身为那罗辛哈，夺回经典并将其化为韦达德里山。

庙中供奉那罗辛哈的五种形相，包括维拉、耆婆罗和瑜伽那罗辛哈。神庙在卡卡提亚帝国时期声名鹊起，泰卢固圣徒兼诗人纳拉亚纳·蒂尔塔曾常来参拜。19世纪，柴明达尔瓦西雷迪·穆克蒂斯瓦拉·普拉萨德·奈杜重修神庙，更换了旗杆，并修建了108级通往克里希纳河的台阶。

en:
Vidisha, the medieval city of Bhilsa in eastern Malwa, is counted among the ancient Jain pilgrimage lands, for Jains believe it was the birthplace of Shitalanatha, the tenth Tirthankara. The oldest shrines in the district date to the 800s and 900s, when the Pratihara and Paramara schools of temple architecture flourished.

At Gyaraspur the rock-cut Maladevi temple, dedicated to Adinatha, and the Bajramath, a Brahmanical Surya temple later given over to Jain images, preserve Tirthankara sculptures. At Badoh the Pataria complex groups twenty-five temples around a central spired shrine; the Gadarmal temple shelters both Hindu and Jain idols.

Bhilsa stood on northern trade routes and suffered conquest: Iltutmish of Delhi stormed it in 1233, Alauddin Khalji sacked it in 1293, and Bahadur Shah of Gujarat plundered it in 1532. The old Jain temples on its outskirts survived the changing rulers.
zh:
毗提舍即中世纪的比尔沙城，地处东摩腊婆，被耆那教列为古老圣地之一，因为相传这里是第十代祖师湿多罗那陀的诞生地。当地最古老的殿宇可追溯至9—10世纪，正值普罗蒂诃罗与波罗摩罗建筑流派兴盛之时。

在吉亚拉斯布尔，凿岩而建、奉祀阿底那特的摩罗提毗寺，以及由婆罗门教日神庙改为供奉祖师像的巴阇罗摩特寺，都保存着祖师雕刻。巴多赫的波塔里亚建筑群以带尖塔的主殿为中心，汇集二十五座庙宇；伽达尔摩罗寺则有印度教与耆那教神像共处一殿。

比尔沙扼守北方商路，一再遭征服：德里的伊勒杜迷失于1233年攻破此城，阿拉乌德丁·卡尔吉1293年劫掠，古吉拉特的巴哈杜尔沙又于1532年洗劫此地。城郊的古老耆那寺庙在历代统治者更迭中存留了下来。

en:
The Vilwadrinatha Temple stands at Thiruvilwamala, on a hillock above the Bharathappuzha river in the Malabar interior. It is dedicated to Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, and his brother Lakshmana, whose idol is rare in Indian temples. It is one of the four great Rama temples of Kerala.

The temple was first administered by five Moosad families, who traced their rights to the sage Parashurama. In 392 the Chera king Cheraman Perumal granted its lands to the Perumpadappu rulers, who enlarged the estate and left worship to a twice-yearly assembly. The temple later passed to the Zamorins of Kozhikode and, after prolonged wars, to the kings of Kochi, under whom it remained a pilgrimage centre.
zh:
鼻缚陀梨那他神庙坐落于马拉巴尔内陆蒂鲁维尔瓦马拉的高丘上，俯瞰巴拉塔普扎河。神庙供奉毗湿奴的第七化身罗摩及其弟罗什曼那，罗什曼那神像在印度十分罕见。它是喀拉拉四大罗摩神庙之一。

神庙最初由五个穆萨德家族管理，他们把治庙之权追溯到仙人持斧罗摩。392年，哲罗国王切拉曼·佩鲁马尔将庙产赐给佩鲁姆帕杜普的统治者，后者扩大了庙地，并把庙务交由每年两次的大会主持。神庙后来转归科泽科德的扎莫林，经过长期交战后又落入科契国王之手，仍是朝圣中心。

en:
The Vimala Temple stands inside the Jagannath Temple complex at Puri on the Odisha coast. Though a small shrine beside the main tower, Shakta and Tantric worshippers revere it as one of the holiest Shakti Pithas dedicated to the Goddess. Its icon of Vimala, the tantric consort of Jagannath, dates to the 500s.

The sandstone and laterite Deula-style building was probably raised in the 800s under the Eastern Ganga dynasty, perhaps on the ruins of an older Somavashi shrine; temple tradition credits the Somavashi king Yayati Keshari with its foundation. The philosopher Adi Shankara is said to have made Vimala the presiding goddess of his Govardhana matha at Puri.

Devotees visit Vimala before Jagannath, and food offered to Jagannath becomes Mahaprasad only after it is also offered to her. A sixteen-day Durga Puja culminating in Vijayadashami is held here every autumn.
zh:
毗摩罗神庙坐落于奥里萨沿海补梨的札格纳特神庙建筑群内。它虽只是主塔旁的一座小殿，却被性力派和密教信徒尊为奉祀女神的至神圣地性力佩特之一。庙中毗摩罗女神是札格纳特的密教法侣，其主像可追溯至6世纪。

以砂岩和红土岩建成的德乌拉风格建筑可能建于9世纪东恒伽王朝时期，也可能坐落在索马万什王朝旧庙的废墟之上；庙方传统则将建庙之功归于索马万什国王耶耶迪·凯沙里。哲学家商羯罗据传以毗摩罗为其在补梨所建戈瓦尔达摩特的主神。

信徒先拜毗摩罗再拜札格纳特，献给札格纳特的食物也只有再供奉过她之后才算圣食。每年秋季这里举行长达十六天的难近母节，以十胜日庆典收尾。

en:
The Vinayaka Temple, formally the Sri Varasidhi Vinayaka Swamy Temple, is a Ganesha shrine at Kanipakam in Andhra Pradesh. Its Ganesha is said to dwell in a well that never runs dry: legend tells of three brothers, one mute, one deaf and one blind, who struck a hard object while digging, saw blood well up and were cured, after which the villagers uncovered the image but could never find its base.

The stone temple was founded under the Chola emperor Kulottunga I, who reigned from 1070 to 1120, and enlarged in 1336 by the emperors of Vijayanagara. Piety held that the image was growing in its well, so that ever less of it could be seen above the water.
zh:
毗那夜迦神庙正式名称为室利·瓦拉悉提·毗那夜迦斯瓦米神庙，是安得拉邦卡尼帕卡姆的一座伽内什神庙。庙中的伽内什相传居于一口永不干涸的井中：传说有三兄弟分别为哑、聋、盲，挖井时农具撞到硬物，井水涌血，三人的残疾随即痊愈；村民随后发现了这尊神像，却始终挖不到它的底座。

这座石庙由朱罗皇帝库洛通加一世（1070—1120年在位）敕建，1336年毗奢耶那伽罗皇帝又加以扩建。信众相信井中的神像在不断长大，水面之上能见到的部分越来越少。

en:
The Vishalakshi Temple stands near Mir Ghat in Varanasi, close to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, and is dedicated to Parvati as Vishalakshi, the wide-eyed goddess. Hindu tradition counts it among the fifty-one Shakti Peethas: when Vishnu dismembered Sati, the gem of her right earring is said to have fallen here, so the goddess is also called Manikarni Devi. Kaal Bhairav is venerated as its guardian.

The Tantric Rudrayamala, composed before 1052, names Varanasi among the ten principal Shakti Peethas. The Skanda Purana tells how Vishalakshi appeared as a housewife to feed the sage Vyasa when the city refused him alms.

Together with the Vishwanath temple, the Ganges and the Kala Bhairava temple, the Vishalakshi Temple forms one of the six sites of Varanasi's Shastanga yoga pilgrimage. It was rebuilt in the nineteenth century by Nattukottai Nagarathar merchants from Tamil Nadu.
zh:
宽目女神庙坐落于瓦拉纳西的米尔河阶附近，距迦尸·毗湿瓦纳特神庙不远，供奉以“宽目”为号的帕尔瓦蒂女神。印度教传统将它列为五十一座性力圣地之一：传说毗湿奴肢解萨蒂遗体时，她右耳环上的宝石坠落于此，因此女神又称摩尼格尔尼女神。圣地的守护男神是迦罗·拜拉弗。

成书不晚于1052年的怛特罗经典《鲁陀罗夜密续》把瓦拉纳西列为十大性力圣地之一。《室建陀往世书》讲到，全城无人愿意布施时，宽目女神化身为主妇向仙人毗耶娑奉上食物。

神庙与毗湿瓦纳特神庙、恒河、迦罗·拜拉弗神庙等共同构成瓦拉纳西六处“六支瑜伽”巡礼地。19世纪泰米尔纳德的纳图科泰·纳加拉塔尔商帮重建了殿宇。

en:
The Vithoba Temple, formally the Shri Vitthal-Rukmini Mandir, stands at Pandharpur in southern Maharashtra on the Chandrabhaga River. It is the chief shrine of Vithoba, a standing form of Vishnu, worshipped with his consort Rakhumai. A small shrine existed here by 1189, and Hoysala inscriptions of 1237 and 1273 to 1277 record grants and the building of the temple, traditionally credited to King Vishnuvardhana on the counsel of the devotee Pundalik.

From the 1200s the shrine became the heart of the Warkari bhakti movement, whose poet-saints sang in Marathi. Pilgrim bands called dindi march to Pandharpur for the Aashadhi and Kartiki Ekadashi festivals.

Much of the structure dates to the 1600s in the later Deccan style. When Afzal Khan moved against the temple in the mid-1600s its priests hid the original image, so the central idol survived.
zh:
鼻多呼婆神庙正式名称为“室利·维塔尔—鲁格米尼神庙”，位于南马哈拉施特拉潘达尔普尔的旃陀罗跋伽河畔，是毗湿奴的站立化身维塔尔（鼻多呼婆）与其配偶拉库迈的主庙。1189年此地已有小型神龛，1237年及1273—1277年的霍伊萨拉铭文记载了赐地和神庙的修建；传统认为庙是毗湿奴瓦尔达纳王受虔信者本达利克劝化而建。

13世纪起，这里成为瓦尔卡里虔信运动的中心，诗人圣徒用马拉地语为其颂诗。每逢阿沙迪与卡尔提卡两节的十一日，成群的“丁迪”朝圣者便步行赶往潘达尔普尔。

现存建筑多为17世纪所建，属后期德干风格。17世纪中叶阿夫扎尔汗图谋毁庙时，祭司藏起原像，使主像得以保全。

en:
Wak'a Pukllana is an adobe and clay pyramid of seven staggered platforms, rising twenty-two metres in the Rímac valley on the central Peruvian coast. Its Quechua name joins wak'a, a shrine of a protector deity, with pukllana, a place of games or rituals.

Between about 200 and 700 it was the chief ceremonial and administrative centre of the Lima culture. Its priests built the pyramid to display power over the valley's water; plaza pits received offerings of fish and other marine produce. Wari materials and the elite tomb of the Lord of the Unkus show the shrine remained in use under Wari influence until about 1000.

After the Wari collapse the Ichma kingdom formed around 1100 and spread into the valley, keeping old wak'a in use. Around 1469 the Inca absorbed the Ichma, and the shrine entered the empire's network of sacred sites.
zh:
普拉那圣所是一座由七层错落台基构成的土坯黏土金字塔，高二十二米，坐落在秘鲁中部沿海的里马克河谷。其克丘亚语名称由wak'a（守护神灵的圣所）与pukllana（举行仪式或竞技之处）组合而成。

约200—700年，它是利马文化最重要的仪式与行政中心。祭司修建金字塔，以彰显其掌控河谷水资源的权力；广场上的坑用来盛放鱼类和其他海产祭品。瓦里文化遗物和精英墓葬“温库斯之主”表明，在瓦里文化影响下该圣所一直使用到约1000年。

瓦里帝国崩溃后，伊什马王国约于1100年形成并扩展到里马克河谷，继续沿用古老圣所。约1469年印加兼并伊什马，这座圣所随之并入帝国的圣地网络。

en:
Wayna Qhari is a mountain south of Cusco, its Quechua name meaning strong young man. Its summit was one of the most important wak'as of the Inca world.

In the dynasty's foundation legend, the Ayar siblings came out of the cave at Paqariq Tampu. Ayar Uchu chose to stay on this hill as a stone idol to speak with their father the Sun and intercede for the lineage. The story told how he flew toward the heavens, returned to tell Ayar Manco to take the name Manco Cápac, and turned into stone with his wings still spread.

He became the guardian wak'a of the new Cusco dynasty. Rulers and pilgrims visited until the Spanish conquest in 1533, after which chroniclers recorded its fame while the summit shrines fell into ruin.
zh:
瓦纳考里山位于库斯科以南，克丘亚语名意为“强壮的青年”，山顶是印加世界最重要的圣所之一。

据王朝起源传说，阿亚尔兄弟姐妹从帕卡里坦博洞穴走出，其中阿亚尔·乌丘选择留在山上化为石像，以便与他们的父亲太阳对话，为氏族祈福。传说他振翅飞向云霄，返回后告知阿亚尔·曼科须改称曼科·卡帕克，随后带着展开的双翼变成石头。

他成为库斯科新王朝的守护圣所，历代君主与朝圣者皆来祭拜，直到1533年西班牙征服库斯科；此后编年史家记下了它的声名，山顶的圣所却逐渐倾颓。

en:
The basilica of Our Lady of the Pillar stands on the bank of the Ebro in Zaragoza. Tradition holds that on 2 January in the year 40 the Virgin Mary appeared to the apostle James the Great, giving him a jasper column and bidding him build a church there. The chapel was reputedly the first church dedicated to Mary; the pillar and image survived Muslim rule.

After Alfonso I of Aragon reconquered Zaragoza in 1118 a Romanesque church arose. A fire in 1434 forced a rebuilding in Mudéjar Gothic form, which kept the alabaster altarpiece carved by Damián Forment.

The Baroque church was begun in 1681 under Charles II; Ventura Rodríguez designed the Holy Chapel housing the statue in 1754, and Francisco de Goya later painted frescoes on its domes. Ignatius of Loyola, Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross made pilgrimages.
zh:
比拉尔圣母圣殿矗立在萨拉戈萨的埃布罗河畔。相传40年1月2日，圣母马利亚向使徒大雅各显现，交给他一根碧玉柱，嘱他在此建堂。随后建起的小堂被认为是第一座奉圣母为主保的教堂，石柱与圣母像在穆斯林统治时期得以保全。

阿拉贡国王阿方索一世于1118年收复萨拉戈萨后，这里建起一座罗马式教堂。1434年的火灾迫使教堂按穆德哈尔哥特风格重建，达米安·福尔门特雕刻的雪花石膏祭坛屏饰保留了下来。

巴洛克教堂于1681年在卡洛斯二世治下动工；文图拉·罗德里格斯于1754年设计了安放圣母像的圣小堂，后来弗朗西斯科·德·戈雅又在穹顶上绘制湿壁画。依纳爵·罗耀拉、阿维拉的特蕾莎和十字若望都曾来朝圣。

en:
Al-Zaytuna, the Mosque of the Olive, is the oldest mosque in Tunis, standing in its medina on the site of a Byzantine building, perhaps a church. Tradition ascribes its foundation in 698 to Hasan ibn al-Nu'man; the Umayyad governor Ubayd Allah ibn al-Habhab rebuilt it around 732.

Its present form dates to the Aghlabid reconstruction completed in 864 or 865 under Emir Abu Ibrahim Ahmad, whose builders reused hundreds of antique columns from Carthage. The Zirids added the courtyard galleries and the Qubbat al-Bahu dome in 991. Under the Hafsids the mosque overtook Kairouan as the foremost seat of learning in the Maghreb; al-Mustansir restored it in 1250.

In 1534 Spanish troops sacked its libraries and scattered its manuscripts. The Ottoman Muradid and Husaynid dynasties restored its teaching role, and the Bakri family supplied its imams from 1624 to 1812.
zh:
宰图纳大清真寺意为“橄榄清真寺”，是突尼斯城最古老的清真寺，坐落于老城，其地原为一座拜占庭建筑，可能是一座教堂。相传它由哈桑·伊本·努阿曼于698年奠基；倭马亚王朝总督欧贝杜拉·伊本·哈卜哈卜约在732年将其重建。

它现存的形制来自阿格拉布王朝的重建，工程在埃米尔阿布·易卜拉欣·艾哈迈德治下于864年或865年完工，工匠们从迦太基废墟中拆用了数百根古代石柱。991年，齐尔王朝增建了庭院回廊和巴胡穹顶。哈夫斯王朝治下，这座清真寺取代凯鲁万，成为马格里布首屈一指的学府；穆斯坦绥尔于1250年加以修缮。

1534年，西班牙军队洗劫了它的藏书室，手稿散佚损毁。奥斯曼时期的穆拉德王朝和侯赛因王朝恢复了它的教学地位，1624—1812年间，巴克利家族世代担任该寺伊玛目。

en:
Abenakian is the speech of the Wabanaki peoples, a dialect chain including Eastern and Western Abenaki and Mi'kmaq. Its speakers call themselves Wôbanakiak, People of the Dawn Land, and the polysynthetic language packs whole sentences into single words.

Champlain met Abenaki farmers on the Kennebec river in 1604, and the English word skunk was borrowed from their speech in the 1630s. Epidemics and pressure from English settlements drove many Abenaki under French protection from 1669, when missions were founded at Odanak and Wôlinak, where Jesuits recorded dialects in grammars and word lists.

Allied with the French, they raided the English frontier through King Philip's War of 1675 and Queen Anne's War, until the Jesuit Sébastien Rale was killed at Norridgewock in 1724 and the Abenaki wars ended the following year.
zh:
阿贝纳基语是瓦巴纳基诸族的语言，方言连续体包括东西两支阿贝纳基方言和米克马克语。使用者自称沃巴纳基阿克人，意为“黎明之地的人”，这种多式综合语能把整句话压缩进一个词。

1604年，尚普兰在肯纳贝克河畔见到务农的阿贝纳基人；17世纪30年代，英语的“臭鼬”一词借自他们的语言。疫病和英国定居者的挤压迫使许多阿贝纳基人从1669年起投入法国庇护之下，法国在奥达纳克和沃利纳克建立传教站，耶稣会士用语法书和词表记录方言。

他们与法国结盟，在1675年的菲利普国王战争和后来的安妮女王战争中不断袭击英国边疆，直到耶稣会士塞巴斯蒂安·拉勒于1724年在诺里奇沃克被杀，阿贝纳基诸战于次年告终。

official_raw.en: An Eastern Algonquian branch spoken in much of Northern New England and the Canadian Maritimes.
official_raw.zh: 在新英格兰北部和加拿大滨海地区大部分区域使用的东阿尔冈昆语分支。

en:
Abun, called Anden by its speakers and Yimbun by the neighbouring Mpur, is a Papuan language of the northern coast of the Bird's Head Peninsula, spoken around Sausapor. It has no demonstrated relatives: Malcolm Ross placed it tentatively in the West Papuan family, but most reference works list it as a language isolate.

The tonal language has four dialects forming a continuum of mutual intelligibility. Long contact with Biak traders and settlers left Austronesian maritime vocabulary in Abun, which the seafaring Biak call Karon Pantai, a derogatory exonym.

From the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the Bird's Head coasts entered the Sultanate of Tidore's tribute system, bound by the legendary alliance between the Biak leader Gurabesi and Sultan Al-Mansur. The Spanish expedition of Luís Vaz de Torres sailed these waters in 1606; Abun villages kept their speech and customs under this loose overlordship.
zh:
阿本语在母语者口中称Anden，邻近的姆普尔人称之为Yimbun，是鸟头半岛北海岸的巴布亚语言，通行于绍萨波尔周围。它没有已证实的亲属语言：马尔科姆·罗斯暂时把它归入西巴布亚语系，但多数参考书将其列为孤立语言。

阿本语是声调语言，分为四种方言，构成互通程度渐变的方言连续体。与比亚克商人和定居者的长期接触为它留下了南岛语航海词汇，航海的比亚克人贬称它为“海岸卡龙”。

从15至16世纪起，鸟头半岛沿海被卷入蒂多雷苏丹国的朝贡体系，其纽带是比亚克首领古拉贝西与苏丹阿尔-曼苏尔之间传说中的联盟。1606年，路易斯·瓦斯·德·托雷斯的西班牙探险队驶过这片水域；在这种松散的宗主权下，阿本村庄保留了自己的语言和风俗。

en:
Adamawa is the conventional name for a loose group of eighty to ninety languages scattered over the Adamawa Plateau and surrounding country in northern Cameroon, southern Chad, eastern Nigeria and the north-west of the Central African Republic. The largest member is Mumuye; many others are small tongues.

Joseph Greenberg assembled them into an Adamawa branch of the Niger–Congo family, though later linguists have treated them as more of a geographic grouping than a true family, some branches lying closer to Gur. For most of history their speakers lived in decentralised farming and pastoral communities between Hausaland and the Bornu and Mandara states.

In 1809 Modibo Adama, a follower of Usman dan Fodio, carried the Fulani jihad into these lands and founded the Adamawa Emirate within the Sokoto Caliphate, drawing the plateau's peoples into the world of Muslim cavalry states and long-distance slave raiding.
zh:
阿达马瓦语是对八九十种关系松散的语言的统称，它们散布在阿达马瓦高原及周边地带，包括喀麦隆北部、乍得南部、尼日利亚东部和中非共和国西北部。其中最大的是穆穆耶语，其余多是使用人数很少的语言。

约瑟夫·格林伯格曾把它们归为尼日尔—刚果语系下的阿达马瓦语支，但后来的语言学家多认为它更像地理分组而非真正的语族，其中有些分支与古尔语更近。在历史上的大部分时间里，说这些语言的族群以分散的农耕和游牧社群生活，夹在豪萨兰与博尔努、曼达拉等政权之间。

1809年，乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥的追随者莫迪博·阿达马把富拉尼圣战带入这片土地，在索科托哈里发国之内建立阿达马瓦酋长国，使高原各族进入穆斯林骑兵政权和长途奴隶劫掠的世界。

en:
Adharic is the North-Western Iranian subgroup named after Adhari, or Old Azeri, the Iranian speech of Azerbaijan before the spread of Turkic. Medieval Arab geographers such as al-Masudi knew it as al-adhariya, and the peasant rebels who followed Babak in the 800s spoke its dialects.

From the 1000s the Seljuk advance brought Turkic tribes into Azerbaijan. Adhari lost its majority position by the end of the 1300s, lingering in mountain enclaves into the 1600s before giving way to Azerbaijani Turkic.

Its relatives include Talysh of Gilan and Ardabil, which Hamdallah Mustawfi in the 1330s described as a Pahlavi-type tongue and which survives in the quatrains of Sheikh Safi of Ardabil, who died in 1334; Tati dialects such as Harzandi; and Zazaki in eastern Anatolia, whose archaic grammar has been argued to be a relic of Parthian.
zh:
阿扎里克语是西北伊朗语的一个子群，得名于阿扎里语，即突厥语传播之前阿塞拜疆地区的伊朗语，亦称古阿塞拜疆语。马苏迪等中世纪阿拉伯地理学家称其为“阿扎里耶”；9世纪追随巴贝克起事的农民说它的各方言。

从11世纪起，塞尔柱人的推进把突厥部落带入阿塞拜疆。阿扎里语到14世纪末失去多数语言的地位，在山地飞地中残存到17世纪，最终让位于阿塞拜疆突厥语。

与它同源的语言包括吉兰和阿尔达比勒的塔利希语，穆斯塔菲在14世纪30年代曾把这一带的语言描述为巴列维型语言，1334年去世的阿尔达比勒谢赫·萨非的四行诗中也保留着它的面貌；哈尔赞迪语等塔蒂方言；以及安纳托利亚东部的扎扎其语，其古老语法被认为可能是帕提亚语的遗存。

en:
Afghani is the name used in Persian historical writings for the Eastern Iranian language otherwise known as Pashto, the mother tongue of the Pashtun tribes of southern and eastern Afghanistan and the Peshawar valley. Its verse grew from an oral tradition of tappa lyrics, with the earliest named poet, Amir Kror Suri, placed in the 700s.

In the 1500s Bayazid Pir Roshan of Waziristan devised a 41-letter Perso-Arabic alphabet for his Roshani movement and composed Khair-ul-Bayan, one of the language's earliest prose works. The scholar Akhund Darweza answered his teachings with Makhzanul Islam.

The 1600s brought a literary golden age under the warrior-poet Khushal Khan Khattak, called the father of Pashto literature, and the Sufi poet Rahman Baba, who died in 1706. Persian long remained the language of courts and government, leaving Afghani as the speech of tribe and camp.
zh:
阿富汗语是波斯历史文献对普什图语的称呼，属于东伊朗语，是阿富汗南部、东部以及白沙瓦河谷普什图诸部的母语。它的诗歌源于口头诗“塔帕”的传统，最早留名的诗人是8世纪的阿米尔·克罗尔·苏里。

16世纪，瓦济里斯坦的巴亚齐德·皮尔·罗山为自己的罗沙尼运动设计了一套41个字母的波斯—阿拉伯字母，并写成最早的普什图语散文著作之一《海尔·巴扬》。学者阿洪德·达尔韦扎著《伊斯兰宝库》回应他的学说。

17世纪迎来文学黄金时代，被誉为普什图文学之父的战士诗人胡沙尔·汗·哈塔克，以及1706年去世的苏菲派诗人拉赫曼·巴巴是其中代表。长期以来波斯语垄断着宫廷和政府，阿富汗语则是部落与营地之间的口头语言。

en:
The Agaw languages, also called Central Cushitic, are a branch of the Afroasiatic family spoken across the Ethiopian highlands from Lake Tana to Lasta, with Bilen reaching into Eritrea and eastern Sudan. Their main members include Awngi, Xamtanga, Bilen and Qimant, whose Qwara and Kayla dialects were once spoken by the Beta Israel.

Agaw speech forms the chief substratum of Amharic and the other Ethio-Semitic languages, which absorbed much of its vocabulary as Semitic spread through the highlands. In the twelfth century Agaw chiefs of Lasta founded the Zagwe dynasty, which ruled Christian Ethiopia until 1270.

Its best-remembered king, Lalibela, gave his name to the rock-hewn churches, and succession followed the Agaw custom of brother succeeding brother. After the Zagwe fall the Agaw kept their tongues in remote highland districts such as Wag and the country around Lake Tana.
zh:
阿高语又称中库希特语，是亚非语系的一支，通行于埃塞俄比亚高原上从塔纳湖到拉斯塔一带，其中比伦语还延伸到厄立特里亚和苏丹东部。主要语言包括阿翁吉语、哈姆坦加语、比伦语和克曼特语，克曼特语的夸拉方言和凯拉方言曾由贝塔以色列人使用。

阿高语是阿姆哈拉语等埃塞俄比亚闪米特语的主要底层语言，后者随闪米特语在高原扩散，吸收了它的大量词汇。12世纪，拉斯塔的阿高首领建立扎格维王朝，统治基督教埃塞俄比亚直至1270年。

王朝最著名的国王拉利贝拉留下了以他命名的整岩凿成教堂群，王位则按阿高人的习俗兄终弟及。扎格维王朝覆灭后，阿高人在瓦格、塔纳湖周边等偏远高原地区继续使用自己的语言。

en: Aikanã is a language isolate spoken by the Aikanã people of Rondônia in western Brazil, around the Corumbiara and Tubarão rivers, where they live alongside Kwaza-speaking communities. Also recorded under the names Tubarão, Corumbiara and Huari, it has a subject–object–verb word order and shows only contact-induced similarities with the neighbouring isolates Kanoê and Kwaza.
zh: 艾卡纳语是巴西西部朗多尼亚州艾卡纳人使用的一种孤立语言，分布在科伦比阿拉河与图巴朗河一带，与说夸扎语的群体相邻而居。它也曾被记作图巴朗语、科伦比阿拉语或瓦里语，语序为主宾动，与邻近的卡诺埃语、夸扎语等孤立语言仅有因接触产生的相似之处。

en:
A'ingae, also called Cofán, is the language of the A'i people living between the Guamués and Aguarico rivers where the Andes meet the Amazon, in northeastern Ecuador and southern Colombia. The name means in the manner of the people, from a'i, person. Once linked to Chibchan or other Andean groupings, it is treated as a language isolate, though it carries borrowings from Tukanoan, Cariban and Quechuan.

Inca pressure had driven the A'i from the cordillera into the lowlands. In the late sixteenth century they destroyed the Spanish town of Mocoa and forced the colonists to withdraw; the Jesuit Rafael Ferrer, who arrived in 1602, was likewise driven out.

Epidemics cut the people from some fifteen thousand to a few hundred, but the language remained the foundation of Cofán identity through the colonial centuries.
zh:
科凡语又称阿依语，是阿依人的语言，通行于厄瓜多尔东北部和哥伦比亚南部、安第斯山脉与亚马孙雨林相接处的瓜穆埃斯河与阿瓜里科河之间。其名称由意为“人”的“阿依”派生，意思是“按人的方式说的话”。它过去曾被归入奇布查语系或其他安第斯语群，后被视为孤立语言，但吸收了图卡诺语、加勒比语和克丘亚语的借词。

印加人的逼迫早已把阿依人从山脉赶入低地。16世纪末，他们摧毁西班牙人的莫科阿镇，迫使殖民者撤退，1602年抵达的耶稣会士拉斐尔·费雷尔同样被赶走。

瘟疫使科凡人从约一万五千人锐减到几百人，但在整个殖民时代，这门语言始终是科凡认同的根基。

en:
Ainu is the language of the Ainu people of Hokkaido, southern Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands, and forms a small language family on its own; no link to any other family has been demonstrated. Place-name evidence suggests it was once spoken in northern Honshu, perhaps by the Emishi, and that the northern Japanese river-name ending -betsu comes from pet, meaning river. The word aynu means person.

From the 1300s Ainu met Japanese traders and settlers, and their language took in many Japanese loanwords while giving a few in return. It also exchanged vocabulary with the neighboring Nivkh.

Its classical form, preserved in oral epics, was polysynthetic. It had no native script and was later written in modified Japanese katakana and Latin letters. On Sakhalin it long served as a lingua franca used by Japanese and Russian officials as well as local peoples.
zh:
阿伊努语是北海道、萨哈林岛南部和千岛群岛的阿伊努人的语言，本身构成一个小语系，未能证明它与任何其他语系有亲缘关系。地名证据显示，阿伊努语一度通行于本州北部，可能是虾夷人的语言；日本北部的河名后缀-betsu来自意为河流的pet。aynu意为“人”。

阿伊努人自14世纪起与日本商人和定居者接触，阿伊努语吸收了大量日语借词，也有少量词反向进入日语。它还与邻近的尼夫赫语互有借词。

见于口传史诗的古典阿伊努语是多式综合语。它没有本族文字，后来以改造的日语片假名和拉丁字母记录。在萨哈林岛，它长期充当通用语，日本和俄罗斯官员与当地各族都借助它沟通。

en:
Ajië, also called Houailou or Wailu, is a Kanak language of the Austronesian family spoken around Houaïlou, Kouaoua and Poya on the east-central coast of Grande Terre, the main island of New Caledonia. It is the principal language of the Wailic branch of the southern New Caledonian languages, part of the Southern Oceanic group.

Like the other Kanak tongues it descends from the speech of the Lapita voyagers who founded coastal settlements in New Caledonia around 1100 BC. Throughout the period described here, Ajië had no native script and was carried by oral tradition.

James Cook sighted Grande Terre in 1774 and named it New Caledonia; the Comte de Lapérouse reconnoitred the west coast in 1788, and from 1793 English whalers mapped the Loyalty Islands.
zh:
阿杰语又称瓦伊卢语，是新喀里多尼亚主岛格朗德特尔岛中东部沿海瓦伊卢、夸瓦和波亚一带通行的卡纳克语言，属南岛语系。它是新喀里多尼亚南部语言瓦伊卢语支的主要语言，该语支隶属于南大洋洲语群。

与其他卡纳克语言一样，阿杰语源自拉皮塔航海者的语言，他们约在公元前1100年开始在新喀里多尼亚沿海建立定居点。在此处所述的时期，阿杰语没有本土文字，依靠口传传承。

1774年詹姆斯·库克望见格朗德特尔岛，并将其命名为新喀里多尼亚；1788年拉彼鲁兹伯爵考察了西海岸，1793年起英国捕鲸人测绘了洛亚蒂群岛。

en:
Akei, also called Tasiriki, is an Oceanic language of the Austronesian family spoken along the southwestern coast of Espiritu Santo in Vanuatu and centred on the village of Tasiriki, a name meaning small water. It is grouped with Wailapa in the Southwest Santo subgroup of the West Santo languages, part of the North-Central Vanuatu branch.

Scholars sometimes treat Akei as a dialect of a proposed Southwest Santo language shared with Araki and Tangoa, or describe it as a dialect chain whose varieties at the two ends are no longer mutually intelligible. It is known by local names including Navaka, Marino, Pilipili and Wailapa.

The Spanish expedition of Pedro Fernandes de Queirós reached Espiritu Santo in 1606. Louis de Bougainville visited in 1768 and James Cook in 1774, when the archipelago received the European name New Hebrides.
zh:
